MCQ Mentor Review Queue

Paper 1: Advanced Accounting · Module 1 · Chapter 1:

Accounts — 55 rows
Easy NORMAL · ASSB History | ICAI Creation
In which year was the Accounting Standards Board (ASSB) constituted by the Institute of Chartered Accountants of India (ICAI)?
A. 1977 ✔
B. 1956
C. 1991
D. 2013
Explanation: The Accounting Standards Board (ASSB) was constituted by the ICAI on 21st April 1977. Its primary function is to formulate Accounting Standards for Indian entities.
Easy NORMAL · Companies Act 2013 | NFRA | Standard Setting Process
Under Section 133 of the Companies Act, 2013, who prescribes the Accounting Standards for companies in India?
A. The Institute of Chartered Accountants of India (ICAI) directly
B. The Central Government after considering recommendations of National Financial Reporting Authority (NFRA) ✔
C. The Reserve Bank of India (RBI)
D. The Securities and Exchange Board of India (SEBI)
Explanation: Section 133 of the Companies Act, 2013 states that the Central Government (Ministry of Corporate Affairs) prescribes the Accounting Standards based on recommendations made by NFRA in consultation with ICAI.
Easy NORMAL · Level I Entity | Non-Company Criteria | Turnover Threshold
What is the turnover threshold above which a non-company entity is categorized as a Level I entity as per ICAI guidelines?
A. Exceeding ₹50 crore
B. Exceeding ₹100 crore
C. Exceeding ₹250 crore ✔
D. Exceeding ₹500 crore
Explanation: As per the revised criteria issued by ICAI for classification of non-company entities, an entity whose turnover (excluding other income) exceeds ₹250 crore in the immediately preceding accounting year is categorized as Level I.
Easy NORMAL · SMC Criteria | Borrowing Threshold | Companies Rules 2021
What is the maximum borrowing threshold (including public deposits) allowed for a company to qualify as a Small and Medium Company (SMC) under Companies (AS) Rules, 2021?
A. Does not exceed ₹10 crore at any time during the preceding accounting year
B. Does not exceed ₹25 crore at any time during the preceding accounting year
C. Does not exceed ₹50 crore at any time during the preceding accounting year ✔
D. Does not exceed ₹100 crore at any time during the preceding accounting year
Explanation: Under the Companies (Accounting Standards) Rules, 2021, an SMC's borrowings (including public deposits) must not exceed ₹50 crore at any time during the immediately preceding accounting year.
Easy NORMAL · IFRS | IASB | Global Standards
Which of the following bodies is responsible for issuing International Financial Reporting Standards (IFRS)?
A. International Accounting Standards Committee (IASC)
B. International Accounting Standards Board (IASB) ✔
C. Financial Accounting Standards Board (FASB)
D. International Sustainability Standards Board (ISSB)
Explanation: The International Accounting Standards Board (IASB), an independent standard-setting body of the IFRS Foundation, formulates and issues IFRS.
Easy NORMAL · Non-Company Entities | Classification Levels
How many levels of classification are specified by ICAI for non-company entities for the applicability of Accounting Standards?
A. Two levels (SMC and Non-SMC)
B. Three levels (Level I, Level II, Level III)
C. Four levels (Level I, Level II, Level III, Level IV) ✔
D. Five levels (Level I to Level V)
Explanation: ICAI revised the classification scheme for non-company entities into four distinct levels: Level I (Large), Level II (Medium), Level III (Small), and Level IV (Micro).
Easy NORMAL · Ind AS Framework | IFRS Convergence
Which of the following statements correctly describes Indian Accounting Standards (Ind AS)?
A. Ind AS are identical copy-paste versions of US GAAP
B. Ind AS are Accounting Standards issued directly by ICAI without MCA notification
C. Ind AS are converged versions of IFRS tailored to the Indian economic and legal environment ✔
D. Ind AS apply only to sole proprietorships and partnership firms
Explanation: Ind AS are Accounting Standards converged with IFRS (incorporating Indian carve-outs/carve-ins) notified by the MCA under the Companies (Ind AS) Rules, 2015.
Easy NORMAL · Level IV Criteria | Micro Entities
What is the maximum turnover ceiling for a non-company entity to be classified as Level IV (Micro Enterprise)?
A. Up to ₹2 crore
B. Up to ₹5 crore
C. Up to ₹10 crore ✔
D. Up to ₹25 crore
Explanation: Level IV non-company entities are those with turnover (excluding other income) not exceeding ₹10 crore in the immediately preceding accounting year and borrowings not exceeding ₹2 crore.
Easy NORMAL · SMC Rules | Listed Entities | Non-SMC
A company whose equity or debt securities are listed on any recognized stock exchange in India is automatically classified as:
A. A Small and Medium Company (SMC)
B. A Non-SMC ✔
C. A Level IV Entity
D. Exempt from Accounting Standards
Explanation: Listed companies or companies in the process of listing cannot qualify as SMCs under the Companies (Accounting Standards) Rules, 2021; they are categorized as Non-SMCs.
Easy NORMAL · AS 3 Overview | Cash Flow Statements
Which accounting standard issued by ICAI deals with 'Cash Flow Statements'?
A. AS 1
B. AS 3 ✔
C. AS 7
D. AS 10
Explanation: AS 3 deals with Cash Flow Statements. Level II, III, and IV non-company entities as well as SMCs are granted certain relaxations/exemptions under this standard depending on statutory provisions.
Medium NORMAL · SMC Conditions | Borrowing Rule Timing
When testing the borrowing condition for SMC status of a company for FY 2024-25, during what timeframe must the borrowing limit of ₹50 crore NOT be exceeded?
A. At the end of the current financial year (31st March 2025)
B. At any time during the immediately preceding financial year (FY 2023-24) ✔
C. At the end of the immediately preceding financial year (31st March 2024) only
D. On average basis during the preceding three financial years
Explanation: The condition specifies that the borrowings (including public deposits) must not exceed ₹50 crore at any time during the immediately preceding accounting year.
Medium NORMAL · Transitional Rules | SMC Reclassification | Two-Year Rule
If an existing Non-SMC entity subsequently satisfies all criteria to become an SMC, for how many consecutive years must it satisfy those criteria before it can avail SMC exemptions?
A. Immediately from the current year
B. One reporting year
C. Two consecutive reporting years ✔
D. Three consecutive reporting years
Explanation: An entity that was previously classified as a Non-SMC but subsequently meets SMC criteria must continue to meet those criteria for two consecutive years before it can claim SMC relaxations/exemptions.
Medium NORMAL · Non-Company Classification | Level II Criteria
Firm Alpha (a partnership firm) has turnover of ₹45 crore and borrowings of ₹12 crore during the preceding accounting year. Under which level of non-company classification does Firm Alpha fall?
A. Level I
B. Level II ✔
C. Level III
D. Level IV
Explanation: Level II criteria for non-company entities: Turnover between ₹50 crore and ₹250 crore OR borrowings between ₹10 crore and ₹50 crore. Since borrowings (₹12 crore) exceed ₹10 crore but do not exceed ₹50 crore, Firm Alpha is Level II.
Medium NORMAL · AS 17 Exemptions | Level II Exemptions
Are non-company entities categorized under Level II exempt from AS 17 (Segment Reporting)?
A. No, AS 17 is fully mandatory for Level II entities
B. Yes, Level II entities are fully exempt from complying with AS 17 ✔
C. Exempt only if turnover is less than ₹20 crore
D. Exempt only if permitted by the Comptroller and Auditor General (CAG)
Explanation: AS 17 (Segment Reporting) is mandatory ONLY for Level I non-company entities. Level II, Level III, and Level IV entities are fully exempt from AS 17.
Medium NORMAL · Ind AS Roadmap | Net Worth Threshold | Phase II
An unlisted company has a Net Worth of ₹260 crore as of 31st March 2024. Which accounting framework is mandatorily applicable to this company for FY 2024-25?
A. Accounting Standards (AS) under Companies (AS) Rules, 2021
B. Indian Accounting Standards (Ind AS) under Companies (Ind AS) Rules, 2015 ✔
C. IFRS directly as issued by IASB
D. US GAAP
Explanation: Under Phase II of the Ind AS roadmap, all unlisted companies having a Net Worth of ₹250 crore or more on 31st March of any financial year are mandatorily required to adopt Ind AS from the immediate next financial year.
Medium NORMAL · AS 18 Applicability | Non-Company Exemptions
Which of the following statements regarding the applicability of AS 18 (Related Party Disclosures) to Non-Company Entities is CORRECT?
A. Exempt for Level II, Level III, and Level IV entities
B. Mandatory for Level I, Level II, and Level III entities, but exempt for Level IV entities ✔
C. Exempt for Level III and Level IV entities only
D. Mandatory for Level I entities only
Explanation: AS 18 (Related Party Disclosures) is fully applicable to Level I, Level II, and Level III non-company entities. Only Level IV (Micro) non-company entities are granted full exemption from AS 18.
Medium NORMAL · NFRA | NACAS | Companies Act Regulatory Setup
Which body replaced the National Advisory Committee on Accounting Standards (NACAS) under the Companies Act, 2013?
A. Accounting Standards Board (ASSB)
B. National Financial Reporting Authority (NFRA) ✔
C. Financial Reporting Review Board (FRRB)
D. Quality Review Board (QRB)
Explanation: The National Financial Reporting Authority (NFRA) constituted under Section 132 of the Companies Act, 2013 replaced NACAS to advise the Central Government on accounting standards and oversee audit quality.
Medium NORMAL · Ind AS Holding-Subsidiary Rule | Consolidated & Standalone
If a company adopting Ind AS has a non-listed subsidiary company with a Net Worth of ₹10 crore, what accounting framework must the subsidiary adopt for its standalone financial statements?
A. Companies (AS) Rules, 2021 as its net worth is below ₹250 crore
B. Ind AS mandatorily, because its holding company is covered under Ind AS ✔
C. Option to choose between AS and Ind AS
D. Level IV Non-company framework
Explanation: Once Ind AS becomes applicable to a parent company, it mandatorily applies to all its holding, subsidiary, joint venture, and associate companies, irrespective of their individual net worth.
Medium NORMAL · ISSB | ESG Reporting | IFRS Foundation
Which standard setting authority was created in 2021 under the IFRS Foundation to establish comprehensive global baseline standards for ESG / sustainability disclosures?
A. Global Reporting Initiative (GRI)
B. Sustainability Accounting Standards Board (SASB)
C. International Sustainability Standards Board (ISSB) ✔
D. Climate Disclosure Standards Board (CDSB)
Explanation: The IFRS Foundation announced the creation of the International Sustainability Standards Board (ISSB) at COP26 in November 2021 to issue IFRS Sustainability Disclosure Standards.
Medium NORMAL · SMC Strictness | Borrowing Exceedance
Under Companies (AS) Rules, 2021, if an SMC incurs a total borrowing of ₹55 crore for 3 days during FY 2023-24, how does it affect its classification for FY 2024-25?
A. It remains an SMC as the average borrowing for the year was under ₹50 crore
B. It becomes a Non-SMC because borrowing exceeded ₹50 crore at any time during the preceding year ✔
C. It remains an SMC if the excess borrowing was repaid within 7 days
D. It becomes a Level IV entity
Explanation: The criterion explicitly specifies that borrowings must not exceed ₹50 crore *at any time* during the immediately preceding accounting year. Exceeding ₹50 crore even for a single day invalidates SMC status.
Medium NORMAL · AS 24 Exemptions | Level III Non-Company
Which of the following accounting standards is FULLY EXEMPT for Level III non-company entities?
A. AS 2 (Valuation of Inventories)
B. AS 10 (Property, Plant and Equipment)
C. AS 24 (Discontinuing Operations) ✔
D. AS 13 (Accounting for Investments)
Explanation: AS 24 (Discontinuing Operations) is exempt for Level III and Level IV non-company entities. AS 2, AS 10, and AS 13 are mandatory across all levels.
Medium NORMAL · Irrevocability of Ind AS | Ind AS Rules
What happens once an entity adopts Ind AS either voluntarily or mandatorily?
A. It can revert back to Indian AS after 3 years
B. It can revert back to Indian AS if its net worth falls below ₹250 crore
C. It cannot revert back to Indian AS (Ind AS adoption is irrevocable) ✔
D. It can switch back if approved by its shareholders in AGM
Explanation: Under the Companies (Ind AS) Rules, 2015, once a company starts applying Ind AS (whether voluntarily or mandatorily), it must continue to comply with Ind AS for all subsequent financial statements (irrevocable rule).
Hard NORMAL · Level I Criteria | Non-Company Threshold Override
Entity B (a non-company entity) has Turnover of ₹80 crore and Borrowings of ₹55 crore during the preceding accounting year. Which level of non-company classification applies to Entity B?
A. Level II, because turnover is less than ₹250 crore
B. Level I, because borrowings exceed ₹50 crore ✔
C. Level III, because turnover is between ₹50 and ₹250 crore
D. Level IV, as it is a non-company entity
Explanation: An entity is categorized as Level I if ANY of the Level I thresholds are crossed. Since borrowings (₹55 crore) exceed ₹50 crore, Entity B becomes a Level I entity regardless of its turnover.
Hard NORMAL · Two-Year Rule | Non-SMC to SMC Transition
If a Non-SMC company incurs a reduction in borrowings and turnover and now qualifies as an SMC, when can it start benefiting from SMC exemptions under Companies (AS) Rules, 2021?
A. In the current year itself if board approval is obtained
B. Only after meeting the SMC criteria for two consecutive accounting years ✔
C. Only after getting permission from MCA and NFRA
D. From the immediate next accounting period following the reduction
Explanation: An entity classified as Non-SMC that subsequently meets SMC criteria must satisfy those criteria for two consecutive financial years before it can claim SMC relaxations.
Hard NORMAL · Holding Subsidiary Rule | Level I Extension
A sole proprietorship trading concern has Turnover of ₹8 crore and bank borrowings of ₹1.5 crore. It holds a 75% stake in a partnership firm that is classified as a Level I non-company entity. What is the level of the sole proprietorship?
A. Level IV, based on its own turnover and borrowings
B. Level I, because it is a holding entity of a Level I entity ✔
C. Level III, because holding entities are downgraded by two levels
D. Level II, based on consolidated figures
Explanation: As per ICAI guidelines, holding entities and subsidiary entities of Level I entities are automatically classified as Level I entities, regardless of their individual standalone turnover or borrowings.
Hard NORMAL · AS 28 Relaxations | Level IV Entities | Value in Use
Regarding AS 28 (Impairment of Assets), how are Level IV non-company entities treated compared to Level I entities?
A. Level IV entities are completely exempt from AS 28
B. AS 28 applies to Level IV entities, but with relaxations in determining value in use (e.g., using reasonable estimates without detailed cash flow projections) ✔
C. AS 28 applies without any relaxations or exemptions to Level IV entities
D. AS 28 applies to Level IV entities only if they have international borrowings
Explanation: AS 28 applies to Level IV entities, but ICAI grants relaxations regarding the calculation of 'value in use'. Level IV entities can estimate value in use using reasonable surrogates/estimates rather than complex discounted cash flow modeling.
Hard NORMAL · NBFC Roadmap | Ind AS Applicability | Phase II NBFC
Company K is an unlisted Non-Banking Financial Company (NBFC) with Net Worth of ₹300 crore as on 31st March 2024. Which accounting framework applies to Company K for FY 2024-25?
A. Companies (AS) Rules, 2021
B. Ind AS under Phase II of the NBFC Roadmap ✔
C. RBI Core Accounting Rules exclusively
D. IFRS direct compliance
Explanation: Under the NBFC Ind AS Roadmap, Phase II made Ind AS mandatory for all unlisted NBFCs having a Net Worth of ₹250 crore or more from 1st April 2019 onwards. Thus, Company K (Net Worth ₹300 cr) must follow Ind AS.
Hard NORMAL · Net Worth Definition | Section 2(57) | Ind AS Threshold
How is 'Net Worth' calculated for determining Ind AS applicability for unlisted companies as per MCA guidelines?
A. Paid-up Equity Share Capital + Reserves out of profits - Accumulated Losses - Deferred Revenue Expenditure - Revaluation Reserves ✔
B. Paid-up Capital + All Reserves + Revaluation Reserves
C. Total Assets minus Total External Liabilities including Preference Shares
D. Paid-up Equity Share Capital + Preference Share Capital + General Reserves + Revaluation Reserves
Explanation: Net worth is calculated as per Section 2(57) of Companies Act 2013: aggregate value of paid-up share capital + reserves created out of profits + securities premium - accumulated losses - deferred expenditure - revaluation reserve.
Hard NORMAL · Downgrading Rules | Two-Year Consecutive Rule
If a non-company entity moves from Level I to Level IV status due to business downsizing, when can it start availing the full exemptions available to Level IV entities?
A. Immediately in the year of downsizing
B. After remaining in Level IV for two consecutive reporting periods ✔
C. After remaining in Level IV for three consecutive reporting periods
D. Only when certified by the ICAI ASSB
Explanation: An entity that drops from a higher level (Level I) to a lower level (Level IV) cannot claim exemptions/relaxations of the lower level until it continues to qualify for the lower level for two consecutive reporting periods.
Hard NORMAL · Statutory Conflict | Hierarchy of Rules | Companies Act Supremacy
Where there is a conflict between the provisions of the Companies Act, 2013 and an Accounting Standard notified under Section 133, which of the two shall prevail?
A. The Accounting Standard notified under Section 133
B. The provisions of the Companies Act, 2013 ✔
C. The guidance note issued by ASSB
D. The matter must be referred to the High Court
Explanation: Accounting Standards are subservient to statutory legislation. If there is a conflict between the Companies Act, 2013 and an Accounting Standard, statutory law (the Companies Act) prevails.
CASE SCENARIO: Vibrant Threads Ltd is an unlisted public manufacturing company incorporated under the Companies Act, 2013. The company is evaluating its accounting framework compliance for FY 2024-25 under the Companies (Accounting Standards) Rules, 2021. The relevant financial parameters of Vibrant Threads Ltd for the preceding three financial years are as follows: - FY 2021-22: Turnover = ₹210 crore; Peak Borrowings = ₹35 crore. - FY 2022-23: Turnover = ₹240 crore; Peak Borrowings = ₹48 crore. - FY 2023-24: Turnover = ₹245 crore; Peak Borrowings = ₹54 crore (for 10 days in Nov 2023 due to temporary working capital loan). Additionally, Vibrant Threads Ltd holds an 80% equity stake in 'WeaveCraft Pvt Ltd', an unlisted small private company with Turnover of ₹12 crore and Peak Borrowings of ₹3 crore during FY 2023-24. Neither company has listed securities or is in the process of listing.
Medium SCENARIO · SMC Classification | Borrowing Limit | Companies Rules 2021
What is the classification of Vibrant Threads Ltd for FY 2024-25 under the Companies (AS) Rules, 2021?
A. Small and Medium Company (SMC)
B. Non-SMC ✔
C. Level IV Non-company Entity
D. Ind AS mandatory company
Explanation: For FY 2024-25, compliance is based on preceding year FY 2023-24 figures. Peak borrowings reached ₹54 crore in FY 2023-24, exceeding the ₹50 crore limit. Hence, Vibrant Threads Ltd is a Non-SMC.
Hard SCENARIO · SMC Definition | Holding Subsidiary Impact
How does the classification of Vibrant Threads Ltd as a Non-SMC for FY 2024-25 affect its subsidiary 'WeaveCraft Pvt Ltd'?
A. WeaveCraft Pvt Ltd remains an SMC because its own borrowings are only ₹3 crore
B. WeaveCraft Pvt Ltd becomes a Non-SMC because it is a subsidiary of a Non-SMC ✔
C. WeaveCraft Pvt Ltd is reclassified as a Level IV non-company entity
D. WeaveCraft Pvt Ltd is exempt from all Accounting Standards
Explanation: Under the definition of SMC in Companies (AS) Rules, 2021, a company that is a subsidiary or holding company of a Non-SMC cannot be treated as an SMC. Thus, WeaveCraft Pvt Ltd becomes a Non-SMC.
Hard SCENARIO · Two Year Rule | Transitional Exemptions
If Vibrant Threads Ltd repays its loans so that peak borrowing in FY 2024-25 drops to ₹30 crore, in which financial year can it first claim SMC relaxations/exemptions?
A. FY 2025-26
B. FY 2026-27
C. FY 2027-28 ✔
D. Immediately in FY 2024-25
Explanation: A Non-SMC that subsequently meets SMC criteria must meet those criteria for two consecutive reporting periods (FY 2024-25 and FY 2025-26) before it can claim SMC exemptions. Thus, it can claim exemptions in FY 2027-28 (based on two consecutive years of compliance).
Medium SCENARIO · AS 3 Applicability | Cash Flow Statement Exemptions
Is Vibrant Threads Ltd required to present a Cash Flow Statement as per AS 3 for FY 2024-25?
A. No, because it is an unlisted company
B. Yes, because it is classified as a Non-SMC and does not qualify for small company exemption under Section 2(40) ✔
C. No, because its turnover is less than ₹250 crore
D. Optional at the discretion of the Board of Directors
Explanation: Cash Flow Statement (AS 3) is mandatory for Non-SMCs. Exemptions under Section 2(40) apply only to One Person Companies, Small Companies, Dormant Companies, and Startups; Vibrant Threads Ltd does not qualify.
CASE SCENARIO: Apex Consultancy Services is a partnership firm providing IT advisory services in India. The firm's partners are analyzing the applicability of Accounting Standards issued by ICAI for FY 2024-25. Financial parameters of Apex Consultancy Services for FY 2023-24: - Turnover (excluding other income): ₹42 crore - Bank Borrowings (Peak balance): ₹8 crore - Fixed Deposits accepted from partners/public: ₹3 crore During FY 2023-24, Apex Consultancy Services acquired a 65% equity stake in 'Global Tech Solutions LLP', a non-company entity with Turnover of ₹280 crore in FY 2023-24.
Medium SCENARIO · Level I Non-Company | Turnover Threshold
What is the non-company classification level of 'Global Tech Solutions LLP' for FY 2024-25?
A. Level I ✔
B. Level II
C. Level III
D. Level IV
Explanation: Global Tech Solutions LLP has a turnover of ₹280 crore in FY 2023-24, which exceeds the ₹250 crore threshold. Therefore, it is a Level I non-company entity.
Hard SCENARIO · Holding Subsidiary Rule | Level I Classification
What is the non-company classification level of 'Apex Consultancy Services' for FY 2024-25?
A. Level III, based on its standalone turnover and borrowings
B. Level II, based on its total borrowings of ₹11 crore
C. Level I, because it is the holding entity of a Level I entity ✔
D. Level IV, because it is a partnership firm
Explanation: Even though Apex's standalone turnover (₹42 cr) and total borrowings (₹11 cr) place it in Level II, holding entities of Level I entities are automatically classified as Level I entities.
Medium SCENARIO · AS 17 | Segment Reporting Exemptions
Can Apex Consultancy Services claim exemption from complying with AS 17 (Segment Reporting) for FY 2024-25?
A. Yes, because its turnover is below ₹50 crore
B. No, because AS 17 is fully mandatory for all Level I entities ✔
C. Yes, because it is a partnership firm
D. Yes, if all partners consent unanimously
Explanation: AS 17 is mandatory for Level I entities. Since Apex Consultancy Services is classified as Level I (due to holding a Level I subsidiary), it cannot claim exemption from AS 17.
Hard SCENARIO · Downgrading Level | Two Year Rule
If Apex Consultancy Services sells its entire stake in Global Tech Solutions LLP during FY 2024-25, when can it start claiming Level III exemptions on a standalone basis (assuming its figures remain Turnover ₹42 cr, Borrowings ₹8 cr)?
A. Immediately in FY 2024-25
B. From FY 2025-26
C. Only after remaining in Level III criteria for two consecutive reporting periods ✔
D. It can never claim Level III exemptions
Explanation: When an entity drops from Level I to a lower level (Level III), it must continue to meet the criteria of the lower level for two consecutive reporting periods before availing of exemptions.
CASE SCENARIO: Nova Retail Services Pvt Ltd is an unlisted private company incorporated in 2015 operating a chain of supermarkets. The company has seen rapid expansion. Its financial position across recent years is summarised below: - 31st March 2022: Net Worth = ₹190 crore; Turnover = ₹450 crore - 31st March 2023: Net Worth = ₹240 crore; Turnover = ₹520 crore - 31st March 2024: Net Worth = ₹270 crore; Turnover = ₹610 crore Nova Retail Services Pvt Ltd has two non-listed subsidiaries: 'Tiny Express Pvt Ltd' (Net Worth ₹12 crore) and 'Fast Logistics Pvt Ltd' (Net Worth ₹8 crore). Neither parent nor subsidiaries are banks, FIs, or NBFCs.
Medium SCENARIO · Ind AS Roadmap | Net Worth Criteria
From which financial year is Ind AS mandatorily applicable to Nova Retail Services Pvt Ltd?
A. FY 2022-23
B. FY 2023-24
C. FY 2024-25 ✔
D. FY 2025-26
Explanation: Under Phase II of the Ind AS roadmap, unlisted companies with Net Worth >= ₹250 crore on 31st March of any FY must adopt Ind AS from the next FY. Net worth reached ₹270 crore on 31st March 2024; hence Ind AS applies from FY 2024-25.
Medium SCENARIO · Ind AS Extension | Subsidiary Applicability
Is Ind AS applicable to 'Tiny Express Pvt Ltd' for FY 2024-25, despite its Net Worth being only ₹12 crore?
A. No, because its Net Worth is below ₹250 crore
B. Yes, mandatory because its parent company Nova Retail Services Pvt Ltd is adopting Ind AS from FY 2024-25 ✔
C. Optional at the choice of Tiny Express Pvt Ltd's Board
D. No, unless its turnover exceeds ₹100 crore
Explanation: Once Ind AS applies to a holding company, it automatically applies to all its holding, subsidiary, joint venture, and associate companies regardless of their individual net worth.
Hard SCENARIO · Irrevocability | Ind AS Framework
If Nova Retail Services Pvt Ltd's Net Worth falls to ₹220 crore on 31st March 2026, can it switch back from Ind AS to Companies (AS) Rules, 2021 for FY 2026-27?
A. Yes, because net worth fell below ₹250 crore
B. Yes, subject to approval from MCA
C. No, once Ind AS is applied, the company must continue applying Ind AS indefinitely ✔
D. Yes, if shareholders pass a special resolution
Explanation: Ind AS adoption is an irrevocable process. Once a company starts preparing statements under Ind AS, it cannot revert to Accounting Standards (AS) even if its Net Worth drops below the threshold.
Hard SCENARIO · Ind AS 101 | First Time Adoption | Comparatives
When Nova Retail Services Pvt Ltd prepares its first Ind AS financial statements for FY 2024-25, what comparative information must it present?
A. No comparative figures are required for the first year of adoption
B. Comparative figures for the preceding year (FY 2023-24) converted to Ind AS ✔
C. Comparative figures for the last 3 preceding years under Indian AS
D. Comparative figures under IFRS as issued by IASB
Explanation: Under Ind AS 101 (First-time Adoption of Ind AS), an entity must present at least one year of comparative information under Ind AS (i.e., FY 2023-24 comparative figures translated to Ind AS).
CASE SCENARIO: In 2024, the Ministry of Corporate Affairs (MCA) and the National Financial Reporting Authority (NFRA) examined the standard-setting mechanism in India. A private corporate group, 'GigaTech Enterprises Group', operates multiple legal entities: 1. GigaTech Solutions Ltd (Unlisted Public Co., Turnover ₹300 crore, Net Worth ₹260 crore) 2. GigaTech Softwares Pvt Ltd (Unlisted Co., Turnover ₹40 crore, Net Worth ₹15 crore) 3. GigaTech Hardware LLP (LLP, Turnover ₹8 crore, Borrowings ₹1.2 crore) The chief accountant is analyzing standard setting authorities, Section 133 of Companies Act 2013, NFRA jurisdiction, and standard classification.
Medium SCENARIO · ASSB Role | Standard Formulation Procedure
Which body formulates Accounting Standards and recommends them to NFRA for consideration before notification by MCA?
A. Accounting Standards Board (ASSB) of ICAI ✔
B. Securities and Exchange Board of India (SEBI)
C. Reserve Bank of India (RBI)
D. Ministry of Finance
Explanation: The Accounting Standards Board (ASSB) set up by ICAI formulates Accounting Standards and submits them to NFRA. NFRA then examines them and makes recommendations to the Central Government (MCA).
Medium SCENARIO · LLP Classification | Non-Company AS Rules
Which set of Accounting Standards applies to 'GigaTech Hardware LLP' for FY 2024-25?
A. Companies (Ind AS) Rules, 2015
B. Companies (AS) Rules, 2021
C. Accounting Standards issued by ICAI for Non-Company Entities (Level IV) ✔
D. IFRS direct framework
Explanation: GigaTech Hardware LLP is an LLP (non-company entity). Statutory Companies Rules do not apply to LLPs directly. The ICAI issued scheme for Non-Company Entities applies; with Turnover ₹8 cr and Borrowings ₹1.2 cr, it is Level IV.
Medium SCENARIO · Section 134(5) | Directors Responsibility Statement
Under Section 134(5)(a) of the Companies Act, 2013, what must Directors state in the Directors' Responsibility Statement regarding Accounting Standards?
A. That Accounting Standards are optional for private companies
B. That in preparation of annual accounts, applicable accounting standards have been followed along with proper explanation for material departures ✔
C. That all accounting standards have been relaxed by the statutory auditor
D. That standards set by FASB US have been complied with
Explanation: Section 134(5)(a) mandates that directors state in the Directors' Responsibility Statement that in the preparation of annual accounts, applicable accounting standards were followed with proper explanation for any material departures.
Hard SCENARIO · Carve Outs | Ind AS vs IFRS
What is the relationship between Ind AS and IFRS regarding 'Carve-outs'?
A. Carve-outs are additions made in Ind AS that do not exist in IFRS
B. Carve-outs are deviations/differences in Ind AS from IFRS to suit Indian legal and economic conditions ✔
C. Carve-outs represent complete rejection of IFRS principles
D. Carve-outs apply only to public sector undertakings
Explanation: Carve-outs refer to departures made in Ind AS from the corresponding IFRS standards to address specific Indian economic, legal, or regulatory circumstances.
CASE SCENARIO: Greenfield Farmers LLP is an agricultural partnership enterprise operating in Punjab. It is not listed and has no financial institutions as partners. Financial details for Greenfield Farmers LLP for FY 2023-24: - Turnover (excluding government grants): ₹7.5 crore - Bank Borrowings (Peak balance): ₹1.6 crore - Total Assets: ₹5.0 crore The management of Greenfield Farmers LLP wants to understand its compliance requirements for FY 2024-25 regarding AS 3 (Cash Flow Statements), AS 17 (Segment Reporting), AS 18 (Related Party Disclosures), and AS 24 (Discontinuing Operations).
Medium SCENARIO · Level IV Classification | Micro Non-Company
What is the non-company classification level of Greenfield Farmers LLP for FY 2024-25?
A. Level I
B. Level II
C. Level III
D. Level IV ✔
Explanation: With turnover up to ₹10 crore (₹7.5 cr) and borrowings up to ₹2 crore (₹1.6 cr), Greenfield Farmers LLP falls under Level IV (Micro non-company entities).
Medium SCENARIO · AS 2 Applicability | Level IV Exemptions
Which of the following standards is FULLY APPLICABLE to Greenfield Farmers LLP without exemption?
A. AS 3 (Cash Flow Statements)
B. AS 17 (Segment Reporting)
C. AS 2 (Valuation of Inventories) ✔
D. AS 24 (Discontinuing Operations)
Explanation: AS 2 (Valuation of Inventories) is mandatory for all non-company entities including Level IV. AS 3, AS 17, and AS 24 are exempt for Level IV entities.
Hard SCENARIO · AS 18 Exemption | Level IV Non-Company
Is Greenfield Farmers LLP required to comply with AS 18 (Related Party Disclosures) for FY 2024-25?
A. Yes, AS 18 is mandatory for all entities regardless of level
B. No, Level IV entities are fully exempt from AS 18 ✔
C. Yes, but with partial disclosures only
D. Exempt only if turnover is less than ₹1 crore
Explanation: Under the revised ICAI scheme for non-company entities, AS 18 (Related Party Disclosures) is fully exempt for Level IV entities.
Hard SCENARIO · Level III Threshold | Reclassification
If Greenfield Farmers LLP takes a new business expansion loan in FY 2024-25 taking peak borrowings to ₹4.0 crore (turnover remaining ₹8.0 cr), what will be its level for FY 2025-26?
A. Level I
B. Level II
C. Level III ✔
D. Level IV
Explanation: For Level III, borrowings are between > ₹2 crore and <= ₹10 crore. Peak borrowing of ₹4.0 crore shifts the entity from Level IV to Level III for FY 2025-26.

Paper 1: Advanced Accounting · Module 1 · Chapter 2:

Accounts — 55 rows
Easy NORMAL · Framework Status | Conflict with AS | Hierarchy of Standards
Under the ICAI Framework for the Preparation and Presentation of Financial Statements, what is the status of the Framework in the event of a conflict with a specific Accounting Standard (AS)?
A. The Framework overrides the Accounting Standard.
B. The Accounting Standard overrides the Framework. ✔
C. The entity may choose whichever treatment results in a higher net profit.
D. The matter must be referred to the Ministry of Corporate Affairs for a ruling.
Explanation: The Framework clearly states that it is not an Accounting Standard and does not override any specific Accounting Standard. In case of a conflict between the Framework and an Accounting Standard, the requirements of the specific Accounting Standard override those of the Framework.
Easy NORMAL · Fundamental Accounting Assumptions | AS 1 | Prudence
Which of the following is NOT categorized as a fundamental accounting assumption in the Framework and AS 1?
A. Going Concern
B. Accrual
C. Consistency
D. Prudence ✔
Explanation: Going Concern, Accrual, and Consistency are the three fundamental accounting assumptions specified in AS 1 and the Framework. Prudence is a qualitative consideration used in selecting accounting policies, not a fundamental accounting assumption.
Easy NORMAL · Asset Definition | Elements of Financial Statements | Control
Which three essential conditions must be satisfied for an item to meet the definition of an 'Asset' according to the Framework?
A. Legal ownership, physical existence, and past cash outflow.
B. Control by the enterprise, result of past events, and expected inflow of future economic benefits. ✔
C. Present legal title, reliable market value, and future tax savings.
D. Management intention to hold long-term, historical cost measurement, and physical form.
Explanation: An asset is defined as a resource controlled by the enterprise as a result of past events and from which future economic benefits are expected to flow to the enterprise. Physical form and legal ownership are not absolute prerequisites.
Easy NORMAL · Income Definition | Equity Contributions | Elements of Financial Statements
The Framework defines 'Income' to include both revenues and gains. Which of the following is explicitly excluded from the definition of income?
A. Gains on disposal of non-current assets
B. Unrealized appreciation on investment property
C. Contributions from equity participants ✔
D. Reversal of excess impairment provisions
Explanation: Income is defined as increases in economic benefits during the accounting period in the form of inflows or enhancements of assets or decreases of liabilities that result in increases in equity, other than those relating to contributions from equity participants.
Medium NORMAL · Substance over Form | Qualitative Characteristics | Asset Recognition
An entity acquires equipment under a contract where legal ownership transfers only upon payment of the final installment, but all operational risks and rewards pass to the entity on day one. How should this equipment be recognized?
A. Recognize as an asset and liability immediately, applying the principle of 'substance over form'. ✔
B. Record as operating lease expenses as installments are paid until legal title transfers.
C. Disclose as a contingent asset in the notes to accounts without financial balance recognition.
D. Record the asset at a nominal value of Re. 1 until full legal title is acquired.
Explanation: Under the principle of 'substance over form', transactions are accounted for in accordance with their economic reality rather than merely their legal form. Since the risk and rewards are transferred, the asset and liability are recognized immediately.
Easy NORMAL · Prudence | Qualitative Characteristics | Reliability
How does the Framework define the qualitative characteristic of 'Prudence'?
A. The deliberate understatement of assets and overstatement of liabilities to create hidden reserves.
B. The inclusion of a degree of caution in exercising judgments needed in making estimates under uncertainty. ✔
C. The policy of recognizing revenues only when cash is fully realized in bank accounts.
D. The immediate write-off of all capital expenditures incurred during the financial year.
Explanation: Prudence is the inclusion of a degree of caution in the exercise of judgments needed in making estimates required under conditions of uncertainty, such that assets or income are not overstated and liabilities or expenses are not understated. It does not permit the creation of hidden or secret reserves.
Easy NORMAL · Measurement Basis | Historical Cost | Valuation Principles
Assets are recorded at the amount of cash or cash equivalents paid or the fair value of consideration given at the time of acquisition. Which measurement basis is described?
A. Current Cost
B. Realisable Value
C. Historical Cost ✔
D. Present Value
Explanation: Historical cost is the measurement basis where assets are recorded at the amount of cash or cash equivalents paid or the fair value of the consideration given to acquire them at the time of their acquisition.
Medium NORMAL · Current Cost | Measurement Basis | Asset Valuation
Under which measurement basis are assets carried at the amount of cash or cash equivalents that would have to be paid if the same or an equivalent asset was acquired currently?
A. Historical Cost
B. Current Cost ✔
C. Settlement Value
D. Present Value
Explanation: Current cost measures assets at the amount of cash or cash equivalents that would have to be paid if the same or an equivalent asset were acquired currently.
Medium NORMAL · Settlement Value | Realisable Value | Measurement Basis
In financial statement preparation, liabilities carried at the undiscounted amount of cash expected to be paid to satisfy obligations in the normal course of business are measured at:
A. Realisable / Settlement Value ✔
B. Present Value
C. Historical Cost
D. Fair Value through Profit and Loss
Explanation: Under the realisable (settlement) value basis, liabilities are carried at their settlement values, which are the undiscounted amounts of cash or cash equivalents expected to be paid to satisfy the liabilities in the normal course of business.
Medium NORMAL · Financial Capital Maintenance | Nominal Monetary Units | Capital Maintenance
Under the concept of Financial Capital Maintenance at nominal monetary units, profit is earned only if:
A. Physical productive capacity at the end of the period exceeds that at the beginning.
B. The financial amount of net assets at the end of the period exceeds that at the beginning, after excluding distributions to and contributions from owners. ✔
C. Net assets at the end of the period, adjusted for inflation, exceed net assets at the beginning.
D. Cash balances at the end of the period exceed cash balances at the beginning.
Explanation: Financial capital maintenance in nominal monetary units measures profit as the increase in nominal financial capital (net assets) over the period, excluding any transactions with owners (contributions and distributions).
Hard NORMAL · Physical Capital Maintenance | Operating Capability | Equity Adjustments
Which capital maintenance concept requires all price changes affecting assets and liabilities to be treated as capital maintenance adjustments in equity rather than profit?
A. Financial capital maintenance in nominal units
B. Financial capital maintenance in constant purchasing power
C. Physical capital maintenance ✔
D. Realized operating cash flow maintenance
Explanation: Under physical capital maintenance (operating capability), all price changes affecting the assets and liabilities of the enterprise are viewed as capital maintenance adjustments that form part of equity, rather than being included in profit or loss.
Easy NORMAL · Neutrality | Reliability | Qualitative Characteristics
Financial information must be free from deliberate bias so that it produces neutral outcomes without influencing decisions toward a predetermined result. Which qualitative characteristic does this describe?
A. Neutrality ✔
B. Comparability
C. Understandability
D. Timeliness
Explanation: To be reliable, the information contained in financial statements must be neutral, meaning free from bias. Financial statements are not neutral if, by the selection or presentation of information, they influence the making of a decision or judgment in order to achieve a predetermined result or outcome.
Easy NORMAL · Recognition Criteria | Probability | Reliable Measurement
An item meeting the definition of an element should be recognized in financial statements if and only if:
A. It is legally enforceable and approved by the board of directors.
B. It is probable that any future economic benefit will flow to/from the enterprise AND its cost or value can be measured reliably. ✔
C. A completed cash flow transaction has taken place during the current financial year.
D. It does not result in an increased tax liability for the reporting period.
Explanation: The Framework mandates two cumulative criteria for recognition of an element: (1) it is probable that any future economic benefit associated with the item will flow to or from the enterprise, and (2) the item has a cost or value that can be measured with reliability.
Medium NORMAL · Timeliness vs Reliability | Constraints | Qualitative Characteristics
An entity delays issuing its annual report by eight months to obtain absolute confirmation of a pending insurance claim. Which constraint trade-off is highlighted?
A. Timeliness versus Reliability ✔
B. Relevance versus Materiality
C. Substance over Form versus Prudence
D. Understandability versus Comparability
Explanation: This situation illustrates the constraint between timeliness and reliability. Delaying reporting improves the reliability of the information regarding the claim but impairs timeliness, rendering the financial statements less relevant for decision-making.
Easy NORMAL · Materiality | Relevance | Qualitative Characteristics
According to the Framework, information is considered material if its omission or misstatement could:
A. Lead to regulatory penalties from government authorities.
B. Influence the economic decisions of users taken on the basis of financial statements. ✔
C. Exceed 5% of gross revenues in all circumstances.
D. Directly alter the credit rating assigned to the entity.
Explanation: Information is material if its omission or misstatement could influence the economic decisions of users taken on the basis of the financial statements. Materiality depends on the size and nature of the item judged in the specific circumstances.
Medium NORMAL · Going Concern | Fundamental Accounting Assumptions | Liquidation Basis
When the going concern assumption of an entity is no longer valid, how should its financial statements be prepared?
A. On a standard historical cost basis with explanatory note disclosure.
B. On a liquidation/net realisable value basis, adjusting asset carrying amounts and providing for liabilities. ✔
C. On a cash basis of accounting excluding all non-cash items.
D. Financial statements must be withheld completely.
Explanation: If the going concern assumption is invalid, financial statements can no longer be prepared on a normal going-concern historical cost basis. They must be prepared on a net realisable / liquidation basis, remeasuring assets at realisable values and recognizing obligations arising from liquidation.
Medium NORMAL · Matching Principle | Expense Recognition | Systematic Allocation
When economic benefits are expected to arise over several accounting periods and the connection with income can only be broadly or indirectly determined, expenses are recognized on the basis of:
A. Immediate full write-off in the year of expenditure.
B. Systematic and rational allocation procedures. ✔
C. Cash outflows as and when disbursements occur.
D. Historical cost adjusted for general purchasing power.
Explanation: When economic benefits are expected to arise over several accounting periods and the association with income can only be broadly or indirectly determined, expenses are recognized in the income statement on the basis of systematic and rational allocation procedures (e.g., depreciation).
Easy NORMAL · Equity Definition | Elements of Financial Statements | Residual Interest
How does the Framework define 'Equity'?
A. Total non-current assets minus total non-current liabilities.
B. Residual interest in the assets of the enterprise after deducting all its liabilities. ✔
C. Paid-up share capital plus statutory reserves.
D. Net current assets available for operational expansion.
Explanation: Equity is defined in the Framework as the residual interest in the assets of the enterprise after deducting all its liabilities.
Easy NORMAL · Users of Financial Statements | Investors | Information Needs
Which user group of financial statements is primarily concerned with the risk inherent in, and return provided by, their investments?
A. Lenders
B. Suppliers and trade creditors
C. Investors ✔
D. Government and regulatory agencies
Explanation: Investors are the providers of risk capital and are concerned with the risk inherent in, and return provided by, their investments. They need information to help them decide whether to buy, hold, or sell shares.
Easy NORMAL · Present Value | Measurement Basis | Discounted Cash Flow
An asset is reported at the present discounted value of future net cash inflows expected to be generated in the normal course of business. Which measurement basis is used?
A. Historical Cost
B. Current Cost
C. Present Value ✔
D. Realisable Value
Explanation: Present value is a financial measurement basis under which assets are carried at the discounted present value of the future net cash inflows that the item is expected to generate in the normal course of business.
Hard NORMAL · Constant Purchasing Power | Financial Capital Maintenance | Profit Determination
Entity Delta started business with capital of ₹2,00,000 on 1st April 2024. During FY 2024-25, the general price index increased by 15%. At year-end (31st March 2025), closing net assets were ₹2,50,000. Under Financial Capital Maintenance in Constant Purchasing Power units, what is Delta's profit?
A. ₹50,000
B. ₹20,000 ✔
C. ₹30,000
D. Nil
Explanation: Capital required to maintain constant purchasing power = ₹2,00,000 * 1.15 = ₹2,30,000. Profit = Closing Net Assets (₹2,50,000) - Adjusted Capital (₹2,30,000) = ₹20,00,000.
Medium NORMAL · Completeness | Reliability | Materiality and Cost
To be reliable, financial statement information must be complete within the bounds of:
A. Legal permissibility and taxation provisions.
B. Materiality and cost. ✔
C. Statutory audit deadlines.
D. Management's discretionary judgment.
Explanation: To be reliable, the information in financial statements must be complete within the bounds of materiality and cost. An omission can cause information to be false or misleading and thus unreliable.
Hard NORMAL · Liability Recognition | Onerous Contracts | Expense Recognition
Entity Omega enters into a construction contract expected to generate losses of ₹8,00,000 due to severe structural modifications required mid-project. How should this loss be recognized under the Framework?
A. Deferred and written off upon final contract handover.
B. Recognized immediately as a provision/expense, as a present obligation with a probable economic outflow exists. ✔
C. Disclosed solely as a note to the financial statements.
D. Capitalized as part of contract work-in-progress assets.
Explanation: Under the Framework's liability and expense recognition principles, an onerous obligation where future costs exceed economic benefits represents a present liability and an immediate expense that must be recognized when probable and measurable.
Medium NORMAL · Consistency | Fundamental Accounting Assumptions | Accounting Policy Changes
The consistency assumption requires that accounting policies are:
A. Never altered under any circumstances.
B. Applied consistently from one period to another, unless a change is required by law/AS or yields better presentation. ✔
C. Identical to those followed by competitors in the same industry.
D. Updated annually to match changing tax regulations.
Explanation: Consistency assumes that accounting policies are followed consistently from one period to another. Changes are permitted only if required by statute, for compliance with an accounting standard, or if it results in a more appropriate presentation.
Medium NORMAL · True and Fair View | Financial Statement Objective | Application of Standards
According to the Framework, financial statements present a 'true and fair view' when:
A. An unqualified audit report is issued by a Chartered Accountant.
B. Qualitative characteristics and applicable Accounting Standards are appropriately applied. ✔
C. Zero tax disputes are pending with revenue authorities.
D. Positive net profits are recorded consistently every year.
Explanation: Financial statements are described as showing a true and fair view, or presenting fairly, if the principal qualitative characteristics are present and appropriate accounting standards are applied.
Hard NORMAL · Physical Capital Maintenance | Holding Gains | Equity Adjustments
Under the Physical Capital Maintenance concept, price increases in held assets are accounted for as:
A. Realized operational gains in the Income Statement.
B. Extraordinary items in Profit and Loss.
C. Capital maintenance adjustments included directly in Equity. ✔
D. Deferred revenue credits in liabilities.
Explanation: Under physical capital maintenance, price increases on assets retained by the enterprise are treated as capital maintenance adjustments forming part of equity, rather than operational profit.
Easy NORMAL · Users of Financial Statements | Government and Agencies | Information Needs
Which user group requires financial statement information to regulate enterprise activities, determine taxation policies, and compile national income statistics?
A. Public at large
B. Government and its agencies ✔
C. Lenders and financial institutions
D. Employees and trade unions
Explanation: Government and its agencies are interested in the allocation of resources and the activities of enterprises. They require information to regulate activities, establish taxation policies, and serve as the basis for national income and similar statistics.
Hard NORMAL · Reliability vs Relevance | Recognition Criteria | Note Disclosure
When an item has strong relevance to decision-making but cannot be measured with acceptable reliability, the Framework dictates that the item should be:
A. Recognized in the balance sheet at a token value of Re. 1.
B. Excluded from financial balance recognition, but disclosed in explanatory notes if material. ✔
C. Included in the Income Statement as an extraordinary expense.
D. Recognized using the highest possible subjective estimate.
Explanation: If an item meets the relevance test but fails the reliable measurement criterion, it cannot be recognized in the body of financial statements. However, disclosure in notes is appropriate when the item is relevant to user evaluation.
Medium NORMAL · Inventory Valuation | Realisable Value | Asset Recognition
A trading firm holds inventory acquired for ₹1,00,000. Due to market decline, expected net realisable value drops to ₹70,000. At what amount should inventory be reported under the Framework?
A. ₹1,00,000
B. ₹70,000 ✔
C. ₹85,000
D. ₹0
Explanation: Assets should not be carried at amounts exceeding expected economic benefits. Inventory measurement follows lower of cost and net realisable value, so it must be reported at ₹70,000, recognizing a ₹30,000 write-down.
Medium NORMAL · Expense Definition | Losses | Elements of Financial Statements
Entity Gamma sells machinery carrying a book value of ₹5,00,000 for ₹3,80,000. The resulting ₹1,20,000 difference meets the Framework's definition of:
A. A capital deficit contribution by owners.
B. An expense, specifically a loss. ✔
C. A long-term deferred liability.
D. A capital reserve charge.
Explanation: Expenses encompass losses as well as expenses arising in the ordinary course of activity. A loss on disposal of non-current assets represents a decrease in economic benefits (and reduction in equity) not relating to distributions to owners.
CASE SCENARIO: Zenith Enterprises began operations on 1st April 2024 with a financial capital of ₹20,00,000, represented by 2,000 units of Product A at ₹1,000 per unit. During FY 2024-25, Zenith sold all 2,000 units for ₹32,00,000 cash. During the year, the general price index rose from 100 to 125 (a 25% inflation rate). At the end of the year on 31st March 2025, the replacement cost of Product A rose to ₹1,400 per unit. Zenith made no equity contributions or withdrawals during the financial year.
Medium SCENARIO · Nominal Capital Maintenance | Profit Determination | Capital Maintenance
What is the net profit earned by Zenith Enterprises under the Financial Capital Maintenance concept in nominal monetary units?
A. ₹12,00,000 ✔
B. ₹7,00,000
C. ₹4,00,000
D. ₹5,00,000
Explanation: Under nominal monetary units, profit = Closing Net Assets (₹32,00,000) - Opening Capital (₹20,00,000) = ₹12,00,000.
Hard SCENARIO · Constant Purchasing Power | Financial Capital Maintenance | Inflation Accounting
What is the net profit earned by Zenith Enterprises under the Financial Capital Maintenance concept in Constant Purchasing Power units?
A. ₹12,00,000
B. ₹7,00,000 ✔
C. ₹4,00,000
D. ₹5,00,000
Explanation: Inflation-adjusted opening capital = ₹20,00,000 * (125 / 100) = ₹25,00,000. Profit under constant purchasing power = Closing Net Assets (₹32,00,000) - Adjusted Capital (₹25,00,000) = ₹7,00,000.
Hard SCENARIO · Physical Capital Maintenance | Operating Capability | Profit Determination
What is the net profit earned by Zenith Enterprises under the Physical Capital Maintenance concept?
A. ₹12,00,000
B. ₹7,00,000
C. ₹4,00,000 ✔
D. ₹2,00,000
Explanation: Capital required to maintain physical productive capacity (2,000 units at ₹1,400 replacement cost) = ₹28,00,000. Profit = Closing Cash (₹32,00,000) - Physical Capital needed (₹28,00,000) = ₹4,00,000.
Medium SCENARIO · Physical Capital Maintenance | Equity Adjustments | Holding Gains
Under the Physical Capital Maintenance concept, how is the ₹8,00,000 price increase (from ₹20,00,000 opening cost to ₹28,00,000 replacement cost) recognized?
A. Credited to Profit and Loss as realized operating revenue.
B. Credited directly to Equity as a capital maintenance adjustment. ✔
C. Debited to Profit and Loss as an extraordinary operating expense.
D. Recognized as a long-term deferred liability in the Balance Sheet.
Explanation: Under physical capital maintenance, holding gains resulting from price changes on assets are not treated as profit. Instead, they are recognized directly in equity as capital maintenance adjustments required to preserve productive capacity.
CASE SCENARIO: Nova Technologies Ltd. is finalizing its financial statements for the year ended 31st March 2025. Management faces four distinct accounting dilemmas: 1. Nova spent ₹40,00,000 on preliminary research for a novel battery technology. Commercial viability is unproven. 2. Nova acquired high-end servers under a 5-year non-cancellable lease matching the total economic life of the servers. Nova incurs maintenance and risk, but legal title remains with the lessor until the final token payment in Year 5. 3. A former employee filed a legal suit claiming ₹60,00,000 for wrongful termination. Legal counsel estimates only a 15% probability that Nova will lose. 4. Nova spent ₹15,00,000 on general brand-building advertisements. While management expects long-term brand equity, future economic inflows cannot be isolated or measured reliably.
Medium SCENARIO · Asset Recognition Criteria | Research Expenditure | Probability Criterion
How should the research expenditure of ₹40,00,000 be treated under the Framework's asset recognition criteria?
A. Capitalized as an Intangible Asset in the Balance Sheet.
B. Expensed immediately in Profit and Loss. ✔
C. Deferred and amortized over a 5-year period.
D. Deducted directly from Shareholder Equity reserves.
Explanation: Because commercial viability is unproven, future economic benefit flow is not probable. Under the Framework, if probability of economic inflow is absent, expenditure must be expensed immediately in Profit and Loss.
Medium SCENARIO · Substance over Form | Qualitative Characteristics | Asset Recognition
The server acquisition should be capitalized as an asset by Nova based on which key qualitative characteristic/principle?
A. Prudence
B. Substance over Form ✔
C. Materiality
D. Timeliness
Explanation: Under 'substance over form', economic reality prevails over legal form. Since Nova assumes all economic risks and rewards for the full economic life, the servers are recognized as assets despite legal title remaining with the lessor.
Hard SCENARIO · Liability Recognition | Contingent Liability | Probability Assessment
How should the legal lawsuit of ₹60,00,000 (15% loss probability) be treated in Nova's financial statements?
A. Recognized as a Provision liability in the Balance Sheet.
B. Written off as an extraordinary loss in Profit and Loss.
C. Disclosed as a Contingent Liability in notes without balance sheet liability recognition. ✔
D. Ignored entirely with no disclosure required.
Explanation: A liability recognition requires a probable outflow of resources (greater than 50%). Since the loss probability is only 15% (not probable), it fails balance sheet liability recognition criteria and must be disclosed as a contingent liability in the notes.
Medium SCENARIO · Reliable Measurement | Recognition Criteria | Intangibles
Why are the ₹15,00,000 brand-building advertisement costs excluded from asset recognition?
A. Because advertisement cost is not physical property.
B. Because future economic benefits cannot be measured with reasonable reliability. ✔
C. Because advertising violates the fundamental going concern assumption.
D. Because advertising is regulated under tax laws only.
Explanation: An asset requires both probable future economic benefits and a cost/value that can be measured with reliability. General brand expenditure cannot be separately identified or measured reliably, failing the reliable measurement recognition criterion.
CASE SCENARIO: Valence Manufacturing Ltd. holds four assets/liabilities at year-end (31st March 2025) and requires valuation guidance under the Framework: - Asset 1: Raw Material 'M' purchased for ₹6,00,000. Replacement cost today is ₹5,10,000. Finished product made from 'M' will be sold at a price above cost. - Asset 2: Finished Goods 'G' produced at cost of ₹10,00,000. Current market selling price is ₹9,20,000, with estimated selling costs of ₹50,000. - Asset 3: Heavy Machinery purchased 4 years ago for ₹25,00,000 (carrying value ₹16,00,000). Current replacement cost of equivalent new machine is ₹20,00,000. Present value of expected future cash flows from continuing usage is ₹14,50,000. - Obligation 4: Foreign supplier debt of $20,000 initially recorded at $1 = ₹75 (₹15,00,000). Closing exchange rate on 31st March 2025 is $1 = ₹83.
Hard SCENARIO · Raw Material Valuation | Lower of Cost and NRV | Asset Measurement
Under the Framework and applicable valuation rules, at what value should Raw Material 'M' be reported?
A. ₹5,10,000
B. ₹6,00,000 ✔
C. ₹5,55,000
D. ₹0
Explanation: Raw materials held for use in production are not written down below cost if the finished products in which they will be incorporated are expected to be sold at or above cost. Hence, Raw Material 'M' remains valued at historical cost ₹6,00,000.
Medium SCENARIO · Inventory NRV | Lower of Cost and NRV | Measurement Basis
At what value should Finished Goods 'G' be carried in the Balance Sheet?
A. ₹10,00,000
B. ₹9,20,000
C. ₹8,70,000 ✔
D. ₹9,50,000
Explanation: Inventories are measured at lower of cost and net realisable value (NRV). NRV = Selling Price (₹9,20,000) - Selling Costs (₹50,000) = ₹8,70,000. Since NRV (₹8,70,000) is lower than cost (₹10,00,000), it is valued at ₹8,70,000.
Medium SCENARIO · Present Value | Measurement Basis | Asset Valuation
What figure represents the Present Value measurement basis for Heavy Machinery (Asset 3)?
A. ₹25,00,000
B. ₹16,00,000
C. ₹20,00,000
D. ₹14,50,000 ✔
Explanation: Present value is defined as the discounted present value of the future net cash inflows expected from the item in the normal course of business, which is explicitly given as ₹14,50,000.
Hard SCENARIO · Settlement Value | Foreign Currency Obligation | Measurement Basis
Under which measurement basis principle is Foreign Obligation 4 adjusted to ₹16,60,000 ($20,000 × ₹83) at year-end?
A. Historical Cost
B. Current Settlement Value at balance sheet date rates ✔
C. Physical Capital Maintenance
D. Discounted Future Cash Flows
Explanation: Settlement value reflects the undiscounted amount of cash required to discharge obligations at the reporting date. Adjusting foreign currency debt to closing spot rates measures the obligation at its current settlement value.
CASE SCENARIO: Aura Retail Ltd., a chain store, faces four accounting evaluation issues in preparing financial reports: Issue A: Aura owns 5,00,000 low-value shopping baskets costing ₹10 each. Tracking individual depreciation across 500 stores would cost ₹12,00,000 in administrative systems. Aura proposes expensing them immediately. Issue B: To beat competitors, management wants to publish financial results 5 days after year-end using unverified sales estimates rather than waiting 25 days for fully audited sales numbers. Issue C: Aura changed its depreciation policy from Straight Line Method to Written Down Value Method purely to reduce reported profits and save manager bonuses, without any change in asset usage pattern or AS compliance. Issue D: Management created a 'General Contingency Reserve' of ₹30,00,000 against vague future business risks, claiming compliance with 'prudence'.
Medium SCENARIO · Benefit and Cost Constraint | Materiality | Qualitative Constraints
Regarding Issue A (shopping baskets), which constraint justifies expensing these items immediately rather than tracking detailed depreciation?
A. Timeliness versus Reliability
B. Balance between Benefit and Cost ✔
C. Substance over Form
D. Prudence versus Neutrality
Explanation: The balance between benefit and cost is a pervasive constraint. The benefits derived from tracking low-value items individually should exceed the cost of providing that detailed accounting info.
Medium SCENARIO · Timeliness vs Reliability | Constraints | Reporting Trade-offs
Issue B (early reporting using estimated figures) highlights a direct trade-off between which two qualitative attributes/constraints?
A. Timeliness and Reliability ✔
B. Materiality and Relevance
C. Substance over Form and Prudence
D. Neutrality and Comparability
Explanation: Releasing results quickly enhances timeliness, but relying on unverified estimates compromises reliability. Management must balance timeliness with reliability to best satisfy economic decision-making needs.
Medium SCENARIO · Consistency | Comparability | Accounting Policy Changes
Issue C (changing accounting policy to manipulate bonuses) violates which fundamental principle/assumption?
A. Going Concern
B. Consistency / Comparability ✔
C. Accrual
D. Materiality
Explanation: Consistency requires accounting policies to be applied uniformly over time. Arbitrary changes without justification (like better presentation or statutory requirement) violate consistency and comparability.
Hard SCENARIO · Prudence | Neutrality | Hidden Reserves
Does Issue D (vague contingency reserve) comply with the Framework's concept of 'Prudence'?
A. Yes, because prudence encourages anticipating all imaginable future operational risks.
B. No, because prudence does not permit the creation of hidden reserves or deliberate overstatement of liabilities/expenses. ✔
C. Yes, provided it is authorized by the board of directors.
D. No, because prudence applies exclusively to assets, not provisions or liabilities.
Explanation: Prudence does not permit the creation of hidden reserves or excessive provisions, as deliberate understatement of assets/income or overstatement of liabilities/expenses makes financial statements non-neutral and unreliable.
CASE SCENARIO: Kestrel Logistics Ltd. suffered severe operational disruption in FY 2024-25. On 20th March 2025, its primary banking facility was withdrawn, and major clients terminated service contracts. On 31st March 2025, management determined that the entity has no realistic alternative but to cease operations and liquidate within 60 days. Financial records at 31st March 2025 show: - Transport Trucks: Original Historical Cost ₹1,00,000,000; Accumulated Depreciation ₹40,00,000; Realisable Value in forced liquidation ₹25,00,000. - Warehouse Lease Agreement: Early termination penalty payable upon breach in April 2025 is ₹10,00,000. - Outstanding Driver Salaries: ₹6,00,000 incurred for services rendered in March 2025. - Spares Inventory: Cost ₹15,00,000; Realizable liquidation value ₹4,00,000.
Medium SCENARIO · Going Concern | Fundamental Accounting Assumptions | Liquidation Impact
Which fundamental accounting assumption is invalidated for Kestrel Logistics Ltd. as of 31st March 2025?
A. Accrual
B. Consistency
C. Going Concern ✔
D. Materiality
Explanation: Since the entity is forced to liquidate within 60 days, it cannot continue operations for the foreseeable future. Thus, the Going Concern assumption is no longer valid.
Hard SCENARIO · Net Realisable Value | Liquidation Measurement Basis | Asset Valuation
At what amount should the Transport Trucks be carried on the Balance Sheet as of 31st March 2025?
A. ₹60,00,000 (Book Value)
B. ₹25,00,000 (Liquidation Value) ✔
C. ₹100,00,000 (Historical Cost)
D. Nil
Explanation: When going concern is invalidated, assets cannot be carried at book values under normal historical cost assumptions. They must be written down to their net realisable / forced liquidation values (₹25,00,000).
Hard SCENARIO · Liability Recognition | Present Obligation | Liquidation Adjustments
How should the Warehouse Lease termination penalty of ₹10,00,000 be treated on 31st March 2025?
A. Ignored because the breach technically occurs in April 2025.
B. Recognized as a present liability/provision because liquidation is imminent. ✔
C. Disclosed only as a non-quantifiable footnote.
D. Deferred and amortized over the original lease duration.
Explanation: Because liquidation is imminent, the termination of the lease becomes an unavoidable present obligation arising from current events, requiring immediate liability recognition on the liquidation basis.
Medium SCENARIO · Inventory Valuation | Realisable Value | Going Concern Invalidation
At what value should Spares Inventory be reported in Kestrel's financial statements?
A. ₹15,00,000
B. ₹4,00,000 ✔
C. ₹9,50,000
D. ₹0
Explanation: Under the net realisable / liquidation framework, inventories are written down to their immediate net liquidation value of ₹4,00,000.

Paper 1: Advanced Accounting · Module 1 · Chapter 3:

Accounts — 55 rows
Easy NORMAL · Non-Corporate Entities | Level I Thresholds
What is the turnover threshold (excluding other income) for a non-corporate entity to be classified as a Level I entity as per ICAI guidelines?
A. Exceeds ₹50 crore
B. Exceeds ₹100 crore
C. Exceeds ₹250 crore ✔
D. Exceeds ₹500 crore
Explanation: As per ICAI guidelines for applicability of Accounting Standards to non-corporate entities, Level I entities are large-sized entities. One of the criteria is that turnover (excluding other income) exceeds ₹250 crore in the immediately preceding accounting year.
Easy NORMAL · SMC Criteria | Corporate Entities
Under the Companies (Accounting Standards) Rules, a company is NOT classified as a Small and Medium-Sized Company (SMC) if its borrowings (including public deposits) at any time during the immediately preceding accounting year exceed:
A. ₹10 crore
B. ₹25 crore
C. ₹50 crore ✔
D. ₹100 crore
Explanation: Under the Companies (Accounting Standards) Rules, one of the essential conditions for an unlisted company to be an SMC is that its borrowings (including public deposits) do not exceed ₹50 crore at any time during the immediately preceding accounting year. If borrowings exceed ₹50 crore, the company is classified as a Non-SMC.
Easy NORMAL · Standard Setting Process | ASB
Which standard-setting body was constituted by the ICAI in 1977 to formulate Accounting Standards in India?
A. National Financial Reporting Authority (NFRA)
B. Accounting Standards Board (ASB) ✔
C. Ministry of Corporate Affairs (MCA)
D. Auditing and Assurance Standards Board (AASB)
Explanation: The Institute of Chartered Accountants of India (ICAI) constituted the Accounting Standards Board (ASB) in 1977. ASB is responsible for formulating Accounting Standards to establish uniform accounting policies and practices in India.
Easy NORMAL · AS 3 Exemption | Companies Act 2013
Under Section 2(40) of the Companies Act, 2013, which of the following corporate entities is explicitly exempted from preparing a Cash Flow Statement (AS 3)?
A. Any unlisted public company
B. One Person Company (OPC) ✔
C. Listed company with turnover below ₹250 crore
D. Non-Banking Financial Company (NBFC)
Explanation: Section 2(40) of the Companies Act, 2013 provides that the financial statements of a One Person Company (OPC), Small Company, Dormant Company, and recognized Startup private company need not include a Cash Flow Statement. Thus, OPC is statutorily exempted from preparing AS 3 Cash Flow Statement.
Easy NORMAL · Non-Corporate Entities | Level Classification
Non-corporate entities are categorized into how many levels by the ICAI for the purpose of applicability of Accounting Standards?
A. Two levels
B. Three levels
C. Four levels ✔
D. Five levels
Explanation: ICAI revised the scheme for classification of non-corporate entities into four distinct levels: Level I (Large size), Level II (Medium size), Level III (Small size), and Level IV (Micro size). Differential relaxations and exemptions are prescribed based on these levels.
Easy NORMAL · Companies Act 2013 | Section 133
Under which section of the Companies Act, 2013 does the Central Government prescribe Accounting Standards as recommended by ICAI and NFRA?
A. Section 129
B. Section 133 ✔
C. Section 134
D. Section 143
Explanation: Section 133 of the Companies Act, 2013 empowers the Central Government to prescribe the standards of accounting or any addendum thereto, as recommended by ICAI and examined/recommended by NFRA.
Easy NORMAL · Ind AS Applicability | Net Worth Threshold
What is the net worth threshold at or above which unlisted Indian companies are required to mandatorily comply with Indian Accounting Standards (Ind AS)?
A. ₹100 crore
B. ₹250 crore ✔
C. ₹500 crore
D. ₹1,000 crore
Explanation: Under the Ind AS roadmap issued by the MCA, all unlisted companies having a net worth of ₹250 crore or more are required to apply Ind AS. Unlisted companies below ₹250 crore net worth continue to apply Accounting Standards (AS).
Easy NORMAL · AS 1 | Fundamental Assumptions
Which of the following is NOT one of the three fundamental accounting assumptions specified in AS 1 'Disclosure of Accounting Policies'?
A. Going Concern
B. Consistency
C. Accrual
D. Prudence ✔
Explanation: AS 1 specifies three fundamental accounting assumptions: Going Concern, Consistency, and Accrual. Prudence is a major consideration in selecting accounting policies, not a fundamental accounting assumption.
Easy NORMAL · Transition Rules | Non-Corporate Entities
When a non-corporate entity moves from a higher level (Level I) to a lower level (Level II), for how many consecutive years must it satisfy the lower level criteria before it can claim relaxations of that lower level?
A. 1 year
B. 2 consecutive years ✔
C. 3 consecutive years
D. No waiting period required
Explanation: An entity that drops from a higher level to a lower level must remain in the lower level for two consecutive years before it can avail the exemptions or relaxations available to that lower level. This prevents frequent status switching due to temporary operational fluctuations.
Easy NORMAL · Transition Rules | Loss of Exemptions
When a Level IV non-corporate entity migrates to Level I during a financial year because its borrowings cross ₹50 crore, when do its exemptions cease to apply?
A. Immediately in the current accounting year ✔
B. After 2 consecutive years
C. From the next financial year only
D. At the discretion of management
Explanation: If an entity moves from a lower level to a higher level, exemptions and relaxations previously enjoyed cease to apply immediately from the current accounting period in which the event causing reclassification occurs.
Medium NORMAL · Level III Criteria | Non-Corporate Borrowings
M/s Alpha Traders is a partnership firm. To be classified as a Level III non-corporate entity, its borrowings (including public deposits) during the immediately preceding accounting year must be:
A. Up to ₹2 crore
B. Exceeding ₹2 crore but not exceeding ₹10 crore ✔
C. Exceeding ₹10 crore but not exceeding ₹50 crore
D. Exceeding ₹50 crore
Explanation: Level III (Small size) non-corporate entities are those whose borrowings (including public deposits) exceed ₹2 crore but do not exceed ₹10 crore at any time during the immediately preceding accounting year (and turnover is > ₹10 crore up to ₹50 crore).
Medium NORMAL · Level II Criteria | Turnover Thresholds
What is the turnover limit range (excluding other income) for a non-corporate entity to be categorized as a Level II (Medium size) entity?
A. Exceeds ₹10 crore but does not exceed ₹50 crore
B. Exceeds ₹50 crore but does not exceed ₹250 crore ✔
C. Exceeds ₹250 crore
D. Up to ₹10 crore
Explanation: For Level II (Medium size) non-corporate entities, turnover (excluding other income) must exceed ₹50 crore but not exceed ₹250 crore in the immediately preceding accounting year.
Medium NORMAL · AS 17 Applicability | Non-Corporate Exemptions
How does AS 17 'Segment Reporting' apply to Level II non-corporate entities under ICAI guidelines?
A. Fully applicable without any exemption or relaxation ✔
B. Completely exempted
C. Applicable only if listed on stock exchanges
D. Applicable with disclosure relaxations
Explanation: AS 17 Segment Reporting is fully applicable to Level I and Level II non-corporate entities without exemptions. Complete exemption from AS 17 is available only to Level III and Level IV non-corporate entities.
Medium NORMAL · SMC Disclosure | Accounting Policy
If a Small and Medium-Sized Company (SMC) opts to avail exemptions/relaxations available to it under Companies (Accounting Standards) Rules, what specific disclosure must it make in its financial statements?
A. No special disclosure is needed
B. It must disclose by way of a note that it is an SMC and has complied with AS applicable to SMCs ✔
C. It must present full reconciliations as if exemptions were not taken
D. It must obtain prior written approval from MCA and disclose the approval number
Explanation: An SMC that avails exemptions/relaxations must explicitly state in the notes to financial statements that it is an SMC and has complied with Accounting Standards applicable to Small and Medium-Sized Companies.
Medium NORMAL · SMC Criteria | Holding-Subsidiary Rule
Zeta Ltd is an unlisted company with turnover of ₹15 crore and zero borrowings. However, it is a subsidiary of Omega Ltd, which is a Non-SMC. Can Zeta Ltd qualify as an SMC?
A. Yes, because its individual turnover is well within SMC limits
B. Yes, provided its shareholders pass a special resolution
C. No, because a subsidiary of a Non-SMC cannot be classified as an SMC ✔
D. No, unless MCA grants a specific exemption
Explanation: Under the Companies (Accounting Standards) Rules, a company that is a holding or subsidiary company of a Non-SMC entity cannot be classified as an SMC, regardless of its individual size or turnover.
Medium NORMAL · Framework | Measurement Bases
According to the Framework for Preparation and Presentation of Financial Statements, under which measurement basis are assets recorded at the discounted present value of future net cash inflows?
A. Historical Cost
B. Current Cost
C. Realizable Value
D. Present Value ✔
Explanation: Under the Present Value measurement basis, assets are carried at the discounted present value of the future net cash inflows that the item is expected to generate in the normal course of business.
Medium NORMAL · AS 28 Relaxations | Level IV Entities
With respect to AS 28 'Impairment of Assets', which specific relaxation is available to Level IV non-corporate entities?
A. Fully exempt from the entire standard AS 28
B. Exempt from calculating Value in Use using discounted cash flow models if reasonable estimate of net selling price is available ✔
C. Allowed to ignore impairment losses completely
D. Exempt from recording impairment loss in profit or loss
Explanation: Level IV non-corporate entities are granted relaxation in AS 28 whereby Value in Use can be estimated based on reasonable indications rather than complex discounted cash flow calculations if net selling price cannot be determined.
Medium NORMAL · Level IV Criteria | Borrowing Limit
What is the maximum borrowing limit (including public deposits) at any time during the immediately preceding accounting year for an entity to qualify as a Level IV non-corporate entity?
A. Does not exceed ₹2 crore ✔
B. Does not exceed ₹5 crore
C. Does not exceed ₹10 crore
D. Does not exceed ₹50 crore
Explanation: Level IV (Micro size) non-corporate entities are entities whose turnover does not exceed ₹10 crore and borrowings (including public deposits) do not exceed ₹2 crore at any time during the immediately preceding accounting year.
Medium NORMAL · SMC Transition | Comparative Figures
When an SMC loses its SMC status and becomes a Non-SMC in the current year, how should it handle the financial figures of the comparative previous accounting period?
A. It must restate previous year figures fully as if it was a Non-SMC
B. Comparative figures need not be revised for exemptions enjoyed in previous year unless required by specific AS ✔
C. It must re-audit previous year financial statements under Non-SMC rules
D. Comparative figures must be completely omitted from financial statements
Explanation: When an SMC becomes a Non-SMC, comparative figures for the previous year need not be revised for exemptions enjoyed in the previous year, unless specific transitional provisions of individual Accounting Standards state otherwise.
