Medium NORMAL · SMC Criteria | Banks and Financial Institutions
Can a small private sector bank with turnover of ₹100 crore and borrowings of ₹20 crore qualify as an SMC under the Companies (Accounting Standards) Rules?
A. Yes, because turnover is below ₹250 crore
B. Yes, because borrowings are below ₹50 crore
C. No, because banks, financial institutions, and insurance companies are excluded from SMC definition regardless of size ✔
D. Yes, if approved by the Reserve Bank of India
Explanation: The definition of SMC explicitly excludes banks, financial institutions, and insurance companies regardless of their turnover or borrowing limits. Therefore, a bank can never qualify as an SMC.
Medium NORMAL · Framework | Qualitative Characteristics
According to the Framework, to be reliable, information in financial statements must be neutral, free from material error, complete, and:
A. Prepared strictly under historical cost
B. Represent faithfully the transactions and events it purports to represent ✔
C. Audited by an independent chartered accountant
D. Approved by the Board of Directors
Explanation: Under the Framework, information possesses the quality of reliability when it is free from material error and bias, and can be depended upon by users to represent faithfully that which it either purports to represent or could reasonably be expected to represent.
Medium NORMAL · AS 15 Relaxation | Level IV Entities
Level IV non-corporate entities enjoy which relaxation regarding defined benefit plans under AS 15 'Employee Benefits'?
A. Full exemption from recognizing liability for short-term benefits
B. Exemption from actuarial valuation for defined benefit plan liability using projected unit credit method, allowing simplified methods ✔
C. Allowed to classify all employee costs as deferred revenue expenditure
D. Exempt from paying statutory provident fund
Explanation: For defined benefit plans, Level IV non-corporate entities are exempt from using the Projected Unit Credit Method and actuarial valuation; they are allowed to measure liabilities using simplified methods (e.g., accrued liability without discounting).
Hard NORMAL · Holding-Subsidiary | Non-Corporate Entities | Level I
Firm X (a partnership firm) has turnover of ₹5 crore and borrowings of ₹50 lakh. However, 80% of its equity interest is held by ABC Ltd, a listed corporate entity. What is the non-corporate entity level classification of Firm X?
A. Level IV
B. Level III
C. Level II
D. Level I ✔
Explanation: If a non-corporate entity is a holding or subsidiary entity of a Level I / Non-SMC entity (such as a listed company), it automatically gets classified as a Level I non-corporate entity, irrespective of its individual turnover and borrowing numbers.
Hard NORMAL · Borrowing Limit Test | Level I Criteria
For determining Level classification for FY 2025-26, an entity checks its figures of FY 2024-25. Turnover was ₹40 crore throughout. Borrowings were zero except for 2 days in Nov 2024 when a temporary bank overdraft reached ₹52 crore. The entity's classification for FY 2025-26 is:
A. Level IV, because overdraft was temporary
B. Level III, because average borrowings were below ₹10 crore
C. Level II, based on turnover criteria
D. Level I, because borrowings exceeded ₹50 crore 'at any time' during the preceding year ✔
Explanation: The borrowing criterion test for entity classification requires checking if borrowings exceed the threshold (₹50 crore for Level I) 'at any time during the immediately preceding accounting year'. Since borrowings hit ₹52 crore for 2 days, it qualifies as Level I.
Hard NORMAL · Transition Rules | 2-Year Rule
A non-corporate entity was Level I in FY 2022-23. In FY 2023-24, its turnover dropped to ₹30 crore and borrowings to ₹1 crore (qualifying for Level III). In FY 2024-25, figures remained in Level III. Can it claim Level III relaxations for FY 2025-26?
A. No, it must wait 3 consecutive years
B. Yes, because it maintained Level III criteria for 2 consecutive years (FY 2023-24 & 2024-25) ✔
C. No, because once Level I, exemptions are lost permanently
D. Yes, instantly from FY 2023-24 without waiting
Explanation: Under ICAI guidelines, when an entity drops from Level I to a lower level (Level III), it must maintain the criteria of the lower level for 2 consecutive accounting years (FY 23-24 and FY 24-25). Once satisfied, it can avail Level III relaxations in FY 2025-26.
Hard NORMAL · AS 23 Applicability | Consolidated Financial Statements
M/s Green Enterprises is a Level IV non-corporate entity holding a 30% investment in an associate partnership firm. Is M/s Green Enterprises required to mandatorily prepare Consolidated Financial Statements under AS 23?
A. Yes, AS 23 is mandatory for all entities having associates
B. No, AS 23 applies only if the entity is required or elects to prepare Consolidated Financial Statements ✔
C. Yes, but with disclosure relaxations
D. No, Level IV entities are banned from investing in associates
Explanation: AS 23 (Accounting for Investments in Associates in Consolidated Financial Statements) does not mandate preparation of Consolidated Financial Statements by itself. It applies only if the entity is required by statute/contract or voluntarily elects to prepare Consolidated Financial Statements.
Hard NORMAL · Framework | Asset Recognition Criteria
An item that meets the definition of an 'Asset' under the Framework should be recognized in the financial statements if and only if:
A. It is owned legally by the enterprise and has historical cost
B. It is probable that future economic benefits will flow to the entity and the item has a cost or value that can be measured with reliability ✔
C. Its fair value is greater than its book value
D. Management intends to hold it for more than 12 months
Explanation: Under the Framework, an item meeting the definition of an element (asset) should be recognized if: (a) it is probable that any future economic benefit associated with the item will flow to or from the entity; and (b) the item has a cost or value that can be measured with reliability.
Hard NORMAL · Framework | Measurement Bases
An enterprise holds machinery. The amount of cash or cash equivalents that could currently be obtained by selling the asset in an orderly disposal is known as its:
A. Historical Cost
B. Current Cost
C. Realizable (Settlement) Value ✔
D. Present Value
Explanation: Realizable value is defined in the Framework as the amount of cash or cash equivalents that could currently be obtained by selling an asset in an orderly disposal.
Hard NORMAL · AS 20 Applicability | Non-Corporate Entities
M/s Apex Traders is a Level II non-corporate sole proprietorship firm. Does AS 20 'Earnings Per Share' apply to it?
A. Yes, fully applicable including diluted EPS
B. Applicable with disclosure relaxations for Diluted EPS
C. Exempted entirely, as AS 20 applies only to corporate entities having share capital ✔
D. Mandatory only if turnover exceeds ₹100 crore
Explanation: AS 20 Earnings Per Share applies only to entities whose equity shares or potential equity shares are listed or in process of listing, and to corporate entities. Non-corporate entities do not have share capital, so AS 20 is completely non-applicable to them.
Hard NORMAL · Section 2(40) | Startup Exemption | AS 3
Under Section 2(40) of the Companies Act, 2013, a private company recognized as a 'startup' by DPIIT is exempt from preparing which component of financial statements?
A. Balance Sheet
B. Profit and Loss Account
C. Cash Flow Statement ✔
D. Notes to Accounts
Explanation: The proviso to Section 2(40) of Companies Act, 2013 explicitly grants exemption from preparing Cash Flow Statement to One Person Companies, Small Companies, Dormant Companies, and recognized Private Startup companies.
CASE SCENARIO: Vidyut Tech Ltd is an unlisted public company incorporated in India. For FY 2024-25, its turnover was ₹220 crore, and it maintained a short-term working capital loan from a bank of ₹42 crore throughout the year. On 15th March 2025, it temporarily took a bridge loan of ₹10 crore, taking total borrowings to ₹52 crore for 5 days before repaying it on 20th March 2025. Vidyut Tech Ltd holds a 100% subsidiary company, Spark Cables Pvt Ltd, which has a turnover of ₹12 crore and borrowings of ₹1 crore. Neither company is in the process of listing. Management is evaluating SMC status for both companies for FY 2025-26 and assessing compliance requirements under AS 3 and AS 17.
Medium SCENARIO · SMC Borrowing Limit | Corporate Classification
What is the classification status of Vidyut Tech Ltd for FY 2025-26 under the Companies (Accounting Standards) Rules?
A. SMC, because average borrowings were below ₹50 crore
B. Non-SMC, because total borrowings exceeded ₹50 crore at a point in FY 2024-25 ✔
C. SMC, because turnover was below ₹250 crore
D. Non-SMC, solely because it is a public company
Explanation: Borrowings crossed ₹50 crore (reaching ₹52 crore) during FY 2024-25 'at any time'. Therefore, Vidyut Tech Ltd fails the borrowing limit criterion of SMC (<= ₹50 crore) and is classified as a Non-SMC for FY 2025-26.
Medium SCENARIO · Subsidiary Status | Non-SMC Propagation
Can Spark Cables Pvt Ltd be classified as an SMC for FY 2025-26?
A. Yes, because its individual turnover and borrowings are within SMC limits
B. No, because its holding company (Vidyut Tech Ltd) is a Non-SMC ✔
C. Yes, if its Board passes a resolution
D. No, because all subsidiaries of public companies are Non-SMCs
Explanation: Under Companies (Accounting Standards) Rules, an entity cannot be classified as an SMC if it is a holding or subsidiary company of a Non-SMC entity. Since holding company Vidyut Tech Ltd is a Non-SMC, Spark Cables Pvt Ltd becomes a Non-SMC.
Hard SCENARIO · AS 17 Applicability | Non-SMC
Is Vidyut Tech Ltd required to present Segment Reporting under AS 17 for FY 2025-26?
A. No, AS 17 applies only to listed companies
B. Yes, AS 17 is fully applicable to Non-SMCs ✔
C. No, because turnover is less than ₹250 crore
D. Yes, but with disclosure relaxations
Explanation: AS 17 Segment Reporting is fully applicable to all Non-SMC companies (both listed and unlisted) without any exemption.
Hard SCENARIO · Cash Flow Statement Exemption | Section 2(40)
If Spark Cables Pvt Ltd qualifies as a 'Small Company' under Section 2(85) of Companies Act 2013, is it required to prepare a Cash Flow Statement for statutory compliance under the Act?
A. Yes, because it is a Non-SMC under AS Rules
B. No, Small Companies are exempted from Cash Flow Statement under Section 2(40) of Companies Act 2013 ✔
C. Yes, because AS 3 overrides Companies Act provisions
D. No, only if turnover is below ₹2 crore
Explanation: Under Section 2(40) of the Companies Act, 2013, financial statements of a 'Small Company' need not include a Cash Flow Statement. The statutory exemption under the Act prevails for filing requirements.
CASE SCENARIO: M/s Apex & Co. is a partnership firm engaged in wholesale trading. Its financial indicators over recent years are as follows: - FY 2022-23: Turnover ₹260 crore, Borrowings ₹60 crore (Classified as Level I for FY 2023-24). - FY 2023-24: Turnover ₹180 crore, Borrowings ₹35 crore (Meets Level II criteria). - FY 2024-25: Turnover ₹160 crore, Borrowings ₹30 crore (Meets Level II criteria). - FY 2025-26: Turnover ₹40 crore, Borrowings ₹8 crore (Meets Level III criteria). The firm wants to determine its Level classification for FY 2024-25, FY 2025-26, and FY 2026-27, and understand when it can avail relaxations/exemptions available to lower levels.
Hard SCENARIO · Transition Rules | 2-Year Waiting Period
For FY 2024-25, can M/s Apex & Co. avail exemptions/relaxations available to Level II non-corporate entities?
A. Yes, immediately in FY 2024-25
B. No, because FY 2023-24 was the 1st year of meeting Level II criteria, and 2 consecutive years are required ✔
C. Yes, because turnover fell below ₹250 crore
D. No, partnership firms cannot claim Level II exemptions
Explanation: When an entity drops from a higher level (Level I) to a lower level (Level II), it must satisfy the lower level criteria for two consecutive accounting years before claiming lower level relaxations. FY 2024-25 is only the 1st year after dropping, so relaxations cannot be availed in FY 2024-25.
Hard SCENARIO · Level II Relaxations | Transition Rules
For FY 2025-26, which Level status relaxations can M/s Apex & Co. claim, given it met Level II criteria in both FY 2023-24 and FY 2024-25?
A. Level I rules apply with no relaxations
B. Level II relaxations, as it completed 2 consecutive years meeting Level II criteria ✔
C. Level III relaxations, instantly
D. Level IV relaxations
Explanation: Having satisfied Level II criteria for two consecutive years (FY 2023-24 and FY 2024-25), M/s Apex & Co. can claim Level II exemptions/relaxations in FY 2025-26.
Medium SCENARIO · Level III Criteria | Non-Corporate Entities
In FY 2026-27, what is the level criteria evaluation of M/s Apex & Co. based on FY 2025-26 figures (Turnover ₹40 cr, Borrowings ₹8 cr)?
A. It meets Level III criteria ✔
B. It meets Level I criteria
C. It meets Level IV criteria
D. It meets Level II criteria
Explanation: For Level III classification, turnover is between ₹10 cr and ₹50 cr, and borrowings are between ₹2 cr and ₹10 cr. FY 2025-26 figures (Turnover ₹40 cr, Borrowings ₹8 cr) meet Level III criteria.
Hard SCENARIO · Loss of Exemption | Immediate Reclassification
If M/s Apex & Co. takes fresh bank loans in October 2026 raising total borrowings to ₹55 crore during FY 2026-27, how does its status change for FY 2026-27?
A. It becomes Level I immediately for FY 2026-27 and loses all exemptions ✔
B. It remains Level II till the end of the year
C. It must wait 2 years before becoming Level I
D. No effect until next financial year
Explanation: When an entity migrates from a lower level to a higher level (Level I), exemptions and relaxations cease to apply immediately from the current financial year in which the threshold is exceeded.
CASE SCENARIO: Reliable Goods Ltd is evaluating several accounting treatments under the ICAI 'Framework for the Preparation and Presentation of Financial Statements': 1. Item A: Machinery purchased 3 years ago for ₹50 lakh. Current replacement cost is ₹70 lakh; cash realizable on immediate sale is ₹40 lakh; present value of net future cash flows is ₹45 lakh. 2. Item B: Internal R&D expenditure of ₹15 lakh incurred in developing a new software process. Ultimate economic benefits are uncertain. 3. Item C: A legal claim against the company of ₹20 lakh where loss is probable and can be measured reliably. The CFO wants to know the appropriate measurement bases and recognition criteria applicable under the Framework.
Easy SCENARIO · Framework | Current Cost
Under the Framework, if Item A (Machinery) is measured at ₹70 lakh (the amount of cash required to purchase the same asset currently), which measurement basis is being applied?
A. Historical Cost
B. Current Cost ✔
C. Realizable Value
D. Present Value
Explanation: Current Cost is defined as the amount of cash or cash equivalents that would have to be paid if the same or an equivalent asset were acquired currently.
Medium SCENARIO · Asset Recognition | Framework
Under the Framework, why should Item B (Internal R&D expenditure with uncertain benefits) NOT be recognized as an asset in the Balance Sheet?
A. Because it has no historical cost
B. Because it fails the recognition criterion of probable future economic benefits ✔
C. Because intangible assets are strictly banned under Framework
D. Because cash has already been paid
Explanation: An asset is recognized in the balance sheet when it is probable that future economic benefits will flow to the entity and the asset has a cost or value that can be measured reliably. Uncertainty of benefits fails the probability test.
Medium SCENARIO · Qualitative Characteristics | Prudence
Under the Framework, Item C (probable legal claim of ₹20 lakh) satisfies the definition of a liability. Which qualitative characteristic ensures liabilities are recognized without understating them?
A. Prudence as part of Reliability ✔
B. Timeliness
C. Materiality
D. Understandability
Explanation: Prudence is the inclusion of a degree of caution in the exercise of judgments, ensuring assets/income are not overstated and liabilities/expenses are not understated, maintaining reliability.
Easy SCENARIO · Measurement Bases | Realizable Value
If Item A (Machinery) is shown at ₹40 lakh (cash obtainable by selling in an orderly disposal), which measurement basis is being used?
A. Historical Cost
B. Present Value
C. Realizable (Settlement) Value ✔
D. Current Cost
Explanation: Realizable value is the amount of cash or cash equivalents that could currently be obtained by selling an asset in an orderly disposal.
CASE SCENARIO: M/s Precision Engineering is a sole proprietorship non-corporate entity engaged in small-scale machining. For FY 2024-25, its turnover was ₹4 crore and bank borrowings were ₹50 lakh. It has zero listed securities and no group entities. The proprietor is reviewing compliance for Accounting Standards and seeks advice on exemptions available for Level IV entities regarding AS 3 (Cash Flow Statement), AS 17 (Segment Reporting), AS 18 (Related Party Disclosures), and AS 28 (Impairment of Assets).
Medium SCENARIO · Level IV Criteria | Non-Corporate Entities
What is the classification level of M/s Precision Engineering for FY 2025-26 under ICAI non-corporate entity guidelines?
A. Level I
B. Level II
C. Level III
D. Level IV ✔
Explanation: Turnover <= ₹10 crore (actual ₹4 cr) and Borrowings <= ₹2 crore (actual ₹50 lakh) classify M/s Precision Engineering as a Level IV (Micro size) non-corporate entity.
Medium SCENARIO · Level IV Exemptions | AS 3 | AS 17
Is M/s Precision Engineering required to comply with AS 3 (Cash Flow Statement) and AS 17 (Segment Reporting)?
A. Fully required for both AS 3 and AS 17
B. Exempt from AS 17, but mandatory for AS 3
C. Exempt from AS 3, but mandatory for AS 17
D. Exempt from both AS 3 and AS 17 ✔
Explanation: Level IV non-corporate entities are completely exempt from both AS 3 (Cash Flow Statement) and AS 17 (Segment Reporting).
Hard SCENARIO · AS 18 Exemption | Level IV Entities
Regarding AS 18 'Related Party Disclosures', what exemption is available to Level IV non-corporate entities?
A. Fully exempt from AS 18 ✔
B. Must comply with full disclosures without relaxation
C. Exempt from AS 18 only if turnover is below ₹1 crore
D. Exempt from disclosing key management personnel remuneration only
Explanation: Level IV non-corporate entities are fully exempt from AS 18 (Related Party Disclosures).
Hard SCENARIO · AS 28 Relaxation | Level IV Entities
Regarding AS 28 'Impairment of Assets', what relaxation is granted to Level IV non-corporate entities regarding 'Value in Use'?
A. They are completely exempt from AS 28
B. They can estimate Value in Use based on reasonable indication without using present value discount techniques ✔
C. They are not allowed to recognize impairment losses
D. They must use a mandatory 15% discount rate
Explanation: Level IV non-corporate entities are granted relaxation in AS 28 whereby Value in Use can be estimated based on reasonable indications rather than complex discounted cash flow calculations.
CASE SCENARIO: Global Spectrum Group consists of multiple corporate and non-corporate entities in India: 1. Spectrum India Ltd: Unlisted public company with Net Worth of ₹320 crore as on 31st March 2025. 2. Spectrum Infra Pvt Ltd: Unlisted subsidiary of Spectrum India Ltd, Net Worth ₹40 crore. 3. Spectrum Retail LLP: Non-corporate partnership entity with turnover ₹600 crore, borrowings ₹80 crore. 4. Spectrum Finance Ltd: Non-Banking Financial Company (NBFC), unlisted, Net Worth ₹180 crore. The board is determining whether Accounting Standards (AS) or Ind AS applies to each group entity for FY 2025-26.
Medium SCENARIO · Ind AS Roadmap | Net Worth Criteria
Which accounting standard framework applies to Spectrum India Ltd for FY 2025-26?
A. Accounting Standards (AS)
B. Indian Accounting Standards (Ind AS) ✔
C. IFRS directly
D. US GAAP
Explanation: Unlisted companies having a Net Worth of ₹250 crore or more are mandatorily required to follow Ind AS. Since Spectrum India Ltd has a Net Worth of ₹320 crore, Ind AS applies.
Hard SCENARIO · Ind AS Subsidiary Propagation | Ind AS Roadmap
Which accounting framework applies to Spectrum Infra Pvt Ltd (unlisted subsidiary of Spectrum India Ltd)?
A. Accounting Standards (AS) because its individual Net Worth is below ₹250 crore
B. Ind AS, because holding company Spectrum India Ltd is covered under Ind AS ✔
C. SMC Accounting Standards
D. Level II Non-corporate standards
Explanation: Under the Ind AS roadmap, holding, subsidiary, joint venture, or associate companies of an entity covered under Ind AS must also adopt Ind AS, regardless of their individual net worth.
Hard SCENARIO · Non-Corporate AS | Ind AS Scope
Which accounting standards framework applies to Spectrum Retail LLP (non-corporate LLP)?
A. Ind AS, because turnover exceeds ₹500 crore
B. Accounting Standards (AS) issued by ICAI (as a Level I non-corporate entity) ✔
C. Ind AS, because it belongs to a group following Ind AS
D. No accounting standards apply to LLPs
Explanation: Ind AS roadmap applies exclusively to corporate entities (companies, NBFCs, Banks, Insurance). Non-corporate entities (LLPs/firms) follow Accounting Standards (AS) issued by ICAI, categorized here as Level I due to turnover > ₹250 crore.
Hard SCENARIO · NBFC Ind AS Roadmap | Accounting Standards
Which framework applies to Spectrum Finance Ltd (unlisted NBFC with Net Worth ₹180 crore)?
A. Ind AS
B. Accounting Standards (AS) prescribed under Companies (AS) Rules ✔
C. Ind AS mandatorily regardless of net worth
D. Direct IFRS compliance
Explanation: Unlisted NBFCs with Net Worth below ₹250 crore are not covered under mandatory Ind AS phase and must follow Accounting Standards (AS) prescribed under Companies (Accounting Standards) Rules.

Paper 1: Advanced Accounting · Module 1 · Chapter 4:

Accounts — 55 rows
Easy NORMAL · AS 1 | Fundamental Assumptions | Accounting Policies
Which of the following is NOT recognized as a Fundamental Accounting Assumption under AS 1 (Disclosure of Accounting Policies)?
A. Going Concern
B. Consistency
C. Prudence ✔
D. Accrual
Explanation: AS 1 explicitly identifies Going Concern, Consistency, and Accrual as the three Fundamental Accounting Assumptions. Prudence is a major consideration in selecting and applying accounting policies, not a fundamental accounting assumption. Therefore, Prudence is the correct answer.
Easy NORMAL · AS 1 | Disclosure Requirements | Fundamental Assumptions
Under AS 1, if all fundamental accounting assumptions are followed in the preparation of financial statements, what disclosure is required?
A. A specific disclosure is required in the notes to accounts stating that all fundamental assumptions were followed.
B. No specific disclosure is required. ✔
C. Disclosure is required only in the Director's Report.
D. Disclosure is required only if the enterprise is a listed entity.
Explanation: According to AS 1, fundamental accounting assumptions are presumed to have been followed in financial statements. Specific disclosure is required only if a fundamental accounting assumption is NOT followed. Hence, no specific disclosure is needed when they are followed.
Easy NORMAL · AS 18 | Related Party Definition | KMP
According to AS 18 (Related Party Disclosures), which of the following relationships automatically constitutes a related party relationship?
A. A single major customer who accounts for 85% of total sales
B. Key Management Personnel (KMP) of the enterprise ✔
C. A provider of finance who exercises normal restrictive covenants
D. A trade union representing 90% of the workforce
Explanation: AS 18 explicitly covers Key Management Personnel (KMP) and their relatives as related parties. Major customers, providers of finance, and trade unions are explicitly excluded from being considered related parties merely by virtue of their normal dealings.
Easy NORMAL · AS 18 | Definition of Relative | Scope
Which of the following persons is EXCLUDED from the definition of 'relative' of an individual under AS 18?
A. Spouse
B. Brother or Sister
C. Grandparent ✔
D. Son or Daughter
Explanation: Under AS 18, 'relative' in relation to an individual means the spouse, son, daughter, brother, sister, father, and mother who are expected to influence, or be influenced by, that individual in dealings with the enterprise. Grandparents are not included in this definition.
Easy NORMAL · AS 20 | WANES | Bonus Issue
Under AS 20 (Earnings Per Share), how should bonus shares issued during the financial year be treated in the calculation of Weighted Average Number of Equity Shares (WANES)?
A. Weighted from the actual date of issue of the bonus shares
B. Treated as if they were issued at the beginning of the earliest period reported ✔
C. Weighted for 6 months irrespective of the date of issue
D. Ignored for Basic EPS and included only for Diluted EPS
Explanation: AS 20 specifies that in case of a bonus issue, equity shares are issued without additional consideration. Therefore, they are treated as if they had been issued at the beginning of the earliest period reported, adjusting WANES retrospectively.
Easy NORMAL · AS 20 | Basic EPS | Formula
What is the basic formula for calculating Basic Earnings Per Share under AS 20?
A. Net Profit before Tax / Total Number of Equity Shares issued
B. Net Profit or Loss for the period attributable to Equity Shareholders / Weighted Average Number of Equity Shares outstanding during the period ✔
C. (Net Profit after Tax + Non-controlling Interest) / Weighted Average Number of Equity Shares
D. Operating Profit / Total Paid-up Equity Share Capital
Explanation: AS 20 defines Basic EPS as Net Profit or Loss for the period attributable to equity shareholders divided by the Weighted Average Number of Equity Shares outstanding during the period. Numerator must be after deducting preference dividends and tax.
Easy NORMAL · AS 24 | Initial Disclosure Event | Discontinuing Operations
Which of the following events triggers the 'Initial Disclosure Event' for a discontinuing operation under AS 24?
A. When the enterprise decides in an informal meeting to shut down a segment
B. Whichever occurs EARLIER: entering into a binding sale agreement OR board approval of a detailed formal plan and making a public announcement ✔
C. Whichever occurs LATER: entering into a binding sale agreement OR board approval of a detailed formal plan and making a public announcement
D. When the actual transfer of all assets of the discontinuing segment is completed
Explanation: AS 24 defines the Initial Disclosure Event as the earlier of two events: (a) the enterprise entering into a binding sale agreement for substantially all assets of the discontinuing operation, or (b) approval by the board of a detailed formal plan and making a public announcement.
Easy NORMAL · AS 24 | Definition | Scope
Under AS 24, a discontinuing operation is a component of an enterprise that represents:
A. Any small product line that is being phased out
B. A separate major line of business or geographical area of operations ✔
C. A temporary suspension of factory operations due to strike
D. Sale of individual obsolete machinery in the ordinary course of business
Explanation: AS 24 requires that a discontinuing operation must represent a separate major line of business or geographical area of operations that can be distinguished operationally and for financial reporting purposes pursuant to a single plan.
Easy NORMAL · AS 18 | Exemptions | State-controlled Enterprises
According to AS 18, transactions with which of the following entities are exempt from disclosure requirements in the financial statements of state-controlled enterprises?
A. Key Management Personnel of the state-controlled enterprise
B. Other state-controlled enterprises ✔
C. Private limited subsidiaries of the state-controlled enterprise
D. Foreign joint ventures of the state-controlled enterprise
Explanation: AS 18 explicitly provides an exemption to state-controlled enterprises from disclosing related party transactions with other state-controlled enterprises. However, disclosures of transactions with KMP or non-state-controlled entities remain applicable.
Easy NORMAL · AS 20 | Anti-dilutive | Diluted EPS
Potential equity shares are considered 'anti-dilutive' under AS 20 when their conversion into equity shares would:
A. Decrease Earnings Per Share from continuing ordinary operations
B. Increase Earnings Per Share from continuing ordinary operations ✔
C. Have zero effect on Earnings Per Share
D. Reduce Loss Per Share from continuing ordinary operations
Explanation: Under AS 20, potential equity shares are anti-dilutive when their conversion would result in an increase in earnings per share (or a decrease in loss per share) from continuing ordinary operations. Anti-dilutive potential shares are excluded from Diluted EPS.
Medium NORMAL · AS 1 | Accounting Policy Change | Disclosure
Alpha Ltd changes its method of charging depreciation from Straight Line Method (SLM) to Written Down Value (WDV) method for all plant items to better reflect the pattern of economic benefits. Under AS 1, how should this change be disclosed?
A. No disclosure is required as depreciation is an accounting estimate, not a policy.
B. The change, reason for change, and its financial effect on current period profit must be disclosed. ✔
C. It must be disclosed retrospectively by adjusting opening retained earnings without disclosure in notes.
D. Only the total accumulated depreciation amount needs to be disclosed.
Explanation: A change in accounting policy or accounting treatment (such as method of depreciation reflecting economic benefit consumption) requires disclosure of the change, reasons for the change, and the financial impact on current period financial statements under AS 1.
Medium NORMAL · AS 1 | Substance over Form | Policy Considerations
An enterprise presents financial statements where 'Substance over Form' was prioritized over technical legal form in recording a lease transaction. Which Accounting Standard governs this overarching principle of policy selection?
A. AS 1 (Disclosure of Accounting Policies) ✔
B. AS 19 (Leases)
C. AS 5 (Net Profit or Loss for the Period)
D. AS 18 (Related Party Disclosures)
Explanation: AS 1 lays down the primary considerations for selection and application of accounting policies, which are Prudence, Substance over Form, and Materiality.
Medium NORMAL · AS 18 | Significant Influence | Disclosure
Company A holds 22% of the voting power in Company B. During the year ended 31st March 2025, Company B sold goods to Company A worth ₹15 Lakhs. No transactions occurred between them in the prior year. Under AS 18, how should Company B disclose this in its financial statements?
A. No disclosure required as 22% voting power only represents significant influence and not control.
B. Disclosure of related party relationship name, nature of relationship, and details of transaction (amount & outstanding balance) is mandatory. ✔
C. Only the name of Company A needs to be disclosed without transaction amounts.
D. Disclosure is required only in Consolidated Financial Statements, not Standalone Financial Statements.
Explanation: Holding 20% or more voting power creates significant influence under AS 18. When related party transactions take place during the period, disclosure of the relationship, description of transaction, volume/amount, and outstanding balances is mandatory in standalone FS.
Medium NORMAL · AS 18 | Common Directorship | Related Party Exclusions
Director X is a Director in both Company P and Company Q. Director X holds 1% equity shares in Company P and 2% equity shares in Company Q, and cannot direct the policies of either enterprise. Are Company P and Company Q related parties under AS 18?
A. Yes, because they have a common director.
B. No, mere common directorship without ability to affect transactions does not make enterprises related parties. ✔
C. Yes, because Director X holds equity shares in both companies.
D. Yes, provided transactions exceed ₹10 Lakhs.
Explanation: AS 18 specifically states that two enterprises are not related parties simply because they have a director in common, unless the director is able to affect the policies of both enterprises in their mutual dealings.
Medium NORMAL · AS 18 | Control | Nil Transaction Disclosure
If a control relationship exists between Holding Co and Subsidiary Co, but NO transactions took place between them during the financial year, what is the requirement under AS 18?
A. No disclosure is required because no transactions took place.
B. The reporting enterprise must disclose the name of the related party and the nature of the related party relationship. ✔
C. Disclosure is required only if requested by auditors.
D. Disclosure is required only if the holding company is a foreign entity.
Explanation: Under AS 18, where CONTROL exists between parties, disclosure of the related party relationship (name and nature) is mandatory irrespective of whether any transactions took place between them during the year.
Medium NORMAL · AS 20 | Basic EPS Calculation | WANES
Beta Ltd had 100,000 equity shares outstanding on 1st April 2024. It issued 20,000 equity shares for cash on 1st October 2024. Net profit after tax for the year ended 31st March 2025 is ₹11,000,000. Calculate Basic EPS under AS 20.
A. ₹100.00 ✔
B. ₹91.67
C. ₹110.00
D. ₹83.33
Explanation: WANES = 100,000 + (20,000 * 6/12) = 100,000 + 10,000 = 110,000 shares. Basic EPS = ₹11,000,000 / 110,000 = ₹100.00.
Medium NORMAL · AS 20 | Share Split | WANES
Gamma Ltd had 200,000 equity shares outstanding on 1st April 2024. On 1st January 2025, the company executed a share split, dividing each existing equity share of ₹10 into 2 equity shares of ₹5 each. What is the WANES for calculating Basic EPS for the year ended 31st March 2025?
A. 250,000 shares
B. 400,000 shares ✔
C. 200,000 shares
D. 300,000 shares
Explanation: A share split increases the number of equity shares without additional consideration. Under AS 20, a share split is treated as if it occurred at the beginning of the earliest period reported. Thus, total shares = 200,000 * 2 = 400,000 shares for the entire year.
Medium NORMAL · AS 20 | Diluted EPS | Convertible Debentures
Under AS 20, when calculating Diluted EPS, what adjustment is required in the numerator (Net Profit attributable to equity shareholders) for convertible debentures?
A. Deduct interest on debentures net of tax effect
B. Add back interest on debentures net of tax effect ✔
C. Add back interest on debentures without adjusting tax effect
D. No adjustment to numerator, only denominator is adjusted
Explanation: If convertible debentures are converted into equity shares, the company saves interest expense on those debentures. Hence, for Diluted EPS, the interest expense saved (net of attributable tax effect) is added back to the net profit attributable to equity shareholders.
Medium NORMAL · AS 20 | Restatement of EPS | Comparative Figures
Delta Ltd reported Basic EPS of ₹15.00 for FY 2023-24 (WANES was 1,000,000 shares). On 1st July 2024, Delta Ltd issued 1 bonus share for every 1 existing share held (1:1 bonus issue). What is the restated Basic EPS for FY 2023-24 to be presented in the comparative column of FY 2024-25 financial statements?
A. ₹15.00
B. ₹7.50 ✔
C. ₹30.00
D. ₹10.00
Explanation: Under AS 20, if bonus shares are issued, the Basic EPS for all prior periods presented must be restated. Restated WANES for FY 2023-24 = 1,000,000 * 2 = 2,000,000 shares. Restated EPS = Original EPS / 2 = ₹15.00 / 2 = ₹7.50.
Medium NORMAL · AS 24 | Initial Disclosure Event | Timing
On 15th December 2024, the Board of Directors of Apex Ltd approved a detailed formal plan to dispose of its Fertilizer Division. On 20th January 2025, a formal public announcement of the plan was made. On 10th February 2025, a binding sale agreement was signed. What is the date of the Initial Disclosure Event under AS 24?
A. 15th December 2024
B. 20th January 2025 ✔
C. 10th February 2025
D. 31st March 2025
Explanation: Initial Disclosure Event is the EARLIER of (a) entering into a binding sale agreement (10th Feb 2025) or (b) board approval of detailed formal plan AND making a public announcement (20th Jan 2025). Approval plus announcement occurred on 20th January 2025, which is earlier than 10th February 2025.
Medium NORMAL · AS 24 | Cash Flow Statement | Disclosures
How should cash flows attributable to operating, investing, and financing activities of a discontinuing operation be presented under AS 24?
A. They should be combined with continuing operations without separate disclosure.
B. Net cash flows attributable to operating, investing, and financing activities of the discontinuing operation must be disclosed separately on the face of cash flow statement or in notes. ✔
C. Only operating cash flows of discontinuing operations need disclosure.
D. Cash flow disclosure is optional under AS 24.
Explanation: AS 24 requires disclosure of the net cash flows attributable to the operating, investing, and financing activities of the discontinuing operation either on the face of the cash flow statement or in the notes to financial statements.
Hard NORMAL · AS 1 | Accounting Policy Change | Unascertainable Future Impact
Company ABC changed its valuation of inventory from FIFO to Weighted Average Cost method. The change resulted in a decrease in current year profit by ₹8 Lakhs, but the effect on future years is not determinable. What is the appropriate disclosure requirement under AS 1?
A. Disclose only the change in policy without any monetary quantification.
B. Disclose the change in policy, reasons for change, current year impact of ₹8 Lakhs reduction in profit, and state that future impact is not determinable. ✔
C. No disclosure is needed since future impact is unknown.
D. Restate prior year financial statements to show Weighted Average Cost.
Explanation: Under AS 1, any change in accounting policy having a material effect must be disclosed along with monetary impact. If the effect on future periods is not ascertainable, that fact must be explicitly stated in the financial statements.
Hard NORMAL · AS 18 | Indirect Relationship | Associate
Holding Ltd owns 60% of Sub Ltd. Sub Ltd owns 40% of Assoc Ltd. Holding Ltd directly holds 10% of Assoc Ltd. How is Assoc Ltd related to Holding Ltd under AS 18?
A. Assoc Ltd is a Subsidiary of Holding Ltd.
B. Assoc Ltd is an Associate of Holding Ltd because Holding Ltd directly and indirectly controls/exercises significant influence over 50% voting power. ✔
C. Assoc Ltd is not a related party of Holding Ltd.
D. Assoc Ltd is a Joint Venture of Holding Ltd.
Explanation: Holding Ltd controls Sub Ltd (60%). Sub Ltd holds 40% in Assoc Ltd, so Sub Ltd has significant influence. Directly Holding Ltd has 10%. Combined effective voting influence/control over Assoc Ltd exceeds 20% (direct 10% + indirect 40% held via subsidiary = 50% voting power influence). Thus, Assoc Ltd is an associate/related party of Holding Ltd.
Hard NORMAL · AS 18 | KMP Relatives | Remuneration & Services
Alpha Ltd pays ₹60 Lakhs as KMP remuneration to its Managing Director Mr. R. During the year, Mr. R's spouse, Mrs. R, provides legal consultancy services to Alpha Ltd worth ₹6 Lakhs. Mrs. R is an independent professional. How should this be disclosed under AS 18 in Alpha Ltd's financial statements?
A. No disclosure required for Mrs. R because legal services were provided on arm's length basis.
B. Both KMP remuneration of Mr. R and the transaction with Mrs. R (relative of KMP) must be disclosed as related party transactions. ✔
C. Only Mr. R's remuneration needs disclosure; transactions with relatives are exempt if under ₹10 Lakhs.
D. Aggregate disclosure of ₹66 Lakhs as KMP remuneration without splitting.
Explanation: Under AS 18, KMP and their relatives are related parties. Both remuneration paid to KMP and commercial transactions with relatives of KMP must be disclosed, regardless of whether they are at arm's length.
Hard NORMAL · AS 20 | Rights Issue | TERP Calculation
Zeta Ltd had 1,000,000 equity shares outstanding on 1st April 2024. On 1st July 2024, it made a Rights Issue in the ratio of 1:4 (1 new share for every 4 shares held) at an issue price of ₹20 per share. The fair value of one equity share immediately prior to the exercise of rights was ₹30. What is the Theoretical Ex-Rights Price (TERP) per share under AS 20?
A. ₹25.00
B. ₹28.00 ✔
C. ₹24.00
D. ₹22.50
Explanation: TERP = [(Fair value of shares prior to rights * No. of shares prior) + (Rights issue price * No. of rights shares)] / Total shares after rights issue. TERP = [(4 * ₹30) + (1 * ₹20)] / (4 + 1) = (120 + 20) / 5 = ₹140 / 5 = ₹28.00.
Hard NORMAL · AS 20 | Diluted EPS | Convertible Debentures
Omega Ltd reported Net Profit after tax of ₹50,000,000 for FY 2024-25 and has 5,000,000 equity shares of ₹10 each. It has 100,000 10% Convertible Debentures of ₹100 each outstanding, each debenture convertible into 2 equity shares. Tax rate is 30%. What is the Diluted EPS under AS 20?
A. ₹9.62
B. ₹9.75 ✔
C. ₹10.00
D. ₹9.50
Explanation: Basic EPS = ₹50,000,000 / 5,000,000 = ₹10.00. Interest saved net of tax = 100,000 * 100 * 10% * (1 - 0.30) = ₹700,000. Adjusted Profit = 50,000,000 + 700,000 = ₹50,700,000. Dilutive shares = 100,000 * 2 = 200,000 shares. Diluted WANES = 5,000,000 + 200,000 = 5,200,000. Diluted EPS = ₹50,700,000 / 5,200,000 = ₹9.75.
Hard NORMAL · AS 20 | Options | Dilutive Potential Shares
A company has 100,000 stock options outstanding exercisable at ₹40 per share. The average fair value of one equity share during the year was ₹50. Under AS 20, what is the incremental number of dilutive potential equity shares to be added to WANES for calculating Diluted EPS?
A. 100,000 shares
B. 80,000 shares
C. 20,000 shares ✔
D. 50,000 shares
Explanation: Number of shares issued for full consideration = (100,000 * ₹40) / ₹50 = 80,000 shares. Incremental free/dilutive shares = Total options - Shares for consideration = 100,000 - 80,000 = 20,000 shares [or 100,000 * (1 - 40/50) = 20,000 shares].
Hard NORMAL · AS 24 | Discontinuing Operation Scope | Asset Disposal
An enterprise sells its idle manufacturing equipment representing 15% of total plant assets from its ongoing main operating unit. The equipment sale is completed in a single deal. Does this transaction qualify as a Discontinuing Operation under AS 24?
A. Yes, because it represents a disposal of a significant portion of assets pursuant to a single plan.
B. No, because selling individual assets without disposing of a major line of business or geographical segment does not satisfy AS 24 definition. ✔
C. Yes, provided the revenue from the equipment is disclosed separately.
D. No, because AS 24 applies only to statutory mergers and amalgamations.
Explanation: AS 24 explicitly clarifies that disposal of individual assets or routine phasing out of products/machinery within an ongoing major line of business does not constitute a discontinuing operation unless it represents a separate major line of business or geographical area.
Hard NORMAL · AS 24 | Subsequent Disclosures | Reporting Requirements
If a discontinuing operation continues operations into the next financial year before final completion, what disclosure is required under AS 24 in subsequent period financial statements?
A. No further disclosures required once initial disclosure event occurred in prior year.
B. Disclosures must be updated in subsequent periods including description of significant changes in the plan, cash flows, and pre-tax profit/loss until completion. ✔
C. The entire operation must be reclassified back to continuing operations.
D. Only the total realized cash consideration needs disclosure.
Explanation: AS 24 mandates that for a discontinuing operation, disclosures must continue in financial statements for subsequent periods until the completion of the disposal plan, including updates on any significant changes in the amounts or timing of cash flows/proceeds.
Hard NORMAL · AS 20 | Diluted EPS | Sequential Dilution Test
Company X has Net Profit of ₹1,000,000 and 100,000 equity shares (Basic EPS = ₹10). It has 10,000 12% Convertible Debentures of ₹100 each (each convertible into 1 share; interest net of tax = ₹8,400) and 5,000 15% Convertible Preference Shares of ₹100 each (dividend = ₹75,000, each convertible into 10 shares). Which potential equity shares are dilutive?
A. Both Convertible Debentures and Convertible Preference Shares are dilutive.
B. Only Convertible Debentures are dilutive (incremental EPS = ₹0.84), while Convertible Preference Shares are anti-dilutive (incremental EPS = ₹1.50). Both are dilutive relative to Basic EPS ₹10, but tested in sequence.
C. Convertible Debentures (incremental EPS ₹0.84) and Convertible Preference Shares (incremental EPS ₹1.50) are both dilutive since their incremental EPS is below basic EPS of ₹10. ✔
D. Neither is dilutive.
Explanation: Incremental EPS of Convertible Debentures = ₹8,400 / 10,000 = ₹0.84. Incremental EPS of Convertible Preference Shares = ₹75,000 / 50,000 = ₹1.50. Since both incremental EPS values (₹0.84 and ₹1.50) are lower than Basic EPS (₹10), both are dilutive potential equity shares when tested individually and sequentially.
CASE SCENARIO: Apex Ltd is preparing its financial statements for the year ended 31st March 2025. On 1st April 2024, the company had 1,000,000 equity shares of ₹10 each outstanding. Net profit attributable to equity shareholders for FY 2024-25 is ₹60,000,000. During the year, the following corporate transactions occurred: 1. On 1st July 2024, Apex Ltd issued rights shares to existing shareholders in the ratio of 1:4 (1 new share for every 4 held) at an issue price of ₹40 per share. The fair value of one equity share immediately prior to the exercise of rights on 1st July 2024 was ₹50. 2. Apex Ltd had 100,000 stock options outstanding throughout the year, exercisable at ₹30 per share. The average fair value per equity share during FY 2024-25 was ₹50. 3. On 1st October 2024, the company issued 50,000 10% Convertible Debentures of ₹100 each. Each debenture is convertible into 2 equity shares. Applicable tax rate is 30%.
Hard SCENARIO · AS 20 | Rights Issue | TERP
What is the Theoretical Ex-Rights Price (TERP) per share and the rights adjustment factor for Apex Ltd under AS 20?
A. TERP = ₹48.00; Adjustment Factor = 1.0417 (or 25/24) ✔
B. TERP = ₹45.00; Adjustment Factor = 1.1111
C. TERP = ₹40.00; Adjustment Factor = 1.2500
D. TERP = ₹50.00; Adjustment Factor = 1.0000
Explanation: TERP = [(4 * ₹50) + (1 * ₹40)] / 5 = (200 + 40) / 5 = ₹48.00. Rights Adjustment Factor = Fair Value prior to rights / TERP = 50 / 48 = 1.041667 (or 25/24).
Hard SCENARIO · AS 20 | WANES | Rights Issue Adjustment
What is the Weighted Average Number of Equity Shares (WANES) for calculating Basic EPS for FY 2024-25 under AS 20?
A. 1,197,917 shares ✔
B. 1,250,000 shares
C. 1,187,500 shares
D. 1,000,000 shares
Explanation: WANES = [1,000,000 * (25/24) * 3/12] + [1,250,000 * 9/12] = 260,416.67 + 937,500 = 1,197,916.67 (approx 1,197,917 shares).
Medium SCENARIO · AS 20 | Stock Options | Dilutive Shares
What is the number of incremental dilutive potential equity shares arising from the stock options to be included in Diluted EPS calculation under AS 20?
A. 40,000 shares ✔
B. 100,000 shares
C. 60,000 shares
D. 20,000 shares
Explanation: Options dilutive shares = Total options * (1 - Exercise Price / Fair Value) = 100,000 * (1 - 30/50) = 100,000 * 0.40 = 40,000 shares.
Hard SCENARIO · AS 20 | Diluted EPS | Comprehensive Calculation
What is the Diluted Earnings Per Share (DEPS) of Apex Ltd for FY 2024-25 under AS 20?
A. ₹46.72 ✔
B. ₹50.09
C. ₹48.61
D. ₹45.10
Explanation: Basic EPS = ₹60,000,000 / 1,197,917 = ₹50.09. Convertible Debentures interest saved net of tax (for 6 months from 1st Oct) = 50,000 * 100 * 10% * 6/12 * (1 - 0.30) = ₹175,000. Incremental shares from debentures weighted for 6 months = (50,000 * 2) * 6/12 = 50,000 shares. Total Diluted WANES = 1,197,917 (Basic) + 40,000 (Options) + 50,000 (Debentures) = 1,287,917 shares. Adjusted Profit = 60,000,000 + 175,000 = ₹60,175,000. Diluted EPS = 60,175,000 / 1,287,917 = ₹46.72.
CASE SCENARIO: Vibrant Infra Ltd (VIL) is an unlisted public company. For the financial year ended 31st March 2025, the accountant is reviewing the following relationships and transactions for compliance with AS 18 (Related Party Disclosures): 1. Mr. Vijay is the Managing Director of VIL. VIL paid him a salary of ₹1.2 Crores. Mr. Vijay's brother, Mr. Ajay, supplied raw materials worth ₹40 Lakhs to VIL at prevailing market rates. 2. VIL holds 25% voting power in Solar Tech Ltd (STL). VIL had no commercial transactions with STL during FY 2024-25. 3. VIL holds 60% equity shares in Metro Projects Ltd (MPL). VIL had zero business transactions with MPL during FY 2024-25. 4. State Bank of India (SBI) provided a term loan of ₹50 Crores to VIL with standard financial covenants. VIL also purchased machinery worth ₹2 Crores from Bharat Heavy Electricals Ltd (BHEL), a state-controlled enterprise.
Medium SCENARIO · AS 18 | KMP Relatives | Arm's Length Exemption
How should the raw material supply transaction with Mr. Ajay (brother of Managing Director Mr. Vijay) be disclosed in VIL's financial statements under AS 18?
A. Exempt from disclosure because the transaction was conducted at prevailing market rates (arm's length).
B. Must be disclosed as a related party transaction including the nature of relationship, description, and amount of ₹40 Lakhs. ✔
C. Disclosed only if the amount exceeds ₹1 Crore.
D. Merged with KMP remuneration of Mr. Vijay without separate disclosure.
Explanation: Under AS 18, relatives of Key Management Personnel are related parties. Transactions with related parties must be disclosed regardless of whether they are on an arm's length basis.
Hard SCENARIO · AS 18 | Significant Influence | Nil Transactions
Is VIL required to disclose its relationship with Solar Tech Ltd (STL) for FY 2024-25 under AS 18?
A. Yes, because holding 25% voting power creates significant influence.
B. No, because no transactions took place during the year and the relationship is only 'significant influence' (not control). ✔
C. Yes, disclosure of relationship name is mandatory even for significant influence without transactions.
D. No, because STL is an unlisted company.
Explanation: Under AS 18, when NO transactions take place during the financial year, disclosures are required ONLY for relationships where CONTROL exists. Since VIL exercises significant influence (not control) over STL and no transactions took place, no disclosure is required.
Medium SCENARIO · AS 18 | Control Relationship | Nil Transaction Requirement
Is VIL required to disclose its relationship with Metro Projects Ltd (MPL) for FY 2024-25 under AS 18?
A. No, because no business transactions took place between VIL and MPL during the year.
B. Yes, because VIL exercises CONTROL (60% holding) over MPL, requiring disclosure of relationship name and nature even without transactions. ✔
C. Disclosure is optional at management's discretion.
D. Disclose only in the Director's Report, not in financial statements.
Explanation: AS 18 mandates that where CONTROL exists, disclosure of the related party relationship (name and nature) is mandatory irrespective of whether any transactions took place between the related parties during the year.
Easy SCENARIO · AS 18 | Exclusions | Provider of Finance
Which of the following entities is EXEMPT from being considered a related party of VIL under AS 18 based on the facts provided?
A. Mr. Vijay (Managing Director)
B. Metro Projects Ltd (Subsidiary)
C. State Bank of India (Provider of Finance) ✔
D. Mr. Ajay (Brother of KMP)
Explanation: AS 18 explicitly excludes providers of finance (such as banks) from being considered related parties merely by virtue of their normal dealings with an enterprise.
CASE SCENARIO: Zenith Consumer Products Ltd has two distinct operating divisions: Division A (Electronics) and Division B (Home Appliances). Both represent major lines of business and are operationally and financially distinguishable. During FY 2024-25, Zenith's management initiated a process regarding Division B: - On 15th September 2024, the Board of Directors approved a detailed formal plan to discontinue Division B by selling its assets piecemeal. - On 1st November 2024, Zenith issued a press release and formally notified stock exchanges about the board's decision to discontinue Division B. - On 15th January 2025, Zenith signed a binding sale agreement to dispose of 60% of Division B's assets to a buyer. - The remaining assets were sold in March 2025. For FY 2024-25, Division B reported revenue of ₹20 Crores, pre-tax operating loss of ₹3 Crores, and income tax benefit of ₹0.9 Crores.
Medium SCENARIO · AS 24 | Initial Disclosure Event | Timing
On which date did the 'Initial Disclosure Event' (IDE) occur for Division B under AS 24?
A. 15th September 2024
B. 1st November 2024 ✔
C. 15th January 2025
D. 31st March 2025
Explanation: Initial Disclosure Event is the EARLIER of (a) entering into binding sale agreement (15th Jan 2025) or (b) approval of detailed formal plan AND making a public announcement (1st Nov 2024). Hence, IDE occurred on 1st November 2024.
Medium SCENARIO · AS 24 | P&L Presentation | Discontinuing Disclosures
How should the pre-tax loss and tax benefit of Division B be presented in Zenith's financial statements for FY 2024-25 under AS 24?
A. Pre-tax loss of ₹3 Crores and tax benefit of ₹0.9 Crores attributable to the discontinuing operation must be disclosed on the face of profit & loss or in notes. ✔
B. Net loss of ₹2.1 Crores must be credited directly to General Reserve.
C. No disclosure is required until all assets are completely transferred.
D. Include Division B's results under Continuing Operations without separate breakdown.
Explanation: AS 24 mandates disclosure of the amount of pre-tax gain/loss recognized on the disposal of assets or settlement of liabilities attributable to discontinuing operation, and the related income tax expense/benefit.
Medium SCENARIO · AS 24 | Cash Flow Statement | Presentation
How should cash flows attributable to Division B be presented in the Cash Flow Statement of Zenith Ltd under AS 24?
A. Net cash flows from operating, investing, and financing activities of Division B must be disclosed separately on the face of Cash Flow Statement or in notes. ✔
B. Cash flows must be omitted from Cash Flow Statement since it is a discontinuing operation.
C. Only financing cash flows of Division B require disclosure.
D. Cash flows should be adjusted against capital reserves.
Explanation: AS 24 requires separate disclosure of net cash flows attributable to operating, investing, and financing activities of the discontinuing operation.
Hard SCENARIO · AS 24 | Scope Exclusion | Major Line of Business
If Zenith Ltd had sold only one idle manufacturing unit of Division B (which did not constitute a separate major line of business or geographical area), how would AS 24 apply?
A. AS 24 would fully apply because it is a disposal of plant assets.
B. AS 24 would NOT apply because disposal of an individual unit within an operating segment does not satisfy the definition of a discontinuing operation. ✔
C. AS 24 would apply only if the sale generated a capital loss.
D. AS 24 applies at management's discretion.
Explanation: AS 24 explicitly excludes from its scope the disposal of individual assets or components that do not represent a separate major line of business or geographical area of operations.
CASE SCENARIO: Nova Retail Ltd operates a chain of supermarkets. For the financial year ended 31st March 2025, the auditor identified the following matters regarding accounting policies: 1. Nova Retail changed its method of valuation of inventory from Weighted Average Cost method to FIFO method to achieve uniformity with its parent company. This change resulted in an increase in closing inventory and current period profit by ₹45 Lakhs. The financial impact on prior periods cannot be reasonably determined. 2. The company capitalized administrative overheads of ₹12 Lakhs into the cost of store fixtures, arguing that corporate management spent time supervising store setup. 3. Due to intense competition, Nova Retail's accumulated losses eroded its net worth by 80%. However, management secured a binding line of credit from promoters for 3 years and restructured store operations, expecting cash inflows.
Medium SCENARIO · AS 1 | Change in Accounting Policy | Disclosure
Under AS 1, is the change in inventory valuation method permissible, and how should it be disclosed?
A. Impermissible; inventory valuation methods can never be changed once chosen.
B. Permissible if it complies with AS 2 / AS 1 or statute; the change, reasons, and ₹45 Lakhs current period profit impact must be disclosed along with a note that prior period impact is undeterminable. ✔
C. Permissible only with prior approval from ICAI.
D. Permissible without disclosure if profit increases.
Explanation: A change in accounting policy is permissible if required by statute, for AS compliance, or for more appropriate presentation. Under AS 1, the impact (₹45 Lakhs profit increase) and reasons must be disclosed, and if past impacts are undeterminable, that fact must be stated.
Hard SCENARIO · AS 1 | Substance over Form | Prudence
Regarding the capitalization of administrative overheads into store fixtures, which principle under AS 1 and general AS principles is violated?
A. Prudence and Substance over Form, as general administrative overheads do not directly add to the location/condition of assets. ✔
B. Consistency Assumption.
C. Going Concern Assumption.
D. Accrual Assumption.
Explanation: Under AS 1 and asset valuation standards, administrative overheads that do not directly contribute to bringing assets to their present location and condition should be expensed. Capitalizing them distorts true financial position, violating Prudence and Substance over Form.
Hard SCENARIO · AS 1 | Going Concern | Fundamental Assumption
Regarding the fundamental accounting assumption of 'Going Concern' for Nova Retail Ltd, what is the reporting requirement under AS 1?
A. Going concern assumption must be treated as failed and liquidation basis must be adopted mandatory.
B. If management reasonably assesses that going concern is valid (supported by promoter credit line), no disclosure of non-going concern is required, but disclosure of material uncertainties in notes may be necessary. ✔
C. Specific disclosure is mandatory stating that Going Concern IS followed.
D. The company must cease financial reporting.
Explanation: Under AS 1, fundamental accounting assumptions are assumed to be followed. If management concludes going concern remains valid despite distress (due to credit support), specific disclosure that fundamental assumption is NOT followed is not required, though material uncertainty disclosures may be made.
Easy SCENARIO · AS 1 | Policy Selection Criteria | Core Principles
What are the three primary considerations prescribed by AS 1 for the selection and application of accounting policies?
A. Prudence, Substance over Form, and Materiality ✔
B. Relevance, Reliability, and Comparability
C. Going Concern, Consistency, and Accrual
D. Historical Cost, Fair Value, and Liquidation Value
Explanation: AS 1 explicitly states that the major considerations governing the selection and application of accounting policies are: (a) Prudence, (b) Substance over Form, and (c) Materiality.
CASE SCENARIO: Orion Enterprises Ltd had 200,000 equity shares of ₹10 each outstanding on 1st April 2024. Profit after tax attributable to equity shareholders for FY 2024-25 is ₹40,000,000. During FY 2024-25, Orion engaged in the following events: 1. On 1st October 2024, Orion issued 100,000 equity shares for cash at market price. 2. On 1st January 2025, Orion declared a bonus issue of 1 equity share for every 3 equity shares held as on that date. 3. Mr. K is the Chief Financial Officer (CFO) of Orion. During the year, Orion paid ₹30 Lakhs as CFO salary to Mr. K. Orion also paid ₹15 Lakhs as professional fee to a legal firm in which Mr. K's son holds a 50% partnership interest. Comparative financial figures for FY 2023-24 showed Net Profit of ₹30,000,000 and 200,000 equity shares.
Hard SCENARIO · AS 20 | WANES Calculation | Bonus & Cash Issue
What is the Weighted Average Number of Equity Shares (WANES) for FY 2024-25 for calculating Basic EPS under AS 20?
A. 333,333 shares ✔
B. 400,000 shares
C. 250,000 shares
D. 300,000 shares
Explanation: Original 200k + Bonus 1:3 on 200k (66.667k) = 266,667 shares for 12 months = 266,667. Issued on 1st Oct 100k + Bonus 1:3 on 100k (33.333k) = 133,333 shares for 6 months = 66,667. Total WANES = 266,667 + 66,667 = 333,334 (or 333,333) shares.
Medium SCENARIO · AS 20 | Comparative EPS Restatement | Bonus Issue
What is the restated Basic EPS for the comparative year FY 2023-24 under AS 20?
A. ₹112.50 ✔
B. ₹150.00
C. ₹75.00
D. ₹100.00
Explanation: Original WANES FY 23-24 = 200,000 shares. Bonus issue ratio 1:3 adds 66,667 bonus shares retrospectively. Restated WANES = 266,667 shares. Restated EPS = ₹30,000,000 / 266,667 = ₹112.50.
Medium SCENARIO · AS 20 | Basic EPS | Calculation
What is the Basic EPS of Orion Enterprises Ltd for FY 2024-25 under AS 20?
A. ₹120.00 ✔
B. ₹100.00
C. ₹133.33
D. ₹160.00
Explanation: Basic EPS FY 2024-25 = Net Profit / WANES = ₹40,000,000 / 333,333 shares = ₹120.00.
Hard SCENARIO · AS 18 | KMP Relative Enterprise | Disclosure
How should the payment of ₹15 Lakhs to the legal firm (where CFO Mr. K's son is a partner) be disclosed under AS 18?
A. No disclosure required as it was paid to a partnership firm, not directly to Mr. K.
B. Must be disclosed as a related party transaction with a relative of KMP/enterprise influenced by relative of KMP. ✔
C. Exempt from disclosure because it is a professional fee.
D. Aggregate with CFO salary and disclose total as ₹45 Lakhs without breakup.
Explanation: Under AS 18, KMP and their relatives are related parties. An enterprise over which a KMP or their relative exercises significant influence (e.g., 50% partner) is a related party. Hence, transaction details of ₹15 Lakhs must be disclosed.

Paper 1: Advanced Accounting · Module 2 · Chapter 5:

Accounts — 55 rows
Easy NORMAL · AS 2 | Inventories | Raw Material Valuation
Under AS 2 'Valuation of Inventories', raw materials and other supplies held for use in the production of inventories are NOT written down below cost if:
A. The finished products in which they will be incorporated are expected to be sold at or above cost. ✔
B. The net realizable value of raw materials is greater than their replacement cost.
C. The fair value of the finished product is less than its cost of production.
D. The raw materials have been held in stock for less than six months.
Explanation: As per AS 2, materials and other supplies held for use in the production of inventories are not written down below cost if the finished products in which they will be incorporated are expected to be sold at or above cost. Raw materials are written down to replacement cost only when there has been a decline in the price of materials and it is estimated that the cost of finished products will exceed net realizable value.
Medium NORMAL · AS 2 | Inventories | Replacement Cost
A company holds 1,000 units of raw material purchased at ₹ 200 per unit. The replacement cost of raw material is ₹ 150 per unit. The finished product requires 1 unit of raw material with an additional conversion cost of ₹ 100 per unit. The estimated selling price of the finished product is ₹ 280 per unit, and selling expenses are ₹ 10 per unit. At what total value should the raw material inventory be carried?
A. ₹ 1,50,000 ✔
B. ₹ 2,00,000
C. ₹ 1,70,000
D. ₹ 1,80,000
Explanation: The Net Realizable Value (NRV) of the finished product is ₹ 270 (₹ 280 - ₹ 10). The total cost to produce the finished product is ₹ 300 (₹ 200 raw material + ₹ 100 conversion). Since the finished product is expected to be sold below cost (NRV ₹ 270 < Cost ₹ 300), the raw material must be written down to its replacement cost of ₹ 150 per unit. Total raw material valuation = 1,000 units × ₹ 150 = ₹ 1,50,000.
Easy NORMAL · AS 2 | Inventories | Cost Formulas
Which of the following cost formulas is explicitly NOT permitted under AS 2 'Valuation of Inventories' for determining the cost of inventories?
A. Last-In, First-Out (LIFO) formula ✔
B. First-In, First-Out (FIFO) formula
C. Weighted Average Cost formula
D. Specific Identification Method
Explanation: AS 2 explicitly prohibits the use of the LIFO (Last-In, First-Out) formula because it often results in inventories being recognized in the balance sheet at amounts far removed from recent cost levels. Permitted cost formulas under AS 2 include FIFO, Weighted Average, and Specific Identification Method.
Medium NORMAL · AS 10 | PPE | Revaluation Model
Under AS 10 'Property, Plant and Equipment', when an item of PPE is revalued upwards for the first time, how should the increase in carrying amount be recognized?
A. Credited directly to Revaluation Surplus under Reserve and Surplus ✔
B. Credited to the Profit and Loss Account as Extraordinary Income
C. Credited to General Reserve
D. Deducted from the accumulated depreciation account
Explanation: Under AS 10, when an asset's carrying amount is increased as a result of a revaluation for the first time, the increase should be credited directly to owners' interests under the heading of Revaluation Surplus. If it reverses a revaluation decrease of the same asset previously recognized in profit or loss, it is recognized in profit or loss to that extent.
Easy NORMAL · AS 10 | PPE | Initial Recognition
Which of the following costs should be EXCLUDED from the initial cost of an item of Property, Plant and Equipment under AS 10?
A. Initial operating losses incurred before the asset achieves planned performance ✔
B. Costs of site preparation
C. Initial delivery and handling costs
D. Professional fees arising directly from bringing the asset to its working condition
Explanation: AS 10 specifically requires initial operating losses, such as those incurred while demand for the asset's output builds up, to be excluded from the carrying amount of an item of PPE. Site preparation, initial delivery, and direct professional fees are directly attributable costs and must be capitalized.
Medium NORMAL · AS 10 | PPE | Component Accounting
An entity purchases a chemical plant for ₹ 50,00,000. Under AS 10, the cost includes a major overhauling component required every 3 years costing ₹ 6,00,000. After 3 years, the overhaul is performed at a cost of ₹ 7,50,000. How should this new overhaul cost be accounted for?
A. Capitalized as a replacement component in PPE, derecognizing the remaining carrying amount of the old overhaul component ✔
B. Charged entirely as a routine repair and maintenance expense in Profit and Loss
C. Adjusted against the Revaluation Surplus balance
D. Deferred and amortized over the remaining life of the main chemical plant
Explanation: AS 10 requires component accounting for major inspections or overhauls. When each major inspection/overhaul is performed, its cost is recognized in the carrying amount of the item of PPE as a replacement if recognition criteria are satisfied, and any remaining carrying amount of the cost of the previous overhaul is derecognized.
Hard NORMAL · AS 10 | PPE | Decommissioning Liability
Under AS 10, an entity measures an asset using the Revaluation Model. If a change in the estimated decommissioning liability reduces the liability, how is this reduction treated?
A. Added to/credited to Revaluation Surplus, except that it is recognized in Profit and Loss to the extent it reverses a revaluation deficit previously recognized in P&L. ✔
B. Recognized immediately in Profit and Loss as an exceptional gain in all circumstances.
C. Credited to a deferred revenue account and recognized over the remaining asset life.
D. Deducted directly from the opening Retained Earnings balance.
Explanation: Under AS 10 (Appendix I principles), for assets measured under the revaluation model, a reduction in the decommissioning liability is credited to Revaluation Surplus, except that it shall be recognized in profit or loss to the extent that it reverses a revaluation deficit on the asset that was previously recognized in profit or loss.
Easy NORMAL · AS 13 | Investments | Classification
Under AS 13 'Accounting for Investments', a 'Current Investment' is defined as an investment that by its nature is readily realizable and is intended to be held for:
A. Not more than one year from the date on which such investment is made. ✔
B. Not more than six months from the date of the balance sheet.
C. Not more than two years from the date on which such investment is made.
D. Indefinite period depending on market fluctuations.
Explanation: As per AS 13, a current investment is an investment that is by its nature readily realizable and is intended to be held for not more than one year from the date on which such investment is made.
Easy NORMAL · AS 13 | Investments | Current Investments Valuation
How are Current Investments valued at the Balance Sheet date as per AS 13?
A. Lower of cost and fair value / net realizable value determined on an individual investment basis or category basis ✔
B. At cost less permanent diminution only
C. Always at fair value with gains taken to profit and loss
D. At lower of cost and net realizable value determined strictly on aggregate portfolio basis only
Explanation: Under AS 13, current investments are carried in the financial statements at lower of cost and fair value (or net realizable value). The valuation is determined either on an individual investment basis or by category of investment, but not on an overall aggregate basis.
Medium NORMAL · AS 13 | Investments | Reclassification
When an investment is reclassified from Long-Term Investments to Current Investments under AS 13, the transfer should be made at:
A. Lower of cost and carrying amount at the date of transfer ✔
B. Fair value at the date of transfer with difference credited to capital reserve
C. Cost irrespective of market value
D. Higher of cost and net realizable value
Explanation: AS 13 prescribes that where long-term investments are reclassified as current investments, transfers are made at the lower of cost and carrying amount at the date of transfer. If written down previously for permanent decline, that written-down carrying amount is compared with cost.
Hard NORMAL · AS 13 | Investments | Rights Issue
An investor purchases 1,000 equity shares of X Ltd. cum-right at ₹ 150 per share. Later, the company announces 1 right share for every 2 shares held at ₹ 80 per share. The investor sells all right entitlements in the market for ₹ 30 per right. If the ex-rights market price of the original shares does not fall below the cost, how should the ₹ 15,000 proceeds from sale of rights be treated under AS 13?
A. Credited to the Profit and Loss Statement ✔
B. Deducted from the cost of original investment in the Balance Sheet
C. Credited to Capital Reserve
D. Deferred as Unearned Income until original shares are sold
Explanation: As per AS 13, rights offer proceeds from the sale of right entitlements are generally credited to the Profit and Loss Statement. They are applied to reduce the carrying amount of investment only when the shares were purchased cum-right and the market value of shares after ex-rights falls below the purchase cost.
Easy NORMAL · AS 16 | Borrowing Costs | Qualifying Asset
Under AS 16 'Borrowing Costs', what is a 'qualifying asset'?
A. An asset that necessarily takes a substantial period of time to get ready for its intended use or sale ✔
B. Any fixed asset purchased on credit terms exceeding 30 days
C. An asset that is funded 100% by specific bank loans
D. An asset whose useful life exceeds 10 accounting periods
Explanation: AS 16 defines a qualifying asset as an asset that necessarily takes a substantial period of time to get ready for its intended use or sale. What constitutes a substantial period depends on the facts and circumstances (ordinarily 12 months unless a shorter duration can be justified).
Medium NORMAL · AS 16 | Borrowing Costs | Capitalization Rate
Entity A has general borrowings of ₹ 10,00,000 at 10% p.a. and ₹ 20,00,000 at 13% p.a. during the year. It uses ₹ 6,00,000 out of general borrowings for the construction of a qualifying asset. What is the weighted average capitalization rate for borrowing costs?
A. 12.00% ✔
B. 11.50%
C. 10.00%
D. 13.00%
Explanation: Weighted average rate = Total Interest on General Borrowings / Total General Borrowings = [(₹ 10,00,000 × 10%) + (₹ 20,00,000 × 13%)] / (₹ 10,00,000 + ₹ 20,00,000) = (1,00,000 + 2,60,000) / 30,00,000 = ₹ 3,60,000 / ₹ 30,00,000 = 12.00%.
Medium NORMAL · AS 16 | Borrowing Costs | Suspension of Capitalization
According to AS 16, capitalization of borrowing costs should be suspended during:
A. Extended periods in which active development of the qualifying asset is interrupted ✔
B. Brief periods when substantial technical and administrative work is taking place
C. Temporary delays that are a necessary part of the process of getting an asset ready for use
D. The entire construction period if general interest rates increase
Explanation: Under AS 16, capitalization of borrowing costs should be suspended during extended periods in which active development is interrupted. However, capitalization is not suspended during a period when substantial technical and administrative work is being carried out or when a temporary delay is a necessary part of the process.
Easy NORMAL · AS 16 | Borrowing Costs | Specific Borrowings
Under AS 16, any income earned on the temporary investment of specific borrowings raised for a qualifying asset prior to its expenditure should be:
A. Deducted from the borrowing costs eligible for capitalization ✔
B. Recognized as income in the Profit and Loss Statement
C. Credited directly to Capital Reserve
D. Ignored for accounting purposes
Explanation: AS 16 states that to the extent funds are borrowed specifically for the purpose of obtaining a qualifying asset, the amount of borrowing costs eligible for capitalization should be determined as actual borrowing costs incurred on that borrowing during the period less any income on temporary investment of those borrowings.
Medium NORMAL · AS 19 | Leases | Finance Lease Classification
Under AS 19 'Leases', which of the following scenarios indicates that a lease is classified as a Finance Lease?
A. At the inception of the lease, the present value of minimum lease payments substantially covers the initial fair value of the leased asset. ✔
B. The lease term is for 10% of the economic life of the asset.
C. The lessee can cancel the lease at any time without paying any penalty.
D. Gains or losses from the fluctuation in the fair value of the residual fall to the lessor.
Explanation: AS 19 provides indicators of a finance lease, one of which is that at the inception of the lease, the present value of the minimum lease payments amounts to at least substantially all of the fair value of the leased asset.
Medium NORMAL · AS 19 | Leases | Unearned Finance Income
In a finance lease transaction, the lessor defines 'Unearned Finance Income' as the difference between:
A. Gross investment in the lease and the net investment in the lease ✔
B. Present value of minimum lease payments and fair value of the asset
C. Minimum lease payments and residual value
D. Lease receipts and initial direct costs incurred by lessor
Explanation: Under AS 19, Unearned Finance Income is defined as the difference between the gross investment in the lease and the net investment in the lease. Gross investment is aggregate of minimum lease payments from lessor perspective plus unguaranteed residual value.
Easy NORMAL · AS 19 | Leases | Operating Lease Costs
How should initial direct costs incurred by a lessee in respect of an operating lease be treated under AS 19?
A. Recognized as an expense in the Profit and Loss Statement in the period in which they are incurred ✔
B. Capitalized as part of the carrying amount of the leased asset
C. Amortized strictly over the economic life of the asset
D. Deducted from the liability for lease payments
Explanation: In an operating lease, initial direct costs incurred by the lessee (such as legal fees, negotiation costs) are recognized as an immediate expense in the Profit and Loss Statement in the period in which they are incurred.
Hard NORMAL · AS 19 | Leases | Sale and Leaseback
If a sale and leaseback transaction results in a Finance Lease, any excess of sale proceeds over the carrying amount of the asset should be:
A. Deferred and amortized by the seller-lessee over the lease term in proportion to the depreciation of the leased asset ✔
B. Recognized immediately as profit in the Profit and Loss Account in the year of sale
C. Credited to General Reserve immediately
D. Adjusted against the fair value of the asset in the books of the lessor
Explanation: Under AS 19, if a sale and leaseback transaction results in a finance lease, any excess or deficiency of sales proceeds over the carrying amount should not be immediately recognized as income or loss. Instead, it should be deferred and amortized over the lease term in proportion to the depreciation of the leased asset.
Medium NORMAL · AS 26 | Intangible Assets | Research Phase
Under AS 26 'Intangible Assets', expenditure incurred on the 'Research Phase' of an internal project must be:
A. Recognized as an expense when it is incurred ✔
B. Capitalized as an intangible asset if future economic benefits are probable
C. Deferred and written off over a period of 5 years
D. Included in the cost of inventory as work-in-progress
Explanation: Under AS 26, no intangible asset arising from research (or from the research phase of an internal project) should be recognized. Expenditure on research should be recognized as an expense when it is incurred because an entity cannot demonstrate that an intangible asset exists that will generate future economic benefits.
Medium NORMAL · AS 26 | Intangible Assets | Amortization Period
As per AS 26, there is a rebuttable presumption that the useful life of an intangible asset will NOT exceed how many years from the date when the asset is available for use?
A. 10 years ✔
B. 5 years
C. 20 years
D. 15 years
Explanation: AS 26 includes a rebuttable presumption that the useful life of an intangible asset will not exceed 10 years from the date when the asset is available for use.
Easy NORMAL · AS 26 | Intangible Assets | Internally Generated Assets
Which of the following internally generated items CANNOT be recognized as an Intangible Asset under AS 26?
A. Internally generated brands, mastheads, publishing titles, and customer lists ✔
B. Purchased software licenses for internal accounting system
C. Patents acquired through business combinations
D. Copyrights acquired from a third party
Explanation: AS 26 explicitly states that internally generated brands, mastheads, publishing titles, customer lists, and items similar in substance should not be recognized as intangible assets because expenditures on them cannot be distinguished from the cost of developing the business as a whole.
Easy NORMAL · AS 28 | Impairment | Recoverable Amount
