Under AS 28 'Impairment of Assets', the 'Recoverable Amount' of an asset is defined as the HIGHER of:
A. Net Selling Price and its Value in Use ✔
B. Carrying Amount and Replacement Cost
C. Historical Cost and Net Realizable Value
D. Fair Value and Salvage Value
Explanation: AS 28 defines Recoverable Amount as the higher of an asset's net selling price and its value in use. If either of these amounts exceeds the carrying amount, the asset is not impaired.
Medium NORMAL · AS 28 | Impairment | Value in Use
'Value in Use' of an asset under AS 28 represents:
A. The present value of estimated future cash flows expected to arise from the continuing use of an asset and from its disposal at the end of its useful life ✔
B. The net amount obtainable from the sale of an asset in an arm's length transaction between knowledgeable, willing parties
C. The current replacement cost minus cumulative depreciation
D. The liquidation value of the asset in an forced transaction
Explanation: AS 28 defines Value in Use as the present value of estimated future cash flows expected to arise from the continuing use of an asset and from its disposal at the end of its useful life.
Hard NORMAL · AS 28 | Impairment | CGU Allocation
When an impairment loss is recognized for a Cash-Generating Unit (CGU) under AS 28, how is the impairment loss allocated?
A. First, to reduce the carrying amount of any goodwill allocated to the CGU, and then to other assets of the CGU pro-rata based on carrying amount. ✔
B. Equally across all assets of the CGU regardless of carrying amount.
C. First to non-current tangible assets, then to goodwill, and finally to current assets.
D. Pro-rata to all assets based on their original historical cost.
Explanation: AS 28 requires that an impairment loss for a CGU be allocated first to reduce the carrying amount of any goodwill allocated to the CGU, and then to the other assets of the unit pro-rata on the basis of the carrying amount of each asset in the unit.
Hard NORMAL · AS 28 | Impairment | Reversal of Impairment
Under AS 28, can an impairment loss recognized for Goodwill be reversed in a subsequent period?
A. No, an impairment loss recognized for Goodwill should NEVER be reversed in a subsequent period. ✔
B. Yes, if the economic indicators show a significant recovery in market value.
C. Yes, provided the reversal is approved by the Board of Directors.
D. Yes, up to the maximum of 50% of the original impairment loss.
Explanation: AS 28 strictly states that an impairment loss recognized for goodwill should not be reversed in a subsequent period unless the impairment loss was caused by a specific external event of an exceptional nature that is not expected to recur and subsequent external events have occurred that reverse the effect of that event (in practice, ICAI syllabus standard rule is strictly prohibited/non-reversible).
Medium NORMAL · AS 10 | PPE | Trial Run Proceeds
Under AS 10, how should net proceeds from selling items produced while bringing an item of PPE to its location and condition (such as samples produced when testing machinery) be treated?
A. Deducted from the directly attributable costs of PPE before capitalization ✔
B. Recognized as revenue in the Profit and Loss Account
C. Credited to Revaluation Reserve
D. Deducted from administrative overheads
Explanation: Under AS 10, testing costs are directly attributable costs. Any net proceeds from selling items produced while bringing the asset to its location and condition (such as test samples) are deducted from the cost of the asset.
Hard NORMAL · AS 16 | Borrowing Costs | Foreign Currency Borrowings
Under AS 16, exchange differences arising from foreign currency borrowings used for acquiring a qualifying asset are treated as borrowing costs to the extent that:
A. They are regarded as an adjustment to interest costs (limit being the difference between foreign interest and domestic interest cost). ✔
B. 100% of the total exchange loss is always capitalized.
C. They exceed the principal amount borrowed.
D. They are recognized in the Foreign Currency Monetary Item Translation Difference Account (FCMITDA).
Explanation: Under AS 16, exchange differences arising from foreign currency borrowings are treated as borrowing costs to the extent that they are regarded as an adjustment to interest costs (calculated as the difference between interest on local borrowings vs foreign borrowings). Any excess exchange loss is expensed in Profit & Loss.
Hard NORMAL · AS 19 | Leases | Land and Building Split
Under AS 19, when a lease includes both land and building elements, how should an entity classify the lease of each element?
A. Land and building elements must be considered separately for lease classification unless title passes to lessee for land. ✔
B. The entire lease is always classified as finance lease because land has indefinite economic life.
C. The entire lease is always classified as operating lease because land cannot be depreciated.
D. The classification depends solely on the value of the building regardless of the land value.
Explanation: Under AS 19, land and building elements of a lease are considered separately for the purpose of lease classification. Since land normally has an indefinite economic life, a land lease is usually an operating lease unless title is expected to pass to the lessee.
Hard NORMAL · AS 26 | Intangible Assets | Website Development Costs
An entity spends ₹ 15,00,000 on developing an internal website purely for promoting and advertising its own products. How should this cost be treated as per the principles of AS 26?
A. Expensed immediately in Profit and Loss as advertising expenditure when incurred ✔
B. Capitalized as an Intangible Asset and amortized over 5 years
C. Capitalized under PPE as office equipment
D. Deferred and shown under Other Non-Current Assets
Explanation: Under AS 26 guidance, expenditure on an internal website developed solely or primarily for promoting and advertising an entity's own products and services cannot demonstrate that future economic benefits will flow directly. Hence, all such costs must be recognized as an expense in Profit & Loss when incurred.
CASE SCENARIO: Vedic Texfab Ltd. purchased a specialized textile processing plant on 1st April 2024. The invoice price was ₹ 80,00,000 (excluding trade discount of ₹ 2,00,000). Statutory import duties paid were ₹ 5,00,000 (non-refundable). Freight and handling charges amounted to ₹ 3,00,000. Site preparation costs incurred were ₹ 2,00,000. Architect design fees directly related to installation were ₹ 1,00,000. Initial operating losses incurred during the first month before reaching commercial capacity were ₹ 4,00,000. Trial run costs were ₹ 1,50,000 and net proceeds from sale of trial run sample output were ₹ 50,000. Present value of estimated decommissioning cost at the end of its 10-year useful life is ₹ 5,00,000.
Medium SCENARIO · AS 10 | PPE | Cost Calculation
What is the initial cost at which the plant should be capitalized in the books on 1st April 2024 under AS 10?
A. ₹ 95,00,000 ✔
B. ₹ 99,00,000
C. ₹ 90,00,000
D. ₹ 94,50,000
Explanation: Cost = Net Invoice (80,00,000 - 2,00,000 = 78,00,000) + Import duties (5,00,000) + Freight (3,00,000) + Site prep (2,00,000) + Architect fees (1,00,000) + Net trial run cost (1,50,000 - 50,000 = 1,00,000) + Decommissioning PV (5,00,000) = ₹ 95,00,000. Initial operating losses (4,00,000) are excluded under AS 10.
Medium SCENARIO · AS 10 | PPE | Revaluation Surplus
The company uses straight-line depreciation over 10 years with zero residual value. On 31st March 2026 (after 2 years), the revaluation model is adopted and market value is determined as ₹ 88,00,000. What amount should be credited to Revaluation Surplus on 31st March 2026?
A. ₹ 12,00,000 ✔
B. ₹ 8,00,000
C. ₹ 15,00,000
D. ₹ 10,00,000
Explanation: Carrying Amount on 31st March 2026 = ₹ 95,00,000 - (₹ 9,50,000 × 2) = ₹ 76,00,000. Revalued Amount = ₹ 88,00,000. Revaluation Surplus = ₹ 88,00,000 - ₹ 76,00,000 = ₹ 12,00,000.
Hard SCENARIO · AS 10 | PPE | Decommissioning Adjustment
On 1st April 2026 (beginning of Year 3), due to changes in discount rates, the present value of the estimated decommissioning liability is revised downwards by ₹ 1,60,000. Under AS 10 (Revaluation Model), how should this reduction be accounted for?
A. Credited to Revaluation Surplus, increasing it from ₹ 12,00,000 to ₹ 13,60,000 ✔
B. Credited to Profit and Loss Account as an exceptional income
C. Deducted from the carrying amount of the asset
D. Credited to General Reserve
Explanation: Under the revaluation model, changes in decommissioning liabilities are added to or deducted from the revaluation surplus. A reduction in liability increases the revaluation surplus from ₹ 12,00,000 to ₹ 13,60,000.
Hard SCENARIO · AS 10 | PPE | Revised Depreciation
What will be the revised annual depreciation expense for Year 3 (FY 2026-27) after accounting for the revaluation on 31st March 2026?
A. ₹ 11,00,000 ✔
B. ₹ 9,50,000
C. ₹ 10,80,000
D. ₹ 12,00,000
Explanation: Carrying amount on 31st March 2026 is ₹ 88,00,000. Remaining useful life is 8 years (10 - 2). Revised Depreciation = ₹ 88,00,000 / 8 years = ₹ 11,00,000.
CASE SCENARIO: Prism Infra Project Ltd. commenced the construction of a commercial shopping complex (a qualifying asset) on 1st April 2024. The project was completed on 31st March 2025. The details of borrowings during FY 2024-25 are: 1. Specific Bank Loan: ₹ 20,00,000 at 12% p.a. taken on 1st April 2024. Funds temporarily invested earned interest income of ₹ 30,000. 2. General Borrowings: - Loan A: ₹ 15,00,000 at 10% p.a. - Loan B: ₹ 25,00,000 at 14% p.a. Expenditures incurred on construction out of general borrowings were: - 1st October 2024: ₹ 12,00,000 - 1st January 2025: ₹ 8,00,000 Active construction was halted for 2 months (October and November 2024) due to an extended labor strike (non-routine interruption).
Medium SCENARIO · AS 16 | Borrowing Costs | Specific Borrowings
What is the net interest cost eligible for capitalization from the Specific Borrowing for FY 2024-25?
A. ₹ 2,10,000 ✔
B. ₹ 2,40,000
C. ₹ 2,70,000
D. ₹ 1,80,000
Explanation: Gross Interest on specific borrowing = ₹ 20,00,000 × 12% = ₹ 2,40,000. Net interest eligible = ₹ 2,40,000 - ₹ 30,00,000 interest income = ₹ 2,10,000.
Medium SCENARIO · AS 16 | Borrowing Costs | Capitalization Rate
What is the weighted average capitalization rate for General Borrowings of Prism Infra Project Ltd. for FY 2024-25?
A. 12.50% ✔
B. 12.00%
C. 11.50%
D. 13.00%
Explanation: Total interest on general borrowings = (15,00,000 × 10%) + (25,00,000 × 14%) = 1,50,000 + 3,50,000 = ₹ 5,00,000. Total general borrowings = ₹ 40,00,000. Weighted Average Rate = 5,00,000 / 40,00,000 = 12.50%.
Medium SCENARIO · AS 16 | Borrowing Costs | Suspension Period
Considering that active construction was suspended for 2 months due to an unexpected labor strike, how should borrowing costs for those 2 months be treated under AS 16?
A. Capitalization of borrowing costs must be suspended during those 2 months and interest expensed to Profit and Loss. ✔
B. Capitalization of borrowing costs continues without interruption because strikes are common.
C. Capitalization is permanently discontinued for the remaining project.
D. Interest for 2 months is added to General Reserve.
Explanation: AS 16 mandates that capitalization of borrowing costs should be suspended during extended periods in which active development is interrupted by non-routine delays such as labor strikes.
Hard SCENARIO · AS 16 | Borrowing Costs | General Borrowings Capitalization
What is the total borrowing cost from general borrowings to be capitalized for FY 2024-25 taking into account the suspension period?
A. ₹ 75,00,00 ✔
B. ₹ 1,00,000
C. ₹ 1,25,000
D. ₹ 50,000
Explanation: For ₹ 12,00,000 incurred on 1st Oct: Oct & Nov suspended. Active period = Dec to Mar (4 months). Interest = 12,00,000 × 12.5% × 4/12 = ₹ 50,000. For ₹ 8,00,000 incurred on 1st Jan: Active period = Jan to Mar (3 months). Interest = 8,00,000 × 12.5% × 3/12 = ₹ 25,000. Total general borrowing interest capitalized = 50,000 + 25,000 = ₹ 75,000.
CASE SCENARIO: Nivaan Investments Ltd. engaged in the following transactions regarding equity shares of Beta Ltd. during FY 2024-25: - 15th May 2024: Purchased 5,000 equity shares of Beta Ltd. (face value ₹ 10) cum-dividend at ₹ 120 per share. - 20th June 2024: Beta Ltd. declared and paid a dividend of ₹ 4 per share for FY 2023-24 (pre-acquisition period). - 10th August 2024: Beta Ltd. issued bonus shares in the ratio of 1:5 (1 bonus share for every 5 shares held). - 15th November 2024: Beta Ltd. issued rights shares in the ratio of 1:3 at ₹ 50 per share. Nivaan Ltd. subscribed to 50% of its rights entitlement and sold the remaining 50% rights entitlement in the market at ₹ 15 per right. - 31st March 2025: Nivaan Ltd. reclassified these shares from Long-Term Investments to Current Investments. Market price on 31st March 2025 was ₹ 80 per share.
Medium SCENARIO · AS 13 | Investments | Pre-acquisition Dividend
What is the total carrying cost of the original 5,000 shares immediately after receiving the pre-acquisition dividend on 20th June 2024?
A. ₹ 5,80,000 ✔
B. ₹ 6,00,000
C. ₹ 6,20,000
D. ₹ 5,60,000
Explanation: Initial cost = 5,000 × ₹ 120 = ₹ 6,00,000. Pre-acquisition dividend received = 5,000 × ₹ 4 = ₹ 20,000. Under AS 13, pre-acquisition dividend is deducted from the cost of investment. Carrying cost = 6,00,000 - 20,000 = ₹ 5,80,000.
Medium SCENARIO · AS 13 | Investments | Bonus and Rights Shares
How many total shares are held by Nivaan Ltd. after receiving bonus shares and subscribing to 50% of the rights shares?
A. 7,000 shares ✔
B. 6,000 shares
C. 8,000 shares
D. 6,500 shares
Explanation: Original = 5,000. Bonus (1:5) = 1,000. Total before rights = 6,000 shares. Rights entitlement (1:3) = 2,000 rights. Subscribed 50% = 1,000 shares. Total shares held = 6,000 + 1,000 = 7,000 shares.
Hard SCENARIO · AS 13 | Investments | Sale of Rights Entitlement
How should the sale of remaining 1,000 rights entitlements at ₹ 15 per right (total ₹ 15,000) be treated under AS 13?
A. Credited to the Profit and Loss Statement as income ✔
B. Deducted from the carrying cost of the investment
C. Credited to Capital Reserve Account
D. Added to the cost of rights shares subscribed
Explanation: Under AS 13, proceeds from the sale of right entitlements are credited to the Profit and Loss Statement unless the market value of original shares falls below cost ex-rights.
Hard SCENARIO · AS 13 | Investments | Reclassification Valuation
What is the carrying amount at which the investment in Beta Ltd. should be reclassified and shown as Current Investment on 31st March 2025?
A. ₹ 5,60,000 ✔
B. ₹ 6,30,000
C. ₹ 5,80,000
D. ₹ 6,00,000
Explanation: Total Cost of 7,000 shares = ₹ 5,80,000 + (1,000 rights × ₹ 50) = ₹ 6,30,000. Cost per share = 6,30,000 / 7,000 = ₹ 90. Market value = ₹ 80 per share. Reclassification is at lower of cost (₹ 90) and fair value (₹ 80). Valuation = 7,000 × ₹ 80 = ₹ 5,60,000.
CASE SCENARIO: On 1st April 2024, Aksat Leasing Ltd. (Lessor) leased equipment to Starline Services Ltd. (Lessee) for a period of 4 years. Key details of the lease agreement: - Fair value of equipment at inception: ₹ 20,00,000. - Annual lease payment payable at the end of each year: ₹ 6,50,000. - Guaranteed Residual Value (GRV) by Lessee: ₹ 1,00,000. - Unguaranteed Residual Value (URV): ₹ 50,000. - Implicit interest rate (IRR): 12% p.a. - PV Factors at 12%: Year 1 = 0.8929, Year 2 = 0.7972, Year 3 = 0.7118, Year 4 = 0.6355.
Medium SCENARIO · AS 19 | Leases | Gross Investment
What is the Gross Investment in the lease for Aksat Leasing Ltd. (Lessor)?
A. ₹ 27,50,000 ✔
B. ₹ 26,00,000
C. ₹ 20,00,000
D. ₹ 21,50,000
Explanation: Gross Investment in Lease = Total Lease Payments (4 × 6,50,000 = 26,00,000) + Guaranteed Residual Value (1,00,000) + Unguaranteed Residual Value (50,000) = ₹ 27,50,000.
Medium SCENARIO · AS 19 | Leases | Unearned Finance Income
What is the 'Unearned Finance Income' for Aksat Leasing Ltd. (Lessor) at inception of the lease?
A. ₹ 7,50,000 ✔
B. ₹ 6,00,000
C. ₹ 7,00,000
D. ₹ 5,50,000
Explanation: Unearned Finance Income = Gross Investment (₹ 27,50,000) - Net Investment (Fair Value ₹ 20,00,000) = ₹ 7,50,000.
Medium SCENARIO · AS 19 | Leases | Lessor Finance Income
What is the Finance Income to be recognized by Aksat Leasing Ltd. in its Profit and Loss Account for Year 1 (FY 2024-25)?
A. ₹ 2,40,000 ✔
B. ₹ 3,00,000
C. ₹ 1,80,000
D. ₹ 2,70,000
Explanation: Finance Income Year 1 = Net Investment at beginning (₹ 20,00,000) × IRR (12%) = ₹ 2,40,000.
Hard SCENARIO · AS 19 | Leases | Lessee Accounting
Starline Services Ltd. (Lessee) depreciates the asset on a straight-line basis over 4 years to its GRV of ₹ 1,00,000. At what initial carrying amount is the leased asset recorded by the lessee, and what is the depreciation for Year 1?
A. Asset recorded at ₹ 20,00,000 and Year 1 depreciation is ₹ 4,75,000 ✔
B. Asset recorded at ₹ 27,50,000 and Year 1 depreciation is ₹ 6,62,500
C. Asset recorded at ₹ 20,00,000 and Year 1 depreciation is ₹ 5,00,000
D. Asset recorded at ₹ 20,37,829 and Year 1 depreciation is ₹ 4,84,457
Explanation: Asset recorded at lower of PV of MLP and Fair Value = ₹ 20,00,000. Annual Depreciation = (₹ 20,00,000 - ₹ 1,00,000 GRV) / 4 years = ₹ 4,75,000.
CASE SCENARIO: Kuber Chemical Ltd. has a distinct Cash-Generating Unit (CGU) producing industrial solvents. On 31st March 2025, due to adverse regulatory changes, the company tests the CGU for impairment. The carrying amounts of the assets of the CGU before impairment testing are: - Goodwill: ₹ 10,00,000 - Factory Building: ₹ 30,00,000 - Plant & Machinery: ₹ 40,00,000 - Intangible Asset (Technical Know-how): ₹ 20,00,000 Total Carrying Amount of CGU = ₹ 1,00,00,000 (₹ 100 Lakhs). Additional Information: - Net Selling Price of the CGU as a whole is estimated at ₹ 65,00,000. - Value in Use of the CGU is calculated as ₹ 70,00,000. - The Net Selling Price of Technical Know-how individually is known to be ₹ 17,00,000.
Medium SCENARIO · AS 28 | Impairment | Recoverable Amount
What is the Recoverable Amount of the Cash-Generating Unit (CGU) on 31st March 2025?
A. ₹ 70,00,000 ✔
B. ₹ 65,00,000
C. ₹ 1,00,00,000
D. ₹ 30,00,000
Explanation: Recoverable Amount = Higher of Net Selling Price (₹ 65,00,000) and Value in Use (₹ 70,00,000) = ₹ 70,00,000.
Medium SCENARIO · AS 28 | Impairment | Total Impairment Loss
What is the total Impairment Loss to be recognized for the CGU on 31st March 2025?
A. ₹ 30,00,000 ✔
B. ₹ 35,00,000
C. ₹ 20,00,000
D. ₹ 10,00,000
Explanation: Impairment Loss = Carrying Amount (₹ 1,00,00,000) - Recoverable Amount (₹ 70,00,000) = ₹ 30,00,000.
Hard SCENARIO · AS 28 | Impairment | Individual Asset Limit
What is the maximum impairment loss that can be allocated to the Intangible Asset (Technical Know-how) under AS 28?
A. ₹ 3,00,000 ✔
B. ₹ 4,44,444
C. ₹ 6,00,000
D. ₹ 10,00,000
Explanation: Under AS 28, the carrying amount of an individual asset shall not be reduced below the highest of its net selling price (₹ 17,00,000), value in use, and zero. Since carrying amount is ₹ 20,00,000 and net selling price is ₹ 17,00,000, maximum impairment loss allocated to Technical Know-how is ₹ 3,00,000.
Hard SCENARIO · AS 28 | Impairment | Asset Carrying Value Allocation
What is the revised carrying amount of Plant & Machinery after the complete allocation of the CGU impairment loss on 31st March 2025?
A. ₹ 30,28,572 ✔
B. ₹ 31,11,111
C. ₹ 28,00,000
D. ₹ 32,00,000
Explanation: Total Loss = 30,00,000. Goodwill = 10,00,000. Remaining = 20,00,000. Initial pro-rata share for Plant = 20,00,000 × (40/90) = 8,88,889. Initial share for Technical Know-how = 20,00,000 × (20/90) = 4,44,444 (capped at 3,00,000). Excess loss of 1,44,444 is reallocated to Building and Plant in ratio 30:40. Plant share of excess = 1,44,444 × 4/7 = 82,539. Total Plant impairment = 8,88,889 + 82,539 = 9,71,428. Revised Carrying Amount = 40,00,000 - 9,71,428 = ₹ 30,28,572.

Paper 1: Advanced Accounting · Module 2 · Chapter 6:

Accounts — 55 rows
Easy NORMAL · AS 29 | Provisions | Measurement
According to AS 29 'Provisions, Contingent Liabilities and Contingent Assets', how should a provision be measured in the balance sheet?
A. At the present value of the expected expenditure discounted at the risk-free rate
B. At the best estimate of the expenditure required to settle the present obligation at the balance sheet date without discounting ✔
C. At the maximum potential loss that could arise from the obligation
D. At the average of the minimum and maximum possible outcome amounts
Explanation: Under AS 29, provisions are measured at the best estimate of the expenditure required to settle the present obligation at the balance sheet date. Unlike Ind AS 37, standard provisions under AS 29 are generally not discounted to present value unless specifically required by another standard.
Easy NORMAL · AS 15 | Short-term Employee Benefits | Definition
Under AS 15 'Employee Benefits', short-term employee benefits are defined as benefits expected to be settled wholly before how many months after the end of the period in which employees render the related service?
A. 6 months
B. 12 months ✔
C. 24 months
D. 36 months
Explanation: AS 15 defines short-term employee benefits as employee benefits (other than termination benefits) that fall due wholly within twelve months after the end of the period in which the employees render the related service.
Easy NORMAL · AS 24 | Initial Disclosure Event | Discontinuing Operations
Which of the following events triggers the 'Initial Disclosure Event' for a discontinuing operation under AS 24?
A. The Board of Directors considers a preliminary feasibility report to sell an operating component
B. The enterprise enters into a binding sale agreement for substantially all assets attributable to the discontinuing operation ✔
C. The firm negotiations with potential buyers begin without any formal board decision
D. The competitor announces a market takeover of the firm's business sector
Explanation: Under AS 24, the Initial Disclosure Event occurs on the earlier of: (a) the enterprise entering into a binding sale agreement for substantially all of the assets attributable to the discontinuing operation, or (b) the board of directors approving a detailed formal plan and making an announcement of the plan.
Easy NORMAL · AS 29 | Contingent Assets | Disclosure Rules
How should a contingent asset be treated in the financial statements under AS 29?
A. Recognized in the Balance Sheet when economic inflow is probable
B. Disclosed in the Notes to Accounts when economic inflow is remote
C. Neither recognized nor disclosed in the financial statements, but disclosed in the Report of the Board of Directors if inflow is probable ✔
D. Recognized directly in the Statement of Profit and Loss as accrued revenue
Explanation: AS 29 prohibits the recognition of contingent assets in financial statements. Where an inflow of economic benefits is probable, the contingent asset is disclosed in the Report of the Board of Directors, not in the financial statements.
Easy NORMAL · AS 15 | Defined Contribution Plan | Actuarial Risk
In a defined contribution plan under AS 15, who bears the actuarial risk and investment risk?
A. The enterprise (employer)
B. The employee ✔
C. The trustee of the fund jointly with the employer
D. The Government pension authority
Explanation: In a defined contribution plan, the enterprise's obligation is limited to the contribution agreed to be paid into the fund. Consequently, actuarial risk and investment risk fall on the employee.
Easy NORMAL · AS 29 | Contingent Liabilities | Recognition Threshold
A company has a present obligation arising from a past event, but it is NOT probable that an outflow of resources embodying economic benefits will be required to settle it. How should this item be treated under AS 29?
A. Recognize a Provision
B. Disclose as a Contingent Liability, unless the possibility of outflow is remote ✔
C. Do not disclose or recognize anything
D. Recognize as a Contingent Asset
Explanation: Under AS 29, a present obligation where an outflow of resources embodying economic benefits is not probable (i.e. possible or less than 50% likely) is disclosed as a contingent liability, unless the possibility of outflow is remote.
Easy NORMAL · AS 24 | Discontinuing Operations | Scope
Does the piecemeal disposal of individual assets of a business line without a detailed formal plan constitute a discontinuing operation under AS 24?
A. Yes, if the aggregate sale value of assets exceeds 10% of total assets
B. Yes, provided all assets are sold within one financial year
C. No, individual asset disposals without a single coordinated plan do not constitute a discontinuing operation ✔
D. Yes, always
Explanation: Under AS 24, a discontinuing operation must be pursuant to a single overall plan to dispose of, abandon, or terminate a major line of business or geographical area. Gradual piecemeal disposals without such a plan do not meet the definition.
Easy NORMAL · AS 15 | Compensated Absences | Short-term Benefits
Under AS 15, how should an enterprise account for non-vesting accumulating compensated absences?
A. No liability is recognized until employees actually take the leave
B. Recognize an expense and liability for the expected cost of the accumulated unutilized leave expected to be used as a result of the unused entitlement ✔
C. Recognize a provision for the total accumulated unutilized leave balance for all employees at gross pay rates
D. Charge the entire accumulated amount directly to reserves
Explanation: For accumulating non-vesting paid absences, AS 15 requires an enterprise to measure the expected cost as the additional amount that it expects to pay as a result of the unused entitlement that has accumulated at the balance sheet date.
Easy NORMAL · AS 29 | Contingent Liabilities | Remote Possibility
When the possibility of an outflow of economic resources to settle an obligation is remote, how is it treated under AS 29?
A. Recognized as a provision
B. Disclosed in the Notes to Accounts
C. No provision and no disclosure required in financial statements ✔
D. Disclosed only in the Directors' Report
Explanation: Under AS 29, if the possibility of any outflow of resources in settlement of an obligation is remote, neither recognition of a provision nor disclosure as a contingent liability is required.
Easy NORMAL · AS 15 | Termination Benefits | Recognition Timing
When should an enterprise recognize an expense and liability for termination benefits under AS 15?
A. Over the remaining service life of the retrenched employees
B. Immediately when the enterprise is demonstrably committed to terminate the employment ✔
C. In equal installments over 5 years starting from the date of payment
D. Only when actual cash payment is disbursed to employees
Explanation: Under AS 15, an enterprise should recognize termination benefits as an expense immediately when the enterprise is demonstrably committed to either terminate employment before normal retirement or provide termination benefits as a result of an offer made to encourage voluntary redundancy.
Medium NORMAL · AS 15 | Past Service Cost | Defined Benefit Plans
Under AS 15, how is unvested past service cost recognized in the Statement of Profit and Loss?
A. Recognized immediately as an expense in the year of amendment
B. Recognized as an expense on a straight-line basis over the average period until the benefits become vested ✔
C. Capitalized as an intangible asset and amortized over 10 years
D. Deducted directly from General Reserves without routing through P&L
Explanation: Under AS 15, past service cost for unvested benefits is recognized as an expense on a straight-line basis over the average period until the benefits become vested. Vested past service cost is recognized immediately.
Medium NORMAL · AS 29 | Onerous Contracts | Provision Calculation
Apex Ltd. enters into an onerous operating lease contract for an empty warehouse. The remaining non-cancellable lease payment is ₹600,000 per annum for 2 years. The cancellation penalty is ₹900,000. Sub-leasing is permitted and estimated to yield ₹400,000 per annum. What is the provision amount under AS 29?
A. ₹1,200,000
B. ₹900,000
C. ₹400,000 ✔
D. ₹800,000
Explanation: An onerous contract provision is measured at the unavoidable costs of meeting obligations, which is the lower of net cost of fulfilling the contract and penalty for non-fulfillment. Fulfilling net cost = (₹600,000 - ₹400,000) × 2 years = ₹400,000. Cancellation penalty = ₹900,000. Provision required = Lower of ₹400,000 and ₹900,000 = ₹400,000.
Medium NORMAL · AS 15 | Discount Rate | Actuarial Assumptions
Under AS 15, which rate should be used to discount post-employment benefit obligations (both funded and unfunded)?
A. The enterprise's weighted average cost of capital (WACC)
B. The prime lending rate of State Bank of India
C. Market yields at the balance sheet date on government bonds ✔
D. The expected rate of return on plan assets
Explanation: Under AS 15, the rate used to discount post-employment benefit obligations should be determined by reference to market yields at the balance sheet date on government bonds.
Medium NORMAL · AS 29 | Warranty Provision | Expected Value
Gamma Ltd. sells goods with a 1-year product warranty. Historical data shows that 80% goods have no defects, 15% have minor defects costing ₹200 to repair per unit, and 5% have major defects costing ₹800 to repair per unit. If 1,000 units were sold during the year, what provision for warranty should be recognized under AS 29?
A. ₹70,000 ✔
B. ₹100,000
C. ₹150,000
D. ₹800,000
Explanation: Using expected value method: Total provision = 1,000 units × [(80% × ₹0) + (15% × ₹200) + (5% × ₹800)] = 1,000 × [0 + ₹30 + ₹40] = 1,000 × ₹70 = ₹70,000.
Medium NORMAL · AS 29 | Reimbursements | Asset Recognition
When an enterprise expects to be reimbursed by a third party (e.g., an insurer) for expenditure required to settle a provision, how should this reimbursement be accounted for under AS 29?
A. Recognized as a net deduction from the provision liability in the Balance Sheet
B. Recognized as a separate asset when it is virtually certain that reimbursement will be received, with the asset not exceeding the provision amount ✔
C. Recognized as income immediately in Statement of Profit and Loss before the provision is settled
D. Disclosed only as a contingent asset in the Directors' Report
Explanation: AS 29 mandates that reimbursement is recognized as a separate asset in the Balance Sheet when it is virtually certain that reimbursement will be received if the obligation is settled. The asset recognized cannot exceed the provision amount.
Medium NORMAL · AS 24 | Disclosures | Discontinuing Operations
Under AS 24, which of the following is NOT a mandatory disclosure requirement in the financial statements for a discontinuing operation?
A. A description of the discontinuing operation
B. The business segment or geographical segment in which it is reported under AS 17
C. The exact name and postal address of prospective buyers of the assets ✔
D. The date and nature of the Initial Disclosure Event
Explanation: AS 24 mandates disclosure of the operation's description, segment details, and date/nature of the initial disclosure event, but does not require disclosing the exact identity or postal address of prospective buyers.
Medium NORMAL · AS 15 | Actuarial Gains and Losses | P&L Treatment
Under AS 15, actuarial gains and losses on defined benefit obligations and plan assets should be:
A. Recognized immediately in the Statement of Profit and Loss as income or expense ✔
B. Deferred and amortized over the expected average remaining working lives of employees
C. Recognized directly in Capital Reserve
D. Carried forward in a special buffer reserve until retirement of employees
Explanation: Under AS 15 (revised), actuarial gains and losses must be recognized immediately in the Statement of Profit and Loss in the period in which they arise.
Medium NORMAL · AS 29 | Restructuring Provision | Scope of Provision
A restructuring provision under AS 29 can include which of the following expenditures?
A. Retraining or relocating continuing staff
B. Marketing and advertising expenditure for new products
C. Direct costs strictly arising from restructuring such as employee severance pay ✔
D. Investment in new systems and distribution networks for continuing operations
Explanation: A restructuring provision includes only direct expenditures arising from restructuring, which are necessarily entailed by restructuring and not associated with ongoing activities. Costs like retraining staff, marketing, or investment in new systems relate to ongoing future operations and cannot be included.
Medium NORMAL · AS 15 | Profit-Sharing and Bonus Plans | Recognition Criteria
Under AS 15, profit-sharing and bonus plans require recognition as a liability and expense when the enterprise has a present legal or constructive obligation AND:
A. The bonus has already been physically distributed to employees
B. A reliable estimate of the obligation can be made ✔
C. The profit after tax exceeds 20% of net worth
D. The Board of Directors passes a final resolution after the AGM
Explanation: Under AS 15, an enterprise recognizes the expected cost of profit-sharing and bonus payments when it has a present legal or constructive obligation to make such payments as a result of past events, AND a reliable estimate of the obligation can be made.
Medium NORMAL · AS 15 | Projected Unit Credit Method | Actuarial Valuation
Which actuarial valuation method is mandated by AS 15 for determining the present value of defined benefit obligations and related current service cost?
A. Pay-as-you-go method
B. Projected Unit Credit Method ✔
C. Entry Age Normal Method without projection
D. Aggregate Cost Method
Explanation: AS 15 explicitly mandates the use of the Projected Unit Credit Method (also known as the accrued benefit method prorated on service) to determine the present value of defined benefit obligations and current service cost.
Medium NORMAL · AS 29 | Restructuring Provision | Constructive Obligation
Delta Ltd. has an ongoing business unit. On 10th March 2026, management decides to close the unit but takes no formal action, makes no announcement, and enters no binding contracts before 31st March 2026. Can a restructuring provision be recognized as of 31st March 2026 under AS 29?
A. Yes, because management intent creates a constructive obligation
B. No, because management decision alone does not raise a valid expectation in those affected before the balance sheet date ✔
C. Yes, provided the closure occurs before financial statements are approved
D. Yes, but only as a contingent liability
Explanation: Under AS 29, a management decision alone does not give rise to a constructive obligation at the balance sheet date unless a detailed formal plan has been approved and implementation started or main features announced to affected parties on or before the balance sheet date.
Medium NORMAL · AS 24 | Initial Disclosure Event | Timing of Disclosure
When an operation meets the definition of a discontinuing operation under AS 24, from which period's financial statements should the initial disclosures begin?
A. From the prospective financial year following the physical closure of operations
B. In the financial statements for the period in which the Initial Disclosure Event occurs ✔
C. Only in the year when all assets of the component are fully liquidated
D. Retrospectively for the past 5 financial years as prior period adjustments
Explanation: AS 24 requires an enterprise to apply the disclosure requirements for a discontinuing operation starting with the financial statements for the period in which the Initial Disclosure Event occurs.
Hard NORMAL · AS 29 | Future Operating Losses | Provisions Prohibition
Under AS 29, can an enterprise create a provision for future operating losses of a business segment?
A. Yes, if expected operating losses are reliably estimated
B. Yes, provided the segment is classified as a discontinuing operation under AS 24
C. No, provisions shall not be recognized for future operating losses because they do not meet the definition of a present obligation arising from past events ✔
D. Yes, but limited to 50% of projected losses
Explanation: AS 29 explicitly states that provisions shall not be recognized for future operating losses because future operating losses do not meet the definition of a liability/present obligation arising from a past event.
Hard NORMAL · AS 24 | AS 4 | Post Balance Sheet Events
If the Initial Disclosure Event for a discontinuing operation occurs AFTER the balance sheet date but BEFORE the financial statements are approved by the Board of Directors, what is the accounting treatment under AS 24 and AS 4?
A. It is an adjusting event; full AS 24 disclosures must be incorporated in the balance sheet and P&L of the current reporting period
B. It is a non-adjusting event; no disclosure is required anywhere
C. It is a non-adjusting event under AS 4, but disclosure of the discontinuing operation is made in the Report of the Board of Directors ✔
D. The financial statements must be delayed until the disposal process is complete
Explanation: If the IDE occurs after the balance sheet date but before approval of financial statements, it does not represent a condition existing at the balance sheet date (non-adjusting event under AS 4). However, disclosure is made in the Board's Report as per AS 24 / AS 4 guidance.
Hard NORMAL · AS 15 | Defined Benefit Asset Ceiling | Surplus Cap
In a defined benefit plan under AS 15, if the net actuarial calculation results in an asset (surplus), how is the maximum asset to be recognized in the Balance Sheet capped?
A. At 100% of the total annual service cost
B. At the lower of the net surplus and the present value of any economic benefits available in the form of refunds from the plan or reductions in future contributions ✔
C. At the total fair value of plan assets
D. Surpluses can never be recognized under AS 15
Explanation: Under AS 15, the asset recognized in the balance sheet is limited to the lower of the net defined benefit asset (surplus) and the present value of economic benefits available in the form of refunds from the plan or reductions in future contributions to the plan.
Hard NORMAL · AS 29 | Joint and Several Liability | Contingent Liabilities
When an enterprise is jointly and severally liable for an obligation with other parties, how should the portion expected to be met by other parties be treated under AS 29?
A. Recognized as a provision for the total 100% liability
B. Treated as a contingent liability for the portion expected to be met by other parties ✔
C. Ignored completely from both Balance Sheet and Notes
D. Recognized as an asset under Reimbursements
Explanation: Under AS 29, that part of the joint and several obligation that is expected to be met by other parties is treated as a contingent liability (and disclosed), while the portion for which an outflow is probable is recognized as a provision.
Hard NORMAL · AS 24 | Comparative Figures | Reclassification
Under AS 24, when an enterprise presents financial statements after the Initial Disclosure Event, how are comparative figures for prior periods presented?
A. Prior period statements are fully restated by removing discontinuing operations from previous revenues
B. Comparative information for prior periods presented in financial statements is reclassified to segregate continuing and discontinuing assets, liabilities, revenues, and expenses ✔
C. Prior period figures are left untouched and no reclassification or disclosure is permitted
D. Prior period financial statements are restated as a cumulative effect adjustment in opening retained earnings
Explanation: AS 24 requires comparative information for prior periods presented in the financial statements to be reclassified to segregate continuing and discontinuing assets, liabilities, revenues, expenses, and cash flows to enable meaningful comparison.
Hard NORMAL · AS 15 | Return on Plan Assets | Actuarial Gain/Loss
Under AS 15, expected return on plan assets is based on market expectations at the beginning of the period for returns over the entire life of the related obligation. How is the difference between expected return and actual return on plan assets accounted for?
A. Amortized over 5 years on a straight-line basis
B. Recognized immediately as an actuarial gain or loss in the Statement of Profit and Loss ✔
C. Adjusted against opening General Reserve
D. Transferred to a separate Asset Equalization Reserve
Explanation: The difference between the actual return on plan assets and the expected return on plan assets constitutes an actuarial gain or loss on plan assets, which is recognized immediately in the Statement of Profit and Loss under AS 15.
Hard NORMAL · AS 29 | Single Obligation Measurement | Best Estimate
A company is defending a lawsuit. Management's legal counsel advises that there is a 60% probability that the company will lose the case and have to pay ₹5,000,000, and a 40% probability that it will win and pay ₹0. How should this be accounted for under AS 29?
A. Recognize a provision of ₹3,000,000 (weighted average outcome)
B. Recognize a provision of ₹5,000,000 ✔
C. Disclose a contingent liability of ₹5,000,000 with zero provision
D. Recognize a provision of ₹2,500,000
Explanation: Where a single obligation is being measured, the most likely outcome generally represents the best estimate under AS 29. Since there is a 60% (probable) chance of losing ₹5,000,000, the provision should be recognized at ₹5,000,000 rather than expected value.
Easy NORMAL · AS 29 | Review of Provisions | Reversal
Under AS 29, if a provision is reviewed at each balance sheet date and it is clear that an outflow of resources is no longer probable, what action must be taken?
A. The provision should be retained in the balance sheet indefinitely until the legal limitation period expires
B. The provision should be written back and reversed to the Statement of Profit and Loss ✔
C. The provision should be transferred directly to Capital Reserve
D. The provision should be reclassified as a deferred liability
Explanation: AS 29 requires provisions to be reviewed at each balance sheet date and adjusted to reflect the current best estimate. If it is no longer probable that an outflow of resources embodying economic benefits will be required to settle the obligation, the provision should be reversed to P&L.
CASE SCENARIO: Kaveri Chemicals Ltd. operates two separate business lines: a Bulk Chemical Plant and a Speciality Solvents division. For the financial year ended 31st March 2026, the following situations arise: 1. In March 2026, the State Environmental Control Board passed a mandatory directive requiring Kaveri Chemicals to decontaminate soil at its Bulk Chemical Plant before April 2028. The estimated cost of decontamination is ₹15,000,000. Under AS 29, the management is evaluating whether to discount this provision. 2. The Speciality Solvents division sold 2,000 chemical containers during 2025-26 under a standard 1-year leakage warranty. Historical performance indicates that 90% of containers experience no leakage, 7% suffer minor leakage (repair cost ₹2,000 per container), and 3% suffer major leakage (replacement cost ₹10,000 per container). 3. An employee filed a damages suit of ₹8,000,000 against the company for workplace injury. Legal experts advise that there is a 30% chance the company will be held liable. 4. For warranty claims exceeding ₹500,000 in total, Kaveri Chemicals holds an indemnity insurance contract with an insurer. The insurer has confirmed in writing that it will reimburse 80% of warranty costs incurred above ₹500,000 once claims are paid.
Medium SCENARIO · AS 29 | Decontamination Provision | Discounting Rule
Regarding the decontamination liability of ₹15,000,000 for the Bulk Chemical Plant, how should it be recognized in the financial statements for FY 2025-26 under AS 29?
A. Recognize a provision at the present value of ₹15,000,000 using a 10% discount rate
B. Recognize a provision at the undiscounted amount of ₹15,000,000 as a present obligation ✔
C. Disclose as a contingent liability because actual payment is due in 2028
D. Do not recognize or disclose until the decontamination work commences in 2028
Explanation: A mandatory directive creates a present obligation from a past event with a probable outflow. Under AS 29, provisions are measured at best estimate and are generally not discounted to present value. Hence, an undiscounted provision of ₹15,000,000 is recognized.
Medium SCENARIO · AS 29 | Warranty Provision | Expected Value
What is the warranty provision required for the Speciality Solvents division as of 31st March 2026 under AS 29?
A. ₹880,000 ✔
B. ₹1,760,000
C. ₹2,000,000
D. ₹120,000
Explanation: Expected cost per container = (90% × ₹0) + (7% × ₹2,000) + (3% × ₹10,000) = ₹0 + ₹140 + ₹300 = ₹440 per container. Total provision for 2,000 containers = 2,000 × ₹440 = ₹880,000.
Hard SCENARIO · AS 29 | Reimbursements | Separate Asset
How should the insurance reimbursement for warranty claims be presented in the Balance Sheet as of 31st March 2026?
A. Deduct ₹304,000 directly from the Warranty Provision liability in the Balance Sheet
B. Recognize a separate Reimbursement Asset of ₹304,000 in the Balance Sheet, as reimbursement is virtually certain ✔
C. Recognize a Reimbursement Asset of ₹704,000
D. Disclose as a Contingent Asset in the Board's Report only
Explanation: Total warranty provision = ₹880,000. Reimbursement applies to excess over ₹500,000 = ₹880,000 - ₹500,000 = ₹380,000. Insurer covers 80% of excess = 80% × ₹380,000 = ₹304,000. Under AS 29, reimbursement is recognized as a separate asset (not netted against liability in Balance Sheet) when virtually certain.
Medium SCENARIO · AS 29 | Contingent Liability | Litigation
How should the pending damages lawsuit of ₹8,000,000 be treated in the financial statements for FY 2025-26 under AS 29?
A. Recognize a provision of ₹2,400,000 (30% of ₹8,000,000)
B. Recognize a provision of ₹8,000,000
C. Disclose as a Contingent Liability in the Notes to Accounts, since the outflow is possible (30%) but not probable ✔
D. Ignore completely without any disclosure since probability is less than 50%
Explanation: A 30% chance represents a possible obligation (not probable, as probability < 50%). Under AS 29, a possible obligation that is not remote must be disclosed as a Contingent Liability in the Notes to Accounts.
CASE SCENARIO: Zenith Engineering Ltd. maintains a funded Defined Benefit Gratuity Scheme for its employees. Actuarial valuation and scheme data for the financial year ended 31st March 2026 reveal the following: • Opening Present Value of Defined Benefit Obligation (DBO) as on 1st April 2025: ₹5,000,000 • Opening Fair Value of Plan Assets as on 1st April 2025: ₹4,000,000 • Discount Rate (based on Government Securities): 10% per annum • Expected Rate of Return on Plan Assets: 10% per annum • Current Service Cost for FY 2025-26: ₹800,000 • Plan amendment on 1st July 2025 granted past service benefits of ₹1,000,000, of which ₹400,000 vested immediately and ₹600,000 vests over 3 remaining years of service. • Benefits paid to retired employees during FY 2025-26: ₹500,000 • Contributions paid by Zenith Engineering into the plan during FY 2025-26: ₹800,000 • Closing DBO as per Actuarial Valuation on 31st March 2026: ₹7,200,000 • Closing Fair Value of Plan Assets as on 31st March 2026: ₹4,900,000
Hard SCENARIO · AS 15 | Actuarial Loss | Defined Benefit Obligation
What is the amount of Actuarial Gain or Loss on the Defined Benefit Obligation (DBO) for FY 2025-26?
A. Actuarial Loss of ₹400,000 ✔
B. Actuarial Gain of ₹400,000
C. Actuarial Loss of ₹200,000
D. Actuarial Loss of ₹600,000
Explanation: Expected DBO at year end = Opening DBO (₹5,000,000) + Interest Cost (10% of ₹5,000,000 = ₹500,000) + Current Service Cost (₹800,000) + Total Past Service Cost (₹1,000,000) - Benefits Paid (₹500,000) = ₹6,800,000. Actual Closing DBO = ₹7,200,000. Actuarial Loss on DBO = ₹7,200,000 - ₹6,800,000 = ₹400,000.
Hard SCENARIO · AS 15 | Actuarial Gain | Plan Assets
What is the Actuarial Gain or Loss on Plan Assets for FY 2025-26?
A. Actuarial Loss of ₹200,000
B. Actuarial Gain of ₹200,000 ✔
C. Actuarial Gain of ₹400,000
D. Actuarial Loss of ₹100,000
Explanation: Expected Plan Assets at year end = Opening Plan Assets (₹4,000,000) + Expected Return (10% of ₹4,000,000 = ₹400,000) + Contributions (₹800,000) - Benefits Paid (₹500,000) = ₹4,700,000. Actual Closing Plan Assets = ₹4,900,000. Actuarial Gain on Plan Assets = ₹4,900,000 - ₹4,700,000 = ₹200,000.
Hard SCENARIO · AS 15 | Net Gratuity Expense | P&L Calculation
What total net expense should Zenith Engineering Ltd. recognize in the Statement of Profit and Loss for FY 2025-26 under AS 15?
A. ₹2,200,000
B. ₹1,900,000
C. ₹2,100,000 ✔
D. ₹1,700,000
Explanation: Net Expense in P&L = Current Service Cost (₹800,000) + Interest Cost (₹500,000) - Expected Return on Plan Assets (₹400,000) + Recognized Past Service Cost [₹400,000 vested + (₹600,000 / 3 yrs unvested) = ₹600,000] + Actuarial Loss on DBO (₹400,000) - Actuarial Gain on Plan Assets (₹200,000) = 800,000 + 500,000 - 400,000 + 600,000 + 400,000 - 200,000 = ₹2,100,000.
Hard SCENARIO · AS 15 | Net Defined Benefit Liability | Balance Sheet
What is the Net Defined Benefit Liability to be reported in the Balance Sheet of Zenith Engineering Ltd. as of 31st March 2026?
A. ₹2,300,000
B. ₹1,900,000 ✔
C. ₹2,700,000
D. ₹1,500,000
Explanation: Net Liability in Balance Sheet = Closing Present Value of DBO (₹7,200,000) - Unrecognized Past Service Cost (₹600,000 total - ₹200,000 recognized = ₹400,000 remaining) - Closing Fair Value of Plan Assets (₹4,900,000) = 7,200,000 - 400,000 - 4,900,000 = ₹1,900,000. (Check: Opening Net Liability ₹1,000,000 + P&L Expense ₹2,100,000 - Contributions ₹800,000 = ₹1,900,000).
CASE SCENARIO: Crimson Consumer Goods Ltd. manufactures textiles and healthcare products. Due to sustained losses in its Textile Division, the Board of Directors took the following actions during FY 2025-26: • On 15th December 2025, the Board approved a detailed formal plan to discontinue the entire Textile Division (which constitutes a separate major line of business and segment). • On 20th January 2026, the company entered into a legally binding agreement to sell the spinning equipment of Unit A of the Textile Division for ₹12,000,000. • On 10th February 2026, Crimson Consumer Goods Ltd. made a formal public announcement of its plan to discontinue the Textile Division. • The financial year ended on 31st March 2026. Financial statements were approved by the Board on 25th May 2026. • Carrying value of total assets of Textile Division as of 31st March 2026 was ₹50,000,000, while their net realizable value was estimated at ₹42,000,000.
Medium SCENARIO · AS 24 | Initial Disclosure Event | Discontinuing Operations
What is the date of the 'Initial Disclosure Event' (IDE) for the discontinuing operation under AS 24?
A. 15th December 2025
B. 20th January 2026 ✔
C. 10th February 2026
D. 31st March 2026
Explanation: Under AS 24, the Initial Disclosure Event occurs on the EARLIER of: (a) binding sale agreement date (20th January 2026), or (b) board approval of detailed plan AND public announcement (10th February 2026). Thus, the binding agreement date (20th January 2026) is the IDE date.
Medium SCENARIO · AS 24 | AS 28 | Impairment Loss
How should the impairment loss on the assets of the Textile Division be recognized in the financial statements for FY 2025-26?
A. Recognize an impairment loss of ₹8,000,000 in the Statement of Profit and Loss for FY 2025-26 ✔
B. Defer the impairment loss until all assets of the division are physically handed over
C. Charge ₹8,000,000 directly to Revaluation Reserve
D. Disclose ₹8,000,000 as a contingent loss without reducing asset carrying values
Explanation: Under AS 24 and AS 28, when an initial disclosure event occurs or assets are held for disposal, their recoverable/net realizable value is assessed. An impairment loss equal to Carrying Value (₹50,000,000) - Net Realizable Value (₹42,000,000) = ₹8,000,000 must be recognized immediately in P&L.
Medium SCENARIO · AS 24 | Disclosures | Financial Presentation
In the financial statements for FY 2025-26, which of the following details regarding the Textile Division MUST be disclosed on the face of or in the notes to the financial statements under AS 24?
A. Pre-tax profit/loss of the discontinuing operation and income tax expense related thereto ✔
B. Names of all individual machine operators who will be laid off
C. Estimated market share of competitors after Crimson's exit
D. Board minutes of all internal strategy meetings held prior to 15th December 2025
Explanation: AS 24 mandates disclosure of the amounts of revenue, expenses, pre-tax profit or loss of the discontinuing operation, and the related income tax expense.
Medium SCENARIO · AS 24 | Cash Flow Statement | Discontinuing Operations
How should cash flow disclosures for the Textile Division be presented in the Cash Flow Statement for FY 2025-26 under AS 24?
A. Cash flows of discontinuing operations should be completely omitted from the Cash Flow Statement
B. Net cash flows attributable to operating, investing, and financing activities of the discontinuing operation must be disclosed on the face or in notes ✔
C. All cash flows of the discontinuing operation must be merged into operating activities only
D. Cash flows should only be disclosed for future prospective years
Explanation: AS 24 mandates disclosure of the net cash flows attributable to the operating, investing, and financing activities of the discontinuing operation either on the face of the cash flow statement or in the notes.
CASE SCENARIO: Apex Retailers Ltd. is preparing its financial statements for the year ended 31st March 2026. The controller faces the following independent issues: Issue 1: Apex entered into a non-cancellable 5-year commercial lease for an outlet at ₹1,200,000/year. 2 years remain. Apex vacated the premises to relocate. The landlord demands a cancellation fee of ₹1,800,000. Apex can sublet the outlet for the remaining 2 years at ₹800,000/year. Issue 2: Division B is incurring losses. The budget for FY 2026-27 projects an operating loss of ₹3,000,000 for Division B. Management wants to create a provision for this projected operating loss as of 31st March 2026. Issue 3: On 25th March 2026, the Board approved a detailed restructuring plan to close Branch X. The plan entails severance payments of ₹1,500,000. However, the plan was communicated to affected employees and public announcement was made on 5th April 2026 (before audit completion).
Medium SCENARIO · AS 29 | Onerous Lease | Provision Calculation
For Issue 1 (Onerous Lease), what provision should Apex Retailers Ltd. recognize as of 31st March 2026 under AS 29?
A. ₹2,400,000
B. ₹1,800,000
C. ₹800,000 ✔
D. ₹1,600,000
Explanation: Onerous contract provision is the lower of net fulfillment cost and cancellation penalty. Net fulfillment cost = (₹1,200,000 rent - ₹800,000 sublet) × 2 years = ₹800,000. Cancellation penalty = ₹1,800,000. Provision required = Lower of ₹800,000 and ₹1,800,000 = ₹800,000.
Easy SCENARIO · AS 29 | Future Operating Losses | Provisions
For Issue 2 (Projected Operating Loss), how should the ₹3,000,000 projected loss of Division B be accounted for as of 31st March 2026 under AS 29?
A. Recognize a provision of ₹3,000,000 as a current liability
B. Recognize a provision of ₹1,500,000 (50% prudential provision)
C. No provision should be recognized because future operating losses do not meet the definition of a present obligation arising from past events ✔
D. Disclose as a Contingent Asset in the Directors' Report
Explanation: AS 29 explicitly prohibits provisions for future operating losses because they do not arise from past events and do not meet the definition of a present obligation.
Hard SCENARIO · AS 29 | Restructuring Provision | Constructive Obligation Timing
For Issue 3 (Restructuring Plan), can Apex Retailers Ltd. recognize a restructuring provision of ₹1,500,000 for Branch X in the balance sheet as of 31st March 2026?
A. Yes, because the Board approved the detailed plan before 31st March 2026
B. No, because a constructive obligation arises only when implementation starts or main features are announced to affected parties ON OR BEFORE 31st March 2026 ✔
C. Yes, because public announcement occurred before audit completion date
D. Yes, provided approval is disclosed in the Directors' Report
Explanation: Under AS 29, a management/board decision taken before the balance sheet date does not create a constructive obligation as of the balance sheet date unless the plan was announced to affected parties or implementation commenced ON OR BEFORE the balance sheet date (31st March 2026). Communication on 5th April 2026 is a post-balance sheet non-adjusting event.
Medium SCENARIO · AS 29 | Provision Reversal | Onerous Contracts
If in FY 2026-27, Apex Retailers Ltd. sub-leases the outlet in Issue 1 for ₹1,300,000/year (which exceeds the lease rent of ₹1,200,000/year), what should happen to the onerous lease provision of ₹800,000?
A. Retain ₹800,000 in Capital Reserve
B. Reverse the ₹800,000 provision to the Statement of Profit and Loss as it is no longer required ✔
C. Amortize the provision over the remaining lease term
D. Transfer ₹800,000 to General Reserve
Explanation: Under AS 29, provisions must be reviewed at each balance sheet date. If an obligation is no longer onerous (sub-lease covers lease liability), an outflow is no longer probable, so the provision must be reversed to Profit and Loss.
CASE SCENARIO: Beta Services Ltd. employs 100 individuals and has the following employee benefit policies for FY 2025-26: 1. Paid Leave Policy: Each employee earns 12 days of paid leave per year. Unused leaves accumulate up to 30 days. The leave is non-vesting (employees cannot encash unused leave upon leaving/retirement, but can take paid leave). Historical data shows average leave utilization: • 70 employees use all 12 days earned in the year. • 30 employees use 10 days and accumulate 2 days each. • Actuarial calculations estimate that out of the accumulated leaves, these 30 employees will actually utilize a total of 45 accumulated leave days in future years. • Average salary per employee per day is ₹1,000. 2. Annual Profit Sharing Bonus: Beta Services Ltd. announced a policy to distribute 5% of Profit Before Tax (PBT) as bonus to employees if PBT exceeds ₹10,000,000. PBT for FY 2025-26 is ₹20,000,000.
Hard SCENARIO · AS 15 | Compensated Absences | Accumulating Non-Vesting
Under AS 15, what provision amount should Beta Services Ltd. recognize for accumulating non-vesting compensated absences at the end of FY 2025-26?
A. ₹60,000
B. ₹45,000 ✔
C. ₹300,000
D. ₹120,000
Explanation: For non-vesting accumulating compensated absences, AS 15 requires measuring expected cost as the additional amount expected to be paid as a result of unused entitlement that has accumulated. Estimated expected utilization = 45 days × ₹1,000/day = ₹45,000.
Medium SCENARIO · AS 15 | Profit-Sharing Bonus | Short-term Benefits
What liability should Beta Services Ltd. recognize for the profit-sharing bonus for FY 2025-26 under AS 15?
A. ₹1,000,000 ✔
B. ₹500,000
C. ₹100,000
D. Nil, until payments are actually disbursed
Explanation: Bonus liability = 5% of PBT when PBT > ₹10,000,000. PBT is ₹20,000,000. Bonus = 5% of ₹20,000,000 = ₹1,000,000. Under AS 15, present constructive obligation with reliable estimate must be recognized as liability and expense.
Medium SCENARIO · AS 15 | Vesting Compensated Absences | Leave Encashment
If Beta Services Ltd. alters its leave policy to make leaves VESTING (encashable in cash upon retirement/resignation), how would the liability measurement change under AS 15?
A. Liability must be measured based on the full total accumulated unutilized leave days for all employees at current salary rate ✔
B. Liability remains based only on expected days used during service
C. No liability is required until retirement
D. Vesting leaves are treated as defined contribution plans
Explanation: For vesting compensated absences, employees are entitled to a cash payment for unutilized entitlement upon leaving. Therefore, the enterprise must recognize a liability for the entire accumulated unused leave balance at the balance sheet date.
Medium SCENARIO · AS 15 | Change in Estimate | Employee Benefit Expense
Suppose in FY 2026-27, employees actually utilize 50 days of accumulated leave instead of the estimated 45 days. How is the difference of 5 days accounted for under AS 15?
A. Prior period error adjustment in opening reserves
B. Recognized as an employee benefit expense in the Statement of Profit and Loss for FY 2026-27 ✔
C. Capitalized as part of intangible assets
D. Charged directly to General Reserve
Explanation: Under AS 15, changes in estimates of short-term employee benefit utilization/obligations are recognized as an expense or income in the Statement of Profit and Loss in the period in which the change occurs.

Paper 1: Advanced Accounting · Module 2 · Chapter 7:

Accounts — 55 rows
Easy NORMAL · AS 4 | Adjusting Events | Subsequent Events
Under AS 4 'Contingencies and Events Occurring After the Balance Sheet Date', which of the following events occurring after the balance sheet date but before approval of financial statements requires an adjustment to assets and liabilities?
A. A fire in the warehouse destroying inventory worth ₹50 lakhs on 10th April
B. Insolvency of a major trade debtor whose financial position was deteriorating prior to the balance sheet date ✔
C. A major decline in market value of investments after the balance sheet date
D. Announcement of a scheme of reconstruction after the balance sheet date
Explanation: AS 4 states that adjustments to assets and liabilities are required for events occurring after the balance sheet date that provide additional information materially affecting the determination of amounts relating to conditions existing at the balance sheet date. Insolvency of a customer confirms the uncollectibility of a debt existing on the balance sheet date, making it an adjusting event.
Easy NORMAL · AS 4 | Proposed Dividend | Notes to Accounts
How should dividends declared/proposed by an enterprise for the financial year after the balance sheet date but before approval of financial statements be treated as per revised AS 4?
A. Recognized as a liability on the balance sheet date
B. Recognized as a provision in the Statement of Profit and Loss
C. Disclosed in the notes to accounts without recognizing as a liability ✔
D. Adjusted directly in the General Reserve account on the balance sheet date
Explanation: As per revised AS 4, if dividends are declared after the balance sheet date, an enterprise should not recognize those dividends as a liability at the balance sheet date because no obligation exists at that date. Such dividends are disclosed in the notes to the financial statements.
Easy NORMAL · AS 5 | Prior Period Items | Financial Presentation
According to AS 5 'Net Profit or Loss for the Period, Prior Period Items and Changes in Accounting Policies', how should prior period items be presented in the Statement of Profit and Loss?
A. Adjusted against the opening balance of retained earnings with restatements
B. Shown separately in the current period Statement of Profit and Loss after determining net profit/loss ✔
C. Included quietly under regular administration expenses without separate line disclosure
D. Deducted directly from the Share Capital account
Explanation: AS 5 requires prior period items to be separately disclosed in the Statement of Profit and Loss in a manner that their impact on the current profit or loss can be perceived. Unlike Ind AS 8, AS 5 does not require retrospective restatement of prior period financial statement figures.
Medium NORMAL · AS 5 | AS 10 | Accounting Estimates | Depreciation
An enterprise changes its method of charging depreciation on plant and machinery from Straight Line Method (SLM) to Written Down Value (WDV) method. As per AS 5 and AS 10 (Revised), this change should be treated as:
A. A change in accounting policy requiring retrospective adjustment
B. A prior period error requiring retrospective restatement
C. A change in accounting estimate accounted for prospectively ✔
D. An extraordinary item credited to the capital reserve
Explanation: Under AS 10 (Revised) and AS 5, a change in depreciation method is treated as a change in an accounting estimate. It is accounted for prospectively by allocating the depreciable amount over the remaining useful life.
Easy NORMAL · AS 11 | Monetary Items | Closing Rate
Under AS 11 'The Effects of Changes in Foreign Exchange Rates', foreign currency monetary items outstanding at the balance sheet date should be reported using the:
A. Average rate of the financial year
B. Transaction date exchange rate
C. Closing exchange rate at the balance sheet date ✔
D. Forward exchange contract rate agreed with the bank
Explanation: AS 11 mandates that at each balance sheet date, foreign currency monetary items (such as cash, receivables, payables, loans) shall be reported using the closing exchange rate.
Easy NORMAL · AS 11 | Non-Monetary Items | Classification
Which of the following items is classified as a NON-MONETARY item under AS 11?
A. Trade Receivables in foreign currency
B. Inventories held in foreign currency location ✔
C. Bank balances held in overseas foreign bank accounts
D. Foreign currency term loan payable
Explanation: Monetary items are money held and assets/liabilities to be received/paid in fixed or determinable amounts of money. Inventories, fixed assets, and investments are non-monetary items under AS 11.
Easy NORMAL · AS 22 | Timing Differences | Deferred Tax
As per AS 22 'Accounting for Taxes on Income', timing differences are defined as:
A. Differences between taxable income and accounting income that originate in one period and are capable of reversal in one or more subsequent periods ✔
B. Differences between accounting income and taxable income that originate in one period and do not reverse subsequently
C. Differences between total cash inflows and total taxable receipts of the enterprise
D. Differences arising purely due to tax rate changes between two financial years
Explanation: Timing differences originate in one period and reverse in one or more subsequent periods, resulting from differences in timing of recognition of items of income or expense for accounting vs taxation purposes.
Medium NORMAL · AS 22 | Virtual Certainty | Unabsorbed Loss | Deferred Tax Asset
Under AS 22, Deferred Tax Assets (DTA) in situations of unabsorbed depreciation or carry forward of losses under tax laws should be recognized ONLY to the extent that there is:
A. Reasonable certainty that sufficient future taxable income will be available
B. Virtual certainty supported by convincing evidence that sufficient future taxable income will be available ✔
C. Absolute guarantee from the tax authorities that losses will be set off
D. Management expectation of profit in the next 10 accounting periods
Explanation: AS 22 lays down a stricter prudence test for entities having unabsorbed depreciation or carried forward tax losses: DTA can be recognized only if there is virtual certainty supported by convincing evidence that sufficient future taxable income will be available.
Medium NORMAL · AS 22 | Permanent Difference | Tax Accounting
A company incurs fine and penalty of ₹5,00,000 for violation of statutory environmental regulations. Under tax laws, penalties for illegal acts are permanently disallowed. Under AS 22, this penalty creates:
A. A Deferred Tax Liability (DTL)
B. A Deferred Tax Asset (DTA)
C. A Permanent Difference requiring no deferred tax creation ✔
D. A timing difference reversing over 5 years
Explanation: Items disallowed permanently under tax laws (and not allowed in subsequent years either) create permanent differences. Permanent differences do not reverse in subsequent periods and hence no deferred tax asset or liability is recognized on them.
Hard NORMAL · AS 4 | Going Concern | Adjusting Events
On 28th March 2026, a company suffered a severe fire destroying its major factory unit. The financial statements were approved on 20th May 2026. Management determines that the loss affects the entity's ability to continue as a going concern. How should this event be treated under AS 4?
A. Disclosed only in the report of the Board of Directors without changing accounts
B. Disclosed as a non-adjusting event in the notes to accounts
C. Financial statements must be prepared on a non-going concern basis ( liquidation/realizable basis), treating it as an adjusting event ✔
D. Ignored in the financial statements of 2025-26 and recorded in 2026-27
Explanation: As per AS 4, if an event after the balance sheet date indicates that the enterprise will not be able to continue as a going concern, the financial statements must be adjusted to reflect the non-going concern status (e.g. assets valued at net realizable value).
Medium NORMAL · AS 5 | Prior Period Error | Omission
An enterprise omitted to accrue interest income of ₹1,20,000 earned on bank fixed deposits during FY 2024-25. The error was discovered during FY 2025-26. How should this amount be recorded under AS 5 in FY 2025-26?
A. Credited directly to Capital Reserve
B. Included in current year's interest income without any separate disclosure
C. Shown as a prior period item in the Statement of Profit and Loss of FY 2025-26 ✔
D. Adjusted by restating the comparative balance sheet of FY 2024-25
Explanation: Prior period items are income or expenses which arise in the current period as a result of errors or omissions in the preparation of financial statements of one or more prior periods. They are disclosed separately in the Statement of Profit and Loss under AS 5.
Medium NORMAL · AS 11 | Non-Integral Foreign Operation | FCTR
Under AS 11, exchange differences arising on the translation of financial statements of a Non-Integral Foreign Operation (NIFO) should be:
A. Recognized as income or expense in the Statement of Profit and Loss immediately
B. Accumulated in a Foreign Currency Translation Reserve (FCTR) until the disposal of the net investment ✔
C. Capitalized into the carrying cost of fixed assets of the foreign operation
D. Deducted directly from current liabilities in the consolidated balance sheet
Explanation: For a Non-Integral Foreign Operation (NIFO), AS 11 requires exchange differences arising on translation to be accumulated in a 'Foreign Currency Translation Reserve' (FCTR) in the balance sheet until the disposal of the net investment.
Medium NORMAL · AS 11 | Exchange Difference | Monetary Liability
An enterprise purchases goods in USD on 1st February 2026 for USD 20,000 when USD 1 = ₹82. On 31st March 2026, the rate is USD 1 = ₹85. Payment is made on 30th April 2026 when USD 1 = ₹84. What is the exchange gain/loss recognized in P&L for FY 2025-26 under AS 11?
A. ₹60,000 Loss ✔
B. ₹60,000 Gain
C. ₹40,000 Loss
D. ₹20,000 Loss
Explanation: At initial recognition (1st Feb): USD 20,000 * 82 = ₹16,40,000 liability. At balance sheet date (31st Mar): USD 20,000 * 85 = ₹17,00,000 liability. Exchange Loss for FY 2025-26 = ₹17,00,000 - ₹16,40,000 = ₹60,00,00 Loss recognized in P&L.
Medium NORMAL · AS 11 | Settlement Gain | Monetary Items
Continuing from the previous transaction, what exchange gain or loss will be recognized in the Profit & Loss statement for FY 2026-27 on settlement date (30th April 2026)?
A. Exchange Gain of ₹20,000 ✔
B. Exchange Loss of ₹20,000
C. Exchange Gain of ₹40,000
D. No exchange gain/loss
Explanation: Carrying liability as on 1st April 2026 = USD 20,000 * 85 = ₹17,00,000. Amount paid on 30th April 2026 = USD 20,00,0 * 84 = ₹16,80,000. Settlement results in an Exchange Gain of ₹17,00,000 - ₹16,80,000 = ₹20,000 in FY 2026-27.
Hard NORMAL · AS 22 | Deferred Tax Liability | Timing Difference
Under AS 22, if tax laws allow 100% depreciation on certain scientific research equipment in Year 1 (₹10,00,000) while financial accounts depreciate it over 5 years on Straight Line Method (₹2,00,000 p.a.), what is the timing difference in Year 1 and its tax effect (assuming tax rate is 30%)?
A. Deductible timing difference ₹8,00,000 leading to DTA of ₹2,40,000
B. Taxable timing difference ₹8,00,000 leading to DTL of ₹2,40,000 ✔
C. Taxable timing difference ₹10,00,000 leading to DTL of ₹3,00,000
D. Permanent difference ₹8,00,000 with no deferred tax impact
Explanation: Taxable income in Year 1 will be lower than accounting income due to excess tax depreciation of ₹8,00,000 (10L - 2L). This is a taxable timing difference of ₹8,00,000, creating a Deferred Tax Liability (DTL) of ₹8,00,000 * 30% = ₹2,40,000.
Medium NORMAL · AS 22 | Offsetting Criteria | Presentation
Which of the following conditions MUST be fulfilled for an enterprise to offset Deferred Tax Assets (DTA) and Deferred Tax Liabilities (DTL) in its balance sheet under AS 22?
A. The enterprise has a legally enforceable right to set off assets against liabilities under income tax laws AND DTAs/DTLs relate to taxes levied by the same governing tax law ✔
B. The management decides to show net figures for better ratio presentation
C. DTA and DTL amounts are equal in magnitude
D. The auditor provides a written approval for offsetting
Explanation: AS 22 allows offsetting of DTA and DTL if and only if the enterprise has a legally enforceable right to set off current tax assets against current tax liabilities and the deferred tax assets and liabilities relate to taxes on income levied by the same governing tax laws.
Hard NORMAL · AS 22 | Deferred Tax Asset | Section 35D
During FY 2025-26, a company incurs preliminary expenses of ₹6,00,000. As per AS 26, the entire amount is written off in P&L in FY 2025-26. However, under Income Tax Act Section 35D, this expenditure is deductible in 5 equal annual installments (₹1,20,000 p.a.). Tax rate is 30%. What deferred tax item is created in FY 2025-26?
A. Deferred Tax Liability of ₹1,44,000
B. Deferred Tax Asset of ₹1,44,000 ✔
C. Deferred Tax Asset of ₹1,80,000
D. Permanent difference of ₹4,80,000
Explanation: Accounting profit is lower by ₹4,80,000 (6,00,000 expensed in accounts - 1,20,000 allowed in tax). In future years, tax laws will allow ₹1,20,000 p.a. deduction while accounts will show zero expense. This creates a deductible timing difference of ₹4,80,000 resulting in DTA = ₹4,80,000 * 30% = ₹1,44,000.
Medium NORMAL · AS 11 | Integral Foreign Operation | Fair Value Translation
An Integral Foreign Operation (IFO) holds foreign currency non-monetary items carried at fair value. Under AS 11, at what exchange rate should these items be translated at the balance sheet date?
A. Historical rate at the date of acquisition
B. Closing exchange rate on the balance sheet date
C. Exchange rate existing on the date when fair value was determined ✔
D. Average rate of the reporting period
Explanation: AS 11 mandates that non-monetary items carried at fair value or net realizable value in an integral foreign operation shall be translated using the exchange rates that existed when the values were determined.
Easy NORMAL · AS 5 | Extraordinary Items | Non-Ordinary Events
Which of the following is an example of an Extraordinary Item under AS 5?
A. Write-down of inventories to net realizable value
B. Loss incurred due to an earthquake destroying a manufacturing plant ✔
C. Provision for bad debts due to slowdown in economy
D. Gain on sale of obsolete office computer equipment
Explanation: Extraordinary items are income or expenses that arise from events or transactions that are clearly distinct from the ordinary activities of the enterprise and, therefore, are not expected to recur frequently or regularly. Earthquake loss is extraordinary.
Medium NORMAL · AS 11 | Forward Exchange Contract | Premium Amortization
Under AS 11, a forward exchange contract is entered into for hedging foreign exchange exposure on a firm commitment. The premium or discount arising on inception of such a forward contract should be:
A. Charged entirely to Statement of Profit and Loss on inception date
B. Capitalized into the cost of related fixed asset
C. Amortized as expense or income over the life of the contract ✔
D. Carried forward in a reserve until settlement
Explanation: AS 11 specifies that any premium or discount arising at the inception of a forward exchange contract intended for hedging purposes should be amortized as expense or income over the life of the contract.
Hard NORMAL · AS 11 | Speculation Contract | Mark to Market
Under AS 11, if a forward contract is entered into for TRADING or SPECULATION purposes, how is the gain or loss on the contract determined and recognized at each balance sheet date?
A. Amortized over the life of the contract
B. Calculated by computing the difference between forward rate for remaining maturity and contract rate, and recognized in Profit & Loss ✔
C. Ignored until the maturity of the contract
D. Transferred directly to General Reserve
Explanation: For trading or speculation forward contracts, AS 11 prohibits premium/discount amortization. Instead, at each balance sheet date, the contract is marked to market by comparing forward rate for remaining term with contract rate, and gains/losses are recognized in P&L.
Hard NORMAL · AS 4 | Adjusting Event | Provision
Alpha Ltd. has an unrecorded liability for compensation payable to workers under a court order passed on 20th March 2026. The amount was agreed upon as ₹10 lakhs on 15th April 2026 before balance sheet approval. What is the treatment in accounts for FY 2025-26 under AS 4?
A. Disclose as a contingent liability in notes
B. Create a provision/adjust liability of ₹10 lakhs in financial statements for FY 2025-26 ✔
C. Record expense in FY 2026-27 when paid
D. Ignore since court order was passed before financial year end without amount
Explanation: The condition (court order against company) existed at the balance sheet date (20th March). The event occurring after balance sheet date (negotiation fixing amount on 15th April) provides additional evidence. Thus, it is an adjusting event under AS 4.
Medium NORMAL · AS 22 | Re-assessment | Deferred Tax Asset
According to AS 22, at each balance sheet date, an enterprise shall re-assess unrecognized Deferred Tax Assets. What action should be taken if criteria for recognition are now met?
A. Do nothing; once unrecognized, DTA cannot be recognized in future
B. Recognize previously unrecognized DTA to the extent it has become reasonably/virtually certain that future taxable income will be available ✔
C. Adjust prior period retained earnings retrospectively
D. Credit the amount directly to Capital Reserve
Explanation: AS 22 requires entities to re-assess unrecognized DTAs at each balance sheet date. The entity recognizes a previously unrecognized DTA to the extent that it has become reasonably or virtually certain (as applicable) that future taxable income will be available.
Easy NORMAL · AS 5 | Change in Policy | Presentation
Under AS 5, a change in accounting policy should be made ONLY if required by statute, for compliance with an accounting standard, or if:
A. Management wants to minimize income tax liability
B. It results in a more appropriate presentation of financial statements ✔
C. The company wants to match figures with competitor companies
D. The board of directors passes a unanimous resolution for tax saving
