Explanation: AS 5 specifies that a change in accounting policy should be made only if required by statute, for compliance with an accounting standard, or if it is considered that the change would result in a more appropriate presentation of financial statements.
Medium NORMAL · AS 5 | Policy Change Disclosure | Material Impact
If a change in accounting policy has a material effect in the current period, what disclosure is mandatory under AS 5?
A. Impact of the change and the financial amount affected (if quantifiable) ✔
B. No disclosure required if management approves
C. Disclosure only in the directors' report
D. Restatement of last 3 years income statement
Explanation: AS 5 states that any change in accounting policy having material effect should be disclosed. The impact and the financial amount resulting from such change should be disclosed to the extent ascertainable.
Medium NORMAL · AS 11 | Exchange Difference | Borrowings
Under AS 11, when a loan in foreign currency is taken to acquire a qualifying fixed asset, how are exchange differences on such loan treated under standard AS 11 rules (excluding Para 46A option)?
A. Capitalized into the cost of the asset
B. Recognized as income or expense in Statement of Profit and Loss ✔
C. Transferred to Foreign Currency Monitory Item Translation Difference Account
D. Adjusted against Share Capital
Explanation: Under standard provisions of AS 11, exchange differences arising on foreign currency monetary liabilities are recognized as income or expense in the Statement of Profit and Loss in the period in which they arise.
Hard NORMAL · AS 22 | Total Tax Expense | Current Tax | Deferred Tax
A company has accounting profit before tax of ₹20,00,000 for FY 2025-26. Income tax computed as per tax law is ₹5,00,000. DTL created during the year is ₹1,00,000 and DTA created is ₹40,000. Total Tax Expense in P&L for FY 2025-26 is:
A. ₹5,60,000 ✔
B. ₹4,40,000
C. ₹5,00,000
D. ₹6,00,000
Explanation: Total Tax Expense = Current Tax Expense + Deferred Tax Charge = ₹5,00,000 + (DTL ₹1,00,000 - DTA ₹40,000) = ₹5,00,000 + ₹60,000 = ₹5,60,000.
Hard NORMAL · AS 11 | Non-Integral Indicators | Classification
Which of the following indicator suggests that a foreign operation is a NON-INTEGRAL foreign operation (NIFO) under AS 11?
A. Foreign operation activities are carried out as an integral extension of the reporting enterprise's operations
B. Transactions with reporting enterprise constitute a high proportion of foreign operation's activities
C. Foreign operation's activities are financed mainly from its own operations or local borrowings rather than by reporting enterprise ✔
D. Sales prices for foreign operation's products respond directly to day-to-day changes in Indian rupee
Explanation: AS 11 lists indicators of NIFO: activities financed mainly from local operations/borrowings, sales prices not primarily affected by local currency changes of parent, local operating expenses paid in local currency.
Medium NORMAL · AS 5 | Prior Period Item | Calculation Error
In FY 2025-26, Beta Ltd. discovered that depreciation on factory building was under-recorded by ₹3,00,000 in FY 2023-24 due to a mathematical computation error. Under AS 5, how should this ₹3,00,000 be treated in FY 2025-26?
A. Charged as current year depreciation under operating costs
B. Disclosed separately as a Prior Period Item in Profit & Loss statement ✔
C. Adjusted prospectively by increasing remaining depreciation rate
D. Ignored as it pertains to a closed accounting year
Explanation: Mathematical errors in prior financial statement calculations represent errors/omissions. Correction of such errors is treated as a Prior Period Item under AS 5 and disclosed separately in P&L of the current period.
Hard NORMAL · AS 22 | Substantively Enacted Rate | Measurement
Under AS 22, enacted or substantively enacted tax rates as of the balance sheet date are used for measuring deferred taxes. If new tax rate was passed by Parliament on 25th March 2026 (applicable for FY 2025-26 onwards), which rate is used to compute deferred tax as on 31st March 2026?
A. Old tax rate existing prior to 25th March
B. New tax rate passed on 25th March 2026 ✔
C. Average of old and new tax rates
D. Rate expected to be enacted in 2030
Explanation: AS 22 mandates that deferred tax assets and liabilities should be measured using the tax rates and tax laws that have been enacted or substantively enacted by the balance sheet date. The new rate passed on 25th March 2026 is enacted by 31st March 2026.
CASE SCENARIO: Apex Traders Ltd. is in the process of finalizing its financial statements for the financial year ended 31st March 2026. The Board of Directors is scheduled to approve the accounts on 20th May 2026. The following developments occurred between 31st March 2026 and 20th May 2026: 1. On 10th April 2026, a major debtor, Mr. Raman, owing ₹8,00,000 as on 31st March 2026, was declared insolvent. His insolvency was triggered by a factory fire at his premises on 5th April 2026. 2. On 25th April 2026, a fire occurred in Apex Traders Ltd.'s main godown destroying uninsured inventory valued at ₹12,00,000. 3. On 2nd May 2026, the accountant discovered an error: rent expense of ₹3,00,000 for FY 2024-25 had been completely omitted from the accounts of FY 2024-25. 4. On 10th May 2026, the company decided to revise the estimated remaining useful life of its delivery trucks from 5 years to 3 years due to heavy wear and tear.
Hard SCENARIO · AS 4 | Non-adjusting Event | Post Balance Sheet Event
How should the insolvency of Mr. Raman (debtor owing ₹8,00,000) be treated in the financial statements for FY 2025-26 under AS 4?
A. Adjusting event requiring provision/write-off of ₹8,00,000 in FY 2025-26 because the debt existed on balance sheet date
B. Non-adjusting event because the insolvency trigger (fire at debtor's factory) occurred after 31st March 2026 ✔
C. Disclosed only as a footnote in Directors' Report
D. Prior period item under AS 5
Explanation: Under AS 4, events occurring after the balance sheet date are non-adjusting if the condition causing the event (fire at debtor's premises on 5th April) did not exist on the balance sheet date (31st March). Thus, insolvency resulting entirely from a post-balance-sheet fire is a non-adjusting event, disclosed in notes if material.
Medium SCENARIO · AS 4 | Non-adjusting Event | Fire Loss
How should the godown fire loss of ₹12,00,000 occurring on 25th April 2026 be treated in financial statements for FY 2025-26 under AS 4?
A. Adjusted in financial statements by writing down inventory on 31st March 2026
B. Treated as a non-adjusting event and disclosed in the report of approving authority / notes to accounts ✔
C. Ignored completely as it occurred after 31st March 2026
D. Treated as an extraordinary prior period loss under AS 5
Explanation: Fire loss after balance sheet date is a non-adjusting event because the fire condition did not exist at the balance sheet date. Being material, disclosure must be made in the report of the approving authority / notes to accounts.
Medium SCENARIO · AS 5 | Prior Period Error | Omission
How should the omitted rent expense of ₹3,00,000 for FY 2024-25 be accounted for in FY 2025-26 under AS 5?
A. Adjusted directly against opening general reserve without showing in Statement of Profit and Loss
B. Disclosed separately as a Prior Period Item in the Statement of Profit and Loss of FY 2025-26 ✔
C. Included quietly in current period rent expense without separate disclosure
D. Restate the prior year financial statements of FY 2024-25
Explanation: Omission of rent in prior year is an error requiring treatment as a Prior Period Item under AS 5. It is disclosed separately in the current period (FY 2025-26) Statement of Profit and Loss.
Medium SCENARIO · AS 5 | AS 10 | Accounting Estimate | Prospective Effect
What is the correct accounting treatment for the revision of estimated remaining useful life of delivery trucks from 5 years to 3 years under AS 5 / AS 10?
A. Accounting policy change requiring retrospective recalculation of depreciation
B. Accounting estimate change applied prospectively by allocating remaining depreciable amount over 3 years ✔
C. Prior period error requiring separate line item disclosure
D. Extraordinary adjustment credited to capital reserve
Explanation: A revision in useful life of an asset is a change in accounting estimate. Under AS 5 and AS 10 (Revised), changes in accounting estimates are applied prospectively in current and future periods.
CASE SCENARIO: Global Tech Ltd., an Indian entity, reports under Indian GAAP (AS). On 1st December 2025, Global Tech Ltd. imported machinery from a US supplier for USD 200,000 when the exchange rate was USD 1 = ₹80. Payment was agreed to be settled on 30th April 2026. The exchange rate on 31st March 2026 was USD 1 = ₹83. On 30th April 2026, payment was completed when USD 1 = ₹82.50. Additionally, Global Tech Ltd. has a branch office in London, UK, which functions as an Integral Foreign Operation (IFO). The branch had trade receivables of GBP 50,000 on 31st March 2026 (rate on 31st March: GBP 1 = ₹105; exchange rate when sales took place: GBP 1 = ₹100). Global Tech Ltd. also owns a subsidiary in Dubai which functions as a Non-Integral Foreign Operation (NIFO).
Medium SCENARIO · AS 11 | Exchange Loss | Monetary Liability
What exchange difference should Global Tech Ltd. recognize in Profit & Loss for FY 2025-26 regarding the imported machinery payable under AS 11?
A. ₹6,00,000 Loss ✔
B. ₹6,00,000 Gain
C. ₹5,00,000 Loss
D. Capitalize ₹6,00,000 into machinery cost
Explanation: Initial recognition: USD 200,000 * 80 = ₹160,00,000. Balance sheet date (31st March 2026): USD 200,000 * 83 = ₹166,00,000. Exchange Loss = ₹166,00,000 - ₹160,00,000 = ₹6,00,000, charged to Profit & Loss.
Medium SCENARIO · AS 11 | Settlement Gain | Foreign Currency
What exchange gain or loss is recognized in Statement of Profit & Loss for FY 2026-27 upon actual payment on 30th April 2026 under AS 11?
A. Exchange Gain of ₹1,00,000 ✔
B. Exchange Loss of ₹1,00,000
C. Exchange Gain of ₹50,000
D. Exchange Loss of ₹50,000
Explanation: Carrying liability as on 1st April 2026 = USD 200,000 * 83 = ₹1,66,00,000. Payment made on 30th April 2026 = USD 200,000 * 82.50 = ₹1,65,00,000. Gain on settlement = ₹1,66,00,000 - ₹1,65,00,000 = ₹1,00,000 credited to P&L in FY 2026-27.
Hard SCENARIO · AS 11 | Integral Foreign Operation | Monetary Translation
How should London Branch's trade receivables of GBP 50,000 be translated at 31st March 2026, and what is the exchange difference under AS 11?
A. Translated at ₹100; No exchange difference
B. Translated at ₹105; Exchange gain of ₹2,50,000 charged to P&L ✔
C. Translated at ₹105; Exchange gain of ₹2,50,000 credited to FCTR reserve
D. Translated at average rate
Explanation: London branch is an Integral Foreign Operation (IFO). Monetary items (receivables) are translated at closing rate (GBP 1 = ₹105). Original transaction was recorded at ₹100. Gain = GBP 50,000 * (105 - 100) = ₹2,50,000 recognized in Statement of Profit and Loss.
Medium SCENARIO · AS 11 | NIFO | FCTR Reserve
Where should exchange differences arising on translation of Dubai Subsidiary's (NIFO) financial statements be accumulated under AS 11?
A. Charged directly to Statement of Profit and Loss
B. Capitalized into cost of subsidiary investment
C. Accumulated in Foreign Currency Translation Reserve (FCTR) ✔
D. Adjusted against Share Premium account
Explanation: Translation differences arising on translating financial statements of a Non-Integral Foreign Operation (NIFO) are accumulated in Foreign Currency Translation Reserve (FCTR) in the balance sheet until disposal of net investment.
CASE SCENARIO: Horizon Ltd. reports Accounting Profit before tax of ₹40,00,000 for the financial year ended 31st March 2026. The tax rate applicable is 30%. On analyzing financial records and tax rules, the following items are noted: 1. Depreciation as per books of account: ₹6,00,000; Depreciation allowable under Income Tax Act: ₹10,00,000. 2. Ineligible political donation disallowed under Tax Act: ₹1,00,000. 3. Expenditure on statutory dues disallowed under Section 43B in FY 2025-26 as it was paid after due date: ₹2,00,000. 4. Opening balances of DTA and DTL as on 1st April 2025 were NIL.
Hard SCENARIO · AS 22 | Taxable Income | Tax Computation
What is the total Taxable Income of Horizon Ltd. for FY 2025-26 under the Income Tax laws?
A. ₹39,00,000 ✔
B. ₹37,00,000
C. ₹43,00,000
D. ₹40,00,000
Explanation: Taxable Income = Accounting Profit (₹40,00,000) - Excess Tax Depreciation (₹10L - ₹6L = ₹4,00,000) + Disallowed political donation (₹1,00,000) + Section 43B disallowance (₹2,00,000) = 40,00,000 - 4,00,000 + 1,00,000 + 2,00,000 = ₹39,00,000.
Medium SCENARIO · AS 22 | Current Tax | Tax Expense
What is the Current Tax Expense for FY 2025-26 under AS 22?
A. ₹12,00,000
B. ₹11,70,000 ✔
C. ₹12,30,000
D. ₹11,10,000
Explanation: Current Tax Expense = Taxable Income * Tax Rate = ₹39,00,000 * 30% = ₹11,70,000.
Hard SCENARIO · AS 22 | Net Deferred Tax | DTL Calculation
What is the Net Deferred Tax position (Asset/Liability) to be recognized in the Balance Sheet as on 31st March 2026?
A. Net Deferred Tax Liability of ₹60,000 ✔
B. Net Deferred Tax Asset of ₹60,000
C. Net Deferred Tax Liability of ₹1,20,000
D. Net Deferred Tax Asset of ₹30,000
Explanation: Timing difference 1 (Depreciation): Tax dep > Book dep by ₹4,00,000 -> Taxable timing diff -> DTL = 4,00,000 * 30% = ₹1,20,000. Timing difference 2 (Sec 43B): Book exp > Tax exp by ₹2,00,000 -> Deductible timing diff -> DTA = 2,00,000 * 30% = ₹60,000. Net DTL = ₹1,20,000 - ₹60,000 = ₹60,000 DTL.
Hard SCENARIO · AS 22 | Total Tax Expense | Profit and Loss Impact
What is the Total Tax Expense (Current Tax + Deferred Tax) charged in the Statement of Profit and Loss for FY 2025-26?
A. ₹12,30,000 ✔
B. ₹11,70,000
C. ₹12,00,000
D. ₹12,60,000
Explanation: Total Tax Expense = Current Tax (₹11,70,000) + Net Deferred Tax Charge (₹60,000) = ₹12,30,000. Alternatively: Tax on [Accounting Profit ₹40L + Permanent Diff ₹1L] * 30% = ₹41L * 30% = ₹12,30,000.
CASE SCENARIO: Zenith Exports Ltd. exported goods to a US customer on 1st January 2026 worth USD 100,000 when the spot exchange rate was USD 1 = ₹80. Payment is due on 31st May 2026. To hedge against foreign currency fluctuation risk, Zenith Exports Ltd. entered into a 5-month forward exchange contract on 1st January 2026 to sell USD 100,000 at a forward rate of USD 1 = ₹83. On 31st March 2026 (the balance sheet date), the spot exchange rate was USD 1 = ₹82. Financial year ends on 31st March 2026.
Medium SCENARIO · AS 11 | Forward Contract | Premium Amortization
What is the total premium on the forward contract and how should it be recognized under AS 11?
A. ₹3,00,000 Premium, amortized over the 5-month contract life ✔
B. ₹3,00,000 Discount, charged immediately to Profit & Loss
C. ₹2,00,000 Premium, capitalized into export sales
D. ₹3,00,000 Premium, credited entirely to FY 2025-26 P&L
Explanation: Total Premium = (Forward Rate ₹83 - Spot Rate ₹80) * USD 100,000 = ₹3,00,000. Under AS 11, forward contract premium for hedging is amortized as income/expense over the contract period (5 months).
Hard SCENARIO · AS 11 | Premium Proportion | Financial Year Allocation
How much forward contract premium should be credited/amortized in the Statement of Profit and Loss for FY 2025-26 (ending 31st March 2026)?
A. ₹3,00,000
B. ₹1,80,000 ✔
C. ₹1,20,000
D. ₹1,50,000
Explanation: Period in FY 2025-26: Jan, Feb, Mar = 3 months out of 5 months. Premium amortized for FY 2025-26 = ₹3,00,000 * (3/5) = ₹1,80,000.
Medium SCENARIO · AS 11 | Debtor Revaluation | Exchange Gain
What exchange difference arises on the revaluation of the foreign currency debtor (USD 100,000) at 31st March 2026 under AS 11?
A. Exchange Gain of ₹2,00,000 credited to P&L ✔
B. Exchange Loss of ₹2,00,000 charged to P&L
C. Exchange Gain of ₹3,00,000 credited to P&L
D. No exchange gain/loss as it is hedged
Explanation: Debtor recorded initially at USD 100,000 * 80 = ₹80,00,000. On 31st March 2026, rate is ₹82. Revalued debtor = USD 100,000 * 82 = ₹82,00,000. Exchange gain = ₹82,00,000 - ₹80,00,000 = ₹2,00,000 credited to Profit & Loss.
Hard SCENARIO · AS 11 | Net P&L Impact | Hedging Accounting
What is the NET impact on the Statement of Profit and Loss for FY 2025-26 from both the foreign debtor revaluation and forward contract premium amortization combined?
A. Net Credit (Income) of ₹3,80,000 ✔
B. Net Credit (Income) of ₹2,00,000
C. Net Debit (Expense) of ₹1,20,000
D. Net Credit (Income) of ₹1,80,000
Explanation: Exchange Gain on Debtor = ₹2,00,000 (Credit) + Forward Premium amortized = ₹1,80,000 (Credit) = Total Net Credit to Profit & Loss of ₹3,80,000.
CASE SCENARIO: Vayu Infra Ltd. is finalizing its accounts for the year ended 31st March 2026. The following three independent cases are brought to the chief financial officer's attention: Case A: On 15th April 2026, before approval of accounts, a major government license was revoked due to regulatory non-compliance, forcing the entity to shut down its primary operating plant. Management concludes that Going Concern assumption is compromised. Case B: The company has unabsorbed tax depreciation of ₹30,00,000 carried forward from FY 2024-25. In FY 2025-26, the company turned profitable and secured binding, long-term non-cancellable export contracts ensuring substantial taxable profits for the next 4 years. Case C: The Board of Directors in its meeting on 20th May 2026 recommended a dividend of ₹10,00,000 for FY 2025-26.
Hard SCENARIO · AS 4 | Going Concern Compromised | Financial Statement Preparation
In Case A, how should the financial statements for FY 2025-26 be prepared following the revocation of license under AS 4?
A. Prepared on going concern basis with disclosure in directors' report
B. Prepared on non-going concern basis (liquidation / net realizable value basis), adjusting carrying values of assets and liabilities ✔
C. Disclosed as a footnote without altering balance sheet numbers
D. Accounts for FY 2025-26 postponed to next financial year
Explanation: Under AS 4, if events after balance sheet date indicate that the going concern assumption is no longer appropriate, the financial statements must be prepared on a non-going concern (liquidation/realizable value) basis.
Medium SCENARIO · AS 22 | DTA Recognition | Virtual Certainty
In Case B, can Vayu Infra Ltd. recognize Deferred Tax Asset (DTA) on unabsorbed depreciation under AS 22?
A. No, DTA on unabsorbed depreciation can never be recognized under any circumstances
B. Yes, provided there is virtual certainty supported by convincing evidence (e.g. binding non-cancellable contracts) that future taxable income will be available ✔
C. Yes, based on general management expectation of future profits without evidence
D. No, only DTL can be recognized
Explanation: AS 22 permits recognition of DTA for unabsorbed depreciation/carried forward loss ONLY when there is virtual certainty supported by convincing evidence. Binding, non-cancellable long-term profit contracts constitute convincing evidence.
Easy SCENARIO · AS 4 | Proposed Dividend | Notes Disclosure
In Case C, how should the recommended dividend of ₹10,00,000 be treated in financial statements for FY 2025-26 under revised AS 4?
A. Provided as a liability in the balance sheet as on 31st March 2026
B. Debited to Profit and Loss statement as an operating cost
C. Not recognized as a liability on balance sheet date, but disclosed in notes to accounts ✔
D. Deducted directly from Share Capital
Explanation: As per revised AS 4, dividends declared after the balance sheet date are not recognized as a liability at the balance sheet date. They are disclosed in the notes to financial statements.
Medium SCENARIO · AS 5 | Accounting Policy Change | Disclosure
If Vayu Infra Ltd. changes its inventory valuation method from FIFO to Weighted Average method in FY 2025-26 for better presentation, how should this be disclosed under AS 5?
A. Disclose reasons for change, change in policy, and financial impact in current year if ascertainable ✔
B. No disclosure necessary as both are permitted under AS 2
C. Disclose only in the tax audit report
D. Restate comparative prior year inventory figures
Explanation: AS 5 mandates that any change in accounting policy which has a material effect should be disclosed along with the financial impact and reasons for change to enable users to understand the impact.

Paper 1: Advanced Accounting · Module 2 · Chapter 8:

Accounts — 55 rows
Easy NORMAL · AS 7 | Segmenting Construction Contracts
According to AS 7 'Construction Contracts', when a contract covers a number of assets, the construction of each asset should be treated as a separate construction contract if:
A. Separate proposals have been submitted for each asset, and each asset has been subject to separate negotiation. ✔
B. The total contract costs and revenues can be identified, regardless of separate proposals.
C. The customer accepts a single bundled price for all assets combined.
D. The assets are constructed simultaneously at the same geographical location.
Explanation: Under AS 7, the construction of each asset should be treated as a separate construction contract when separate proposals have been submitted, each asset has been subject to separate negotiation (where contractor and customer can accept or reject that part), and costs and revenues of each asset can be identified.
Easy NORMAL · AS 9 | Rendering of Services
Under AS 9 'Revenue Recognition', revenue from service transactions rendered over time should be recognized using:
A. Completed contract method only.
B. Proportionate completion method or completed service contract method depending on the nature of transaction. ✔
C. Cash basis upon receipt of full service fees.
D. Straight-line basis over a mandatory 12-month period.
Explanation: AS 9 provides that performance should be measured under either the proportionate completion method or the completed service contract method, depending on whether the service consists of the execution of a series of acts or a single/specific act.
Easy NORMAL · AS 7 | Contract Costs
Which of the following items should be EXCLUDED from contract costs under AS 7?
A. Costs of materials consumed in construction.
B. Depreciation of plant and equipment used on the contract.
C. General administration costs for which reimbursement is not specified in the contract. ✔
D. Direct site supervision costs.
Explanation: General administration costs for which reimbursement is not specified in the contract are excluded from contract costs under AS 7 and charged directly to the Statement of Profit and Loss.
Easy NORMAL · AS 9 | Interest Income
Under AS 9, interest revenue should be recognized on which of the following bases?
A. Cash basis when payment is actually received.
B. Time proportion basis taking into account the amount outstanding and the rate applicable. ✔
C. Equal installments over the contract period irrespective of outstanding balance.
D. When the underlying principal amount is fully recovered.
Explanation: AS 9 mandates that interest revenue shall be recognized on a time proportion basis taking into account the amount outstanding and the applicable interest rate.
Medium NORMAL · AS 7 | Contract Revenue | Incentive Payments
Under AS 7, incentive payments are included in contract revenue when:
A. The contract is at least 90% complete.
B. The contractor decides to bill the customer for early completion.
C. The contract is sufficiently advanced that it is probable that the specified performance standards will be met or exceeded, and the amount can be measured reliably. ✔
D. The customer gives written approval after the contract completion.
Explanation: AS 7 states that incentive payments are included in contract revenue when the contract is sufficiently advanced that it is probable that the specified performance standards will be met or exceeded, and the incentive amount can be measured reliably.
Easy NORMAL · AS 9 | Consignment Sales
When goods are sold on a 'Consignment' basis, when should the consignor recognize revenue under AS 9?
A. When goods are dispatched to the consignee.
B. When the consignee receives the goods at their warehouse.
C. When the consignee sells the goods to a third party. ✔
D. When the consignee remits the cash to the consignor.
Explanation: Under AS 9, revenue from consignment sales is recognized by the consignor only when the goods are sold by the consignee to a third party, as risk and rewards are transferred at that point.
Easy NORMAL · AS 7 | Percentage of Completion Method
Build Tech Ltd. entered into a fixed price contract of ₹500 lakhs. Total estimated cost was ₹400 lakhs. At year-end, costs incurred were ₹100 lakhs. Percentage of completion and contract revenue to be recognized are:
A. 25% and ₹125 lakhs ✔
B. 20% and ₹100 lakhs
C. 25% and ₹100 lakhs
D. 20% and ₹125 lakhs
Explanation: Percentage of completion = Costs incurred / Total estimated cost = ₹100 lakhs / ₹400 lakhs = 25%. Contract revenue to be recognized = 25% of ₹500 lakhs = ₹125 lakhs.
Easy NORMAL · AS 9 | Dividend Income
How should dividends from investments in shares be recognized under AS 9?
A. On a time proportion basis over the financial year.
B. When the declaree company publishes its audited accounts.
C. When the owner's right to receive payment is established. ✔
D. When cash dividend is credited to the bank account.
Explanation: AS 9 states that revenue from dividend on investments in shares is recognized when the owner's right to receive payment is established (typically when dividends are declared by shareholders in an AGM).
Medium NORMAL · AS 7 | Expected Loss Recognition
Under AS 7, when it is probable that total contract costs will exceed total contract revenue, the expected loss should be:
A. Recognized as an expense immediately, regardless of the stage of completion. ✔
B. Recognized proportionately over the remaining period of the contract.
C. Deferred and amortized after contract completion.
D. Ignored until the contract is completely finished.
Explanation: According to AS 7 paragraph 35, when it is probable that total contract costs will exceed total contract revenue, the expected loss should be recognized as an expense immediately regardless of the stage of completion or work performed.
Medium NORMAL · AS 9 | Rendering of Services | Tuition Fees
Under AS 9, revenue from tuition fees received for a course spanning 6 months across two financial years should be recognized:
A. 100% in the financial year in which fees are collected.
B. 100% in the financial year in which the course ends.
C. Pro-rata over the period of the course as services are rendered. ✔
D. At the option of the management based on tax preference.
Explanation: Tuition fees represent rendering of service over time; hence revenue should be recognized pro-rata over the period of the course as the services are provided across the financial accounting periods.
Medium NORMAL · AS 7 | Degree of Completion
A contractor undertakes a construction contract for ₹800 lakhs. Costs incurred to date are ₹300 lakhs and estimated costs to complete are ₹500 lakhs. Work certified is ₹250 lakhs. Using the cost proportion method under AS 7, what is the degree of completion?
A. 31.25%
B. 37.50% ✔
C. 60.00%
D. 50.00%
Explanation: Total estimated contract cost = Costs incurred (₹300) + Costs to complete (₹500) = ₹800 lakhs. Degree of completion = Cost incurred / Total estimated cost = ₹300 / ₹800 = 37.5%.
Easy NORMAL · AS 9 | Uncertainty of Collection
Under AS 9, if at the time of sale of goods there is significant uncertainty regarding ultimate collection of the consideration, revenue recognition should be:
A. Recognized fully and provision for bad debts created.
B. Postponed until the uncertainty is resolved. ✔
C. Recognized to the extent of cost of goods sold only.
D. Recognized at 50% of the invoice value.
Explanation: AS 9 paragraph 9 specifies that where the ability to assess the ultimate collection with reasonable certainty is lacking at the time of raising any claim, revenue recognition should be postponed until such uncertainty is removed.
Easy NORMAL · AS 7 | Cost Plus Contract
In a Cost Plus Contract under AS 7, the contractor is reimbursed for:
A. Only direct material costs plus a fixed percentage of total revenue.
B. Allowable or otherwise defined costs plus a percentage of these costs or a fixed fee. ✔
C. A fixed agreed sum irrespective of actual costs incurred.
D. Costs incurred plus an escalation clause for inflation only.
Explanation: AS 7 defines a cost plus contract as a construction contract in which the contractor is reimbursed for allowable or otherwise defined costs, plus a percentage of these costs or a fixed fee.
Easy NORMAL · AS 9 | Royalty Income
Under AS 9, royalties should be recognized on which accounting basis?
A. Cash basis as and when received.
B. Accrual basis in accordance with the terms of the relevant agreement. ✔
C. At the end of the patent/licensing term in lump sum.
D. Equal monthly installments over 5 years.
Explanation: AS 9 requires royalties (for use of assets like patents, trademarks, copyrights) to be recognized on an accrual basis in accordance with the terms of the relevant agreement.
Hard NORMAL · AS 7 | Variations | Multi-period Revenue
Apex Contractors had an initial contract value of ₹1,000 lakhs. During Year 2, customer approved a variation increasing contract value by ₹100 lakhs. Costs incurred till Year 2 are ₹660 lakhs and total estimated costs are ₹880 lakhs. Revenue recognized in Year 1 was ₹250 lakhs. Revenue to be recognized in Year 2 is:
A. ₹575 lakhs ✔
B. ₹825 lakhs
C. ₹500 lakhs
D. ₹570 lakhs
Explanation: Updated Contract Value = ₹1,000 + ₹100 = ₹1,100 lakhs. Stage of completion = ₹660 / ₹880 = 75%. Cumulative revenue to end of Year 2 = 75% of ₹1,100 = ₹825 lakhs. Revenue for Year 2 = Cumulative revenue (₹825) - Year 1 revenue (₹250) = ₹575 lakhs.
Medium NORMAL · AS 9 | Bill and Hold Sales
Under AS 9, when goods are sold on 'Bill and Hold' terms (delivery delayed at buyer's request), revenue can be recognized if:
A. The buyer makes full advance payment.
B. It is probable that delivery will be made, item is identified, ready for delivery, and usual payment terms apply. ✔
C. The seller transfers physical possession to a public warehouse.
D. The buyer signs a non-cancellable indemnity bond.
Explanation: Under AS 9, in 'bill and hold' sales, revenue is recognized before physical delivery if the buyer takes title and accepts billing, provided it is probable delivery will be made, the goods are identified and ready, and buyer acknowledges delay instructions.
Medium NORMAL · AS 7 | Claims
Under AS 7, claims are included in contract revenue only when:
A. The contractor has submitted the claim to an arbitration panel.
B. Negotiations have reached an advanced stage such that it is probable the customer will accept the claim, and the amount can be measured reliably. ✔
C. The court issues an order enforcing payment.
D. The customer pays 50% advance against the claim.
Explanation: Under AS 7, a claim is an amount that contractor seeks to collect from customer as reimbursement for costs not included in contract price. It is included in revenue only when negotiations have reached an advanced stage, customer acceptance is probable, and amount is reliably measurable.
Medium NORMAL · AS 9 | Agency Relationship | Gross vs Net
An agency company sells goods on behalf of a principal for ₹10,000. The agent is entitled to a 10% commission. How should the agent recognize revenue under AS 9?
A. Gross revenue of ₹10,000 and expense of ₹9,000.
B. Net revenue of ₹1,000 commission. ✔
C. Gross revenue of ₹9,000.
D. Revenue recognition deferred until principal receives money.
Explanation: In an agency relationship, gross inflows include amounts collected on behalf of the principal which do not result in increase in equity for the agent. Revenue of the agent is only the amount of commission ( net ₹1,000).
Easy NORMAL · AS 7 | Direct Contract Costs
Under AS 7, costs that relate directly to a specific contract include:
A. Insurance of general corporate office.
B. Site labor costs, including site supervision. ✔
C. Depreciation of idle equipment not used on any contract.
D. Research and development costs not specified in contract.
Explanation: Site labor costs, including site supervision, are directly attributable costs related to a specific contract under AS 7.
Medium NORMAL · AS 9 | Subscription Income
A publisher receives ₹12,000 as annual subscription fees for a monthly magazine in advance on 1st October. The financial year ends on 31st March. Under AS 9, how much revenue should be recognized in the financial year of receipt?
A. ₹12,000
B. ₹6,000 ✔
C. ₹3,000
D. Nil
Explanation: Subscription revenue for publications issued on a regular time basis should be recognized on a straight-line basis over the subscription period. October to March represents 6 months out of 12; hence ₹12,000 * 6/12 = ₹6,000.
Medium NORMAL · AS 7 | Unrecoverable Costs
When costs incurred on a construction contract are not recoverable (e.g., contract validity subject to pending litigation), how should they be treated under AS 7?
A. Capitalized under Work-in-Progress asset.
B. Recognized immediately as an expense. ✔
C. Disclosed as a contingent liability only.
D. Deferred until litigation is settled.
Explanation: Under AS 7, when the outcome of a construction contract cannot be estimated reliably or costs incurred are not recoverable, costs should be recognized as an expense in the period in which they are incurred.
Medium NORMAL · AS 9 | Advertising Income
Under AS 9, revenue from advertising agency commission for media space/time booked should be recognized when:
A. The advertisement contract is signed.
B. The related advertisement or commercial appears before the public. ✔
C. The client pays the agency bill.
D. The media house sends the bill to the agency.
Explanation: According to AS 9 appendix, media commissions received by advertising agencies are recognized when the related advertisement or commercial appears before the public.
Hard NORMAL · AS 7 | Contract Profit Calculation
In a construction contract, total contract price is ₹1,200 lakhs. Cumulative costs incurred till end of Year 1 are ₹300 lakhs, and estimated further costs to complete are ₹900 lakhs. During Year 2, costs incurred are ₹500 lakhs and estimated further costs to complete are ₹400 lakhs. What is the contract profit or loss to be recognized in Year 2 P&L?
A. Zero profit/loss
B. ₹50 lakhs loss
C. ₹100 lakhs loss
D. Zero profit in Year 1 and Zero profit in Year 2 ✔
Explanation: Year 1: Total estimated costs = 300 + 900 = 1200 lakhs. Total profit expected = 1200 - 1200 = 0. Revenue Y1 = (300/1200)*1200 = 300. Y1 Profit = 300 - 300 = 0. Year 2: Cumulative costs = 300 + 500 = 800 lakhs. Total estimated costs = 800 + 400 = 1200 lakhs. Expected profit = 1200 - 1200 = 0. Cumulative revenue = (800/1200)*1200 = 800 lakhs. Y2 Revenue = 800 - 300 = 500 lakhs. Y2 Profit = 500 - 500 = 0.
Hard NORMAL · AS 9 | Layaway Sales
Under AS 9, revenue from sale of goods on 'Layaway Sales' (where buyer makes a series of installments and seller delivers only after final payment) is recognized when:
A. The first installment is received.
B. 50% of installments are received.
C. Goods are delivered, provided a significant deposit has been received and goods are on hand. ✔
D. The agreement is signed.
Explanation: Under layaway sales, revenue is recognized when the goods are delivered. However, if experience indicates that most such sales are completed, revenue may be recognized when a significant deposit is received, provided goods are on hand and identified.
Medium NORMAL · AS 7 | Combining Contracts
Contractor X enters into a single contract for constructing three structures for a single client. Under AS 7, the contractor must combine the construction of the three structures and treat it as a single contract if:
A. The group of contracts is negotiated as a single package with a single overall profit margin. ✔
B. The structures are located in different cities.
C. Each structure has separate design blueprints.
D. The customer pays in three separate bank transfers.
Explanation: AS 7 requires a group of contracts/assets to be treated as a single construction contract when the group is negotiated as a single package, contracts are closely interrelated with an overall profit margin, and performed concurrently or sequentially.
Easy NORMAL · AS 9 | Trade Discounts | Turnover Calculation
Under AS 9, trade discounts and volume rebates should be:
A. Deducted from gross turnover to determine recognized revenue. ✔
B. Shown as an operating expense in P&L.
C. Ignored while recognizing revenue.
D. Credited to capital reserve account.
Explanation: AS 9 defines revenue as the gross inflow of cash or consideration. Trade discounts and volume rebates given to customers are deducted from gross turnover to determine net revenue recognized.
Medium NORMAL · AS 7 | Plant Depreciation | Contract Cost
Under AS 7, how should plant and machinery specially purchased for a specific construction contract be treated?
A. Full purchase cost charged to contract costs in the first year.
B. Depreciation over its useful life allocated as contract cost for the duration used on the contract. ✔
C. Excluded from contract costs entirely.
D. Capitalized in client's books directly.
Explanation: Depreciation of plant and equipment used on the contract is an attributable contract cost under AS 7 over the duration of its use on that contract.
Hard NORMAL · AS 9 | Installation Fees
Under AS 9, when an installation fee is charged for installing software/equipment, when should this fee be recognized as revenue?
A. Immediately upon receipt of money.
B. By reference to the stage of completion of installation, unless incidental to the sale of goods. ✔
C. At the end of warranty period.
D. Over 5 years evenly.
Explanation: Installation fees are recognized as revenue by reference to the stage of completion of installation, unless they are incidental to the sale of a product, in which case they are recognized when the goods are sold.
Hard NORMAL · AS 7 | Gross Amount Due From/To Customers | Disclosures
Under AS 7, what is the amount of 'Gross amount due from customers for contract work' to be disclosed as an asset?
A. Contract costs incurred plus recognized profits less recognized losses and progress billings (when this sum is positive). ✔
B. Total progress billings received minus contract costs incurred.
C. Contract price minus total progress billings received.
D. Contract costs incurred minus retention money.
Explanation: AS 7 paragraph 39 defines 'Gross amount due from customers' as (Costs Incurred + Recognized Profits - Recognized Losses) minus Progress Billings, where this net amount is positive (an asset). If negative, it is 'Gross amount due to customers' (a liability).
Medium NORMAL · AS 9 | Sale on Approval
Company A sells goods to Company B for ₹500,000 on 'sale or return' (approval basis). Company B has 30 days to return. At the balance sheet date, 10 days have elapsed and B has neither accepted nor returned the goods. How should Company A recognize this under AS 9?
A. Recognize revenue of ₹500,000 completely.
B. Do not recognize revenue; retain goods in inventory at cost. ✔
C. Recognize 50% revenue.
D. Recognize full revenue but make 100% provision for bad debts.
Explanation: Under AS 9, for goods delivered on approval/sale or return terms, revenue is recognized only when the buyer has formally accepted the goods or the time limit for rejection has expired. Since approval is pending and time hasn't expired, no revenue is recognized.
CASE SCENARIO: Infra Developers Ltd. was awarded a construction contract on 1st April 2024 to build a commercial bridge complex for an agreed fixed price of ₹2,000 lakhs. The initial financial details and actual estimates were as follows: - Year 1 (2024-25): Costs incurred = ₹500 lakhs; Estimated additional costs to complete = ₹1,000 lakhs; Progress billings during Year 1 = ₹450 lakhs; Amount collected against billings = ₹400 lakhs. - Year 2 (2025-26): Costs incurred during Year 2 = ₹900 lakhs (Cumulative costs incurred = ₹1,400 lakhs); Estimated additional costs to complete = ₹700 lakhs (Total estimated costs increased to ₹2,100 lakhs); Progress billings raised during Year 2 = ₹950 lakhs (Cumulative billings = ₹1,400 lakhs); Amount collected during Year 2 = ₹900 lakhs. The company measures stage of completion using the cost proportion method as per AS 7 'Construction Contracts'.
Medium SCENARIO · AS 7 | Percentage of Completion Method | Contract Revenue
For Year 1 (2024-25), what is the percentage of completion and the revenue to be recognized in the Statement of Profit and Loss?
A. 25% completion; Revenue = ₹500 lakhs
B. 33.33% completion; Revenue = ₹666.67 lakhs ✔
C. 33.33% completion; Revenue = ₹500 lakhs
D. 25% completion; Revenue = ₹450 lakhs
Explanation: Total estimated cost Y1 = 500 + 1000 = ₹1,500 lakhs. Stage of completion = 500 / 1500 = 33.33%. Revenue to be recognized = 33.33% of ₹2,000 lakhs = ₹666.67 lakhs.
Hard SCENARIO · AS 7 | Expected Contract Loss
At the end of Year 2 (2025-26), what is the total expected contract loss and how should it be treated under AS 7?
A. Expected loss is ₹100 lakhs, recognized proportionately over Year 2 and Year 3.
B. Expected loss is ₹100 lakhs, recognized as an expense immediately in Year 2. ✔
C. Expected loss is ₹700 lakhs, deferred until completion.
D. Expected loss is ₹100 lakhs, adjusted against progress billings liability.
Explanation: Total estimated contract cost at end of Y2 = ₹1,400 + ₹700 = ₹2,100 lakhs. Contract price = ₹2,000 lakhs. Total expected loss = 2100 - 2000 = ₹100 lakhs. Under AS 7 para 35, total expected loss of ₹100 lakhs must be recognized as an expense immediately.
Hard SCENARIO · AS 7 | Yearly Profit Loss Calculation
What is the net profit or loss to be recognized in the Statement of Profit and Loss for Year 2 (2025-26) alone?
A. Loss of ₹100.00 lakhs
B. Loss of ₹266.67 lakhs ✔
C. Loss of ₹166.67 lakhs
D. Profit of ₹66.67 lakhs
Explanation: In Y1, profit recognized = Revenue (666.67) - Costs (500) = ₹166.67 lakhs profit. By end of Y2, total expected contract loss is ₹100 lakhs (cumulative position must show cumulative loss of ₹100 lakhs). To reflect a cumulative loss of ₹100 lakhs when Y1 showed +166.67 lakhs profit, Y2 P&L charge must be: Expected Cumulative Loss (-100) - Y1 Profit (+166.67) = Loss of ₹266.67 lakhs in Y2.
Hard SCENARIO · AS 7 | Gross Amount Due To/From Customers
At the end of Year 2 (2025-26), what is the 'Gross amount due to/from customers' to be disclosed in the balance sheet under AS 7?
A. Gross amount due from customers of ₹100 lakhs
B. Gross amount due to customers of ₹100 lakhs ✔
C. Gross amount due to customers of ₹200 lakhs
D. Gross amount due from customers of ₹50 lakhs
Explanation: Formula: Costs Incurred (1400) + Recognized Profits/Losses (-100) - Progress Billings (1400) = 1300 - 1400 = -₹100 lakhs. Since it is negative, it represents a 'Gross amount due to customers' of ₹100 lakhs (a liability).
CASE SCENARIO: TechVision Solutions Ltd. provides enterprise software solutions and hardware equipment. During FY 2024-25, the company engaged in the following transactions: 1. On 1st October 2024, sold specialized hardware worth ₹50 lakhs to Client A. The hardware installation was complex and completed on 15th December 2024. Payment was received in full on 31st January 2025. 2. On 1st July 2024, entered into a 3-year Annual Maintenance Contract (AMC) for ₹36 lakhs with Client B, received fully in advance. Service is rendered evenly over 3 years (36 months). 3. On 1st January 2025, granted a software user license key to Client C for ₹12 lakhs. The software is delivered and functional immediately, with no further performance required by TechVision. 4. Sold goods to Client D for ₹20 lakhs with delayed payment terms (credit period 1 year). The normal cash sale price of goods is ₹18 lakhs.
Medium SCENARIO · AS 9 | Installation Services | Sale of Goods
Regarding Transaction 1 (Hardware sale to Client A), when and how much revenue should TechVision recognize in FY 2024-25 under AS 9?
A. ₹50 lakhs on 1st October 2024 upon contract signing.
B. ₹50 lakhs on 15th December 2024 when installation is completed. ✔
C. ₹50 lakhs on 31st January 2025 upon cash receipt.
D. ₹25 lakhs on 15th December 2024 and ₹25 lakhs on cash receipt.
Explanation: Where installation is significant and complex, performance is not complete until installation is finished. Therefore, revenue of ₹50 lakhs is recognized on 15th December 2024 upon completion of installation.
Medium SCENARIO · AS 9 | Rendering of Services | AMC Revenue
For Transaction 2 (3-year AMC with Client B), how much revenue should be recognized in the P&L for FY 2024-25 (ended 31st March 2025)?
A. ₹36 lakhs
B. ₹9 lakhs ✔
C. ₹12 lakhs
D. ₹18 lakhs
Explanation: The AMC runs from 1st July 2024 to 30th June 2027 (36 months). In FY 2024-25, 9 months (July 2024 to March 2025) have elapsed. Revenue recognized = ₹36 lakhs * (9/36) = ₹9 lakhs.
Medium SCENARIO · AS 9 | License Fee Revenue
For Transaction 3 (Software user license to Client C), how much revenue should be recognized in FY 2024-25?
A. ₹3 lakhs (pro-rata for 3 months)
B. ₹12 lakhs fully in FY 2024-25 ✔
C. Nil, until the end of 1st year of license
D. ₹6 lakhs
Explanation: When an entity grants a license where software is delivered, functional, and no ongoing obligations remain, the entire license fee (₹12 lakhs) is recognized as revenue upon transfer/delivery.
Hard SCENARIO · AS 9 | Financing Component | Interest Income
In Transaction 4 (Sale to Client D for ₹20 lakhs with normal price ₹18 lakhs), how should the ₹20 lakhs consideration be split under AS 9?
A. ₹20 lakhs recognized as sale of goods revenue immediately.
B. ₹18 lakhs recognized as sale of goods revenue immediately, and ₹2 lakhs recognized as interest income over the 1-year credit period. ✔
C. ₹20 lakhs deferred until payment is collected after 1 year.
D. ₹18 lakhs sale revenue and ₹2 lakhs capital reserve.
Explanation: When the payment is deferred beyond normal credit terms, the arrangement contains a financing element. Under AS 9, sale of goods is recognized at fair value/cash price (₹18 lakhs) immediately, and the excess (₹2 lakhs) is recognized as interest revenue over the credit period.
CASE SCENARIO: Urban Structures Ltd. undertakes two construction projects during FY 2024-25 for separate clients: Project Alpha: A residential complex under a single contract with Client X for ₹1,500 lakhs. During the year, Urban Structures incurred ₹400 lakhs cost. Total estimated cost was ₹1,000 lakhs. Client X approved a variation order increasing contract scope and price by ₹100 lakhs. The variation costs are estimated at ₹60 lakhs. Project Beta: Construction of a commercial building for Client Y for ₹800 lakhs. Costs incurred during FY 2024-25 were ₹200 lakhs, but due to severe structural instability and legal disputes over land title, Urban Structures cannot reliably estimate the total outcome or total costs to complete. However, costs incurred of ₹200 lakhs are expected to be recoverable from Client Y.
Hard SCENARIO · AS 7 | Contract Variation | Stage of Completion
For Project Alpha, what is the revised total estimated cost and stage of completion percentage at the end of FY 2024-25?
A. Total estimated cost = ₹1,060 lakhs; Completion = 37.74% ✔
B. Total estimated cost = ₹1,000 lakhs; Completion = 40.00%
C. Total estimated cost = ₹1,060 lakhs; Completion = 40.00%
D. Total estimated cost = ₹1,600 lakhs; Completion = 25.00%
Explanation: Revised Total Estimated Cost = Original estimated cost (₹1,000) + Variation cost (₹60) = ₹1,060 lakhs. Stage of completion = Cost incurred (₹400) / Revised total cost (₹1,060) = 37.7358% (approx 37.74%).
Hard SCENARIO · AS 7 | Contract Revenue Calculation
For Project Alpha, what is the total contract revenue to be recognized in FY 2024-25?
A. ₹566.10 lakhs
B. ₹603.84 lakhs ✔
C. ₹600.00 lakhs
D. ₹400.00 lakhs
Explanation: Revised Contract Price = Original Price (₹1,500) + Variation (₹100) = ₹1,600 lakhs. Revenue recognized = Stage of completion (37.7358%) * ₹1,600 lakhs = ₹603.77 ~ ₹603.84 lakhs.
Hard SCENARIO · AS 7 | Unreliable Outcome Contract
How should contract revenue and profit for Project Beta be recognized in FY 2024-25 under AS 7?
A. Recognize revenue of ₹200 lakhs and zero profit. ✔
B. Recognize zero revenue and zero cost in P&L.
C. Recognize estimated revenue of ₹800 lakhs and expected loss immediately.
D. Recognize revenue of ₹200 lakhs and profit of ₹50 lakhs.
Explanation: Under AS 7 paragraph 31, when the outcome of a construction contract cannot be estimated reliably, revenue should be recognized only to the extent of contract costs incurred that are probable of recovery (₹200 lakhs). Thus, contract costs (₹200 lakhs) are recognized as expense, resulting in zero profit.
Hard SCENARIO · AS 7 | Unrecoverable Costs | P&L Impact
Suppose for Project Beta, costs incurred were ₹200 lakhs but ONLY ₹120 lakhs were probable of recovery. What amount of loss should be recognized in P&L?
A. ₹80 lakhs loss ✔
B. Zero loss
C. ₹200 lakhs loss
D. ₹120 lakhs loss
Explanation: Revenue recognized = recoverable amount = ₹120 lakhs. Total costs incurred recognized as expense = ₹200 lakhs. Net loss in P&L = ₹120 - ₹200 = -₹80 lakhs (loss of ₹80 lakhs).
CASE SCENARIO: Global Goods Ltd., a diversified trading entity, engaged in four distinct sales arrangements during FY 2024-25: 1. Consignment Sales: Dispatched goods costing ₹10 lakhs to Agent X on consignment. Agent X sold 60% of these goods for ₹9 lakhs before 31st March 2025 and deducted 10% commission. The remaining 40% remained unsold in Agent X's godown. 2. Sale on Approval: Sent goods worth ₹5 lakhs (selling price ₹7 lakhs) to Customer Y on 15th March 2025 with a 30-day return policy. Customer Y accepted 50% of the goods on 25th March 2025 and gave no reply for the rest by 31st March 2025. 3. Guaranteed Buyback Transaction: Sold specialized machinery to Customer Z for ₹50 lakhs on 1st April 2024 with a concurrent binding clause to buy back the machinery after 2 years at ₹60 lakhs. 4. Escalation Claim: Incurred extra freight of ₹2 lakhs on a fixed price goods supply contract due to fuel surcharge, which Customer W agreed to reimburse verbally, but written confirmation is pending.
Medium SCENARIO · AS 9 | Consignment Revenue
For Transaction 1 (Consignment), how much revenue should Global Goods Ltd. recognize in FY 2024-25?
A. ₹9.0 lakhs gross revenue ✔
B. ₹8.1 lakhs net revenue
C. ₹15.0 lakhs full contract value
D. ₹6.0 lakhs cost of goods
Explanation: Under AS 9, consignor recognizes revenue when goods are sold by consignee to third parties. Consignee sold 60% for ₹9 lakhs. Gross revenue recognized by Global Goods is ₹9 lakhs (and commission of ₹0.9 lakh is booked as expense).
Hard SCENARIO · AS 9 | Sale on Approval | Inventory Valuation
For Transaction 2 (Sale on Approval), what revenue and inventory cost should Global Goods reflect at 31st March 2025?
A. Revenue = ₹7.0 lakhs; Closing Inventory = Nil
B. Revenue = ₹3.5 lakhs; Closing Inventory = ₹2.5 lakhs ✔
C. Revenue = Nil; Closing Inventory = ₹5.0 lakhs
D. Revenue = ₹3.5 lakhs; Closing Inventory = Nil
Explanation: For 50% accepted goods: Revenue = 50% of ₹7 lakhs = ₹3.5 lakhs. For 50% unaccepted goods where time limit (30 days) has not expired by 31st March: No revenue recognized, goods remain in closing inventory at 50% of cost = ₹2.5 lakhs.
Hard SCENARIO · AS 9 | Substance Over Form | Financing Arrangement
For Transaction 3 (Guaranteed Buyback), how should Global Goods treat the ₹50 lakhs cash received in FY 2024-25 under revenue recognition principles?
A. Recognize ₹50 lakhs as sales revenue immediately.
B. Recognize ₹50 lakhs as financing inflow/borrowing, not revenue. ✔
C. Recognize ₹10 lakhs profit immediately.
D. Recognize ₹25 lakhs sales revenue in Year 1 and ₹25 lakhs in Year 2.
Explanation: A sale with a concurrent agreement to repurchase the asset at a higher price is in substance a financing arrangement (borrowing) rather than a genuine transfer of risks and rewards of ownership. Hence, no revenue is recognized.
Medium SCENARIO · AS 9 | Uncertainty in Revenue Recognition
For Transaction 4 (Extra Freight Claim), should the ₹2 lakhs escalation claim be recognized as revenue in FY 2024-25?
A. Yes, because fuel prices increased standard cost.
B. No, revenue recognition should be postponed as ultimate collection lacks reasonable certainty without written confirmation. ✔
C. Yes, 50% should be recognized on prudence.
D. Yes, full ₹2 lakhs credited to general reserve.
Explanation: Under AS 9, when significant uncertainty exists regarding ultimate collection or acceptance of an additional claim, revenue recognition must be postponed until certainty/formal agreement is established.
CASE SCENARIO: Pragya Infrastructure & Services Ltd. operates across multiple sectors. Below are details of revenue items for FY 2024-25: 1. Construction Segment (AS 7): A 3-year contract started on 1st April 2024 for ₹3,000 lakhs. Total costs incurred during FY 2024-25 = ₹800 lakhs. Total estimated costs to complete = ₹1,600 lakhs. Progress billings = ₹900 lakhs. 2. Dividend Income (AS 9): Declared dividend of ₹15 lakhs by Subsidiary A on 28th March 2025 (Pragya holds 70% equity). Money received on 10th April 2025. 3. Royalty Income (AS 9): Received ₹10 lakhs royalty for patent usage from Licensee B for the 2-year period April 2024 to March 2026 in advance on 1st April 2024. 4. Interest Income (AS 9): Fixed deposit of ₹100 lakhs @ 10% p.a. placed on 1st October 2024 for 1 year. Interest payable on maturity.
Medium SCENARIO · AS 7 | Contract Profit
Under Segment 1 (Construction), what is the contract profit to be recognized in P&L for FY 2024-25?
A. ₹200 lakhs ✔
B. ₹600 lakhs
C. ₹100 lakhs
D. ₹1,000 lakhs
Explanation: Total Estimated Cost = 800 + 1600 = ₹2,400 lakhs. Total Contract Profit expected = 3000 - 2400 = ₹600 lakhs. Completion stage = 800 / 2400 = 33.33%. Revenue recognized = 33.33% * 3000 = ₹1,000 lakhs. Profit recognized = Revenue (1000) - Cost (800) = ₹200 lakhs.
Easy SCENARIO · AS 9 | Dividend Income
Under Segment 2 (Dividend), when and how much dividend income should Pragya recognize in FY 2024-25?
A. ₹15 lakhs in FY 2024-25 when declared on 28th March 2025. ✔
B. ₹15 lakhs in FY 2025-26 when cash is received on 10th April 2025.
C. ₹10.5 lakhs (70% share) in FY 2024-25.
D. Nil, dividend income is exempt from revenue recognition.
Explanation: Under AS 9, dividend income is recognized when the right to receive payment is established (which occurs upon declaration by the company on 28th March 2025). The declared dividend is ₹15 lakhs.
Medium SCENARIO · AS 9 | Royalty Income | Accrual Basis
Under Segment 3 (Royalty), how much royalty income should be recognized in FY 2024-25?
A. ₹10 lakhs
B. ₹5 lakhs ✔
C. Nil
D. ₹2.5 lakhs
Explanation: AS 9 mandates royalty recognition on an accrual basis in accordance with agreement terms. ₹10 lakhs covers 2 years (24 months). For FY 2024-25 (12 months), revenue recognized = ₹10 lakhs * (12/24) = ₹5 lakhs.
Medium SCENARIO · AS 9 | Interest Income | Time Proportion
Under Segment 4 (Interest Income), how much interest income should be accrued in FY 2024-25?
A. ₹10 lakhs
B. ₹5 lakhs ✔
C. Nil (since interest is received on maturity in next FY)
D. ₹2.5 lakhs
Explanation: Under AS 9, interest is recognized on a time proportion basis. FD placed on 1st Oct 2024 to 31st March 2025 = 6 months. Interest accrued = ₹100 lakhs * 10% * (6/12) = ₹5 lakhs.

Paper 1: Advanced Accounting · Module 2 · Chapter 9:

Accounts — 55 rows
Easy NORMAL · AS 4 | Adjusting Events | Financial Statements
Under AS 4 'Contingencies and Events Occurring After the Balance Sheet Date', how should a adjusting event after the balance sheet date be treated in the financial statements?
A. It requires disclosure only in the Report of the Board of Directors.
B. It requires adjustment to assets and liabilities in the financial statements for the period. ✔
C. It requires disclosure only in the Notes to Accounts without adjusting financial statement figures.
D. It requires no disclosure or adjustment if the amount is lower than ₹1,000.
Explanation: According to AS 4, adjusting events are those that provide additional evidence of conditions that existed at the balance sheet date. Assets and liabilities should be adjusted for events occurring after the balance sheet date that provide additional information materially affecting the determination of the amounts relating to conditions existing at the balance sheet date.
Medium NORMAL · AS 4 | Post Balance Sheet Events | Bad Debts
A debtor owing ₹5,00,000 to Alpha Ltd. became insolvent on 15th April 2026. The balance sheet date is 31st March 2026, and financial statements were approved on 30th May 2026. Financial position of the debtor was deteriorating prior to 31st March 2026. How should Alpha Ltd. treat this event?
A. Treat as a non-adjusting event and disclose in the Board's Report.
B. Adjust the provision for doubtful debts as at 31st March 2026 because insolvency provides evidence of conditions existing at balance sheet date. ✔
C. Ignore the event completely as it occurred after the financial year ended.
D. Adjust the accounts of the financial year 2026-27 instead of 2025-26.
Explanation: Insolvency of a debtor shortly after the balance sheet date usually indicates that the condition of insolvency existed at the balance sheet date. Hence, as per AS 4, it is an adjusting event requiring provision/adjustment in the financial statements for the year ended 31st March 2026.
Easy NORMAL · AS 5 | Prior Period Items | Accounting Errors
Under AS 5 'Net Profit or Loss for the Period, Prior Period Items and Changes in Accounting Policies', how are prior period items defined?
A. Incomes or expenses which arise from ordinary activities of the current period.
B. Incomes or expenses which arise in the current period as a result of errors or omissions in the preparation of financial statements of one or more prior periods. ✔
C. Changes in accounting estimates made during the current financial year.
D. Expenses resulting from extraordinary events such as natural disasters occurring during the current year.
Explanation: AS 5 defines prior period items as incomes or expenses which arise in the current period as a result of errors or omissions in the preparation of the financial statements of one or more prior periods.
Medium NORMAL · AS 5 | Accounting Estimate | Depreciation
Beta Ltd. revised the useful life of a machine from 10 years to 8 years in the current financial year due to technological obsolescence. How should this change be accounted for under AS 5?
A. As a prior period item requiring retrospective restatement.
B. As a change in accounting policy requiring retroactive adjustment to retained earnings.
C. As a change in accounting estimate, processed prospectively in current and future periods. ✔
D. As an extraordinary item shown separately after Profit Before Tax.
Explanation: A revision in the estimated useful life of a depreciable asset is a change in an accounting estimate. Under AS 5, changes in accounting estimates are accounted for prospectively in the period of change and subsequent periods if affected.
Easy NORMAL · AS 11 | Monetary Items | Foreign Currency
Under AS 11 'The Effects of Changes in Foreign Exchange Rates', which of the following is classified as a monetary item?
A. Property, Plant and Equipment
B. Inventories held in foreign warehouse
C. Trade Receivables in foreign currency ✔
D. Equity Investments in foreign subsidiaries
Explanation: Monetary items are money held and assets and liabilities to be received or paid in fixed or determinable amounts of money. Trade receivables are monetary items, whereas property, plant and equipment, inventories, and equity investments are non-monetary items.
Medium NORMAL · AS 11 | Exchange Difference | Monetary Liabilities
On 1st January 2026, Gamma Ltd. imported raw materials costing USD 50,000 when 1 USD = ₹82. On 31st March 2026 (closing date), the exchange rate was 1 USD = ₹84. The liability remained unpaid at year end. What is the exchange difference and its accounting treatment under AS 11?
A. ₹1,00,000 gain, recognized in Capital Reserve
B. ₹1,00,000 loss, credited to Inventory account
C. ₹1,00,000 loss, recognized as an expense in Profit and Loss Statement ✔
D. ₹1,00,000 gain, deferred in Foreign Currency Translation Reserve
Explanation: Foreign currency monetary liabilities (Trade Payables) are reported using the closing rate. Increase in liability rate from ₹82 to ₹84 results in an exchange loss of USD 50,000 x (84 - 82) = ₹1,00,000, which under AS 11 is recognized in the Statement of Profit and Loss.
Medium NORMAL · AS 11 | Non-integral Operation | Translation Reserve
Under AS 11, exchange differences arising on translation of financial statements of a non-integral foreign operation should be:
A. Recognized immediately in the Statement of Profit and Loss.
B. Accumulated in a Foreign Currency Translation Reserve until disposal of net investment. ✔
C. Deducted directly from the carrying amount of fixed assets.
D. Capitalized as part of capital work-in-progress.
Explanation: Under AS 11, exchange differences arising on translation of financial statements of non-integral foreign operations are accumulated in a foreign currency translation reserve until the disposal of the net investment.
Easy NORMAL · AS 12 | Government Grants | Capital Reserve
Under AS 12 'Accounting for Government Grants', a government grant in the nature of promoters' contribution should be credited to:
A. Statement of Profit and Loss under Other Income.
B. Capital Reserve. ✔
C. Deferred Government Grant Account.
D. General Reserve.
Explanation: Government grants in the nature of promoters' contribution are given as a total package towards total capital outlay or contribution towards setting up an enterprise. Under AS 12, such grants are treated as capital reserve.
Easy NORMAL · AS 12 | Government Grants | Fixed Asset Grants
Delta Ltd. received a government grant of ₹20,00,000 for acquiring a specific plant costing ₹1,00,00,000. Under AS 12, which of the following is an acceptable accounting method for presenting this grant?
A. Deduct the grant from the gross cost of the plant to arrive at book value. ✔
B. Credit the entire grant to retained earnings immediately.
C. Show the grant as a liability under short-term borrowings.
D. Adjust the grant against trade payables.
Explanation: AS 12 permits two methods for grants related to specific fixed assets: Method 1: Deduct the grant from the gross value of the asset; Method 2: Treat the grant as deferred income and recognize in P&L over the useful life of the asset.
Medium NORMAL · AS 12 | Refund of Grant | Revenue Grant
If a government grant related to revenue becomes refundable due to non-fulfillment of specified conditions, how should the refund be accounted for under AS 12?
A. Adjusted against retained earnings retrospectively.
B. First applied against unamortized deferred credit balance, and any excess charged to Profit and Loss. ✔
C. Debited directly to Capital Reserve account.
D. Ignored if the amount is refundable in installments.
Explanation: Under AS 12, a grant refundable related to revenue is first applied against any unamortized deferred credit remaining in respect of the grant. To the extent that the refund exceeds any such deferred credit, or where no deferred credit exists, the refund is charged immediately to the Profit and Loss statement.
Easy NORMAL · AS 16 | Qualifying Asset | Borrowing Costs
Under AS 16 'Borrowing Costs', which of the following assets qualifies as a 'qualifying asset'?
A. Inventories that are routinely manufactured in large quantities on a repetitive basis over 2 days.
B. A power plant construction project that necessarily takes 18 months to get ready for its intended use. ✔
C. Financial assets such as investments in equity shares.
D. An office building ready for immediate occupancy at the date of purchase.
Explanation: A qualifying asset under AS 16 is an asset that necessarily takes a substantial period of time (usually 12 months or more) to get ready for its intended use or sale. A power plant taking 18 months fits this definition.
Medium NORMAL · AS 16 | Suspension of Capitalization | Borrowing Costs
Under AS 16, capitalization of borrowing costs should be suspended during:
A. Extended periods in which active development of the asset is interrupted. ✔
B. Periods when substantial technical and administrative work is being carried out.
C. Brief delays that are a necessary part of the process of getting an asset ready for use.
D. The entire period of active construction.
Explanation: AS 16 requires that capitalization of borrowing costs should be suspended during extended periods in which active development is interrupted. It is not suspended when temporary delays are necessary or during administrative/technical work.
Easy NORMAL · AS 22 | Timing Differences | Deferred Tax
Under AS 22 'Accounting for Taxes on Income', what gives rise to a 'timing difference'?
A. Differences between taxable income and accounting income that originate in one period and are capable of reversal in one or more subsequent periods. ✔
B. Differences between taxable income and accounting income that originate in one period and never reverse subsequently.
C. Fines and penalties disallowed permanently by tax authorities.
D. Tax-exempt dividend income.
Explanation: Timing differences are differences between taxable income and accounting income for a period that originate in one period and are capable of reversal in one or more subsequent periods.
Hard NORMAL · AS 22 | Virtual Certainty | Deferred Tax Asset
Under AS 22, Deferred Tax Asset (DTA) in respect of unabsorbed depreciation or carried forward tax losses should be recognized ONLY to the extent that:
A. There is reasonable certainty supported by convincing evidence that future taxable income will be available.
B. There is virtual certainty supported by convincing evidence that sufficient future taxable income will be available against which such DTA can be realized. ✔
C. Management intends to carry on business operations for at least 3 years.
D. The company has sufficient share capital and general reserves.
Explanation: AS 22 mandates a stricter test for recognizing DTAs on unabsorbed depreciation or carry forward losses: DTA should be recognized only to the extent that there is virtual certainty supported by convincing evidence that sufficient future taxable income will be available.
Easy NORMAL · AS 26 | Research Expenditure | Intangible Assets
Under AS 26 'Intangible Assets', how should expenditure incurred during the 'Research Phase' of an internal project be accounted for?
A. Capitalized as an intangible asset if expected revenue exceeds cost.
B. Recognized as an expense when it is incurred. ✔
C. Deferred and amortized over a period not exceeding 5 years.
D. Added to the cost of related plant and machinery.
Explanation: AS 26 states that no intangible asset arising from research (or research phase) should be recognized. Expenditure on research should be recognized as an expense when it is incurred because an enterprise cannot demonstrate that an intangible asset exists.
Medium NORMAL · AS 26 | Amortization | Useful Life
Under AS 26, there is a rebuttable presumption that the useful life of an intangible asset will not exceed how many years from the date when the asset is available for use?
A. 5 years
B. 10 years ✔
C. 20 years
D. 15 years
Explanation: AS 26 provides a rebuttable presumption that the useful life of an intangible asset will not exceed 10 years from the date when the asset is available for use.
Easy NORMAL · AS 29 | Provisions | Recognition Criteria
Under AS 29 'Provisions, Contingent Liabilities and Contingent Assets', a provision should be recognized when:
A. An enterprise has a present obligation as a result of a past event, it is probable that an outflow of resources will be required, and a reliable estimate can be made. ✔
B. An enterprise has a possible obligation arising from past events whose existence will be confirmed only by future events.
C. There is a possible inflow of economic benefits arising from unplanned events.
D. Management decides to reserve funds for future operational expansion.
Explanation: Under AS 29, a provision is recognized when: (a) an enterprise has a present obligation as a result of a past event; (b) it is probable (more likely than not) that an outflow of resources embodying economic benefits will be required to settle the obligation; and (c) a reliable estimate can be made of the amount of the obligation.
Medium NORMAL · AS 29 | Contingent Assets | Financial Disclosures
How are Contingent Assets treated under AS 29?
A. Recognized in Profit and Loss Statement as revenue.
B. Disclosed in the Financial Statements as a Provision.
C. Neither recognized nor disclosed in financial statements, but disclosed in the Board's Report if inflow is probable. ✔
D. Recognized as non-current assets in the Balance Sheet.
Explanation: AS 29 states that contingent assets are neither recognized nor disclosed in financial statements. However, if an inflow of economic benefits is probable, it is usually disclosed in the report of the approving authority (Board of Directors report).
Medium NORMAL · AS 15 | Actuarial Gains/Losses | Defined Benefit Plan
Under AS 15 'Employee Benefits', actuarial gains and losses relating to defined benefit post-employment plans should be recognized:
A. In the Statement of Profit and Loss immediately. ✔
B. Deferred over the average remaining working lives of employees.
C. Credited directly to Revaluation Reserve.
D. Adjusted against Opening Retained Earnings without entering P&L.
Explanation: Under AS 15 (Revised), actuarial gains and losses should be recognized immediately in the Statement of Profit and Loss as income or expense.
Easy NORMAL · AS 28 | Recoverable Amount | Impairment
Under AS 28 'Impairment of Assets', 'Recoverable Amount' of an asset is defined as:
A. Lower of Net Selling Price and Value in Use.
B. Higher of Net Selling Price and Value in Use. ✔
C. Lower of Historical Cost and Net Realizable Value.
D. Higher of Replacement Cost and Value in Use.
Explanation: AS 28 defines Recoverable Amount as the higher of an asset's net selling price and its value in use.
Medium NORMAL · AS 28 | Value in Use | Cash Flows
Under AS 28, 'Value in Use' is calculated as:
A. Present value of estimated future cash flows expected to arise from the continuing use of an asset and from its disposal at end of useful life. ✔
B. Gross undiscounted sum of future cash inflows from asset operation.
C. Market value minus estimated costs of disposal.
D. Historical acquisition cost adjusted for inflation.
Explanation: Under AS 28, Value in Use is the present value of estimated future cash flows expected to arise from the continuing use of an asset and from its disposal at the end of its useful life.
Hard NORMAL · AS 24 | Discontinuing Operations | Initial Disclosure Event
Under AS 24 'Discontinuing Operations', when does the initial disclosure event occur?
A. When the Board passes a preliminary resolution to consider discontinuing a segment.
B. On the earlier of: entering into a binding sale agreement OR Board approving and announcing a detailed formal plan. ✔
C. When the sale of all assets of the component is fully completed.
D. At the end of the financial year in which operations cease.
Explanation: Under AS 24, initial disclosure event is the occurrence of one of the following, whichever is earlier: (a) enterprise entering into a binding sale agreement for substantially all assets of discontinuing operation, or (b) approval and public announcement of a detailed formal plan by the enterprise's board.
Medium NORMAL · AS 17 | Segment Reporting | Reportable Segment Criteria
Under AS 17 'Segment Reporting', a business or geographical segment is reportable if its revenue from sales to external customers and from transactions with other segments is:
A. 5% or more of total revenue, external and internal, of all segments.
B. 10% or more of total revenue, external and internal, of all segments. ✔
C. 15% or more of external revenue of all segments.
D. 20% or more of net operational profit.
Explanation: Under AS 17, a segment is a reportable segment if its revenue from external customers and transactions with other segments is 10% or more of total revenue (external and internal) of all segments.
Hard NORMAL · AS 17 | 75 Percent Rule | External Revenue
Under AS 17, if total external revenue attributable to reportable segments identified by 10% criteria constitutes less than what percentage of total enterprise revenue, additional segments must be identified?
A. 50%
B. 60%
C. 75% ✔
D. 90%
Explanation: AS 17 specifies that if total external revenue attributable to reportable segments constitutes less than 75% of total enterprise revenue, additional segments should be identified as reportable segments until at least 75% of total enterprise revenue is included in reportable segments.
Medium NORMAL · AS 20 | Bonus Issue | Basic EPS
Under AS 20 'Earnings Per Share', how are bonus shares issued during the financial year treated in computing Basic EPS?
A. Weighted from the exact date of allotment of bonus shares.
B. Treated as if they were issued at the beginning of the earliest period reported. ✔
C. Excluded from Basic EPS calculation and included only in Diluted EPS.
D. Weighted for 6 months standard period regardless of allotment date.
Explanation: Under AS 20, in case of bonus issue, equity shares are issued without consideration. Therefore, they are treated as if they had been issued at the beginning of the earliest period reported (retrospective adjustment).
Medium NORMAL · AS 19 | Finance Lease | Lessee Accounting
Under AS 19 'Leases', in the financial statements of a lessee, an asset acquired under a finance lease should be recognized at:
A. Lower of fair value of leased asset and present value of minimum lease payments at inception. ✔
B. Higher of fair value of leased asset and present value of minimum lease payments at inception.
C. Total undiscounted lease payments payable over the lease term.
D. Liquidation value of the asset at end of lease term.
Explanation: Under AS 19, at the inception of a finance lease, the lessee should recognize the lease as an asset and a liability at an amount equal to the lower of the fair value of the leased asset and the present value of the minimum lease payments.
Easy NORMAL · AS 4 | Proposed Dividend | Post Balance Sheet Event
Under AS 4 (Revised), how should dividend proposed by the Board of Directors after the balance sheet date but before approval of financial statements be treated?
A. Recognized as a liability in the Balance Sheet of current financial year.
B. Disclosed in the Notes to Accounts for the current financial year and recognized as liability when declared/approved in AGM. ✔
C. Adjusted directly against General Reserve in current year Balance Sheet.
D. Ignored completely from both Balance Sheet and Notes.
Explanation: Under AS 4 (Revised), proposed dividend does not represent a present obligation at the balance sheet date. Therefore, it is disclosed in Notes to Accounts for that year, and recognized as liability only when declared by shareholders in the AGM.
Easy NORMAL · AS 18 | Related Party | KMP Disclosure
Under AS 18 'Related Party Disclosures', which of the following relationships automatically creates a 'Related Party' relationship requiring disclosure?
A. A single customer with whom the enterprise transacts 60% of its volume of business.
B. Key Management Personnel (KMP) and their close family members. ✔
C. A provider of finance (banker) extending loan to the enterprise.
D. A trade union holding negotiations with management.
Explanation: AS 18 explicitly identifies Key Management Personnel (KMP) and their relatives as related parties. Customers, suppliers, providers of finance, and trade unions are specifically excluded from being related parties solely by virtue of their normal dealings.
Hard NORMAL · AS 16 | Capitalization Calculation | General Borrowings
Epsilon Ltd. incurred ₹12,00,000 on general borrowing at an average interest rate of 10% per annum. During the year, it utilized ₹8,00,000 out of general borrowing on 1st April 2025 for construction of a qualifying asset, which was completed on 31st December 2025 (9 months). What is the maximum borrowing cost that can be capitalized under AS 16?
A. ₹80,000
B. ₹60,000 ✔
C. ₹1,20,000
D. ₹90,000
Explanation: Borrowing cost to be capitalized = Capital expenditure on qualifying asset x Borrowing rate x Construction period = ₹8,00,000 x 10% x (9/12) = ₹60,000. Capitalization ceases when construction is substantially complete (31st Dec).
Medium NORMAL · AS 22 | Balance Sheet Presentation | Deferred Tax Liability
Under AS 22, if an entity has a timing difference that results in a net Deferred Tax Liability (DTL), how should DTL be disclosed in the Balance Sheet?
A. Under Current Liabilities as short-term provision.
B. Under Non-Current Liabilities on the face of the Balance Sheet separately from current liabilities and non-current liabilities. ✔
C. Deducted directly from Share Capital.
D. Deducted from Property, Plant and Equipment cost.
Explanation: Under AS 22 and Schedule III to Companies Act 2013, Deferred Tax Liabilities are disclosed under Non-Current Liabilities (and DTA under Non-Current Assets) separately on the face of the Balance Sheet.
CASE SCENARIO: Apex Infrastructure Ltd. is engaged in constructing a major power generation plant (a qualifying asset under AS 16). Construction began on 1st April 2025. To fund the project, Apex Ltd. raised a specific loan of ₹50,00,000 at 12% per annum on 1st April 2025. Pending utilization, idle funds from the loan were temporarily invested for 3 months, earning interest income of ₹60,000. Additionally, the company spent ₹20,00,000 from its general borrowings (weighted average cost of general borrowing is 10% p.a.) on 1st July 2025. Construction was halted from 1st October 2025 to 30th November 2025 (2 months) due to an abnormal labor strike. Active construction resumed on 1st December 2025 and continued till 31st March 2026. On 1st April 2025, Apex Ltd. also received a specific capital grant of ₹10,00,000 from the Central Government towards the power plant, which the company decided to deduct from the cost of the asset under AS 12.
Hard SCENARIO · AS 16 | Specific Borrowing | Suspension of Capitalization
What is the net eligible borrowing cost to be capitalized from the SPECIFIC LOAN for the year ended 31st March 2026, considering the abnormal strike period under AS 16?
A. ₹6,00,000
B. ₹4,40,000 ✔
C. ₹5,40,000
D. ₹5,00,000
Explanation: Total specific interest for 12 months = ₹50,00,000 x 12% = ₹6,00,000. Interest during abnormal delay (2 months) must be suspended and charged to P&L: ₹6,00,000 x (2/12) = ₹1,00,000. Interest income earned on temporary investment = ₹60,00. Net specific borrowing cost capitalized = (₹6,00,000 - ₹1,00,000) - ₹60,000 = ₹4,40,000.
Hard SCENARIO · AS 16 | General Borrowing | Active Period
What is the borrowing cost to be capitalized from GENERAL BORROWINGS for the year ended 31st March 2026 under AS 16?
A. ₹1,50,000
B. ₹1,16,667 ✔
C. ₹1,00,000
D. ₹2,00,000
