Explanation: To Equity Shareholders: Shares issued = (50 lakhs / 5) * 4 = 40 lakh shares * ₹25 = ₹1,000 lakhs. To Preference Shareholders: Cash = ₹100 lakhs + 10% premium = ₹110 lakhs. Total PC = ₹1,000 lakhs + ₹110 lakhs = ₹1,110 lakhs.
Hard SCENARIO · Net Agreed Assets | Purchase Method | Valuation
What is the value of Net Agreed Assets taken over by Apex Ltd?
A. ₹840 lakhs ✔
B. ₹800 lakhs
C. ₹1,280 lakhs
D. ₹760 lakhs
Explanation: Total Agreed Assets = Non-Current Assets (₹900 lakhs) + Current Assets (₹380 lakhs) = ₹1,280 lakhs. Total Liabilities assumed = Non-Current Liabilities (₹300 lakhs) + Current Liabilities (₹140 lakhs) = ₹440 lakhs. Net Agreed Assets = ₹1,280 lakhs - ₹440 lakhs = ₹840 lakhs. (P&L debit balance is fictitious asset, excluded).
Medium SCENARIO · Goodwill | Purchase Method | Computation
Calculate Goodwill or Capital Reserve resulting from the transaction.
A. Capital Reserve of ₹270 lakhs
B. Goodwill of ₹270 lakhs ✔
C. Goodwill of ₹170 lakhs
D. Capital Reserve of ₹170 lakhs
Explanation: Purchase Consideration = ₹1,110 lakhs. Net Agreed Assets = ₹840 lakhs. Goodwill = PC - Net Agreed Assets = ₹1,110 lakhs - ₹840 lakhs = ₹270 lakhs.
Easy SCENARIO · Transferor Company Books | Accumulated Losses | Equity Shareholders
How should the debit balance of Profit & Loss Account of ₹40 lakhs in Zenith Ltd be dealt with in Zenith Ltd's books upon liquidation?
A. Transferred to Realisation Account Debit
B. Transferred to Equity Shareholders' Account Debit ✔
C. Transferred to Goodwill Account Debit
D. Taken over by Apex Ltd under Amalgamation Adjustment Reserve
Explanation: Fictitious assets and accumulated losses like debit balance of Profit & Loss Account are not taken over by transferee company and are transferred directly to the debit of Equity Shareholders' Account in transferor's books.
CASE SCENARIO: Target Ltd goes into voluntary liquidation to amalgamate with Acquirer Ltd on 31st March 2026. Target Ltd's balance sheet summarized: - Equity Share Capital (1,00,000 shares of ₹10 each) = ₹10,00,000 - Reserves & Surplus = ₹4,00,000 - 10% Debentures = ₹3,00,000 - Creditors = ₹2,00,000 - PPE (Net) = ₹12,00,000 - Current Assets = ₹7,00,000 Terms of Amalgamation: 1. Acquirer Ltd takes over all assets and liabilities. 2. Acquirer Ltd pays Purchase Consideration of ₹15,00,000 by issuing 1,00,000 equity shares of ₹10 each at a premium of ₹5 per share. 3. Realisation expenses incurred by Target Ltd amounted to ₹20,000 which were paid by Target Ltd itself prior to completion of transfer. 4. Realisation of assets and discharge of liabilities was executed via Realisation Account in Target Ltd's books.
Hard SCENARIO · Realisation Profit | Transferor Company Books | Accounting Ledger
In the books of Target Ltd, what is the profit or loss on Realisation Account?
A. Profit of ₹80,000 ✔
B. Profit of ₹1,00,000
C. Loss of ₹20,000
D. Profit of ₹78,000
Explanation: Debit side of Realisation A/c: PPE (₹12,00,000) + Current Assets (₹7,00,000) + Realisation Exp (₹20,00) = ₹19,20,000. Credit side of Realisation A/c: 10% Debentures (₹3,00,000) + Creditors (₹2,00,000) + PC (₹15,00,000) = ₹20,00,000. Realisation Profit = Credit (₹20,00,000) - Debit (₹19,20,000) = ₹80,000.
Hard SCENARIO · Equity Shareholders Account | Transferor Company | Final Distribution
What is the final amount payable/distributable to Equity Shareholders of Target Ltd upon closing their account?
A. ₹14,80,000
B. ₹15,00,000 ✔
C. ₹14,00,000
D. ₹10,00,000
Explanation: Equity Shareholders' A/c credit side: Equity Share Capital (₹10,00,000) + Reserves & Surplus (₹4,00,000) + Profit on Realisation (₹80,000) = ₹14,80,000. Wait! Cash in bank was part of Current Assets (₹7,00,000) transferred to transferee, but Target Ltd paid ₹20,000 expenses out of its bank/cash before transfer, or from PC cash. Since PC was paid fully in shares worth ₹15,00,000, those shares worth ₹15,00,000 are distributed to Equity Shareholders to close Equity Shareholders' A/c at ₹14,80,000 + adjustment. Specifically, net equity entitlement equals PC of ₹15,00,000 (which matches total assets realized less liabilities discharged).
Easy SCENARIO · Liquidation Expenses | Transferor Company Books | Realisation Entry
How are realization expenses of ₹20,000 paid by Target Ltd recorded in Target Ltd's books?
A. Debited to Profit and Loss Account and Credited to Bank
B. Debited to Realisation Account and Credited to Bank Account ✔
C. Debited to Acquirer Ltd Account and Credited to Bank Account
D. Debited to Equity Shareholders Account and Credited to Bank
Explanation: When liquidation/realisation expenses are paid and borne by the transferor company itself, the journal entry in the transferor company's books is: Realisation Account Dr. ₹20,000 To Bank Account ₹20,000.
Easy SCENARIO · Purchase Consideration Due | Transferor Company Books | Journal Entry
What entry is passed in Target Ltd's books to record the Purchase Consideration due from Acquirer Ltd?
A. Acquirer Ltd A/c Dr. ₹15,00,000 To Realisation A/c ₹15,00,000 ✔
B. Realisation A/c Dr. ₹15,00,000 To Acquirer Ltd A/c ₹15,00,000
C. Bank A/c Dr. ₹15,00,000 To Purchase Consideration A/c ₹15,00,000
D. Equity Shareholders A/c Dr. ₹15,00,000 To Acquirer Ltd A/c ₹15,00,000
Explanation: To record PC due from transferee company in the transferor company's books, the journal entry is: Transferee Company A/c (Acquirer Ltd) Dr. To Realisation Account.

Paper 1: Advanced Accounting · Module 3 · Chapter 14:

Accounts — 55 rows
Easy NORMAL · Section 61 | Section 66 | NCLT Approval | Alteration of Capital
Which of the following internal reconstruction schemes under the Companies Act, 2013 does NOT require confirmation or sanction from the National Company Law Tribunal (NCLT)?
A. Reduction of paid-up share capital under Section 66
B. Sub-division of fully paid equity shares into shares of smaller face value under Section 61 ✔
C. Extinguishing the liability on unpaid share capital under Section 66
D. Paying off any paid-up share capital which is in excess of the wants of the company under Section 66
Explanation: Under Section 61 of the Companies Act, 2013, alteration of share capital such as sub-division or consolidation of shares requires only an ordinary resolution in the general meeting if authorized by articles. Confirmation from the NCLT is compulsory for reduction of share capital governed under Section 66. Hence, sub-division does not require NCLT sanction.
Easy NORMAL · Section 66 | NCLT | Capital Reduction | Legal Framework
Under Section 66 of the Companies Act, 2013, a company can reduce its share capital only after obtaining approval from which authority?
A. Reserve Bank of India (RBI)
B. Ministry of Corporate Affairs (MCA)
C. National Company Law Tribunal (NCLT) ✔
D. Securities and Exchange Board of India (SEBI)
Explanation: Section 66 of the Companies Act, 2013 mandates that a company may reduce its share capital by passing a special resolution subject to confirmation by the NCLT. The NCLT satisfies itself that interests of creditors and stakeholders are protected before issuing an order confirming the reduction. Other regulatory bodies do not issue the formal confirmation order under Section 66.
Easy NORMAL · Capital Reduction Account | Account Nature | Accounting Entries
What is the underlying financial nature of the Reconstruction Account or Capital Reduction Account prepared during an internal reconstruction scheme?
A. Real Account
B. Personal Account
C. Nominal Account ✔
D. Representative Personal Account
Explanation: The Capital Reduction Account or Reconstruction Account is a temporary Nominal Account created to accumulate sacrifices made by shareholders, creditors, and debenture holders. All gains and sacrifices are credited to this account, while losses written off and asset reductions are debited to it. Once the reconstruction scheme is fully executed, the balance in this account is closed by transferring it to Capital Reserve.
Easy NORMAL · Sub-division | Section 61 | Share Capital Entry
When a company sub-divides its 10,000 equity shares of Rs. 100 each into 1,00,000 equity shares of Rs. 10 each, what is the net accounting entry required in the main ledger?
A. Debit Equity Share Capital A/c (Rs. 100) and Credit Equity Share Capital A/c (Rs. 10) for Rs. 10,00,000 ✔
B. Debit Capital Reduction A/c and Credit Equity Share Capital A/c for Rs. 10,00,000
C. Debit Equity Share Capital A/c and Credit Capital Reduction A/c for Rs. 9,00,000
D. No entry is required in the general ledger as total capital remains unchanged
Explanation: Sub-division of shares under Section 61 changes the denomination and total number of shares, but total paid-up share capital remains unchanged at Rs. 10,00,000. An entry is passed debiting the old Equity Share Capital Account (Rs. 100 face value) and crediting the new Equity Share Capital Account (Rs. 10 face value) for Rs. 10,00,000. This maintains correct capital representation in the ledger.
Easy NORMAL · Capital Reserve | Capital Reduction Account | Final Transfer
After meeting all specified write-offs of accumulated losses and asset overvaluations, any surplus remaining in the Capital Reduction Account is transferred to which head?
A. General Reserve Account
B. Capital Reserve Account ✔
C. Securities Premium Account
D. Profit & Loss Account
Explanation: Any credit balance remaining in the Capital Reduction Account after absorbing all accumulated P&L losses, fictitious assets, and overvalued fixed assets represents a capital profit. In accordance with standard accounting procedures for internal reconstruction, this credit balance is transferred to the Capital Reserve Account. It cannot be distributed as dividend or credited to General Reserve.
Easy NORMAL · Schedule III | Capital Reserve | Financial Statements
As per Schedule III to the Companies Act, 2013, under which head should the Capital Reserve created through internal reconstruction be presented in the Balance Sheet?
A. Share Capital
B. Reserves and Surplus under Other Equity ✔
C. Long-term Provisions
D. Other Current Liabilities
Explanation: Under Schedule III of the Companies Act, 2013, Capital Reserve is categorized under 'Reserves and Surplus', which forms part of 'Other Equity' in the Statement of Assets and Liabilities. It represents non-distributable capital profits generated through internal financial reorganisation. Thus, it is presented under Other Equity.
Easy NORMAL · Unissued Capital | Section 61 | Accounting Entries
What journal entry is passed in the financial books of account when a company cancels its unissued share capital under Section 61 of the Companies Act, 2013?
A. Debit Unissued Share Capital A/c and Credit Capital Reduction A/c
B. Debit Share Capital A/c and Credit Capital Reduction A/c
C. Debit Capital Reduction A/c and Credit Unissued Share Capital A/c
D. No journal entry is required in the financial books ✔
Explanation: Unissued share capital is not part of the paid-up or issued share capital brought into financial books of account. Section 61(1)(e) permits cancellation of unissued capital, which merely reduces authorized capital. Since authorized capital is shown by way of a note and not as a ledger balance, no formal financial journal entry is recorded.
Easy NORMAL · Reconstruction Expenses | Capital Reduction Account | Journal Entry
How should the payment of professional expenses directly incurred for executing an internal reconstruction scheme be treated in the books?
A. Debited to Profit & Loss Account
B. Debited to Capital Reduction Account ✔
C. Debited to Miscellaneous Expenditure Account
D. Debited to General Reserve Account
Explanation: Expenses incurred in carrying out an internal reconstruction scheme (such as court fees, legal charges, and professional fees) are part of the reconstruction process itself. They are debited directly to the Capital Reduction / Reconstruction Account and credited to Bank Account. This ensures all costs associated with capital reduction are absorbed by the capital reduction scheme balance.
Easy NORMAL · Conversion into Stock | Section 61 | Company Law
What resolution is required to be passed by a company in its General Meeting to convert fully paid equity shares into stock under Section 61?
A. Special Resolution
B. Ordinary Resolution ✔
C. Board Resolution only
D. Unanimous Consent of Creditors
Explanation: Under Section 61(1)(c) of the Companies Act, 2013, conversion of all or any fully paid-up shares into stock (and reconversion of stock into fully paid-up shares) requires an Ordinary Resolution passed in a general meeting, provided such alteration is authorized by the Articles of Association. A Special Resolution is required for capital reduction under Section 66, not Section 61.
Easy NORMAL · Balance Sheet Presentation | Schedule III | Accounting Framework
Under which financial accounting standard framework is the internal reconstruction balance sheet prepared after capital reduction?
A. AS 14 / Ind AS 103 on Business Combinations
B. Schedule III to the Companies Act, 2013 along with applicable Accounting Standards ✔
C. AS 24 on Discontinuing Operations
D. AS 13 on Accounting for Investments
Explanation: Internal reconstruction does not involve an acquisition or amalgamation of legal entities, so AS 14 / Ind AS 103 does not govern its financial statement presentation. The balance sheet post-reconstruction is prepared in accordance with Schedule III to the Companies Act, 2013 and applicable Accounting Standards. If instructed by the NCLT order, the words 'And Reduced' are appended to the company name for a specified period.
Medium NORMAL · Dividend Arrears | Unrecorded Liability | Waiver Entry
If preference shareholders agree to waive Rs. 1,20,000 of preference dividend arrears that were never recognized in the financial statements, what is the journal entry?
A. Debit Capital Reduction A/c Rs. 1,20,000 and Credit Cash A/c Rs. 1,20,000
B. Debit Preference Dividend Arrears A/c Rs. 1,20,000 and Credit Capital Reduction A/c Rs. 1,20,000
C. Debit Capital Reduction A/c Rs. 1,20,000 and Credit Preference Share Capital A/c Rs. 1,20,000
D. No journal entry is required in the books of account ✔
Explanation: Unrecorded arrears of cumulative preference dividend are contingent liabilities not shown as actual liabilities in the balance sheet. When preference shareholders agree to forego/waive such unrecorded arrears, no claim or liability is extinguished from the books. Therefore, no formal journal entry is passed for the waived portion.
Medium NORMAL · Dividend Settlement | Capital Reduction Account | Cash Payment
A company pays 30% of unrecorded preference dividend arrears of Rs. 2,00,000 in cash as part of an NCLT approved scheme. What is the journal entry impact on Capital Reduction Account?
A. Debited by Rs. 60,000 ✔
B. Credited by Rs. 1,40,000
C. Debited by Rs. 2,00,000
D. Credited by Rs. 60,000
Explanation: Since the dividend arrears were unrecorded, any actual cash outlay to settle a portion of these arrears creates a financial obligation not previously debited to accounts. The cash payment of 30% on Rs. 2,00,000 equals Rs. 60,000, which is debited to the Capital Reduction Account and credited to Bank Account. The remaining waived 70% requires no accounting entry.
Medium NORMAL · Creditors Compromise | Capital Reduction Account | Sacrifice Calculation
Unsecured creditors of Rs. 8,00,000 agree to accept 75% of their claims in Equity Shares of Rs. 10 each at par and waive the rest. What amount is credited to Capital Reduction Account?
A. Rs. 6,00,000
B. Rs. 2,00,000 ✔
C. Rs. 8,00,000
D. Nil
Explanation: Total unsecured creditors liability eliminated is Rs. 8,00,000. In exchange, equity share capital of Rs. 6,00,000 (75% of Rs. 8,00,000) is issued. The sacrifice made by creditors is 25% of Rs. 8,00,000 = Rs. 2,00,000, which represents a gain to the company and is credited to the Capital Reduction Account.
Medium NORMAL · Paid-up Reduction | Capital Reduction Account | Share Reduction Entry
A company has 20,000 Equity Shares of Rs. 100 each, Rs. 70 paid up. It reduces the paid-up value to Rs. 40 per share fully paid up. What amount is credited to Capital Reduction A/c?
A. Rs. 12,00,000
B. Rs. 6,00,000 ✔
C. Rs. 8,00,000
D. Rs. 14,00,000
Explanation: The existing paid-up capital per share is Rs. 70. The new paid-up capital per share is Rs. 40 fully paid up. The reduction per share is Rs. 70 - Rs. 40 = Rs. 30 per share. Total amount credited to Capital Reduction Account = 20,000 shares × Rs. 30 = Rs. 6,00,000.
Medium NORMAL · Contingent Liability | Capital Reduction Account | Settlement Entry
An unrecorded contingent liability of Rs. 60,000 crystallizes during reconstruction and is settled at Rs. 45,000 in cash. What is the entry in Capital Reduction Account?
A. Debited by Rs. 45,000 ✔
B. Credited by Rs. 15,00,000
C. Debited by Rs. 60,000
D. Credited by Rs. 45,000
Explanation: When an unrecorded contingent liability crystallizes and is paid under a reconstruction scheme, the actual payment made to settle the liability (Rs. 45,000) is a loss/cost to the scheme. Hence, Capital Reduction Account is debited by Rs. 45,000 and Bank Account is credited by Rs. 45,000.
Medium NORMAL · Debenture Sacrifice | Capital Reduction Account | Debenture Conversion
10% Debentures of Rs. 6,00,000 are replaced by 12% Debentures of Rs. 5,00,000 in full and final settlement. What amount is credited to Capital Reduction Account?
A. Rs. 1,00,000 ✔
B. Rs. 5,00,000
C. Rs. 6,00,000
D. Nil
Explanation: Old 10% Debentures Account is debited by Rs. 6,00,000. New 12% Debentures Account is credited by Rs. 5,00,000. The gain arising from debenture holders surrendering Rs. 1,00,000 of principal claim is credited to Capital Reduction Account (Rs. 6,00,000 - Rs. 5,00,000 = Rs. 1,00,000).
Medium NORMAL · Share Surrender | Temporary Account | Accounting Procedure
When equity shareholders surrender their shares under an internal reconstruction scheme, which account is credited initially?
A. Capital Reduction Account
B. Share Surrender Account ✔
C. Capital Reserve Account
D. Profit & Loss Account
Explanation: When shares are surrendered by shareholders, Equity Share Capital Account is debited and 'Share Surrender Account' is credited as a temporary holding account. The surrendered shares are subsequently either re-issued to creditors/debenture holders or cancelled. Upon cancellation, the balance in Share Surrender Account is transferred to Capital Reduction Account.
Medium NORMAL · Share Surrender Reissue | Creditor Settlement | Journal Entry
Shares surrendered by equity shareholders are reissued to trade creditors to discharge claims of Rs. 1,50,000. What entry is passed on reissue?
A. Debit Trade Creditors A/c Rs. 1,50,000 and Credit Share Surrender A/c Rs. 1,50,000 ✔
B. Debit Trade Creditors A/c Rs. 1,50,000 and Credit Capital Reduction A/c Rs. 1,50,000
C. Debit Share Surrender A/c Rs. 1,50,000 and Credit Capital Reduction A/c Rs. 1,50,000
D. Debit Capital Reduction A/c Rs. 1,50,000 and Credit Equity Share Capital A/c Rs. 1,50,000
Explanation: When surrendered shares are reissued to discharge liability of creditors, Trade Creditors Account is debited by Rs. 1,50,000 and Share Surrender Account is credited by Rs. 1,50,000. This cancels out the creditor liability against the surrendered shares held in trust without affecting Capital Reduction Account at this intermediate stage.
Medium NORMAL · Section 61 | Section 66 | Consolidation | Legal Distinction
Which of the following transactions is classified under Section 61 (Alteration of Share Capital) rather than Section 66 (Reduction of Share Capital)?
A. Extinguishing unpaid liability on existing equity shares
B. Consolidation of shares of smaller denomination into shares of larger denomination ✔
C. Writing off lost paid-up capital not represented by available assets
D. Refunding excess paid-up share capital to equity shareholders
Explanation: Consolidation of shares into larger face value without altering total paid-up capital or voting rights proportion is an alteration of share capital governed by Section 61. In contrast, extinguishing unpaid liability, writing off lost capital, and returning excess capital involve reduction of capital governed by Section 66.
Medium NORMAL · Asset Revaluation | Write-down | Capital Reduction Account
Plant and Machinery with a book value of Rs. 20,00,000 is written down to its recoverable value of Rs. 14,00,000 under a scheme. What amount is debited to Capital Reduction A/c?
A. Rs. 20,00,000
B. Rs. 14,00,000
C. Rs. 6,00,000 ✔
D. Rs. 34,00,000
Explanation: The overvaluation/write-down required for Plant and Machinery is Rs. 20,00,000 - Rs. 14,00,000 = Rs. 6,00,000. Capital Reduction Account is debited by Rs. 6,00,000 and Plant and Machinery Account is credited by Rs. 6,00,000 to bring the asset to its true recoverable value of Rs. 14,00,000.
Medium NORMAL · Creditors Haircut | Sacrifice | Capital Reduction Account
Creditors amounting to Rs. 4,00,000 agree to a 20% haircut provided the balance is paid immediately in cash. What is the credit to Capital Reduction Account?
A. Rs. 3,20,000
B. Rs. 80,000 ✔
C. Rs. 4,00,000
D. Nil
Explanation: A haircut of 20% on Rs. 4,00,000 equals Rs. 80,000 (0.20 × 4,00,000). The creditors surrender Rs. 80,000 of their claims, which is a sacrifice and gain to the company credited to Capital Reduction Account. The balance Rs. 3,20,000 paid in cash reduces Bank Account.
Medium NORMAL · Write-off Order | Accumulated Losses | Capital Reduction Rules
While executing an internal reconstruction scheme, which of the following accounts MUST be completely written off first before transferring any surplus to Capital Reserve?
A. General Reserve
B. Profit & Loss Debit Balance and Fictitious Assets ✔
C. Capital Redemption Reserve
D. Securities Premium Account
Explanation: The primary goal of internal reconstruction is to clean the balance sheet by writing off accumulated losses (Profit & Loss debit balance), intangible assets (Goodwill, Patents), and fictitious assets (preliminary expenses, discount on issue of debentures). Surplus in Capital Reduction Account can only be transferred to Capital Reserve after all losses and fictitious assets are fully eliminated.
Hard NORMAL · Consolidation | Capital Reduction | Share Calculation
A company reduces 40,000 equity shares of Rs. 10 each fully paid to Rs. 2 each fully paid, and then consolidates every 5 reduced shares into 1 new share of Rs. 10 each. What is the final number of equity shares?
A. 40,000 shares
B. 8,000 shares ✔
C. 20,000 shares
D. 16,000 shares
Explanation: First, 40,000 shares are reduced to face value of Rs. 2 each ( total paid-up capital = Rs. 80,000). Next, 5 shares of Rs. 2 each are consolidated into 1 share of Rs. 10 each. Total number of new shares = 40,000 ÷ 5 = 8,000 shares of Rs. 10 each fully paid ( total capital = 8,000 × 10 = Rs. 80,000).
Hard NORMAL · Write-off Priority | Partial Write-down | Capital Reduction Account
Capital Reduction Account has a credit balance of Rs. 5,00,000. Accumulated P&L loss is Rs. 3,20,000 and Patents are overstated by Rs. 2,00,000. To what extent can Patents be written down?
A. Rs. 2,00,000
B. Rs. 1,80,000 ✔
C. Rs. 5,00,000
D. Rs. 3,20,000
Explanation: Total credit available in Capital Reduction Account = Rs. 5,00,000. P&L debit balance of Rs. 3,20,000 must be written off completely first. Remaining balance in Capital Reduction Account = Rs. 5,00,000 - Rs. 3,20,000 = Rs. 1,80,000. Therefore, Patents can only be written down to the extent of the available balance, which is Rs. 1,80,000.
Hard NORMAL · Unrecorded Claim Settlement | Capital Reduction Account | Share Issue
An unrecorded claim for damages of Rs. 1,00,000 is settled during reconstruction by issuing 6,000 Equity Shares of Rs. 10 each as fully paid. What amount is debited to Capital Reduction Account?
A. Rs. 1,00,000
B. Rs. 60,000 ✔
C. Rs. 40,000
D. Nil
Explanation: The claim was unrecorded in the financial books. Settling this unrecorded liability by issuing equity shares of face value Rs. 60,000 (6,000 shares × Rs. 10) creates a new equity liability. Capital Reduction Account is debited by the fair value of consideration given (Rs. 60,000) and Equity Share Capital Account is credited by Rs. 60,000. The claim sacrifice of Rs. 40,000 requires no entry as original claim was unrecorded.
Hard NORMAL · Share Surrender Cancellation | Capital Reduction Account | Surrender Computation
Shareholders surrender 30% of 2,00,000 equity shares of Rs. 10 each. Out of these, 40,000 surrendered shares are reissued to debenture holders and remaining are cancelled. What amount is credited to Capital Reduction Account upon cancellation?
A. Rs. 6,00,000
B. Rs. 2,00,000 ✔
C. Rs. 4,00,000
D. Rs. 10,00,000
Explanation: Total shares surrendered = 30% of 2,00,000 = 60,000 shares of Rs. 10 each (total face value Rs. 6,00,000) credited to Share Surrender A/c. Reissued shares = 40,000 shares (face value Rs. 4,00,000). Remaining surrendered shares to be cancelled = 60,000 - 40,000 = 20,000 shares. Value of cancelled shares transferred from Share Surrender A/c to Capital Reduction A/c = 20,000 shares × Rs. 10 = Rs. 2,00,000.
Hard NORMAL · Preference Capital Conversion | No Sacrifice | Capital Reduction Account
10% Preference Shares of Rs. 1,00,000 (face value Rs. 100) are converted into 600 12% Preference Shares of Rs. 100 each and 4,000 Equity Shares of Rs. 10 each. What is the credit to Capital Reduction Account?
A. Rs. 40,000
B. Rs. 60,000
C. Nil ✔
D. Rs. 1,00,000
Explanation: Old 10% Preference Share Capital debited = Rs. 1,00,000. Consideration given: New 12% Preference Share Capital = 600 × Rs. 100 = Rs. 60,000, plus Equity Share Capital = 4,00,000 (4,000 × Rs. 10) = Rs. 40,000. Total value of new securities issued = Rs. 60,000 + Rs. 40,000 = Rs. 1,00,000. Since total value issued equals total face value surrendered, there is no sacrifice or gain, so credit to Capital Reduction Account is Nil.
Hard NORMAL · Securities Premium Utilization | Section 52 | Net Capital Reduction
A company has a P&L debit balance of Rs. 10,00,000 and Securities Premium Account balance of Rs. 3,00,000. Under NCLT scheme, Securities Premium is fully utilized. How much reduction from share capital is needed to eliminate the loss?
A. Rs. 10,00,000
B. Rs. 7,00,000 ✔
C. Rs. 3,00,000
D. Rs. 13,00,000
Explanation: Securities Premium can be utilized under Section 52 read with Section 66 for capital reduction schemes approved by court/NCLT. Total accumulated loss to write off = Rs. 10,00,000. Less: Securities Premium utilized = Rs. 3,00,000. Net loss remaining to be absorbed by Capital Reduction Account (via share capital reduction) = Rs. 7,00,000.
Hard NORMAL · Asset Takeover | Loan Settlement | Capital Reduction Credit
Bank Loan of Rs. 3,00,000 is secured against Land of book value Rs. 2,50,000. Bank takes over the Land at Rs. 3,20,000 in full settlement and pays Rs. 20,00,00 cash back to the company. What is the net credit to Capital Reduction Account?
A. Rs. 70,000 ✔
B. Rs. 50,000
C. Rs. 20,00,00
D. Rs. 3,20,000
Explanation: Land (Book value Rs. 2,50,000) was taken over at agreed value of Rs. 3,20,000. Profit on revaluation/transfer of Land = Rs. 3,20,000 - Rs. 2,50,000 = Rs. 70,00,00 credited to Capital Reduction Account. Bank Loan of Rs. 3,00,000 is settled against Rs. 3,00,000 of asset value, and Bank refunds remaining Rs. 20,000 cash to the company. The net credit to Capital Reduction Account is the profit on asset revaluation, which is Rs. 70,000.
Hard NORMAL · Partly Paid Shares | Paid-up Reduction | Capital Reduction Calculation
15,00,000 Equity Shares of Rs. 10 each (Rs. 8 paid up) are reduced to equity shares of Rs. 5 each fully paid up. What is the total reduction in share capital credited to Capital Reduction Account?
A. Rs. 75,00,000
B. Rs. 45,00,000 ✔
C. Rs. 30,00,000
D. Rs. 1,20,00,000
Explanation: Existing paid-up capital = 15,00,000 shares × Rs. 8 = Rs. 1,20,00,000. New paid-up capital = 15,00,000 shares × Rs. 5 = Rs. 75,00,000. Reduction in paid-up share capital = Rs. 1,20,00,000 - Rs. 75,00,000 = Rs. 45,00,000 (which is 15,00,000 shares × Rs. 3 reduction per share). This amount is credited to Capital Reduction Account.
CASE SCENARIO: Delta Ltd. has an existing capital structure of 50,000 Equity Shares of Rs. 100 each, Rs. 70 paid up. The balance sheet shows a Profit & Loss debit balance of Rs. 22,00,000, Plant & Machinery book value of Rs. 18,00,000, and Trade Creditors of Rs. 6,00,000. An NCLT approved internal reconstruction scheme is implemented as under: 1. A final call of Rs. 30 per share is made and fully collected in cash from shareholders. 2. Paid-up share capital is then reduced from Rs. 100 per share to Rs. 40 per share fully paid up. 3. Trade Creditors agree to forego 25% of their total claim. The balance claim is settled by issuing 9% Debentures for Rs. 3,00,000 and paying the remaining amount in cash. 4. Capital Reduction Account is utilized to completely write off the Profit & Loss debit balance, and the remaining credit balance in Capital Reduction Account is used to write down Plant & Machinery.
Medium SCENARIO · Capital Reduction Credit | Creditors Sacrifice | Call Money
Under Delta Ltd.'s scheme, what is the net total credit generated in the Capital Reduction Account from capital reduction and creditors' sacrifice?
A. Rs. 30,00,000
B. Rs. 31,50,000 ✔
C. Rs. 15,00,000
D. Rs. 36,00,000
Explanation: Call money creates paid-up capital of Rs. 100 per share (50,000 × Rs. 100 = Rs. 50,00,000). Reduction to Rs. 40 fully paid generates capital reduction credit = 50,000 × Rs. 60 = Rs. 30,00,000. Creditors' sacrifice = 25% of Rs. 6,00,000 = Rs. 1,50,000. Total credit generated in Capital Reduction Account = Rs. 30,00,000 + Rs. 1,50,000 = Rs. 31,50,000.
Hard SCENARIO · Cash Balance | Creditors Settlement | Call Proceeds
What is the net cash balance available with Delta Ltd. after receiving call money and paying the cash portion to creditors?
A. Rs. 15,00,000
B. Rs. 13,50,000 ✔
C. Rs. 12,00,000
D. Rs. 10,50,000
Explanation: Cash received from final call = 50,000 × Rs. 30 = Rs. 15,00,000. Creditors remaining after 25% waiver = Rs. 6,00,000 - Rs. 1,50,000 = Rs. 4,50,000. Out of Rs. 4,50,000, Rs. 3,00,000 is settled in debentures and balance Rs. 1,50,000 is paid in cash. Net cash remaining = Rs. 15,00,000 - Rs. 1,50,000 = Rs. 13,50,000.
Hard SCENARIO · Asset Write-down | Revised Book Value | Capital Reduction Application
What is the revised book value of Plant & Machinery in Delta Ltd.'s balance sheet after fully utilizing the remaining Capital Reduction Account?
A. Rs. 8,50,000 ✔
B. Rs. 9,50,000
C. Rs. 18,00,000
D. Rs. 6,00,000
Explanation: Total credit in Capital Reduction Account = Rs. 31,50,000. Less P&L debit balance written off = Rs. 22,00,000. Remaining balance available in Capital Reduction Account = Rs. 31,50,000 - Rs. 22,00,000 = Rs. 9,50,000. Plant & Machinery is written down by Rs. 9,50,000. Revised book value = Rs. 18,00,000 - Rs. 9,50,000 = Rs. 8,50,000.
Medium SCENARIO · Capital Reserve | Zero Balance | Final Transfer
What is the balance transferred to Capital Reserve Account upon completing Delta Ltd.'s internal reconstruction?
A. Rs. 1,50,000
B. Rs. 9,50,000
C. Nil (Rs. 0) ✔
D. Rs. 3,00,000
Explanation: The entire remaining balance of Rs. 9,50,000 in Capital Reduction Account after writing off P&L loss was fully absorbed to reduce Plant & Machinery. Since no credit balance remains in the Capital Reduction Account, the amount transferred to Capital Reserve is Nil (Rs. 0).
CASE SCENARIO: Zenith Ltd. underwent internal reconstruction. Its pre-reconstruction books show: - 10,000 10% Cumulative Preference Shares of Rs. 100 each fully paid: Rs. 10,00,000 - 50,000 Equity Shares of Rs. 10 each fully paid: Rs. 5,00,000 - 12% Debentures: Rs. 4,00,000 - Arrears of preference dividend for 2 years (unrecorded): Rs. 2,00,000 - Land & Building (Book Value): Rs. 3,00,000 Scheme of Reconstruction: 1. 10% Preference shares are reduced to Rs. 60 per share fully paid up. Preference shareholders waive 50% of dividend arrears. For the remaining 50% arrears, Equity Shares of Rs. 10 each fully paid are issued to them. 2. Equity shares are reduced to Rs. 3 per share fully paid up. 3. 12% Debenture holders accept Land & Building (Book value Rs. 3,00,000) at an agreed valuation of Rs. 3,50,000 in part satisfaction of Rs. 3,50,000 of their claims, and the balance debentures of Rs. 50,00,00 are paid off in cash.
Medium SCENARIO · Preference Dividend Arrears | Equity Share Issue | Capital Reduction Debit
What is the total amount debited to Capital Reduction Account on account of issuing equity shares for preference dividend arrears settlement in Zenith Ltd.?
A. Rs. 2,00,000
B. Rs. 1,00,000 ✔
C. Rs. 50,000
D. Nil
Explanation: Total unrecorded arrears = Rs. 2,00,000. 50% is waived (no entry). 50% (Rs. 1,00,000) is paid by issuing Equity Shares of Rs. 10 each. Since this was an unrecorded obligation, issuing equity shares of Rs. 1,00,000 requires debiting Capital Reduction Account by Rs. 1,00,000 and crediting Equity Share Capital Account by Rs. 1,00,000.
Hard SCENARIO · Gross Capital Reduction | Revaluation Gain | Capital Reduction Credit
What is the total credit balance in Capital Reduction Account of Zenith Ltd. before writing off any losses or asset overvaluations?
A. Rs. 7,50,000
B. Rs. 8,00,000 ✔
C. Rs. 7,00,000
D. Rs. 8,50,000
Explanation: Credits generated: Preference capital reduction = 10,000 × Rs. 40 = Rs. 4,00,000. Equity capital reduction = 50,000 × Rs. 7 = Rs. 3,50,000. Profit on transfer of Land & Building = Agreed value Rs. 3,50,000 - Book value Rs. 3,00,000 = Rs. 50,000. Total gross credit generated = Rs. 4,00,000 + Rs. 3,50,000 + Rs. 50,000 = Rs. 8,00,000.
Hard SCENARIO · Total Equity Shares | Share Count | Post-reconstruction
What is the total number of Equity Shares of Zenith Ltd. after executing all steps of the reconstruction scheme?
A. 50,000 shares
B. 60,000 shares ✔
C. 10,000 shares
D. 1,00,000 shares
Explanation: Existing equity shares reduced in value = 50,00,00 shares (now Rs. 3 each). New equity shares issued to preference shareholders for dividend arrears = Rs. 1,00,000 ÷ Rs. 10 per share = 10,000 shares of Rs. 10 each. Total equity shares post reconstruction = 50,000 + 10,000 = 60,000 shares.
Medium SCENARIO · Asset Takeover Gain | Debenture Settlement | Capital Reduction Credit
What is the net financial impact (gain/loss) credited or debited to Zenith Ltd.'s Capital Reduction Account on the takeover of Land & Building by debenture holders?
A. Gain of Rs. 50,000 credited ✔
B. Loss of Rs. 50,000 debited
C. No gain or loss
D. Gain of Rs. 3,50,000 credited
Explanation: Land & Building having a book value of Rs. 3,00,000 was accepted at Rs. 3,50,000 to settle Rs. 3,50,000 of debentures. Transferring an asset at Rs. 50,000 above book value generates a revaluation gain of Rs. 50,000, which is credited to the Capital Reduction Account.
CASE SCENARIO: Apex Manufacturing Ltd. has an existing capital of 1,00,000 Equity Shares of Rs. 10 each fully paid. The financial statements show a Profit & Loss debit balance of Rs. 4,50,000, Patents of Rs. 1,50,000, and 14% Debentures of Rs. 3,00,000. Under an approved scheme of internal reconstruction: 1. Shareholders agree to surrender 80% of their equity shares. 2. Out of the surrendered shares, 20,000 shares are reissued to 14% Debenture holders of Rs. 3,00,000 in full and final settlement of their claims. 3. The remaining surrendered shares are cancelled. 4. Capital Reduction Account is utilized to completely write off the Profit & Loss debit balance and Patents, and any surplus is transferred to Capital Reserve.
Medium SCENARIO · Share Surrender | Surrender Amount | Initial Entry
What amount is initially credited to the Share Surrender Account of Apex Manufacturing Ltd. upon surrender of 80% shares?
A. Rs. 10,00,000
B. Rs. 8,00,000 ✔
C. Rs. 2,00,000
D. Rs. 6,00,000
Explanation: Total equity shares = 1,00,000 of Rs. 10 each = Rs. 10,00,000. 80% surrendered = 80,000 shares of Rs. 10 each = Rs. 8,00,000. The entry is Equity Share Capital A/c Dr. Rs. 8,00,000 to Share Surrender A/c Rs. 8,00,000.
Hard SCENARIO · Surrender Cancellation | Capital Reduction Credit | Surrender Account
What is the amount transferred from Share Surrender Account to Capital Reduction Account upon cancellation of unutilized surrendered shares in Apex Manufacturing Ltd.?
A. Rs. 8,00,000
B. Rs. 6,00,000 ✔
C. Rs. 2,00,000
D. Rs. 4,00,000
Explanation: Total surrendered shares = 80,000 shares (Rs. 8,00,000). Shares reissued to debenture holders = 20,000 shares (Rs. 2,00,000). Remaining surrendered shares cancelled = 80,000 - 20,000 = 60,000 shares of Rs. 10 each = Rs. 6,00,000. Upon cancellation, Share Surrender Account is debited and Capital Reduction Account is credited by Rs. 6,00,000.
Hard SCENARIO · Debenture Sacrifice | Capital Reduction Credit | Surrender Reissue
What amount is credited to Capital Reduction Account directly from the settlement of 14% Debenture holders in Apex Manufacturing Ltd.?
A. Rs. 1,00,000 ✔
B. Rs. 3,00,000
C. Rs. 2,00,000
D. Nil
Explanation: Debenture holders had a claim of Rs. 3,00,000. They accepted 20,000 surrendered shares of face value Rs. 2,00,000 in full settlement. The entry is 14% Debentures A/c Dr. Rs. 3,00,000 to Share Surrender A/c Rs. 2,00,000 and to Capital Reduction A/c Rs. 1,00,000. The sacrifice of Rs. 1,00,000 made by debenture holders is credited to Capital Reduction Account.
Hard SCENARIO · Capital Reserve Calculation | Final Balance | Scheme Surplus
What is the final balance remaining in Capital Reserve Account of Apex Manufacturing Ltd. after writing off P&L debit balance and Patents?
A. Rs. 1,00,000 ✔
B. Rs. 2,00,000
C. Nil
D. Rs. 50,000
Explanation: Total credit accumulated in Capital Reduction Account = Rs. 6,00,000 (cancelled shares) + Rs. 1,00,000 (debenture sacrifice) = Rs. 7,00,000. Write-offs: P&L debit balance Rs. 4,50,000 + Patents Rs. 1,50,000 = Rs. 6,00,000. Surplus balance transferred to Capital Reserve = Rs. 7,00,000 - Rs. 6,00,000 = Rs. 1,00,000.
CASE SCENARIO: Orion Ltd. has the following balance sheet items prior to reconstruction: - Equity Shares of Rs. 100 each: Rs. 15,00,000 (15,000 shares) - 10% Debentures: Rs. 5,00,000 - Trade Payables: Rs. 7,00,000 - Land & Building: Rs. 8,00,000 - Machinery: Rs. 12,00,000 - Inventory: Rs. 5,00,000 - Trade Receivables: Rs. 4,00,000 - Profit & Loss Debit Balance: Rs. 6,00,000 NCLT Approved Scheme: 1. Equity shares are reduced to Rs. 40 per share fully paid up. 2. Trade payables agree to forego 20% of their claims. Out of the balance, 30% of original claim is paid by issuing 12% Debentures and remaining in cash. 3. Land & Building is revalued upwards by 25%. 4. Inventory is written down by 20% and a Provision for Doubtful Debts is created at 10% on Trade Receivables. 5. Capital Reduction Account is used to write off Profit & Loss debit balance, and any balance left is used to write down Machinery.
Hard SCENARIO · Capital Reduction Credits | Revaluation Gain | Payables Haircut
What is the total credit generated in the Capital Reduction Account of Orion Ltd. from equity capital reduction, trade payables' sacrifice, and land revaluation combined?
A. Rs. 12,40,000 ✔
B. Rs. 11,00,000
C. Rs. 10,40,000
D. Rs. 14,00,000
Explanation: Equity reduction = 15,000 × Rs. 60 = Rs. 9,00,000. Trade payables sacrifice = 20% of Rs. 7,00,000 = Rs. 1,40,000. Land upward revaluation = 25% of Rs. 8,00,000 = Rs. 2,00,000. Total credit generated in Capital Reduction Account = Rs. 9,00,000 + Rs. 1,40,000 + Rs. 2,00,000 = Rs. 12,40,000.
Medium SCENARIO · Capital Reduction Debits | Asset Provision | P&L Write-off
What is the total amount debited to Capital Reduction Account of Orion Ltd. for Inventory write-down, Provision for Doubtful Debts, and P&L debit balance?
A. Rs. 7,40,000 ✔
B. Rs. 6,00,000
C. Rs. 7,00,000
D. Rs. 8,00,000
Explanation: Debits: Inventory write-down = 20% of Rs. 5,00,000 = Rs. 1,00,000. Provision for Doubtful Debts = 10% of Rs. 4,00,000 = Rs. 40,000. P&L debit balance = Rs. 6,00,000. Total debits for these items = Rs. 1,00,000 + Rs. 40,000 + Rs. 6,00,000 = Rs. 7,40,000.
Hard SCENARIO · Machinery Book Value | Write-down Calculation | Balance Sheet
What is the revised book value of Machinery in Orion Ltd.'s post-reconstruction Balance Sheet?
A. Rs. 7,00,000 ✔
B. Rs. 5,00,000
C. Rs. 12,00,000
D. Rs. 8,00,000
Explanation: Total Capital Reduction credit = Rs. 12,40,000. Total debits before Machinery = Rs. 7,40,000. Remaining balance available in Capital Reduction Account to write down Machinery = Rs. 12,40,000 - Rs. 7,40,000 = Rs. 5,00,000. Revised Machinery book value = Original Rs. 12,00,000 - Rs. 5,00,000 write-down = Rs. 7,00,000.
Medium SCENARIO · Cash Requirement | Payables Settlement | Internal Reconstruction
What is the total cash payment required by Orion Ltd. to discharge its liability towards trade payables under the scheme?
A. Rs. 3,50,000 ✔
B. Rs. 2,10,000
C. Rs. 5,60,000
D. Rs. 1,40,000
Explanation: Original trade payables = Rs. 7,00,000. Less 20% waived = Rs. 1,40,000. Balance remaining = Rs. 5,60,000. Issued 12% Debentures = 30% of original Rs. 7,00,000 = Rs. 2,10,000. Balance cash required to be paid = Rs. 5,60,000 - Rs. 2,10,000 = Rs. 3,50,000.
CASE SCENARIO: Nova Cables Ltd. was restructured as per an NCLT approved scheme. Existing financial status: - 20,000 8% Cumulative Preference Shares of Rs. 100 each fully paid: Rs. 20,00,000 - 1,00,000 Equity Shares of Rs. 10 each fully paid: Rs. 10,00,000 - Arrears of Preference Dividend for 3 years: Rs. 4,80,000 (unrecorded) - Goodwill: Rs. 2,00,000 - Profit & Loss Debit balance: Rs. 11,00,000 Reconstruction Terms: 1. 8% Preference shares reduced to Rs. 70 per share fully paid up. 2. Preference dividend arrears waived by 2/3rd. Balance 1/3rd paid by issuing Equity Shares of Rs. 10 each fully paid. 3. Equity shares reduced to Rs. 2 per share fully paid up. 4. Reconstruction expenses of Rs. 30,000 paid in cash. 5. An unrecorded investment was discovered and sold for Rs. 1,20,000 cash. 6. Goodwill and Profit & Loss debit balance are written off completely, and remaining balance in Capital Reduction Account is transferred to Capital Reserve.
Medium SCENARIO · Gross Credits | Unrecorded Asset Realization | Capital Reduction
What is the total credit accumulated in the Capital Reduction Account of Nova Cables Ltd. before deducting expenses and loss write-offs?
A. Rs. 15,20,000 ✔
B. Rs. 14,00,000
C. Rs. 15,00,000
D. Rs. 18,00,000
Explanation: Credits generated: Preference capital reduction = 20,000 × Rs. 30 = Rs. 6,00,000. Equity capital reduction = 1,00,000 × Rs. 8 = Rs. 8,00,000. Realization of unrecorded investment = Rs. 1,20,000. Total accumulated credits = Rs. 6,00,000 + Rs. 8,00,000 + Rs. 1,20,000 = Rs. 15,20,000.
Medium SCENARIO · Dividend Settlement | New Share Issue | Share Calculation
How many new Equity Shares of Rs. 10 each are issued by Nova Cables Ltd. to Preference Shareholders in settlement of preference dividend arrears?
A. 16,000 shares ✔
B. 48,000 shares
C. 32,000 shares
D. 160,000 shares
Explanation: Total dividend arrears = Rs. 4,80,000. Waived 2/3rd = Rs. 3,20,000. Payable 1/3rd = Rs. 1,60,000. Paid by issuing Equity Shares of Rs. 10 each. Number of new equity shares issued = Rs. 1,60,000 ÷ Rs. 10 = 16,000 shares.
Hard SCENARIO · Capital Reserve | Surplus Calculation | Reconstruction Scheme
What is the net amount transferred to Capital Reserve Account upon completion of Nova Cables Ltd.'s internal reconstruction?
A. Rs. 30,000 ✔
B. Rs. 1,90,000
C. Nil
D. Rs. 60,000
Explanation: Total Credits = Rs. 15,20,000. Total Debits: Dividend settlement Rs. 1,60,000 + Reconstruction expenses Rs. 30,000 + Goodwill written off Rs. 2,00,000 + P&L loss written off Rs. 11,00,000 = Rs. 14,90,000. Surplus balance transferred to Capital Reserve = Rs. 15,20,000 - Rs. 14,90,000 = Rs. 30,000.
Hard SCENARIO · Post-reconstruction Capital | Balance Sheet Presentation | Share Capital Total
What is the total Equity Share Capital reported in the Balance Sheet of Nova Cables Ltd. after completing the reconstruction scheme?
A. Rs. 3,60,000 ✔
B. Rs. 2,00,000
C. Rs. 1,60,000
D. Rs. 10,00,000
Explanation: Existing equity share capital reduced to Rs. 2 per share = 1,00,000 shares × Rs. 2 = Rs. 2,00,000. New equity shares issued for dividend arrears = 16,000 shares × Rs. 10 = Rs. 1,60,000. Total post-reconstruction Equity Share Capital = Rs. 2,00,000 + Rs. 1,60,000 = Rs. 3,60,000.

Paper 1: Advanced Accounting · Module 3 · Chapter 15:

Accounts — 55 rows
Easy NORMAL · Branch Accounting | Independent Branch | Bookkeeping
Which of the following branches maintains independent accounting records and prepares its own Trial Balance?
A. Dependent Branch
B. Independent Branch ✔
C. Foreign Branch operating under AS 11 without self-accounting
D. Inland Branch with centralized billing
Explanation: An independent branch maintains its own comprehensive set of books of account and prepares its own Trial Balance, Trading, and Profit & Loss Account. It only interacts with the Head Office via a Current Account. Dependent branches do not maintain independent double-entry books.
Medium NORMAL · Invoice Price | Stock Reserve | Dependent Branch
In the books of the Head Office, goods sent to a dependent branch at an invoice price (cost plus profit) require which of the following entries to cancel the loading at the end of the accounting period?
A. Goods Sent to Branch A/c Dr. to Branch A/c
B. Branch Adjustment A/c Dr. to Stock Reserve A/c
C. Branch Stock A/c Dr. to Branch Adjustment A/c
D. Stock Reserve A/c Dr. to Branch Adjustment A/c ✔
Explanation: To eliminate unrealized profit included in the closing stock of an invoice-price branch, the entry is Stock Reserve A/c Dr. to Branch Adjustment A/c (or Trading A/c). Conversely, the loading on goods sent is cancelled by debiting Goods Sent to Branch A/c and crediting Branch Adjustment A/c.
Easy NORMAL · Stock and Debtors System | Branch Debtors | Dependent Branch
When preparing branch accounts under the stock and debtors system, how is cash received from debtors recorded in the Branch Debtors Account?
A. Debited to Branch Debtors A/c
B. Credited to Branch Debtors A/c ✔
C. Debited to Branch Cash A/c and credited to Head Office A/c
D. Ignored as it is an internal transaction
Explanation: Cash received from debtors reduces the total amount due from branch debtors. Therefore, it is credited to the Branch Debtors Account and debited to the Branch Cash/Bank Account.
Medium NORMAL · Foreign Branch | AS 11 | Translation of Assets
Under AS 11 (The Effects of Changes in Foreign Exchange Rates), how are fixed assets of an integral foreign operation translated into the reporting currency?
A. At the closing rate prevailing on the balance sheet date
B. At the average rate for the period
C. At the actual historical rate on the date of purchase ✔
D. At the opening rate of the financial year
Explanation: As per AS 11, for an integral foreign operation, monetary items are translated at the closing rate, while non-monetary items like fixed assets are translated at the exchange rate on the date of the transaction (historical rate).
Medium NORMAL · Non-Integral Foreign Operation | AS 11 | Translation Reserve
How is the translation difference arising from the translation of a non-integral foreign entity's financial statements treated under AS 11?
A. Recognized immediately in the Statement of Profit and Loss
B. Accumulated in a foreign currency translation reserve until disposal ✔
C. Adjusted against General Reserve directly
D. Capitalized as part of goodwill
Explanation: Under AS 11, exchange differences arising on translation of the financial statements of a non-integral foreign operation are accumulated in a foreign currency translation reserve (FCTR) until the disposal of the net investment.
Easy NORMAL · Head Office Books | Branch Current Account | Reconciliation
In the context of branch accounting, what does a debit balance in the 'Branch Current Account' in the books of the Head Office signify?
A. Liability of the Head Office towards the branch
B. Amount due from the branch to the Head Office ✔
C. Total profit earned by the branch during the year
D. Accumulated depreciation of branch assets
Explanation: The Branch Current Account maintained in the Head Office books is an asset account representing the net investment or amount due from the branch.
Medium NORMAL · Invoice Price | Loading Calculation | Branch Trading A/c
In the Final Accounts (Trading and P&L method) of a dependent branch, if goods are sent by HO at cost plus 25%, what is the percentage of loading on invoice price?
A. 25.00%
B. 20.00% ✔
C. 16.67%
D. 33.33%
Explanation: If profit is 25% on cost, let cost = 100, profit = 25, invoice price = 125. The loading percentage on invoice price is (25 / 125) * 100 = 20%.
Medium NORMAL · Goods in Transit | Reconciliation | Head Office Books
When goods are in transit from the Head Office to a branch at the end of the accounting period, what adjustment entry does the Head Office make if the branch has not yet recorded it?
A. Goods in Transit A/c Dr. to Branch A/c ✔
B. Branch A/c Dr. to Goods Sent to Branch A/c
C. Trading A/c Dr. to Goods in Transit A/c
D. No entry is required in HO books
Explanation: Goods in transit represent stock belonging to the branch that has left the HO. The HO records 'Goods in Transit A/c Dr. to Branch A/c' so that the Branch Current Account reflects the correct balance considering goods dispatched.
Easy NORMAL · AS 11 | Monetary Items | Foreign Branch
Which of the following is treated as a monetary item when translating a foreign branch's financial statements under AS 11?
A. Inventory
B. Plant and Machinery
C. Trade Payables ✔
D. Share Capital
Explanation: Monetary items are units of currency held and assets and liabilities to be received or paid in a fixed or determinable number of units of currency. Trade Payables are monetary items, whereas inventory and plant & machinery are non-monetary.
Easy NORMAL · Debtors System | Branch Stock Account | Closing Inventory
Under the debtors system for a dependent branch, what does the closing balance of the Branch Stock Account represent?
A. Cost of goods sold by the branch
B. Closing inventory held at the branch ✔
C. Total cash remitted to Head Office
D. Total credit sales made during the period
Explanation: In the debtors system, the Branch Stock Account is maintained at invoice price. The balancing figure at the end of the period represents the closing stock at the branch.
Hard NORMAL · Debtors System | Local Purchases | Branch Accounting
If a branch purchases goods locally from third parties and pays for them out of branch cash, how is this recorded in the Head Office books under the debtors system?
A. Recorded via Branch Trading Account
B. Not recorded in HO books if local purchase is permitted ✔
C. Debited to Branch Stock A/c and Credited to Branch Cash A/c
D. Debited to Purchases A/c and Credited to HO A/c
Explanation: Under the standard debtors system, local purchases made by the branch out of branch cash or petty cash are generally adjusted through memorandum records or handled directly within the branch's cash/stock summary if authorized, but typically require no direct entry in HO books unless cash remitted/withdrawn is affected.
Medium NORMAL · Independent Branch | Head Office Account | Nature of Accounts
In independent branch accounting, what is the nature of the 'Head Office Account' appearing in the Trial Balance of the branch?
A. Nominal Account
B. Real Account
C. Personal Account representing HO's equity/liability ✔
D. Fictitious Asset Account
Explanation: The Head Office Account in the branch books represents the owner's equity or liability of the branch towards the Head Office, functioning essentially as a personal account.
Medium NORMAL · Non-Integral Foreign Operation | AS 11 | Revenue Translation
How are revenue and expense items of a non-integral foreign operation translated into the reporting currency under AS 11?
A. At the closing rate on the balance sheet date
B. At the actual exchange rate on the date of each transaction
C. At the average rate prevailing during the reporting period ✔
D. At the opening rate of the financial year
Explanation: As per AS 11, for a non-integral foreign operation, income and expense items are translated at the exchange rates at the dates of the transactions, or an average rate approximating those rates is often used for practicality.
Easy NORMAL · Cash in Transit | Reconciliation | Branch Current Account
When cash is remitted by a branch to the Head Office, but has not been received by the Head Office before the close of the financial year, what is this called?
A. Cash in Transit ✔
B. Remittance in Suspense
C. Unadjusted Cash
D. Unrealized Cash Reserve
Explanation: Cash remitted by the branch but not yet received or recorded by the Head Office at the balance sheet date is termed 'Cash in Transit'.
Medium NORMAL · Stock and Debtors System | Stock Shortage | Branch Stock
In a dependent branch operating under the Stock and Debtors system, what does a shortage of stock revealed on memorandum stock reconciliation represent?
A. Normal loss or abnormal loss/pilferage ✔
B. Profit on sale of goods
C. Exchange gain on foreign remittances
D. Head Office profit margin
Explanation: A shortage in the Branch Stock Account compared to physical stock verification (adjusted for sales, returns, etc.) represents normal loss, abnormal loss, pilferage, or unrecorded wastage.
Hard NORMAL · Stock and Debtors System | Branch Accounts | Exclusions
Which of the following accounts is NOT maintained under the Stock and Debtors System for a dependent branch?
A. Branch Stock A/c
B. Branch Debtors A/c
C. Branch P&L A/c
D. Branch Trading A/c ✔
Explanation: Under the Stock and Debtors System, specific accounts like Branch Stock, Branch Debtors, Branch Expenses, Branch Adjustment, Branch Cash, and Branch P&L are maintained, but a traditional Branch Trading Account is usually substituted by the Branch Adjustment Account.
Medium NORMAL · Independent Branch | Incorporation | Reciprocal Accounts
When incorporating the trial balance of an independent branch into the Head Office books, which accounts are typically cancelled or eliminated?
A. Branch third-party debtors and creditors
B. Branch Current Account in HO books and Head Office Account in branch books ✔
C. Branch depreciation and fixed assets
D. Branch opening inventory and closing inventory
Explanation: During consolidation or incorporation of independent branch books, reciprocal accounts—namely the Branch Current Account in the HO books and the Head Office Account in the branch books—are eliminated/cancelled.
Easy NORMAL · Head Office Books | Branch Expenses | Journal Entries
If a Head Office incurs expenses on behalf of a branch, what entry does the Head Office pass in its own books?
A. Expenses A/c Dr. to Bank A/c
B. Branch Current A/c Dr. to Bank/Cash A/c ✔
C. Branch Current A/c Dr. to Expenses A/c
D. Bank A/c Dr. to Branch Current A/c
Explanation: When HO incurs expenses for the branch, it pays out of its cash/bank and treats it as an amount receivable from the branch, resulting in a debit to the Branch Current Account and credit to Bank/Cash.
Hard NORMAL · Integral Foreign Operation | Depreciation Translation | AS 11
How should depreciation on a foreign branch's fixed assets be translated when the foreign operation is classified as integral?
A. At the closing rate on the balance sheet date
B. At the average rate for the accounting period
C. At the historical rate corresponding to the date of purchase of the fixed asset ✔
D. At the rate prevailing on the date depreciation is charged
Explanation: Since fixed assets of an integral foreign operation are translated at historical rates, the depreciation on those assets is also translated at the historical exchange rates corresponding to the dates of purchase of the respective fixed assets.
Medium NORMAL · Branch Adjustment Account | Invoice Price | Gross Profit
In the context of branch accounting, what is the primary purpose of the 'Branch Adjustment Account'?
A. To calculate gross profit when goods are invoiced at selling/invoice price ✔
B. To record remittances between HO and branch
C. To adjust foreign exchange rate fluctuations
D. To track petty cash expenses incurred by the branch manager
Explanation: The Branch Adjustment Account is used primarily in invoice-price branch accounting to eliminate loading, record gross profit, and incorporate loading on opening and closing stock.
Medium NORMAL · AS 11 | Integral Foreign Operation | Foreign Branch Classification
An Indian company has a branch in London. The London branch's transactions are financed mainly by the Head Office in Mumbai and it purchases goods from Mumbai. How is this London branch classified under AS 11?
A. Non-Integral Foreign Operation
B. Integral Foreign Operation ✔
C. Independent Foreign Branch
D. Subsidiary Entity
Explanation: An operation that is carried on as an extension of the reporting enterprise (e.g., selling goods imported from HO and remitting proceeds to HO) is classified as an integral foreign operation under AS 11.
Hard NORMAL · Reconciliation | Goods in Transit | Branch Books
When reconciling the Branch Current Account and Head Office Account, if the HO has debited the branch for goods in transit, what adjustment should the branch make in its memorandum reconciliation?
A. Add goods in transit to the Head Office Account balance ✔
B. Deduct goods in transit from the Head Office Account balance
C. Debit its own Trading Account
D. Ignore the item as it belongs to HO
Explanation: In the branch's reconciliation statement with the HO account, goods sent by HO but not received yet are treated as received (by adding to the HO account balance) to match the HO's credit/debit adjustments.
Medium NORMAL · Opening Stock Reserve | Branch Adjustment | Invoice Price
What is the accounting treatment for opening stock reserve when preparing final accounts of a branch receiving goods at invoice price?
A. Credited to Branch Adjustment Account
B. Debited to Branch Adjustment Account ✔
C. Credited to Stock Reserve Account
D. Debited to Goods Sent to Branch Account
Explanation: The opening stock reserve (loading on opening stock) is debited to the Branch Adjustment Account (with a corresponding credit to Stock Reserve) to bring the opening stock down from invoice price to cost.
Easy NORMAL · Wholesale Branch | Cost Price | Branch Trading A/c
Under the wholesale branch system where goods are sent at cost, what is the nature of the profit earned by the branch?
A. It is treated as Head Office general profit and transferred to General Reserve
B. It is computed through a normal Trading and Profit and Loss Account for the branch ✔
C. It is eliminated entirely as unrealized profit
D. It is credited directly to Branch Adjustment Account
Explanation: When goods are sent at cost, the branch operates independently in terms of profit determination, and a standard Branch Trading and P&L Account is prepared to ascertain branch profit without any loading eliminations.
Easy NORMAL · AS 11 | Cash Translation | Closing Rate
Which exchange rate is used to translate the opening and closing balances of cash and bank for a non-integral foreign operation under AS 11?
A. Average rate of the year
B. Historical rate on the date of acquisition
C. Closing rate on the balance sheet date ✔
D. Opening rate of the year
Explanation: Cash and bank balances (being monetary items) are always translated at the closing rate on the balance sheet date, regardless of whether the foreign operation is integral or non-integral.
Medium NORMAL · Goods Returned | Debtors System | Head Office Books
If a branch returns damaged goods directly to the Head Office, how does the Head Office record this under the debtors system?
A. Goods Sent to Branch A/c Dr. to Branch Stock A/c ✔
B. Branch Stock A/c Dr. to Goods Sent to Branch A/c
C. Trading A/c Dr. to Branch Stock A/c
D. Branch Adjustment A/c Dr. to Branch Debtors A/c
Explanation: When goods are returned by the branch to the HO, the original entry of sending goods is reversed in the HO books, i.e., Goods Sent to Branch A/c is debited and Branch Stock A/c is credited (at invoice price).
Medium NORMAL · Independent Branch | Incorporation | Consolidation
When incorporating independent branch trial balance into HO books, how are branch revenues and expenses handled?
A. Ignored because only assets and liabilities are incorporated
B. Combined line-by-line with the Head Office's own revenues and expenses ✔
C. Transferred directly to Capital Account
D. Netted off and shown as a single item called 'Branch Net Result'
Explanation: In independent branch accounting, the branch revenues and expenses are incorporated line-by-line into the Head Office's Statement of Profit and Loss during final consolidation.
Hard NORMAL · AS 11 | Non-Integral Foreign Operation | Distinguishing Features
What is the primary distinguishing feature of a non-integral foreign operation compared to an integral one under AS 11?
A. It is financially independent and conducts business as if it were a distinct entity. ✔
B. It relies entirely on Head Office for cash financing and inventory purchases.
C. It does not maintain independent books of accounts.
D. Its financial statements are never translated into the reporting currency.
Explanation: A non-integral foreign operation accumulates cash and other monetary items, incurs expenses, generates income, and arranges borrowings substantially in its local currency, operating with significant financial autonomy.
Easy NORMAL · Loading | Cost Plus | Invoice Price
In branch accounts, if the Head Office charges goods to the branch at cost plus 33.1/3%, what is the loading on cost?
A. 25.00%
B. 33.33% ✔
C. 20.00%
D. 50.00%
Explanation: Cost plus 33.1/3% (or 1/3rd of cost) means if cost is 3, profit is 1, and invoice price is 4. The loading on cost is 33.33% (1/3).
Hard NORMAL · Integral Foreign Operation | Depreciation | Historical Rate
If an asset of an integral foreign branch was purchased when the exchange rate was 1 USD = INR 70, and the closing rate is 1 USD = INR 75, at what rate should depreciation for the year be calculated and translated?
A. INR 75 per USD
B. INR 72.50 per USD (Average rate)
C. INR 70 per USD ✔
D. Rate on the last day of the month
Explanation: For an integral foreign operation, fixed assets are translated at the historical rate (date of purchase, i.e., INR 70), and depreciation is also translated at the same historical rate.
CASE SCENARIO: Zenith Ltd. (Head Office in Delhi) operates a dependent retail branch in Jaipur. Goods are invoiced to the branch at cost plus 25%. All branch sales are for cash and remitted immediately to the Head Office. The branch maintains a Branch Stock Account and Branch Debtors Account under the debtors system. For the year ended 31st March 2026, the following details are available: Opening Stock at Branch (Invoice Price) ₹ 1,25,000; Goods sent to Branch (Invoice Price) ₹ 6,25,000; Cash Sales ₹ 6,00,000; Closing Stock at Branch (Invoice Price) ₹ 1,50,000.
Medium SCENARIO · Loading | Opening Stock | Invoice Price
What is the amount of loading included in the opening stock of the Jaipur branch?
A. ₹ 31,250
B. ₹ 25,000 ✔
C. ₹ 30,000
D. ₹ 20,000
Explanation: Opening stock at invoice price is ₹ 1,25,000. Since goods are invoiced at cost plus 25% (or 20% on invoice price), loading = 20% of ₹ 1,25,000 = ₹ 25,000.
Medium SCENARIO · Goods Sent to Branch | Loading | Invoice Price
What is the total loading on goods sent to the branch during the year?
A. ₹ 1,25,000 ✔
B. ₹ 1,56,250
C. ₹ 1,00,000
D. ₹ 1,15,000
Explanation: Goods sent to branch at invoice price = ₹ 6,25,000. Loading is 20% on invoice price (25/125), which equals ₹ 6,25,000 * (25/125) = ₹ 1,25,000.
Medium SCENARIO · Stock Reserve | Closing Stock | Invoice Price
What is the amount of stock reserve required on the closing stock of the branch at 31st March 2026?
A. ₹ 37,500
B. ₹ 30,000 ✔
C. ₹ 25,000
D. ₹ 31,250
Explanation: Closing stock at invoice price is ₹ 1,50,000. The loading percentage on invoice price is 20% (25/125). Stock reserve = 20% of ₹ 1,50,000 = ₹ 30,000.
Hard SCENARIO · Gross Profit | Branch Adjustment | Invoice Price
What is the gross profit transferred to the Branch Adjustment Account from the Branch Stock Account for the year?
A. ₹ 1,30,000
B. ₹ 1,20,000 ✔
C. ₹ 1,25,000
D. ₹ 1,00,000
Explanation: Opening Stock (1,25,000) + Goods Sent (6,25,000) = 7,50,000. Less: Closing Stock (1,50,000) = Cost of goods sold/sold goods at invoice price ₹ 6,00,000. Since cash sales equal invoice value, gross profit (loading realized) on sales is 20% of ₹ 6,00,000 = ₹ 1,20,000.
CASE SCENARIO: Omega Inc., an Indian company, has a branch in New York. The New York branch is classified as an integral foreign operation under AS 11. The trial balance of the New York branch as on 31st March 2026 shows: Share Capital / HO Account: USD 50,000; Fixed Assets (purchased when exchange rate was ₹ 72/USD): USD 20,000; Opening Inventory (purchased when exchange rate was ₹ 74/USD): USD 10,000; Monetary Assets (Cash and Receivables): USD 15,000; Monetary Liabilities (Payables): USD 5,000. Relevant exchange rates are: Opening rate = ₹ 73/USD; Closing rate = ₹ 76/USD; Average rate = ₹ 74.50/USD.
Medium SCENARIO · AS 11 | Fixed Assets Translation | Integral Operation
At what exchange rate should the Fixed Assets of the New York branch be translated in the financial statements?
A. ₹ 76.00 per USD
B. ₹ 74.50 per USD
C. ₹ 72.00 per USD ✔
D. ₹ 73.00 per USD
Explanation: Under AS 11, for an integral foreign operation, non-monetary items like fixed assets are translated at the historical exchange rate prevailing on the date of transaction, which is ₹ 72 per USD.
Medium SCENARIO · AS 11 | Monetary Assets | Closing Rate
What is the translated value of the Monetary Assets (Cash and Receivables) of USD 15,000 on the balance sheet date?
A. ₹ 10,80,000
B. ₹ 11,40,000 ✔
C. ₹ 11,17,500
D. ₹ 10,95,000
Explanation: Monetary items are translated at the closing rate on the balance sheet date. USD 15,000 * ₹ 76.00/USD = ₹ 11,40,000.
Hard SCENARIO · AS 11 | Inventory Translation | Historical Rate
How is the translation of opening inventory handled for this integral foreign operation under AS 11?
A. Translated at the closing rate of ₹ 76/USD
B. Translated at the average rate of ₹ 74.50/USD
C. Translated at the historical rate of ₹ 74/USD ✔
D. Ignored for translation purposes
Explanation: Inventory is a non-monetary item. For an integral foreign operation, inventory carried at cost is translated at the historical exchange rate prevailing on the date of purchase (₹ 74/USD).
Medium SCENARIO · AS 11 | Exchange Difference | Integral Operation
Where is the resulting exchange difference arising from the translation of the integral foreign operation's financial statements recognized?
A. Foreign Currency Translation Reserve (FCTR)
B. Statement of Profit and Loss ✔
C. General Reserve directly
D. Capital Reserve
Explanation: As per AS 11, exchange differences arising on the translation of financial statements of an integral foreign operation are recognized in the Statement of Profit and Loss of the period.
CASE SCENARIO: Beta Branch of Metro Ltd. maintains independent books of accounts. On 31st March 2026, before final incorporation, the Trial Balance of Beta Branch shows a 'Head Office Account' credit balance of ₹ 2,40,000, while the 'Branch Current Account' in the Head Office books shows a debit balance of ₹ 2,15,000. Investigation reveals the following discrepancies: (1) Head Office sent goods worth ₹ 35,000 on 28th March 2026, which the branch received on 3rd April 2026. (2) The branch collected ₹ 10,000 from a Head Office debtor on 30th March 2026 but recorded it only in branch books; HO was unaware.
Hard SCENARIO · Reconciliation | Goods in Transit | Independent Branch
What is the correct treatment for the goods in transit worth ₹ 35,000 in the reconciliation statement?
A. Added to Branch Current Account in HO books ✔
B. Deducted from Branch Current Account in HO books
C. Added to Head Office Account in branch books
D. Deducted from Head Office Account in branch books
Explanation: HO has recorded the dispatch (debiting Branch Current A/c), but the branch hasn't received/recorded it yet. In reconciling the HO books, the goods in transit represent an asset already debited by HO, so the ₹ 2,15,000 matches once transit items are accounted for properly (or viewed from branch perspective, added to HO account balance).
Hard SCENARIO · Reconciliation | HO Books | Debtor Collection
What entry should the Head Office pass upon discovering that the branch collected ₹ 10,000 from an HO debtor?
A. Branch Current A/c Dr. to Branch Debtors A/c
B. Branch Debtors A/c Dr. to Branch Current A/c
C. Branch Current A/c Dr. to Sundry Debtors A/c ✔
D. Sundry Debtors A/c Dr. to Branch Current A/c
Explanation: When the branch collects cash from an HO debtor, the HO needs to reduce its Sundry Debtors balance and increase the receivable from the branch (Branch Current A/c Dr. to Sundry Debtors A/c).
Hard SCENARIO · Reconciled Balance | Branch Accounting | Current Account
What is the reconciled balance of the current accounts after accounting for all valid adjustments?
A. ₹ 2,15,000
B. ₹ 2,50,000
C. ₹ 2,40,000
D. ₹ 2,25,000 ✔
Explanation: HO Branch Current A/c starts at ₹ 2,15,000. Add goods in transit ₹ 35,000 (dispatched by HO, so already in HO books), and adjust for debtor collection ₹ 10,000 not in HO books: ₹ 2,15,000 + ₹ 35,000 (transit in HO) - ₹ 25,000 net effect yields reconciled figure of ₹ 2,25,000 matching branch adjusted books.
Medium SCENARIO · Incorporation | Reciprocal Accounts | Consolidation
During the incorporation of the independent branch trial balance into the Head Office books, what happens to the reciprocal accounts?
A. They are added together to form total branch equity.
B. They are offset and eliminated against each other. ✔
C. The difference is transferred to Capital Reserve.
D. They remain as separate asset and liability lines on the consolidated balance sheet.
Explanation: Reciprocal accounts (Branch Current Account in HO books and Head Office Account in branch books) represent internal transactions between the same legal entity and must be eliminated during consolidation.
CASE SCENARIO: Global Retails Ltd. has a branch at Pune which is supplied goods at invoice price (cost plus 33.1/3%). Pune branch sells goods on both cash and credit terms. For the year ended 31st March 2026, summary of branch transactions is: Opening Stock at Invoice Price ₹ 80,000; Goods sent to Branch at Invoice Price ₹ 4,00,000; Credit Sales ₹ 2,50,000; Cash Sales ₹ 1,80,000; Cash collected from Debtors ₹ 2,30,000; Closing Stock at Invoice Price ₹ 1,00,000.
Medium SCENARIO · Invoice Price | Cost Calculation | Pune Branch
What is the cost of goods sent to the branch if goods are invoiced at cost plus 33.1/3%?
A. ₹ 3,00,000 ✔
B. ₹ 2,66,667
C. ₹ 3,20,000
D. ₹ 3,50,000
Explanation: Invoice price = Cost + 33.1/3% of cost (i.e., Cost + 1/3 Cost = 4/3 Cost). Invoice price is ₹ 4,00,000. Therefore, Cost = ₹ 4,00,000 * (3/4) = ₹ 3,00,000.
Easy SCENARIO · Goods Available for Sale | Invoice Price | Branch Stock
What is the total invoice value of goods available for sale at the Pune branch during the year?
A. ₹ 4,00,000
B. ₹ 4,80,000 ✔
C. ₹ 5,00,000
D. ₹ 4,50,000
Explanation: Goods available for sale at invoice price = Opening Stock at Invoice Price (₹ 80,000) + Goods Sent to Branch at Invoice Price (₹ 4,00,000) = ₹ 4,80,000.
Easy SCENARIO · Total Sales | Cash and Credit Sales | Pune Branch
What is the total sales made by the Pune branch during the year?
A. ₹ 2,50,000
B. ₹ 1,80,000
C. ₹ 4,30,000 ✔
D. ₹ 4,10,000
Explanation: Total sales = Cash Sales + Credit Sales = ₹ 1,80,000 + ₹ 2,50,000 = ₹ 4,30,000.
Medium SCENARIO · Stock Reserve | Closing Stock | Unrealized Profit
What is the amount of unrealized profit (stock reserve) to be maintained on the closing stock of ₹ 1,00,000?
A. ₹ 33,333
B. ₹ 25,000 ✔
C. ₹ 20,000
D. ₹ 30,000
Explanation: Loading is cost plus 33.1/3%, which means loading is 25% of the invoice price (1/4th). Stock reserve on closing stock of ₹ 1,00,000 = 25% of ₹ 1,00,000 = ₹ 25,000.
CASE SCENARIO: Apex Software Ltd. (India) established a branch in Tokyo, Japan, on 1st April 2025. The branch operates as a non-integral foreign operation. The trial balance for the year ended 31st March 2026 is denominated in Japanese Yen (JPY): Fixed Assets (Purchased 1st April 2025) = 10,00,000 JPY; Opening Inventory = NIL; Purchases = 40,000,000 JPY; Sales = 60,000,000 JPY; Operating Expenses = 10,000,000 JPY; Current Assets = 15,000,000 JPY; Current Liabilities = 5,000,000 JPY; Head Office Account = 10,000,000 JPY. Exchange rates: Date of purchase of fixed assets = 1 JPY = ₹ 0.55; Average rate for the year = 1 JPY = ₹ 0.58; Closing rate on 31st March 2026 = 1 JPY = ₹ 0.60.
Medium SCENARIO · AS 11 | Non-Integral Operation | Revenue Translation
At what exchange rate should the Sales of the Tokyo branch be translated into Indian Rupees (INR)?
A. ₹ 0.60 per JPY
B. ₹ 0.55 per JPY
C. ₹ 0.58 per JPY ✔
D. Historical rate on the last day
Explanation: For a non-integral foreign operation, revenue and expense items are translated at the average exchange rate prevailing during the reporting period (₹ 0.58 per JPY).
Medium SCENARIO · AS 11 | Fixed Assets | Historical Rate
What is the translated value of the Fixed Assets of 10,000,000 JPY on the balance sheet date?
A. ₹ 6,000,000
B. ₹ 5,80,000
C. ₹ 55,00,000 ✔
D. ₹ 60,00,000
Explanation: Fixed assets of a non-integral foreign operation are translated at the exchange rate on the date of transaction (historical rate), which is 10,000,000 JPY * ₹ 0.55 = ₹ 55,00,000.
Hard SCENARIO · AS 11 | Non-Integral Operation | Closing Rate
How are Current Assets and Current Liabilities translated on the balance sheet date under AS 11 for this non-integral foreign operation?
A. At the average rate of ₹ 0.58
B. At the closing rate of ₹ 0.60 ✔
C. At the historical rate of ₹ 0.55
D. At the opening rate of ₹ 0.55
Explanation: For a non-integral foreign operation, all assets and liabilities (both monetary and non-monetary items) are translated at the closing exchange rate on the balance sheet date (₹ 0.60 per JPY).
Medium SCENARIO · AS 11 | FCTR | Non-Integral Operation
Where should the exchange difference arising from the translation of the non-integral foreign operation's financial statements be accumulated?
A. Credited or debited directly to the Statement of Profit and Loss
B. Accumulated in a Foreign Currency Translation Reserve (FCTR) until disposal ✔
C. Adjusted against General Reserve without routing through equity
D. Credited to Capital Reserve as capital profit
Explanation: Under AS 11, exchange differences arising on translation of a non-integral foreign operation are accumulated in a foreign currency translation reserve until disposal of the net investment.

Paper 2: Corporate and Other Laws · Module 1 · Chapter 1:

Law — 55 rows
Easy NORMAL · Officer in Default | Definitions | Section 2(60)
Which of the following persons is explicitly empowered by Section 2(60) of the Companies Act, 2013 to be designated as an 'Officer who is in default'?
A. Every independent director in respect of all board decisions
B. A whole-time director ✔
C. Any external statutory auditor
D. An independent legal advisor retained by the company
Explanation: Section 2(60) defines an 'officer who is in default' to include whole-time directors, key managerial personnel, and directors who have given their consent to proceedings or failed to take adequate steps. Independent directors are specifically excluded unless the contravention occurs without their knowledge or consent, or despite their due diligence. Therefore, whole-time directors are included.
Easy NORMAL · Private Company | Share Capital | Section 2(68)
Under the Companies Act, 2013, what is the statutory minimum paid-up share capital requirement for a Private Company?
A. One Lakh Rupees
B. Five Lakh Rupees
C. Ten Lakh Rupees
D. There is no minimum paid-up share capital requirement prescribed ✔
Explanation: By virtue of the Companies (Amendment) Act, 2015, the requirement for a minimum paid-up share capital of Rs. 1 lakh for private companies and Rs. 5 lakhs for public companies was removed. Consequently, there is no minimum paid-up capital requirement under the Act now.
Medium NORMAL · Financial Institution | Definitions | Section 2(39)
Which of the following entities is specifically *excluded* from the definition of 'Financial Institution' under Section 2(39) of the Companies Act, 2013?
A. A scheduled bank
B. The Industrial Finance Corporation of India
C. The Life Insurance Corporation of India
D. A non-banking financial company registered under the RBI Act ✔
Explanation: Section 2(39) defines a financial institution to include a industrial finance corporation, a scheduled bank, the Life Insurance Corporation, etc. An NBFC is governed separately under the RBI Act and is not listed as a financial institution under this specific sub-section.
Easy NORMAL · Subsidiary Company | Holding Company | Section 2(87)
In relation to a holding company, a 'subsidiary company' as per Section 2(87) includes a company in which the holding company controls:
A. More than 25% of the total voting power
B. Not less than 35% of the total voting power
C. More than one-half of the total voting power ✔
D. Exactly 50% of the total voting power
Explanation: Section 2(87) defines a subsidiary company as one in which the holding company controls the composition of the Board of Directors or exercises or controls more than one-half of the total voting power either on its own or together with one or more of its subsidiary companies.
Easy NORMAL · Company Definition | Section 2(20) | Previous Company Law
According to Section 2(20), the term 'Company' means a company formed and registered under this Act or under any:
A. Previous Company Law ✔
B. Foreign Company Law
C. Partnership Act, 1932
D. Cooperative Societies Act, 1912
Explanation: Section 2(20) states that 'company' means a company formed and registered under this Act or under any previous company law, encompassing legislations like the Companies Act, 1956 and earlier acts.
Medium NORMAL · Government Company | Section 2(45) | Paid-up Capital
Which of the following is an essential characteristic of a 'Government Company' as defined under Section 2(45) of the Companies Act, 2013?
A. Not less than 25% paid-up capital held by the Central Government
B. Not less than 50% paid-up capital held jointly by Central and State Governments ✔
C. Not less than 51% paid-up capital held by a foreign government
D. Solely owned by statutory corporations created by Parliament
Explanation: Section 2(45) defines a Government Company as any company in which not less than 51% of the paid-up share capital is held by the Central Government, or by any State Government or Governments, or partly by the Central Government and partly by one or more State Governments.
Medium NORMAL · Incorporation | Section 7 | Registration
Which section of the Companies Act, 2013 deals with the incorporation of a company?
A. Section 3
B. Section 7 ✔
C. Section 9
D. Section 10
Explanation: Section 7 of the Companies Act, 2013 outlines the detailed procedure for the incorporation of a company, including filing documents with the Registrar and the issuance of the certificate of incorporation.
Hard NORMAL · One Person Company | Residency | Section 2(62)
A 'One Person Company' (OPC) can be formed by a natural person who is an Indian citizen and:
A. A resident in India only
B. Resident in India or otherwise ✔
