C. A non-resident Indian holding a PIO card
D. A resident in India for not less than 182 days in the previous calendar year
Explanation: As amended by the Companies (Incorporation) Second Amendment Rules, 2021, the residency requirement of being a resident in India for not less than 182 days has been reduced to 120 days, and an OPC can be incorporated by a natural person who is an Indian citizen, whether resident in India or otherwise.
Medium NORMAL · One Person Company | Nominee | Minor
Can a minor be admitted as a member or nominee of a One Person Company (OPC) under the Companies Act, 2013?
A. Yes, through a natural guardian
B. Yes, with prior approval of the National Company Law Tribunal
C. No, a minor cannot become a member or nominee of an OPC ✔
D. Yes, provided the minor's shares are fully paid-up
Explanation: As per the rules governing OPCs, a minor cannot become a member or nominee of the OPC or hold share with beneficial interest. Allowing a minor would contravene the contractual capacity requirements for company membership.
Easy NORMAL · Effect of Registration | Section 9 | Body Corporate
What is the legal effect of registration of a company under Section 9 of the Companies Act, 2013?
A. It creates a partnership among shareholders
B. It incorporates the company into a body corporate with perpetual succession and a common seal (optional) ✔
C. It transfers ownership of all promoter assets to the directors automatically
D. It grants the company tax exemption for the first five financial years
Explanation: Section 9 provides that from the date of incorporation mentioned in the certificate of incorporation, the subscribers shall be a body corporate capable of exercising all functions of an incorporated company with perpetual succession and a common seal (optional now).
Medium NORMAL · Holding Shares | Depository | Section 2(57)
Under Section 2(57), 'to hold' shares in a company includes being a beneficial owner of shares whose name is entered in the records of a:
A. Stock exchange
B. Depository ✔
C. Registrar of Companies
D. National Company Law Tribunal
Explanation: Section 2(57) defines 'to hold' in relation to shares to include a person whose name is entered as a beneficial owner in the records of a depository, acknowledging dematerialized shareholding.
Easy NORMAL · Foreign Company | Section 2(42) | Definitions
Which of the following definitions under Section 2 encompasses a company incorporated outside India that has a place of business in India whether by itself or through an agent?
A. Section 2(20) - Company
B. Section 2(42) - Foreign Company ✔
C. Section 2(46) - Holding Company
D. Section 2(68) - Private Company
Explanation: Section 2(42) defines a 'foreign company' as any company or body corporate incorporated outside India which has a place of business in India whether by itself or through an agent, physically or through electronic mode.
Medium NORMAL · Company Limited by Guarantee | Section 2(22) | Liability
A company limited by guarantee may have a share capital. What is the liability of members in such a company in the event of winding up?
A. Unlimited liability up to personal assets
B. Up to the amount guaranteed and unpaid on shares held, if any ✔
C. Strictly limited to the nominal value of the shares without any guarantee amount
D. Zero liability if the company is solvent
Explanation: Under Section 2(22), a company limited by guarantee means a company having the liability of its members limited by the memorandum to such amount as the members may respectively undertake to contribute to the assets of the company in the event of its being wound up, plus any unpaid amount on shares if it has a share capital.
Medium NORMAL · Associate Company | Significant Influence | Section 2(6)
An 'associate company' in relation to another company, as defined in Section 2(6), means a company in which that other company has:
A. Control of at least 10% of total voting power
B. Significant influence, which means control of at least 20% of total voting power or business control under an agreement ✔
C. Control of exactly 50% of total voting power
D. Subsidiary control of more than 50% voting power
Explanation: Section 2(6) defines an associate company as a company in which that other company has a significant influence, which is defined as control of at least 20% of total voting power, or control of business under an agreement.
Hard NORMAL · Public Company | Section 2(71) | Capital
According to Section 2(71), a 'Public Company' is a company which is not a private company and has a minimum paid-up share capital as:
A. May be prescribed ✔
B. Not less than Rs. 5 Lakhs
C. Not less than Rs. 10 Lakhs
D. Not less than Rs. 1 Crore
Explanation: Section 2(71) defines a public company as a company which is not a private company and has a minimum paid-up share capital, as may be prescribed. Presently, no minimum paid-up share capital is prescribed by rules.
Hard NORMAL · Subsidiary of Public Company | Section 2(71) | Deemed Public Company
Can a private company that is a subsidiary of a public company be treated as a private company for all exemptions under the Companies Act, 2013?
A. Yes, because its articles contain all restrictions under Section 2(68)
B. No, a private company that is a subsidiary of a public company is deemed to be a public company for the purposes of the Act ✔
C. Yes, provided its turnover is below 100 crores
D. No, unless approved by the Central Government
Explanation: As per the proviso to Section 2(71), a private company which is a subsidiary of a public company shall be deemed to be a public company for the purposes of this Act even where such subsidiary company continues to be a private company in its articles.
Easy NORMAL · Definitions | Section 2 | Statutory Interpretation
Which section of the Companies Act, 2013 contains definitions of various terms used throughout the statute?
A. Section 1
B. Section 2 ✔
C. Section 3
D. Section 4
Explanation: Section 2 of the Companies Act, 2013 is the interpretation clause containing definitions of various technical and legal terms used across the Act.
Easy NORMAL · Share Definition | Section 2(84) | Stock
Under Section 2(84), 'share' means a share in the share capital of a company and includes:
A. Debentures
B. Stock ✔
C. Public deposits
D. Bonds
Explanation: Section 2(84) defines 'share' to mean a share in the share capital of a company and includes stock, except where a distinction between stock and share is expressed or implied.
Hard NORMAL · Deposits | Exclusions | Rules
Which of the following is excluded from the definition of 'deposit' under the Companies (Acceptance of Deposits) Rules, 2014?
A. Amount raised by issuance of non-convertible debentures not constituting a charge on assets
B. Any amount received from a relative of a director of the company, accompanied by a declaration that it is not out of borrowed funds ✔
C. Unsecured loans taken from commercial banks
D. Advance received against sale of goods to be delivered within 365 days
Explanation: Under the Deposit Rules, amounts received from a relative of a director (or member in case of private company) accompanied by a written declaration that the money is not given out of borrowed funds are excluded from the definition of 'deposits'. Advances for goods within 365 days are also excluded, but bank loans are borrowings, not relative advances.
Easy NORMAL · Application of Act | Section 1 | Territorial Jurisdiction
What is the extent of territorial jurisdiction of the Companies Act, 2013?
A. Whole of India ✔
B. Whole of India including Jammu & Kashmir and all Union Territories
C. India and foreign subsidiaries of Indian companies
D. Only mainland states of India excluding Special Economic Zones
Explanation: Section 1(2) specifies that the Companies Act, 2013 extends to the whole of India.
Medium NORMAL · Formation of Company | Section 3 | OPC
Which provision governs the incorporation of a One Person Company (OPC), restricting membership to a natural person?
A. Section 3 ✔
B. Section 7
C. Section 8
D. Section 9
Explanation: Section 3 of the Companies Act, 2013 specifies formation of companies, providing that a company may be formed for any lawful purpose by seven or more persons (public), two or more persons (private), or one person (OPC).
Medium NORMAL · Dormant Company | Section 455 | Accounting Transactions
In the context of 'dormant company' under Section 455, a company is classified as dormant if it has not been carrying on any business or operation, or has not made any significant accounting transaction during the last:
A. One financial year
B. Two consecutive financial years ✔
C. Three consecutive financial years
D. Five financial years
Explanation: Section 455 provides that a company which has not been carrying on any business or operation, or has not made any significant accounting transaction during the last two consecutive financial years, or has not filed financial statements and annual returns during the last two consecutive financial years, may apply to the Registrar to obtain dormant status.
Hard NORMAL · Significant Accounting Transaction | Section 455 | Dormant Company
Which of the following activities does *not* constitute a 'significant accounting transaction' for a dormant company under Section 455?
A. Payment of fees by a company to the Registrar
B. Payments of statutory dues to authorities
C. Allotment of shares for cash ✔
D. Office space rent paid to maintain its registered office
Explanation: Section 455 defines 'significant accounting transaction' as any transaction other than: (i) payment of fees by a company to the Registrar; (ii) payments of statutory dues; (iii) allotment of shares to fulfill requirements of the Act; and (iv) office maintenance expenses. Allotment of shares for cash is an active financial operation.
Hard NORMAL · Body Corporate | Section 2(11) | Exclusions
Which of the following bodies corporate is specifically excluded from the definition of a 'Body Corporate' under Section 2(11)?
A. A cooperative society registered under any law relating to cooperative societies ✔
B. A limited liability partnership
C. A foreign company
D. A public financial institution
Explanation: Section 2(11) defines 'body corporate' to include a company incorporated outside India, but specifically excludes (i) a co-operative society registered under any law relating to co-operative societies, and (ii) any other body corporate specified by the Central Government.
Easy NORMAL · Private Company | Maximum Members | Section 2(68)
What does Section 2(68) mandate regarding the maximum number of members in a private company?
A. Maximum 50 members
B. Maximum 100 members
C. Maximum 200 members ✔
D. No limit on maximum members
Explanation: Section 2(68) defines a private company as one having a minimum paid-up share capital as prescribed, and which by its articles restricts the right to transfer its shares and limits the number of its members to 200 (excluding employee-members and past employee-members).
Medium NORMAL · Private Company | Limit of Members | Section 2(68)
In computing the limit of 200 members in a private company, which of the following persons are excluded?
A. Persons who are in the employment of the company
B. Persons who were formerly in the employment of the company and were members while in that employment and have continued to be members after the employment ceased
C. Both (A) and (B) ✔
D. All preference shareholders holding shares for more than 2 years
Explanation: The proviso to Section 2(68) states that where two or more persons hold one or more shares in a company jointly, they shall be treated as a single member, and persons in employment and persons who were formerly in employment and continue as members after cessation of employment are excluded from the limit of 200.
Easy NORMAL · Section 8 Company | Charitable Objects | License
Which section of the Companies Act, 2013 deals with companies with charitable and other objects (License under Section 8)?
A. Section 7
B. Section 8 ✔
C. Section 9
D. Section 12
Explanation: Section 8 of the Companies Act, 2013 deals with formation of companies with charitable objects, promotion of commerce, art, science, sports, education, research, social welfare, religion, charity, protection of environment, etc., intending to apply profits towards promoting its objects and prohibiting dividend payment.
Hard NORMAL · Section 8 Company | Membership | Partnership Firm
Can a partnership firm be a member of a Section 8 Company under the Companies Act, 2013?
A. No, partnership firms cannot be members
B. Yes, a partnership firm can be a member of a Section 8 company ✔
C. Yes, provided the partnership is registered under the Partnership Act
D. Only if approved by the Central Government
Explanation: A partnership firm, being capable of holding property and being a legal person in certain contexts (or association of persons), can be a member of a Section 8 company. Unlike ordinary companies where partnership is sometimes barred, Section 8 allows registered partnerships, associations, and bodies corporate to be members.
Medium NORMAL · Key Managerial Personnel | Section 2(51) | Definitions
Which of the following is an accurate statement concerning 'Key Managerial Personnel' (KMP) under Section 2(51)?
A. Every manager of a company is automatically a KMP
B. Chief Executive Officer is included even if not designated as such
C. Company Secretary is a KMP ✔
D. Internal Auditor is statutorily designated as a KMP
Explanation: Section 2(51) defines KMP to include: (i) Chief Executive Officer or managing director or manager; (ii) Company Secretary; (iii) Whole-time director; (iv) Chief Financial Officer; and (v) such other officer, not more than one level below the directors who is in whole-time employment, as designated by the Board. Internal auditors are not statutory KMPs.
Medium NORMAL · Public Financial Institution | Section 2(72) | Definitions
Under Section 2(72), a 'Public Financial Institution' (PFI) includes which of the following institutions?
A. Any cooperative bank operating in rural districts
B. IDBI Bank Limited ✔
C. Any foreign investment bank with branches in Mumbai
D. Any non-banking financial institution registered with SEBI
Explanation: Section 2(72) lists specific institutions as Public Financial Institutions, which includes IDBI Bank Limited, LIC, UTI, and specified institutions established under Central Acts.
CASE SCENARIO: GreenTech Agro Solutions Limited is a public company incorporated under the Companies Act, 2013, with a registered office in Pune. It holds 55% of the total voting power in BioPower Energy Private Limited. BioPower Energy Private Limited, in turn, holds 30% of the total voting power in EcoSoil Nutrients Private Limited. GreenTech Agro Solutions Limited also holds a direct 25% voting power in EcoSoil Nutrients Private Limited. Furthermore, GreenTech Agro Solutions Limited has an independent nominee agreement giving it significant influence over another firm, AgroInputs India Limited.
Medium SCENARIO · Subsidiary Company | Section 2(87) | Voting Power
What is the status of BioPower Energy Private Limited in relation to GreenTech Agro Solutions Limited?
A. Associate company
B. Subsidiary company ✔
C. Joint venture
D. Holding company
Explanation: Under Section 2(87), since GreenTech Agro Solutions Limited controls more than one-half (55%) of the total voting power of BioPower Energy Private Limited, BioPower Energy Private Limited is a subsidiary of GreenTech Agro Solutions Limited.
Hard SCENARIO · Subsidiary Company | Chain Subsidiary | Section 2(87)
What is the relationship between GreenTech Agro Solutions Limited and EcoSoil Nutrients Private Limited?
A. EcoSoil is a direct subsidiary of GreenTech
B. EcoSoil is a subsidiary of GreenTech due to combined voting power control ✔
C. EcoSoil is completely independent
D. EcoSoil is a holding company of GreenTech
Explanation: GreenTech holds 25% directly, and its subsidiary BioPower holds 30%. Under Section 2(87), control of voting power can be exercised on its own or together with one or more of its subsidiary companies (25% + 30% = 55%). Therefore, EcoSoil is a subsidiary of GreenTech.
Medium SCENARIO · Associate Company | Section 2(6) | Significant Influence
What is the status of AgroInputs India Limited in relation to GreenTech Agro Solutions Limited?
A. Subsidiary company
B. Associate company ✔
C. Wholly owned subsidiary
D. Government company
Explanation: Under Section 2(6), an associate company includes a company in which another company has significant influence, including business control under an agreement. Since GreenTech has an agreement giving it significant influence over AgroInputs, it qualifies as an associate company.
Hard SCENARIO · Deemed Public Company | Section 2(71) | Subsidiary
Will BioPower Energy Private Limited be deemed a public company under the Companies Act, 2013 despite being registered as a private company?
A. Yes, because it is a subsidiary of a public company ✔
B. No, private companies never lose their private status
C. Yes, provided its turnover exceeds Rs. 200 crores
D. No, unless its articles are forcibly altered by NCLT
Explanation: As per the proviso to Section 2(71), a private company that is a subsidiary of a public company is deemed to be a public company for the purposes of the Act, despite retaining its private corporate form in its articles.
CASE SCENARIO: Mr. Raghav, an Indian citizen residing permanently in London for the past 5 years, intends to incorporate a One Person Company (OPC) in Mumbai under the Companies Act, 2013, to engage in software exports. He names his sister, Ms. Ritu (a resident of Delhi and an Indian citizen), as his nominee with her prior written consent. Mr. Raghav proposes to operate the company single-handedly and expects initial paid-up capital of Rs. 40,000.
Medium SCENARIO · One Person Company | NRIs | Residency Rules
Is Mr. Raghav eligible to incorporate an OPC in India despite residing in London?
A. No, because he has not resided in India for 182 days in the previous year
B. Yes, since an Indian citizen, whether resident in India or otherwise, can incorporate an OPC ✔
C. No, non-resident Indian citizens are barred from forming an OPC
D. Yes, provided he obtains prior clearance from the Reserve Bank of India
Explanation: Under the amended rules for One Person Companies, a natural person who is an Indian citizen, whether resident in India or otherwise, is eligible to incorporate an OPC.
Medium SCENARIO · OPC Nominee | Residency | Eligibility
Is Ms. Ritu eligible to be appointed as the nominee for Mr. Raghav's OPC?
A. No, because she is a resident of Delhi and Mr. Raghav resides in London
B. Yes, as she is an Indian citizen and a resident in India, given her written consent ✔
C. No, siblings cannot be nominees for an OPC
D. Yes, provided she contributes 50% of the initial capital
Explanation: Rule 3 of the Companies (Incorporation) Rules stipulates that only a natural person who is an Indian citizen and resident in India shall be a nominee for the sole member of a OPC, upon giving prior written consent.
Easy SCENARIO · OPC Capital | Minimum Paid-up Capital | Incorporation
What is the minimum paid-up share capital requirement for Mr. Raghav's OPC upon incorporation?
A. Rs. 1,00,000
B. Rs. 5,00,000
C. Rs. 40,000 as proposed, since there is no minimum capital requirement under the Act ✔
D. Rs. 10,00,000
Explanation: With the removal of minimum paid-up capital limits for private and public companies under the Companies Act, 2013, an OPC can be incorporated with any nominal capital, including Rs. 40,000.
Medium SCENARIO · One Person Company | Restriction on Membership | Rule 3
Can Mr. Raghav simultaneously be a member or nominee in another OPC incorporated by his friend in Bangalore?
A. Yes, up to a maximum of two OPCs
B. No, a natural person cannot be a member of more than one OPC at any point in time and cannot be a nominee in more than one OPC ✔
C. Yes, if the business objects of both OPCs are entirely different
D. No, unless authorized by the Registrar of Companies
Explanation: Rule 3 explicitly prohibits a natural person from being a member of more than one OPC at any given time and from being a nominee in more than one OPC.
CASE SCENARIO: HealAndCare Foundation is a company incorporated under Section 8 of the Companies Act, 2013 to promote advanced medical research and provide free medication to underprivileged cancer patients. The company earns surplus revenues through nominal fees charged for diagnostic camps. Over two financial years, the company accumulated a substantial surplus. The Board of Directors passed a resolution to distribute a 5% dividend to its members and to issue bonus shares to the founding members out of this surplus.
Medium SCENARIO · Section 8 Company | Prohibition of Dividend | Charitable Objects
Is the Board's decision to distribute a 5% dividend to its members valid under the Companies Act, 2013?
A. Valid, since the surplus was earned from diagnostic operations
B. Valid, provided ordinary resolution is passed in General Meeting
C. Invalid, because Section 8 companies are prohibited from paying dividends to their members ✔
D. Valid, up to a maximum ceiling of 10% dividend
Explanation: Section 8 companies are formed with charitable objects and must apply their profits or other income solely in promoting their objects. They are strictly prohibited from paying any dividend to their members.
Hard SCENARIO · Section 8 Company | Alteration of Memorandum | Approval
Can HealAndCare Foundation alter its memorandum with respect to its objects without Central Government approval?
A. Yes, by passing a special resolution in a general meeting
B. No, any alteration of the memorandum or articles of a Section 8 company requires previous approval of the Central Government (or Regional Director) ✔
C. Yes, provided the ROC is notified within 30 days
D. No alteration is permitted under any circumstances
Explanation: Under Section 8(4)(i), a Section 8 company cannot alter the provisions of its memorandum or articles except with the previous approval of the Central Government (power delegated to Regional Director).
Hard SCENARIO · Section 8 Company | Amalgamation | Merger
Can HealAndCare Foundation amalgamate with another company that is not a Section 8 company?
A. Yes, freely through a scheme of merger
B. No, amalgamation is permitted only with another Section 8 company having similar objects ✔
C. Yes, with NCLT approval
D. No amalgamation is allowed whatsoever
Explanation: Under the rules, a Section 8 company may only amalgamate with another company registered under Section 8 and having similar objects, ensuring the charitable purpose is not compromised.
Medium SCENARIO · Section 8 Company | Revocation of License | Penalties
If HealAndCare Foundation violates any of the conditions specified in Section 8, what action can the Central Government take?
A. Levy a minor fine on the directors and let the company function
B. Revoke the license of the company and direct it to wind up or amalgamate with another Section 8 company ✔
C. Convert the company into a public company automatically without winding up
D. Imprison the founder members for 7 years
Explanation: Under Section 8(6), if the company defaults in complying with requirements or violates conditions, the Central Government may revoke its license, after which the company may be wound up or amalgamated with another Section 8 company.
CASE SCENARIO: Zenith Real Estate Developers Limited was incorporated in 2018. Due to a prolonged market downturn and pending litigations over title deeds of its major land parcels, the company did not carry on any business or operation, nor did it make any significant accounting transaction during the financial years 2023-24 and 2024-25. The management wishes to keep the corporate entity alive without incurring heavy compliance costs and filing regular operational returns, and thus considers applying for dormant status under Section 455.
Medium SCENARIO · Dormant Company | Section 455 | Eligibility
Is Zenith Real Estate Developers Limited eligible to apply for dormant company status under Section 455?
A. No, because it is a public company
B. Yes, since it has not carried on any business or operation and made no significant accounting transactions for the last two consecutive financial years ✔
C. No, because it has pending litigations
D. Yes, provided it obtains a no-objection certificate from all its debtors
Explanation: Section 455 allows a company that has not carried on business or operations or made any significant accounting transactions during the last two consecutive financial years to apply to the Registrar for obtaining dormant status.
Hard SCENARIO · Dormant Company | Special Resolution | Rules
What procedural requirement must Zenith fulfill before making an application to the Registrar for dormant status?
A. Pass an ordinary resolution at a general meeting or issue a notice to all shareholders requiring consent
B. Pass a special resolution in a general meeting or obtain consent of at least 75% shareholders in value ✔
C. Obtain unanimous consent of all directors only
D. Appoint a judicial manager through the NCLT
Explanation: Rule 3 of the Companies (Miscellaneous) Rules, 2014 specifies that a company can apply for dormant status only after passing a special resolution at a general meeting or issuing a notice to all shareholders and getting consent of at least 75% in value.
Medium SCENARIO · Dormant Company | Significant Accounting Transaction | Section 455
During the dormant period, which of the following expenses incurred by Zenith will *not* violate its dormant status?
A. Payment of fees to the Registrar of Companies and office maintenance charges ✔
B. Purchase of new land parcels for future projects
C. Disbursement of commercial loans to sister concerns
D. Issuance of new equity shares for cash consideration to expand operations
Explanation: Under Section 455, payment of statutory fees to the Registrar and payments for maintenance of its office and records do not constitute 'significant accounting transactions' and are permitted for dormant companies.
Hard SCENARIO · Dormant Company | Maximum Period | Rule 7
What is the maximum continuous period for which a company can remain under a dormant status as per the rules?
A. Three consecutive financial years
B. Five consecutive financial years ✔
C. Ten consecutive financial years
D. Indefinitely until revived by the Registrar
Explanation: Under Rule 7 of the Companies (Miscellaneous) Rules, 2014, the maximum period for which a company can remain as a dormant company is restricted to 5 consecutive financial years.
CASE SCENARIO: Apex Infrastructure Projects Limited has a complex corporate structure. During a statutory audit, an investigation was initiated regarding non-compliance with corporate filings. The Board of Directors consisted of a Managing Director, three Whole-Time Directors, two Independent Directors, and a Company Secretary. The Chief Financial Officer also participated in board meetings. Due to a failure to file annual financial statements, a penalty notice was issued by the Registrar under the Companies Act, 2013.
Medium SCENARIO · Officer in Default | Section 2(60) | KMP
Who among the following would be classified as an 'Officer who is in default' under Section 2(60) for the default in filing annual returns?
A. The independent directors in all circumstances
B. The Managing Director, Whole-Time Directors, Company Secretary, and Chief Financial Officer ✔
C. Only the external statutory auditor
D. The external legal consultant who drafted the notices
Explanation: Section 2(60) designates key managerial personnel such as Managing Directors, Whole-Time Directors, Company Secretaries, and Chief Financial Officers as officers who are in default when contraventions occur.
Hard SCENARIO · Independent Director | Officer in Default | Section 2(60)
Will the Independent Directors be held liable as 'officers in default' for the above default?
A. Yes, all directors are jointly and severally liable without exception
B. No, unless the contravention had occurred with their knowledge, attributable through board processes, or where they had not acted diligently ✔
C. Yes, because they attended the board meetings
D. No, independent directors are completely immune to any legal penalties under company law
Explanation: Section 2(60) explicitly shields independent directors from being designated as officers in default unless the default occurs with their knowledge (attributable through board minutes) or without their exercising adequate due diligence.
Easy SCENARIO · Key Managerial Personnel | Company Secretary | Section 2(51)
What category of personnel does the Company Secretary belong to under Section 2(51)?
A. Key Managerial Personnel ✔
B. Promoter group
C. Independent professional
D. Nominee director
Explanation: Section 2(51) explicitly lists a Company Secretary as a Key Managerial Personnel (KMP) of the company.
Easy SCENARIO · Limited Liability | Company Limited by Shares | Fundamental Principles
Apex Infrastructure Projects Limited is held to be a company limited by shares. What does this fundamentally imply regarding member liability?
A. Members are liable with their personal residential properties for all corporate debts
B. Liability of members is limited to the amount unpaid on the shares respectively held by them ✔
C. Members have zero liability even if shares are partly paid-up
D. Members must contribute proportionally to corporate losses upon demand by trade creditors
Explanation: By definition under Section 2(22) or general corporate principles of a company limited by shares, the liability of its members is limited to the amount, if any, unpaid on the shares held by them.

Paper 2: Corporate and Other Laws · Module 1 · Chapter 2:

Law — 55 rows
Easy NORMAL · Formation of Company | Public Company | Section 3
Under Section 3 of the Companies Act, 2013, what is the minimum number of persons required to form a public company?
A. Two persons
B. Seven persons ✔
C. Three persons
D. Ten persons
Explanation: Section 3 of the Companies Act, 2013 stipulates that a public company may be formed for any lawful purpose by seven or more persons. For a private company, the requirement is two or more persons, and for an OPC, only one person is needed.
Easy NORMAL · Memorandum of Association | Company Charter | Section 4
Which of the following documents contains the fundamental conditions upon which a company is allowed to be built under the Companies Act, 2013?
A. Articles of Association
B. Memorandum of Association ✔
C. Prospectus
D. Certificate of Incorporation
Explanation: The Memorandum of Association (MoA) is the charter of the company and defines its scope of operations, objects, and the limits outside which a company cannot act. It forms the foundation upon which the company is built.
Medium NORMAL · One Person Company | Nominee | Rule 3
A One Person Company (OPC) must nominate a nominee in its memorandum. When is the prior written consent of such nominee required to be filed with the Registrar?
A. At the time of incorporation ✔
B. Within 30 days of incorporation
C. At the time of filing annual return
D. Within 60 days of incorporation
Explanation: Rule 3 of the Companies (Incorporation) Rules, 2014 mandates that the memorandum of an OPC shall indicate the name of the nominee who shall, in the event of the subscriber's death or incapacity, become the member. The prior written consent of this nominee must be filed with the Registrar at the time of incorporation.
Easy NORMAL · Registered Office | Section 12 | Incorporation Matters
What is the maximum permissible period within which a newly incorporated company must maintain its registered office from the date of incorporation under Section 12?
A. 15 days
B. 30 days ✔
C. 45 days
D. 60 days
Explanation: Section 12(1) of the Companies Act, 2013 requires a company to have a registered office capable of receiving and acknowledging all communications and notices within 30 days of its incorporation.
Hard NORMAL · Incorporation Documents | Section 7 | Statutory Registers
Under Section 7(4) of the Companies Act, 2013, for how many years must a company preserve all books and papers relating to its incorporation at its registered office?
A. 3 years
B. 5 years
C. 8 years
D. From the date of incorporation till its dissolution ✔
Explanation: Section 7(4) of the Companies Act, 2013 mandates that the company shall maintain and keep at its registered office copies of all documents and information originally filed with the Registrar until its dissolution.
Medium NORMAL · Change of Name | Section 13 | Central Government Approval
Which of the following entities is empowered to accord approval for a change of name of a company that involves the substitution of words indicating a change in economic activity?
A. National Company Law Tribunal
B. Central Government (Registrar of Companies) ✔
C. Securities and Exchange Board of India
D. Regional Director
Explanation: Under Section 13 read with the relevant rules, a change of name of a company requires a special resolution and approval of the Central Government (delegated to the Registrar of Companies).
Medium NORMAL · Reservation of Name | Rule 9 | SPICe+
If a company makes an application for reservation of name using the RUN (Reserve Unique Name) or SPICe+ web service, for how many days is the approved name reserved for a *new* company?
A. 10 days
B. 20 days ✔
C. 30 days
D. 60 days
Explanation: As per Rule 9 of the Companies (Incorporation) Rules, 2014, the Registrar shall reserve a name for a new company for a period of 20 days from the date of approval (or such extended period as may be permitted upon payment of additional fees).
Hard NORMAL · Fraudulent Incorporation | Section 7(7) | NCLT Powers
What is the consequence if a company is found to have been incorporated by furnishing false or incorrect information or by suppressing any material fact under Section 7(7)?
A. Only a compounding fine on the promoters
B. The Tribunal may direct winding up, or direct that liability shall be unlimited ✔
C. Automatic conversion into a partnership firm
D. Mandatory imprisonment of all independent directors
Explanation: Section 7(7) empowers the Tribunal (NCLT), on an application made to it, to pass orders such as directing the regulation of the management, winding up of the company, or declaring that the liability of the members shall be unlimited, when incorporation has been obtained by fraud or false information.
Hard NORMAL · Section 8 Company | Alteration of Memorandum | Central Government Approval
Can a charitable company registered under Section 8 alter the objects clause in its Memorandum of Association?
A. Yes, by ordinary resolution and Central Government approval
B. Yes, by special resolution and prior approval of the Central Government ✔
C. No, Section 8 companies can never alter their objects
D. Yes, simply by filing an e-form with the ROC without any special resolution
Explanation: Under Section 8(4)(i), a Section 8 company cannot alter the provisions of its memorandum or articles except with the previous approval of the Central Government, and such alteration must also comply with provisions regarding special resolutions.
Hard NORMAL · Pre-incorporation Contracts | Ratification | Contract Act
Which of the following is NOT a permissible form of pre-incorporation contract liability ratification by a company under Indian company law?
A. Express novation of contract
B. Adoption of the contract by the company after incorporation
C. Automatic statutory ratification upon obtaining the Certificate of Incorporation ✔
D. Entering into a new contract on the same terms after incorporation
Explanation: Pre-incorporation contracts cannot be ratified automatically upon incorporation because a company does not exist prior to its incorporation. Valid legal options include novation, fresh contract, or specific adoption as per Indian Contract Act principles.
Easy NORMAL · SPICe+ | MCA Services | Electronic Incorporation
What is the designated web-based service introduced by the Ministry of Corporate Affairs (MCA) for simplified proforma for incorporating a company electronically?
A. SPICe+ ✔
B. RUN-MCA
C. DIR-3 KYC
D. MGT-7A
Explanation: SPICe+ (Simplified Proforma for Incorporating Company Electronically Plus) is an integrated web form offering multiple services like name reservation, incorporation, DIN allotment, PAN/TAN application, etc.
Medium NORMAL · One Person Company | Rule 3 | Eligibility Compliance
In the case of a One Person Company, if the sole member becomes a member in another OPC due to being a nominee in that other OPC, within how many days must the limit be complied with?
A. 30 days
B. 90 days
C. 180 days ✔
D. 365 days
Explanation: Rule 3(7) of the Companies (Incorporation) Rules specifies that where a person is a member in one OPC and becomes a nominee in another such company, such person shall meet the eligibility criteria within a period of 180 days.
Medium NORMAL · Memorandum of Association | Mandatory Clauses | Section 4
Which of the following particulars is NOT required to be stated in the Memorandum of Association of a limited company?
A. Name clause
B. Registered office state clause
C. First directors appointment clause ✔
D. Liability clause
Explanation: Section 4 lists the mandatory clauses of the Memorandum: Name, State, Objects, Liability, and Capital. The appointment of first directors is typically dealt with in the Articles or separate board resolutions/regulatory filings, not as a mandatory clause of the MoA.
Medium NORMAL · Section 10 | Binding Effect | MoA and AoA
Under Section 10 of the Companies Act, 2013, what is the legal effect of the registered Memorandum and Articles of Association once they are bound?
A. They bind the company and its members as if signed by each member ✔
B. They are merely recommendatory guidelines
C. They are binding only on the promoters
D. They have no legal standing until a court order is passed
Explanation: Section 10 states that when the memorandum and articles are registered, they bind the company and the members thereof to the same extent as if they respectively had been signed by each member and contained covenants on the part of each member to observe all provisions.
Medium NORMAL · Private Company | Deposits | Incorporation Rules
Which type of company is prohibited from accepting any deposits from the public under the provisions of the Companies Act, 2013?
A. Public company with a net worth of over 500 crores
B. Private company ✔
C. Banking company
D. Non-banking financial company registered with RBI
Explanation: While public companies can accept deposits under strict regulations, private companies are generally restricted from accepting deposits from the general public (though they can accept from members/directors as per exemptions). However, looking strictly at the chapter on incorporation and basic rules, private companies cannot invite deposits from the public.
Easy NORMAL · Registered Office | Section 12 | Change of Address
What is the maximum time limit specified for a company to notify the Registrar of any change in its registered office address from the date of such change?
A. 15 days
B. 30 days ✔
C. 60 days
D. 90 days
Explanation: Section 12(4) of the Companies Act, 2013 provides that notice of every change of the situation of the registered office, verified in the prescribed manner, shall be given to the Registrar within 30 days of the change.
Easy NORMAL · Articles of Association | Alteration | Section 14
If an existing company wants to alter its Articles of Association, which resolution must be passed by the shareholders?
A. Ordinary Resolution
B. Special Resolution ✔
C. Board Resolution only
D. Unanimous Resolution
Explanation: Section 14 of the Companies Act, 2013 mandates that subject to the provisions of this Act and the conditions contained in its memorandum, a company may alter its articles by passing a special resolution.
Hard NORMAL · Conversion of Company | Public to Private | Section 13/18
Which of the following authorities has the power to accord sanction for the conversion of a public company into a private company?
A. Registrar of Companies
B. National Company Law Tribunal (Central Government) ✔
C. Securities and Exchange Board of India
D. High Court
Explanation: Conversion of a public company into a private company requires approval from the Central Government (powers delegated to the Regional Director / Tribunal as per statutory amendments).
Medium NORMAL · Subscriber to Memorandum | Minor | Capacity to Contract
Can a minor be a subscriber to the Memorandum of Association of a company under the Companies Act, 2013?
A. Yes, through a natural guardian
B. No, a minor's agreement is void ab initio, hence a minor cannot be a subscriber ✔
C. Yes, provided the share capital is fully paid up
D. Yes, if approved by the Board of Directors
Explanation: Since a minor lacks the capacity to contract under the Indian Contract Act, 1872, a minor cannot be a subscriber to the memorandum of association. Shares cannot be allotted to a minor except if they are fully paid and acquired by way of transfer/transmission.
Medium NORMAL · Doctrine of Indoor Management | Turquand Rule | Articles of Association
What is the status of the doctrine of indoor management in relation to the Memorandum and Articles of Association?
A. It protects the company from outsiders
B. It protects outsiders dealing with the company from internal irregularities ✔
C. It allows directors to bypass the Articles
D. It overrides statutory provisions of the Companies Act
Explanation: The doctrine of indoor management (Turquand's Rule) protects outsiders who deal with a company in good faith from being affected by internal irregularities or procedural non-compliance within the company.
Hard NORMAL · Reduction of Members | Section 3A | Liability of Members
Under Section 3A of the Companies Act, 2013, if the number of members of a public company falls below seven and it continues to carry on business for more than how many months, every such member shall be severally liable?
A. 3 months
B. 6 months ✔
C. 9 months
D. 12 months
Explanation: Section 3A provides that if the number of members is reduced below the statutory minimum (7 for public, 2 for private) and business is carried on for more than 6 months, every person who is a member during that time with knowledge shall be severally liable for the payment of debts contracted during that time.
Hard NORMAL · Company Name | Rule 8 | Central Government Approval
Which of the following cannot be included in the name of a company unless previous approval of the Central Government is obtained?
A. Industrial
B. Cooperative
C. Federal ✔
D. Limited
Explanation: Rule 8 of the Companies (Incorporation) Rules specifies words which require prior approval of the Central Government, such as 'Federal', 'Republic', 'State', 'Bank', 'Union', etc., as they might imply government patronage.
Easy NORMAL · Doctrine of Ultra Vires | Memorandum of Association | Company Powers
What does the 'Doctrine of Ultra Vires' signify in company law?
A. Acts done by directors beyond their authority but within company powers
B. Acts done beyond the powers of the company as defined in its Memorandum ✔
C. Acts done by members without board approval
D. Internal management procedures
Explanation: An act is ultra vires the company if it is beyond the powers conferred upon the company by its Memorandum of Association. Such acts are void and cannot be ratified even by all members.
Easy NORMAL · SPICe+ | Incorporation Form | MCA Portal
Which form is used for filing the application for incorporation of a company electronically under the SPICe+ framework?
A. INC-32
B. SPICe+ (INC-32) ✔
C. INC-7
D. INC-22
Explanation: SPICe+ has replaced the old INC-32 form as the integrated web form for company incorporation under the Companies Act, 2013.
Medium NORMAL · Section 8 Company | Share Capital | Incorporation
In the case of a Section 8 company, what is the minimum capital requirement prescribed under the Act?
A. 1 Lakh rupees
B. 5 Lakhs rupees
C. 10 Lakhs rupees
D. No minimum capital requirement ✔
Explanation: Section 8 companies do not have any prescribed minimum paid-up share capital requirement under the Companies Act, 2013, unlike private or public companies which historically had minimum capital thresholds.
Hard NORMAL · Foreign Company | Section 380 | Place of Business
Can a foreign company establish a place of business in India without registering with the Registrar of Companies?
A. Yes, if it operates for less than 90 days
B. No, it must deliver required documents to the ROC within 30 days of establishment ✔
C. Yes, if it has a local agent
D. No, but it has 180 days to register
Explanation: Section 380 of the Companies Act, 2013 requires every foreign company to deliver specified documents and particulars to the Registrar of Companies within 30 days of establishing a place of business in India.
Easy NORMAL · Section 9 | Incorporation Effect | Corporate Personality
What is the effect of registration of a company under Section 9 of the Companies Act, 2013?
A. It creates a partnership between subscribers
B. It creates a body corporate with perpetual succession and a common seal (optional) ✔
C. It makes directors personally liable for all future debts
D. It requires annual renewal of incorporation
Explanation: Section 9 provides that from the date of incorporation, the subscribers to the memorandum and other persons shall be a body corporate capable of exercising all functions, having perpetual succession and a common seal.
Medium NORMAL · Section 10A | Commencement of Business | Subscription Money
When can a company commence its business or exercise borrowing powers after incorporation?
A. Immediately upon getting the Certificate of Incorporation
B. Only after filing a declaration under Section 10A regarding receipt of subscription money ✔
C. After holding its first Annual General Meeting
D. After obtaining a separate trading license from the High Court
Explanation: Section 10A of the Companies Act, 2013 stipulates that a company having a share capital cannot commence any business or exercise borrowing powers unless a director files a verification declaration within 180 days that every subscriber has paid the value of shares agreed.
Medium NORMAL · Promoters | Fiduciary Duty | Secret Profits
If a promoter makes a secret profit from a transaction entered into on behalf of a prospective company, what is the legal remedy available to the company?
A. The company can only reprimand the promoter
B. The company can rescind the contract and recover the secret profit ✔
C. The company must pay an additional bonus to the promoter
D. The contract becomes automatically binding with no remedies
Explanation: Promoters stand in a fiduciary position towards the company they promote. They cannot make any secret profits, and if they do, the company can compel them to account for such profits or rescind the contract.
Easy NORMAL · SPICe+ | Incorporation Documents | Required Filings
Which of the following documents is NOT required to be filed along with SPICe+ for the incorporation of a company?
A. Subscriber sheet / Memorandum and Articles
B. Proof of registered office address
C. Audited balance sheet of promoters for the last 3 years ✔
D. Declaration by professionals and subscribers in INC-9
Explanation: Promoters' historical audited balance sheets are not required for company incorporation. The required documents include MoA, AoA, registered office proof, declarations (INC-9), and identity proofs of subscribers/directors.
CASE SCENARIO: Mr. Rohan, an enthusiastic entrepreneur, decides to start a software development business in Pune. He plans to register a private limited company named 'TechInnovate Solutions Private Limited' with five initial subscribers. He prepares the Memorandum of Association and Articles of Association. During the incorporation process, Rohan acts quickly to secure a commercial property as the registered office, but due to delays in final paperwork, the registered office address is registered 45 days after the date of incorporation.
Medium SCENARIO · Registered Office | Section 12 | Time Limit
Is the registration of the registered office address within 45 days compliant with Section 12 of the Companies Act, 2013?
A. Yes, because private companies get a grace period of 60 days
B. No, Section 12 requires the company to have a registered office within 30 days of incorporation ✔
C. Yes, if approved by the Regional Director
D. No, but it attracts only a minor fee without legal consequences
Explanation: Section 12(1) of the Companies Act, 2013 mandates that a company must have a registered office capable of receiving communications within 30 days of its incorporation. Registering it after 45 days is a non-compliance.
Medium SCENARIO · Private Company | Subscribers | Section 3
With five subscribers, does 'TechInnovate Solutions Private Limited' satisfy the minimum subscriber requirement for a private company?
A. No, a private company requires at least seven subscribers
B. Yes, a private company requires a minimum of two subscribers, and five is compliant ✔
C. No, it must have exactly ten subscribers
D. Yes, but only if all subscribers are corporate bodies
Explanation: Under Section 3 of the Companies Act, 2013, a private company requires a minimum of two persons to form it. Having five subscribers fully satisfies this legal requirement.
Medium SCENARIO · Section 10 | Binding Nature | MoA and AoA
What is the legal nature of the Memorandum and Articles prepared by Rohan once the company is successfully incorporated?
A. They are bilateral agreements between Rohan and the Registrar
B. They constitute a contract between the company and its members as per Section 10 ✔
C. They are internal guidelines that do not bind the members
D. They have no legal force until approved by NCLT
Explanation: Under Section 10, once registered, the MoA and AoA bind the company and its members to the same extent as if they had been signed by each member, establishing a statutory contract.
Medium SCENARIO · One Person Company | Nominee | Rule 3
If Rohan had instead decided to form a One Person Company (OPC) for the same business, what would have been the mandatory requirement regarding a nominee?
A. No nominee is required for software businesses
B. A nominee must be appointed whose prior written consent is filed with the Registrar at incorporation ✔
C. A nominee must be a public financial institution
D. The nominee must hold 51% of the shares
Explanation: For an OPC, Rule 3 requires the memorandum to indicate the name of a nominee who shall become the member in case of death or incapacity, and their prior written consent must be filed at incorporation.
CASE SCENARIO: A group of six philanthropic individuals intend to incorporate a company under Section 8 of the Companies Act, 2013, named 'GreenEarth Foundation', with the object of promoting environmental awareness and wildlife conservation. They intend to apply all their profits towards promoting their objects and prohibit the payment of any dividend to their members. They submit their application for a license to the Central Government / Registrar.
Medium SCENARIO · Section 8 Company | Charitable Objects | Formation
Is 'GreenEarth Foundation' eligible for a Section 8 license with six initial subscribers?
A. No, Section 8 requires a minimum of 50 subscribers
B. Yes, Section 8 companies can be formed by individuals or associations for charitable objects without any special high subscriber minimums beyond standard private/public rules ✔
C. No, charitable companies must be registered as public companies with at least 7 subscribers
D. Yes, but they must have a minimum capital of 50 lakhs
Explanation: Section 8 allows persons or associations of persons to form a company for charitable objects with restricted profit distribution. They can be registered as private or public companies complying with basic member requirements.
Hard SCENARIO · Section 8 Company | Alteration of Memorandum | Central Government Approval
Can 'GreenEarth Foundation' alter the objects clause in its Memorandum of Association after incorporation?
A. No, Section 8 company objects can never be altered
B. Yes, but only with the previous approval of the Central Government and via special resolution ✔
C. Yes, by passing a simple board resolution
D. Yes, by notifying the local municipal authority
Explanation: Section 8(4) stipulates that a Section 8 company cannot alter the provisions of its memorandum or articles except with the previous approval of the Central Government.
Medium SCENARIO · Section 8 Company | Prohibition of Dividend | Charitable Purpose
What happens to the restriction on payment of dividends for members of 'GreenEarth Foundation'?
A. Dividends can be paid up to 10% per annum
B. Dividends are strictly prohibited, and profits must be applied solely to the promotion of its objects ✔
C. Dividends can be distributed if approved by ordinary resolution
D. Dividends are permitted only after 5 years of operation
Explanation: A Section 8 company is prohibited from paying any dividend to its members; its profits and income must be applied solely for the promotion of the objects for which it is established.
Hard SCENARIO · Section 8 Company | Revocation of License | Winding Up / Amalgamation
If at any time the Central Government revokes the Section 8 license of 'GreenEarth Foundation' due to violation of conditions, what action can the Government take?
A. Only impose a monetary penalty on the founders
B. Direct the company to wind up or amalgamate with another Section 8 company having similar objects ✔
C. Automatically convert the company into an unlimited partnership
D. Dissolve the company and forfeit all its assets to the promoters
Explanation: Under Section 8(6), upon revocation of the license, the Central Government may order the company to be wound up, or amalgamated with another Section 8 company, after giving an opportunity of being heard.
CASE SCENARIO: Apex Infrastructure Limited is an existing public company incorporated under the Companies Act, 2013. The Board of Directors wishes to alter the Articles of Association to include restrictive clauses on share transfers and wants to convert the company into Apex Infrastructure Private Limited. The company has 80 members on its register. The management calls an extraordinary general meeting to pass the necessary resolutions.
Medium SCENARIO · Articles of Association | Alteration | Section 14
What type of resolution is required for altering the Articles of Association under Section 14 of the Companies Act, 2013?
A. Ordinary Resolution
B. Special Resolution ✔
C. Unanimous Board Resolution
D. Resolution requiring 100% consent
Explanation: Section 14 of the Companies Act, 2013 explicitly states that a company may alter its articles by passing a special resolution.
Hard SCENARIO · Conversion of Company | Public to Private | Central Government Approval
To convert Apex Infrastructure Limited into a private company, whose approval is mandatory under the Companies Act, 2013?
A. Securities and Exchange Board of India (SEBI)
B. Central Government (Regional Director / Tribunal) ✔
C. Reserve Bank of India
D. Registrar of Companies only via e-form without sanction
Explanation: Conversion of a public company into a private company requires the sanction/approval of the Central Government (powers delegated to Regional Director/Tribunal) in accordance with Section 13 and 18 read with rules.
Medium SCENARIO · Private Company Definition | Maximum Members | Section 2(68)
Does the number of members (80 members) comply with the maximum limit prescribed for a private company under the Companies Act, 2013?
A. No, the maximum limit for a private company is 50 members
B. Yes, the maximum limit for a private company is 200 members ✔
C. No, private companies cannot have more than 20 members
D. Yes, because public companies converting to private have no member limits
Explanation: Section 2(68) defines a private company as one which has a minimum of 2 members and restricts the maximum number of its members to 200 (excluding employee-members and past employee-members). 80 members is well within this limit.
Hard SCENARIO · Conversion Sanction | Shareholder Interests | Tribunal Powers
If a dissenting minority shareholder challenges the conversion in court, what is the primary consideration the Tribunal evaluates?
A. Whether the conversion prejudices the interests of shareholders or creditors ✔
B. Whether the company has paid dividends for the last 10 years
C. Whether the company's registered office is in a metropolitan city
D. Whether the promoters are Indian citizens
Explanation: When evaluating conversion of a public company to a private company, the Tribunal/Central Government ensures that adequate provision is made for safeguarding the interests of creditors and dissenting shareholders.
CASE SCENARIO: Mr. Vikram starts a trading business and promotes 'Vikram Agro-Products Private Limited'. During the promoter stage, before obtaining the Certificate of Incorporation, Vikram enters into a lease agreement on behalf of the prospective company with a landlord for a warehouse. After the company is incorporated, the board of directors continues to use the warehouse and pays rent, but never formally executes a new contract or novates the old agreement.
Medium SCENARIO · Pre-incorporation Contracts | Promoter Liability | Adoption
What is the legal status of the lease agreement entered into by Vikram prior to incorporation?
A. It is automatically binding on the company from day one
B. It is a pre-incorporation contract which is not automatically binding on the company unless adopted/novated ✔
C. It is completely illegal and void under criminal law
D. It binds the landlord personally with no recourse
Explanation: Pre-incorporation contracts entered into by promoters on behalf of a yet-to-be-formed company are not automatically binding on the company upon incorporation unless the company adopts the contract or enters into a fresh novation.
Medium SCENARIO · Pre-incorporation Contracts | Novation | Adoption
Can the company adopt or ratify the pre-incorporation contract expressly after its incorporation?
A. Yes, by adopting it or entering into a new contract on the same terms (novation) ✔
B. No, a company can never adopt a pre-incorporation contract under any circumstance
C. Yes, automatically after 6 months of use
D. Only if approved by the National Company Law Tribunal
Explanation: While ratification in the strict agency sense is not possible because the principal (company) did not exist when the contract was made, the company can become bound by entering into a new contract (novation) or specific adoption.
Medium SCENARIO · Promoters | Fiduciary Duties | Incorporation Stage
What position do Vikram and the other promoters hold in relation to the prospective company during the promotion phase?
A. They are mere employees with no fiduciary duties
B. They stand in a fiduciary relationship towards the company ✔
C. They are statutory directors automatically
D. They act as legal guardians of the company
Explanation: Promoters stand in a fiduciary (position of trust) relationship with the company they promote, meaning they must not make secret profits and must act in good faith.
Medium SCENARIO · Secret Profits | Promoter Liability | Fiduciary Duty
If Vikram had made a secret profit from the lease transaction without disclosing it to the subscribers, what remedy is available to the company?
A. The company can recover the secret profit or rescind the transaction ✔
B. The company must reward Vikram with additional shares
C. The contract becomes voidable only at the option of the landlord
D. No remedy, as promoters are immune from profits
Explanation: If a promoter makes a secret profit in a transaction on behalf of the company, the company can compel the promoter to disgorge the secret profit or rescind the transaction for breach of fiduciary duty.
CASE SCENARIO: Zenith Global Limited is incorporated with an authorized share capital of 50 lakhs divided into equity shares. The Certificate of Incorporation is issued by the Registrar of Companies on 1st October. The directors are eager to commence business operations and issue a large supply order on 10th October without filing the statutory declaration required under Section 10A of the Companies Act, 2013.
Medium SCENARIO · Section 10A | Commencement of Business | Subscription Money
Is Zenith Global Limited legally permitted to commence business operations or exercise borrowing powers on 10th October?
A. Yes, because incorporation gives immediate commencement rights
B. No, a company having share capital cannot commence business without filing the Section 10A declaration regarding subscription money ✔
C. Yes, if the board passes an ordinary resolution
D. No, unless approved by SEBI
Explanation: Section 10A explicitly prohibits a company having a share capital from commencing business or exercising borrowing powers unless a director files a declaration verifying that every subscriber has paid the value of shares.
Medium SCENARIO · Section 10A | Time Limit | Declaration filing
Within what maximum time frame from the date of incorporation must the Section 10A declaration be filed by a director?
A. 30 days
B. 60 days
C. 180 days ✔
D. 365 days
Explanation: Section 10A(1)(a) requires that the declaration by a director must be filed with the Registrar within a period of 180 days of the date of incorporation of the company.
Hard SCENARIO · Section 10A Penalties | Default Consequences | Officer Liability
What are the penal consequences for the company and defaulting officers if business is commenced in violation of Section 10A?
A. Only a warning letter from the ROC
B. Penalty of fifty thousand rupees for the company and one thousand rupees per day for defaulting officers, plus potential removal of name ✔
C. Immediate imprisonment of all shareholders for 7 years
D. Mandatory dissolution by High Court order only
Explanation: Section 10A prescribes a penalty of fifty thousand rupees for the company and one thousand rupees for each day during which the default continues for every officer in default, along with Registrar action for striking off if no business is commenced.
Medium SCENARIO · Section 9 | Certificate of Incorporation | Corporate Personality
From which date does Zenith Global Limited acquire its corporate personality and perpetual succession?
A. From the date of filing the SPICe+ form
B. From the date mentioned in the Certificate of Incorporation ✔
C. From the date of the first board meeting
D. From the date Section 10A declaration is filed
Explanation: Under Section 9, from the date of incorporation mentioned in the Certificate of Incorporation issued by the Registrar, the subscribers become a body corporate with perpetual succession.

Paper 2: Corporate and Other Laws · Module 1 · Chapter 3:

Law — 55 rows
Easy NORMAL · Prospectus | Definitions | Section 2(70)
Which of the following documents is specifically defined under Section 2(70) of the Companies Act, 2013 as including any notice, circular, advertisement, or other document inviting offers from the public for the subscription or purchase of any securities of a body corporate?
A. Abridged Prospectus
B. Prospectus ✔
C. Shelf Prospectus
D. Red Herring Prospectus
Explanation: Section 2(70) of the Companies Act, 2013 defines a prospectus as any document described or issued as a prospectus including a red herring prospectus or shelf prospectus or any notice, circular, advertisement or other document inviting offers from the public for the subscription or purchase of any securities of a body corporate.
Easy NORMAL · Abridged Prospectus | Section 33 | Application Form
When a company issues an Abridged Prospectus along with a form of application for purchase of any of its securities, what is the legal position regarding the inclusion of the abridged prospectus?
A. It is optional for private companies but mandatory for public companies.
B. Every application form for securities must be accompanied by an abridged prospectus. ✔
C. It is required only if the applicant specifically requests it in writing.
D. It is required only for rights issues and bonus issues.
Explanation: According to Section 33(1) of the Companies Act, 2013, no form of application for the purchase of any of the securities of a company shall be issued unless such form is accompanied by an abridged prospectus containing all necessary disclosures.
Easy NORMAL · Shelf Prospectus | Section 31 | Validity Period
What is the maximum period for which a Shelf Prospectus can be stated to be valid by a company issuing a class or classes of securities under Section 31 of the Companies Act, 2013?
A. Six months
B. One year ✔
C. Two years
D. Three years
Explanation: Under Section 31 of the Companies Act, 2013, a shelf prospectus issued by any class or classes of companies shall be valid for a period not exceeding one year from the date of opening of the first issue of securities under that prospectus.
Medium NORMAL · Red Herring Prospectus | Section 32 | Book Building
A company issues a Red Herring Prospectus (RHP) prior to the issue of securities. Which of the following details is typically *not* included in an RHP?
A. Quantum of securities
B. Price of the securities ✔
C. General nature of business
D. Financial background of promoters
Explanation: Section 32 defines a red herring prospectus as one which lacks complete particulars about the quantum or price of the securities being offered, as these are determined after the book-building process concludes.
Medium NORMAL · Red Herring Prospectus | Filing | RoC
When does a Red Herring Prospectus need to be filed with the Registrar of Companies (RoC)?
A. At least 3 days prior to the opening of the issue ✔
B. At least 7 days prior to the opening of the issue
C. At least 15 days prior to the opening of the issue
D. At least 30 days prior to the opening of the issue
Explanation: Under Section 32(1) of the Companies Act, 2013, a company proposing to make an offer of securities may issue a red herring prospectus prior to the issue of securities and must file it with the Registrar at least 3 days prior to the opening of the subscription list and the issue.
Medium NORMAL · Red Herring Prospectus | Filing | Section 32
What must a company do upon the closing of the offer under a Red Herring Prospectus regarding the final details of the issue?
A. File a fresh prospectus with SEBI only
B. State the final price and quantum of securities and file it with the Registrar and SEBI ✔
C. Obtain a court order confirming the price
D. Issue a notice in a local newspaper without filing with RoC
Explanation: Section 32(4) specifies that upon the closing of the offer, the red herring prospectus shall be filed with the Registrar and SEBI, stating the total capital raised, closing price of securities, and other details not included earlier.
Easy NORMAL · Misstatement | Criminal Liability | Section 34
Which section of the Companies Act, 2013 deals with criminal liability for misstatements in a prospectus?
A. Section 34 ✔
B. Section 35
C. Section 38
D. Section 40
Explanation: Section 34 of the Companies Act, 2013 imposes criminal liability on any person who authorizes the issue of a prospectus containing untrue or misleading statements, attracting punishment under Section 447.
Medium NORMAL · Civil Liability | Section 35 | Directors and Promoters
Under Section 35 of the Companies Act, 2013, who among the following is *not* typically held liable to pay compensation for loss or damage sustained by any person who subscribed for securities acting on a misleading prospectus?
A. Every person who is a director of the company at the time of the issue
B. Every person who has authorized themselves to be named as a director in the prospectus
C. An ordinary employee of the company who had no role in drafting the prospectus ✔
D. Every promoter of the company
Explanation: Section 35 specifies civil liability for directors, promoters, and persons named as directors with their consent. Ordinary employees without management/drafting responsibilities are not categorized among those strictly liable under Section 35.
Hard NORMAL · Criminal Liability | Section 447 | Penalty
What is the penalty range for fraud under Section 447, which is triggered when Section 34 (criminal liability for misstatement in prospectus) is invoked?
A. Imprisonment from 6 months up to 3 years
B. Imprisonment from 6 months up to 10 years and fine up to the amount involved ✔
C. Only monetary fine without imprisonment
D. Imprisonment for a fixed term of 5 years
Explanation: Section 34 attracts punishment under Section 447, which mandates imprisonment for a term not less than 6 months extending up to 10 years, and a fine not less than the amount involved in the fraud, extending up to 3 times the amount involved.
Hard NORMAL · Fictitious Name | Section 38 | Personation
Under Section 38 of the Companies Act, 2013, what penalty is prescribed for any person who makes or abets making of an application in a fictitious name for acquiring securities in a company?
A. Imprisonment up to 1 year or fine up to Rs. 50,000
B. Imprisonment for a term of 1 to 5 years and fine ✔
C. Strictly a civil penalty equal to twice the application money
D. No criminal penalty, only cancellation of application
Explanation: Section 38 prescribes punishment for personation in acquisitions, stating that any person who makes an application in a fictitious name shall be punishable with imprisonment for a term of 1 to 5 years.
Medium NORMAL · Stock Exchange | Section 40 | Public Offer
When a company makes a public offer, every company must make an application to one or more recognized stock exchange(s) for permission for the securities to be dealt with on such stock exchange, as mandated by which section?
A. Section 39
B. Section 40 ✔
C. Section 26
D. Section 42
Explanation: Section 40 of the Companies Act, 2013 requires every company making a public offer to make an application before issuing prospectus to one or more recognized stock exchange or exchanges and obtain permission thereof.
Hard NORMAL · Minimum Subscription | Section 39 | Interest on Refund
Under Section 39(3) of the Companies Act, 2013, if a company fails to repay application money within the prescribed time after the minimum subscription is not received, what is the rate of interest payable by the company and its officers in default?
A. 6% per annum
B. 12% per annum
C. 15% per annum ✔
D. 18% per annum
Explanation: Section 39(3) dictates that if the stated minimum subscription is not received and application money is not repaid within 15 days from the closure of the issue, the company and every officer in default shall be liable to repay application money with interest at the rate of 15% per annum.
Medium NORMAL · Private Placement | Section 42 | Maximum Persons
What is the maximum number of persons to whom a private placement of securities can be made in a financial year, as per the rules prescribed under Section 42 of the Companies Act, 2013, excluding qualified institutional buyers and employees under ESOP?
A. 50 persons
B. 100 persons
C. 200 persons ✔
D. 499 persons
Explanation: Section 42 read with relevant rules specifies that an offer or invitation through private placement can be made to not more than 200 persons in the aggregate in a financial year, excluding QIBs and employees given securities under ESOP.
Medium NORMAL · Private Placement | Banking Channels | Rule 14
Moneys received under a private placement offer must be paid through which of the following modes?
A. Cash only
B. Cheque or demand draft or other banking channels only, but not cash ✔
C. Either cash up to Rs. 10,000 or cheque
D. Cryptocurrency or bank transfer
Explanation: Rule 14 of the Companies (Prospectus and Allotment of Securities) Rules, 2014 mandates that monies payable on subscription to private placement shall be paid through cheque or demand draft or other banking channels, and not by cash.
Medium NORMAL · Return of Allotment | Form PAS-3 | Private Placement
Within how many days from the date of allotment of securities under a private placement must a company file a return of allotment with the Registrar in Form PAS-3?
A. 15 days
B. 30 days ✔
C. 60 days
D. 90 days
Explanation: Section 42(9) and Rule 14 require a company making any allotment of securities under private placement to file with the Registrar a return of allotment in Form PAS-3 within 30 days from the date of the allotment.
Hard NORMAL · Civil Liability | Defenses | Section 35
Which of the following is an exception where a civil liability defense under Section 35 is available to a director who otherwise consented to be named in the prospectus?
A. The director did not read the prospectus before signing.
B. The director withdrew consent publicly before the issue of the prospectus and gave reasonable public notice. ✔
C. The director relied entirely on the company secretary's advice.
D. The prospectus was approved by the Board of Directors unanimously.
Explanation: Section 35(2) provides a defense from civil liability if a director proves that, having consented to become a director of the company, they withdrew their consent before the issue of the prospectus, and that it was issued without their authority or consent.
Hard NORMAL · Private Placement | Separate Bank Account | Section 42
Can a company utilize any monies raised through private placement before making the relevant allotment of securities and filing the return of allotment?
A. Yes, immediately upon receiving the application money.
B. Yes, up to 50% of the money received.
C. No, monies received must be kept in a separate bank account and cannot be utilized until allotment is made. ✔
D. Yes, if approved by an ordinary resolution.
Explanation: Section 42(6) states that monies received on application under private placement shall be kept in a separate bank account in a scheduled bank and shall not be utilized for any purpose other than for adjustment against allotment or repayment for failure to allot.
Medium NORMAL · GDR | Definitions | Section 2(44)
What constitutes a 'Global Depository Receipt' (GDR) under Section 2(44) of the Companies Act, 2013?
A. Any instrument issued outside India by a company, foreign or domestic, for local deposits.
B. Any instrument in the form of a depository receipt, created by a foreign depository outside India, authorizing acquisition of securities issued by an Indian company. ✔
C. A receipt issued by the Reserve Bank of India for holding foreign exchange.
D. A bond issued by the Central Government in global markets.
Explanation: Section 2(44) defines Global Depository Receipt as any instrument in the form of a depository receipt, created by a foreign depository outside India and authorized by a company, making an issue of depository receipts.
Hard NORMAL · Penalty | Form PAS-3 | Section 42
If a company defaults in filing the return of allotment in Form PAS-3 within the prescribed 30 days under private placement provisions, what is the penalty structure for the company and officers in default?
A. Rs. 1,000 per day up to a maximum of Rs. 1,00,000
B. A penalty of one thousand rupees for each day during which such default continues but not exceeding twenty-five lakh rupees for the company and officer in default ✔
C. Immediate winding up of the company
D. Strict criminal imprisonment without fine options
Explanation: Section 42(10) prescribes that if a company defaults in filing the return of allotment within the specified period, the company, promoters and directors shall be liable to a penalty of Rs. 1,000 for each day during which default continues, up to a maximum of Rs. 25 lakhs.
Medium NORMAL · Prospectus | Section 26 | Signing of Prospectus
Under Section 26 of the Companies Act, 2013, every prospectus issued by or on behalf of a public company must be dated and signed by whom?
A. The Chief Executive Officer alone
B. All the directors or proposed directors of the company or their duly authorized attorneys ✔
C. The Registrar of Companies
D. The statutory auditor of the company
Explanation: Section 26(4) states that every prospectus shall be dated and signed by every director or proposed director named in the prospectus or by his duly authorized attorney.
Medium NORMAL · Prospectus | Auditor Reports | Section 26
Which of the following matters must be explicitly reported upon by the statutory auditors in a prospectus as required under Section 26?
A. Profits and losses of the company for each of the 5 financial years immediately preceding the issue of prospectus ✔
B. Projected future market share for the next 10 years
C. Personal tax returns of all individual promoters
D. Daily attendance records of employees
Explanation: Section 26(1) requires the prospectus to set out reports by the auditors of the company with respect to profits and losses of the company for each of the 5 financial years immediately preceding the financial year of the issue.
Medium NORMAL · Shelf Prospectus | Objective | Section 31
What is the primary objective of requiring a company to issue a 'Shelf Prospectus'?
A. To bypass SEBI approvals entirely for equity shares
B. To allow a company to issue one or more issues of securities over a certain period without the need of issuing a fresh prospectus for each offer ✔
C. To permanently avoid publishing annual financial statements
D. To raise funds exclusively from foreign institutional investors
Explanation: A shelf prospectus allows a class or classes of companies (like public financial institutions or banks) to issue securities in one or more tranches over a period of up to one year without issuing a full prospectus every single time.
Hard NORMAL · Shelf Prospectus | Eligible Companies | Section 31
Which of the following entities is permitted to issue a 'Shelf Prospectus' under the rules and provisions of the Companies Act, 2013?
A. Any newly incorporated private company
B. Any company engaged in retail trade
C. Public Financial Institutions, Banks or Public Sector Companies as specified by SEBI ✔
D. Foreign companies operating without an Indian branch
Explanation: Section 31 restricts the issuance of a shelf prospectus to such classes of companies as the Securities and Exchange Board of India (SEBI) may specify in this behalf, primarily Public Financial Institutions, banks, and large public sector issuers.
Hard NORMAL · Private Placement | Deemed Public Offer | Section 42
What is the consequence if an invitation to subscribe for securities is made to 250 persons without complying with the private placement provisions under Section 42?
A. It is treated as a valid private placement.
B. It is deemed to be a public offer, attracting all public offer regulations and severe penalties. ✔
C. It is automatically converted into a bonus issue.
D. The company is dissolved without judicial intervention.
Explanation: Section 42(2) stipulates that if an offer or invitation is made to more than the prescribed number of persons (200), it shall be deemed to be a public offer and shall require compliance with all provisions of public offers, besides attracting monetary penalties.
Medium NORMAL · Allotment of Securities | Time Limit | Section 39
What is the maximum time limit within which a company making a public offer must allot securities after the closure of the subscription list?
A. 30 days ✔
B. 60 days
C. 90 days
D. 120 days
