CASE SCENARIO: Aura Cosmetics Private Limited has 50 members and a paid-up share capital of Rs. 5 crore, free reserves of Rs. 2 crore, and securities premium of Rs. 1 crore. The company needs funds for business expansion and decides to accept an unsecured loan of Rs. 2.5 crore from Mr. Karan, who is a director of the company. Mr. Karan provides a declaration stating that the money is out of his own personal funds and not borrowed from anyone else.
Medium SCENARIO · Aggregate Capital and Reserves | Private Company | Computation
What is the total aggregate of paid-up share capital, free reserves, and securities premium account for Aura Cosmetics Private Limited?
A. Rs. 5 crore
B. Rs. 7 crore
C. Rs. 8 crore ✔
D. Rs. 6 crore
Explanation: Paid-up Share Capital (Rs. 5 crore) + Free Reserves (Rs. 2 crore) + Securities Premium Account (Rs. 1 crore) = Rs. 8 crore.
Medium SCENARIO · Director Loan | Exclusion from Deposit | Rule 2(1)(c)
How will the Rs. 2.5 crore loan received from Mr. Karan (a director) with his declaration be treated under the Companies (Acceptance of Deposits) Rules, 2014?
A. It will be classified as a public deposit subject to Section 73
B. It will be excluded from the definition of 'deposit' under Rule 2(1)(c) ✔
C. It will be classified as a debenture
D. It will be treated as an illegal deposit
Explanation: Under Rule 2(1)(c)(viii), any amount received from a person who, at the time of receipt, was a director of the company is excluded from the definition of a deposit, provided the director furnishes a written declaration that the amount is out of their own funds and not borrowed.
Hard SCENARIO · Director Relative | Declaration | Exclusions
Suppose Mr. Karan was NOT a director, but the brother of a director, and gave the loan with a similar declaration. Would it still be excluded from deposits?
A. Yes, relatives of directors are always excluded
B. Yes, because a relative's loan with a non-borrowed fund declaration is also excluded under Rule 2(1)(c)(viii) ✔
C. No, relatives can never lend money to private companies
D. No, only loans from institutional lenders are excluded
Explanation: Rule 2(1)(c)(viii) also covers amounts received from a relative of a director of the company at the time of receipt, provided the relative furnishes a written declaration that the amount is not given out of borrowed funds.
Hard SCENARIO · Member Deposit Limit | Private Company | Rule 3
What would be the maximum ceiling limit for accepting ordinary deposits from members for Aura Cosmetics Private Limited if it decides to invite member deposits?
A. 10% of aggregate of share capital, reserves, and premium
B. 25% of aggregate of share capital, reserves, and premium
C. 35% of aggregate of share capital, reserves, and premium ✔
D. 50% of aggregate of share capital, reserves, and premium
Explanation: For a private company (which is not an eligible company), deposits from members can be accepted up to 35% of the aggregate of its paid-up share capital, free reserves, and securities premium account, subject to passing an ordinary or special resolution as mandated by rules.
CASE SCENARIO: Solaris Power Limited, an eligible public company under Section 76, accepted deposits worth Rs. 20 crore from the public on 1st October 2024. The deposits are secured against plant and machinery. Due to severe market downturns in 2025, the company failed to repay deposits amounting to Rs. 5 crore that matured on 30th September 2025. Depositors have approached the company and threatened legal action.
Medium SCENARIO · Secured Deposits | Charge Creation | Rule 6
Within how many days from 1st October 2024 was Solaris Power Limited required to create a charge on its assets for securing the deposits?
A. Within 15 days
B. Within 30 days ✔
C. Within 60 days
D. Within 90 days
Explanation: Rule 6 mandates that every company accepting secured deposits must create a charge on its assets (excluding intangible assets) within 30 days of acceptance of deposits.
Medium SCENARIO · Tribunal Powers | Default in Repayment | Section 75
What action can the Tribunal take under Section 75 upon application by the aggrieved depositors who have not been repaid?
A. Direct the company to forthwith repay the deposits along with interest ✔
B. Order immediate liquidation of the company without inquiry
C. Transfer ownership of the company to the depositors
D. Impose a penalty only on the external auditor
Explanation: Under Section 75, if the company fails to repay deposits, the Tribunal may, on its own motion or on an application by a depositor, direct the company to repay the deposit forthwith along with interest due.
Hard SCENARIO · Section 76A | Penalties | Contravention
What penalty does Solaris Power Limited face under Section 76A for defaulting on deposit repayments and contravening deposit provisions?
A. A fine of not less than Rs. 50 lakh extending up to Rs. 5 crore
B. A fine of not less than Rs. 1 crore or twice the amount of deposit accepted, whichever is lower, extending up to Rs. 10 crore ✔
C. A flat penalty of Rs. 10 crore without any lower limit
D. Only imprisonment of the Managing Director for 10 years without fine
Explanation: Section 76A specifies that for contravention of deposit provisions, the company shall be punishable with a fine of not less than Rs. 1 crore or twice the amount of deposit accepted, whichever is lower, extending up to Rs. 10 crore.
Medium SCENARIO · Default Consequence | Prohibition on Renewal | Rule 3
Can Solaris Power Limited accept or renew any new deposits from the public while the default of Rs. 5 crore continues?
A. Yes, up to 50% of its normal limit
B. Yes, if approved by the Board of Directors
C. No, the company is strictly prohibited from accepting or renewing any deposits while the default continues ✔
D. Yes, provided fresh credit rating is obtained
Explanation: Rule 3(1) and general regulatory provisions prohibit any company in default of deposit repayment from accepting or renewing any deposits until the default is fully rectified.
CASE SCENARIO: Neptune Maritime Services Limited is preparing to accept deposits from the public as an eligible company under Section 76. The company’s Board is finalizing the text of the circular advertisement, compliance certificates, credit rating reports, and arrangement of the Deposit Repayment Reserve Account for deposits maturing in the next financial year.
Medium SCENARIO · Circular Registration | Rule 4 | ROC Filing
How many days before the actual issue of the circular or advertisement inviting deposits must Neptune Maritime Services Limited deliver a copy of it to the Registrar for registration?
A. At least 7 days before
B. At least 15 days before
C. At least 30 days before ✔
D. At least 45 days before
Explanation: Rule 4(1) requires that a copy of the circular or advertisement inviting deposits, signed by all directors, must be delivered to the Registrar for registration at least 30 days before the date of its issue.
Hard SCENARIO · Deposit Repayment Reserve | Rule 13 | Compliance Deadline
What is the deadline for Neptune Maritime Services Limited to deposit at least 20% of its deposits maturing during the following financial year into the Deposit Repayment Reserve Account?
A. On or before 30th April of each year ✔
B. On or before 30th June of each year
C. On or before 31st March of each year
D. Within 30 days of maturity
Explanation: Rule 13 mandates that every company shall, on or before the 30th day of April of each year, deposit at least 20% of the amount of its deposits maturing during the following financial year in a scheduled bank under a designated Deposit Repayment Reserve Account.
Hard SCENARIO · Circular Validity | Rule 4(11) | AGM
What is the validity period of the circular or advertisement inviting deposits issued by Neptune Maritime Services Limited?
A. 30 days from issue
B. 6 months from the closure of the financial year or the date of AGM at which financial statements are laid, whichever is earlier ✔
C. 12 months from the date of issue
D. Until revoked by the Registrar
Explanation: Rule 4(11) states that a circular or advertisement inviting deposits remains valid until the expiry of 6 months from the date of closure of the financial year in which it is issued or the date on which financial statements are laid at the AGM, whichever is earlier.
Medium SCENARIO · Form DPT-3 | Annual Return | Rule 16
When must Neptune Maritime Services Limited file its annual return of deposits in Form DPT-3 with the Registrar?
A. On or before 30th June of every year ✔
B. On or before 30th April of every year
C. On or before 31st March of every year
D. Within 60 days of the AGM
Explanation: Rule 16 requires every company to file Form DPT-3 on or before the 30th day of June of every year, reporting particulars of deposits and exempt transactions as of 31st March of that year.
CASE SCENARIO: Titanium Logistics Private Limited receives various funds during the financial year: Rs. 50 lakh as an advance from a customer for freight services to be rendered within 4 months; Rs. 20 lakh as a non-interest-bearing security deposit from an employee earning an annual salary of Rs. 8 lakh under an employment contract; Rs. 15 lakh as a commercial paper issue; and Rs. 10 lakh as an unverified loan from a casual acquaintance.
Medium SCENARIO · Advance for Services | Rule 2(1)(c) | Exclusions
How will the Rs. 50 lakh advance received from the customer for services to be rendered within 4 months be treated under the Deposit Rules?
A. Treated as a public deposit immediately
B. Excluded from the definition of 'deposit' because it is an advance for services appropriated within 365 days ✔
C. Treated as an illegal loan
D. Classified as debenture capital
Explanation: Rule 2(1)(c)(xii)(a) excludes amounts received as an advance for the supply of goods or provision of services accounted for in terms of money, provided the goods/services are appropriated within 365 days from the date of acceptance of advance.
Hard SCENARIO · Employee Security Deposit | Rule 2(1)(c) | Thresholds
How will the Rs. 20 lakh security deposit taken from the employee earning an annual salary of Rs. 8 lakh be classified?
A. Excluded from deposits since it is an employee security deposit up to annual salary
B. Treated entirely as a deposit because Rs. 20 lakh exceeds the employee's annual salary of Rs. 8 lakh ✔
C. Treated as a debenture
D. Excluded unconditionally regardless of salary amount
Explanation: Rule 2(1)(c)(x) excludes employee security deposits *not exceeding* their annual salary. Since the security deposit (Rs. 20 lakh) exceeds the annual salary of the employee (Rs. 8 lakh), the entire amount (or the excess depending on exact interpretation, but rule specifies 'not exceeding his annual salary' as condition for exclusion; exceeding it makes it a deposit).
Medium SCENARIO · Commercial Paper | Exclusions | Rule 2(1)(c)
Is the Rs. 15 lakh raised through the issue of commercial papers considered a 'deposit'?
A. Yes, all short-term debt instruments are deposits
B. No, commercial papers are specifically excluded from the definition of deposit under Rule 2(1)(c) ✔
C. Yes, unless issued by a banking company
D. No, only if listed on a stock exchange
Explanation: Rule 2(1)(c)(vii) excludes any amount raised by the issue of commercial papers or other instruments in accordance with guidelines issued by the Reserve Bank of India.
Hard SCENARIO · Unverified Loan | Definition of Deposit | Rule 2(1)(c)
How will the Rs. 10 lakh unverified loan from a casual acquaintance be treated under the Companies Act, 2013?
A. Excluded from deposits as a casual loan
B. Treated as a deposit because it does not fall under any of the recognized exclusion categories in Rule 2(1)(c) ✔
C. Treated as share capital
D. Exempt if interest is below 4%
Explanation: Any amount received as a loan or deposit from an individual (casual acquaintance) who is neither a director, relative, nor institutional lender does not qualify for any exclusion under Rule 2(1)(c) and is therefore classified as a deposit.

Paper 2: Corporate and Other Laws · Module 1 · Chapter 6:

Law — 55 rows
Easy NORMAL · Definition of Charge | Section 2(16) | Scope of Registration
According to the Companies Act, 2013, what does the term 'charge' include for the purpose of registration under Chapter VI?
A. Only a mortgage created on the immovable property of a company
B. A lien on the assets of the company ✔
C. A pledge of movable goods held in the ordinary course of business
D. An assignment of actionable claims without security
Explanation: Under Section 2(16) of the Companies Act, 2013, 'charge' means an interest or lien created on the property or assets of a company or any of its undertakings or both as security and includes a mortgage. A lien is expressly included, whereas a mere pledge of movable goods is generally excluded from registration under Chapter VI.
Easy NORMAL · Creation of Charge | Section 77 | Time Limit
Within how many days from the date of creation of a charge must particulars of the charge be filed with the Registrar under Section 77 by a company incorporated in India?
A. 15 days
B. 30 days ✔
C. 60 days
D. 90 days
Explanation: Section 77(1) mandates that every company creating a charge within or outside India, on its property or assets or any of its undertakings, shall register the particulars of the charge signed by the company and the charge-holder within 30 days of its creation.
Medium NORMAL · Section 77 Proviso | Condonation of Delay | Additional Fee
If a company fails to register a charge within the initial 30 days of its creation, up to what maximum total period (from the date of creation) can the Registrar allow registration upon payment of additional fee, for a charge created after the commencement of the Companies (Amendment) Ordinance, 2019?
A. 30 days
B. 60 days ✔
C. 90 days
D. 300 days
Explanation: As per the proviso to Section 77(1), if the registration is not made within 30 days, the Registrar may allow it to be filed within a further period of 60 days (total 60 days from creation) on payment of prescribed additional fee.
Medium NORMAL · Section 87 | Regional Director Powers | Rectification of Charges
If a charge created by a company is not registered within the extended period of 60 days under Section 77(1), who has the power to grant an extension of time under Section 87?
A. The Regional Director (RD) ✔
B. The National Company Law Tribunal (NCLT)
C. The Registrar of Companies (ROC)
D. The Securities and Exchange Board of India (SEBI)
Explanation: Under Section 87 read with the relevant rules, the Central Government (powers delegated to the Regional Director) is empowered to condone delay and allow rectification or late filing of charges if it is satisfied that the omission was accidental or inadvertent or of such nature as not to prejudice the interest of creditors/shareholders.
Medium NORMAL · Section 77 | Effect of Non-Registration | Liquidator and Creditors
What is the consequence of non-registration of a charge created by a company, as specified under Section 77 read with Section 84, against the liquidator and any creditor of the company?
A. The charge becomes completely void ab initio for all purposes.
B. The charge is void against the liquidator and any creditor of the company. ✔
C. The underlying debt becomes immediately irrecoverable.
D. The directors are personally imprisoned for 6 months.
Explanation: Section 78/84 and established jurisprudence dictate that if a charge required to be registered is not registered, it is void against the liquidator and any creditor of the company, meaning the secured creditor ranks merely as an unsecured creditor upon winding up.
Medium NORMAL · Section 78 | Right of Charge-holder | Default by Company
Can a charge-holder apply for the registration of a charge if the company itself fails to do so within the initial 30 days under Section 78?
A. No, only the company can apply for registration under any circumstances.
B. Yes, the person in whose favour the charge is created may apply to the Registrar and recover expenses from the company. ✔
C. Yes, but only after obtaining prior written permission from the NCLT.
D. No, the charge-holder must file a civil suit for specific performance.
Explanation: Section 78 provides that where a company fails to register a charge within the 30-day period, the person in whose favour the charge is created may apply to the Registrar for registration, and upon registration, recover the expenses from the company.
Easy NORMAL · Section 77(2) | Certificate of Registration | Form CHG-2
When a charge is registered with the Registrar, what certificate does the Registrar issue to the company under Section 77(2)?
A. Certificate of Incorporation
B. Certificate of Registration of Charge ✔
C. Certificate of Commencement of Business
D. Certificate of Satisfaction of Charge
Explanation: Section 77(2) requires the Registrar to issue a certificate of registration of charge in the prescribed form (Form CHG-2) upon the registration of the particulars of a charge.
Medium NORMAL · Section 77(2) | Conclusive Evidence | Evidentiary Value
What is the evidentiary value of the Certificate of Registration issued by the Registrar under Section 77?
A. It is rebuttable evidence that all requirements of Chapter VI have been complied with.
B. It is conclusive evidence that the requirements of Chapter VI as to registration have been complied with. ✔
C. It is merely an administrative acknowledgement with no legal evidentiary value.
D. It serves as conclusive evidence regarding the validity of the underlying contract.
Explanation: Section 77(2) explicitly states that the certificate issued by the Registrar shall be conclusive evidence that the requirements of Chapter VI as to registration have been complied with.
Easy NORMAL · Section 82 | Satisfaction of Charge | Time Limit
Within how many days must a company give intimation to the Registrar regarding the payment or satisfaction in full of any charge registered under Chapter VI, pursuant to Section 82?
A. 15 days
B. 30 days ✔
C. 60 days
D. 90 days
Explanation: Section 82(1) stipulates that a company shall inform the Registrar within a period of 30 days of the payment or satisfaction in full of any charge registered under this chapter.
Medium NORMAL · Form CHG-4 | Satisfaction of Charge | Rules 2014
What form is prescribed under the Companies (Registration of Charges) Rules, 2014, for filing the notice of satisfaction of a charge with the Registrar?
A. Form CHG-1
B. Form CHG-4 ✔
C. Form CHG-7
D. Form CHG-9
Explanation: Form CHG-4 is the prescribed form under the rules for giving notice of satisfaction in full of a charge to the Registrar.
Hard NORMAL · Section 82(2) | Notice to Charge-holder | ROC Procedure
What action does the Registrar take upon receipt of intimation of satisfaction of a charge under Section 82?
A. Issues a notice to show cause to the company why it paid off the debt.
B. Sends a notice to the holder of the charge calling for objections, if any, within a specified time. ✔
C. Immediately destroys the historical charge records without informing anyone.
D. Directs the company to liquidate its assets.
Explanation: Under Section 82(2), upon receipt of intimation under Section 82(1), the Registrar issues a show-cause notice to the charge-holder calling for objections, if any, within such time not exceeding 14 days, as may be specified, as to why payment or satisfaction should not be recorded.
Easy NORMAL · Section 85 | Register of Charges | Registered Office
Under Section 85, every company is required to keep a register of charges at its registered office. Which of the following details must be entered in this register?
A. Only the name of the company's bankers
B. Particulars of all charges created or modified, affecting properties of the company ✔
C. The personal income tax returns of the directors
D. The minutes of general meetings related to dividend declaration
Explanation: Section 85 mandates that every company shall keep at its registered office a register of charges and enter therein particulars of all charges explicitly created or modified, affecting any property or assets of the company.
Medium NORMAL · Section 85(2) | Inspection of Register | Members and Creditors
Who is entitled to inspect the register of charges and instrument of charges maintained by a company under Section 85?
A. Only the equity shareholders of the company
B. Any creditor or member of the company free of cost, and any other person on payment of a prescribed fee ✔
C. Only the Central Government and statutory auditors
D. Any member of the general public without any conditions
Explanation: Section 85(2) provides that the register of charges and instrument of charges shall be open for inspection during business hours by any member or creditor without fee, and by any other person on payment of prescribed fee.
Medium NORMAL · Section 86 | Punishment for Default | Offences and Penalties
What is the penalty under Section 86 if a company defaults in complying with any of the provisions of Chapter VI relating to the registration of charges, and no specific penalty is provided elsewhere?
A. Only a warning letter from the ROC
B. Punishment with fine for the company and imprisonment/fine for defaulting officers ✔
C. Immediate compulsory winding up of the company by the Supreme Court
D. Forfeiture of all shares held by the promoters
Explanation: Section 86 specifies penalties for non-compliance, making the company liable to a substantial monetary fine, and every officer in default punishable with imprisonment and/or fine.
Medium NORMAL · Section 77 | Property Outside India | Jurisdiction
Does the requirement of registration of charges under Section 77 apply to a charge created on property situated outside India by a company incorporated in India?
A. No, charges on foreign property are completely exempt.
B. Yes, it applies whether the property or undertaking is situated within or outside India. ✔
C. Yes, but only if the property is situated in a Commonwealth country.
D. No, only foreign companies are required to register foreign properties.
Explanation: Section 77(1) explicitly states that the duty to register applies to every company creating a charge 'on its property or assets or any of its undertakings, whether within or outside India'.
Medium NORMAL · Form CHG-1 | Creation and Modification | Rules 2014
Which form is used for registering the creation or modification of a charge (other than those related to debentures) under the Companies (Registration of Charges) Rules, 2014?
A. Form CHG-1 ✔
B. Form CHG-4
C. Form CHG-8
D. Form INC-22
Explanation: Form CHG-1 is the prescribed form for registration of creation or modification of charges other than debentures. Form CHG-9 is used for debentures including rectification.
Medium NORMAL · Section 79 | Modification of Charge | Applicability
What is the legal implication when a company modifies a charge (e.g., change in terms of repayment or increased limit), but fails to register such modification?
A. Modification does not require registration under any circumstances.
B. The provisions relating to registration of charges apply to modification of charges in the same manner as a charge. ✔
C. Only the original creation becomes void, while the modification remains valid.
D. The company is exempt from filing Form CHG-1 for modifications.
Explanation: Section 79 explicitly enacts that the provisions of Chapter VI relating to registration of charges shall apply to a modification of any charge in the same manner as they apply to a charge created ab initio.
Hard NORMAL · Section 81 | Receiver Appointment | Notice to ROC
Under Section 81, when a receiver of the property of a company is appointed, within how many days must notice of such appointment be given to the company and the Registrar?
A. 7 days
B. 15 days
C. 30 days ✔
D. 45 days
Explanation: Section 81 requires any person who obtains an order for the appointment of a receiver of the property of a company, or appoints such receiver under any powers contained in any instrument, to give notice of the same to the company and the Registrar within 30 days of the order/appointment.
Hard NORMAL · Form CHG-6 | Receiver/Cessation | ROC Filings
What form is utilized by a receiver to file notice of their appointment or cessation with the Registrar under Section 81?
A. Form CHG-1
B. Form CHG-2
C. Form CHG-6 ✔
D. Form CHG-8
Explanation: Form CHG-6 is the prescribed form under the Companies (Registration of Charges) Rules, 2014 for filing notice of appointment or cessation of a receiver or liquidator.
Hard NORMAL · Section 87 | Central Government / RD | Rectification of Omissions
Can the Central Government direct a company to rectify any omission or misstatement in filing particulars of a charge or its satisfaction under Section 87?
A. No, once filed, corrections can only be made by order of the Supreme Court.
B. Yes, on an application by the company or any interested person, if it is satisfied that the omission/misstatement was accidental or inadvertent. ✔
C. No, rectifications are strictly prohibited under the Companies Act, 2013.
D. Yes, but only suo motu without any application.
Explanation: Section 87 empowers the Central Government (Regional Director) to direct rectification of omission or misstatement in the registration, modification, or satisfaction of charges if satisfied that it was accidental, inadvertent, or did not prejudice interests.
Medium NORMAL · Section 80 | Constructive Notice | Subsequent Acquirer
Does the registration of a charge operate as constructive notice to any person who subsequently acquires the property on which the charge is created?
A. No, registration is only for internal government records and confers no notice.
B. Yes, registration of a charge constitutes constructive notice to the public/subsequent acquirers under Section 80. ✔
C. Only if the subsequent acquirer personally inspects the company's factory.
D. No, constructive notice applies only to the Memorandum and Articles of Association, not charges.
Explanation: Section 80 provides that any person acquiring any property, assets or part thereof on which a charge is subsisting shall be deemed to have notice of the charge from the date of its registration under Section 77 (constructive notice).
Hard NORMAL · Section 77(3) | Types of Charges | Mandatory Registration
Which of the following charges requires mandatory registration under Section 77 of the Companies Act, 2013?
A. A charge on uncalled share capital of the company ✔
B. A pledge of goods stored in a public warehouse
C. A floating charge on stock-in-trade created in the ordinary course of business (where exempted by specific rules)
D. A statutory charge arising by operation of law (e.g., tax lien) without any act of parties
Explanation: Section 77(3) lists specific types of charges that require registration, including a charge on uncalled share capital, a charge on call made but not paid, a floating charge, etc. A pledge of goods and general statutory liens arising without agreement are generally distinct.
Hard NORMAL · Acquisition of Property | Mutatis Mutandis | Section 77
If a company acquires any property which is subject to a charge, is the company under an obligation to register the particulars of such charge?
A. No, because the charge was created by the previous owner, not the company.
B. Yes, the provisions of Section 77 apply mutatis mutandis to a company acquiring property subject to a charge. ✔
C. Only if the property is located outside India.
D. No, the seller alone is responsible for registering the charge transfer.
Explanation: Section 78/77 rules state that when a company acquires any property which is subject to a charge, the provisions of registering charges apply mutatis mutandis to such property acquired by the company as if it had created the charge itself.
Hard NORMAL · Section 86(1) | Penalties for Non-Registration | Officer in Default
What is the penalty prescribed under Section 86(1) for a company that defaults in registering a charge under Section 77?
A. A penalty of one lakh rupees
B. A penalty of five lakh rupees
C. A penalty of not less than one lakh rupees which may extend to ten lakh rupees ✔
D. Strict imprisonment of all directors for 2 years
Explanation: Section 86(1) prescribes that if any company defaults in complying with Section 77, the company shall be liable to a penalty of five lakh rupees and every officer in default shall be liable to a penalty of fifty thousand rupees which may extend to one lakh rupees (note: exact statutory penal amounts under current Act/Amendments).
Hard NORMAL · Section 82 Proviso | Delayed Satisfaction | Additional Fee
Can a company file particulars of satisfaction of a charge beyond the period of 30 days specified under Section 82(1)?
A. No, satisfaction can never be registered after 30 days.
B. Yes, the ROC may allow satisfaction to be filed within a further period of 300 days on payment of prescribed additional fees. ✔
C. Only with the special leave of the Supreme Court.
D. Yes, without any additional fees or time limit whatsoever.
Explanation: Provisos to Section 82/83 allow the ROC to accept delayed intimation of satisfaction of charges up to a extended period (often up to 300 days total under general filing rules) upon payment of prescribed additional or higher fees.
Medium NORMAL · Section 78 | Recovery of Expenses | Charge-holder Rights
In case a charge is registered by the charge-holder under Section 78 because of the company's default, what remedy does the charge-holder have to recover registration expenses?
A. File a winding-up petition directly without notice
B. Recover the amount of fees and expenses paid from the company as debt ✔
C. Confiscate the company's registered office building
D. Deduct the amount from the principal loan amount without company consent
Explanation: Section 78 explicitly entitles the charge-holder who incurs expenses in getting the charge registered to recover such amount from the company.
Medium NORMAL · Section 85(1) | Instrument of Charge | Registered Office Records
Which of the following instruments must be kept by the company along with the register of charges at its registered office under Section 85?
A. Only the board resolution approving the loan
B. A copy of every instrument creating or modifying any charge requiring registration ✔
C. The personal guarantees signed by independent directors
D. Tax audit reports for the last 5 years
Explanation: Section 85(1) specifies that a copy of every instrument creating or modifying any charge requiring registration under Chapter VI shall be kept at the registered office of the company along with the register of charges.
Hard NORMAL · Section 86(2) | Willful Suppression | Section 447 Fraud
If an officer of a company willfully furnishes any false or incorrect information or knowingly suppresses any material information required under Section 77 or Section 79, what penal consequence do they face?
A. They shall be liable for fraud under Section 447 of the Companies Act, 2013. ✔
B. They receive a simple verbal reprimand from the ROC.
C. They are disqualified from holding bank accounts only.
D. They are exempt from liability if the company pays a fine.
Explanation: Section 86(2) provides that if any person willfully furnishes any false or incorrect information or knowingly suppresses any material information, they shall be liable for action under Section 447 (Fraud).
Hard NORMAL · Negative Lien | Scope of Charge | Section 2(16) vs Covenants
Is a negative lien clause (an undertaking by a company not to create further charges on its property) required to be registered under Section 77 of the Companies Act, 2013?
A. Yes, all negative covenants must be registered as charges.
B. No, a negative lien does not create a security interest or charge on the property and hence does not require registration. ✔
C. Yes, but only if approved by the stock exchange.
D. No, unless the debt exceeds 100 crores.
Explanation: A negative lien is merely a negative covenant or promise not to encumber assets further and does not create any beneficial interest, lien, or security on the property itself. Therefore, it does not fall within the definition of a charge under Section 2(16) and does not require registration under Section 77.
Easy NORMAL · Objective of Registration | Transparency | Public Notice
What is the primary objective of registering charges created by a company under Chapter VI of the Companies Act, 2013?
A. To generate tax revenue for the Ministry of Corporate Affairs
B. To protect prospective creditors and members by giving them public notice of existing encumbrances on company assets ✔
C. To enable the Central Government to manage the day-to-day operations of the company
D. To fix executive salaries in the company
Explanation: The fundamental purpose of charge registration is to ensure transparency and provide public/constructive notice to any person dealing with the company so they are aware of existing encumbrances on the company's assets.
CASE SCENARIO: Zenith Engineering Limited created a mortgage on its factory land and building in favour of Apex Bank Ltd. on 10th May 2026 to secure a term loan of Rs. 5 crores. Due to an administrative oversight by the company secretary, the particulars of the charge were not filed with the Registrar within 30 days. On 5th July 2026, Apex Bank (the charge-holder) discovered this omission and decided to take matters into its own hands under the provisions of the Companies Act, 2013.
Medium SCENARIO · Section 77 | Calculation of 30 Days | Case Scenario
What was the last date by which Zenith Engineering Limited should have originally filed the particulars of the charge under Section 77(1)?
A. 25th May 2026
B. 9th June 2026 ✔
C. 10th June 2026
D. 9th July 2026
Explanation: The charge was created on 10th May 2026. Counting 30 days from 10th May (excluding the date of creation: 20 days in May + 9 days in June), the initial 30-day period expires on 9th June 2026.
Medium SCENARIO · Section 78 | Charge-holder Application | Expenses Recovery
Can Apex Bank Ltd. (the charge-holder) apply to the Registrar for registration of this charge since Zenith Engineering Limited failed to do so within 30 days?
A. No, only the company can apply for charge registration.
B. Yes, Apex Bank can apply under Section 78 and subsequently recover registration expenses from Zenith Engineering Limited. ✔
C. Yes, but only after filing a criminal complaint against the company secretary.
D. No, Apex Bank must wait for NCLT permission.
Explanation: Under Section 78, if a company fails to register a charge within 30 days, the person in whose favour the charge is created (Apex Bank) may apply to the Registrar for registration and recover the expenses from the company.
Medium SCENARIO · Section 77 Proviso | Extended Window | Additional Fee
Assuming Zenith Engineering Limited itself applies for registration on 1st July 2026 (within the extended window allowed by the ROC), what is required for the ROC to accept such filing?
A. Payment of standard fee only
B. Payment of prescribed additional fee as the filing is made beyond 30 days but within 60 days of creation ✔
C. Prior approval of the Supreme Court
D. Passing of an ordinary resolution in a general meeting
Explanation: Under the proviso to Section 77(1), for charges created after the amendment, if filing is done beyond 30 days but within a total of 60 days from creation, the Registrar may allow it upon payment of prescribed additional fee.
Hard SCENARIO · Effect of Non-Registration | Liquidation | Secured vs Unsecured
If neither the company nor Apex Bank registers the charge and Zenith Engineering Limited goes into liquidation, what is the legal status of Apex Bank's charge?
A. Apex Bank retains absolute priority as a secured creditor.
B. The charge is void against the liquidator and any creditor of the company, making Apex Bank an unsecured creditor. ✔
C. The term loan is automatically written off by the government.
D. Apex Bank becomes a shareholder of Zenith Engineering Limited.
Explanation: As per Section 77 read with Section 84, an unregistered charge is void against the liquidator and any creditor of the company, meaning the creditor loses its secured status and ranks as an unsecured creditor.
CASE SCENARIO: Vanguard Technologies Ltd. had registered a charge over its plant and machinery in favour of Global Finance Corp on 1st January 2025. On 15th March 2026, Vanguard Technologies Ltd. fully repaid the loan and satisfied the charge. However, the company omitted to inform the Registrar within the stipulated time. Meanwhile, Global Finance Corp received notice from the ROC regarding this satisfaction and raised no objections within the specified timeline. The company later maintained all statutory registers properly at its registered office.
Medium SCENARIO · Section 82(1) | Satisfaction Intimation | Timeline
Within how many days from 15th March 2026 was Vanguard Technologies Ltd. required to intimate the Registrar regarding the full satisfaction of the charge under Section 82(1)?
A. 15 days
B. 30 days ✔
C. 60 days
D. 90 days
Explanation: Section 82(1) requires the company to give intimation of payment or satisfaction in full of a registered charge to the Registrar within 30 days of such satisfaction.
Medium SCENARIO · Form CHG-4 | Satisfaction of Charge | Rules
What form must Vanguard Technologies Ltd. use to file the notice of satisfaction of the charge with the Registrar?
A. Form CHG-1
B. Form CHG-4 ✔
C. Form CHG-6
D. Form CHG-9
Explanation: Form CHG-4 is the specific prescribed form under the Companies (Registration of Charges) Rules, 2014 for intimating the payment or satisfaction in full of a charge.
Hard SCENARIO · Section 82(2) | Show Cause Notice | Charge-holder
When the Registrar receives the intimation of satisfaction, what maximum time limit is typically given to the charge-holder (Global Finance Corp) to show cause why satisfaction should not be recorded, under Section 82(2)?
A. 7 days
B. 14 days ✔
C. 30 days
D. 60 days
Explanation: Section 82(2) specifies that the Registrar shall issue a notice to the holder of the charge calling for objections, if any, within such time not exceeding 14 days as may be specified.
Medium SCENARIO · Section 85 | Registered Office | Register of Charges
Where must Vanguard Technologies Ltd. keep its register of charges and instrument of charges for inspection by members and creditors under Section 85?
A. At the corporate office of Global Finance Corp
B. At the registered office of the company ✔
C. At the nearest stock exchange building
D. Only at the residence of the Managing Director
Explanation: Section 85 explicitly mandates that every company shall keep at its registered office a register of charges and a copy of every instrument creating or modifying any charge.
CASE SCENARIO: Dynamic Logistics Ltd. created a floating charge on its entire fleet of delivery trucks in favour of Express Credit Bank on 1st February 2026. Due to an internal dispute among directors, the filing was delayed beyond the 60-day maximum period allowed by the Registrar under Section 77. The management now wishes to rectify this omission and approaches competent authorities. Additionally, a receiver was appointed over certain assets of the company on 1st April 2026 by an order of the court.
Hard SCENARIO · Section 87 | Central Government / RD | Condonation of Delay
Since the delay exceeded the maximum period of 60 days from creation that the ROC can condone under Section 77, which authority must Dynamic Logistics Ltd. approach for condonation and extension of time?
A. The Securities and Exchange Board of India (SEBI)
B. The Central Government (Regional Director) under Section 87 ✔
C. The Reserve Bank of India (RBI)
D. The Registrar of Companies (suo motu)
Explanation: Under Section 87, where the filing is delayed beyond the powers of the ROC under Section 77, the Central Government (Regional Director) is empowered to condone the delay and direct rectification upon application.
Hard SCENARIO · Section 81 | Receiver Appointment | Notice Period
Within how many days must notice of the appointment of the receiver of Dynamic Logistics Ltd.'s property be given to the company and the Registrar under Section 81?
A. 15 days
B. 30 days ✔
C. 60 days
D. 90 days
Explanation: Section 81 requires notice of the appointment of a receiver to be given to the company and the Registrar within 30 days of the order or appointment.
Hard SCENARIO · Form CHG-6 | Receiver Notice | ROC Filing
Which form is prescribed for filing notice of the appointment of the receiver with the Registrar under Section 81?
A. Form CHG-1
B. Form CHG-4
C. Form CHG-6 ✔
D. Form CHG-8
Explanation: Form CHG-6 is the prescribed form for registering the appointment or cessation of a receiver or liquidator under the Companies (Registration of Charges) Rules, 2014.
Hard SCENARIO · Floating Charge | Crystallization | Legal Nature
What is the legal nature of a 'floating charge' created on the fleet of delivery trucks of Dynamic Logistics Ltd. before it crystallizes?
A. It is an immediate fixed security on specific trucks currently owned.
B. It is an equitable charge on present and future assets of a circulating character which remains dormant until crystallization. ✔
C. It is legally invalid under Indian company law.
D. It is treated as an unsecured loan for all statutory purposes.
Explanation: A floating charge is a security on property of a circulating or fluctuating nature (like stock-in-trade or vehicles in fleet) which allows the company to deal with the assets in the ordinary course of business until it crystallizes upon an event such as default or winding up.
CASE SCENARIO: Pioneer Agro Industries Ltd. acquired a warehouse on 10th February 2026. The warehouse was already subject to an existing mortgage charge created by the previous owner in favour of Metro Bank. Pioneer Agro Industries Ltd. failed to register particulars of this acquired charge within the standard statutory time frame. Later, an outsider, Mr. X, acquired a portion of the company's property and claimed ignorance of Metro Bank's charge, arguing he had no personal knowledge of it.
Medium SCENARIO · Acquisition of Property | Mutatis Mutandis | Section 77
Are the provisions relating to registration of charges applicable to Pioneer Agro Industries Ltd. with respect to the warehouse acquired with an existing charge?
A. No, registration applies only to charges created directly by the company.
B. Yes, the provisions apply mutatis mutandis to property acquired subject to a charge. ✔
C. Only if approved by the Regional Director.
D. No, the previous owner alone remains responsible.
Explanation: Under the Companies Act, when a company acquires any property subject to a charge, the registration provisions apply mutatis mutandis as if the company had created the charge itself.
Medium SCENARIO · Section 80 | Constructive Notice | Subsequent Acquirer
Assuming Metro Bank's charge was duly registered under Section 77, what is the legal position regarding Mr. X's claim of ignorance?
A. Mr. X's claim is valid because he had no actual knowledge of the charge.
B. By virtue of Section 80, registration operates as constructive notice, so Mr. X is deemed to have notice of the charge. ✔
C. Metro Bank must compensate Mr. X for his loss.
D. The charge becomes void against Mr. X automatically.
Explanation: Section 80 provides that registration of a charge constitutes constructive notice to any person who subsequently acquires the property, regardless of whether they had actual notice.
Medium SCENARIO · Acquiring Company | Duty to Register | Section 77
Who is primarily responsible for filing the particulars of the charge when a company acquires property subject to a charge?
A. The previous owner of the property
B. The acquiring company (Pioneer Agro Industries Ltd.) ✔
C. Metro Bank exclusively
D. The local municipal corporation
Explanation: The acquiring company bears the primary statutory obligation to register the particulars of the charge within the prescribed time under Section 77/78 rules.
Hard SCENARIO · Section 86(2) | Suppression of Information | Section 447
If Pioneer Agro Industries Ltd. willfully suppresses material information regarding this charge during registration filings, what penal consequence may the officers face under Section 86(2)?
A. Liability for fraud under Section 447
B. A minor warning letter with zero penalty ✔
C. Mandatory community service
D. Revocation of the company's trademark only
Explanation: Section 86(2) provides that any person who willfully furnishes false/incorrect information or knowingly suppresses material information shall be liable for action under Section 447 (Fraud).
CASE SCENARIO: Alpha Consumer Goods Ltd. issued debentures secured by a charge on its fixed assets. The company created the charge on 1st March 2026. Due to a clerical error in the company's secretarial department, Form CHG-9 for the debenture charge was not filed within 30 days. The debenture-holders are concerned about their security and priority. The company secretary now seeks to regularize the default using the appropriate legal provisions and forms.
Medium SCENARIO · Form CHG-9 | Debentures | Rules 2014
Which specific form is prescribed under the Companies (Registration of Charges) Rules, 2014 for registration of creation or modification of charges relating to debentures?
A. Form CHG-1
B. Form CHG-4
C. Form CHG-6
D. Form CHG-9 ✔
Explanation: Form CHG-9 is specifically prescribed for registration of creation or modification of charges for debentures or rectification thereof.
Medium SCENARIO · Section 77(2) | Certificate of Registration | Conclusive Evidence
What evidentiary value does the Certificate of Registration of Charge issued by the ROC for this debenture charge hold?
A. It is conclusive evidence that all requirements of Chapter VI as to registration have been complied with. ✔
B. It is prima facie evidence which can be easily challenged in any court without proof.
C. It has no legal standing unless endorsed by the debenture trustees.
D. It is valid only for tax assessment purposes.
Explanation: Section 77(2) explicitly provides that the certificate of registration issued by the Registrar is conclusive evidence that all requirements of Chapter VI with respect to registration have been complied with.
Hard SCENARIO · Debentures | Non-Registration Effect | Winding Up
If Alpha Consumer Goods Ltd. fails to register the debenture charge within the maximum extended period permitted by the ROC, what is the impact on the debenture-holders during company winding up?
A. They retain priority over all other unsecured creditors.
B. The charge is void against the liquidator and creditors, ranking them as ordinary unsecured creditors. ✔
C. The debentures are converted into equity shares automatically.
D. The directors become personally liable to pay the full debenture amount immediately.
Explanation: Non-registration renders the charge void against the liquidator and creditors of the company, meaning the secured debenture-holders lose their priority and rank as unsecured creditors.
Medium SCENARIO · Section 85(2) | Inspection | Members and Creditors
Who is entitled to inspect the register of charges and instrument of charges maintained by Alpha Consumer Goods Ltd. under Section 85?
A. Only the debenture trustees
B. Any member or creditor free of cost, and any other person on payment of a prescribed fee ✔
C. Only the statutory auditors of the company
D. The general public without paying any fee under any circumstances
Explanation: Section 85(2) allows inspection of the register of charges and instrument of charges by any member or creditor without fee, and by any other person on payment of the prescribed fee during business hours.

Paper 2: Corporate and Other Laws · Module 2 · Chapter 7:

Law — 55 rows
Easy NORMAL · AGM | Time Gap | Section 96
According to the Companies Act, 2013, what is the maximum time gap allowed between two consecutive Annual General Meetings (AGMs) of a listed company?
A. 15 months ✔
B. 12 months
C. 6 months
D. 18 months
Explanation: Under Section 96 of the Companies Act, 2013, the maximum interval between two consecutive AGMs shall not exceed 15 months. This ensures timely reporting and shareholder oversight in companies.
Easy NORMAL · First AGM | Incorporation | Section 96
Within what period must a company hold its first Annual General Meeting from the date of its incorporation?
A. Within 6 months
B. Within 9 months ✔
C. Within 12 months
D. Within 15 months
Explanation: As per the second proviso to Section 96(1), every company must hold its first AGM within 9 months from the closing of the first financial year. If the first AGM is held within this period, the Registrar is not required to grant any extension.
Medium NORMAL · AGM Extension | RoC Powers | Section 96
Who has the authority to grant an extension of time for holding an Annual General Meeting (other than the first AGM) under the Companies Act, 2013?
A. National Company Law Tribunal (NCLT)
B. Registrar of Companies (RoC) ✔
C. Central Government
D. Securities and Exchange Board of India (SEBI)
Explanation: Under the first proviso to Section 96(1), the Registrar of Companies (RoC) may, for any special reason, extend the time within which any AGM (other than the first AGM) shall be held, by a period not exceeding 3 months.
Easy NORMAL · AGM Timing | National Holiday | Section 96
At what time and on what type of day must an Annual General Meeting be held according to Section 96?
A. Anytime during business hours on any day
B. During business hours on a national holiday
C. During business hours on any day that is not a National Holiday ✔
D. At any hour on a business day
Explanation: Section 96(2) specifies that every AGM shall be called during business hours, that is, between 9 a.m. and 6 p.m. on any day that is not a National Holiday.
Medium NORMAL · Shorter Notice | AGM | Section 101
What is the minimum shorter notice requirement for calling an AGM if consent is accorded in writing or by electronic mode by members holding not less than __% of the share capital giving right to vote at such meeting?
A. 90%
B. 95% ✔
C. 98%
D. 100%
Explanation: Under Section 101(1), an AGM may be called after giving a shorter notice if consent is given in writing or by electronic mode by not less than 95% of the members entitled to vote at such meeting.
Medium NORMAL · Quorum | Public Company | Section 103
In the case of a public company, what is the quorum required for a general meeting if the number of members as on the date of the meeting is more than 1,000 but up to 5,000?
A. 5 members personally present
B. 15 members personally present ✔
C. 30 members personally present
D. 50 members personally present
Explanation: Section 103 prescribes that for a public company, the quorum is 15 members personally present if the number of members is more than 1,000 but up to 5,000.
Easy NORMAL · Quorum | Private Company | Section 103
If a company does not have articles providing for a larger quorum, what is the quorum for a general meeting of a private company?
A. 1 member personally present
B. 2 members personally present ✔
C. 3 members personally present
D. 5 members personally present
Explanation: Section 103(1)(a)(i) states that unless the articles of a company provide for a larger number, the quorum for a private company shall be 2 members personally present.
Easy NORMAL · Minutes | Time Limit | Section 118
Within how many days from the conclusion of a general meeting must a company prepare and sign the minutes of that meeting?
A. 15 days
B. 30 days ✔
C. 45 days
D. 60 days
Explanation: As per Section 118(1) read with Secretarial Standards, minutes of every general meeting must be signed and entered in books kept for that purpose within 30 days of the conclusion of the meeting.
Hard NORMAL · Demand for Poll | Voting | Section 109
Who can demand a poll under Section 109 before or on the declaration of the result of the voting on any resolution on a show of hands, in a company having a share capital?
A. Any single member holding any number of shares
B. Members present in person or by proxy holding not less than 1/10th of the total voting power or having a paid-up capital of at least 5 lakh rupees ✔
C. Only the Chairman of the meeting
D. Members holding at least 50% of the voting power
Explanation: Under Section 109, a poll may be demanded by members present in person or by proxy, having not less than one-tenth of the total voting power or holding shares on which an aggregate sum of not less than 5 lakh rupees (or such higher amount as prescribed) has been paid-up.
Medium NORMAL · Proxy | Validity | Section 105
What is the maximum validity period of a proxy deposited with a company before a general meeting?
A. 30 days
B. 48 hours before the meeting
C. Valid until the meeting is concluded, unless revoked ✔
D. 6 months
Explanation: A proxy is valid for the meeting for which it is deposited (including any adjournment thereof) unless revoked by the member prior to the meeting. The instrument of proxy must be deposited 48 hours before the meeting.
Medium NORMAL · Ordinary Business | AGM | Section 102
Which of the following matters is NOT mandatorily required to be transacted as an ordinary business at an Annual General Meeting?
A. Consideration of financial statements and reports of the Board and Auditors
B. Declaration of dividend
C. Appointment of a director in place of those retiring
D. Appointment and fixation of remuneration of cost auditors ✔
Explanation: Section 102 classifies only four matters as ordinary business at an AGM: consideration of financial statements/reports, declaration of dividend, appointment of retiring directors, and appointment/remuneration of statutory auditors. Cost auditor appointment is special business.
Easy NORMAL · Explanatory Statement | Special Business | Section 102
What is the statutory requirement regarding the explanatory statement to be annexed to the notice of a general meeting under Section 102?
A. It is required only for ordinary business items.
B. It must be annexed for all items of special business to be transacted at the meeting. ✔
C. It is required only if requested by 10% of shareholders.
D. It is never required for private companies.
Explanation: Section 102 mandates that a statement setting out all material facts concerning each item of special business to be transacted at a general meeting must be annexed to the notice.
Medium NORMAL · Adjourned Meeting | Quorum | Section 103
If a meeting is adjourned due to lack of quorum, to what day, time, and place is it adjourned automatically by default under Section 103, unless otherwise specified by the Board?
A. Same day in the next week at the same time and place ✔
B. Next working day at the same time and place
C. Exactly 30 days later at the registered office
D. The meeting stands cancelled permanently
Explanation: Section 103(2) provides that if quorum is not present within half an hour from the time appointed, the meeting stands adjourned to the same day in the next week at the same time and place, or such other date, time, and place as the Board may determine.
Hard NORMAL · Proxy | Section 105 | Voting
Can a member of a company limited by shares, having the right to vote at a meeting, appoint multiple proxies under the Act, unless the articles restrict it?
A. No, only one proxy is allowed per member.
B. Yes, a member can appoint one or more proxies to attend and vote on the same poll. ✔
C. Yes, but only up to a maximum of 5 proxies.
D. Only institutional investors can appoint multiple proxies.
Explanation: Under Section 105(1), a member entitled to attend and vote is entitled to appoint another person as a proxy to attend and vote instead of the member. Multiple proxies can be appointed if permitted by rules/articles, though a proxy does not have the right to speak on a show of hands.
Medium NORMAL · EGM Requisition | Section 100 | Requisitionists
In an Extraordinary General Meeting (EGM) called by requisitionists under Section 100, what happens if the Board does not proceed to call a meeting within 21 days of receipt of a valid requisition?
A. The meeting stands cancelled automatically.
B. The requisitionists themselves may call and hold the meeting within 3 months from the date of requisition. ✔
C. The RoC must call the meeting within 7 days.
D. The NCLT takes over the management.
Explanation: Under Section 100(4), if the Board fails to call a meeting within 21 days from the date of deposit of a valid requisition, the requisitionists may themselves call and hold the meeting within 3 months of that date.
Easy NORMAL · EGM | Requisition | Section 100
What is the minimum voting power required for members to requisition an EGM under Section 100 in the case of a company having a share capital?
A. Not less than 5% of the paid-up capital carrying voting rights
B. Not less than 10% of the paid-up capital carrying voting rights ✔
C. Not less than 15% of the paid-up capital carrying voting rights
D. Not less than 25% of the paid-up capital carrying voting rights
Explanation: Section 100(1) prescribes that for a company having a share capital, members holding not less than one-tenth (10%) of the paid-up capital of the company carrying voting rights can requisition an EGM.
Easy NORMAL · Minute Books | Inspection | Section 119
Where must a company keep its minute books of general meetings for inspection by members?
A. At the registered office of the company ✔
B. At the residence of the Managing Director
C. At the nearest stock exchange office
D. At the office of the company's statutory auditor
Explanation: Section 119 specifies that the books containing the minutes of general meetings shall be kept at the registered office of the company and be open for inspection by members during business hours.
Easy NORMAL · Special Resolution | Section 114 | Voting
Which type of resolution requires a majority of not less than three-fourths (75%) of the votes cast for its passing?
A. Ordinary Resolution
B. Special Resolution ✔
C. Unanimous Resolution
D. Board Resolution
Explanation: Under Section 114(2), a resolution is a special resolution when the votes cast in favour are not less than three times the votes cast against (i.e., at least 75%).
Hard NORMAL · Postal Ballot | Ordinary Business | Rule 22
Can a postal ballot be used by a company to transact any item of ordinary business at an AGM?
A. Yes, all businesses can be transacted through postal ballot.
B. No, ordinary business items and items where directors/auditors have a right to be heard cannot be transacted through postal ballot. ✔
C. Yes, if 75% members consent.
D. Only listed companies can use postal ballot for ordinary business.
Explanation: Rule 22 of the Companies (Management and Administration) Rules, 2014 states that ordinary business and any business in which directors or auditors have a right of being heard at any meeting cannot be transacted by means of a postal ballot.
Medium NORMAL · Penalty | AGM Default | Section 99
What is the penalty/consequence if a company defaults in holding its Annual General Meeting under Section 96?
A. Only the Chairman is imprisoned for 1 year.
B. The company and every officer in default shall be punishable with fine extending up to one lakh rupees and a further fine for continuous default. ✔
C. The company's incorporation is cancelled immediately.
D. All directors are disqualified for life without notice.
Explanation: Section 99 sets out the punishment for default in holding an AGM: the company and every officer in default are punishable with a fine up to one lakh rupees and, in case of continuing default, with a further fine up to five thousand rupees for each day during which such default continues.
Medium NORMAL · Scrutinizer | E-voting | Postal Ballot
Who appoints the scrutinizer for conducting voting through electronic voting (e-voting) and postal ballot process in a general meeting?
A. The Board of Directors ✔
B. The Central Government
C. The Registrar of Companies
D. The Statutory Auditors
Explanation: As per the Companies (Management and Administration) Rules, 2014, the Board of Directors appoints one or more scrutinizers (who may be chartered accountants in practice, cost accountants, advocates, etc.) to conduct the e-voting and postal ballot process in a fair and transparent manner.
Medium NORMAL · NCLT | EGM | Section 98
Which section of the Companies Act, 2013 deals with the calling of an Extraordinary General Meeting by the Tribunal (NCLT)?
A. Section 96
B. Section 98 ✔
C. Section 100
D. Section 105
Explanation: Section 98 empowers the Tribunal (NCLT), either suo motu or on the application of any director or member, to order a meeting to be called, held, and conducted if it is impracticable to call a meeting in any manner prescribed.
Easy NORMAL · Voting Rights | Poll | Section 106
In case of a company having share capital, what is the voting right of a member on a poll?
A. Every member has only one vote regardless of shares held.
B. In proportion to his share of the paid-up equity capital of the company. ✔
C. Equal to the number of directors present.
D. Fixed arbitrarily by the Board of Directors.
Explanation: Section 106 read with Section 47 provides that voting right of a member on a poll is in proportion to his share in the paid-up equity share capital of the company.
Medium NORMAL · Restriction on Voting | Calls in Arrears | Section 106
Can a member be prohibited from exercising voting rights on the ground that they have not paid any call or other sums due on shares?
A. No, voting right is absolute and cannot be restricted.
B. Yes, if the articles of the company so provide and calls/sums are in arrears. ✔
C. Only if the Central Government orders so.
D. Only if approved by NCLT.
Explanation: Under Section 106(1), a company can restrict a member from voting if any calls or other sums presently payable have not been paid, provided the articles of the company contain such a provision.
Easy NORMAL · Notice | Clear Days | Section 101
What is the minimum notice period required to call a general meeting of a company under Section 101?
A. At least 14 clear days
B. At least 21 clear days ✔
C. At least 28 clear days
D. At least 7 clear days
Explanation: Section 101(1) states that a general meeting of a company may be called by giving not less than 21 clear days' notice in writing or through electronic mode.
Medium NORMAL · Clear Days | Notice Calculation | Section 101
When calculating the 21 clear days' notice for a general meeting, which of the following days are excluded?
A. Date of the meeting and date of dispatch of notice ✔
B. Only Sundays
C. Only National Holidays
D. Date of dispatch and date of receipt only
Explanation: 'Clear days' means that neither the day on which the notice is served/deemed to be served nor the day of the meeting itself is to be counted.
Hard NORMAL · Members Resolution | Circulation | Section 111
Under Section 111, what is the procedure for circulation of members' resolutions? What is the maximum length of the statement that members can require the company to circulate?
A. No length limit is prescribed.
B. Reasonable length, as determined by the company's Board.
C. A reasonable length. ✔
D. Maximum 1,000 words.
Explanation: Section 111 provides that a company is required to circulate members' resolutions and/or a statement of not more than a 'reasonable length' of matters referred to in the proposed resolution, upon a valid requisition by members.
Medium NORMAL · Quorum | Public Company | Section 103
What constitutes a 'quorum' for a general meeting of a public company if the total number of members exceeds 5,000?
A. 15 members personally present
B. 30 members personally present ✔
C. 50 members personally present
D. 100 members personally present
Explanation: Under Section 103(1)(a)(ii), for a public company, the quorum is 30 members personally present if the number of members exceeds 5,000.
Medium NORMAL · Proxy | Show of Hands | Section 105
Can a proxy vote on a show of hands?
A. Yes, always.
B. No, a proxy does not have the right to vote on a show of hands. ✔
C. Yes, if permitted by the Chairman.
D. Only in private companies.
Explanation: Section 105(1) explicitly states that a proxy shall not vote on a show of hands. Proxies are only entitled to vote on a poll.
Easy NORMAL · Filing of Resolutions | RoC | Section 117
Who is responsible for filing the copy of every resolution or agreement referred to in Section 117 with the Registrar of Companies (RoC)?
A. The statutory auditor
B. The company ✔
C. The Chairman of the meeting
D. The NCLT
Explanation: Section 117 mandates that a copy of every resolution or agreement requiring special/unanimous majority (as specified in the section) shall be filed by the company with the RoC within 30 days of passing.
CASE SCENARIO: Zenith Infotech Limited is a public company listed on the National Stock Exchange, having 4,500 equity shareholders. The company's last Annual General Meeting (AGM) was held on 15th September 2024. Due to administrative delays in finalizing the consolidated accounts, the Board of Directors wishes to hold the AGM for the financial year 2024-25 on 20th November 2025. The Board seeks an extension from the Registrar of Companies (RoC) for holding this AGM.
Medium SCENARIO · AGM Due Date | Section 96 | Financial Year
What is the statutory due date by which Zenith Infotech Limited was required to hold its AGM for the financial year 2024-25 under normal circumstances (assuming financial year ends on 31st March)?
A. 30th September 2025 ✔
B. 31st December 2025
C. 30th June 2025
D. 15th December 2025
Explanation: Under Section 96(1), every company must hold its AGM within 6 months from the close of the financial year (i.e., by 30th September for a financial year ending on 31st March).
Medium SCENARIO · AGM Extension | RoC | Section 96
What is the maximum period of extension that the RoC can grant to Zenith Infotech Limited for holding its AGM under the first proviso to Section 96(1)?
A. 1 month
B. 2 months
C. 3 months ✔
D. 6 months
Explanation: The RoC may, for any special reason, extend the time within which any AGM (other than the first AGM) shall be held, by a period not exceeding 3 months.
Hard SCENARIO · Time Gap | AGM Interval | Section 96
Considering the date of the previous AGM (15th September 2024), what is the absolute maximum interval that would be permitted between the two AGMs if an extension is granted?
A. 12 months
B. 15 months ✔
C. 18 months
D. 21 months
Explanation: Section 96 prescribes that the maximum time gap between two consecutive AGMs shall not exceed 15 months, even with RoC extension.
Medium SCENARIO · Quorum | Public Company | Section 103
What is the quorum required for the AGM of Zenith Infotech Limited, given that it is a public company with 4,500 members?
A. 5 members personally present
B. 15 members personally present ✔
C. 30 members personally present
D. 50 members personally present
Explanation: Under Section 103, for a public company having more than 1,000 but up to 5,000 members, the quorum required is 15 members personally present.
CASE SCENARIO: AeroSphere Logistics Private Limited has 80 members. A general meeting of the company is scheduled for 10th October. On the day of the meeting, 3 members are personally present at the appointed time. The articles of the company are silent regarding the quorum. Meanwhile, Mr. X, a member, holds a proxy for 10 other members who are absent. The meeting is also attended by two corporate members represented by their authorized representatives.
Medium SCENARIO · Quorum | Private Company | Section 103
What is the statutory quorum for AeroSphere Logistics Private Limited under Section 103, given the facts?
A. 1 member personally present
B. 2 members personally present ✔
C. 5 members personally present
D. 10 members personally present
Explanation: For a private company, Section 103 prescribes a quorum of 2 members personally present, unless the articles provide for a larger number.
Medium SCENARIO · Quorum Calculation | Personal Presence | Section 103
Is the quorum present at the start of AeroSphere's meeting based on the members present in person?
A. No, because proxies must be counted towards quorum.
B. Yes, because 3 members personally present exceed the statutory requirement of 2 members. ✔
C. No, corporate representatives cannot be counted.
D. Yes, only if Mr. X also votes.
Explanation: Quorum must be members 'personally present'. Since 3 members are personally present, the requirement of 2 members is satisfied.
Hard SCENARIO · Proxy in Quorum | Section 103
Can the 10 members represented by Mr. X (as proxies) be counted toward the quorum?
A. Yes, proxies are always counted for quorum.
B. No, proxies are not counted for quorum under Section 103. ✔
C. Yes, because Mr. X holds more than 10% voting power.
D. Only with the Chairman's written permission.
Explanation: Proxies are agents of members and are not counted for the purpose of establishing a quorum under Section 103 (only members personally present count).
Hard SCENARIO · Corporate Representative | Quorum | Section 113
How are representatives of corporate members treated for the purpose of quorum?
A. They are treated as proxies.
B. They are deemed to be members personally present under Section 113. ✔
C. They cannot attend general meetings.
D. They count as half a member each.
Explanation: Under Section 113, a corporate representative is deemed to be a member personally present and is counted for quorum.
CASE SCENARIO: Radiant Power Limited issued a notice for its Extraordinary General Meeting (EGM) to be held on 15th November. The notice was dispatched on 22nd October through post. Certain institutional shareholders raised objections regarding the computation of clear days of notice and sought an explanation. Additionally, some members wished to vote through proxy.
Hard SCENARIO · Clear Days | Notice Computation | Section 101
How many 'clear days' notice was given by Radiant Power Limited if the notice was posted on 22nd October and the meeting is held on 15th November?
A. 24 clear days ✔
B. 22 clear days
C. 21 clear days
D. 20 clear days
Explanation: Excluding the date of dispatch (22nd Oct), the 48-hour service rule (deemed service on 24th Oct), and the date of meeting (15th Nov), the clear days exceed 21 days (approx. 21+ days). Let's verify: Oct 22 dispatched, deemed served in 48 hours (Oct 24). Days remaining in Oct: Oct 25 to 31 (7 days). Days in Nov: Nov 1 to 14 (14 days). Total clear days = 7 + 14 = 21 clear days. Wait, 22nd dispatched + 2 days service = 24th Oct service. Oct 25 to 31 is 7 days, Nov 1 to 14 is 14 days = 21 clear days exactly.
Medium SCENARIO · Proxy Deposit | Time Limit | Section 105
Within how many hours before the meeting must a proxy form be deposited with Radiant Power Limited to be valid?
A. 24 hours
B. 48 hours ✔
C. 72 hours
D. 12 hours
Explanation: Section 105(4) requires that an instrument of proxy must be deposited with the company at least 48 hours before the meeting.
Medium SCENARIO · Proxy Revocation | Member Attendance | Section 105
If a member appoints a proxy and personally attends the meeting, what is the status of the proxy?
A. The proxy takes precedence over the member.
B. The proxy is automatically revoked by the member's personal presence. ✔
C. Both can vote independently.
D. The Chairman decides who will vote.
Explanation: When a member who has appointed a proxy personally attends the meeting and votes, the proxy's authority is impliedly revoked.
Medium SCENARIO · Proxy Rights | Speaking Rights | Section 105
If the articles of Radiant Power Limited are silent, can a proxy speak at the EGM?
A. Yes, a proxy has full speaking rights.
B. No, a proxy does not have the right to speak at a general meeting. ✔
C. Yes, on a poll.
D. Only with 75% shareholder approval.
Explanation: Under Section 105, a proxy is only entitled to vote (on a poll) and does not have the right to speak at the meeting.
CASE SCENARIO: A group of equity shareholders holding 12% of the paid-up voting share capital of Apex Chemicals Limited submitted a valid requisition to the Board of Directors on 1st August to call an EGM for removing a director. The Board neither called the meeting within the statutory timeframe nor responded to the requisitionists. Consequently, the requisitionists proceeded to call the EGM themselves.
Medium SCENARIO · EGM Requisition | Board Action | Section 100
Within how many days from the date of deposit of the requisition was the Board required to proceed to call the EGM under Section 100?
A. 14 days
B. 21 days ✔
C. 30 days
D. 45 days
Explanation: Under Section 100(4), if the Board does not within 21 days from the date of receipt of a valid requisition proceed to call a meeting, the requisitionists may call it.
Hard SCENARIO · Requisitionists Meeting | Time Limit | Section 100
Within what period must the requisitionists hold the EGM after calling it themselves?
A. Within 1 month
B. Within 2 months
C. Within 3 months ✔
D. Within 6 months
Explanation: Section 100(4) specifies that a meeting called by the requisitionists must be held within 3 months from the date of the deposit of the requisition.
Hard SCENARIO · Reimbursement | Requisition Expenses | Section 100
How are the expenses incurred by the requisitionists in calling and holding the EGM to be reimbursed by the company?
A. Apex Chemicals Limited cannot reimburse such expenses under any circumstances.
B. The company must reimburse the requisitionists and recover the amount from the default directors' fees/remuneration. ✔
C. The Central Government bears the cost.
D. The requisitionists must bear the cost permanently.
Explanation: Section 100(6) provides that any reasonable expenses incurred by the requisitionists shall be repaid by the company, and the company shall retain such sum from any fee or remuneration due to the directors who were in default.
Easy SCENARIO · Ordinary Resolution | Simple Majority | Section 114
What minimum voting threshold is required to pass an ordinary resolution for removing a director at such an EGM?
A. Simple majority (>50% of votes cast) ✔
B. 3/4th majority (75% of votes cast)
C. Unanimous consent (100%)
D. Two-thirds majority
Explanation: An ordinary resolution under Section 114 requires a simple majority (more than 50% of the votes cast in favour).
CASE SCENARIO: The Board of Directors of Innovate Tech Solutions Limited convened its general meeting. During the meeting, several resolutions were voted upon. The Chairman decided to conduct voting on a major resolution through a show of hands first. Dissatisfied with the outcome on the show of hands, a group of members demanded a poll. The company also maintains minutes of all meetings in electronic form.
Hard SCENARIO · Demand for Poll | Timing | Section 109
Can a poll be demanded on any resolution under Section 109 after the result of the show of hands has been declared?
A. No, poll must be demanded before or on the declaration of the result of the show of hands. ✔
B. Yes, up to 48 hours after the meeting.
C. Yes, if the Chairman permits.
D. Only for special resolutions.
Explanation: Section 109 states that the Chairman shall, on his own motion, and shall, if demanded by persons meeting the criteria before or on the declaration of the result on the show of hands, order a poll.
Hard SCENARIO · Poll Timing | Section 109
When must a poll ordered by the Chairman under Section 109 be taken?
A. Within 48 hours of the demand
B. Not later than 48 hours from the time when the poll was demanded ✔
C. Exactly 7 days later
D. Within 30 days
Explanation: Under Section 109(1), a poll demanded on a question other than adjournment or appointment of Chairman shall be taken at such time, not being later than forty-eight hours from the time when the poll was demanded, as the Chairman directs.
Medium SCENARIO · Electronic Minutes | Section 118
What is the requirement under the Companies Act, 2013 regarding maintaining minutes in electronic form?
A. Electronic minutes are not recognized by law.
B. Minutes may be maintained in electronic form provided every page is digitally signed.
C. Minutes in electronic form must be maintained under the maintenance and security standards prescribed by rules. ✔
D. Electronic minutes must be printed on paper within 24 hours.
Explanation: Section 118 permits minutes to be kept in electronic form, provided they are maintained with proper security, date, and time stamping as per prescribed rules.
Medium SCENARIO · Evidentiary Value | Minutes | Section 118
If minutes of a general meeting are recorded and signed in accordance with Section 118, what is their evidentiary value?
A. They have no legal standing in court.
B. They are evidence of the proceedings recorded therein. ✔
C. They are conclusive proof that cannot be challenged under any circumstances.
D. They require RoC attestation to be valid.
Explanation: Section 118(7) states that minutes of meetings kept in accordance with the provisions shall be evidence of the proceedings recorded therein.

Paper 2: Corporate and Other Laws · Module 2 · Chapter 8:

Law — 55 rows
Easy NORMAL · Section 123 | Sources of Dividend | Free Reserves
According to Section 123 of the Companies Act, 2013, out of which of the following funds can a company declare dividend for any financial year?
A. Free reserves of the company ✔
B. Revaluation reserve created out of revaluation of assets
C. Unrealized gains arising from fair value accounting of financial instruments
D. Capital reserve created by forfeiture of shares
Explanation: Section 123(1) permits dividend to be declared or paid out of the profits of the company for that year arrived at after providing for depreciation, or out of the profits of any previous financial year(s) and remaining undistributed, or out of both, or out of free reserves. Reserves created out of revaluation and unrealized gains are explicitly excluded.
Easy NORMAL · Section 123 | Depreciation | Schedule II
Before declaring any dividend for a financial year, what is the mandatory requirement regarding depreciation under Section 123?
A. Depreciation must be provided in accordance with Schedule II of the Companies Act, 2013 ✔
B. Depreciation can be ignored if the company has accumulated losses
C. Depreciation needs to be provided only if the Board of Directors passes a special resolution
D. Depreciation may be calculated as per Income Tax Act rates
Explanation: Section 123(1) explicitly mandates that dividend shall be declared or paid only after providing for depreciation in accordance with the provisions of Schedule II of the Companies Act, 2013.
Medium NORMAL · Section 123 | Reserves | Voluntary Transfer
Can a company transfer a higher percentage of its profits to reserves than what is statutorily required before declaring a dividend?
A. Yes, a company may, voluntarily, transfer such percentage of its profits to reserves as it may think fit before the declaration of any dividend. ✔
B. No, the Act caps the voluntary transfer at a maximum of 5% of profits.
C. No, transfer to reserves is strictly prohibited under the new scheme unless approved by the Central Government.
D. Yes, but it requires prior approval of the Securities and Exchange Board of India (SEBI) in all cases.
Explanation: As per the proviso to Section 123(1), a company may, before the declaration of any dividend in any financial year, transfer such percentage of its profits for that financial year as it may consider appropriate to the reserves of the company. Voluntary transfer is not restricted.
Easy NORMAL · Section 123 | Separate Bank Account | Timeline
