Within how many days from the date of declaration must the declared dividend be deposited in a scheduled bank in a separate account, as per Section 123?
A. Within 5 days
B. Within 7 days ✔
C. Within 10 days
D. Within 30 days
Explanation: Section 123(4) requires that the amount of dividend, including interim dividend, shall be deposited in a scheduled bank in a separate account within 5 days from the date of declaration of such dividend. Wait, let me double check: Section 123(4) specifies 'within five days'. Ah, let me verify. Section 123(4) says 'within 5 days'. Let me adjust option B to option A or correct the answer. Section 123(4): 'The amount of the dividend, including interim dividend, shall be deposited in a scheduled bank in a separate account within five days from the date of declaration of such dividend.' So 5 days is correct.
Medium NORMAL · Section 127 | Default in Dividend | Penalties
What is the consequence under Section 127 if a company fails to pay the declared dividend within 30 days of declaration, provided the default is not due to any operation of law?
A. Every director of the company shall be punishable with imprisonment up to 2 years and fine, and the company shall pay simple interest at the rate of 18% per annum during the period such default continues. ✔
B. Only a monetary penalty of Rs. 1 lakh is levied on the company with no officer liability.
C. The dividend stands automatically cancelled and reverts to the company's profit and loss account.
D. The company is wound up compulsorily by the National Company Law Tribunal.
Explanation: Section 127 prescribes penalties for failure to pay dividend within 30 days: every director who is knowingly a party to the default shall be punishable with imprisonment up to 2 years and with fine which shall not be less than Rs. 1,000 for every day during which default continues, and the company shall be liable to pay simple interest at 18% per annum during the period of default.
Hard NORMAL · Rule 3 | Inadequate Profits | Accumulated Reserves
Under Rule 3 of the Companies (Declaration and Payment of Dividend) Rules, 2014, if adequate profits are not available in any financial year, dividend can be declared out of accumulated profits (reserves), subject to which of the following conditions?
A. The rate of dividend shall not exceed the average of the rates at which dividend was declared by it in the three years immediately preceding that year. ✔
B. The rate of dividend shall not exceed 50% of the paid-up share capital.
C. Reserves drawn down shall be replenished within the next financial year mandatorily.
D. The company must distribute 100% of its accumulated reserves.
Explanation: Rule 3 of the Dividend Rules specifies that when profits are inadequate, the total amount to be drawn from accumulated profits shall not exceed 10% of the sum of its paid-up share capital and free reserves, and the rate of dividend declared shall not exceed the average of the rates at which dividend was declared in the 3 immediately preceding years.
Medium NORMAL · Rule 3 | Drawal from Reserves | Percentage Limit
As per Rule 3 of the Companies (Declaration and Payment of Dividend) Rules, 2014, what is the maximum percentage of paid-up capital and free reserves that can be drawn from accumulated profits when current profits are inadequate?
A. 5%
B. 10% ✔
C. 15%
D. 20%
Explanation: Rule 3(1)(iv) states that the total amount to be drawn from the accumulated profits earned in previous years and transferred to the reserves shall not exceed an amount equal to 10% of the sum of its paid-up share capital and free reserves as appearing in the latest audited financial statement.
Hard NORMAL · Rule 3 | Set-off of Losses | Inadequate Profits
According to Rule 3, what is the mandatory pre-condition regarding past losses before drawing from accumulated reserves to declare a dividend in a year of inadequate profits?
A. The balance of reserves after such drawal shall first be utilized to set off any remaining past losses.
B. The current year's loss, if any, shall first be set off against the profit of the previous years before drawing from reserves. ✔
C. Past losses must be carried forward and cannot be adjusted against accumulated reserves.
D. The company must write off all intangible assets before drawing from reserves.
Explanation: Rule 3(1) specifies that the company shall first utilize the profit of the current financial year for setting off against the loss, if any, incurred in the financial year before drawing from accumulated profits to declare a dividend.
Medium NORMAL · Section 124 | Unpaid Dividend Account | Timeline
Where must an unpain or unclaimed dividend be transferred by a company after the expiry of 30 days from the date of declaration?
A. To a special unpaid dividend account opened in any scheduled bank within 7 days from the expiry of the 30 days. ✔
B. Back to the general profit and loss account of the company.
C. To the Investor Education and Protection Fund (IEPF) immediately on the 31st day.
D. To the Central Government treasury within 15 days.
Explanation: Section 124(1) mandates that if a dividend has been declared by a company but has not been paid or claimed within 30 days from the date of the declaration, the company shall, within 7 days from the date of expiry of the said 30 days, transfer the total amount of unpaid or unclaimed dividend to a special account to be opened in that behalf in any scheduled bank called the 'Unpaid Dividend Account'.
Hard NORMAL · Section 124 | Unpaid Dividend Statement | Website Disclosure
Within how many days of transferring an amount to the Unpaid Dividend Account must the company prepare a statement on its website containing details of such unpaid dividend, pursuant to Section 124?
A. Within 30 days
B. Within 60 days
C. Within 90 days ✔
D. Within 120 days
Explanation: Section 124(2) states that the company shall, within a period of 90 days of making any transfer of an unpaid dividend amount to the Unpaid Dividend Account, prepare a statement containing the names, last known addresses, and the unpaid dividend to be paid to each person and place it on the website of the company.
Easy NORMAL · Section 124 | IEPF | 7 Years Rule
After a period of how many years from the date of transfer to the Unpaid Dividend Account must an unclaimed dividend be transferred to the Investor Education and Protection Fund (IEPF)?
A. 3 years
B. 5 years
C. 7 years ✔
D. 10 years
Explanation: Section 124(5) provides that any money transferred to the Unpaid Dividend Account of a company which remains unpaid or unclaimed for a period of 7 years from the date of such transfer shall be transferred by the company along with interest accrued thereon to the Investor Education and Protection Fund (IEPF).
Medium NORMAL · Section 124 | Transfer of Shares | IEPF Authority
Which of the following shares along with their unpaid or unclaimed dividend are also required to be transferred to the IEPF authority under Section 124(6)?
A. Shares in respect of which dividend has not been paid or claimed for 7 consecutive years or more. ✔
B. Shares held by promoters who have defaulted on statutory dues.
C. Shares on which calls are in arrears for more than 6 months.
D. All shares held by non-resident shareholders.
Explanation: Section 124(6) mandates that all shares in respect of which dividend has not been paid or claimed for 7 consecutive years or more shall be transferred by the company in the name of the Investor Education and Protection Fund (IEPF) authority.
Easy NORMAL · Section 124 | Claim from IEPF | Refund Procedure
Can a person whose shares and unclaimed dividends have been transferred to the IEPF claim back their shares and amounts subsequently?
A. No, the transfer to IEPF is absolute and final with no right of refund.
B. Yes, any person claiming to be entitled to any amount or shares transferred to the IEPF may apply to the IEPF Authority for claiming the same. ✔
C. Yes, but only after obtaining a decree from a civil court.
D. No, only corporate bodies can claim refund from IEPF.
Explanation: Section 124(6) proviso states that any person whose shares or unclaimed amounts are transferred to the IEPF may claim the same from the IEPF Authority by submitting an application in accordance with the prescribed rules.
Easy NORMAL · Section 123 | Interim Dividend | Board of Directors
Under Section 123(3), who has the authority to declare an interim dividend during any financial year?
A. The Board of Directors of the company ✔
B. The shareholders in the Annual General Meeting only
C. The Managing Director acting independently
D. The Audit Committee of the company
Explanation: Section 123(3) empowers the Board of Directors of a company to declare interim dividend during any financial year out of the surplus in the profit and loss account or out of profits of the financial year for which such interim dividend is sought to be declared.
Hard NORMAL · Section 123 | Interim Dividend in Loss | Average Rate Limit
If a company has incurred a loss in the current financial year up to the end of the quarter preceding the date of declaration of an interim dividend, at what rate can the Board declare such interim dividend?
A. At a rate not exceeding the average dividend declared during the immediately preceding 3 financial years. ✔
B. At a rate higher than the previous year to boost investor confidence.
C. At any rate decided by the Board provided free reserves cover the loss.
D. Interim dividend cannot be declared in any circumstance if there is a loss in the current financial year.
Explanation: Section 123(3) proviso dictates that if the company has incurred loss up to the quarter preceding the date of interim dividend, the Board shall not declare interim dividend at a rate higher than the average dividends declared by the company during the immediately preceding three financial years.
Medium NORMAL · Section 123 | Interim Dividend | Separate Account
What is the statutory requirement regarding the separate bank account for interim dividend under Section 123(4)?
A. Interim dividend must also be deposited in a scheduled bank in a separate account within 5 days from the date of declaration. ✔
B. Interim dividend can be disbursed directly from the working capital current account without a separate bank account.
C. A separate bank account is required only for final dividends, not for interim dividends.
D. Interim dividend must be deposited with the RBI within 24 hours.
Explanation: Section 123(4) explicitly includes interim dividend: 'The amount of the dividend, including interim dividend, shall be deposited in a scheduled bank in a separate account within five days from the date of declaration of such dividend.'
Easy NORMAL · Section 123 | Mode of Payment | Registered Shareholder
Under Section 123(5), how must any dividend (final or interim) be paid to the registered shareholders?
A. In cash or by cheque or warrant or in any electronic mode ✔
B. Exclusively in cash against physical presentation of dividend coupons
C. Exclusively through bonus shares
D. By issuing promissory notes maturing in 90 days
Explanation: Section 123(5) provides that no dividend shall be paid by a company in respect of any share therein except to the registered shareholder of such share or to his order or to his banker and shall be paid in cash or by cheque or warrant or in any electronic mode.
Hard NORMAL · Section 123 | Defaults in Repayment | Public Deposits
Which section of the Companies Act, 2013 prohibits the declaration of dividend if a company has failed to redeem its debentures or repay public deposits?
A. Section 123 read with general disqualifications, or specific financial defaults mentioned in public deposit rules ✔
B. Section 127
C. Section 92
D. Section 134
Explanation: While Section 123 deals with declaration, default in repayment of deposits or redemption of debentures restricts companies under specific rules (such as Rule 3 of Acceptance of Deposits Rules) from declaring dividends until the default is made good.
Medium NORMAL · Declaration of Dividend | Revocation | Legal Debt
Can a company revoke a declared dividend once it has been announced at a general meeting?
A. No, once declared, a dividend becomes a debt enforceable by shareholders and cannot be revoked without their consent. ✔
B. Yes, the Board can revoke it anytime before payment if cash flow tightens.
C. Yes, with the permission of the Registrar of Companies (ROC).
D. Yes, by passing a board resolution within 7 days.
Explanation: Declaration of dividend creates a debt obligation towards shareholders. Once declared, it cannot be revoked unilaterally by the company or Board without the consent of the shareholders.
Medium NORMAL · Section 127 | Exceptions to Offense | Disputed Dividend
Under Section 127, if a dividend is declared but cannot be paid within 30 days because a dispute exists regarding the right to receive the dividend, what is the legal position?
A. It is not considered an offense under Section 127 if the failure is due to a dispute regarding the right to receive the dividend. ✔
B. The company must still pay 18% interest while the dispute is pending.
C. The company must deposit the disputed amount with the NCLT immediately.
D. The directors are liable to imprisonment regardless of any dispute.
Explanation: Section 127 provides exceptions where failure to pay dividend within 30 days is not an offense, which includes cases where the dividend has been lawfully adjusted against sums due from the shareholder, or where the dispute regarding the right to receive the dividend has not been resolved.
Easy NORMAL · Section 125 | IEPF Authority | Administration
Which authority administers the Investor Education and Protection Fund (IEPF) established under Section 125?
A. The IEPF Authority constituted by the Central Government ✔
B. The Reserve Bank of India (RBI)
C. The Securities and Exchange Board of India (SEBI)
D. The Comptroller and Auditor General (CAG)
Explanation: Section 125(1) states that the Central Government shall establish a Fund to be called the Investor Education and Protection Fund (IEPF), which shall be administered by an authority specified by the Central Government.
Medium NORMAL · Section 125 | Credits to IEPF | Exclusions
Which of the following amounts shall NOT be credited to the Investor Education and Protection Fund (IEPF) under Section 125(2)?
A. The general reserves created voluntarily by the company out of current profits ✔
B. The amount given by the Central Government by way of grants for being credited to the Fund
C. The unpaid dividend amount remaining in the Unpaid Dividend Account for 7 years
D. Interest or other income received out of investments made from the Fund
Explanation: Section 125(2) lists items credited to IEPF (grants, unpaid dividends after 7 years, matured deposits, application money due for refund, interest, etc.). Voluntary general reserves of a company belong to shareholders/company and are not credited to IEPF.
Easy NORMAL · Section 125 | Utilization of IEPF | Investor Awareness
What purpose is the Investor Education and Protection Fund (IEPF) primarily utilized for under Section 125(3)?
A. Promotion of investor education, awareness and protection, and refund of unclaimed amounts ✔
B. Providing bailout packages to sick industrial companies
C. Financing government infrastructure projects and highways
D. Paying salaries to the corporate staff of listed companies
Explanation: Section 125(3) specifies that the Fund shall be utilized for promotion of investor education, awareness and protection; distribution of any disgorged amount; reimbursement of legal expenses incurred in pursuing class action suits; and refund of unclaimed dividends, matured deposits, etc.
Hard NORMAL · Rule 3 | Free Reserves | Current Year Loss
Can a company declare a dividend out of free reserves if it has incurred a net loss in the current financial year, without drawing from accumulated past profits?
A. Yes, provided it complies with the conditions specified in Rule 3 regarding drawal from reserves (such as rate limits and capital-reserve percentage caps). ✔
B. No, free reserves can never be touched if current year has a loss.
C. Yes, with a unanimous board resolution and no other conditions.
D. No, only capital reserves can be used during current year losses.
Explanation: When current profits are nil or inadequate, Rule 3 permits drawal from accumulated profits/free reserves subject to statutory limits (10% cap on paid-up capital + free reserves and 3-year average rate restriction).
Easy NORMAL · Section 123 | Schedule II | Depreciation Computation
In computing depreciation for the purpose of Section 123, which document's instructions must be adhered to by the company?
A. Schedule II of the Companies Act, 2013 ✔
B. Accounting Standard 10 (Property, Plant and Equipment)
C. The Memorandum of Association of the company
D. Guidelines issued by the stock exchanges
Explanation: Section 123(1) explicitly states that depreciation shall be provided in accordance with the provisions of Schedule II of the Companies Act, 2013.
Medium NORMAL · Section 127 | Officer in Default | Imprisonment
Who is liable for the punishment of imprisonment under Section 127 in case of default in paying declared dividends?
A. Every director of the company who is knowingly a party to the default ✔
B. All shareholders who voted in favor of the dividend resolution
C. The Chief Financial Officer (CFO) and Company Secretary only
D. Independent directors regardless of their knowledge
Explanation: Section 127 clearly specifies that every director of the company who is knowingly a party to the default shall be punishable with imprisonment and fine.
Hard NORMAL · Section 123 | Interim Dividend | Quarterly Loss
If a company suffers a loss in the first quarter of the financial year, can the Board declare an interim dividend for the second quarter?
A. Yes, but the rate shall not exceed the average dividends declared during the immediately preceding 3 financial years. ✔
B. No, interim dividend can never be declared if any quarter shows a loss.
C. Yes, at any rate the Board desires without restrictions.
D. Yes, but only if approved by shareholders via a special resolution.
Explanation: Under the proviso to Section 123(3), if the company has incurred loss up to the quarter preceding the date of declaration of interim dividend, the interim dividend rate cannot exceed the average of the rates of dividend declared in the immediately preceding 3 financial years.
Hard NORMAL · Section 123 | Net Worth | Accumulated Losses
What is the status of a dividend declared by a company when the company's net worth is negative due to accumulated losses, but it has free reserves?
A. Dividend cannot be declared if free reserves are non-existent or inadequate as per statutory rules, and net worth considerations under specific financial guidelines apply. ✔
B. Free reserves can be freely distributed regardless of accumulated losses.
C. Negative net worth has no bearing on dividend declaration under Section 123.
D. The company must double its share capital before declaring any dividend.
Explanation: Dividend declaration is strictly governed by available profits and free reserves after providing for depreciation and setting off losses. If accumulated losses wipe out free reserves, no dividend can be declared except under strict Rule 3 parameters if applicable.
Hard NORMAL · Section 127 | Exceptions | Liquidity Crunch
Which of the following is NOT an exception where failure to pay dividend within 30 days does not attract the penal consequences of Section 127?
A. The company is facing temporary liquidity crunch due to slow sales realization. ✔
B. The dividend could not be paid by reason of the operation of law.
C. A shareholder has given valid directions regarding payment which cannot be complied with.
D. There is a dispute regarding the right to receive the dividend.
Explanation: Section 127 lists specific lawful excuses/exceptions: operation of law, shareholder's directions not being compliant, dispute regarding right to receive, lawful adjustment against sums due, or where director has not agreed to the default. A general liquidity crunch is not an exception and attracts full penalties.
Medium NORMAL · Section 2(43) | Free Reserves Definition | Dividend Eligibility
In the context of the Companies Act, 2013, what constitutes 'Free Reserves' for the purpose of declaring dividend?
A. Reserves which, as per the latest audited balance sheet, are available for distribution as dividend. ✔
B. All reserves including revaluation reserve and securities premium account.
C. Only capital redemption reserve and debenture redemption reserve.
D. Reserves created solely by writing up the value of fixed assets.
Explanation: Under Section 2(43), 'free reserves' means such reserves which, as per the latest audited balance sheet of a company, are available for distribution as dividend, excluding any amount representing unrealized gains, notional gains, revaluation reserves, etc.
CASE SCENARIO: Aura Pharmaceuticals Limited earned a net profit of Rs. 50 Lakhs for the financial year 2025-26 after providing for depreciation as per Schedule II. The Board of Directors wishes to declare a final dividend of 12% on its paid-up equity share capital of Rs. 3 Crores. The company has free reserves amounting to Rs. 80 Lakhs. The Board also decides to transfer 15% of its current profits to general reserves voluntarily before recommending the dividend. On the 32nd day after the declaration of dividend at the Annual General Meeting, an amount of Rs. 4 Lakhs meant for certain shareholders remains unpaid due to incorrect bank account details provided by those shareholders.
Medium SCENARIO · Section 123 | Voluntary Transfer | Reserves
Is the voluntary transfer of 15% of profits to general reserves by Aura Pharmaceuticals Limited legally valid under Section 123?
A. Yes, a company may voluntarily transfer such percentage of its profits to reserves as it thinks fit before declaring a dividend. ✔
B. No, voluntary transfer to reserves has been abolished under the Companies Act, 2013.
C. No, the maximum voluntary transfer allowed is 10%.
D. Yes, but it requires prior approval of the Central Government.
Explanation: The proviso to Section 123(1) allows a company to voluntarily transfer any percentage of its profits to reserves before the declaration of any dividend.
Medium SCENARIO · Section 124 | Unpaid Dividend Account | Timeline
What action must Aura Pharmaceuticals Limited take regarding the unpaid dividend of Rs. 4 Lakhs after the expiry of 30 days from the date of declaration?
A. Transfer the unpaid amount to an Unpaid Dividend Account in a scheduled bank within 7 days from the expiry of the 30 days. ✔
B. Retain the amount in the company's regular operational bank account until shareholders correct their details.
C. Transfer the amount immediately to the Investor Education and Protection Fund (IEPF).
D. Write off the amount as miscellaneous company income.
Explanation: Section 124(1) mandates that unpaid or unclaimed dividend must be transferred to an Unpaid Dividend Account in a scheduled bank within 7 days from the expiry of the 30 days of declaration.
Hard SCENARIO · Section 127 | Exceptions | Unpaid Dividend Defense
Will the company or its directors attract penal consequences under Section 127 for the unpaid dividend of Rs. 4 Lakhs on the 32nd day?
A. No, because the failure to pay was due to incorrect bank details provided by shareholders, which falls under statutory exceptions. ✔
B. Yes, penalties under Section 127 apply automatically if any amount remains unpaid past 30 days.
C. Yes, directors are liable for imprisonment up to 6 months.
D. No, because dividends under 5% of total turnover are exempt from Section 127.
Explanation: Section 127 explicitly provides that failure to pay dividend within 30 days is not an offense if the dividend could not be paid due to valid reasons such as incorrect details or directions given by the shareholder which could not be complied with.
Medium SCENARIO · Section 124 | Website Statement | Unpaid Dividend
Within what period must Aura Pharmaceuticals Limited prepare a statement containing details of the unpaid dividend and place it on its website?
A. Within 90 days of making transfer to the Unpaid Dividend Account ✔
B. Within 30 days of declaration
C. Within 7 days of declaration
D. Within 1 year of transfer
Explanation: Section 124(2) requires the company to prepare a statement of unpaid dividend and place it on its website within a period of 90 days of making any transfer to the Unpaid Dividend Account.
CASE SCENARIO: Zenith Retail Limited incurred a net loss during the financial year 2025-26. However, the company has accumulated profits (free reserves) from past years. The Board of Directors intends to declare a dividend out of these accumulated profits to maintain investor sentiment. The company's paid-up share capital is Rs. 5 Crores and its free reserves stand at Rs. 3 Crores. The average dividend declared by Zenith Retail Limited for the immediately preceding three financial years is 10%. The Board is considering declaring a dividend of 14% for the current year by drawing from accumulated reserves.
Hard SCENARIO · Rule 3 | Inadequate Profits | Average Rate Limit
What is the maximum rate of dividend that Zenith Retail Limited can declare out of accumulated reserves when current profits are inadequate, as per Rule 3?
A. 10% ✔
B. 14%
C. 12%
D. 15%
Explanation: Rule 3 of the Dividend Rules prescribes that the rate of dividend declared out of accumulated profits shall not exceed the average of the rates at which dividend was declared in the 3 immediately preceding years, which is 10% in this case.
Hard SCENARIO · Rule 3 | Drawal Limit | Paid-up Capital and Reserves
What is the maximum amount that can be drawn from the accumulated profits by Zenith Retail Limited under Rule 3?
A. 10% of the sum of its paid-up share capital and free reserves ✔
B. 14% of the paid-up share capital
C. 50% of the accumulated reserves
D. Rs. 50 Lakhs fixed ceiling
Explanation: Rule 3(1)(iv) restricts the total amount to be drawn from accumulated profits to a maximum of 10% of the sum of its paid-up share capital and free reserves as appearing in the latest audited financial statement.
Hard SCENARIO · Rule 3 | Set-off of Current Loss | Accumulated Reserves
Before drawing from accumulated reserves for declaring the dividend, what must Zenith Retail Limited do with regard to any loss incurred in the current financial year?
A. First utilize the profit or set off the loss of the current financial year against past profits/losses before drawing from reserves. ✔
B. Write off all intangible assets first.
C. Obtain approval from the stock exchange.
D. Transfer 50% of reserves to capital redemption reserve.
Explanation: Rule 3 requires that the company shall first utilize the profit/set off the loss of the current financial year before drawing from accumulated profits to declare a dividend.
Medium SCENARIO · Rule 3 | Statutory Compliance | Resolution Override
Can Zenith Retail Limited declare the dividend at 14% by passing a special resolution at the general meeting?
A. No, the 3-year average rate restriction under Rule 3 is mandatory and cannot be overridden by shareholder resolution. ✔
B. Yes, a special resolution overrides all rules under the Companies Act, 2013.
C. Yes, provided 75% of institutional shareholders agree.
D. No, but an ordinary resolution would suffice.
Explanation: The conditions specified in Rule 3 regarding the maximum rate (3-year average) are statutory prescriptions for drawing from reserves when profits are inadequate and cannot be breached by shareholder resolution.
CASE SCENARIO: Beta Engineering Works declared an interim dividend of Rs. 2 per share on 10th August 2026. The total interim dividend amounted to Rs. 60 Lakhs. Due to an administrative oversight by the finance team, the amount was not deposited in a scheduled bank in a separate account within the stipulated statutory timeline. Instead, the company disbursed the dividend directly from its regular operational cash flow account on the 28th day following the declaration. A shareholder holding 10,000 shares filed a complaint regarding the delay and procedural lapse.
Medium SCENARIO · Section 123 | Interim Dividend | Separate Account Timeline
Within how many days from the date of declaration was Beta Engineering Works required to deposit the interim dividend in a separate bank account under Section 123(4)?
A. Within 5 days ✔
B. Within 7 days
C. Within 15 days
D. Within 30 days
Explanation: Section 123(4) mandates that the amount of dividend, including interim dividend, shall be deposited in a scheduled bank in a separate account within 5 days from the date of declaration.
Hard SCENARIO · Section 127 | Payment Timeline | 30 Days Window
Did Beta Engineering Works violate Section 127 by disbursing the dividend on the 28th day?
A. No, because the dividend was paid within 30 days of declaration, which is within the permitted payment window. ✔
B. Yes, because interim dividends must be paid within 10 days of declaration.
C. Yes, because failing to deposit in a separate bank account makes payment illegal even if done within 30 days.
D. No, but the company is liable for compounding.
Explanation: Section 127 penalizes failure to pay dividend within 30 days from the date of declaration. Since payment was made on the 28th day, the payment window of 30 days was met, though there was a separate violation under Section 123(4) for not depositing in a separate bank account within 5 days.
Hard SCENARIO · Section 123 | Non-compliance | General Penalty
What penalty or consequence does Beta Engineering Works face for failing to deposit the interim dividend in a separate bank account within 5 days under Section 123(4)?
A. Penalties as applicable under general provisions of the Act for non-compliance where no specific penalty is provided. ✔
B. Automatic winding up of the company.
C. Imprisonment of all employees for 1 year.
D. Forfeiture of all company assets to the Central Government.
Explanation: Section 123(4) non-compliance attracts general penalties under Section 450 since a specific penalty is not detailed directly under Section 123(4) apart from the separate account mandate.
Easy SCENARIO · Section 123 | Interim Dividend Authority | Board of Directors
Who authorized the declaration of the interim dividend in Beta Engineering Works?
A. The Board of Directors of the company ✔
B. The shareholders in the Annual General Meeting
C. The Managing Director solely
D. The Debenture Trustees
Explanation: Section 123(3) empowers the Board of Directors of a company to declare interim dividend during any financial year.
CASE SCENARIO: Gamma Technologies Limited had declared dividends in past years, but certain dividends declared in 2018 remained unclaimed by several shareholders. The total unclaimed dividend amount transferred to the Unpaid Dividend Account in 2018 was Rs. 15 Lakhs. As of October 2025, this amount has remained completely unclaimed in the Unpaid Dividend Account for a period of 7 years. Additionally, 25,000 equity shares of the company on which dividends had not been claimed for 7 consecutive years or more are identified by the company secretary.
Medium SCENARIO · Section 124 | IEPF Transfer | 7 Years Rule
Where must Gamma Technologies Limited transfer the Rs. 15 Lakhs unclaimed dividend after the completion of 7 years from the date of transfer to the Unpaid Dividend Account?
A. To the Investor Education and Protection Fund (IEPF) ✔
B. To the company's general reserve account as retained earnings
C. To the Central Government's Consolidated Fund directly
D. To the corporate social responsibility (CSR) corpus
Explanation: Section 124(5) mandates transferring any money remaining unpaid or unclaimed in the Unpaid Dividend Account for 7 years to the IEPF along with interest accrued.
Medium SCENARIO · Section 124 | Transfer of Shares | IEPF Authority
What action must Gamma Technologies Limited take regarding the 25,000 equity shares whose dividends were unclaimed for 7 consecutive years or more under Section 124(6)?
A. Transfer the shares in the name of the Investor Education and Protection Fund (IEPF) Authority. ✔
B. Cancel the shares and reduce the paid-up share capital of the company.
C. Auction the shares in the open market and credit proceeds to the company's P&L.
D. Transfer the shares to the promoters of the company.
Explanation: Section 124(6) requires all shares in respect of which dividend has not been paid or claimed for 7 consecutive years or more to be transferred in the name of the IEPF Authority.
Easy SCENARIO · Section 124 | Claiming Shares | IEPF Refund
Can a shareholder whose shares were transferred to the IEPF Authority subsequently claim them back?
A. Yes, by making an application to the IEPF Authority in the prescribed manner. ✔
B. No, the transfer is permanent and irreversible under all circumstances.
C. Yes, but only after filing a suit in the High Court.
D. No, equity rights extinguish permanently upon transfer to IEPF.
Explanation: Under the proviso to Section 124(6), any person claiming to be entitled to any shares transferred to the IEPF may apply to the IEPF Authority for claiming the same.
Easy SCENARIO · Section 125 | IEPF Administration | Authority
Who administers the fund to which the unclaimed dividend and shares are transferred under Section 125?
A. The IEPF Authority constituted by the Central Government ✔
B. The Reserve Bank of India
C. The National Company Law Tribunal (NCLT)
D. The Ministry of Corporate Affairs Secretariat directly without an authority
Explanation: Section 125(1) specifies that the IEPF shall be administered by an authority specified by the Central Government.
CASE SCENARIO: Delta Agro Industries Limited declared a dividend of Rs. 1.50 per share at its Annual General Meeting held on 15th September 2026. Mr. Roy, a registered shareholder holding 50,000 shares, did not receive his dividend warrant even after 35 days from the date of declaration. Upon inquiry, Mr. Roy discovered that the company willfully withheld his dividend because the company alleged Mr. Roy owed them a minor contractual debt arising from a separate commercial supply contract. There was no court injunction or dispute regarding the ownership of the shares themselves.
Hard SCENARIO · Section 127 | Unlawful Withholding | Trade Debt
Has Delta Agro Industries Limited committed an offense under Section 127 for failing to pay Mr. Roy's dividend within 30 days?
A. Yes, because withholding dividend against a separate commercial trade debt without lawful adjustment provisions under the Act violates Section 127. ✔
B. No, companies can adjust any pending dues of any nature against dividends.
C. No, because trade debts automatically act as legal stay on dividends.
D. Yes, but only the company is penalized; directors have absolute immunity.
Explanation: Section 127 permits lawful adjustment against sums due from the shareholder to the company in relation to shares (such as calls in arrears). Withholding dividend for a separate commercial trade debt outside share-related sums is illegal and attracts Section 127 penalties.
Medium SCENARIO · Section 127 | Interest Rate | 18 Percent
What rate of interest is the company liable to pay to Mr. Roy under Section 127 during the period the default continues?
A. Simple interest at the rate of 18% per annum ✔
B. Compound interest at 12% per annum
C. Bank rate plus 2%
D. Fixed statutory interest of 6% per annum
Explanation: Section 127 explicitly mandates that in case of default in paying declared dividend within 30 days, the company shall be liable to pay simple interest at the rate of 18% per annum during the period such default continues.
Medium SCENARIO · Section 127 | Director Penalties | Imprisonment and Fine
What is the penal liability of the directors of Delta Agro Industries Limited who knowingly were party to this default under Section 127?
A. Punishable with imprisonment up to 2 years and with fine not less than Rs. 1,000 for every day during which default continues. ✔
B. Punishable with community service only.
C. Fine of flat Rs. 5,000 with no imprisonment risk.
D. Disqualification from directorship for life without court review.
Explanation: Section 127 prescribes imprisonment up to 2 years and a fine of not less than Rs. 1,000 per day of default for every director knowingly a party to the default.
Medium SCENARIO · Section 127 | Calls in Arrears | Lawful Adjustment
Can Delta Agro Industries Limited legally adjust the dividend against calls in arrears due on shares held by a shareholder?
A. Yes, lawful adjustment against sums due from the shareholder in respect of shares is an explicit exception under Section 127. ✔
B. No, dividend must be paid in cash regardless of calls in arrears.
C. Yes, but only with prior written permission of SEBI.
D. No, calls in arrears can only be recovered through liquidation.
Explanation: Section 127 provides an exception where failure to pay is not an offense if the dividend has been lawfully adjusted by the company against any sum due from the shareholder in respect of shares.

Paper 2: Corporate and Other Laws · Module 2 · Chapter 9:

Law — 55 rows
Easy NORMAL · Books of Account | Registered Office | Section 128
Which of the following books of account must be kept by every company at its registered office as per Section 128 of the Companies Act, 2013?
A. Books of account showing only cash receipts and disbursements
B. Books of account and other relevant books and papers and financial statement giving true and fair view of the state of the company's affairs ✔
C. Detailed minutes of all general meetings and board meetings only
D. Register of members and debenture holders only
Explanation: Section 128(1) mandates that every company shall prepare and keep at its registered office books of account and other relevant books and papers and financial statements reflecting a true and fair view of the state of the affairs of the company.
Medium NORMAL · Preservation of Books | Section 128 | Financial Years
For how many preceding financial years must a company maintain its books of account in good order under Section 128 of the Companies Act, 2013?
A. 5 financial years
B. 7 financial years ✔
C. 8 financial years
D. 10 financial years
Explanation: Section 128(1) requires a company to keep proper books of account and other relevant books and papers for a period of not less than eight financial years immediately preceding a financial year, or where the company has been in existence for less than eight years, for all such preceding years.
Hard NORMAL · Electronic Mode | Server Location | Rule 3 Accounts Rules
Where a company maintains its books of account in electronic mode, what is the mandatory requirement regarding the location of the server?
A. The server must be hosted exclusively within the territorial limits of India at all times.
B. The server may be located anywhere globally provided the backup is kept in India.
C. The server for hosting the backed-up books of account must be physically located in India. ✔
D. There is no restriction on server location if the company is an unlisted private entity.
Explanation: Rule 3 of the Companies (Accounts) Rules, 2014 states that where books of account are maintained in electronic mode, the periodic backup of the books of account accessible in India must be kept on servers physically located in India at all times.
Easy NORMAL · Inspection | Directors | Section 128
Who among the following has the statutory right to inspect the books of account of a company kept at its registered office during business hours?
A. Any equity shareholder of the company
B. Any unsecured creditor of the company
C. Any director of the company ✔
D. The statutory registrar of employees
Explanation: As per Section 128(3), the books of account and other books and papers of the company shall be open for inspection by any director during business hours.
Medium NORMAL · Financial Statements | AGM | Section 134
Within what period must a financial statement be placed before the Annual General Meeting (AGM) of a company under Section 134?
A. At every annual general meeting of the company ✔
B. Once in every three calendar years
C. Within 6 months from the end of every financial year
D. Within 90 days from the close of the financial year
Explanation: Section 134(1) read with Section 96 mandates that financial statements must be laid before every annual general meeting of the company.
Easy NORMAL · Definition | Financial Statement | Section 2(40)
Which of the following is NOT a component of 'Financial Statement' for a company under Section 2(40)?
A. Balance sheet as at the end of the financial year
B. Profit and loss account or income and expenditure account
C. Cash flow statement for the financial year
D. Internal auditor's comprehensive report ✔
Explanation: Section 2(40) defines financial statement as including a balance sheet, profit and loss account (or income and expenditure account), cash flow statement, statement of changes in equity (if applicable), and any explanatory note. Internal auditor's report is not part of the statutory financial statement definition.
Medium NORMAL · Cash Flow Statement | Exemptions | Section 2(40)
Which class of companies is specifically exempted from preparing a Cash Flow Statement as part of its financial statements?
A. All listed companies
B. One Person Company (OPC), small company, dormant company, and private company (start-up) ✔
C. Government companies engaged in defense production
D. Foreign companies operating a branch office in India
Explanation: The proviso to Section 2(40) states that the financial statement may not include the cash flow statement in case of a One Person Company, small company, dormant company, and private company (if it is a start-up as per DPIIT notification).
Hard NORMAL · Signing of Financial Statements | Section 134 | Key Managerial Personnel
Who is required to sign the financial statements of a company under Section 134(1)?
A. Only the Managing Director and the Company Secretary
B. The chairperson of the company if authorized by the Board, or two directors out of which one shall be Managing Director and the Chief Executive Officer, CFO, and Company Secretary, wherever they are appointed. ✔
C. Any single independent director and the statutory auditor
D. All the shareholders present at the AGM
Explanation: Section 134(1) prescribes that financial statements shall be signed by the chairperson of the company where he is authorized by the Board or by two directors out of which one shall be managing director and the Chief Executive Officer, Chief Financial Officer and Company Secretary, wherever they are appointed.
Hard NORMAL · Penalty | Section 128 | Contravention
What is the penalty for the Managing Director or CFO (or other officer in charge) in case of contravention of provisions relating to books of account under Section 128?
A. Imprisonment for a term up to 1 year only
B. A monetary penalty of not less than fifty thousand rupees which may extend to five lakh rupees ✔
C. Mandatory disqualification from directorship for 5 years without monetary fine
D. Fine of exactly one lakh rupees
Explanation: Section 128(6) states that if the managing director, whole-time director in charge of finance, Chief Financial Officer or any other person of a company charged by the Board fail to take reasonable steps to secure compliance, they shall be punishable with imprisonment for a term which may extend to 1 year or with fine between fifty thousand and five lakh rupees, or both.
Medium NORMAL · Voluntary Revision | Section 131 | Central Government Approval
What is the primary condition for a company to voluntarily revise its financial statements or Board's report under Section 130 and 131?
A. Prior approval of the National Company Law Tribunal (NCLT)
B. Approval of the Central Government (MCA) ✔
C. Simple majority vote of retail shareholders
D. Recommendation of the statutory auditors alone
Explanation: Section 131 permits voluntary revision of financial statements or Board's report with the approval of the Central Government (delegated to Regional Director) if they do not comply with Section 129 or 134.
Easy NORMAL · Re-opening of Accounts | Section 130 | NCLT
Under Section 130, who has the authority to order the re-opening and revision of accounts on the grounds of fraud or mismanagement?
A. The Registrar of Companies (ROC)
B. The National Company Law Tribunal (NCLT) ✔
C. The Securities and Exchange Board of India (SEBI)
D. The Comptroller and Auditor General (CAG)
Explanation: Section 130 empowers the NCLT to order a company to re-open its books of account and revise its financial statements if it is of the opinion that the relevant accounts were prepared in a fraudulent manner or the affairs of the company were mismanaged.
Medium NORMAL · Re-opening of Accounts | Section 130 | Applicants
Which bodies or authorities can apply to the NCLT for re-opening of accounts under Section 130?
A. Central Government, Income Tax authorities, SEBI, or any other statutory body/person concerned ✔
B. Only the minority shareholders holding at least 10% voting power
C. Only the statutory auditor of the company
D. Any trade union operating within the company
Explanation: Section 130(1) allows application to NCLT by the Central Government, Income-tax authorities, SEBI, Reserve Bank of India, Registrar, or any other statutory regulatory body or person.
Hard NORMAL · Notice Period | Section 130 | NCLT
What is the mandatory period up to which a notice of application for re-opening of accounts under Section 130 must be given by NCLT to the concerned authorities?
A. 7 days
B. 15 days ✔
C. 30 days
D. 60 days
Explanation: Section 130(2) requires the NCLT to give notice to the Central Government, Income-tax authorities, and SEBI/regulatory body and take into consideration their representations before passing any order under Section 130.
Hard NORMAL · Limit of Years | Section 130 | Section 131
Can accounts re-opened or revised under Section 130 or 131 be subsequently prepared for a period prior to the preceding how many financial years?
A. 3 financial years
B. 5 financial years
C. 8 financial years ✔
D. 10 financial years
Explanation: Section 130(3) and Section 131(1) proviso specify that accounts shall not be re-opened or revised for more than eight financial years immediately preceding the current financial year.
Easy NORMAL · Consolidated Financial Statements | Section 129 | Subsidiaries
Which type of companies are required to prepare Consolidated Financial Statements (CFS) in addition to standalone financial statements?
A. Every company without exception
B. Companies having one or more subsidiaries, associate companies, or joint ventures ✔
C. Only listed public companies
D. Only government companies with paid-up capital exceeding 100 crores
Explanation: Section 129(3) mandates that where a company has one or more subsidiaries, it shall, in addition to standalone statements, prepare a consolidated financial statement of the company and of all the subsidiaries in the same form and manner as its own.
Medium NORMAL · Penalty | Section 129 | Officer in Default
What is the penalty prescribed under Section 129(7) for a company officer in default for contravening the provisions relating to financial statements?
A. Imprisonment up to 1 year or fine between Rs. 50,000 and Rs. 5,00,000, or both ✔
B. Only a fixed penalty of Rs. 10,000
C. Fine of Rs. 5,00,000 without any option of imprisonment
D. Cancellation of company registration immediately
Explanation: Section 129(7) prescribes punishment for the officer in default as imprisonment for a term up to 1 year or with fine not less than Rs. 50,000 which may extend to Rs. 5,00,000, or both.
Easy NORMAL · CSR | Board's Report | Section 134
Corporate Social Responsibility (CSR) reporting forms an integral part of which document under the Companies Act, 2013?
A. Auditor's Report
B. Board's Report ✔
C. Prospectus
D. Annual Return (MGT-7)
Explanation: Section 134(3)(o) requires the Board's report to include details about the policy developed and implemented by the company on Corporate Social Responsibility initiatives.
Medium NORMAL · CSR Committee | Section 135 | Applicability Thresholds
Which companies are required to constitute a Corporate Social Responsibility (CSR) Committee under Section 135?
A. Every company registered under the Act
B. Companies satisfying net worth of Rs. 500 cr+, turnover of Rs. 1000 cr+, or net profit of Rs. 5 cr+ during the immediately preceding financial year ✔
C. Only companies listed on recognized stock exchanges
D. All banking companies irrespective of their turnover
Explanation: Section 135(1) applies to every company having net worth of Rs. 500 crore or more, turnover of Rs. 1000 crore or more, or a net profit of Rs. 5 crore or more during the immediately preceding financial year.
Easy NORMAL · CSR Spend | Section 135 | Average Net Profits
What is the minimum percentage of average net profits of the preceding three financial years that a qualifying company must spend on CSR activities?
A. 1% ✔
B. 2%
C. 3%
D. 5%
Explanation: Section 135(5) requires the Board of every qualifying company to ensure that the company spends, in every financial year, at least 2% of the average net profits of the company made during the three immediately preceding financial years.
Hard NORMAL · Unspent CSR | Schedule VII | Section 135
If a company fails to spend the mandatory CSR amount in a financial year, and such unspent amount does NOT relate to any ongoing project, what must the company do with the unspent amount?
A. Transfer it to the Prime Minister's National Relief Fund within 30 days
B. Transfer it to a Fund specified in Schedule VII within a period of 6 months of the expiry of the financial year ✔
C. Retain it in the profit and loss account as general reserve
D. Distribute it as special dividend to shareholders
Explanation: Section 135(5) read with rules specifies that any unspent CSR amount, other than relating to an ongoing project, shall be transferred to a Fund specified in Schedule VII within 6 months of the expiry of the financial year.
Hard NORMAL · Ongoing Project | Unspent CSR Account | Section 135
Where the unspent CSR amount relates to an 'ongoing project', within what timeframe must the company transfer such amount to a special unspent CSR account?
A. Within 30 days from the end of the financial year ✔
B. Within 6 months from the end of the financial year
C. Within 3 years from the date of transfer
D. Within 90 days from the end of the financial year
Explanation: Section 135(6) requires that any unspent amount pertaining to an ongoing project shall be transferred by the company within a period of 30 days from the end of the financial year to a special account to be opened by the company in any scheduled bank called the 'Unspent Corporate Social Responsibility Account'.
Medium NORMAL · Unspent CSR Account | Time Limit | Section 135
Within how many years must the amount transferred to the 'Unspent Corporate Social Responsibility Account' for an ongoing project be utilized by the company?
A. 1 financial year
B. 2 financial years from the date of such transfer
C. 3 financial years from the date of such transfer ✔
D. 5 financial years
Explanation: Section 135(6) provides that such amount transferred to the Unspent CSR Account must be spent by the company in pursuance of its obligation toward the CSR policy within a period of 3 financial years from the date of such transfer.
Hard NORMAL · Penalty | Section 135 | CSR Default
What is the penalty for default in complying with CSR spend or transfer provisions under Section 135(7)?
A. Company is liable to penalty of twice the amount required to be transferred to the Fund/Unspent CSR Account or Rs. 1 crore, whichever is less, and every officer in default is liable to 1/10th of the amount or Rs. 2 lakh, whichever is less ✔
B. Mandatory winding up of the company and imprisonment of directors
C. Fixed penalty of Rs. 10 lakh on the company only
D. No monetary penalty, only warning notice from ROC
Explanation: Section 135(7) prescribes that the company shall be liable to a penalty of twice the amount required to be transferred to the Fund/Unspent CSR Account, or Rs. 1 crore, whichever is less, and every officer in default shall be liable to 1/10th of the amount or Rs. 2 lakh, whichever is less.
Easy NORMAL · CSR Committee | Policy Formulation | Section 135
Which committee is responsible for formulating and recommending the CSR policy to the Board in qualifying companies?
A. Audit Committee
B. Nomination and Remuneration Committee
C. Corporate Social Responsibility Committee ✔
D. Stakeholders Relationship Committee
Explanation: Section 135(2) mandates that the CSR Committee shall formulate and recommend to the Board, a Corporate Social Responsibility Policy indicating activities to be undertaken.
Medium NORMAL · CSR Committee Composition | Private Company | Section 135
What is the composition requirement of the CSR Committee for an unlisted public company or private company that has only two directors on its Board?
A. The committee must be formed with minimum three directors including one independent director
B. The committee shall consist of two directors ✔
C. Exemption from forming CSR committee is granted if there are less than three directors
D. The Board itself functions as the CSR Committee without restriction
Explanation: Proviso to Section 135(1) states that where a company is not required to appoint an independent director under Section 149(4), it shall have its CSR Committee with two or more directors.
Easy NORMAL · Filing of Financial Statements | Section 137 | ROC
Who is required to file a copy of the financial statements, along with all required documents, with the Registrar of Companies (ROC) under Section 137?
A. Every company ✔
B. Only listed companies
C. Only companies having paid-up capital above Rs. 10 crore
D. Government companies audited by Comptroller and Auditor General
Explanation: Section 137(1) applies to every company, requiring it to file with the Registrar the financial statements including consolidated financial statements along with all documents required to be attached.
Easy NORMAL · Filing Timeline | Section 137 | AGM
Within what period from the date of the Annual General Meeting must the financial statements be filed with the ROC under Section 137(1)?
A. 30 days ✔
B. 60 days
C. 90 days
D. 6 months
Explanation: Section 137(1) stipulates that a copy of the financial statements, including consolidated financial statement, adopted at the AGM shall be filed with the Registrar within 30 days of the date of AGM.
Medium NORMAL · AGM Not Held | Filing of Accounts | Section 137
If the Annual General Meeting of a company is NOT held or cannot be held, within what period from the close of the financial year must the financial statements still be filed with the ROC?
A. Within 30 days from the last date on which the AGM ought to have been held ✔
B. Within 6 months from the close of the financial year
C. Within 90 days from the close of the financial year
D. No filing is required if AGM is not held
Explanation: First proviso to Section 137(1) specifies that where the financial statements are not adopted at the AGM or AGM is not held, they shall be filed with the Registrar within 30 days of the last date on which the AGM ought to have been held, along with the reasons.
Medium NORMAL · Penalty for Non-Filing | Section 137 | ROC
What is the statutory penalty for a company upon default in filing financial statements under Section 137?
A. Penalty of Rs. 1,000 for every day during which the failure continues subject to a maximum of Rs. 10,00,000 ✔
B. Fixed penalty of Rs. 50,000 only
C. Imprisonment of all shareholders
D. Strike off of company name immediately without notice
Explanation: Section 137(3) provides that if a company fails to file financial statements, the company shall be liable to a penalty of Rs. 1,000 for each day during which such failure continues, subject to a maximum of Rs. 10,00,000.
Medium NORMAL · Officer in Default | Section 137 | Filing Penalty
Which of the following persons is specifically punishable under Section 137(3) in case of failure to file financial statements?
A. The managing director and the Chief Financial Officer (CFO)
B. The company secretary and every director of the company who is in default ✔
C. Only the external statutory auditor
D. All registered shareholders holding more than 5% shares
Explanation: Section 137(3) prescribes penalty for the managing director and Chief Financial Officer, if any, and, if not, then to every director who is in default, along with the company secretary, with penalty and imprisonment terms specified.
CASE SCENARIO: Zenith Pharma Limited is a listed public company having a paid-up share capital of Rs. 40 crores and a turnover of Rs. 250 crores during the financial year 2024-25. The company maintains its primary books of account in electronic mode on a cloud server located in Frankfurt, Germany, with a real-time backup server maintained in Mumbai, India. During an internal audit, it is discovered that the financial statements for the year 2022-23 contained erroneous accounting entries due to inadvertent misclassification of capital expenditure as revenue expenditure. The Board wishes to rectify these accounts voluntarily.
Medium SCENARIO · Electronic Books | Rule 3 | Server Backup
Is the maintenance of books of account in electronic mode by Zenith Pharma Limited compliant with the Companies (Accounts) Rules, 2014?
A. No, because the primary books cannot be stored on a cloud server outside India.
B. Yes, because the periodic backup of the books of account is kept on a server physically located in India. ✔
C. No, because listed companies are strictly prohibited from maintaining electronic books.
D. Yes, provided the German server is owned by the Government of India.
Explanation: Rule 3 of the Companies (Accounts) Rules, 2014 permits electronic maintenance of books provided that the servers for hosting the backed-up books of account are physically located in India at all times.
Medium SCENARIO · Voluntary Revision | Section 131 | Central Government
What legal procedure must Zenith Pharma Limited follow if it intends to voluntarily revise its financial statements for the year 2022-23?
A. Pass an ordinary resolution at a general meeting without any government approval
B. Apply to the National Company Law Tribunal (NCLT) under Section 130
C. Obtain approval from the Central Government (Regional Director) under Section 131 ✔
D. File revised statements directly with ROC without prior permissions
Explanation: Section 131 allows a company to voluntarily revise its financial statements by obtaining the prior approval of the Central Government (powers delegated to Regional Director), when they do not comply with Section 129.
Hard SCENARIO · Voluntary Revision | Limit of Years | Section 131
What is the maximum number of preceding financial years for which Zenith Pharma Limited can revise its accounts under Section 131?
A. 2 financial years
B. 3 financial years
C. 5 financial years
D. 8 financial years ✔
Explanation: The proviso to Section 131(1) stipulates that voluntary revision shall not be made in respect of more than eight financial years immediately preceding the current financial year.
Hard SCENARIO · Section 128 | Penalty | Managing Director
If Zenith Pharma Limited fails to keep proper books of account at its registered office as required by Section 128, what penalty is attracted by the Managing Director in charge?
A. Imprisonment up to 1 year or fine between Rs. 50,000 and Rs. 5,00,000, or both ✔
B. A fixed penalty of Rs. 10,00,000
C. Only disqualification from directorship for 2 years
D. Fine equal to 50% of the company's turnover
Explanation: Section 128(6) penalizes the managing director or CFO for failure to take reasonable steps with imprisonment up to 1 year or fine ranging from Rs. 50,000 to Rs. 5,00,000, or both.
CASE SCENARIO: GreenEarth Agro Industries Private Limited is a profitable company. For the financial year 2024-25, its financial parameters are as follows: Net Worth is Rs. 550 crores, Turnover is Rs. 1,100 crores, and Net Profit is Rs. 6 crores. The company constitutes a CSR Committee and resolves to spend its CSR budget. However, at the close of the financial year, out of the total mandatory CSR obligation of Rs. 1.20 crores, the company spent only Rs. 80 lakhs on regular community welfare projects. The remaining Rs. 40 lakhs was unspent, out of which Rs. 25 lakhs relates to an ongoing school building project initiated last year, and Rs. 15 lakhs relates to a completed tree plantation drive.
Medium SCENARIO · CSR Applicability | Section 135 | Thresholds
Is GreenEarth Agro Industries Private Limited statutorily required to constitute a CSR Committee under Section 135?
A. No, because it is a private limited company.
B. Yes, because its turnover exceeds Rs. 1,000 crores and net profit exceeds Rs. 5 crores. ✔
C. No, because its net worth is below Rs. 1,000 crores.
D. Yes, only if ordered by the Registrar of Companies.
Explanation: Section 135(1) applies if any of the three thresholds (Net Worth Rs. 500 cr+, Turnover Rs. 1000 cr+, Net Profit Rs. 5 cr+) is met. Here, turnover (Rs. 1,100 cr) and net profit (Rs. 6 cr) exceed the thresholds.
Hard SCENARIO · Unspent CSR | Schedule VII | Section 135
What is the legal requirement for GreenEarth Agro Industries Private Limited regarding the unspent CSR amount of Rs. 15 lakhs relating to the completed tree plantation drive?
A. It must be transferred to the Unspent CSR Account within 30 days.
B. It must be transferred to a Fund specified in Schedule VII within 6 months of the expiry of the financial year. ✔
C. It can be carried forward as a reserve for future tree plantation.
D. It is waived off since the company spent majority of its budget.
Explanation: Section 135(5) mandates that unspent amount other than relating to an ongoing project must be transferred to a Fund specified in Schedule VII within 6 months of the expiry of the financial year.
Hard SCENARIO · Ongoing Project | Unspent CSR Account | Section 135
What is the requirement for the unspent CSR amount of Rs. 25 lakhs relating to the ongoing school building project?
A. Transfer it to an 'Unspent CSR Account' in a scheduled bank within 30 days of the end of the financial year. ✔
B. Transfer it to the Prime Minister's National Relief Fund within 7 days.
C. Spend it within 30 days from the end of the financial year.
D. Surrender it to the Ministry of Corporate Affairs immediately.
Explanation: Section 135(6) requires that unspent amount pertaining to an ongoing project be transferred within 30 days of the end of the financial year to a special account called 'Unspent Corporate Social Responsibility Account'.
Medium SCENARIO · Unspent CSR Account | Time Limit | Section 135
Within what maximum period must the Rs. 25 lakhs transferred to the Unspent CSR Account be utilized by the company?
A. 1 financial year
B. 2 financial years
C. 3 financial years from the date of such transfer ✔
D. 5 financial years
Explanation: Section 135(6) specifies that the amount transferred to the Unspent CSR Account must be spent by the company within a period of 3 financial years from the date of such transfer.
CASE SCENARIO: Apex Global Limited, a listed company, held its Annual General Meeting (AGM) for the financial year 2024-25 on September 28, 2025. Due to administrative delays and a change in statutory auditors, the adoption of financial statements was postponed, and consequently, the financial statements were not adopted at the said AGM. The company finally filed its financial statements with the Registrar of Companies (ROC) on November 25, 2025.
Medium SCENARIO · AGM Timing | Section 96 | Financial Year Close
By what date ought Apex Global Limited to have held its AGM for the financial year 2024-25 under general provisions?
A. August 31, 2025
B. September 30, 2025 ✔
C. October 31, 2025
D. December 31, 2025
Explanation: Section 96 requires an AGM to be held within 6 months from the close of the financial year (i.e., by September 30 for a financial year ending on March 31). Apex held it on September 28, 2025, which was within time.
Medium SCENARIO · Filing Deadline | Section 137 | Unadopted Statements
What is the statutory due date for filing financial statements with the ROC under Section 137(1) when financial statements are not adopted at the AGM?
A. Within 30 days from the date of the AGM
B. Within 30 days from the last date on which the AGM ought to have been held ✔
C. Within 60 days from the close of the financial year
D. Within 90 days from the date of the AGM
Explanation: First proviso to Section 137(1) states that where financial statements are not adopted at the AGM, they shall be filed with the Registrar within 30 days of the last date on which the AGM ought to have been held.
Hard SCENARIO · Filing Calculation | Section 137 | Due Date
Considering the facts, what was the last date by which Apex Global Limited should have filed its unadopted financial statements with the ROC?
A. October 28, 2025
B. October 30, 2025 ✔
C. November 28, 2025
D. December 30, 2025
Explanation: Since the AGM ought to have been held by September 30, 2025, filing must be done within 30 days thereof, making the due date October 30, 2025.
Medium SCENARIO · Penalty for Non-Filing | Section 137 | Daily Fine
Given that Apex Global Limited filed its financial statements on November 25, 2025, which is past the due date, what penalty is the company liable to under Section 137(3)?
A. A penalty of Rs. 1,000 for every day during which failure continues, subject to a maximum of Rs. 10,00,000 ✔
B. A fixed penalty of Rs. 50,000 without daily accumulation
C. Imprisonment of all directors for 6 months
D. Fine of Rs. 1 crore flat
Explanation: Section 137(3) prescribes a penalty of Rs. 1,000 for each day during which the failure to file financial statements continues, subject to a maximum ceiling of Rs. 10,00,000 for the company.
CASE SCENARIO: Vanguard Technologies Private Limited is a wholly owned subsidiary of Vanguard Inc., USA. The company closes its financial year on March 31, 2025. The Board of Directors prepared the financial statements for the year 2024-25. The company's board consists of two directors, Mr. A and Mr. B. The company has appointed a Chief Financial Officer (CFO) and a Company Secretary (CS). When preparing the financial statements, the Board wonders who is legally mandated to sign these financial statements under Section 134(1).
Medium SCENARIO · Signing | Section 134 | KMP
Who among the following must sign the financial statements of Vanguard Technologies Private Limited as per Section 134(1)?
A. Only Mr. A as the sole authorized director
B. The chairperson authorized by the Board or two directors (including Managing Director if any), along with CFO and CS (where appointed) ✔
C. Only the Chief Financial Officer and statutory auditor
D. The holding company's directors in the USA
Explanation: Section 134(1) mandates that financial statements be signed by the chairperson authorized by the Board or two directors (one being MD if appointed), and the CEO, CFO, and CS, wherever they are appointed.
Hard SCENARIO · Cash Flow Statement | Subsidiary | Section 2(40) Exemption
Is Vanguard Technologies Private Limited required to include a Cash Flow Statement in its financial statements under Section 2(40)?
A. Yes, all companies without exception must file a cash flow statement.
B. No, because it is a private company and a subsidiary of a foreign corporate body.
C. No, because OPC, small companies, dormant companies, and private company start-ups are exempted, but being a subsidiary of a foreign corporate body, it does not automatically enjoy the start-up private company exemption unless it qualifies under specific rules.
D. Yes, since it is a subsidiary of a foreign company, cash flow is mandatory. ✔
Explanation: The exemption from cash flow statement under Section 2(40) is available to OPC, small companies, dormant companies, and private company start-ups. Since Vanguard is a subsidiary of a foreign body corporate (not an Indian start-up private company), cash flow statement is required.
Medium SCENARIO · CFS | Section 129 | Subsidiary
Under Section 129(3), what additional financial statement must Vanguard Technologies Private Limited prepare if it has its own subsidiary company in India?
A. Consolidated Financial Statement (CFS) along with standalone statement ✔
B. Only segment reporting statements
C. Tax audit report in Form 3CD
D. Quarterly un-audited results
Explanation: Section 129(3) mandates that where a company has one or more subsidiaries, it shall prepare a Consolidated Financial Statement of the company and all subsidiaries in the same form and manner as its own.
Easy SCENARIO · Registered Office | Books of Account | Section 128
Where must Vanguard Technologies Private Limited keep its books of account as per Section 128?
A. At its registered office in India ✔
B. At the holding company's headquarters in USA
C. At the statutory auditor's office in India
D. At any place in India decided by the CFO
Explanation: Section 128(1) requires every company to prepare and keep books of account and other relevant papers at its registered office in India.
CASE SCENARIO: A serious financial scam comes to light in Stellar Infrastructure Limited. The Serious Fraud Investigation Office (SFIO) and Income Tax authorities suspect that the financial statements of the company for the past 5 financial years were manipulated and prepared in a fraudulent manner to inflate profits and secure bank loans. The regulatory authorities decide to approach the National Company Law Tribunal (NCLT) for re-opening the company's books of account.
Easy SCENARIO · Re-opening of Accounts | Section 130 | NCLT
Which section of the Companies Act, 2013 governs the re-opening of accounts on Court or Tribunal orders based on fraud or mismanagement?
A. Section 128
B. Section 129
C. Section 130 ✔
D. Section 131
Explanation: Section 130 deals specifically with the re-opening of accounts on Tribunal's or Court's orders where accounts were prepared in a fraudulent manner or due to mismanagement.
Medium SCENARIO · Section 130 | Applicants | Regulatory Bodies
Which authorities are specifically empowered under Section 130(1) to apply to the NCLT for re-opening of accounts?
A. Central Government, Income-tax authorities, SEBI, RBI, or any other statutory regulatory body ✔
B. Any retail shareholder holding a single share
C. Only the statutory auditors of the company
D. Any commercial bank that has granted a loan
Explanation: Section 130(1) lists Central Government, Income-tax authorities, SEBI, RBI, Registrar, or any other statutory regulatory body as authorized applicants to NCLT.
Hard SCENARIO · NCLT Notice | Section 130 | Representations
Before passing an order under Section 130, what procedural step must the NCLT mandatorily undertake with respect to notices?
A. Give notice to Central Government, Income-tax authorities, and SEBI/regulatory body and consider their representations ✔
B. Publish a public advertisement in international newspapers and wait for 90 days
C. Obtain unanimous consent of all equity shareholders
D. Direct the police commissioner to arrest the Board of Directors
Explanation: Section 130(2) requires the NCLT to give notice to the Central Government, Income-tax authorities, and SEBI or any other statutory body and take into consideration their representations before passing any order.
Medium SCENARIO · Time Limit | Section 130 | Retrospective Accounts
What is the maximum retrospective timeframe limitation up to which accounts can be re-opened under Section 130?
A. 3 financial years
B. 5 financial years
C. 8 financial years immediately preceding the current financial year ✔
D. No time limit whatsoever
Explanation: Section 130(3) restricts re-opening of accounts to not more than eight financial years immediately preceding the current financial year.

Paper 2: Corporate and Other Laws · Module 2 · Chapter 10:

Law — 55 rows
Easy NORMAL · First Auditor | Board Appointment | Section 139(6)
Who holds the primary responsibility for appointing the first auditor of a company other than a Government company under Section 139(6) of the Companies Act, 2013?
A. The Board of Directors ✔
B. The members in a general meeting
C. The Comptroller and Auditor-General of India
D. The Regional Director
Explanation: According to Section 139(6) of the Companies Act, 2013, the first auditor of a company, other than a Government company, shall be appointed by the Board of Directors within 30 days of the date of registration of the company. If the Board fails, it informs the members to appoint the auditor.
Easy NORMAL · First Auditor | Time Limit | Section 139(6)
Within what period from the date of registration must the Board of Directors appoint the first auditor of a non-Government company?
A. 15 days
B. 30 days ✔
C. 60 days
D. 90 days
Explanation: Section 139(6) mandates that the Board of Directors of a non-Government company must appoint the first auditor within 30 days from the date of registration of the company.
Medium NORMAL · First Auditor | Default by Board | Member Appointment
What happens if the Board of Directors of a non-Government company fails to appoint the first auditor within the stipulated 30-day period?
A. The office of the auditor remains vacant permanently for that year.
B. The Central Government directly makes the appointment.
C. The company shall inform the members, who shall appoint the auditor within 90 days at an extraordinary general meeting. ✔
D. The Registrar of Companies automatically assumes the role of the auditor.
Explanation: Under Section 139(6), if the Board fails to appoint the first auditor within 30 days, it shall inform the members of the company, who shall within 90 days at an extraordinary general meeting (EGM) appoint such auditor.
Easy NORMAL · Government Company | CAG Appointment | First Auditor
For a Government company or any other company owned or controlled, directly or indirectly, by the Central Government, who appoints the first auditor under Section 139(7)?
A. The Board of Directors within 30 days
B. The Comptroller and Auditor-General of India (CAG) within 60 days from registration ✔
C. The members in the first Annual General Meeting
D. The National Company Law Tribunal (NCLT)
Explanation: Section 139(7) states that in the case of a Government company, the first auditor shall be appointed by the Comptroller and Auditor-General of India within 60 days from the date of registration of the company.
Medium NORMAL · Auditor Rotation | Tenure | Section 139(2)
What is the maximum tenure for which an individual can be appointed as an auditor in a listed company before mandatory rotation applies under Section 139(2)?
A. One term of 3 consecutive years
B. One term of 5 consecutive years
C. Two terms of 5 consecutive years each ✔
D. Maximum of 10 consecutive years without limit
Explanation: Section 139(2) provides that an individual can be appointed as an auditor for not more than one term of 5 consecutive years. However, they can be re-appointed for another term of 5 consecutive years after a cooling period, making a maximum of two terms of 5 years each.
Medium NORMAL · Cooling Period | Auditor Rotation | Section 139(2)
What is the mandatory cooling period required for an individual auditor after completing their maximum tenure in a company where rotation of auditors applies?
A. 2 consecutive years
B. 3 consecutive years
C. 5 consecutive years ✔
D. 10 consecutive years
Explanation: According to Section 139(2), an individual who has completed their term of 5 consecutive years (or two terms totaling 10 years, depending on the rule applicability) cannot be re-appointed as auditor of the same company for a period of 5 years from the completion of their term.
Medium NORMAL · Audit Firm Rotation | Tenure | Section 139(2)
Under Section 139(2), what is the maximum continuous tenure permitted for an audit firm in a listed company?
A. One term of 5 years
B. Two terms of 5 consecutive years each ✔
C. Three terms of 5 consecutive years each
D. Five consecutive years with no renewal
Explanation: Section 139(2) specifies that an audit firm can be appointed for not more than two terms of 5 consecutive years each, followed by a mandatory cooling period of 5 years.
Hard NORMAL · Rule 5 | Rotation Thresholds | Unlisted Companies
Which of the following classes of companies, other than listed companies, are specifically required to comply with the mandatory rotation of auditors provisions under Rule 5 of the Companies (Audit and Auditors) Rules, 2014?
A. All private limited companies regardless of paid-up share capital
B. Unlisted public companies having paid-up share capital of rupees 10 crore or more ✔
C. All dormant companies
D. All Nidhi companies with any deposit size
Explanation: Rule 5 of the Companies (Audit and Auditors) Rules, 2014 requires unlisted public companies having paid-up share capital of Rs. 10 crore or more, and private limited companies having paid-up share capital of Rs. 50 crore or more, to rotate their auditors.
Easy NORMAL · Disqualifications | Section 141(3) | Re-appointment
Can a retiring auditor be re-appointed at an Annual General Meeting (AGM) if they have become disqualified under Section 141(3)?
A. Yes, if the Board unanimously recommends them.
B. Yes, with the prior approval of the Registrar of Companies.
C. No, a disqualified person cannot be appointed or re-appointed as an auditor. ✔
D. Yes, provided 75% of members vote in favor.
Explanation: Section 141(3) outlines disqualifications for appointment as an auditor. A person who incurs a disqualification cannot be appointed or re-appointed, and any ongoing appointment ceases immediately upon disqualification.
Easy NORMAL · Eligibility | Section 141(3) | Disqualifications
Which of the following persons is NOT disqualified from being appointed as an auditor of a company under Section 141(3)?
A. A body corporate other than a Limited Liability Partnership
B. An officer or employee of the company
C. A person who, or whose relative or partner, holds any security of or interest in the company of face value rupees 500
D. A chartered accountant in practice who is holding a valid Certificate of Practice ✔
Explanation: A practicing Chartered Accountant with a valid COP is eligible for appointment, provided they do not suffer from any specific disqualifications listed in Section 141(3) such as being an officer/employee, holding securities above the permitted limit, or being a corporate body.
Medium NORMAL · Holding Securities | Disqualification Limit | Section 141(3)
What is the maximum face value limit of securities that a relative of an auditor can hold in the company, subsidiary, holding, or associate company without disqualifying the auditor under Section 141(3)(d)(i)?
A. Rupees 1,000
B. Rupees 50,000
C. Rupees 1,00,000 ✔
D. Rupees 5,00,000
Explanation: Under Section 141(3)(d)(i), a person is disqualified if they, their relative, or partner holds any security of or interest in the company, its subsidiary, holding, or associate company of face value exceeding Rs. 1,00,000 (as amended by the Companies (Amendment) Act, 2017).
Hard NORMAL · Corrective Action | Timeframe | Section 141(3)
If a relative of an auditor acquires securities exceeding the permitted threshold of rupees 1,00,000 post-appointment, what corrective action must be taken and within what timeframe?
