Explanation: Section 24(1) provides that a person may cease to be a partner in accordance with the agreement or, in the absence of agreement, by giving 30 days' notice to the other partners of their intention to resign.
CASE SCENARIO: Zenith Advisory LLP was incorporated in Mumbai with three partners: Alpha Corp (a body corporate incorporated in Singapore), Mr. Rohan (an Indian resident), and Ms. Priya (who stays in London and visits India for only 30 days in a financial year). Due to a business dispute, Alpha Corp decides to withdraw its nominee designated partner without appointing a replacement, and Ms. Priya refuses to act as a designated partner. The LLP agreement is silent on the mechanism of appointing designated partners.
Medium SCENARIO · Designated Partner | Resident | Scenario Analysis
Considering the residency requirement under Section 7, which of the partners in Zenith Advisory LLP is qualified to act as a 'resident in India' designated partner?
A. Alpha Corp
B. Mr. Rohan ✔
C. Ms. Priya
D. None of them
Explanation: Section 7 requires at least one designated partner to be resident in India (stay in India for not less than 182 days in the preceding financial year). Mr. Rohan is an Indian resident, whereas Ms. Priya stayed for only 30 days, failing the test.
Medium SCENARIO · Designated Partners | Minimum Requirement | Compliance
If Alpha Corp withdraws its nominee and no replacement is appointed, what is the minimum number of designated partners Zenith Advisory LLP must maintain under the Act?
A. At least one
B. At least two ✔
C. At least three
D. No minimum is required if total partners are above two
Explanation: Section 7 mandates that every LLP must have at least two designated partners who are individuals. If the number falls below two, the LLP is in default.
Hard SCENARIO · Non-Resident | Designated Partner | Residency
Can Ms. Priya, being a partner who stays abroad for most of the year, be appointed as a designated partner of Zenith Advisory LLP?
A. Yes, provided she holds an Indian PAN card
B. Yes, as an ordinary designated partner, but she cannot fulfill the resident-in-India requirement ✔
C. No, individuals who are non-residents can never be designated partners under any circumstance
D. Yes, if Alpha Corp guarantees her residency
Explanation: An individual who is a non-resident can be a designated partner, but they will not satisfy the specific requirement that at least one designated partner must be resident in India.
Hard SCENARIO · Default | Penalties | Designated Partners
If the LLP fails to maintain the minimum required designated partners for more than 6 months, who faces penal consequences under the LLP Act?
A. Only Alpha Corp as the foreign body corporate
B. The LLP and every partner/defaulting officer of the LLP ✔
C. Only the Registrar of Companies
D. No penalty applies if the total partners exceed two
Explanation: Section 7 and associated penalty provisions state that if an LLP contravenes the provisions relating to designated partners, the LLP and every designated partner/partner in default are punishable with a fine.
CASE SCENARIO: A partnership firm named 'M/s Quick Logistics', consisting of three partners (A, B, and C), decided to convert into a Limited Liability Partnership under the name 'Quick Logistics LLP' following the Second Schedule of the LLP Act, 2008. At the time of conversion, the firm had outstanding unsecured loans from various creditors. The partners did not file Form 3 containing the LLP agreement within 30 days of incorporation, and partner A performed an unauthorized contract beyond his authority, causing loss to a third party who was aware of A's lack of authority.
Medium SCENARIO · Conversion | Vesting of Assets | Second Schedule
What is the legal effect of the conversion of M/s Quick Logistics into Quick Logistics LLP on the property and liabilities of the firm?
A. All property, assets, and liabilities of the firm automatically vest in the LLP without requiring separate conveyancing. ✔
B. All previous liabilities are extinguished upon conversion.
C. The firm continues to exist alongside the LLP as a subsidiary.
D. Only movable assets transfer to the LLP, while liabilities remain with the firm.
Explanation: As per the Second Schedule of the LLP Act, upon conversion, all tangible and intangible property, assets, rights, privileges, liabilities, and obligations of the firm stand transferred to and vest in the LLP without any further act or deed.
Medium SCENARIO · LLP Agreement | Form 3 | Filing Delay
What penalty or consequence follows the failure of Quick Logistics LLP to file Form 3 (LLP Agreement) within 30 days of incorporation?
A. The incorporation certificate is revoked automatically.
B. The LLP and every partner are liable to a monetary penalty for non-compliance. ✔
C. The partners face compulsory imprisonment for 3 months.
D. The LLP agreement becomes permanently void and cannot be registered.
Explanation: Failing to file Form 3 within the stipulated time attracts monetary penalties for the LLP and its designated partners as specified under Section 23 read with the penal provisions of the Act.
Hard SCENARIO · Partner Authority | Unauthorized Acts | Third Party Knowledge
Is Quick Logistics LLP bound by the unauthorized contract entered into by partner A with the third party?
A. Yes, because all partners possess implied authority for all commercial contracts.
B. No, because the LLP is not bound by anything done by a partner if the partner has no authority and the third party knows that. ✔
C. Yes, because third parties are never required to check partner authority in an LLP.
D. No, because only designated partners can bind an LLP.
Explanation: Section 28(2) specifies that an LLP is not bound by anything done by a partner in dealing with a person if the partner has no authority to act for the LLP and the person knows that the partner has no authority.
Medium SCENARIO · Creditors | Conversion | Liabilities
Following the conversion, what happens to the unsecured creditors of the erstwhile partnership firm?
A. They lose their right to claim since the legal entity has changed.
B. They remain creditors of the newly formed LLP, and their rights are unaffected by the conversion. ✔
C. They must re-file their claims through court litigation.
D. Their debts are converted into equity shares of the LLP.
Explanation: The Second Schedule ensures that all obligations, debts, and liabilities of the firm prior to conversion devolve upon the resulting LLP, preserving the rights of all creditors.
CASE SCENARIO: Vanguard Tech Solutions LLP was formed by four software engineers. Due to internal disagreements, Partner X decided to retire from the LLP. The LLP agreement contained a clause specifying a 14-day notice period for voluntary retirement. However, Partner X served a 30-day notice. Simultaneously, the LLP failed to file its Statement of Account and Solvency (Form 8) for the financial year ending March 31, and the Registrar initiated inquiry proceedings.
Medium SCENARIO · Cessation | Retirement | LLP Agreement
How is the retirement of Partner X governed when the LLP agreement prescribes a specific notice period?
A. The agreement provision prevails, making the 14-day notice period applicable. ✔
B. The statutory default period of 30 days under the Act overrides the agreement.
C. Partner X cannot retire without the unanimous consent of all creditors.
D. Retirement is invalid unless approved by the Tribunal.
Explanation: Section 24(1) states that a person may cease to be a partner in accordance with agreement with the other partners; hence, the notice period specified in the LLP agreement governs the retirement.
Hard SCENARIO · Cessation Notice | Filing | Liability Release
When does Partner X officially cease to be a partner and get relieved of future partner liabilities?
A. Immediately upon posting the notice
B. Only when notice of cessation is filed with the Registrar and recorded, or upon expiration of the notice ✔
C. Only after the financial year audit is completed
D. When the Tribunal issues a discharge certificate
Explanation: Section 25 mandates that notice of cessation of a partner must be filed with the Registrar within 30 days, and a partner continues to be regarded as a partner until the public notice/filing reflects their cessation, or in accordance with the agreement.
Hard SCENARIO · Form 8 | Solvency Statement | Timeline
What is the statutory requirement regarding the preparation and filing of Form 8 (Statement of Account and Solvency) for Vanguard Tech Solutions LLP?
A. It must be filed within 30 days of the end of the financial year.
B. It must be prepared within 6 months of the end of the financial year and filed in Form 8 within the prescribed due date. ✔
C. It is optional for LLPs with turnover below Rs. 40 lakhs.
D. It is filed only once in every five years.
Explanation: Under Rule 25 and Section 34, every LLP must maintain a Statement of Account and Solvency within 6 months of the end of the financial year and file Form 8 with the Registrar within 30 days of expiration of that 6-month period.
Medium SCENARIO · Notice of Change | Partners | Section 25
If Partner X ceased to be a partner, what is the responsibility for filing the notice of change in partners with the Registrar?
A. Partner X alone is responsible for filing the notice.
B. The LLP must file the notice of change of partners within 30 days of the cessation. ✔
C. The Central Government files the notice automatically.
D. No filing is required if the remaining partners agree.
Explanation: Section 25(1) places the obligation on the LLP to file a notice of any change in its partners with the Registrar within 30 days of such change taking place.
CASE SCENARIO: Apex Global Ventures LLP was suspected of carrying on fraudulent transactions to cheat its suppliers. The Central Government ordered an inspection of the LLP's books under Section 43. During the inquiry, Partner M disclosed crucial documents and internal emails proving systemic fraud by the managing designated partner, Mr. K. Partner M sought protection under the whistleblowing provisions of the LLP Act.
Medium SCENARIO · Investigation | Central Government | Section 43
Under Section 43, who holds the authority to order an investigation into the affairs of Apex Global Ventures LLP?
A. The High Court of the State
B. The Central Government ✔
C. The Reserve Bank of India
D. The Registrar of Companies independently
Explanation: Section 43 explicitly empowers the Central Government to appoint inspectors to investigate the affairs of an LLP based on specified grounds or reports.
Hard SCENARIO · Whistleblowing | Penalty Waiver | Section 31
What relief or benefit can Partner M potentially receive under Section 31 for cooperating as a whistleblower?
A. Complete exemption from all civil debts of the LLP
B. Reduction or waiver of penalty that may be leviable against them ✔
C. Automatic promotion to the position of managing designated partner
D. Cash reward equivalent to the fraud amount
Explanation: Section 31 provides that the Tribunal or Central Government may reduce or waive any penalty against a partner or employee who provides useful information leading to a conviction or penalty under the Act.
Hard SCENARIO · Fraudulent Trading | Personal Liability | Section 30
If Mr. K is found guilty of carrying on business with intent to defraud creditors under Section 30, what personal liability does he face?
A. Liability limited to his capital contribution only
B. Unlimited personal liability for all debts of the LLP without any limitation, along with imprisonment and fines ✔
C. Only a nominal fine of Rs. 1,000
D. Liability only if the creditors file a civil suit
Explanation: Section 30 makes persons knowingly party to fraudulent trading personally liable, without any limitation, for all or any of the debts or other liabilities of the LLP, in addition to penal imprisonment and fines.
Medium SCENARIO · Winding Up by Tribunal | Fraud | Grounds
Can Apex Global Ventures LLP be wound up by the Tribunal due to fraudulent activities?
A. No, winding up can only be voluntary for LLPs.
B. Yes, if the Tribunal is of the opinion that it is just and equitable or that the LLP has acted fraudulently, it may order winding up. ✔
C. Only if 100% of partners consent to Tribunal intervention.
D. No, fraud only attracts financial penalties, not winding up.
Explanation: Section 64 sets out grounds for winding up by the Tribunal, including when the LLP has been used for fraudulent purposes or if the Tribunal thinks it is just and equitable to wind up the LLP.
CASE SCENARIO: GreenFields Agro LLP was established with two corporate bodies as partners: AgriCorp Ltd. and BioInnovations Inc., along with two individual designated partners, Mr. Sharma and Ms. Verma. Due to a severe economic downturn, the LLP incurred heavy trading losses, and its liabilities exceeded its total assets. The partners wish to initiate a voluntary winding up of the LLP.
Medium SCENARIO · Voluntary Winding Up | Resolution | Section 63
What is the primary condition for initiating voluntary winding up of GreenFields Agro LLP under Section 63?
A. Approval from the local municipal corporation
B. Passing a resolution to wind up voluntarily and complying with the LLP agreement or statutory procedure ✔
C. Approval from the Supreme Court of India
D. Full repayment of all creditors prior to passing any resolution
Explanation: Section 63 states that an LLP may be wound up voluntarily if the LLP passes a resolution to wind up voluntarily and follows the prescribed process under the LLP Rules.
Easy SCENARIO · Partners | Body Corporate | Eligibility
Can corporate bodies like AgriCorp Ltd. and BioInnovations Inc. act as partners in GreenFields Agro LLP?
A. No, only living individuals can be partners in an LLP.
B. Yes, corporate bodies, companies, and foreign LLPs are fully competent to be partners in an LLP. ✔
C. Yes, but only if they hold more than 50% of the voting power.
D. No, corporate bodies can only be designated partners, not ordinary partners.
Explanation: Section 2(1)(d) and Section 5 of the LLP Act permit any individual or body corporate to be a partner in a Limited Liability Partnership.
Medium SCENARIO · Limited Liability | Corporate Partners | Winding Up
During the winding up of GreenFields Agro LLP, what is the extent of liability of AgriCorp Ltd. and BioInnovations Inc. for the shortfall in assets?
A. Unlimited personal liability of both parent companies
B. Liability limited to their agreed capital contribution to the LLP ✔
C. No liability whatsoever once winding up is initiated
D. Joint liability with the designated partners' personal assets
Explanation: The core feature of an LLP is limited liability. Partners (whether individuals or corporate bodies) are not personally liable for the debts of the LLP beyond their agreed contribution.
Hard SCENARIO · Liquidator | Voluntary Winding Up | Procedure
Who is responsible for overseeing the voluntary winding up process of the LLP once the resolution is passed?
A. The Registrar of Companies directly
B. A Company Liquidator or liquidator appointed for the LLP in accordance with the rules ✔
C. The Chief Justice of the High Court
D. The oldest designated partner automatically
Explanation: Voluntary winding up procedures under the LLP Act and Rules require the appointment of a liquidator who manages the realization of assets and settlement of claims.

Paper 2: Corporate and Other Laws · Module 3 · Chapter 1:

Law — 55 rows
Easy NORMAL · Objective | Introduction | Interpretation
What is the primary objective of the General Clauses Act, 1897?
A. To provide substantive criminal law procedures for all central acts
B. To shorten the language used in Central Acts and provide uniform rules of interpretation ✔
C. To override the Constitution of India in matters of central legislation
D. To exclusively regulate the taxation powers of the Central and State Governments
Explanation: According to the ICAI study material, the General Clauses Act, 1897 is enacted to shorten the language of Central Acts, provide uniform definitions of frequently used terms, and lay down rules of interpretation to avoid repetition.
Easy NORMAL · Application | Constitution | Central Acts
Does the General Clauses Act, 1897 apply to the Constitution of India?
A. Yes, fully and without any exception
B. No, it does not apply to the Constitution of India ✔
C. Yes, but only to the Directive Principles of State Policy
D. Only when specifically notified by the President of India
Explanation: The General Clauses Act applies to all Central Acts and Regulations, but it does not apply to the Constitution of India, as the Constitution is the supreme law and has its own interpretation provisions.
Medium NORMAL · Central Government | Definitions | Section 3
Under Section 3(8) of the General Clauses Act, 1897, 'Central Government' in relation to anything done or to be done after the commencement of the Constitution means:
A. The President ✔
B. The Prime Minister and the Union Cabinet
C. The Governor-General in Council
D. The President acting with the aid and advice of the Council of Ministers
Explanation: Under Section 3(8)(b)(i), 'Central Government' in relation to anything done or to be done after the commencement of the Constitution means the President, who acts on the aid and advice of the Council of Ministers, but the statutory term refers to the President.
Medium NORMAL · Commencement | Section 5 | Assent
An act is passed by Parliament on 10th January 2026, receives Presidential assent on 15th January 2026, and is published in the Official Gazette on 20th January 2026. The Act does not specify any particular date for its commencement. When will it come into operation?
A. 10th January 2026
B. 15th January 2026 ✔
C. 20th January 2026
D. 15th February 2026
Explanation: Under Section 5 of the General Clauses Act, where an Act does not express any specific date of commencement, it comes into operation on the day on which it receives the assent of the President (i.e., 15th January 2026).
Medium NORMAL · Commencement | Section 5 | Timing
If a Central Act passed after the commencement of the Constitution is expressed to come into operation on a particular day, when does it commence?
A. At the sunrise on that day
B. At the expiration of the day preceding that day ✔
C. At noon on that day
D. Seven days after that day
Explanation: Section 5 of the General Clauses Act provides that a Central Act comes into operation on the expiration of the day preceding the day on which it is expressed to come into force, unless a different intention is expressed.
Hard NORMAL · Repeal | Section 6 | Accrued Rights
What is the legal effect of the repeal of a Central Act under Section 6 of the General Clauses Act, 1897, unless a different intention appears?
A. It revives anything not in force or existing at the time the repeal takes effect
B. It affects any previous operation of any enactment so repealed or anything duly done or suffered thereunder
C. It does not affect any right, privilege, obligation, or liability acquired, accrued, or incurred under the repealed enactment ✔
D. It automatically invalidates all pending legal proceedings instituted under the repealed act
Explanation: Section 6 protects accrued rights and liabilities. Specifically, the repeal does not affect any right, privilege, obligation, or liability acquired, accrued, or incurred under the repealed enactment, nor does it affect ongoing investigations or legal proceedings unless a contrary intention appears.
Hard NORMAL · Section 6A | Repeal | Amendments
Under Section 6A of the General Clauses Act, where any Central Act repeals any enactment by which the text of any Central Act was amended, what is the status of the amendments?
A. The amendments automatically stand repealed along with the repealing act
B. The repeal of the amending enactment does not, unless a different intention appears, affect the continuance of any such amendment made by the enactment so repealed ✔
C. The original unamended text revives immediately without any further notification
D. The amendments become voidable at the option of the Central Government
Explanation: According to Section 6A, the repeal of an amending Act does not affect the continuance of the amendment made by the repealed Act to the original legislation, unless a different intention appears.
Medium NORMAL · Section 8 | Construction of References | Repeal and Re-enactment
When an Act repeals and re-enacts with or without modification any provisions of a former enactment, references in any other enactment or instrument to the provisions so repealed shall, unless a different intention appears, be construed as references to:
A. The provisions so repealed
B. The provisions so re-enacted ✔
C. The provisions of the Constitution of India
D. Null and void provisions
Explanation: Under Section 8 of the General Clauses Act, where an enactment is repealed and re-enacted, references to the repealed provisions in other enactments or instruments are construed as references to the provisions so re-enacted.
Medium NORMAL · Section 9 | Computation of Time | Interpretation
According to Section 9 of the General Clauses Act, how are the words 'from' and 'to' interpreted when calculating time in a Central Act?
A. 'From' excludes the first day, and 'to' includes the last day ✔
B. 'From' includes the first day, and 'to' excludes the last day
C. Both 'from' and 'to' include the respective days
D. Both 'from' and 'to' exclude the respective days
Explanation: Section 9 lays down that in any Central Act, it shall be sufficient, for the purpose of excluding the first in a series of days or any other period of time, to use the word 'from', and for the purpose of including the last in a series of days or any other period of time, to use the word 'to'.
Hard NORMAL · Section 27 | Service by Post | Deemed Service
If a Central Act requires any document to be served by post, when is the service deemed to be effected, assuming proper addressing, prepaying, and posting under Section 27?
A. At the exact moment the letter is dropped in the post box
B. At the time at which the letter would be delivered in the ordinary course of post ✔
C. Only when the recipient signs the acknowledgment card
D. Seven days after posting, irrespective of postal distance
Explanation: Section 27 states that where any legislation authorizes or requires document service by post, service is deemed to be effected by properly addressing, prepaying, and posting a registered letter, and, unless the contrary is proved, to have been effected at the time at which the letter would be delivered in the ordinary course of post.
Medium NORMAL · Good Faith | Section 3 | Definitions
Under Section 3(22) of the General Clauses Act, 'Good Faith' is defined in civil law contexts. Which of the following best reflects the statutory meaning?
A. An act done honestly, whether it is done negligently or not
B. An act is deemed to be done in good faith where it is in fact done honestly, whether it is done negligently or not ✔
C. An act done with absolute perfection and complete absence of any clerical error
D. An act done with due care and caution and never involving any negligence
Explanation: Under the General Clauses Act (Section 3(22)), a thing is deemed to be done in 'good faith' where it is in fact done honestly, whether it is done negligently or not. (Note: This contrasts with the Indian Penal Code definition which requires due care and attention).
Easy NORMAL · Section 14 | Powers | Exercise
What does Section 14 of the General Clauses Act provide regarding powers conferred on authorities?
A. Powers can be exercised only once and exhaust themselves
B. Powers conferred can be exercised from time to time as occasion requires ✔
C. Powers can be exercised only with prior written permission of the Supreme Court
D. Powers lapse automatically after one year from the date of enactment
Explanation: Section 14 provides that where a power is conferred by any Central Act or Regulation, then that power may be exercised from time to time as occasion requires, unless a different intention appears.
Medium NORMAL · Section 16 | Appointment | Dismissal
Under Section 16 of the General Clauses Act, the power to make any appointment includes the power to:
A. Suspend or dismiss any person appointed, subject to any statutory conditions ✔
B. Increase the salary of the appointee beyond budget limits
C. Transfer the appointee to a foreign country without consent
D. Exempt the appointee from criminal liability
Explanation: Section 16 states that the power to appoint includes the power to suspend or dismiss any person appointed by any such authority or officer, unless a different intention appears.
Easy NORMAL · Person | Section 3 | Definitions
According to Section 3(42) of the General Clauses Act, 'Person' includes:
A. Only natural human beings
B. Any company or association or body of individuals, whether incorporated or not ✔
C. Only registered corporate entities and public sector undertakings
D. Foreign governments but not domestic companies
Explanation: Section 3(42) defines 'person' to include any company or association or body of individuals, whether incorporated or not, in addition to natural human beings.
Easy NORMAL · Year | Section 3 | Calendar
Under Section 3(65) of the General Clauses Act, 'Year' shall mean a year reckoned according to:
A. The financial year commencing on 1st April
B. The British calendar (Gregorian calendar) ✔
C. The Hindu Vikram Samvat calendar
D. The lunar calendar system
Explanation: Section 3(65) defines 'year' to mean a year reckoned according to the British calendar (Gregorian calendar).
Easy NORMAL · Section 13 | Gender | Number
What is the rule regarding gender and number under Section 13 of the General Clauses Act?
A. Words importing the masculine gender shall be taken to include females, and words in singular include plural and vice versa, unless there is anything repugnant in the subject or context ✔
B. Masculine gender strictly excludes feminine gender unless explicitly stated otherwise
C. Singular words never include plural words under any circumstances
D. Neuter gender words apply exclusively to corporate entities
Explanation: Section 13 prescribes that in all Central Acts and Regulations, unless there is anything repugnant in the subject or context, words importing the masculine gender include females, and words in the singular include the plural, and vice versa.
Medium NORMAL · Section 21 | Power to Issue | Amend and Rescind
When a Central Act confers power to make rules, regulations, or bye-laws, what does Section 21 imply regarding the power to amend, vary, or rescind them?
A. Rules made once can never be amended or rescinded by the same authority
B. The power to make includes the power to add to, amend, vary, or rescind rules, regulations, or bye-laws, subject to similar conditions ✔
C. Only the judiciary can amend or rescind rules made by executive authorities
D. Rules can only be rescinded after approval by a public referendum
Explanation: Section 21 embodies the rule that the power to issue notifications, orders, rules, or bye-laws includes the power to add to, amend, vary, or rescind them, exercisable in the like manner and subject to the like sanction and conditions.
Medium NORMAL · Immovable Property | Section 3 | Definitions
Under Section 3(26) of the General Clauses Act, 'Immovable property' includes:
A. Standing timber, growing crops, and grass
B. Land, benefits to arise out of land, and things attached to the earth or permanently fastened to anything attached to the earth ✔
C. Registered trademarks, patents, and copyrights
D. Money deposited in current bank accounts
Explanation: Section 3(26) defines 'immovable property' to include land, benefits to arise out of land, and things attached to the earth, or permanently fastened to anything attached to the earth (expressly excluding standing timber, growing crops, and grass).
Easy NORMAL · Registered | Section 3 | Definitions
Under Section 3(48) of the General Clauses Act, 'Registered', used with reference to a document, means registered under:
A. The Companies Act in force
B. The law for the time being in force for the registration of documents ✔
C. The Reserve Bank of India guidelines
D. The Indian Stamp Act exclusively
Explanation: Section 3(48) defines 'registered' to mean registered under the law for the time being in force for the registration of documents (such as the Registration Act, 1908).
Easy NORMAL · Schedule | Section 3 | Definitions
According to Section 3(50) of the General Clauses Act, what does 'Schedule' mean?
A. A timetable for parliamentary debates
B. A schedule to the Central Act or Regulation in which the word occurs ✔
C. An internal memo circulated by government departments
D. A financial budget document presented annually
Explanation: Section 3(50) defines 'Schedule' to mean a schedule to the Central Act or Regulation in which the word occurs.
Medium NORMAL · Oath | Section 3 | Affirmation
How is 'Oath' defined under Section 3(37) of the General Clauses Act?
A. A formal promise made exclusively in a religious ceremony
B. An oath shall include affirmation and declaration in the case of persons by law allowed to affirm or declare instead of swearing ✔
C. A signed written undertaking submitted to a police officer
D. A secret pledge taken by political party members
Explanation: Section 3(37) defines 'Oath' to include affirmation and declaration in the case of persons by law allowed to affirm or declare instead of swearing.
Medium NORMAL · Section 10 | Computation of Time | Holidays
What is the effect of an act being done on a 'holiday' as per Section 10 of the General Clauses Act, where an act or proceeding is directed or allowed to be done in any court or office on a certain day or within a prescribed period?
A. The act becomes permanently void and cannot be performed
B. If the court or office is closed on that day, the act or proceeding shall be considered as done in due time if it is done on the next day afterwards on which the court or office is open ✔
C. The period is shortened by one day to adjust for the holiday
D. A penalty is automatically levied on the person obligated to perform the act
Explanation: Section 10 provides that if any act or proceeding is directed or allowed to be done in any court or office on a certain day or within a prescribed period, then, if the court or office is closed on that day or the last day of the period, the act/proceeding shall be deemed in time if done on the next day the court/office is open.
Easy NORMAL · Government | Section 3 | Definitions
Under Section 3(23) of the General Clauses Act, what does 'Government' or 'the Government' include?
A. Only the Central Government
B. Both the Central Government and any State Government ✔
C. Only municipal corporations and local authorities
D. Foreign governments recognized by India
Explanation: Section 3(23) defines 'Government' or 'the Government' to include both the Central Government and any State Government.
Hard NORMAL · Interpretation | Ut Res Magis Valeat Quam Pereat | Statutory Construction
In construing a statutory provision, if two interpretations are possible, one of which validates the provision while the other renders it redundant or unconstitutional, which rule or principle guides the courts?
A. Literal interpretation strictly without looking at consequences
B. Principle of Ut Res Magis Valeat Quam Pereat (it is better for a thing to have effect than to be made void) ✔
C. Automatic reliance on administrative circulars
D. Strict penal interpretation in favor of the prosecution
Explanation: Under canons of statutory interpretation supported by general principles and the General Clauses Act framework, courts prefer an interpretation that makes the legislation effective and workable rather than one that renders it void or redundant.
Medium NORMAL · Sign | Section 3 | Mark
Under Section 3(54) of the General Clauses Act, 'Sign' with its grammatical variations and cognate expressions, with reference to a person who is unable to write his name, includes:
A. Making his thumb impression or mark upon the document
B. Verbally authorizing a third party to forge the signature ✔
C. Leaving the signature column completely blank
D. Submitting a photograph instead of a signature
Explanation: Wait, let's verify Section 3(56) or 3(54): Under Section 3(56), 'Sign', with its grammatical variations and cognate expressions, shall, with reference to a person who is unable to write his name, include his mark, with its grammatical variations and cognate expressions.
Easy NORMAL · Section 15 | Appointment | Public Officer
If a Central Act confers power to appoint a public officer, what does Section 15 state regarding the appointment by name or office?
A. Appointments must always be made by personal name only
B. Appointments may be made either by name or by virtue of office ✔
C. Appointments must be made exclusively through competitive civil services examinations
D. Appointments cannot be made by office under any circumstances
Explanation: Section 15 specifies that where a Central Act confers a power to appoint any public officer, such appointment may be made either by name or by virtue of office.
Hard NORMAL · Political Agent | Section 3 | Definitions
Under Section 3(43) of the General Clauses Act, what is the definition of 'Political Agent'?
A. An elected member of Parliament representing a constituency
B. The principal officer appointed by the Central Government to exercise political functions in a specified territory ✔
C. A registered lobbyist hired by corporate entities
D. Any spokesperson of a recognized political party
Explanation: Section 3(43) defines 'Political Agent' as the principal officer appointed by the Central Government to exercise political functions in any territory outside India or within India as notified.
Hard NORMAL · Section 25 | Recovery of Fines | Application
Which of the following sections of the General Clauses Act deals with the recovery of fines?
A. Section 25 ✔
B. Section 6
C. Section 10
D. Section 27
Explanation: Section 25 of the General Clauses Act, 1897 deals with the recovery of fines, providing that sections 63 to 70 of the Indian Penal Code and the provisions of the Code of Criminal Procedure shall apply to such recovery.
Hard NORMAL · Section 6 | Repeal | Statutory Interpretation
What is the legal implication when an Act repeals any enactment and provides substantive new provisions without saving clauses?
A. Section 6 of the General Clauses Act automatically operates to save accrued rights, liabilities, and pending legal proceedings, unless a different intention appears ✔
B. All previous liabilities and penalties are completely wiped out without exception
C. Pending suits are transferred to the executive branch of government
D. The repealing act becomes null and void ab initio
Explanation: Section 6 acts as a statutory safety net. Even if a repealing act does not contain express saving clauses, Section 6 applies unless a different intention appears in the repealing enactment.
Easy NORMAL · Commencement | Section 3 | Definitions
Under Section 3(13) of the General Clauses Act, 'Commencement' used with reference to an Act or Regulation means:
A. The day on which the Bill is first introduced in Parliament
B. The day on which the Act or Regulation comes into operation ✔
C. The day on which the President signs the assent document
D. The day on which the notification is drafted by the ministry
Explanation: Section 3(13) defines 'Commencement' with reference to an Act or Regulation to mean the day on which the Act or Regulation comes into operation.
CASE SCENARIO: The Parliament of India passed the 'Commercial Enterprises (Regulation) Act, 2025'. The Act did not specify any date of commencement in its text. It received the assent of the President on 12th November 2025 and was published in the Official Gazette on 18th November 2025. Section 45 of the Act empowered the Central Government to frame rules for commercial registration. On 1st December 2025, the Central Government framed Commercial Rules, 2025. Later, due to industry feedback, the Central Government sought to amend these rules on 10th January 2026.
Medium SCENARIO · Commencement | Section 5 | Assent
What is the exact date of commencement of the Commercial Enterprises (Regulation) Act, 2025?
A. 12th November 2025 ✔
B. 18th November 2025
C. 1st December 2025
D. 1st January 2026
Explanation: Under Section 5 of the General Clauses Act, where an Act does not express a specific date of commencement, it comes into operation on the day on which it receives the assent of the President, which is 12th November 2025.
Medium SCENARIO · Section 21 | Rules | Amend and Rescind
Under which section of the General Clauses Act does the Central Government derive the power to amend or rescind the Commercial Rules, 2025?
A. Section 14
B. Section 16
C. Section 21 ✔
D. Section 27
Explanation: Section 21 of the General Clauses Act provides that the power to make rules, regulations, notifications, or bye-laws includes the power to add to, amend, vary, or rescind them.
Hard SCENARIO · Commencement | Section 5 | Timing
Suppose the Commercial Enterprises (Regulation) Act, 2025 was expressed to come into force on '1st December 2025'. According to Section 5, when exactly would it take effect?
A. At sunrise on 1st December 2025
B. At the expiration of 30th November 2025 ✔
C. At noon on 1st December 2025
D. At midnight between 1st and 2nd December 2025
Explanation: Section 5 specifies that where a Central Act is expressed to come into operation on a particular day, it shall come into operation on the expiration of the day preceding that day.
Medium SCENARIO · Section 14 | Powers | Exercise
If the Central Government exercises its rule-making power multiple times as occasions arise under the Act, which section validates such continuous exercise?
A. Section 14 ✔
B. Section 6
C. Section 8
D. Section 13
Explanation: Section 14 establishes that where a power is conferred by a Central Act, such power may be exercised from time to time as occasion requires.
CASE SCENARIO: M/s Apex Traders, a partnership firm, entered into a statutory contract regulated by the 'Industrial Development Act, 2018'. In 2024, Parliament repealed the Industrial Development Act, 2018 and enacted the 'New Industrial Enterprises Act, 2024', which contained provisions re-enacting several clauses of the old Act with modifications. Prior to the repeal, M/s Apex Traders had incurred a liability of Rs. 5,00,000 under the old Act. The repealing Act did not contain any specific saving clause regarding past liabilities.
Hard SCENARIO · Section 6 | Repeal | Liabilities
What is the legal status of the liability of Rs. 5,00,000 incurred by M/s Apex Traders under the repealed Act?
A. The liability is automatically extinguished because the old Act was repealed without a saving clause
B. Under Section 6, the liability is saved, and M/s Apex Traders remains liable despite the repeal ✔
C. The liability is transferred to the State Government treasury
D. The liability becomes voidable at the discretion of the firm
Explanation: Section 6 of the General Clauses Act provides that repeal does not affect any liability incurred under the repealed enactment, unless a different intention appears, operating as a statutory saving clause.
Hard SCENARIO · Section 8 | Construction of References | Re-enactment
How shall references in other existing contracts to the provisions of the repealed Industrial Development Act, 2018 be construed after the enactment of the New Industrial Enterprises Act, 2024?
A. As references to nothing, rendering the contracts void
B. As references to the provisions so re-enacted under the New Industrial Enterprises Act, 2024, under Section 8 ✔
C. As references exclusively to the Constitution of India
D. As references to state-level municipal bylaws
Explanation: Under Section 8 of the General Clauses Act, where an enactment is repealed and re-enacted, references in other enactments or instruments to the repealed provisions shall be construed as references to the provisions so re-enacted.
Medium SCENARIO · Person | Section 3 | Partnership
Under the General Clauses Act, how is 'M/s Apex Traders' (a partnership firm) classified when the term 'Person' is used in the statute?
A. It is excluded from the definition of person
B. It is included under 'Person' as an association or body of individuals, whether incorporated or not ✔
C. It is classified strictly as a government department
D. It is recognized only if registered under the Companies Act
Explanation: Section 3(42) defines 'person' to include any company or association or body of individuals, whether incorporated or not, which covers partnership firms.
Medium SCENARIO · Section 13 | Gender | Number
If M/s Apex Traders consists of partners, how does Section 13 apply regarding gender and number in the interpretation of the Act?
A. Masculine terms apply only to male partners
B. Words importing the masculine gender include females, and singular includes plural, unless repugnant to the context ✔
C. Singular words strictly exclude plural partners
D. Neuter gender applies exclusively to corporate partners
Explanation: Section 13 dictates that unless repugnant to the subject or context, words importing masculine gender include females and singular words include plural and vice versa.
CASE SCENARIO: Mr. Vikram, a businessman, was served with a statutory notice issued by a regulatory authority under a Central Act requiring him to submit compliance documents within 30 days. The notice was sent via registered post, properly addressed and prepaid, on 1st March 2026. Due to postal delays, the letter reached Mr. Vikram on 10th March 2026. The 30th day for submission fell on Sunday, 31st March 2026, on which date the regulatory office was completely closed for a public holiday.
Hard SCENARIO · Section 27 | Service by Post | Deemed Service
Under Section 27 of the General Clauses Act, when is the service of the statutory notice deemed to have been effected on Mr. Vikram?
A. On 10th March 2026 when he physically received it
B. At the time at which the letter would be delivered in the ordinary course of post ✔
C. On 1st March 2026 the moment it was handed to the post office
D. Only after Mr. Vikram files an acknowledgment receipt
Explanation: Section 27 states that service is deemed to be effected by properly addressing, prepaying, and posting a registered letter, and to have been effected at the time at which the letter would be delivered in the ordinary course of post.
Medium SCENARIO · Section 10 | Holidays | Computation of Time
According to Section 10 of the General Clauses Act, since the office was closed on Sunday, 31st March 2026, by when must Mr. Vikram submit the compliance documents?
A. On Saturday, 30th March 2026
B. On the next day afterwards on which the office is open (i.e., Monday, 1st April 2026) ✔
C. He is granted an automatic extension of 30 additional days
D. The notice stands lapsed and cannot be complied with
Explanation: Section 10 provides that if the prescribed period ends on a day on which the court or office is closed, the act is considered done in due time if performed on the next day the office is open.
Medium SCENARIO · Section 9 | Computation of Time | Exclusion
When calculating the 30-day period starting 'from' 1st March 2026, how is the first day treated under Section 9 of the General Clauses Act?
A. 1st March 2026 is excluded from the calculation ✔
B. 1st March 2026 is fully included in the calculation
C. Two days are added as penalty for starting on the 1st
D. The calculation is based on the lunar calendar
Explanation: Under Section 9, the use of the word 'from' excludes the first day in a series of days or period of time.
Easy SCENARIO · Year | Section 3 | Calendar
If the statutory time period expired on the last day, and that day was reckoned according to the British calendar, which section defines 'Year' or 'Calendar' in this context?
A. Section 3(65) ✔
B. Section 3(26)
C. Section 3(42)
D. Section 3(13)
Explanation: Section 3(65) defines 'year' to mean a year reckoned according to the British calendar.
CASE SCENARIO: The Central Board of Excise and Customs issued an order appointing Mr. Sharma as a 'Special Adjudication Officer' by virtue of his office as Joint Commissioner. Six months later, the Board decided to suspend Mr. Sharma pending an inquiry into administrative irregularities. Mr. Sharma challenged the suspension, arguing that the appointing authority did not possess the power to suspend him once appointed without a separate disciplinary statute.
Medium SCENARIO · Section 16 | Appointment | Suspension
Under Section 16 of the General Clauses Act, does the power to make an appointment include the power to suspend or dismiss?
A. No, suspension requires a separate constitutional amendment
B. Yes, the power to appoint includes the power to suspend or dismiss any person appointed, unless a different intention appears ✔
C. Only dismissal is included, while suspension is strictly prohibited
D. Only the High Court can suspend a public officer appointed by the Board
Explanation: Section 16 expressly lays down that the power to appoint includes the power to suspend or dismiss the person appointed, unless a different intention appears in the enactment.
Medium SCENARIO · Section 15 | Appointment | Public Officer
Under Section 15 of the General Clauses Act, was the Board's appointment of Mr. Sharma 'by virtue of his office' legally valid?
A. No, public officers must always be appointed by personal name only
B. Yes, appointments under Central Acts may be made either by name or by virtue of office ✔
C. Only the President of India can make appointments by virtue of office
D. Appointments by office are void ab initio
Explanation: Section 15 specifies that where a Central Act confers power to appoint any public officer, such appointment may be made either by name or by virtue of office.
Hard SCENARIO · Good Faith | Section 3 | Negligence
If Mr. Sharma acted honestly in an administrative decision, although he committed a minor procedural negligence, how is 'Good Faith' evaluated under Section 3(22) of the General Clauses Act?
A. It is not in good faith because negligence was present
B. It is deemed to be done in good faith if it is in fact done honestly, whether negligent or not ✔
C. Good faith requires absolute perfection without any procedural error
D. Good faith is determined exclusively by police investigation reports
Explanation: Section 3(22) defines good faith under the General Clauses Act as anything done honestly, whether done negligently or not.
Easy SCENARIO · Official Gazette | Section 3 | Definitions
If the order appointing Mr. Sharma was notified in the Official Gazette, what does Section 3(39) generally define 'Official Gazette' to mean?
A. Any privately published newspaper in the district
B. The Gazette of India or the Official Gazette of a State ✔
C. Social media handles of government ministries
D. Annual reports published by corporate bodies
Explanation: Section 3(39) defines 'Official Gazette' to mean the Gazette of India or the Official Gazette of a State, as applicable.
CASE SCENARIO: An economic legislation enacted by Parliament contained provisions penalizing tax evasion, including the imposition of substantial financial fines. A corporate entity, Zeta Ltd., was found guilty of violating the statute. Zeta Ltd. contended that since the company is an artificial legal person and not a natural human being, penal fines and criminal provisions under the Act should not apply to it. Furthermore, the company owned a commercial warehouse built permanently on land, which the tax authorities sought to attach as immovable property.
Medium SCENARIO · Person | Section 3 | Company
Under Section 3(42) of the General Clauses Act, does the term 'Person' include Zeta Ltd., an artificial corporate body?
A. No, 'person' strictly refers to living human beings
B. Yes, 'person' includes any company or association or body of individuals, whether incorporated or not ✔
C. Only public sector companies are included under 'person'
D. Foreign companies are included, but domestic companies are excluded
Explanation: Section 3(42) defines 'person' to include any company or association or body of individuals, whether incorporated or not.
Medium SCENARIO · Immovable Property | Section 3 | Warehouse
How is Zeta Ltd.'s commercial warehouse permanently fastened to the earth classified under Section 3(26) of the General Clauses Act?
A. Movable property because it is a commercial asset
B. Immovable property because it includes things attached to the earth or permanently fastened to anything attached to the earth ✔
C. Intangible property like a trademark
D. Standing timber
Explanation: Section 3(26) defines 'immovable property' to include land, benefits arising out of land, and things attached to the earth or permanently fastened to anything attached to the earth.
Hard SCENARIO · Section 25 | Recovery of Fines | Application
Which section of the General Clauses Act governs the recovery of fines imposed on Zeta Ltd. under the Central Act?
A. Section 25 ✔
B. Section 6
C. Section 27
D. Section 10
Explanation: Section 25 of the General Clauses Act specifically deals with the recovery of fines, making provisions of the IPC and CrPC applicable to such recovery.
Medium SCENARIO · Section 13 | Number | Singular and Plural
If the Act used words importing the singular number with respect to offending directors of Zeta Ltd., how does Section 13 apply?
A. Singular words strictly apply to only one director and never more
B. Words in the singular include the plural and vice versa, unless repugnant to the context ✔
C. Plural words require explicit re-enactment by Parliament
D. Singular words apply exclusively to female directors
Explanation: Section 13 prescribes that words in the singular include the plural and vice versa, unless there is anything repugnant in the subject or context.

Paper 2: Corporate and Other Laws · Module 3 · Chapter 2:

Law — 55 rows
Easy NORMAL · Literal Rule | Primary Rule | Plain Meaning
What is the primary objective of interpreting a statute when the language of the legislative enactment is plain, clear, and unambiguous?
A. To ascertain the intention of the legislature exclusively from the words used ✔
B. To modify the meaning to achieve a perceived social justice outcome
C. To consult parliamentary debates and committee reports to find hidden intents
D. To read words into the statute to cure any perceived legislative oversight
Explanation: Under the primary rule of literal construction, when words are clear and unambiguous, the intention of the legislature must be gathered from the language itself. No external aids or modifications are permitted unless the plain meaning leads to an absurdity.
Easy NORMAL · Golden Rule | Absurdity | Statutory Modification
Which rule of interpretation is applied when the literal meaning of a statutory provision leads to a manifest absurdity, repugnancy, or inconsistency with the rest of the Act?
A. The Mischief Rule
B. The Golden Rule ✔
C. The Rule of Ejusdem Generis
D. The Rule of Contemporanea Expositio
Explanation: The Golden Rule serves as a modification of the literal rule. It permits the court to modify the ordinary grammatical meaning of words just to the extent necessary to avoid absurdity, repugnancy, or inconsistency.
Easy NORMAL · Mischief Rule | Heydon's Case | Historical Background
In which landmark English case was the 'Mischief Rule' (or Heydon's Rule) first laid down?
A. Salomon v. Salomon & Co. Ltd.
B. Heydon's Case ✔
C. Eastman Photographic Materials Co. v. Comptroller General
D. R v. Judge of the City of London Court
Explanation: Heydon's Case (1584) established the Mischief Rule, which directs courts to consider the common law before the Act, the mischief and defect for which the common law did not provide, and the true reason of the remedy.
Medium NORMAL · Ejusdem Generis | Genus | Specific and General Words
When applying the rule of 'Ejusdem Generis', what is the fundamental prerequisite regarding the specific words listed in the statute?
A. They must be exhaustive and cover all conceivable objects.
B. They must constitute a distinct category or genus without any common feature.
C. They must constitute an ascertainable category or genus to which the general words can be related. ✔
D. They must be followed by a non-obstante clause.
Explanation: Ejusdem Generis ('of the same kind or species') requires that the preceding specific words form a distinct genus or category. General words following them are then construed as applying only to things of the same kind.
Medium NORMAL · Strict Construction | Penal Statute | Ambiguity
How is a penal statute traditionally construed by the courts in case of an ambiguity regarding the coverage of an offense or penalty?
A. Strictly in favor of the State to ensure public safety
B. Liberally to fulfill the broad socio-economic objectives of the legislature
C. Strictly in favor of the subject or accused person ✔
D. Dynamically based on contemporary social mores
Explanation: Penal statutes and taxing statutes must be construed strictly. If two reasonable meanings are possible, the construction which favors the subject (the accused or taxpayer) must be adopted.
Medium NORMAL · Non-Obstante Clause | Overriding Effect | Statutory Provisions
What is the legal effect of a 'Non-Obstante Clause' (typically beginning with 'Notwithstanding anything contained in...') in a statutory provision?
A. It subjects the provision to all other prevailing laws.
B. It overrides any contrary provisions contained in other parts of the same Act or other statutes. ✔
C. It acts merely as a descriptive preamble without operational force.
D. It requires mandatory prior presidential assent before enforcement.
Explanation: A non-obstante clause is a legislative device used to give the enacting part of a section an overriding effect over any contrary provision in the same or another statute.
Easy NORMAL · Internal Aids | Statement of Objects and Reasons | Bill Background
Which internal aid to interpretation explains the immediate objectives and reasons for introducing a Bill in the legislature, though it cannot control the clear meaning of the enactment?
A. Marginal Note
B. Proviso
C. Preamble
D. Statement of Objects and Reasons ✔
Explanation: The Statement of Objects and Reasons accompanies a Bill to explain the background and purpose of the proposed legislation. While useful for understanding the historical setting, it is not part of the enacted statute and cannot override clear statutory text.
Medium NORMAL · Proviso | Exception | Internal Aids
What is the primary function of a 'Proviso' in a statute?
A. To repeal existing inconsistent enactments automatically
B. To carve out an exception or qualify the main enacting portion of the section ✔
C. To provide long titles for judicial reference
D. To replace the substantive penal clauses with civil remedies
Explanation: A proviso is normally inserted to qualify or except something out of the main enactment, or to provide something which would otherwise be outside the enacting clause. It must not be construed as a general independent enactment.
Medium NORMAL · Marginal Notes | Internal Aids | Legislative Process
Are marginal notes (side notes) appended to sections of an Act considered a safe and conclusive guide for interpreting the scope of that section?
A. Yes, because they are inserted by the legislature during the final vote.
B. No, because they are not part of the statute as passed by the legislature and are merely inserted for convenience. ✔
C. Yes, provided they are supported by contemporary exposition.
D. No, unless the section is completely silent on its title.
Explanation: Marginal notes are not framed by the legislature nor voted upon; they are inserted by editors or draftsmen for convenience. Hence, they cannot control the plain meaning of the section, though they may offer some guidance if ambiguity exists.
Easy NORMAL · Noscitur a Sociis | Contextual Meaning | Associated Words
What does the maxim 'Noscitur a Sociis' signify in statutory interpretation?
A. A word is known by the company it keeps ✔
B. Express mention of one thing implies the exclusion of another
C. General words must be restricted to things of the same genus
D. The contemporaneous exposition is the best and strongest in law
Explanation: Noscitur a Sociis means that the meaning of an ambiguous word or phrase is ascertained by examining the words associated with it in the context ('a word is known by the company it keeps').
Medium NORMAL · Expressio Unius | Exclusion | Statutory Maxims
What is the implication of the maxim 'Expressio Unius Est Exclusio Alterius'?
A. To express one thing is to exclude another ✔
B. No person can be punished twice for the same offense
C. The language must be read in its ordinary grammatical sense
D. An exception proves the rule in cases not excepted
Explanation: Expressio Unius Est Exclusio Alterius means that the express mention of one thing implies the exclusion of another. If a statute specifies certain items, unmentioned items of the same class are presumed to be excluded.
Hard NORMAL · External Aids | Legislative Debates | Hansard
When can an external aid such as 'legislative debates' (Hansard) be referred to by a court for interpreting a modern statute under Indian law?
A. Whenever the literal interpretation is contested by either party
B. To discover the subjective intent of individual members who voted
C. To ascertain the historical background and the mischief sought to be remedied when the text is ambiguous ✔
D. Under no circumstances, as parliamentary history is completely barred in India
Explanation: While earlier courts strictly barred legislative debates, modern jurisprudence permits reference to parliamentary history, speeches, and committee reports (external aids) to understand the surrounding circumstances and mischief when ambiguity exists.
Medium NORMAL · Taxing Statute | Strict Construction | No Equity
How are taxing statutes generally interpreted by Indian courts?
A. Strictly; there is no equity in taxation, and a taxpayer cannot be taxed unless the language unambiguously imposes it ✔
B. Liberally; to ensure maximum revenue collection for public welfare programs
C. Purposively; ignoring literal words to capture economic substance
D. Dynamically; adjusting tax rates based on inflation indices
Explanation: Taxing statutes must be interpreted strictly. There is no room for intendment or equity; if a person is not plainly brought within the letter of the law, they cannot be taxed.
Easy NORMAL · Preamble | Internal Aids | Statute Purpose
What is the role of a 'Preamble' in an Act of Parliament?
A. It contains the operative penal provisions for violation of the Act.
B. It acts as a key to open the minds of the makers and sets out the main scope and purpose of the Act. ✔
C. It provides procedural rules for subordinate legislation.
D. It overrides explicit substantive sections in case of a direct conflict.
Explanation: The preamble expresses the scope, object, and purpose of the Act. It is often described as a 'key to the understanding of the Act', though it cannot restrict or extend the clear and unambiguous enacting provisions.
Hard NORMAL · Contemporanea Expositio | Historical Interpretation | Long Usage
What does the maxim 'Contemporanea Expositio Est Optima Et Fortissima In Lege' mean?
A. The best and strongest interpretation of a statute is that which is made by contemporary authorities over a long period ✔
B. Statutes enacted contemporaneously must be read together as a code
C. Later laws repeal earlier inconsistent laws
D. General provisions do not derogate from special provisions
Explanation: Contemporanea Expositio means that a statute is best interpreted according to the construction put upon it by contemporary authority and long usage, especially in respect of older or ancient statutes.
Hard NORMAL · Repeal | Accrued Rights | General Clauses Act
What is the effect of a repeal of a validating Act or a statute on rights and liabilities already acquired or accrued under it, as per general General Clauses Act principles?
A. All past transactions become null and void automatically.
B. Accrued rights and incurred liabilities are generally protected unless a contrary intention appears. ✔
C. The repeal has retrospective criminal liability for past acts.
D. The repealed Act continues in force indefinitely without notification.
Explanation: Unless a different intention appears, the repeal of an enactment does not affect any right, privilege, obligation, or liability previously acquired, accrued, or incurred under the repealed enactment (Section 6 of the General Clauses Act principles incorporated in interpretation).
Medium NORMAL · Harmonious Construction | Ut Res Magis Valeat Quam Pereat | Conflicting Provisions
When two provisions in the same statute appear to be repugnant to each other, what is the primary duty of the court in interpretation?
A. To strike down both provisions for uncertainty
B. To harmonize them so that full effect can be given to both, if possible (Ut Res Magis Valeat Quam Pereat) ✔
C. To automatically apply the latter provision as it was enacted last in the text
D. To refer the matter back to the executive for clarification
Explanation: Courts must attempt to harmonize conflicting provisions so that effect is given to both (Ut Res Magis Valeat Quam Pereat — it is better that a thing should have effect than that it should perish), rather than rendering one nugatory.
Medium NORMAL · Subordinate Legislation | Ultra Vires | Enabling Act
What is the primary function of 'Subordinate Legislation' (such as rules, regulations, and bylaws) framed under an enabling Act?
A. To amend or repeal the parent enabling Act at will
B. To carry out the purposes of the parent Act without exceeding the powers conferred (ultra vires) ✔
C. To levy retrospective taxes without parliamentary approval
D. To override fundamental constitutional rights
Explanation: Subordinate legislation must remain within the four corners of the parent (enabling) Act. Any rule or regulation that goes beyond the authority conferred by the parent Act is ultra vires and void.
Medium NORMAL · Generalia Specialibus Non Derogant | Special vs General | Statutory Conflict
What does the legal maxim 'Generalia Specialibus Non Derogant' imply?
A. General things do not derogate from special things ✔
B. Special things must always yield to general enactments
C. General laws automatically repeal special laws
D. Special provisions apply only when general provisions are silent
Explanation: Generalia specialibus non derogant means that if a special provision is made on a specific subject matter, that subject matter is excluded from the general provision.
Easy NORMAL · External Aids | Dictionaries | Internal vs External
Which of the following is classified as an 'External Aid' to statutory interpretation?
A. Marginal notes
B. Schedules
C. Dictionaries ✔
D. Headings of chapters
Explanation: Dictionaries are external aids to interpretation because they exist outside the statutory text. Marginal notes, schedules, and chapter headings are internal aids found within the statute itself.
Hard NORMAL · Casus Omissus | Judicial Restraint | Filling Gaps
Under what circumstance may a court read words into an Act of Parliament (filling a 'casus omissus')?
A. Whenever the court believes the legislature forgot to mention a desirable policy
B. Never, as courts cannot supply a casus omissus unless clear and unmistakable context demands it to avoid total absurdity ✔
C. Whenever the executive ministry issues a circular requesting expansion
D. In all cases of beneficial social legislation
Explanation: A casus omissus (an omission in a statute) cannot be supplied by a court of law, except in the case of clear and gross necessity where the literal interpretation leaves the statute totally unworkable or absurd.
Medium NORMAL · Schedules | Internal Aids | Statute Structure
What is the significance of 'Schedules' appended to an Act?
A. They are merely decorative annexures with no legal binding force.
B. They form an integral part of the statute and contain operational details, forms, or lists subsidiary to the main sections. ✔
C. They override the main body of the Act if there is any inconsistency.
D. They are treated as external aids created by administrative committees.
Explanation: Schedules are an integral part of the statute, often containing transitional provisions, forms, or lists of repealed enactments. However, if there is an irreconcilable conflict between the body of the Act and a schedule, the body prevails.
Medium NORMAL · Beneficial Construction | Social Welfare | Liberal Interpretation
How should a 'Beneficial Construction' (liberal interpretation) be applied to social welfare or labor legislations?
A. Strictly against the worker to protect employer capital
B. So as to suppress the mischief and advance the remedy intended by the legislature ✔
C. By ignoring the statutory language entirely in favor of equity
D. By restricting benefits exclusively to unionized members
Explanation: Beneficial construction requires that where a statute is enacted for the benefit of a particular class (e.g., labor or consumers), it should be interpreted liberally to advance the remedy and suppress the mischief, rather than adopting a narrow literal constriction.
Hard NORMAL · Proviso | Repugnancy | Harmonious Construction
What is the legal effect of a 'Proviso' when it is repugnant to the substantive enacting part of a section?
A. The proviso is completely void and ignored.
B. The proviso prevails as it is the later clause in the section text.
C. The court must harmonize them; if impossible, the proviso operates as an exception to the main enactment pro tanto. ✔
D. The entire section is struck down for internal contradiction.
Explanation: A proviso is meant to qualify the main enactment. If there is a direct repugnancy between the proviso and the main body, the proviso operates as an exception to the extent of the inconsistency, though harmonizing is always the first attempt.
Medium NORMAL · Ejusdem Generis | Specific and General | Class of Words
Which of the following describes the rule of 'Ejusdem Generis'?
A. Where specific words are followed by general words, the general words are construed as applying to things of the same class as the specific words. ✔
B. Where general words precede specific words, the specific words restrict the general words retroactively.
C. Words in a statute must be given their dictionary meaning regardless of context.
D. Earlier statutes govern later statutes on the same subject.
Explanation: Ejusdem Generis dictates that when specific words of the same family or genus are followed by general terms (e.g., 'dogs, cats, and other animals'), the general term ('other animals') is restricted to domestic quadrupeds of a similar nature.
Hard NORMAL · Dictionary Meanings | Trade Usage | Commercial Statutes
What role do 'Dictionary meanings' play when a technical term is used in a commercial or trade statute?
A. Dictionary meanings override trade usage in every instance.
B. Trade or commercial usage and understanding take precedence over general dictionary meanings if the term has acquired a specific trade sense. ✔
C. Dictionaries are strictly prohibited in commercial law interpretation.
D. Judges must rely exclusively on foreign legal dictionaries.
Explanation: In commercial and trade statutes, words are understood in the sense in which they are used in commerce and trade, even if it differs from the general or literal dictionary meaning.
Medium NORMAL · Headings | Internal Aids | Statutory Grouping
What is the purpose of a 'Heading' prefixed to a group of sections in an Act?
A. To serve as a preamble for the entire enactment
B. To act as a key to interpret the meaning of ambiguous sections within that group ✔
C. To replace the marginal notes completely
D. To act as an absolute binding enactment overriding section texts
Explanation: Headings prefixed to sections or groups of sections operate as internal aids and can be referred to as a key to resolve ambiguity or to determine the scope of the sections falling under them.
Medium NORMAL · Ut Res Magis Valeat Quam Pereat | Workable Interpretation | Validation
What is meant by the rule 'Ut Res Magis Valeat Quam Pereat'?
A. It is better for a statute to be declared void than to cause ambiguity.
B. An interpretation which validates and gives effect to a provision should be chosen over one that renders it meaningless or dead. ✔
C. Penal statutes must be strictly construed against the State.
D. Specific words override general words.
Explanation: Ut Res Magis Valeat Quam Pereat means 'it is better that a thing should have effect than that it should perish'. Courts must lean towards an interpretation that makes the statute workable and valid rather than redundant.
Hard NORMAL · Commencement | Presidential Assent | General Clauses Act
When is an Act of Parliament deemed to come into operation if no specific commencement date is stated within the Act itself (under general statutory rules in India)?
A. On the date the Bill was first introduced in Parliament
B. On the date it receives the assent of the President ✔
C. Six months after presidential assent
D. On the date published in the official gazette by executive notification
Explanation: As per Section 5 of the General Clauses Act, where an Act is not expressed to come into operation on a particular day, it shall come into operation on the day on which it receives the assent of the President (or Governor in case of State Acts).
Hard NORMAL · Explanation | Internal Aids | Scope Clarification
Can an internal aid such as 'Explanation' attached to a section expand the plain meaning of the main provision?
A. No, an explanation can only clarify obscurity and cannot enlarge the main section's scope.
B. Yes, an explanation is designed to clarify the meaning and can sometimes broaden or explain the true intent of the section. ✔
C. Explanations have no legal standing whatsoever.
D. Explanations automatically repeal the main section if there is friction.
Explanation: An explanation is inserted to clarify any obscurity or ambiguity in the main provision. While its primary purpose is explanation, it often broadens or explains the true scope of the provision to ensure the legislative intent is fulfilled.
CASE SCENARIO: Zenith Corp, a manufacturing company registered in Mumbai, faced a regulatory inquiry regarding a waste disposal provision under the National Environmental Safety Act, 2010. Section 45 of the Act prohibited factories from discharging 'acids, alkalis, oils, or other deleterious liquids' into municipal drains. Zenith Corp discharged biodegradable liquid detergent waste, arguing it was neither an acid, alkali, nor oil. The pollution control board contended that detergent waste fell under 'other deleterious liquids'. The Act also contained a marginal note to Section 45 titled 'Disposal of industrial effluents', and a proviso permitting treated organic waste under specific licenses.
Hard SCENARIO · Ejusdem Generis | Scenario | Statutory Construction
Which rule of statutory interpretation is most appropriate for the court to determine whether 'liquid detergent waste' falls under 'other deleterious liquids' following 'acids, alkalis, oils'?
A. Heydon's Mischief Rule
B. Rule of Ejusdem Generis ✔
C. Golden Rule of Absurdity
D. Contemporanea Expositio
Explanation: The rule of Ejusdem Generis applies here because specific words ('acids, alkalis, oils') form a genus, followed by general words ('other deleterious liquids'). The general words must be interpreted in light of the specific polluting characteristics of the preceding items.
Medium SCENARIO · Marginal Notes | Internal Aids | Scenario
What is the legal standing of the marginal note 'Disposal of industrial effluents' attached to Section 45?
A. It is a conclusive indicator that only heavy industrial effluents are prohibited.
B. It is an internal aid that may offer slight guidance but cannot control the clear enacting words of Section 45. ✔
C. It overrides the specific categories listed in the text of the section.
D. It constitutes an external aid framed by administrative tribunals.
Explanation: Marginal notes are internal aids to interpretation. While they can provide general context or guidance if ambiguity exists, they cannot restrict or override the clear operational language of the statutory section.
Medium SCENARIO · Proviso | Exception | Scenario
How should the proviso permitting treated organic waste under specific licenses be interpreted in relation to the main enacting provision of Section 45?
A. As an independent charging section creating new offenses
B. As an exception carved out from the main prohibition to qualify its operation ✔
C. As a non-obstante clause overriding all environmental safety norms
D. As a preamble describing legislative history
Explanation: A proviso is designed to qualify or carve out an exception from the main enacting provision. Here, it creates a specific exception for treated organic waste under license, leaving the general prohibition intact otherwise.
Hard SCENARIO · Penal Statute | Strict Construction | Scenario
If Section 45 imposed criminal penalties for violation, how should the court construe the ambiguous phrase 'other deleterious liquids'?
A. Liberally in favor of the pollution board to protect public health
B. Strictly in favor of Zenith Corp, resolving any reasonable doubt in favor of the accused ✔
C. Dynamically based on contemporary environmental lobbying
D. By consulting cabinet committee minutes without restriction
Explanation: Penal statutes carrying criminal sanctions must be construed strictly. If an ambiguity exists regarding whether detergent waste is covered, the interpretation favoring the subject (Zenith Corp) must be adopted.
CASE SCENARIO: The State Legislature of Maharashtra passed the Urban Commercial Tenancy Act, 2024. Section 12 stated that 'no landlord shall evict a tenant except on grounds of non-payment of rent.' However, Section 18 of the same Act contained a non-obstante clause: 'Notwithstanding anything contained in Section 12, a landlord running a registered educational trust may evict commercial tenants for bona fide institutional expansion.' A dispute arose between landlord Apex Trust and tenant Metro Bookstores, where Apex Trust sought eviction for institutional expansion under Section 18, while Metro Bookstores relied on Section 12.
Medium SCENARIO · Non-Obstante Clause | Overriding Effect | Scenario
What is the legal effect of the non-obstante clause in Section 18 ('Notwithstanding anything contained in Section 12...')?
A. It renders Section 12 entirely unconstitutional and nullified.
B. It gives Section 18 an overriding effect over Section 12 to the extent of institutional expansion by registered educational trusts. ✔
C. It subordinates Section 18 to Section 12 in all commercial tenancy matters.
D. It serves merely as a preamble without operational impact.
Explanation: A non-obstante clause is a legislative tool intended to give the enacting part in which it is used an overriding effect over contrary provisions in the same or other acts, specifically here permitting Apex Trust to evoke eviction under Section 18.
Medium SCENARIO · Harmonious Construction | Ut Res Magis Valeat Quam Pereat | Scenario
If Sections 12 and 18 appeared to directly clash without a non-obstante clause, which rule of interpretation would the court first employ?
A. The rule of harmonious construction (Ut Res Magis Valeat Quam Pereat) ✔
B. The rule of literal destruction of both clauses
C. The rule of strict penal construction
D. Reference to foreign judicial precedents
Explanation: When two provisions in an Act appear repugnant, the court's primary duty is to harmonize them so that effect is given to both, fulfilling the principle of Ut Res Magis Valeat Quam Pereat.
Hard SCENARIO · Noscitur a Sociis | Statutory Context | Scenario
How should the term 'landlord' appearing in the Act be interpreted if the statute is silent on whether it includes sub-lessors?
A. By applying the principle of Noscitur a Sociis and examining associated tenancy terms in the context of the Act ✔
B. By arbitrarily substituting the definition from the Rent Control Act of 1948 without context
C. By assuming the legislature forgot sub-lessors and ignoring the omission
D. By applying the strict taxing statute rule
Explanation: When a term's scope is ambiguous, Noscitur a Sociis ('a word is known by the company it keeps') guides the court to ascertain its meaning from the surrounding statutory context and associated provisions.
Medium SCENARIO · Headings | Internal Aids | Scenario
Are the headings prefixed to the chapters of the Urban Commercial Tenancy Act, 2024 considered binding operational law?
A. Yes, they carry equal weight to the substantive sections.
B. No, headings are internal aids used only as a key to interpret ambiguous sections and cannot override clear section text. ✔
C. Yes, provided they were debated on the floor of the assembly.
D. No, headings are classified as external aids.
Explanation: Headings are internal aids. While useful for resolving ambiguities or understanding the structural grouping, they cannot control or override the plain and clear text of the operative sections.
CASE SCENARIO: In 2025, the Parliament enacted the Digital Assets Taxation Act. Section 8 imposed a levy of 30% on 'transfer of any virtual digital asset, cryptocurrency, or token'. Taxpayer Rohan transferred a non-fungible digital token representing ownership of digital art and claimed exemption under a broad welfare notification issued by the Finance Ministry under a general rule-making power in Section 25. The tax department argued that Section 8 was a specific charging provision, and general rules could not exempt asset transfers not expressly provided for in the parent Act.
Medium SCENARIO · Taxing Statute | Strict Construction | Scenario
How must Section 8 of the Digital Assets Taxation Act be interpreted as a taxing statute?
A. Strictly; there is no equity in taxation, and tax liability must be explicitly and unambiguously imposed by the letter of the law ✔
B. Liberally; to maximize government revenue for digital infrastructure
C. Purposively; disregarding statutory text to capture economic reality
D. Dynamically; adjusting rates based on cryptocurrency market fluctuations
Explanation: Taxing statutes are construed strictly. If a taxpayer does not fall squarely within the letter of the charging provision, no tax can be imposed by intendment or equity.
Hard SCENARIO · Subordinate Legislation | Ultra Vires | Scenario
Which maxim governs the relationship between the parent Act's specific charging provision (Section 8) and subordinate rule-making power (Section 25)?
A. Generalia specialibus non derogant
B. Subordinate legislation cannot override or contradict the parent Act's substantive provisions (Ultra Vires) ✔
C. Contemporanea expositio est optima et fortissima in lege
D. Expressio unius est exclusio alterius
Explanation: Subordinate legislation (rules, notifications) must remain within the scope of the parent Act. Any rule that grants an exemption contrary to or exceeding the parent Act's charging provisions is ultra vires and void.
Medium SCENARIO · Preamble | Internal Aids | Scenario
