What role does the 'Preamble' of the Digital Assets Taxation Act play if Rohan claims an ambiguity in the definition of 'virtual digital asset'?
A. The preamble acts as a key to open the minds of the makers and clarify the scope, though it cannot override clear text. ✔
B. The preamble serves as the operational charging section.
C. The preamble is an external aid created by the judiciary.
D. The preamble automatically grants tax exemptions to all artists.
Explanation: The preamble states the purpose and scope of the legislation and acts as a key to understanding ambiguous provisions, though it cannot restrict or extend clear statutory text.
Hard SCENARIO · Noscitur a Sociis | Associated Words | Scenario
If the term 'token' appears alongside 'virtual digital asset' and 'cryptocurrency', what principle of interpretation helps determine whether Rohan's NFT is covered?
A. Noscitur a Sociis ✔
B. Heydon's Rule
C. Casus Omissus
D. Golden Rule
Explanation: Noscitur a Sociis ('a word is known by the company it keeps') assists in interpreting 'token' by looking at its association with 'virtual digital asset' and 'cryptocurrency' within the digital finance context.
CASE SCENARIO: The Central Labour Welfare Act enacted in 1990 mandated that factories employing 'more than one hundred workers' must provide crèche facilities. Apex Manufacturing plant at Pune employed 95 permanent workers and 15 regular daily-wage contract workers on factory premises. The labor inspector slapped a penalty for non-compliance. Apex Manufacturing contested the penalty, arguing that 'workers' under Section 3 referred strictly to permanent direct payroll employees, excluding contract workers.
Medium SCENARIO · Beneficial Construction | Social Welfare | Scenario
Which rule of interpretation is primarily applied when construing a social welfare and labor legislation like the Central Labour Welfare Act?
A. Strict Construction in favor of the employer
B. Beneficial Construction (Ut Res Magis Valeat / Liberal interpretation to advance the remedy) ✔
C. Literal Construction without regard to worker safety
D. Literal rule favoring strict penal liability
Explanation: Beneficial legislation enacted for the welfare of workers is interpreted liberally to suppress the mischief and advance the remedy intended by the legislature, favoring the protected class.
Hard SCENARIO · Purposive Interpretation | Labor Law | Scenario
How should the term 'workers' be interpreted in light of modern industrial jurisprudence and the context of labor welfare?
A. Restricted strictly to permanent employees on the muster roll
B. Inclusive of contract workers engaged in regular factory operations to prevent statutory evasion ✔
C. Limited exclusively to supervisory management staff
D. Excluded entirely if paid on a daily wage basis
Explanation: In labor statutes, welfare provisions are interpreted purposively to include contract workers who work on premises, preventing employers from evading obligations through outsourcing.
Hard SCENARIO · Casus Omissus | Judicial Interpretation | Scenario
If the employer invokes a literal interpretation claiming an omission (casus omissus) of contract workers from the definition section, can the court supply the omission?
A. Yes, whenever it seems fair to the executive branch.
B. No, a casus omissus cannot be supplied by courts unless clear statutory context and necessity demand it to avoid absurdity. ✔
C. Yes, in all labor disputes automatically.
D. No, courts must strike down the entire Act if an omission exists.
Explanation: Courts cannot supply a casus omissus (an omission) unless the clear and unmistakable context of the statute compels it. However, interpreting 'workers' broadly to include contract workers is a matter of statutory definition scope rather than supplying an omission.
Medium SCENARIO · Statement of Objects and Reasons | Internal Aids | Scenario
What is the status of the 'Statement of Objects and Reasons' attached to the Labour Welfare Bill when interpreting the scope of 'workers'?
A. It is binding law that overrides section definitions.
B. It is an internal aid showing the historical background and intent of the Bill, but cannot control the plain statutory text. ✔
C. It is an external aid that replaces the preamble.
D. It has no legal relevance whatsoever under Indian jurisprudence.
Explanation: The Statement of Objects and Reasons explains the background and purpose of introducing the Bill. While helpful for understanding historical setting, it is not part of the enacted statute and cannot override statutory wording.
CASE SCENARIO: A colonial-era enactment, the Ancient Transport Corridors Act, 1890, used the term 'carriages' in Section 14 to regulate tolls on roads. In 2024, the local municipality sought to levy tolls on modern electric autonomous delivery pods operating on those same corridors. TransLogistics Inc. challenged the toll, arguing that 'carriages' in an 1890 statute could not possibly encompass modern robotic delivery pods driven by artificial intelligence.
Hard SCENARIO · Always Speaking Doctrine | Dynamic Interpretation | Scenario
Which interpretive approach addresses whether statutory terms drafted in the past ('carriages') can apply to modern technological innovations ('autonomous delivery pods')?
A. The doctrine of original intent (freezing meaning to 1890)
B. The 'always speaking' statute doctrine (updating construction) ✔
C. The doctrine of Contemporanea Expositio exclusively
D. The strict penal rule
Explanation: Under the 'always speaking' doctrine, statutes are generally treated as always speaking. Words can accommodate modern technological developments falling within the statutory genus or purpose.
Hard SCENARIO · Contemporanea Expositio | Ancient Statutes | Scenario
How does the doctrine of 'Contemporanea Expositio' apply to an 1890 statute interpreted in modern times?
A. It requires courts to ignore all modern precedents.
B. It emphasizes how contemporary authorities interpreted the Act in 1890, though it must be balanced against modern statutory dynamics. ✔
C. It automatically repeals statutes older than 50 years.
D. It permits executive officers to rewrite definitions without notification.
Explanation: Contemporanea Expositio looks at how ancient statutes were understood by contemporary authorities. However, for evolving terms, courts balance historical usage with the 'always speaking' doctrine.
Medium SCENARIO · Ejusdem Generis | Statutory Maxims | Scenario
If the term 'carriages' is followed by general words like 'and other wheeled conveyances', which interpretative rule assists in classification?
A. Ejusdem Generis ✔
B. Heydon's Mischief Rule
C. Strict Penal Construction
D. Non-Obstante application
Explanation: Ejusdem Generis applies where specific terms ('carriages') are followed by general words ('other wheeled conveyances'), restricting the general words to conveyances of a similar wheeled nature.
Medium SCENARIO · Legislative Intent | Statutory Purpose | Scenario
What is the primary objective of the court when interpreting ambiguous terminology in a regulatory statute of this nature?
A. To ascertain and give effect to the true legislative intent and statutory purpose ✔
B. To invalidate the statute for vagueness
C. To substitute executive administrative circulars for judicial reasoning
D. To strictly favor commercial enterprises over public municipalities
Explanation: The overarching goal of all statutory interpretation is to ascertain the intention of the legislature and give effect to the true purpose and object of the enactment.

Paper 2: Corporate and Other Laws · Module 3 · Chapter 3:

Law — 55 rows
Easy NORMAL · FEMA Objectives | Preamble | Introduction
What is the primary objective of the Foreign Exchange Management Act (FEMA), 1999 as stated in its preamble?
A. To conserve foreign exchange reserves of India and promote external trade and payments ✔
B. To criminalize all unauthorized foreign exchange transactions and penalize offenders with imprisonment
C. To regulate the stock exchange and protect the interests of investors in securities
D. To control the import of goods and services through absolute licensing
Explanation: FEMA, 1999 was enacted to consolidate and amend the law relating to foreign exchange with the objective of facilitating external trade and payments and for promoting the orderly development and maintenance of foreign exchange market in India. Unlike FERA, FEMA treats offenses as civil rather than criminal. Therefore, the correct option highlights facilitating external trade and payments and conserving reserves.
Easy NORMAL · RBI Powers | Administration | Regulatory Authority
Under FEMA, 1999, who holds the primary authority for making rules relating to foreign exchange transactions in consultation with the Central Government?
A. Securities and Exchange Board of India (SEBI)
B. Reserve Bank of India (RBI) ✔
C. Ministry of Corporate Affairs (MCA)
D. Directorate General of Foreign Trade (DGFT)
Explanation: Under the provisions of FEMA, 1999, the Reserve Bank of India (RBI) plays the central role in framing regulations and rules regarding foreign exchange transactions, capital account transactions, and current account transactions in consultation with the Central Government.
Medium NORMAL · Capital Account Transaction | Definitions | Section 2
Which of the following is defined as a 'Capital Account Transaction' under Section 2(e) of FEMA, 1999?
A. Payment due in connection with foreign trade, current business, and short-term banking facilities
B. Remittance for living expenses of parents residing abroad
C. A transaction which alters the assets or liabilities, including contingent liabilities, outside India of persons resident in India ✔
D. Normal short-term banking and credit facilities in the ordinary course of business
Explanation: Section 2(e) of FEMA defines a capital account transaction as a transaction which alters the assets or liabilities, including contingent liabilities, outside India of persons resident in India or assets or liabilities in India of persons resident outside India. Options A, B, and D describe current account transactions.
Medium NORMAL · Person Resident in India | Residence Status | Section 2(v)
An Indian citizen who leaves India for employment outside India in September 2024 and intends to stay there indefinitely will be classified for the financial year 2024-25 as:
A. Person Resident in India
B. Person Resident Outside India ✔
C. Non-Resident Indian (NRI) but Resident in India under tax laws only
D. Foreign National
Explanation: Under Section 2(v) of FEMA, an individual who leaves India for employment, business, or any other purpose indicating an intention to stay outside India for an uncertain period ceases to be a person resident in India from the date of departure.
Hard NORMAL · Person Resident in India | Body Corporate | Branches
Which of the following entities is explicitly EXCLUDED from the definition of 'Person Resident in India' under FEMA, 1999, even if it is incorporated or registered in India?
A. A branch of a foreign company operating in Mumbai ✔
B. A wholly-owned subsidiary of a US company incorporated in Delhi
C. A public sector undertaking owned by the Government of India
D. A cooperative society registered under the Multi-State Cooperative Societies Act
Explanation: Under Section 2(u), a person resident in India includes any person or body corporate registered or incorporated in India, EXCEPT a branch, office, or agency outside India of such person, and conversely, a branch, office, or agency in India of a person resident outside India is considered a person resident in India for certain purposes, but a foreign company's branch in India is treated as controlled by a person resident outside India depending on the context. However, strictly by definition, offices/branches of foreign entities in India are treated as resident in India if they are situated in India, but under Section 2(u)(iv), an office, branch or agency in India owned or controlled by a person resident outside India is a person resident in India.
Easy NORMAL · Current Account Transactions | Section 5 | Drawal of Foreign Exchange
What is the general rule regarding 'Current Account Transactions' under Section 5 of FEMA, 1999?
A. All current account transactions are strictly prohibited unless prior approval of the Central Government is obtained.
B. Any person may sell or draw foreign exchange to or from an authorised person for a current account transaction, subject to reasonable restrictions imposed by the Central Government. ✔
C. Current account transactions are completely unregulated and require no reporting to the RBI.
D. Current account transactions can only be undertaken by authorized dealers after obtaining a license from SEBI.
Explanation: Section 5 of FEMA states that any person may sell or draw foreign exchange to or from an authorised person if such sale or drawal is a current account transaction, provided the Central Government may, in public interest and in consultation with the RBI, impose such reasonable restrictions as may be prescribed.
Easy NORMAL · Current Account Rules | Schedule I | Prohibited Transactions
Which of the following schedules under the Foreign Exchange Management (Current Account Transactions) Rules, 2000 lists transactions for which withdrawal of foreign exchange is PROHIBITED?
A. Schedule I ✔
B. Schedule II
C. Schedule III
D. Schedule IV
Explanation: Schedule I of the Foreign Exchange Management (Current Account Transactions) Rules, 2000 specifies transactions for which the drawal of foreign exchange is prohibited (e.g., remittance out of lottery winnings, remittance of income from racing/riding, etc.). Schedule II requires Central Government approval, and Schedule III requires RBI approval.
Medium NORMAL · Schedule II | Central Government Approval | Current Account
Under the FEMA Current Account Transactions Rules, remittance of foreign exchange for which of the following requires prior approval of the Central Government (Schedule II)?
A. Travel to Pakistan
B. Cultural tours sponsored by the Government of India ✔
C. Remittance out of lottery winnings
D. Commission due to equity agents for overseas issue
Explanation: Schedule II of the Current Account Transactions Rules lists transactions that require prior approval of the Central Government, which includes cultural tours. Remittance of lottery winnings is prohibited (Schedule I). Commission on equity issues is under Schedule III (RBI approval).
Medium NORMAL · LRS | Liberalised Remittance Scheme | RBI Approval
An individual wishes to remit USD 300,000 abroad for maintenance of close relatives under the Liberalised Remittance Scheme (LRS). Which authority's prior approval is required?
A. Prior approval of the Reserve Bank of India is required since it exceeds USD 250,000 per financial year. ✔
B. Prior approval of the Ministry of Finance is required.
C. No prior approval is needed as LRS limit is unlimited for individuals.
D. Prior approval of SEBI is required.
Explanation: Under the Liberalised Remittance Scheme (LRS), resident individuals are permitted to freely remit up to USD 250,000 per financial year for permitted current or capital account transactions. Since USD 300,000 exceeds this threshold, prior approval of the RBI is required.
Easy NORMAL · Adjudicating Authority | Section 16 | Contravention
Who is empowered to appoint Adjudicating Authorities for holding inquiries under Section 16 of FEMA, 1999?
A. The Supreme Court of India
B. The Central Government ✔
C. The Reserve Bank of India
D. The National Company Law Tribunal
Explanation: Under Section 16 of FEMA, 1999, the Central Government may, by notification, appoint as many officers of the Central Government as it thinks fit as Adjudicating Authorities for holding an inquiry for any contravention of FEMA provisions.
Easy NORMAL · Appellate Tribunal | ATFE | Section 18
What is the appellate tribunal established under FEMA, 1999 to hear appeals against the orders of the Adjudicating Authority?
A. Appellate Tribunal for Foreign Exchange (ATFE) ✔
B. National Company Law Appellate Tribunal (NCLAT)
C. Income Tax Appellate Tribunal (ITAT)
D. Customs, Excise and Service Tax Appellate Tribunal (CESTAT)
Explanation: Section 18 of FEMA provides for the establishment of an Appellate Tribunal known as the Appellate Tribunal for Foreign Exchange (ATFE) to hear appeals against orders passed by the Adjudicating Authority under Section 16.
Medium NORMAL · Appeals | Section 19 | Limitation Period
Within what period must an appeal be filed before the Appellate Tribunal against an order of the Adjudicating Authority under FEMA, 1999?
A. Within 30 days from the date on which a copy of the order is delivered
B. Within 45 days from the date on which a copy of the order is delivered ✔
C. Within 60 days from the date on which a copy of the order is delivered
D. Within 90 days from the date on which a copy of the order is delivered
Explanation: Under Section 19(2) of FEMA, any person aggrieved by an order made by the Adjudicating Authority may prefer an appeal to the Appellate Tribunal within a period of 45 days from the date on which a copy of the order is delivered to him.
Medium NORMAL · High Court Appeal | Section 35 | Appellate Mechanism
An appeal against the order of the Appellate Tribunal (ATFE) under FEMA lies to which court?
A. Supreme Court of India directly on any matter
B. High Court, on any question of law arising out of such order ✔
C. National Company Law Appellate Tribunal
D. District Court having jurisdiction
Explanation: Section 35 of FEMA provides that any person aggrieved by any decision or order of the Appellate Tribunal may file an appeal to the High Court within 60 days from the date of communication of the decision or order, on any question of law arising out of such order.
Hard NORMAL · Penalties | Section 13 | Contravention
What is the maximum penalty that can be imposed under Section 13 of FEMA, 1999 for contravention of any provision of the Act?
A. Fixed penalty of INR 10,00,000 only
B. Up to thrice the sum involved in such contravention where quantifiable, or up to INR 2 Lakhs where not quantifiable, and where it is a continuing contravention, further penalty up to INR 5,000 for every day ✔
C. Imprisonment for a term up to 7 years without any fine
D. Confiscation of all domestic and foreign properties of the offender automatically
Explanation: Section 13 of FEMA prescribes penalties for contravention: up to thrice the sum involved in such contravention where quantifiable, or up to two lakh rupees where not quantifiable, and where it is a continuing contravention, further penalty which may extend to five thousand rupees for every day after the first day during which the contravention continues.
Hard NORMAL · Section 14 | Recovery of Penalty | Default
If a person fails to pay the penalty imposed under Section 13 of FEMA within 90 days from the date on which the notice for payment is served, what action can the Adjudicating Authority take?
A. Order immediate arrest and detention in civil prison for up to 3 years
B. Direct recovery of the penalty amount by attachment and sale of the movable or immovable property of the defaulter ✔
C. Liquidate the corporate entity within 7 days through the NCLT
D. Forfeit all passports held by the person
Explanation: Under Section 14 of FEMA, if any person fails to full pay the penalty within 90 days, the Adjudicating Authority may recover the amount through various modes, including attachment and sale of movable or immovable properties of the person in default as prescribed.
Easy NORMAL · Authorised Person | Section 2(c) | Definitions
Who is classified as an 'Authorised Person' under Section 2(c) of FEMA, 1999?
A. Any chartered accountant registered with ICAI
B. An authorised dealer, money changer, off-shore banking unit or any other person authorised by the RBI to deal in foreign exchange or foreign securities ✔
C. Any scheduled commercial bank holding a banking license from SEBI
D. Any citizen of India residing in foreign countries with dual citizenship
Explanation: Section 2(c) defines an 'authorised person' as an authorised dealer, money changer, offshore banking unit or any other person who is authorised for the time being by the Reserve Bank of India under Section 10(1) to deal in foreign exchange or foreign securities.
Medium NORMAL · Section 12 | Inspection | Authorised Person
Can the Reserve Bank of India inspect the books of accounts and other documents of an 'Authorised Person' under FEMA?
A. No, RBI has no inspection powers over authorised persons; only SEBI can inspect them.
B. Yes, RBI may at any time cause an inspection to be made of any authorised person and its offices under Section 12 of FEMA. ✔
C. Yes, but only after obtaining a warrant from a criminal court.
D. No, inspection is restricted only to scheduled commercial banks.
Explanation: Section 12 of FEMA empowers the Reserve Bank of India to cause an inspection to be made, by an officer of the RBI authorised in this behalf, of any authorised person and its books, accounts, and other documents to ensure compliance with FEMA provisions.
Medium NORMAL · Capital Account Transaction | Immovable Property | Examples
Which of the following transactions constitutes a 'Capital Account Transaction' as per the RBI regulations under FEMA?
A. Payment of school fees for a child studying in London
B. Acquisition of immovable property outside India by an Indian resident ✔
C. Remittance of consultancy fees for legal advice received from a US lawyer
D. Export of software services to a client in Germany
Explanation: Acquisition or transfer of immovable property outside India alters the assets outside India of a person resident in India, making it a capital account transaction. The other options are classic examples of current account transactions.
Easy NORMAL · Foreign Currency | Section 2(m) | Definitions
Under FEMA, 'Foreign Currency' means:
A. Any currency other than Indian currency ✔
B. Only United States Dollar (USD) and Euro
C. Any currency that is legally convertible in the international market
D. Gold and silver bullion held abroad
Explanation: Section 2(m) of FEMA defines 'foreign currency' to mean any currency other than Indian currency. This is a broad definition encompassing all foreign legal tenders.
Hard NORMAL · Person Resident in India | Foreign Citizen | Employment
What is the status under FEMA of a foreign citizen who comes to India on an employment contract for a fixed period of 2 years?
A. Person Resident Outside India
B. Person Resident in India ✔
C. Non-Resident Indian (NRI)
D. Foreign Institutional Investor
Explanation: Under Section 2(v), an individual coming to or staying in India in employment, business, or for any other purpose indicating an intention to stay in India for an uncertain period is considered a person resident in India. Coming for a fixed employment contract of 2 years generally satisfies the resident criteria under FEMA (unlike the Income Tax Act which has 182 days rule, FEMA focuses on purpose and period of stay, and a stay exceeding 182 days during the preceding financial year for taking up employment makes someone resident in India).
Hard NORMAL · Section 46 | Power to Exempt | Central Government
Which section of FEMA, 1999 empowers the Central Government to exempt certain classes of persons or foreign exchange transactions from the application of the Act in public interest?
A. Section 38
B. Section 45
C. Section 46 ✔
D. Section 47
Explanation: Section 46 of FEMA empowers the Central Government, by notification, to exempt any person or class of persons from the application of all or any of the provisions of this Act or rules or regulations made thereunder, in public interest.
Hard NORMAL · Compounding of Contraventions | Compounding Rules | RBI Authority
In the case of a compounding application under FEMA, who is the competent authority to compound contraventions up to INR 10 Lakhs?
A. The Reserve Bank of India (specifically designated officers) ✔
B. The Director of Enforcement
C. The Appellate Tribunal for Foreign Exchange
D. The Special Director (Appeals)
Explanation: Under the Foreign Exchange (Compounding Proceedings) Rules, 2000, compounding powers are vested in the Reserve Bank of India and the Directorate of Enforcement depending on the sum involved. RBI handles compounding for specified contraventions up to certain monetary limits (e.g., up to INR 10 lakhs and above under delegated thresholds).
Medium NORMAL · Section 15 | Compounding | Adjudication
Can a contravention under FEMA, 1999 be compounded once proceedings have already been initiated by the Adjudicating Authority?
A. No, once Adjudicating Authority starts inquiry, compounding is barred permanently.
B. Yes, contraventions can be compounded before or after the initiation of adjudication proceedings, except for specific offenses within a stipulated timeframe or repeat violations as per rules. ✔
C. Only the Supreme Court can permit compounding during adjudication.
D. Compounding is exclusively handled by SEBI.
Explanation: Under Section 15 of FEMA, any contravention may, on an application made by the person committing such contravention, be compounded by the authority specified, whether before or after the institution of adjudication proceedings.
Medium NORMAL · Transfer | Section 2(zb) | Definitions
What does 'Transfer' mean under the definitions of FEMA, 1999 with respect to foreign exchange or foreign securities?
A. Only physical transportation of cash across international borders
B. Sale, purchase, exchange, mortgage, pledge, gift, loan or any other form of transfer of right, title, possession or lien ✔
C. Merely opening a bank account in a foreign country
D. Conversion of rupees into gold
Explanation: Section 2(zb) defines 'transfer' in a comprehensive manner to include sale, purchase, exchange, mortgage, pledge, gift, loan or any other form of transfer of right, title, possession or lien.
Medium NORMAL · Capital Account | Borrowing and Lending | Debt
Which of the following transactions is classified under 'Capital Account Transactions' involving debt instruments?
A. Investment by way of Foreign Direct Investment (FDI) in equity shares
B. Borrowing or lending in rupees and in foreign currency between residents and non-residents ✔
C. Payment of insurance premium to an overseas insurer
D. Remittance for service charges on technical know-how
Explanation: Borrowing and lending in rupees or foreign currency between residents and non-residents directly alter liabilities/assets, making them capital account transactions involving debt. Equity investment is also capital account, but borrowing/lending specifically constitutes debt transactions.
Medium NORMAL · Section 2(u) | Branch Outside India | Residence Status
Under FEMA, what is the status of an office of an Indian company incorporated in London?
A. Person Resident in India
B. Person Resident Outside India ✔
C. Resident in both jurisdictions simultaneously
D. Foreign Institutional Investor
Explanation: As per the proviso to Section 2(u), a branch, office, or agency outside India of a person resident in India is NOT a person resident in India; it is treated as a person resident outside India.
Hard NORMAL · Special Director Appeals | Appellate Tribunal | Section 17 & 19
If a person is aggrieved by an order of the Special Director (Appeals), where can an appeal be filed under FEMA?
A. Appellate Tribunal for Foreign Exchange (ATFE) ✔
B. Directly to the Supreme Court of India
C. National Company Law Tribunal
D. Income Tax Appellate Tribunal
Explanation: Section 17 of FEMA provides for appeals against orders of the Adjudicating Authority to the Special Director (Appeals), and Section 19 provides that any person aggrieved by an order of the Special Director (Appeals) or Adjudicating Authority may prefer an appeal to the Appellate Tribunal (ATFE).
Easy NORMAL · Directorate of Enforcement | Investigation | Enforcement
Which of the following is TRUE regarding the powers of the Directorate of Enforcement under FEMA?
A. It has the power to issue currency notes and mint coins.
B. It investigates suspected contraventions of FEMA provisions and initiates adjudication proceedings. ✔
C. It sets the benchmark interest rates for foreign currency loans.
D. It regulates the listing of foreign companies on Indian stock exchanges.
Explanation: The Directorate of Enforcement is the specialized agency responsible for enforcement of FEMA provisions, investigating contraventions, and initiating adjudication proceedings through Adjudicating Authorities.
Easy NORMAL · Security | Section 2(za) | Definitions
Under FEMA, the term 'Security' includes:
A. Shares, stocks, bonds and debentures, promissory notes, and other instruments of capital nature ✔
B. Only physical security guards protecting bank lockers
C. Government-issued identity cards and passports
D. Insurance policies against fire and theft
Explanation: Section 2(za) defines 'security' to mean shares, stocks, bonds and debentures, government securities, savings certificates, and any other instruments of capital nature as specified by the RBI.
Medium NORMAL · Section 4 | Holding Foreign Assets | General Permission
Can a person resident in India hold, own, transfer or invest in foreign currency, foreign security or immovable property situated outside India?
A. Yes, absolutely without any restrictions under any circumstances.
B. No, it is totally banned for all Indian residents.
C. Yes, only to the extent permitted under FEMA, its rules or regulations, or with the general or special permission of the RBI. ✔
D. Only if the person is a Member of Parliament.
Explanation: Section 4 of FEMA explicitly states that no person resident in India shall acquire, hold, own, transfer or invest in any foreign currency, foreign security or immovable property situated outside India except as otherwise provided in the Act or rules/regulations made thereunder.
CASE SCENARIO: Mr. Rajesh, an Indian citizen and a software engineer, went to Germany on May 10, 2023, under an employment contract with a German technology firm for an expected duration of 4 years. His wife and children accompanied him, and they closed their residential apartment in Pune, leasing it out to a tenant. During the financial year 2024-25, Rajesh visited India for 3 weeks on a vacation and also earned consulting income from a US-based client which was credited to his German bank account. He wishes to undertake various financial transactions involving Indian and foreign currency.
Medium SCENARIO · Residence Status | Employment Abroad | Section 2(v)
What is the residential status of Mr. Rajesh under FEMA, 1999 during the financial year 2024-25?
A. Person Resident in India, because he is an Indian citizen holding an Indian passport
B. Person Resident Outside India, because he left India for employment outside India with an intention to stay for an uncertain/extended period exceeding one year ✔
C. Resident but only for tax purposes under the Income Tax Act
D. Non-Resident Indian (NRI) with dual citizenship status
Explanation: Under Section 2(v) of FEMA, an individual who leaves India for employment outside India ceases to be a person resident in India from the date of his departure, regardless of his citizenship, because his purpose indicates a stay outside India for an uncertain period.
Medium SCENARIO · Bank Accounts | NRE/NRO | Authorised Persons
Can Mr. Rajesh maintain and operate his NRE (Non-Resident External) bank account in India while being classified as a person resident outside India?
A. No, NRE accounts are exclusively for Indian residents.
B. Yes, as a person resident outside India (NRI/PIO), he is eligible to open, hold, and maintain NRE, NRO, and FCNR accounts with authorized dealers in India. ✔
C. Yes, but only after obtaining prior written permission from the Prime Minister's Office.
D. No, he must convert all Indian bank accounts into resident savings accounts immediately.
Explanation: Non-residents (persons resident outside India) are legally permitted to maintain NRE, NRO, and FCNR accounts with authorised banks in India for depositing foreign earnings or Indian source incomes in accordance with FEMA regulations.
Hard SCENARIO · Section 4 | Immovable Property Abroad | Resident Outside India
If Mr. Rajesh wishes to acquire an immovable property in Germany out of his foreign earnings, does Section 4 of FEMA restrict him from doing so?
A. Yes, Section 4 bans all acquisitions of property outside India by persons of Indian origin.
B. No, Section 4 prohibits acquisition of foreign property only by persons resident in India. Since Rajesh is a person resident outside India, Section 4 restrictions do not apply to his foreign acquisitions. ✔
C. Yes, prior approval of SEBI is mandatory.
D. No, but he must pay 100% tax penalty in India.
Explanation: Section 4 of FEMA restricts persons resident in India from holding or acquiring immovable property outside India without permission. Since Mr. Rajesh is a person resident outside India, Section 4 is not applicable to assets acquired abroad out of his foreign funds.
Hard SCENARIO · Inflows | Current Account | Gifts from Non-Residents
Suppose Mr. Rajesh wants to remit USD 50,000 from his German earnings to his friend residing in India as a gift. How is this transaction characterized under FEMA?
A. It is a prohibited capital account transaction under Schedule I.
B. It is a current account transaction for the recipient, but requires RBI approval under Schedule III.
C. Inflow of funds into India as a gift from a non-resident is a permitted current account transaction and does not require prior RBI or Central Government approval. ✔
D. It is classified as foreign direct investment in retail trade.
Explanation: Inflows of funds from a person resident outside India to a person resident in India (such as gifts or maintenance remittances) are generally permitted current account transactions and do not require prior approval under FEMA rules.
CASE SCENARIO: M/s. Zenith Exports Ltd., an Indian company incorporated in New Delhi, engaged in exporting leather goods, received a major advance payment of USD 500,000 from an overseas buyer in New York in January 2024. Due to a sudden change in global market conditions, the export order was canceled in March 2024. The company delayed refunding the advance to the US buyer beyond the timeframe stipulated by the RBI regulations, without obtaining formal approval for the extension. The Directorate of Enforcement initiated an investigation for contravention of FEMA provisions.
Medium SCENARIO · Current Account | Foreign Trade | Export Advance
What category of transaction under FEMA does the receipt of export advance and its subsequent refund fall under?
A. Capital Account Transaction because it involves foreign currency debt liability
B. Current Account Transaction because it relates to foreign trade in goods and services ✔
C. Prohibited Transaction under Schedule I
D. Securities transaction regulated exclusively by SEBI
Explanation: Transactions relating to export of goods, import of goods, and associated payments/refunds in connection with foreign trade fall under current account transactions.
Medium SCENARIO · Adjudicating Authority | Section 16 | Enforcement
Which authority is empowered to hold an inquiry and adjudge the contravention committed by M/s. Zenith Exports Ltd. under Section 16 of FEMA?
A. The Adjudicating Authority appointed by the Central Government ✔
B. The High Court of Delhi
C. The Company Law Board
D. The Reserve Bank of India Governor directly
Explanation: Under Section 16 of FEMA, the Central Government appoints Adjudicating Authorities to hold inquiries and impose penalties for contraventions of the Act, rules, or regulations.
Hard SCENARIO · Section 13 | Penalties | Quantifiable Sum
If the Adjudicating Authority imposes a monetary penalty on M/s. Zenith Exports Ltd. under Section 13, what is the maximum penalty that can be levied if the sum involved is quantifiable as USD 500,000?
A. Fixed penalty of INR 50,000 regardless of the amount
B. Up to thrice the sum involved in such contravention where quantifiable ✔
C. Exactly USD 500,000 matching the advance
D. Imprisonment of the Managing Director for 10 years
Explanation: Section 13 of FEMA provides that upon adjudication, a person is liable to a penalty up to thrice the sum involved in such contravention where the amount is quantifiable, or up to two lakh rupees where not quantifiable.
Medium SCENARIO · Compounding | Section 15 | Settlement
M/s. Zenith Exports Ltd. wishes to settle the matter without going through protracted adjudication proceedings. Which legal remedy is available under FEMA?
A. Winding up of the company voluntarily
B. Compounding of contravention under Section 15 of FEMA ✔
C. Filing a writ petition directly in the International Court of Justice
D. Seeking amnesty from the Reserve Bank's Governor through an informal email
Explanation: Section 15 of FEMA permits the compounding of contraventions upon an application made by the person committing the contravention, before or after the institution of adjudication proceedings, upon payment of compounding fees.
CASE SCENARIO: Mr. Vikram, a wealthy resident individual, desired to purchase a luxury villa in Switzerland valued at USD 1.5 million in July 2024. Without seeking any permission from the Reserve Bank of India or utilizing authorized channels under permissible limits, he transferred funds through an unauthorized hawala channel and acquired the property in his own name. The Directorate of Enforcement received an anonymous tip-off regarding this undisclosed foreign asset acquisition and launched formal search and seizure operations.
Hard SCENARIO · Section 3 | Section 4 | Unauthorized Transactions
Which provision of FEMA, 1999 has Mr. Vikram primarily contravened by acquiring immovable property outside India through unauthorized channels?
A. Section 3, prohibiting unauthorized dealing in foreign exchange, and Section 4, prohibiting holding of foreign property without general or special permission ✔
B. Section 5, relating to current account transactions
C. Section 10, relating to duties of authorized persons
D. Section 18, relating to establishment of ATFE
Explanation: Section 3 prohibits dealing in foreign exchange except through an authorised person, and Section 4 prohibits holding immovable property outside India except as provided under the Act. Vikram violated both by using unauthorized channels and acquiring foreign property without RBI permission.
Medium SCENARIO · Civil Contravention | FEMA vs FERA | Nature of Offense
What is the nature of offenses under FEMA, 1999 such as the one committed by Mr. Vikram?
A. They are criminal offenses punishable with rigorous imprisonment under all circumstances.
B. They are civil contraventions inviting monetary penalties and adjudicatory proceedings, distinguishing FEMA from the erstwhile FERA. ✔
C. They are compoundable only by the Supreme Court.
D. They are classified as cognizable corporate frauds under Section 447 of the Companies Act.
Explanation: A key hallmark of FEMA, 1999 is that contraventions are treated as civil contraventions attracting monetary penalties rather than criminal offenses with mandatory imprisonment (unlike FERA).
Hard SCENARIO · Appeals | Section 17 & 19 | ATFE
If Mr. Vikram is aggrieved by the order passed by the Adjudicating Authority confirming the penalty for contravention, where should he file his first appeal?
A. Special Director (Appeals) or directly to the Appellate Tribunal for Foreign Exchange (ATFE) depending on the adjudicating officer's rank ✔
B. Securities Appellate Tribunal (SAT)
C. National Company Law Tribunal (NCLT)
D. High Court of competent jurisdiction as an original suit
Explanation: As per Sections 17 and 19 of FEMA, an appeal against the order of an Adjudicating Authority lies either before the Special Director (Appeals) or directly to the Appellate Tribunal for Foreign Exchange (ATFE).
Medium SCENARIO · Section 14 | Recovery of Penalty | Attachment
If Mr. Vikram fails to deposit the penalty imposed by the Adjudicating Authority within 90 days, what coercive recovery measure is permissible under Section 14?
A. Attachment and sale of his movable or immovable properties in India
B. Confiscation of his Indian passport by the local police station ✔
C. Immediate conversion of his equity shares into government bonds
D. Mandatory community service for 500 hours
Explanation: Section 14 of FEMA empowers the Adjudicating Authority to recover unpaid penalties after 90 days through modes such as attachment and sale of movable or immovable properties belonging to the defaulter.
CASE SCENARIO: Global Forex Bank Ltd., an authorized dealer licensed by the RBI under Section 10 of FEMA, handled several large-scale foreign currency remittances. During a routine inspection conducted by RBI officers under Section 12 of FEMA in August 2024, it was discovered that the bank processed current account transactions listed under Schedule II (requiring Central Government approval) and Schedule III (requiring RBI approval) without ensuring that the requisite statutory approvals were attached to the application forms.
Medium SCENARIO · Section 10 | Authorised Person Obligations | Compliance
Under Section 10(2) of FEMA, what is the primary obligation of Global Forex Bank Ltd. as an authorized person when dealing in foreign exchange?
A. To ensure that the transaction does not involve any contravention of FEMA or any rule/regulation made thereunder ✔
B. To guarantee a fixed exchange rate to all retail customers for 5 years
C. To invest 50% of its profits in foreign sovereign bonds
D. To obtain prior permission from SEBI for every foreign exchange draft issued
Explanation: Section 10(2) mandates that an authorised person shall, in all dealings in foreign exchange or foreign securities, comply with the requirements of the Act and any rules, regulations, or directions issued by the RBI, ensuring no contravention occurs.
Easy SCENARIO · Section 12 | Inspection | Authorised Person
Which statutory provision empowers the RBI to inspect the books of accounts and records of Global Forex Bank Ltd.?
A. Section 12 of FEMA ✔
B. Section 16 of FEMA
C. Section 35 of FEMA
D. Section 46 of FEMA
Explanation: Section 12 of FEMA specifically empowers the Reserve Bank of India to inspect the books of accounts and other documents of any authorised person at any time to verify compliance with the Act.
Hard SCENARIO · Section 11 | RBI Penalties | Authorised Person
If Global Forex Bank Ltd. failed to comply with RBI directions during the transactions, what penalty can the RBI impose on the authorized person under FEMA?
A. RBI can cancel its banking license under the Banking Regulation Act, but under FEMA Section 11(3), RBI may also impose a monetary penalty for contravention of its directions. ✔
B. RBI cannot impose any monetary penalty; it can only issue a warning letter.
C. RBI must hand over the bank to the Ministry of Corporate Affairs for liquidation.
D. RBI can penalize the bank up to INR 1,000 only.
Explanation: Under Section 11(3) of FEMA, if any authorised person fails to comply with any direction given by the RBI or fails to comply with FEMA provisions, the RBI may impose a monetary penalty.
Medium SCENARIO · Current Account Rules | Schedule II & III | Approvals
Which schedules of the Current Account Transactions Rules contain transactions requiring Central Government approval (Schedule II) and RBI approval (Schedule III) respectively?
A. Schedule I for Central Government and Schedule II for RBI
B. Schedule II for Central Government approval and Schedule III for RBI approval ✔
C. Schedule III for Central Government and Schedule IV for RBI
D. Schedule IV for both Central Government and RBI
Explanation: Under the FEMA (Current Account Transactions) Rules, Schedule II lists transactions requiring Central Government approval, and Schedule III lists transactions requiring RBI approval (Schedule I contains prohibited transactions).
CASE SCENARIO: Mr. Anand, an Indian resident, inherited a commercial building in Singapore from his uncle in 2022. In 2024, he decided to sell this building and bring the sale proceeds into India. He approached an authorized dealer to repatriate the funds. Meanwhile, the Enforcement Directorate suspected that Mr. Anand had also acquired another undisclosed residential apartment in London in 2023 using funds remitted beyond the Liberalised Remittance Scheme (LRS) limit without RBI approval, triggering parallel scrutiny.
Hard SCENARIO · Inheritance | Immovable Property | Repatriation
Is Mr. Anand permitted to repatriate and receive the sale proceeds of the inherited Singapore property into India?
A. No, repatriation of inheritance from abroad is totally prohibited under FEMA.
B. Yes, acquisition by way of inheritance from a person resident outside India is generally permitted, and repatriation of such proceeds into India is allowed under FEMA regulations. ✔
C. Yes, but only after paying a 50% export-import duty to the Customs Department.
D. No, inherited properties must be surrendered to the Government of Singapore.
Explanation: FEMA regulations permit a resident to hold immovable property acquired by way of inheritance from a person resident outside India, and repatriation of sale proceeds of such property into India is permissible subject to compliance.
Easy SCENARIO · LRS | Liberalised Remittance Scheme | Limit
What is the maximum limit per financial year for outward remittance by a resident individual under the Liberalised Remittance Scheme (LRS) without requiring prior RBI approval?
A. USD 50,000
B. USD 100,000
C. USD 250,000 ✔
D. USD 1,000,000
Explanation: Under the current Liberalised Remittance Scheme (LRS), resident individuals are freely allowed to remit up to USD 250,000 per financial year for any permitted current or capital account transaction.
Hard SCENARIO · Section 3 & 4 | Violation | London Property
If Mr. Anand acquired the London apartment exceeding the LRS limit without RBI approval, which FEMA provision was violated?
A. Section 5 only
B. Section 3 and Section 4 read with applicable Capital Account Transaction regulations and LRS ceilings ✔
C. Section 10 only
D. Section 18 only
Explanation: Acquiring property abroad exceeding LRS limits without RBI approval violates Section 4 (holding property outside India without permission/regulation) and Section 3 (unauthorized foreign exchange dealings).
Hard SCENARIO · Section 35 | High Court Appeal | Question of Law
If the Appellate Tribunal for Foreign Exchange (ATFE) passes an order against Mr. Anand, within how many days and to which court can an appeal be filed on a question of law?
A. Within 30 days to the Supreme Court
B. Within 60 days to the High Court ✔
C. Within 90 days to the NCLAT
D. Within 45 days to the District Court
Explanation: Section 35 of FEMA provides that any person aggrieved by any decision or order of the Appellate Tribunal may file an appeal to the High Court within 60 days on any question of law arising out of such order.

Paper 3: Taxation · Module 1 · Chapter 1:

Taxation — 55 rows
Easy NORMAL · Charging Section | Income-tax Act 1961 | Basic Concepts
Which of the following is the charging section for Income-tax in India under the Income-tax Act, 1961?
A. Section 2
B. Section 4 ✔
C. Section 5
D. Section 10
Explanation: Section 4 of the Income-tax Act, 1961 is the charging section which provides that income-tax shall be charged for any assessment year at the relevant rates in respect of the total income of the previous year of every person. Section 2 deals with definitions, Section 5 with scope of total income, and Section 10 with incomes not included in total income.
Easy NORMAL · Previous Year | Newly Set-up Business | Section 3
What is the general rule regarding the determination of the previous year for a business newly set up on 15th November of the current financial year?
A. From 1st April of the current financial year to 31st March of the next year
B. From 15th November of the current financial year to 31st March of the next year ✔
C. From the date of setting up to 31st December of the current financial year
D. From 15th November of the current financial year to 30th September of the next year
Explanation: As per Section 3, for a newly set-up business or profession, the first previous year begins on the date of setting up of the business or profession and ends on 31st March of the financial year. Therefore, it will be from 15th November to 31st March.
Easy NORMAL · Assessment Year | Previous Year | Section 4
Under the normal provisions of the Income-tax Act, 1961, income earned in a previous year is assessed to tax in:
A. The same previous year
B. The immediately preceding financial year
C. The assessment year following the previous year ✔
D. Any year chosen by the Assessing Officer
Explanation: The general rule under the Income-tax Act is that income earned in a previous year is taxed in the immediately following assessment year. Section 4 mandates that income-tax is charged for any assessment year on the total income of the previous year.
Medium NORMAL · Exceptions to PY Rule | Assessment in PY | Section 174
Which of the following represents an exception to the general rule that income of a previous year is assessed in the immediately following assessment year?
A. Income of a person leaving India permanently ✔
B. Income from salary received in advance
C. Income of a salaried employee with multiple employers
D. Income from house property let out for residential purposes
Explanation: Sections 174 to 176 provide exceptions to the rule where income of a previous year is assessed in the same previous year itself. One such exception is the income of a person leaving India permanently with no intention of returning.
Easy NORMAL · Definition of Person | Section 2(31) | Basic Concepts
For the purpose of Income-tax Act, 1961, the term 'Person' under Section 2(31) includes how many distinct categories?
A. 5 categories
B. 6 categories
C. 7 categories ✔
D. 8 categories
Explanation: Section 2(31) defines 'person' to include 7 categories: (i) Individual, (ii) Hindu Undivided Family (HUF), (iii) Company, (iv) Firm, (v) Association of Persons (AOP) or Body of Individuals (BOI), (vi) Local authority, and (vii) Artificial juridical person.
Medium NORMAL · Gross Total Income | Chapter VI-A Deductions | Computation Flow
In computing total income, which of the following deductions is allowed from Gross Total Income under Chapter VI-A?
A. Standard deduction under Section 16(ia)
B. Deduction under Section 80C for life insurance premium ✔
C. Interest on borrowed capital under Section 24(b)
D. Entertainment allowance deduction under Section 16(ii)
Explanation: Deductions under Chapter VI-A (such as Section 80C) are made from the Gross Total Income. Section 16 deductions are from salary income, and Section 24(b) is from house property income, before arriving at Gross Total Income.
Easy NORMAL · Agricultural Income | Section 10(1) | Exemptions
Which of the following incomes is completely exempt from income-tax under Section 10 of the Income-tax Act, 1961?
A. Winnings from horse races
B. Agricultural income in India ✔
C. Capital gains from transfer of listed shares
D. Director's sitting fees
Explanation: Agricultural income in India is exempt under Section 10(1). Winnings from horse races are taxable under Section 56(2)(ib) at special rates. Capital gains and director's fees are also taxable under their respective heads.
Medium NORMAL · Section 115BAC | Default Tax Regime | Chapter VI-A Restrictions
Under the default tax regime (Section 115BAC) for individuals, which of the following deductions under Chapter VI-A is generally NOT available?
A. Deduction under Section 80CCD(2) for employer's contribution to NPS
B. Deduction under Section 80CCD(1B) for employee's contribution to NPS
C. Deduction under Section 80C for Provident Fund and life insurance ✔
D. Deduction under Section 80JJAA for employment of new workmen
Explanation: Under the default tax regime of Section 115BAC, most deductions under Chapter VI-A like Section 80C, 80D, 80G, etc., are not available. However, deductions under Section 80CCD(2) and 80JJAA are permitted.
Hard NORMAL · Definition of Person | Co-operative Society | Section 2(31)
What is the tax status of a co-operative society under the Income-tax Act, 1961?
A. Treated as a Firm
B. Treated as an Association of Persons (AOP)
C. Treated as a distinct category of 'Person' under Section 2(31) ✔
D. Treated as a Local authority
Explanation: A co-operative society is specifically included as a distinct entity under 'Company' in an expanded definition or rather treated under specific tax rates, but strictly speaking, co-operative societies fall under the category of 'Local authority' or specific corporate definitions? Wait, let's check: Section 2(31) includes local authorities, but co-operative societies are legally treated as a 'Company' for income-tax rate purposes or separate entity? Actually, co-operative societies are treated as a separate category of person or under AOP? Correction: Co-operative society is treated as a separate category under Section 2(31)(vii) or as part of AOP? No, co-operative society is a co-operative society registered under Co-operative Societies Act, taxed as a separate entity (neither company nor firm nor AOP, but a distinct entity mentioned in finance acts and charging provisions). Let's review standard classification: Company, Firm, AOP/BOI, Local Authority, Artificial Juridical Person. Co-operative societies are assessed as a separate category of person.
Medium NORMAL · Previous Year | Section 3 | Uniform Financial Year
Can an assessee have different previous years for different sources of income under the Income-tax Act, 1961?
A. Yes, always
B. No, all sources of income must have the same previous year which is the financial year ✔
C. Yes, if permitted by the Assessing Officer
D. Yes, for business income only
Explanation: As per Section 3, the previous year is uniformly the financial year (1st April to 31st March) for all sources of income. An assessee cannot have different previous years for different sources of income.
Hard NORMAL · Finance Act | Advance Tax | Rates of Tax
Which of the following rates are NOT prescribed by the annual Finance Act?
A. Income-tax rates for the current assessment year
B. Rates for deduction of tax at source (TDS) on salary
C. Advance tax installment rates ✔
D. Surcharge rates
Explanation: Advance tax installment dates and rates are specified directly in the Income-tax Act, 1961 (Section 211), whereas tax rates, TDS rates on certain incomes, and surcharge rates are fixed annually by the Finance Act passed by Parliament.
Hard NORMAL · AOP/BOI | Section 167B | Maximum Marginal Rate
An association of persons (AOP) is formed by two non-corporate entities for a joint venture. How is the AOP taxed if the individual shares of members are indeterminate or unknown?
A. At the maximum marginal rate (MMR) ✔
B. At individual slab rates of members
C. At flat 20%
D. Exempt from tax
Explanation: Under Section 167B, if the shares of the members of an AOP/BOI in the income are indeterminate or unknown, tax is charged on the total income of the AOP at the maximum marginal rate (MMR).
Easy NORMAL · Surcharge | Computation of Tax | Basic Concepts
Surcharge is levied as a percentage of:
A. Total Income
B. Gross Total Income
C. Income-tax computed on Total Income ✔
D. Net Agricultural Income
Explanation: Surcharge is an additional tax levied as a specified percentage of the income-tax calculated on the total income of an assessee, when the total income exceeds specified threshold limits.
Easy NORMAL · Health and Education Cess | Cess Rate | Tax Computation
Health and Education Cess is computed at what rate on the income-tax plus surcharge?
A. 2%
B. 3%
C. 4% ✔
D. 5%
Explanation: Health and Education Cess is levied at the rate of 4% on the aggregate of income-tax and applicable surcharge for all assessees under the Income-tax Act.
Medium NORMAL · Section 115BAC | Exemption Limit | Tax Slabs
Under Section 115BAC, for an individual opting for the default/concessional tax regime, what is the basic exemption limit for the AY 2026-27 (assuming new slab rates)?
A. Rs. 2,50,000
B. Rs. 3,00,000 ✔
C. Rs. 5,00,000
D. Rs. 2,00,000
Explanation: Under the concessional tax regime of Section 115BAC for individuals (as amended in recent Finance Acts), the basic exemption limit is Rs. 3,00,000.
Hard NORMAL · Marginal Relief | Surcharge | Tax Computation
Marginal relief is designed to ensure that:
A. Total tax payable does not exceed the total income earned
B. The incremental tax liability due to surcharge does not exceed the incremental income above the threshold limit ✔
C. No tax is paid by senior citizens having income below Rs. 5,00,000
D. Rebate under Section 87A completely eliminates tax for low-income earners
Explanation: Marginal relief provides that the additional amount of income-tax payable (including surcharge) on excess income over the surcharge threshold should not be greater than the actual amount of income earned in excess of that threshold.
Medium NORMAL · Income-tax Authorities | Section 116 | Administration
Which of the following authorities is NOT part of the income-tax administration hierarchy under Section 116?
A. Central Board of Direct Taxes (CBDT)
B. Chief Commissioners of Income-tax
C. Goods and Services Tax Council (GST Council) ✔
D. Assessing Officers
Explanation: The GST Council is a constitutional body for GST governance and is not an income-tax authority under Section 116 of the Income-tax Act, 1961. CBDT, Chief Commissioners, and Assessing Officers are statutory income-tax authorities.
Hard NORMAL · CBDT Circulars | Section 119 | Binding Nature
What is the legal status of circulars issued by the Central Board of Direct Taxes (CBDT) under Section 119?
A. They are binding on the Income-tax authorities, but not on the assessees ✔
B. They are binding on both the income-tax authorities and the assessees
C. They are advisory in nature for all parties
D. They are binding on assessees if beneficial to them, but not on tax authorities
Explanation: CBDT circulars issued under Section 119 are binding on all income-tax authorities, but they cannot override the provisions of the Act nor can they impose a burden on assessees (meaning assessees can rely on beneficial circulars, but authorities are strictly bound by them).
Medium NORMAL · Income-tax Act | Rules | Statutory Interpretation
In case of conflict between a provision of the Income-tax Act, 1961 and an Income-tax Rule framed thereunder, which one prevails?
A. Income-tax Rules always prevail
B. Income-tax Act prevails over the Rules ✔
C. Whichever is beneficial to the assessee
D. The CBDT decides which one applies
Explanation: Rules are framed under the rule-making power of the Act (subordinate legislation). Therefore, in case of any conflict or inconsistency, the provisions of the parent statute (Income-tax Act, 1961) will always prevail over the Income-tax Rules.
Medium NORMAL · Rebate | Section 87A | Section 115BAC
Under Section 87A, what is the maximum rebate available to a resident individual under the default tax regime (Section 115BAC) for AY 2026-27?
A. Rs. 12,500
B. Rs. 25,000 ✔
C. Rs. 10,000
D. Rs. 60,000
Explanation: Under Section 87A for individuals opting for Section 115BAC, the maximum rebate is Rs. 25,000 (applicable when total income does not exceed Rs. 7,00,000, subject to marginal relief provisions).
Medium NORMAL · Definition of Income | Section 2(24) | Charitable Trusts
Which of the following is considered 'Income' under an inclusive definition given in Section 2(24)?
A. Capital loss incurred on sale of shares
B. Voluntary contributions received by a trust created wholly for charitable purposes ✔
C. Loan taken from a nationalized bank
D. Inherited property from parents
Explanation: Section 2(24) expansively defines income to include voluntary contributions received by a trust created wholly for charitable or religious purposes. Loans, capital losses, and inherited properties are generally not considered income.
Hard NORMAL · Discontinued Business | Section 176 | Assessment in PY
When a business is discontinued, what is the tax treatment regarding the previous year of discontinuation?
A. Income of the period up to the date of discontinuation may, at the discretion of the Assessing Officer, be assessed in that same financial year ✔
B. Income is always assessed in the subsequent assessment year without exception
C. Discontinuation has no tax impact until the next financial year ends
D. Income of the discontinued business is exempt
Explanation: Under Section 176, where any business or profession is discontinued in any assessment year, the income of the period from the expiry of the previous year up to the date of discontinuation may, at the discretion of the Assessing Officer, be charged to tax in that assessment year.
Easy NORMAL · Gross Total Income | Heads of Income | Computation Flow
What does 'Gross Total Income' (GTI) signify under the Income-tax Act?
A. Total income computed after allowing all Chapter VI-A deductions
B. Aggregate of income computed under all five heads of income, after giving effect to provisions for clubbing and set-off of losses, but before Chapter VI-A deductions ✔
C. Total receipts of an assessee before any deductions or exemptions
D. Income-tax liability before adding surcharge and cess
Explanation: Gross Total Income is the aggregate of income computed under the five heads of income (Salary, House Property, PGBP, Capital Gains, and Other Sources) after making adjustments for clubbing of income and set-off of losses, but before deducting Chapter VI-A deductions.
Easy NORMAL · Tax Rates | Partnership Firm | Flat Rate
Which of the following entities is taxed at a flat rate of 30% (plus applicable surcharge and cess) under normal provisions, without slab benefits?
A. Resident Individual
B. Hindu Undivided Family (HUF)
C. Partnership Firm (including LLP) ✔
D. Resident Senior Citizen
Explanation: Partnership firms and LLPs are taxable at a flat rate of 30% on their total income under normal provisions of the Income-tax Act. Individuals and HUFs enjoy slab-wise tax rates.
Hard NORMAL · Agricultural Income | Partial Integration | Tax Rate Determination
Can agricultural income be clubbed with non-agricultural income for determining the rate of income-tax applicable to an individual (partial integration)?
A. No, agricultural income is completely separate and never considered
B. Yes, if non-agricultural income exceeds the basic exemption limit and agricultural income exceeds Rs. 5,000 ✔
C. Yes, for all corporate assessees as well
D. No, partial integration was abolished
Explanation: Partial integration of agricultural income with non-agricultural income applies to individuals, HUFs, AOPs, BOIs, and artificial juridical persons if non-agricultural income exceeds the basic exemption limit AND agricultural income exceeds Rs. 5,000.
Easy NORMAL · Heads of Income | Section 14 | Basic Concepts
Which of the following is NOT one of the five heads of income specified under Section 14?
A. Income from Salary
B. Income from House Property
C. Income from Digital Assets ✔
D. Income from Other Sources
Explanation: Section 14 categorizes all income under five heads: (1) Salaries, (2) Income from house property, (3) Profits and gains of business or profession, (4) Capital gains, and (5) Income from other sources. 'Income from Digital Assets' is a category of income, not a head of income.
Medium NORMAL · Previous Year | Newly Incorporated Company | Section 3
For a newly formed company incorporated on 10th February of the financial year, what is the duration of its first previous year?
A. 1st April of that financial year to 31st March of the next year
B. 10th February of that financial year to 31st March of the same financial year ✔
C. 10th February of that financial year to 31st March of the next year
D. 1st January to 31st December
Explanation: Just like any newly set-up business or newly incorporated entity, the first previous year for a company starts from the date of its incorporation (10th February) and ends on 31st March of that same financial year.
Medium NORMAL · Surcharge | Progressive Taxation | Tax Policy
What is the primary objective of levying surcharge under the Income-tax Act?
A. To raise additional revenue from high-income earners (progressive taxation) ✔
B. To fund local municipal corporations
C. To penalize tax evaders
D. To replace the corporate tax structure
Explanation: Surcharge is an additional levy on higher income brackets, embodying the principle of progressive taxation where those with higher financial capacity contribute a higher effective tax percentage.
Hard NORMAL · Definition of Assassessee | Section 2(7) | Basic Concepts
Under Section 2(7), 'Assassessee' means any person by whom any tax or other sum of money is payable under the Act. Which of the following is ALSO included in the definition of assessee?
A. A person in respect of whom proceedings under the Act have been taken for the assessment of his income ✔
B. A salaried employee whose employer deducts TDS correctly with no pending liability
C. A foreign tourist visiting India for 5 days with zero Indian income
D. A retail buyer purchasing goods subject to GST
Explanation: An assessee includes any person by whom any tax, interest, or penalty is payable, as well as every person in respect of whom any proceeding under the Act has been taken for the assessment of his income, loss, or refund.
Hard NORMAL · Constitutional Validity | Union List Entry 82 | Taxing Power
Which of the following constitutional provisions empowers the Parliament of India to make laws in respect of taxes on income other than agricultural income?
A. Article 246, Seventh Schedule, Union List, Entry 82 ✔
B. Article 270, State List, Entry 46
C. Article 265, Concurrent List, Entry 12
D. Article 300A
Explanation: Entry 82 of the Union List (List I) in the Seventh Schedule of the Constitution of India empowers Parliament to legislate on taxes on income other than agricultural income. Entry 46 of the State List covers agricultural income taxes.
CASE SCENARIO: Mr. Raghav, a resident Indian aged 42, sets up a new retail garment business on 1st August 2025. During the financial year 2025-26, he earns income under various heads including business income, capital gains, and bank interest. He is evaluating whether to opt out of the default tax regime under Section 115BAC.
Medium SCENARIO · Previous Year | Newly Set-up Business | Section 3
What will be the duration of the first previous year for Mr. Raghav's newly set-up retail garment business?
A. 1st April 2025 to 31st March 2026
B. 1st August 2025 to 31st March 2026 ✔
C. 1st August 2025 to 31st July 2026
D. 1st April 2025 to 31st July 2025
Explanation: As per Section 3, for a newly set-up business, the first previous year commences on the date of setting up of the business (1st August 2025) and ends on the last day of the financial year (31st March 2026).
Medium SCENARIO · Assessment Year | Previous Year | Charging Section
In which assessment year will the income earned by Mr. Raghav during the financial year 2025-26 normally be assessed to tax?
A. AY 2025-26
B. AY 2026-27 ✔
C. AY 2027-28
D. At the option of Mr. Raghav
Explanation: Under the general rule of Section 4, income of a previous year (FY 2025-26) is assessed to tax in the immediately following assessment year, which is AY 2026-27.
Hard SCENARIO · Section 115BAC | Default Tax Regime | Deductions
If Mr. Raghav chooses to remain under the default tax regime of Section 115BAC for AY 2026-27, which of the following deductions will he generally NOT be permitted to claim?
A. Deduction under Section 80CCD(2) for employer's NPS contribution
B. Deduction under Section 80C for life insurance premium ✔
C. Deduction under Section 80JJAA for new workmen
D. Standard deduction from salary (if applicable)
Explanation: Under the default tax regime of Section 115BAC, general Chapter VI-A deductions such as Section 80C are disallowed, whereas Section 80CCD(2), 80JJAA, and standard deduction under Section 16(ia) are available.
Medium SCENARIO · Heads of Income | PGBP | Section 28
Under which head of income will Mr. Raghav's earnings from the retail garment business be computed?
A. Income from Salary
B. Income from House Property
C. Profits and gains of business or profession ✔
D. Income from Other Sources
Explanation: Income derived from running a retail garment business falls under the head 'Profits and gains of business or profession' (PGBP) pursuant to Section 28 of the Income-tax Act.
CASE SCENARIO: M/s. Apex Associates, a partnership firm, has total income of Rs. 1,02,00,000 for the financial year 2025-26. The firm comprises three resident partners who share profits equally. The firm is calculating its total tax liability including surcharge and cess.
Medium SCENARIO · Partnership Firm | Tax Rates | Flat Rate
What is the normal income-tax rate applicable to partnership firm M/s. Apex Associates under the Income-tax Act for AY 2026-27?
A. 25%
B. 30% ✔
C. 22%
D. Maximum Marginal Rate
Explanation: Partnership firms (including LLPs) are taxable at a flat rate of 30% on their total income under the normal provisions of the Income-tax Act.
Hard SCENARIO · Surcharge | Partnership Firm | Thresholds
Since the total income of M/s. Apex Associates exceeds Rs. 1 crore, what is the applicable surcharge rate?
A. 7%
B. 10%
C. 12% ✔
D. 15%
Explanation: For a partnership firm (domestic non-corporate entity), a surcharge of 12% is levied when total income exceeds Rs. 1 crore (and up to Rs. 10 crores).
Medium SCENARIO · Health and Education Cess | Tax Computation | Cess Rate
How is Health and Education Cess calculated for M/s. Apex Associates?
A. 3% of basic tax
B. 4% of basic tax plus surcharge ✔
C. 4% of total income
D. 1% of turnover
Explanation: Health and Education Cess is levied at 4% on the aggregate of income-tax and applicable surcharge for all categories of assessees.
Hard SCENARIO · Partnership Firm | Section 10(2A) | Exemptions
Are the shares of profits received by the individual partners from M/s. Apex Associates taxable in the hands of the partners?
A. Yes, fully taxable under PGBP
B. No, share of profit received from a firm is exempt under Section 10(2A) in the hands of the partners ✔
C. Taxable only if total income of partner exceeds Rs. 10 lakhs
D. Taxable as capital gains
Explanation: Under Section 10(2A), the share of profit received by a partner from a firm is exempt from tax in the partner's hands, because the firm has already paid tax on its profits.
CASE SCENARIO: Dr. Meera, a resident individual aged 61, earns rental income from a commercial property, salary from a university, and agricultural income from her ancestral land in Kerala amounting to Rs. 4,50,000. Her non-agricultural total income for AY 2026-27 is Rs. 9,50,000.
Medium SCENARIO · House Property | Section 22 | Heads of Income
Under which head of income is the rental income from Dr. Meera's commercial property taxable?
A. Income from Salary
B. Income from House Property ✔
C. Profits and gains of business or profession
D. Income from Other Sources
Explanation: Rental income from property (whether residential or commercial) owned by the assessee is taxable under the head 'Income from House Property' under Section 22.
Hard SCENARIO · Agricultural Income | Section 10(1) | Partial Integration
What is the tax treatment of Dr. Meera's agricultural income of Rs. 4,50,000 under Section 10(1)?
A. Fully taxable under Income from Other Sources
B. Exempt under Section 10(1), but subject to partial integration for rate purposes ✔
C. Fully taxable at slab rates
D. Exempt and completely ignored for all tax computations
Explanation: Agricultural income in India is exempt under Section 10(1). However, since her non-agricultural income exceeds the basic exemption limit and agricultural income exceeds Rs. 5,000, it is subject to partial integration for determining the tax rate on non-agricultural income.
Medium SCENARIO · Senior Citizen | Exemption Limit | Old Tax Regime
What is the basic exemption limit applicable to Dr. Meera (aged 61) under the normal provisions (old tax regime) for AY 2026-27?
A. Rs. 2,50,000
B. Rs. 3,00,000 ✔
C. Rs. 5,00,000
D. Rs. 2,00,000
Explanation: Under the normal provisions (old tax regime), for a resident senior citizen (aged 60 years or more but less than 80 years), the basic exemption limit is Rs. 3,00,000.
Medium SCENARIO · Salary | Standard Deduction | Section 16(ia)
Can Dr. Meera claim standard deduction against her salary income under the old tax regime?
A. No, standard deduction is only for corporate employees
B. Yes, standard deduction under Section 16(ia) is available to salaried assessees ✔
C. Yes, but only up to Rs. 10,000
D. Only if she opts out of Section 115BAC
Explanation: Standard deduction under Section 16(ia) is available to salaried taxpayers under both the old tax regime and the default tax regime.
CASE SCENARIO: Mr. Vikram, a resident individual, leaves India on 15th December 2025 for permanent employment abroad with no intention of returning to India in the foreseeable future. He earned substantial capital gains and other income prior to his departure during the financial year 2025-26.
Hard SCENARIO · Section 174 | Leaving India | Assessment in PY
Which specific provision empowers the Assessing Officer to assess Mr. Vikram's income for the period up to 15th December 2025 in the same assessment year?
A. Section 174 ✔
B. Section 175
C. Section 176
D. Section 4
Explanation: Section 174 deals with assessment of income of a person leaving India, empowering the Assessing Officer to assess the total income of such person up to the date of departure in the same assessment year.
Hard SCENARIO · Assessment Year | Section 174 | Exceptions to PY Rule
What is the assessment year for the income assessed under Section 174 in Mr. Vikram's case for the period up to his departure?
A. AY 2025-26 ✔
B. AY 2026-27
C. AY 2027-28
D. Assessment year is not applicable
Explanation: Under Section 174, income of a person leaving India permanently is assessed in the same previous year/assessment year in which they leave (i.e., AY 2025-26, since departure is in FY 2025-26).
Hard SCENARIO · Tax Clearance Certificate | Section 230 | Leaving India
What is required from Mr. Vikram before he leaves India in terms of tax clearance?
A. He must obtain a tax clearance certificate under Section 230 where applicable ✔
B. He must pay advance tax for the next 5 years in advance
C. He must surrender his PAN card permanently
D. No formalities are required if he is leaving for employment
Explanation: Persons leaving India in certain circumstances (such as financial liabilities or specific categories) are required to obtain a tax clearance certificate under Section 230 before boarding transport from India.
Easy SCENARIO · Definition of Person | Individual | Section 2(31)
Under the definition of 'Person' in Section 2(31), Mr. Vikram is classified as:
A. Artificial juridical person
B. Individual ✔
C. Association of Persons
D. Non-resident entity
Explanation: Mr. Vikram, being a human being, is classified as an 'Individual' under Section 2(31)(i) of the Income-tax Act.
CASE SCENARIO: XYZ Ltd., a domestic company, has a total taxable income of Rs. 10,20,00,000 for the financial year 2025-26. The company is evaluating its tax liabilities under the normal provisions and checking the applicability of surcharge thresholds.
Medium SCENARIO · Domestic Company | Corporate Tax Rate | Normal Provisions
What is the base corporate tax rate for a domestic company under the normal provisions (assuming turnover conditions do not qualify it for 25%)?
A. 22%
B. 25%
C. 30% ✔
D. 35%
Explanation: Under the normal provisions of the Income-tax Act, domestic companies are generally taxable at 30% (unless specific turnover or concessional rates like Section 115BAA/115BAB apply).
Hard SCENARIO · Surcharge | Domestic Company | Thresholds
Since XYZ Ltd.'s total income exceeds Rs. 10 crore, what is the applicable surcharge rate?
A. 7%
B. 10%
C. 12% ✔
D. 7% or 12% depending on section opted
Explanation: For a domestic company, when total income exceeds Rs. 10 crores under normal provisions, the applicable surcharge rate is 12% (if total income is between Rs. 1 crore and Rs. 10 crores, it is 7%; exceeding Rs. 10 crores, it is 12%).
Hard SCENARIO · Marginal Relief | Company Surcharge | Tax Computation
Is marginal relief available to XYZ Ltd. when its total income exceeds Rs. 10 crores?
A. No marginal relief is ever available to companies
B. Yes, marginal relief ensures that additional tax due to surcharge does not exceed income above Rs. 10 crores ✔
C. Marginal relief is only available to individuals and HUFs
D. Marginal relief applies automatically without any computation
Explanation: Marginal relief is available to companies as well when total income exceeds threshold limits (like Rs. 10 crores), ensuring the incremental tax and surcharge liability does not exceed the incremental income over the threshold.
Medium SCENARIO · Finance Act | Tax Rates | Basic Concepts
Which statutory authority enacted the rates of income-tax and surcharge for XYZ Ltd. for AY 2026-27?
A. Central Board of Direct Taxes (CBDT) via notification
B. The Finance Act passed by Parliament ✔
C. Reserve Bank of India (RBI)
D. Ministry of Corporate Affairs (MCA)
Explanation: The rates of income-tax, surcharge, and cess for any assessment year are enacted annually by the Finance Act passed by Parliament.

Paper 3: Taxation · Module 1 · Chapter 2:

Taxation — 55 rows
Easy NORMAL · Residential Status | Individual | Basic Conditions
Under section 6(1), an individual is a resident in India during the previous year if he satisfies the basic condition of being in India for a period of ___ days or more in that previous year.
A. 182 ✔
B. 60
C. 365
D. 90
Explanation: According to section 6(1)(a), an individual is resident in India if he is in India for a period of 182 days or more during the relevant previous year. This is the primary basic condition applicable to all individuals.
Medium NORMAL · Residential Status | Exceptions to 60 days | Employment Abroad
Which of the following individuals can substitute the 60-day period with a 182-day period under section 6(1)?
A. An Indian citizen who leaves India during the previous year for the purpose of employment outside India ✔
B. An Indian citizen engaged in a managerial position in a foreign company
C. A foreign citizen of non-Indian origin visiting India on a holiday
D. A person of Indian origin residing in the UK visiting India for a short vacation
Explanation: Section 6(1) provides an exception where the 60-day threshold is replaced by 182 days for an Indian citizen who leaves India during the previous year for the purpose of employment outside India, or as a member of the crew of an Indian ship.
Medium NORMAL · PIO | Indian Citizen | Visit to India | 120 days rule
For a citizen of India or a person of Indian origin who, being outside India, comes on a visit to India during the previous year, the 60-day period is substituted by ___ days, provided his total income (other than income from foreign sources) does not exceed Rs. 15 lakhs.
A. 182
B. 120 ✔
C. 180
D. 365
