D. Article 32
Explanation: Article 301 of the Constitution states that trade, commerce, and intercourse throughout the territory of India shall be free, which necessitated careful structuring of IGST to prevent trade barriers between states.
Medium NORMAL · Cascading Effect | Pre-GST Regime | Cross-credit
Under the pre-GST indirect tax regime, what was the primary cause of the 'cascading effect'?
A. Non-availability of cross-credit between Central taxes (like Excise) and State taxes (like VAT) ✔
B. Excessive use of electronic invoicing
C. Uniform tax rates across all states
D. Exemption of small traders from taxation
Explanation: The cascading effect occurred because Central taxes paid on inputs could not be set off against State taxes output liabilities (and vice versa), leading to tax being levied on tax.
Easy NORMAL · CBIC | Administration | Indirect Taxes
Which of the following entities functions as the apex operational body for administering central indirect tax laws including GST at the national level?
A. Central Board of Direct Taxes (CBDT)
B. Central Board of Indirect Taxes and Customs (CBIC) ✔
C. Goods and Services Tax Network (GSTN)
D. Securities and Exchange Board of India (SEBI)
Explanation: The Central Board of Indirect Taxes and Customs (CBIC) under the Ministry of Finance administers central indirect tax laws, including CGST, IGST, and Customs.
Medium NORMAL · Petroleum Products | GST Council | Constitutional Provisions
In the context of petroleum and natural gas, when can the GST Council notify the levy of GST on crude oil and high-speed diesel?
A. Automatically after 10 years from GST rollout
B. Only upon the recommendation of the GST Council ✔
C. By a direct executive order of the Prime Minister
D. After ratification by all 28 states unconditionally
Explanation: As per Article 246A and related constitutional provisions, GST on petroleum crude, HSD, petrol, natural gas, and ATF will be levied from a date to be recommended by the GST Council.
CASE SCENARIO: M/s Apex Manufacturing Ltd., located in the State of Gujarat, procures raw materials worth Rs. 10,00,000 from local suppliers within Gujarat and pays CGST and SGST. It also imports specialized machinery from Germany, paying Basic Customs Duty and IGST. The company manufactures finished goods and sells 60% of its production to buyers in Maharashtra and 40% to buyers within Gujarat.
Medium SCENARIO · Inter-state Supply | IGST | Place of Supply
What type of tax will M/s Apex Manufacturing Ltd. charge on the sale of goods made to buyers located in Maharashtra?
A. CGST and SGST
B. IGST ✔
C. UTGST and CGST
D. State VAT
Explanation: Since the location of the supplier is in Gujarat and the place of supply (buyer) is in Maharashtra, it is an inter-state supply, which attracts Integrated Goods and Services Tax (IGST).
Medium SCENARIO · Intra-state Supply | CGST | SGST
What type of tax will M/s Apex Manufacturing Ltd. charge on the sale of goods made to buyers located within Gujarat?
A. IGST only
B. CGST and SGST ✔
C. CGST and UTGST
D. Basic Customs Duty
Explanation: When both the supplier and the buyer are located within the same state (Gujarat), it is an intra-state supply, attracting CGST and SGST concurrently.
Hard SCENARIO · Input Tax Credit | IGST Utilization | Import of Machinery
Can M/s Apex Manufacturing Ltd. utilize the IGST paid on the import of machinery against the CGST/SGST liability arising on intra-state sales?
A. No, import IGST cannot be utilized for domestic supplies
B. Yes, IGST credit can be utilized against CGST and SGST liability in the prescribed order ✔
C. Yes, but only against SGST and never against CGST
D. No, import duties cannot be set off under GST
Explanation: Input Tax Credit (ITC) of IGST paid on imports is seamlessly integrated into the GST credit pool and can be utilized against CGST and SGST liabilities after utilizing available IGST liability first.
Hard SCENARIO · Destination-Based Tax | IGST Apportionment | Consumption Principle
Which constitutional principle ensures that the revenue from the IGST charged on sales to Maharashtra eventually benefits the consuming state?
A. Origin-based taxation principle
B. Destination-based consumption tax principle ✔
C. Central revenue pooling principle
D. State equalization grant principle
Explanation: GST is a destination-based consumption tax; hence, the IGST collected on inter-state sales is apportioned to the consuming state where the goods are finally consumed.
CASE SCENARIO: The State of Zeta has recently witnessed a sharp decline in its state tax revenues following the nationwide rollout of GST. The state finance minister raises concerns in a GST Council meeting regarding budgetary shortfalls. Simultaneously, the Council discusses whether to bring electricity and alcoholic liquor for human consumption under the GST net, and whether to revise the compensation cess rates on luxury vehicles.
Medium SCENARIO · GST Compensation | Protected Revenue | Compensation Cess
What constitutional mechanism was originally established to protect states like Zeta from revenue shortfalls during the initial years of GST?
A. Permanent special grants from the RBI
B. GST Compensation to States Act providing guaranteed revenue growth backed by a compensation cess ✔
C. Automatic borrowing rights from international banks
D. Exemption from paying Central taxes
Explanation: The GST (Compensation to States) Act, 2017 guaranteed states a 14% protected revenue growth for a transition period, funded through a compensation cess levied on luxury and demerit goods.
Hard SCENARIO · Alcoholic Liquor | Constitutional Amendment | Article 366(12A)
Can the GST Council unilaterally bring 'alcoholic liquor for human consumption' under GST without a constitutional amendment?
A. Yes, by a three-fourths majority vote in the GST Council
B. No, because the Constitution explicitly excludes alcoholic liquor from the definition of GST under Article 366(12A) ✔
C. Yes, if all Union Territories agree
D. Yes, through an executive notification issued by the Ministry of Finance
Explanation: Alcoholic liquor for human consumption is excluded by definition in Article 366(12A). Bringing it under GST requires a formal constitutional amendment passed by Parliament and ratified by states.
Medium SCENARIO · GST Council | Voting Majority | Article 279A
What voting majority is required in the GST Council for decisions regarding changes in compensation cess or tax rates?
A. Simple majority (more than 50%)
B. Unanimous consensus of all members
C. Not less than three-fourths of the weighted votes of members present and voting ✔
D. Two-thirds majority of central members only
Explanation: All decisions of the GST Council, including rates, exemptions, and cesses, must be taken by a majority of not less than three-fourths of the weighted votes of the members present and voting.
Hard SCENARIO · Electricity | Exclusions | Pre-GST Laws
What is the status of electricity under the GST framework?
A. Taxed at a special merit rate of 5%
B. Exempted under GST while continuing to be governed by state electricity duties and pre-GST laws ✔
C. Taxed under IGST for inter-state transmission
D. Subsumed completely into CGST
Explanation: Electricity is neither subsumed into GST nor taxed under GST currently; it continues to be governed by pre-GST laws and state-level electricity duties.
CASE SCENARIO: A multi-national enterprise, Global Tech Corp, provides IT-enabled consultancy services from its office in Bengaluru to a client in Chennai. In the same tax period, Global Tech Corp also procures office stationery locally in Bengaluru, paying CGST and SGST, and avails cloud computing services from a server hosted in Mumbai, paying IGST.
Medium SCENARIO · Inter-state Supply | Services | Place of Supply
What category of supply is the consultancy service provided by Global Tech Corp from Bengaluru to the client in Chennai?
A. Intra-state supply
B. Inter-state supply ✔
C. Export of service
D. Exempt supply
Explanation: Since the location of the supplier (Bengaluru, Karnataka) and the place of supply (Chennai, Tamil Nadu) are in two different states, it is an inter-state supply attracting IGST.
Medium SCENARIO · Input Tax Credit | Office Stationery | Set-off
How should Global Tech Corp treat the CGST and SGST paid on local procurement of office stationery?
A. Claim it as an expense in the Profit and Loss account
B. Claim it as Input Tax Credit (ITC) to set off against its output tax liabilities ✔
C. Claim a refund directly from the State Government treasury
D. Ignore it as non-allowable credit
Explanation: Taxes paid on local procurements used in the course or furtherance of business qualify as Input Tax Credit (ITC) and can be utilized to offset output tax liabilities, preventing cascading.
Medium SCENARIO · Inter-state Supply | Cloud Computing | IGST
Which tax will be levied on the cloud computing service procured from Mumbai by the Bengaluru office?
A. CGST and SGST
B. IGST ✔
C. Customs Duty
D. Service Tax
Explanation: Supply of services between Mumbai (Maharashtra) and Bengaluru (Karnataka) is an inter-state supply of services, which attracts Integrated Goods and Services Tax (IGST).
Medium SCENARIO · IGST Act 2017 | Legislation | Inter-state Supply
Which legislative enactment governs the levy of IGST on inter-state supply of services in India?
A. The CGST Act, 2017
B. The IGST Act, 2017 ✔
C. The Customs Act, 1962
D. The Finance Act, 1994
Explanation: The Integrated Goods and Services Tax Act, 2017 (IGST Act) governs the levy and collection of IGST on all inter-state supplies of goods and services and on imports into India.
CASE SCENARIO: A legislative drafting committee is reviewing the historical evolution of indirect taxes in India to prepare a training module for CA Intermediate students. The committee is analyzing why certain taxes like Central Excise Duty and State VAT were replaced, why Customs Duty was retained, and how the dual GST structure was embedded into the Constitution through specific legislative entries.
Medium SCENARIO · Customs Duty | Imports | Subsumed Taxes
Why was Basic Customs Duty retained outside the GST framework?
A. Because customs duties are exclusively levied on domestic consumption within states
B. Because customs duty protects domestic industry from foreign competition and is levied on goods entering India from outside the country, separate from domestic supply ✔
C. Because the Constitution prohibits merging customs with GST
D. Because international trade agreements forbid subsuming customs duties
Explanation: Basic Customs Duty is levied on imports from foreign territories under the Customs Act to regulate foreign trade and protect domestic industry, and is distinct from domestic supplies taxed under GST.
Hard SCENARIO · Union List | Entry 92C | Seventh Schedule
Which entry in the Union List (List I of the Seventh Schedule) was amended or deleted to accommodate the taxation of services under GST?
A. Entry 92 (Taxes on sale or purchase of newspapers)
B. Entry 92C (Taxes on services) ✔
C. Entry 84 (Duties of excise)
D. Entry 54 (Taxes on sale or purchase of goods)
Explanation: Entry 92C of the Union List, which earlier dealt with 'Taxes on services', was deleted by the Constitution (101st Amendment) Act, 2016, as services are now taxed under Article 246A via CGST and IGST.
Medium SCENARIO · Cascading Effect | Dual GST | Value Addition
What primary economic defect of the pre-GST regime was addressed by the introduction of the dual GST model?
A. High compliance cost for large enterprises
B. Cascading effect of taxes due to lack of seamless input tax credit across central and state levies ✔
C. Excessive collection of direct income taxes
D. Fluctuations in foreign exchange reserves
Explanation: The dual GST model eliminated the cascading effect by allowing cross-utilization of CGST and SGST (or seamless IGST credit), ensuring tax is levied only on value addition.
Hard SCENARIO · Model GST Law | SGST | GST Council Harmonization
Under the dual GST framework, if a state enacts a State GST law, what is the mandatory constitutional prerequisite regarding conformity with model laws?
A. State laws must be identical to Central law in all substantive matters recommended by the GST Council
B. State GST laws can have completely independent tax rate slabs and exemption limits ✔
C. State GST laws require prior presidential assent before draft preparation
D. State GST laws apply only to manufacturing sectors
Explanation: While SGST laws are enacted by respective state legislatures, they generally conform to the Model SGST Act recommended by the GST Council to maintain uniformity in definitions, procedures, and tax incidence across India.
CASE SCENARIO: Zenith Enterprises operates a chain of retail stores across multiple states and Union Territories, including Delhi (UT with legislature), Andaman and Nicobar Islands (UT without legislature), and Uttar Pradesh. The company transfers goods inter-branch, makes retail sales to consumers, and procures taxable services from local consultants.
Medium SCENARIO · UTGST | Union Territories | Andaman and Nicobar
For retail sales made from a store in Andaman and Nicobar Islands to a local customer, which taxes will Zenith Enterprises charge?
A. CGST and SGST
B. CGST and UTGST ✔
C. IGST only
D. VAT and Excise
Explanation: Andaman and Nicobar Islands is a Union Territory without a legislature. Intra-UT supplies in such territories attract CGST and UTGST concurrently.
Medium SCENARIO · Delhi | SGST | Union Territory with Legislature
For retail sales made from a store in Delhi to a local customer, which taxes will Zenith Enterprises charge?
A. CGST and UTGST
B. CGST and SGST ✔
C. IGST only
D. Delhi Sales Tax
Explanation: Delhi is a Union Territory with its own legislature (treated as a State for GST purposes). Intra-state/intra-UT supplies in Delhi attract CGST and SGST concurrently.
Hard SCENARIO · UTGST Act 2017 | Union Territories | Legislation
What is the legal status of UTGST under the GST legislative framework?
A. It is levied under the Union Territory Goods and Services Tax Act, 2017 for UTs without legislatures ✔
B. It is a state tax levied by neighboring state governments
C. It is an optional tax levied by municipal corporations
D. It replaces IGST for all domestic transactions
Explanation: UTGST is levied under the UTGST Act, 2017 in Union Territories without a legislature (such as Chandigarh, Dadra and Nagar Haveli and Daman and Diu, Andaman and Nicobar Islands, Lakshadweep, Ladakh).
Hard SCENARIO · Stock Transfer | Distinct Persons | Schedule I Supply
If Zenith Enterprises transfers goods from its warehouse in Uttar Pradesh to its retail branch in Delhi, how is this transaction treated under GST?
A. Not a supply since it is between branches of the same entity
B. Deemed supply of goods between distinct persons, attracting IGST ✔
C. Exempted from all taxes as internal stock transfer
D. Subject to CGST and SGST of Uttar Pradesh only
Explanation: Under Section 7 read with Schedule I of the CGST Act, supply of goods between different establishments of the same person having separate registrations (in different states/UTs) is treated as a supply ('distinct persons') and attracts IGST.

Paper 3: Taxation · Module 1 · Chapter 2:

Taxation — 55 rows
Easy NORMAL · Schedule III | Employer-Employee | Scope of Supply
Which of the following activities does NOT constitute a 'supply' under section 7 of the CGST Act, 2017, even if made for a consideration?
A. Import of services for a business purpose without consideration
B. Services by an employee to the employer in the course of or in relation to employment ✔
C. Supply of goods by an unincorporated association of persons to a member for consideration
D. Disposal of business assets on which input tax credit has been availed
Explanation: According to Section 7(2)(a) read with Schedule III of the CGST Act, 2017, services by an employee to the employer in the course of or in relation to employment are treated neither as a supply of goods nor as a supply of services. Therefore, it is outside the scope of GST.
Medium NORMAL · Schedule I | Distinct Persons | No Consideration
Mr. A, a registered taxpayer in Delhi, transfers stock of goods from his principal place of business in Delhi to his registered branch in Mumbai without any consideration. What will be the tax treatment of this transaction under GST?
A. It is not a supply since there is no consideration.
B. It is a supply of goods because it is made between distinct persons even without consideration. ✔
C. It is an exempt supply under Schedule III.
D. It is a supply of services since no ownership is transferred.
Explanation: As per Schedule I of the CGST Act, 2017, permanent transfer or disposal of business assets where input tax credit has been availed is treated as supply even if made without consideration. Further, supplies made between distinct persons (same PAN, different state registrations) even without consideration are treated as supply.
Easy NORMAL · Schedule III | Actionable Claims | Negative List
Which of the following activities is specifically included in Schedule III as 'neither supply of goods nor supply of services'?
A. Actionable claims, other than lottery, betting and gambling ✔
B. Supply of goods from a bonded warehouse before clearance for home consumption
C. Works contract services supplied to the Central Government
D. Temporary transfer of intellectual property right
Explanation: Schedule III of the CGST Act, 2017 lists activities or transactions which shall be treated neither as a supply of goods nor a supply of services. Actionable claims, other than lottery, betting and gambling, form part of this negative list.
Medium NORMAL · Composite Supply | Restaurant Services | Section 2(30)
A restaurant provides a package consisting of food, soft drinks, and live musical entertainment for a single consolidated price. How is this transaction classified under GST?
A. As separate supplies of goods and services attracting individual rates
B. As a composite supply where the principal supply is restaurant service ✔
C. As a mixed supply where the highest rate of tax applies
D. As an exempt supply of entertainment services
Explanation: Provision of food along with other services like live music in a restaurant naturally bundles the services in the ordinary course of business. As per Section 2(30), this constitutes a composite supply, and the tax rate applicable to the principal supply (restaurant service) applies.
Medium NORMAL · Mixed Supply | Section 2(74) | Tax Rate Determination
A gift pack containing a branded watch, a leather wallet, and imported chocolates is sold for a single lump sum price of Rs. 5,000. These items are not naturally bundled in the ordinary course of business. How will this transaction be treated under GST?
A. Composite supply taxable at the rate of the watch
B. Mixed supply taxable at the highest rate applicable to any of the items in the pack ✔
C. Multiple independent supplies attracting respective individual tax rates
D. Exempt supply since it is sold as a gift pack
Explanation: Under Section 2(74) of the CGST Act, 2017, a mixed supply means two or more individual supplies of goods or services made in conjunction with each other for a single price, where such supply does not constitute a composite supply. Each of these items can be supplied independently. Therefore, it is treated as a mixed supply and taxed at the rate applicable to the item attracting the highest rate of tax.
Hard NORMAL · Government Services | Taxable Supply | Renting
Which of the following transactions undertaken by a central government department will be treated as a supply of goods or services under GST?
A. Services by way of any activity in relation to a function entrusted to a Panchayat under Article 243G of the Constitution
B. Services by way of public health, sanitation, and water supply
C. Services by way of renting of immovable property to a registered business entity ✔
D. Services by way of issuing passports and visa
Explanation: While most sovereign functions of government are excluded, renting of immovable property by the government to a registered business entity is a taxable supply of service under forward charge / reverse charge as applicable, unlike sovereign regulatory functions which are not supplies.
Hard NORMAL · Import of Services | Schedule I | Related Person
M/s Alpha Ltd. imports architectural design services from an unrelated designer located in London for its upcoming factory building in Pune, without paying any consideration. Does this qualify as a supply?
A. No, because there is no consideration involved.
B. Yes, import of services by a taxable person from a related person or from any of his other establishments outside India, even without consideration, is a supply. ✔
C. Yes, import of services for any purpose, even without consideration and from an unrelated person, is always a supply under Section 7(1)(b).
D. No, since factory buildings are capital goods.
Explanation: Under Section 7(1)(b) read with paragraph 4 of Schedule I, import of services by a taxable person from a related person or from any of his other establishments outside India, in the course or furtherance of business, shall be treated as a supply even if made without consideration. Since the designer is unrelated, import without consideration does not constitute supply.
Medium NORMAL · Schedule II | Transfer of Title | Supply of Goods
Which of the following is considered a 'supply of goods' as per Schedule II of the CGST Act, 2017?
A. Transfer of right in goods or of undivided share in goods without the transfer of title thereof
B. Transfer of title in goods under an agreement that property shall pass at a future date upon payment ✔
C. Transfer of un-divided share in goods without transfer of title
D. Supply of services by way of a works contract
Explanation: As per Para 1(b) of Schedule II, any transfer of title in goods under an agreement which stipulates that property in goods shall pass at a future date upon payment of full consideration is a supply of goods.
Medium NORMAL · Schedule II | Business Assets | Supply of Goods
Under Schedule II, transfer of business assets where goods forming part of the assets of a business are transferred or disposed of by or under the directions of the person carrying on the business so as no longer to form part of those assets, whether or not for a consideration, is treated as:
A. Supply of services
B. Supply of goods ✔
C. Neither supply of goods nor supply of services
D. Exempt supply
Explanation: As per Para 4(a) of Schedule II of the CGST Act, 2017, such transfer or disposal of business assets is explicitly treated as a supply of goods.
Easy NORMAL · Actionable Claims | Lottery | Schedule III
Actionable claims specified under GST law that are subject to GST include:
A. Lottery, betting, and gambling ✔
B. Unsecured loans and promissory notes
C. Book debts and bills of exchange
D. Fixed deposit receipts
Explanation: Schedule III provides that actionable claims, other than lottery, betting, and gambling, shall be treated neither as supply of goods nor supply of services. Thus, lottery, betting, and gambling are taxable actionable claims treated as supply of goods.
Hard NORMAL · Director Remuneration | Reverse Charge | Schedule III
An individual acts as a Director of a private limited company and receives remuneration. How is this remuneration treated under GST?
A. Always treated as supply of services taxable under forward charge
B. Treated as supply of services taxable under reverse charge when paid to an independent director, but employer-employee relationship applies for executive whole-time directors ✔
C. Exempt under all circumstances as employment
D. Treated as supply of goods
Explanation: Remuneration paid to independent directors (not being employees of the company) is taxable under reverse charge mechanism as supply of services. However, services rendered by an employee-director (who is an employee) in the course of employment are covered under Schedule III (neither supply of goods nor services).
Hard NORMAL · Exemptions | Funeral Services | Scope vs Exemption
What is the taxability of 'services by way of burial, cremation, mortuary or funeral services including transportation of the deceased' under the CGST Act, 2017?
A. Taxable at 18% under forward charge
B. Taxable at 5% under composite supply
C. Neither supply of goods nor supply of services (Schedule III)
D. Exempt by way of specific notification entry, though falling within the definition of supply ✔
Explanation: Funeral, burial, cremation or mortuary services are supplies of service, but they are specifically exempt under the exemption notifications issued under GST, unlike Schedule III items which are outside the definition of supply entirely.
Easy NORMAL · Schedule III | Constitutional Functionaries | MPs and MLAs
Which of the following activities performed by a constitutional functionary is outside the scope of supply?
A. Services by a Member of Parliament or Member of State Legislature ✔
B. Services provided by a practicing Chartered Accountant
C. Services provided by a high-court advocate
D. Services provided by a registered real estate agent
Explanation: As per Schedule III, services by any person holding an office in pursuance of the provisions of the Constitution in that capacity (such as MPs, MLAs, members of local authorities) are treated neither as supply of goods nor supply of services.
Medium NORMAL · Hire Purchase | Schedule II | Supply of Goods
When goods are supplied on hire purchase, the transfer of goods is treated as:
A. Supply of services only
B. Supply of goods ✔
C. Neither supply of goods nor services
D. Purely a financial transaction
Explanation: Hire purchase agreements involve transfer of title in goods at a future date upon payment of final installment. As per Schedule II, this is classified as a supply of goods.
Hard NORMAL · Schedule II | Private Use | Supply of Services
If a person carrying on a business permanently puts business assets to private use or makes them available to any person for use for any purpose other than business, whether or not for a consideration, it is treated as:
A. Supply of services ✔
B. Supply of goods
C. Exempt supply
D. Not a supply
Explanation: As per Schedule II, where goods forming part of business assets are transferred or disposed of for non-business use, it is treated as a supply of services.
Medium NORMAL · Section 7(1)(a) | Course of Business | Elements of Supply
Which of the following is an essential element of 'supply' under Section 7(1)(a) of the CGST Act?
A. Supply must be made for a profit motive.
B. Supply must be made by a taxable person in the course or furtherance of business. ✔
C. Supply must be made only between registered persons.
D. Supply must involve physical movement of goods.
Explanation: Section 7(1)(a) requires that all forms of supply of goods or services such as sale, transfer, barter, exchange, licence, rental, lease or disposal made or agreed to be made for a consideration by a person in the course or furtherance of business must be present.
Hard NORMAL · Section 7(1)(aa) | Clubs and Associations | Mutuality
Under Section 7(1)(aa), the activities or transactions by a person, other than an individual, to its members or constituents or vice-versa, for cash, deferred payment or other valuable consideration shall be:
A. Treated as supply based on the principle of mutuality
B. Treated as not a supply due to the doctrine of incorporation
C. Deemed to be a supply, overcoming the principle of mutuality ✔
D. Exempted entirely from GST
Explanation: Section 7(1)(aa), inserted retrospectively, explicitly treats activities by clubs, associations, or societies to their members (or vice-versa) as supply, thereby abrogating the common law principle of mutuality.
Easy NORMAL · Consideration | Schedule I | General Principle
Can a transaction be subjected to GST if there is no 'consideration' and it does not fall under Schedule I?
A. Yes, if the value exceeds Rs. 50,000.
B. Yes, if it is done by a company.
C. No, consideration is an essential prerequisite for supply under Section 7(1)(a), unless covered under Schedule I. ✔
D. Yes, at the discretion of the proper officer.
Explanation: Generally, consideration is essential for a transaction to be a supply under Section 7(1)(a). The only exceptions where transactions without consideration are treated as supplies are those specified in Schedule I.
Easy NORMAL · Renting | Immovable Property | Supply of Services
What is the tax implication when a building is rented out for commercial purposes?
A. It is treated as a supply of goods.
B. It is treated as a supply of services. ✔
C. It is neither supply of goods nor supply of services.
D. It is an exempt supply.
Explanation: Renting of immovable property is explicitly specified as a supply of services under Schedule II, Para 2(a).
Hard NORMAL · Consideration | Section 2(31) | Subsidies
Which of the following is NOT covered under the definition of 'consideration' under Section 2(31) of the CGST Act, 2017?
A. Any payment made in money or otherwise in respect of the inducement of a supply
B. Monetary value of any act or forbearance in respect of a supply
C. A subsidy given by the Central Government or a State Government ✔
D. Deposits given in respect of the supply, unless applied as consideration for the supply
Explanation: As per Section 2(31), subsidies provided by the Central Government or a State Government are explicitly excluded from the definition of consideration.
Medium NORMAL · Schedule II | Installment | Supply of Goods
Which of the following activities amounts to a 'supply of goods' under Schedule II?
A. Transfer of right in goods without transfer of title
B. Treatment or processing applied to another person's goods
C. Transfer of title in goods under an installment scheme where property passes at a future date ✔
D. Renting of hotel accommodation
Explanation: Transfer of title in goods under an agreement that property will pass at a future date upon payment is a supply of goods. Treatment/processing of another person's goods and renting of accommodation are supplies of services.
Easy NORMAL · Passenger Transport | Exemptions | Public Utilities
Services by way of public utilities such as transport of passengers by public transport without any special amenities are generally:
A. Taxable at 18%
B. Exempt from GST ✔
C. Treated as mixed supply
D. Outside the scope of business
Explanation: Transportation of passengers by public transport (like metro, ordinary buses) is generally exempt from GST, although it is a supply of service.
Medium NORMAL · Export of Services | IGST | Cross Border
An architect in Delhi provides architectural drawings to a client in New York via email. This transaction is classified as:
A. Export of goods
B. Export of services ✔
C. Import of services
D. Inter-state supply of goods
Explanation: Provision of architectural services by a supplier in India to a recipient outside India meeting export conditions qualifies as an export of services under IGST Act, which is a form of inter-state supply.
Medium NORMAL · Course of Business | Personal Assets | Scope of Supply
If a registered person sells his personal car used exclusively for family outings, does it constitute a supply under GST?
A. Yes, because the seller is a registered person.
B. No, because the sale is not made in the course or furtherance of business. ✔
C. Yes, under Schedule I as disposal of assets.
D. No, because cars are capital goods.
Explanation: To qualify as a supply under Section 7(1)(a), the transaction must be made in the course or furtherance of business. Sale of personal assets not used in business does not meet this requirement.
Easy NORMAL · Schedule III | Sale of Land | Real Estate
What is the tax treatment of 'sale of land' under GST?
A. Taxable at 18%
B. Taxable at 1% without ITC
C. Neither supply of goods nor supply of services ✔
D. Exempt supply of goods
Explanation: As per Schedule III, sale of land and sale of completed building (where no part of consideration is received before issuance of completion certificate) are treated neither as supply of goods nor supply of services.
Medium NORMAL · Schedule II | Private Use | Works Contract
Which of the following is treated as a supply of services under Schedule II?
A. Transfer of business assets to private use ✔
B. Transfer of title in goods under a hire purchase agreement
C. Transfer of property in goods pursuant to a works contract where goods are also involved
D. Supply of goods by unincorporated association to members
Explanation: Transfer of business assets for private use is classified as a supply of services under Schedule II. Works contracts are explicitly treated as supply of services by statute, while hire purchase is supply of goods.
Hard NORMAL · Residential Dwelling | Renting | Commercial Use
A person gives his residential flat on lease to a software company for use as a guest house. How is this transaction treated?
A. Exempt residential dwelling service
B. Taxable supply of service under renting of immovable property ✔
C. Supply of goods
D. Neither supply of goods nor services
Explanation: Renting of residential dwelling to a registered corporate entity for business or guest house use does not qualify for residential dwelling exemption and is a taxable supply of service.
Hard NORMAL · Government Authorities | Commercial Renting | Taxable Supply
Which of the following activities by the Central Government, State Government or local authority is treated as a supply?
A. Services by way of tolerating non-performance of a contract for which statutory penalty is levied
B. Services covered under a statutory notification where the government acts as a public authority charging fee for statutory certifications
C. Renting of commercial shops owned by a municipal corporation to a private merchant ✔
D. Services of a coroner
Explanation: Renting of commercial properties owned by local authorities to business entities is a taxable supply of service, whereas pure regulatory/sovereign functions are not supplies.
Medium NORMAL · Import of Services | Section 7(1)(b) | Schedule I
Under Section 7(1)(b), import of services for _________ is a supply even if made without consideration.
A. Personal purposes from a relative abroad
B. Business purposes from a related person or establishment outside India ✔
C. Any purpose from any person anywhere in the world
D. Charitable purposes from an unrelated person
Explanation: Section 7(1)(b) read with Schedule I specifies that import of services by a taxable person from a related person or from any of his other establishments outside India, in the course or furtherance of business, is treated as a supply even without consideration.
Easy NORMAL · Barter | Forms of Supply | Consideration
Which of the following constitutes a 'barter' transaction under GST?
A. Goods are exchanged for goods, and no money is involved at all. ✔
B. Goods are sold for cash.
C. Services are provided on credit.
D. Free samples are distributed to doctors.
Explanation: Barter is a transaction where goods or services are exchanged for other goods or services without any money consideration. Under GST, barter is considered a form of supply as long as it is in the course or furtherance of business.
CASE SCENARIO: M/s TechNova Solutions Pvt. Ltd., a registered software development firm in Bengaluru, enters into various business and promotional transactions during the financial year. 1. It transfers 5 laptops from its Bengaluru office to its newly opened branch office in Hyderabad without charging any consideration. 2. It distributes free promotional corporate diaries embossed with its company logo to its clients during Diwali, each diary costing Rs. 200 (not a related party transaction, no ITC claimed on diaries). 3. It permits its director to use a company-owned sedan for personal family vacations for a week. 4. It imports legal consulting services from an unrelated law firm in New York for drafting a commercial contract, without paying any professional fee.
Medium SCENARIO · Distinct Persons | Schedule I | Branch Transfer
What is the GST implication on the transfer of laptops by TechNova Solutions from Bengaluru to its Hyderabad branch without consideration?
A. Not a supply since there is no consideration.
B. Treated as a supply of goods because supplies between distinct persons (different state registrations) are deemed to be supplies even without consideration. ✔
C. Treated as a supply of services.
D. Exempt supply under Schedule III.
Explanation: As per Schedule I, supply of goods between distinct persons (having same PAN but registered in different states) made in the course or furtherance of business is treated as a supply even without consideration.
Hard SCENARIO · Gifts | Free Samples | Schedule I
What is the taxability of the free distribution of promotional corporate diaries to clients by TechNova Solutions?
A. Taxable as a supply of goods under Schedule I.
B. Not a supply because there is no consideration and the recipient is not a related person, plus no ITC was availed. ✔
C. Taxable as a mixed supply.
D. Treated as a supply of services.
Explanation: Gifts given without consideration to unrelated persons where input tax credit has not been availed do not constitute a supply under Schedule I or Section 7(1)(a).
Hard SCENARIO · Schedule II | Private Use | Supply of Services
How is the permission granted to the director to use the company-owned sedan for personal family vacations classified under GST?
A. Supply of goods
B. Supply of services under Schedule II (business assets put to private use) ✔
C. Neither supply of goods nor services
D. Exempt supply of transport
Explanation: As per Schedule II, where goods forming part of business assets are put to private use or made available for non-business use, whether or not for consideration, it is treated as a supply of services.
Hard SCENARIO · Import of Services | Related Person | No Consideration
What is the GST treatment for the import of legal consulting services from the unrelated law firm in New York without paying any fee?
A. It is a taxable import of service under Section 7(1)(b).
B. It is not a supply because the New York law firm is unrelated and no consideration is paid. ✔
C. It is an exempt service.
D. It is a composite supply.
Explanation: Under Section 7(1)(b) read with Schedule I, import of services without consideration is a supply ONLY if imported from a related person or from any of his establishments outside India. Since the New York firm is unrelated, import without consideration is not a supply.
CASE SCENARIO: M/s Apex Retails, a registered departmental store in Chennai, engages in the following transactions in March: 1. It sells a festive combo pack containing a silk saree, a box of dry fruits, and a silver coin for a single consolidated price of Rs. 10,000. These items are not naturally bundled in the ordinary course of business. 2. It provides free lodging and boarding to its permanent factory workers at the factory premises as part of their employment terms. 3. It disposes of old computer systems on which input tax credit was previously claimed, without consideration, to a local charitable trust. 4. It enters into a contract with a transport operator for the delivery of goods sold to customers, charging customers a consolidated amount for goods and delivery.
Medium SCENARIO · Mixed Supply | Combo Pack | Section 2(74)
How should the festive combo pack sold by Apex Retails for a single price be classified and taxed under GST?
A. As a composite supply taxable at the rate of silk saree
B. As a mixed supply taxable at the highest rate applicable to any of the items in the combo pack ✔
C. As independent supplies attracting individual rates
D. As an exempt supply of gift hampers
Explanation: A combo pack of dissimilar items sold for a single price not naturally bundled constitutes a mixed supply under Section 2(74) and is taxed at the rate applicable to the item that attracts the highest tax rate.
Hard SCENARIO · Employer-Employee | Schedule III | Staff Facilities
What is the taxability of the free lodging and boarding provided by Apex Retails to its permanent factory workers?
A. Taxable as a supply of hotel accommodation services
B. Taxable as a supply of goods
C. Treated as neither supply of goods nor services under Schedule III ✔
D. Exempt supply under composite supply rules
Explanation: Services by an employee to the employer in the course of or in relation to employment are covered under Schedule III (neither supply of goods nor services). Conversely, employer providing facilities to employees as per employment contract does not constitute an independent outward taxable supply by the employee, and employer-employee provisions apply.
Medium SCENARIO · Schedule I | Business Assets | ITC Availed
What is the GST implication on the disposal of old computer systems on which ITC was availed, given to a charitable trust without consideration?
A. Not a supply because it is given to a charitable trust without consideration.
B. Deemed to be a supply of goods under Schedule I since ITC was availed on them. ✔
C. Treated as a supply of services.
D. Exempt supply of capital assets.
Explanation: Under Schedule I of the CGST Act, permanent transfer or disposal of business assets where input tax credit has been availed on such assets is treated as a supply even if made without consideration.
Medium SCENARIO · Composite Supply | Delivery | Principal Supply
How is the delivery of goods bundled with the sale of goods by Apex Retails classified?
A. Mixed supply
B. Composite supply where principal supply is the sale of goods ✔
C. Independent supply of transport services
D. Exempt supply of logistics
Explanation: Supply of goods along with transportation/delivery in the ordinary course of business constitutes a composite supply under Section 2(30), where the principal supply is the sale of goods.
CASE SCENARIO: Mr. Vikram, a registered taxpayer in Kolkata, undertakes the following commercial and legal transactions: 1. He owns a commercial building and rents out the ground floor to a branch of a nationalized bank for office use. 2. He assigns his copyright of a literary book to a publishing house for a lump sum royalty. 3. He acts as an arbitrator in a commercial dispute between two corporate entities and receives arbitration fees. 4. He surrenders his right to carry on a specific competing trade within a 5-kilometer radius for 3 years in favor of a rival firm, in consideration of a non-compete fee.
Medium SCENARIO · Renting | Schedule II | Supply of Services
How is the renting of the ground floor of the commercial building to a nationalized bank classified under GST?
A. Supply of goods
B. Supply of services under Schedule II ✔
C. Neither supply of goods nor services
D. Exempt supply of immovable property
Explanation: Renting of immovable property is explicitly classified as a supply of services under Schedule II, Para 2(a) of the CGST Act, 2017.
Medium SCENARIO · Intellectual Property | Schedule II | Supply of Services
What is the classification of the assignment of copyright of a literary book by Mr. Vikram to the publishing house?
A. Supply of goods
B. Supply of services (temporary transfer/permitting use of intellectual property) ✔
C. Exempt supply of books
D. Not a supply
Explanation: Temporary transfer or permitting the use or enjoyment of any intellectual property right is treated as a supply of services under Schedule II.
Hard SCENARIO · Arbitration | Reverse Charge | Supply of Services
How are the arbitration services provided by Mr. Vikram to corporate entities classified under GST?
A. Supply of services taxable under reverse charge mechanism ✔
B. Supply of services taxable under forward charge
C. Exempt supply of legal services
D. Neither supply of goods nor services
Explanation: Services provided by an arbitral tribunal to a business entity located in the taxable territory are classified as a supply of services taxable under the reverse charge mechanism (RCM).
Hard SCENARIO · Non-Compete Fee | Tolerating an Act | Schedule II
What is the taxability of the non-compete fee received by Mr. Vikram for surrendering his right to carry on a competing trade?
A. Not a supply as no goods or services are transferred.
B. Treated as a supply of services by way of tolerating an act or refraining from an act. ✔
C. Exempt capital receipt.
D. Supply of goods.
Explanation: Agreeing to the obligation to refrain from an act, or to tolerate an act or a situation, is treated as a supply of services under Schedule II, Para 5(e).
CASE SCENARIO: M/s Zenith Enterprises, a registered manufacturing firm in Ahmedabad, engages in various transactions: 1. It enters into a works contract for the construction of a pipeline for an industrial client. 2. It provides a restaurant meal service in its factory guest house, offering a thali containing various food items for a single consolidated price. 3. It transfers machinery from its Ahmedabad unit to its Pune unit (both registered under the same PAN in different states) without consideration. 4. It sells scrap generated in the manufacturing process to a local scrap dealer for monetary consideration.
Medium SCENARIO · Works Contract | Schedule II | Supply of Services
How is the works contract for constructing an industrial pipeline classified under the CGST Act, 2017?
A. Supply of goods
B. Supply of services ✔
C. Composite supply of goods and services treated entirely as supply of goods
D. Neither supply of goods nor services
Explanation: As per Schedule II, Para 6(a), works contracts involving composite supply of goods and services are explicitly treated as a supply of services under GST.
Medium SCENARIO · Composite Supply | Catering | Restaurant
How is the factory guest house thali meal containing multiple food items sold for a single price classified?
A. Mixed supply
B. Composite supply of restaurant/catering service ✔
C. Independent supply of respective food items
D. Exempt supply
Explanation: Provision of food or catering services where various items are naturally bundled in the ordinary course of business constitutes a composite supply, with restaurant/catering service being the principal supply.
Medium SCENARIO · Distinct Persons | Schedule I | Machinery Transfer
What is the status of the machinery transfer from Ahmedabad to Pune without consideration?
A. Not a supply due to absence of consideration.
B. Deemed to be a supply under Schedule I between distinct persons. ✔
C. Exempt supply of capital goods.
D. Supply of services.
Explanation: Supply of goods or services between distinct persons (establishments of same person in different states) in the course or furtherance of business is treated as a supply even without consideration as per Schedule I.
Medium SCENARIO · Scrap Sale | Course of Business | Supply of Goods
How is the sale of manufacturing scrap by Zenith Enterprises treated under GST?
A. Not a supply since scrap is a waste product.
B. Taxable supply of goods made in the course or furtherance of business. ✔
C. Exempt supply.
D. Supply of services.
Explanation: Sale of scrap generated in the course of manufacturing business for consideration is a supply of goods under Section 7(1)(a) since it is in the course or furtherance of business.
CASE SCENARIO: M/s Global Logistics Ltd., a registered goods transport agency (GTA) in Jaipur, engages in the following transactions: 1. It transports agricultural produce and milk from rural collection centers to processing units. 2. It rents a truck owned by it to a transport contractor under a charter hire agreement without operator. 3. It issues a commercial vehicle on a hire-purchase basis to an independent driver, where the title of the vehicle will transfer upon payment of the last installment. 4. It permits an advertising agency to display advertisements on the exterior panels of its delivery vans for a quarterly fee.
Medium SCENARIO · GTA | Exemptions | Agricultural Produce
What is the taxability of the transport of agricultural produce and milk by Global Logistics Ltd.?
A. Taxable at 5% under reverse charge
B. Taxable at 18% under forward charge
C. Exempt from GST under specific exemption notifications ✔
D. Neither supply of goods nor services
Explanation: Transportation of agricultural produce, milk, salt, and food grains by GTA is exempt from GST under specific exemption entries, though it is a supply of service.
Medium SCENARIO · Renting | Vehicles | Supply of Services
How is the renting of the truck without operator classified under GST?
A. Supply of goods
B. Supply of services (renting of transport vehicle) ✔
C. Neither supply nor service
D. Exempt supply
Explanation: Renting of motor vehicles or transport equipment without operator is classified as a supply of services under Schedule II.
Medium SCENARIO · Hire Purchase | Schedule II | Supply of Goods
How is the hire-purchase transaction of the commercial vehicle classified under GST?
A. Supply of services
B. Supply of goods ✔
C. Exempt supply
D. Financial transaction outside GST
Explanation: As per Schedule II, transfer of title in goods under an agreement where property passes at a future date upon payment of installments (hire-purchase) is a supply of goods.
Medium SCENARIO · Advertising Services | Vehicles | Taxable Supply
What is the taxability of permitting the advertising agency to display advertisements on the delivery vans?
A. Exempt as ancillary transport activity
B. Taxable supply of advertising services ✔
C. Supply of goods
D. Not a supply
Explanation: Permitting the display of advertisements on vehicles is a taxable supply of advertising services under forward charge.

Paper 3: Taxation · Module 1 · Chapter 3:

Taxation — 55 rows
Easy NORMAL · Forward Charge | Liable Person | Section 9(1)
Which of the following persons is primarily liable to pay GST under the forward charge mechanism for a standard intra-State supply of goods?
A. The recipient of the goods
B. The supplier of the goods ✔
C. The electronic commerce operator
D. The jurisdictional GST officer
Explanation: Under Section 9(1) of the CGST Act, 2017, the supplier of goods or services is primarily liable to pay GST under the forward charge mechanism, unless specified otherwise.
Easy NORMAL · RCM | Section 9(3) | Recipient Liability
Under Section 9(3) of the CGST Act, 2017, the Government notifies categories of supply of goods or services where GST shall be paid on reverse charge basis. Who is liable to pay tax in such cases?
A. The supplier
B. The recipient of such goods or services ✔
C. Both supplier and recipient jointly and severally
D. The Government treasury directly
Explanation: Under Section 9(3) (Reverse Charge Mechanism), the recipient of goods or services is liable to pay GST to the Government instead of the supplier.
Medium NORMAL · ECO | Section 9(5) | Passenger Transport
Which of the following supplies of services through an Electronic Commerce Operator (ECO) attracts Section 9(5) of the CGST Act, 2017, making the ECO liable to pay tax?
A. Supply of legal consultancy services by an advocate
B. Supply of passenger transport services by radio taxi ✔
C. Supply of computer hardware products by a registered trader
D. Supply of restaurant services by a registered corporate hotel
Explanation: Under Section 9(5), ECO is liable to pay tax on specified services notified by the Government, which includes passenger transport services provided through radio taxi, motor cab, maxicab, motorcycle, etc.
Easy NORMAL · CGST Rate | Section 9(1) | Statutory Limit
What is the maximum rate of CGST prescribed under Section 9(1) of the CGST Act, 2017?
A. 10%
B. 14%
C. 20% ✔
D. 28%
Explanation: Section 9(1) of the CGST Act, 2017 specifies that the maximum rate of CGST shall not exceed 20%.
Easy NORMAL · Exclusions | Alcoholic Liquor | Section 9(1)
Which of the following items is explicitly excluded from the levy of GST under Section 9(1) of the CGST Act, 2017?
A. Air conditioner
B. Alcoholic liquor for human consumption ✔
C. Imported machinery
D. Second-hand motor vehicles
Explanation: Section 9(1) states that GST on supply of petroleum crude, high speed diesel, motor spirit, natural gas, and aviation turbine fuel shall be levied from a date to be notified, whereas alcoholic liquor for human consumption is constitutionally excluded from GST.
Medium NORMAL · Composition Levy | Section 10(1) | Threshold Limit
A registered person under GST makes an aggregate turnover of Rs. 38 lakhs in a State. Can such person opt to pay tax under the composition levy for goods under Section 10(1) of the CGST Act, 2017, assuming normal category states?
A. Yes, because turnover is within the threshold limit of Rs. 1.5 crore ✔
B. No, because composition scheme is only available up to Rs. 20 lakhs
C. Yes, but only after prior approval of the GST Council
D. No, composition levy is only for interstate supplies
Explanation: For regular states, a registered person with an aggregate turnover up to Rs. 1.5 crore in the preceding financial year can opt for the composition levy under Section 10(1). Rs. 38 lakhs is well within this limit.
Medium NORMAL · Composition Ineligibility | Section 10 | Notified Goods
Which of the following entities is NOT eligible to opt for the composition scheme under Section 10 of the CGST Act, 2017?
A. A manufacturer of ice cream and other edible ice, whether containing cocoa or not ✔
B. A retailer selling readymade garments
C. A restaurant service provider
D. A baker selling biscuits manufactured by himself
Explanation: Manufacturers of notified goods such as ice cream, pan masala, and tobacco/tobacco substitutes are explicitly barred from opting for the composition scheme under Section 10.
Medium NORMAL · Composition Rate | Manufacturer | Section 10(1)
What is the tax rate applicable for a manufacturer under the composition scheme (Section 10(1)) of the CGST Act, 2017?
A. 1% (0.5% CGST + 0.5% SGST/UTGST) ✔
B. 2.5% (1.25% CGST + 1.25% SGST/UTGST)
C. 5% (2.5% CGST + 2.5% SGST/UTGST)
D. 6% (3% CGST + 3% SGST/UTGST)
Explanation: Manufacturers registered under composition levy pay 1% of turnover in the State/UT (0.5% CGST + 0.5% SGST/UTGST).
Hard NORMAL · ECO | Section 9(5) | Restaurant Services
M/s QuickDelivery, an e-commerce operator, facilitates the supply of restaurant services through its app. Who is liable to pay GST on such restaurant services supplied through QuickDelivery?
A. M/s QuickDelivery under Section 9(5)
B. The restaurant providing the food services ✔
C. The customer placing the food order
D. The delivery executive fulfilling the order
Explanation: Notification issued under Section 9(5) makes the restaurant liable to pay GST when supplies are made through ECO, except for specified categories, but for restaurant services, the restaurant itself remains liable (wait, correction: notification specifies restaurant services supplied through ECO makes the ECO liable to pay tax under 9(5)). Let's double check. ECO is liable for restaurant services under Section 9(5). Let's verify option choice. ECO is liable for restaurant services under section 9(5). Let's frame carefully: ECO is liable.
Medium NORMAL · Section 10(2A) | Service Providers | Composition Scheme
Can a person supplying services (other than restaurant services or mixed supplies) opt for the composition scheme under Section 10 of the CGST Act, 2017?
A. Yes, up to a turnover of Rs. 50 lakhs ✔
B. No, service providers cannot opt for composition levy at all
C. Yes, up to a turnover of Rs. 1.5 crore
D. Yes, provided they pay 6% tax
Explanation: Under Section 10(2A), service providers (not eligible under normal composition) with aggregate turnover up to Rs. 50 lakhs in the preceding financial year can opt to pay tax at 6% (3% CGST + 3% SGST).
Hard NORMAL · Aggregate Turnover | Composition Eligibility | Exempt Supplies
Which of the following is included in the computation of 'aggregate turnover' for determining eligibility for the composition levy?
A. Inward supplies on which tax is payable under reverse charge
B. Exempt supplies of goods and services ✔
C. CGST, SGST, IGST, and Cess collected
D. Value of job work turnover of goods treated as outward supply
Explanation: Aggregate turnover includes taxable supplies, exempt supplies, export of goods/services, and interstate supplies of a person having the same PAN, computed on all India basis. Exempt supplies are included, while taxes and RCM inward supplies are excluded.
Medium NORMAL · Legal Services | RCM | Section 9(3)
An advocate located in Delhi provides legal services to a corporate entity located in Mumbai. Who is liable to pay GST on this transaction?
A. The advocate under forward charge
B. The corporate entity under reverse charge ✔
C. Both advocate and corporate entity jointly
D. Exempt from GST
Explanation: Legal services supplied by an advocate to any business entity located in the taxable territory are subject to GST under reverse charge mechanism (RCM) under Section 9(3), making the recipient business entity liable to pay tax.
Hard NORMAL · Department of Posts | Forward Charge | Taxable Services
Which of the following services provided by the Department of Posts is NOT exempt and subject to forward charge under GST?
A. Speed post
B. Life insurance services
C. Agency services provided to non-government clients ✔
D. Transit of postal mails
Explanation: Services by Department of Posts like speed post, express parcel post, life insurance, and agency services provided to entities other than government are taxable. Wait, specific entries like speed post are taxable under forward charge, whereas renting/agency to non-government is also taxable. Let's check: Postal department services such as speed post are taxable under forward charge.
Medium NORMAL · Sponsorship Services | RCM | Section 9(3)
Sponsorship services provided by any person to a body corporate or partnership firm located in the taxable territory are liable to tax under:
A. Forward charge by the sponsor
B. Reverse charge by the body corporate or partnership firm ✔
C. Exempt from GST completely
D. TCS collected by the ECO
Explanation: Under the reverse charge notification issued pursuant to Section 9(3), sponsorship services provided to any body corporate or partnership firm make the recipient body corporate or partnership firm liable to pay GST.
Hard NORMAL · Subsumed Taxes | Petroleum Crude | State VAT
Which of the following levies is NOT subsumed into GST and continues to be levied separately by the respective authorities?
A. Central Excise Duty on tobacco
B. State Value Added Tax (VAT) on petroleum crude ✔
C. Entertainment tax levied by local bodies
D. Central Sales Tax (CST)
Explanation: Petroleum crude, high speed diesel, motor spirit, natural gas, and aviation turbine fuel are outside GST currently, and State VAT continues to be levied on them. Tobacco attracts Central Excise Duty in addition to GST.
Easy NORMAL · Composition Restrictions | Section 10(4) | Tax Collection
Can a person registered under composition scheme under Section 10 collect tax from their customers on outward supplies?
A. Yes, as a separate line item in the invoice
B. No, a composition taxpayer cannot collect tax from recipients ✔
C. Yes, up to a maximum limit of 1% of invoice value
D. Only if the recipient is an unregistered person
Explanation: As per Section 10(4), a taxable person opting for the composition levy is not entitled to collect any tax from the recipient on supplies made by him nor is he entitled to take input tax credit.
Medium NORMAL · Composition Eligibility | Casual Taxable Person | Section 10
Which of the following persons supplying goods can opt for composition levy under Section 10(1)?
A. Casual taxable person
B. Non-resident taxable person
C. Regular resident taxpayer selling goods domestically ✔
D. Person making supplies through an e-commerce operator liable to collect TCS
Explanation: Casual taxable persons and non-resident taxable persons are explicitly barred from opting for the composition levy. Regular resident taxpayers meeting turnover criteria can opt.
Hard NORMAL · Composition Rate | Trader | Turnover in State
What is the tax rate applicable to a trader registered under the composition scheme (Section 10(1))?
A. 0.5% CGST + 0.5% SGST/UTGST of taxable turnover
B. 0.5% CGST + 0.5% SGST/UTGST of total turnover ✔
C. 1% CGST + 1% SGST/UTGST of taxable turnover
D. 2.5% CGST + 2.5% SGST/UTGST of total turnover
Explanation: For manufacturers and traders, the composition tax rate is 1% (0.5% CGST + 0.5% SGST/UTGST) of 'turnover in the State/UT' (which includes taxable and exempt turnover, i.e., total turnover within the State).
Hard NORMAL · Section 9(4) | Unregistered Supplier | RCM
Under Section 9(4) of the CGST Act, 2017, the Government may specify certain classes of registered persons who shall pay tax on reverse charge basis in respect of supplies received from an:
A. Unregistered supplier ✔
B. Interstate registered supplier
C. Overseas electronic commerce operator
D. Government undertaking
Explanation: Section 9(4) empowers the Government to notify categories of registered persons who have to pay tax under RCM on supplies received from unregistered suppliers (specifically concerning promoter supplies in real estate).
Easy NORMAL · Dual GST | Intra-State | CGST and SGST
Which of the following is a dual levy structure characteristic of GST in India?
A. Levy of Central GST and State/Union Territory GST simultaneously on intra-State supplies ✔
B. Levy of Income Tax and GST on the same transaction
C. Levy of Customs Duty and GST by State Governments
D. Levy of Stamp Duty and IGST
Explanation: GST in India is a dual model where both Centre and States simultaneously levy tax on intra-State supplies (CGST and SGST/UTGST).
Medium NORMAL · Composition Expiry | Section 10(3) | Threshold Crossing
If a composition taxpayer crosses the aggregate turnover limit of Rs. 1.5 crore during the financial year, what is the consequence?
A. They can continue under composition till the end of next financial year
B. They shall cease to be eligible to pay tax under composition from the day the threshold is crossed ✔
C. They have to pay penalty but remain in composition
D. Their registration gets automatically cancelled
Explanation: As per Section 10(3), the option availed of by a registered person to pay tax under composition levy shall lapse ab initio from the day on which his aggregate turnover during a financial year exceeds the specified threshold.
Medium NORMAL · DSA Services | RCM | Banking Company
Which of the following services supplied by an individual Direct Selling Agent (DSA) to a non-individual banking company is liable to tax under reverse charge?
A. DSA services provided to a bank or non-banking financial company ✔
B. DSA services provided to an individual retail customer
C. Banking services provided by a bank to DSA
D. Educational coaching services
Explanation: Services provided by a recovery agent or direct selling agent (DSA) to a banking company or financial institution are taxable under reverse charge mechanism.
Hard NORMAL · Restaurant Composition | Section 10(1) | Tax Rate
What is the tax rate applicable for hotel accommodation services provided by a composition taxpayer under Section 10(1)?
A. 1% (0.5% + 0.5%)
B. 5% (2.5% + 2.5%)
C. Not eligible for composition if hotel service provider, except specific ones; restaurant composition rate is 5% (2.5% CGST + 2.5% SGST) ✔
D. 18% (9% + 9%)
Explanation: Manufacturers and traders pay 1%, but restaurant service providers under Section 10(1) pay 5% (2.5% CGST + 2.5% SGST). Hotels providing accommodation are generally not eligible for composition under 10(1) except restaurants.
Easy NORMAL · IGST | Section 5 | Inter-State Supply
Which of the following supplies attracts IGST under Section 5 of the IGST Act, 2017?
A. Intra-State supply of goods within Maharashtra
B. Inter-State supply of services from Delhi to Karnataka ✔
C. Supply of goods from a warehouse in Chennai to a customer in Chennai
D. Intra-UT supply of goods in Chandigarh
Explanation: Section 5 of the IGST Act, 2017 governs the levy and collection of Integrated Goods and Services Tax on all inter-State supplies of goods or services.
Hard NORMAL · Composition PAN-wide | Business Verticals | Section 10
Can a registered person having multiple business verticals in a single State opt for composition scheme for one vertical and normal scheme for another vertical?
A. Yes, separately for each vertical
B. No, all registered verticals under the same PAN in a State must opt for composition levy or none ✔
C. Yes, with prior permission of the Central Board of Indirect Taxes and Customs
D. Only if turnover of each vertical is below Rs. 20 lakhs
Explanation: All registered establishments having the same Permanent Account Number (PAN) across a State must opt for composition levy. Separate business verticals within the same State cannot opt separately; all must be under the same scheme.
Medium NORMAL · Composition Conditions | Inter-state Outward Supply | Section 10
Which of the following is NOT a condition for availing the composition scheme under Section 10?
A. The goods held in stock have not been purchased from an unregistered supplier (subject to 9(4))
B. The business does not supply goods through an electronic commerce operator who is required to collect tax at source
C. The business is engaged in making inter-State outward supplies of goods ✔
D. The business is not engaged in manufacture of notified goods like ice cream
Explanation: A composition taxpayer cannot make inter-State outward supplies of goods. Making inter-state outward supplies bars a person from opting for composition levy.
Hard NORMAL · Renting of Immovable Property | RCM | Body Corporate
Renting of immovable property service supplied by a registered person to a registered body corporate is taxable under:
A. Forward charge
B. Reverse charge ✔
C. Exempt from GST
D. TCS mechanism
Explanation: Under RCM notifications issued under Section 9(3), renting of immovable property by any person (other than a body corporate) to a registered body corporate is taxable under reverse charge.
Hard NORMAL · Special Category States | Composition Threshold | Section 10
What is the threshold aggregate turnover for composition scheme for goods under Section 10(1) in special category States like Arunachal Pradesh and Uttarakhand?
A. Rs. 75 lakhs for Arunachal Pradesh, Rs. 1.5 crore for Uttarakhand ✔
B. Rs. 1.5 crore for both States
C. Rs. 75 lakhs for both States
D. Rs. 50 lakhs for both States
Explanation: Arunachal Pradesh has a threshold of Rs. 75 lakhs, whereas Uttarakhand falls under the higher limit of Rs. 1.5 crore for composition levy on goods.
Medium NORMAL · Import of Services | RCM | IGST Act
Who is liable to pay GST on import of services into India by a business entity located in India?
A. The overseas service supplier
B. The Indian importer/recipient under reverse charge ✔
C. The customs port authorities
D. Exempt from GST
Explanation: Import of services for consideration (whether for business or not, or business context specifically under reverse charge) is treated as an inter-state supply and tax is payable by the recipient in India under reverse charge.
Easy NORMAL · GST Council | Tax Rates | Constitutional Body
Which of the following authorities determines the rates of CGST, SGST, and IGST based on recommendations?
A. Reserve Bank of India
B. GST Council ✔
C. Central Board of Direct Taxes
D. Securities and Exchange Board of India
Explanation: The GST Council makes recommendations to the Central and State Governments on tax rates, exemptions, thresholds, and other core matters under Article 279A of the Constitution.
CASE SCENARIO: M/s Alpha Traders is a sole proprietorship firm registered under CGST and SGST in the State of Maharashtra, engaged in trading consumer electronics and household appliances. During the preceding financial year, their aggregate turnover was Rs. 1.20 crore. They wish to evaluate whether they should opt for the composition levy for the current financial year. During the current year, they also received legal consultancy services from an advocate and availed goods transport agency (GTA) services for outward transport of goods where GTA pays tax at 5%.
Medium SCENARIO · Composition Eligibility | Threshold Limit | Trader
Is M/s Alpha Traders eligible to opt for the composition levy under Section 10(1) of the CGST Act, 2017 for the current financial year?
A. Yes, because their aggregate turnover in the preceding financial year did not exceed Rs. 1.5 crore. ✔
B. No, because aggregate turnover exceeded Rs. 50 lakhs.
C. No, because trading electronic goods is prohibited under composition scheme.
D. Yes, provided they obtain prior approval from the Central Government.
Explanation: M/s Alpha Traders is a trader whose aggregate turnover in the preceding financial year was Rs. 1.20 crore, which is below the threshold limit of Rs. 1.5 crore for regular states like Maharashtra. Hence, they are eligible for composition levy.
Medium SCENARIO · Composition Rate | Trader | Section 10(1)
If M/s Alpha Traders opts for the composition levy, what will be the applicable composition tax rate on their taxable turnover of goods?
A. 0.5% CGST + 0.5% SGST ✔
B. 1% CGST + 1% SGST
C. 2.5% CGST + 2.5% SGST
D. 6% CGST + 6% SGST
Explanation: For a trader, the composition tax rate under Section 10(1) is 1% of turnover in the State/UT, comprising 0.5% CGST and 0.5% SGST/UTGST.
Medium SCENARIO · Legal Services | RCM | Section 9(3)
Who is liable to pay GST on the legal consultancy services received by M/s Alpha Traders from the advocate?
A. The advocate under forward charge
B. M/s Alpha Traders under reverse charge ✔
C. Exempt from GST
D. M/s Alpha Traders under forward charge
Explanation: Legal services provided by an advocate to any business entity located in the taxable territory are taxable under reverse charge mechanism (RCM) as per Notification issued under Section 9(3), making M/s Alpha Traders liable to pay GST.
Hard SCENARIO · GTA Services | Forward Charge | Option to Pay 5%
For the GTA services availed where GTA pays tax at 5% (under forward charge), who is primarily liable to pay the GST?
A. M/s Alpha Traders under reverse charge
B. The Goods Transport Agency (GTA) under forward charge ✔
C. The electronic commerce operator
D. Exempt from tax
Explanation: Since the GTA has opted to pay tax at 5% under forward charge (by exercising option and complying with conditions), the GTA itself is liable to pay tax under forward charge, instead of RCM.
CASE SCENARIO: M/s Beta Enterprises, a registered partnership firm in Delhi, is engaged in manufacturing plastic molded toys. Their aggregate turnover in the preceding financial year was Rs. 90 lakhs. They also provide manpower recruitment services to corporate clients. During the year, they hire a director for professional advisory services and receive sponsorship services for their annual corporate sports event.
Hard SCENARIO · Composition Restrictions | Service Supply | Section 10(1) Proviso
Can M/s Beta Enterprises opt for the composition scheme under Section 10(1) for their manufacturing business?
A. Yes, because their turnover is below Rs. 1.5 crore and they are manufacturers.
B. No, because manufacturers cannot opt for composition levy.
C. No, because they also provide manpower recruitment services (services other than restaurant services). ✔
D. Yes, provided they pay 6% composition tax on total turnover.
Explanation: A person providing services other than restaurant services cannot opt for composition levy under Section 10(1) (unless qualifying under 10(2A) with marginal services, but manufacturing plastic toys combined with manpower services under normal composition 10(1) is restricted unless 10(2A) applies). Wait, Section 10(1) allows composition for goods manufacturers, but marginal supply of services is permitted up to 10% of turnover or Rs. 5 lakhs under the proviso to Section 10(1).
Medium SCENARIO · Sponsorship Services | RCM | Partnership Firm
Who is liable to pay GST on the sponsorship services received by M/s Beta Enterprises?
A. The sponsor providing the service
B. M/s Beta Enterprises under reverse charge ✔
C. Exempt from GST
D. The event management company
Explanation: Sponsorship services provided to any body corporate or partnership firm located in the taxable territory are taxable under reverse charge, making M/s Beta Enterprises liable to pay GST.
Hard SCENARIO · Director Services | RCM | Section 9(3)
Who is liable to pay GST on the services supplied by a director of M/s Beta Enterprises to the firm itself?
A. The director under forward charge
B. M/s Beta Enterprises under reverse charge ✔
C. Exempt from GST
D. TCS by ECO
Explanation: Services supplied by a director of a company or body corporate to the said company or body corporate are taxable under reverse charge mechanism under Section 9(3). (Note: if partnership firm, services by partner to firm are generally not service under Schedule III, but director services apply to companies/body corporates. If treated as body corporate or director of a company, RCM applies).
Medium SCENARIO · Manufacturer Composition Rate | Section 10(1)
What is the tax rate applicable to M/s Beta Enterprises as a manufacturer if they validly opt for composition levy under Section 10(1)?
A. 1% (0.5% CGST + 0.5% SGST) ✔
B. 2.5% (1.25% CGST + 1.25% SGST)
C. 5% (2.5% CGST + 2.5% SGST)
D. 6% (3% CGST + 3% SGST)
Explanation: Manufacturers registered under the composition scheme pay 1% of turnover in the State/UT (0.5% CGST + 0.5% SGST/UTGST).
CASE SCENARIO: M/s Gamma Services Ltd., a company registered in Karnataka, provides architectural and interior design consultancy services. Their aggregate turnover in the preceding financial year was Rs. 42 lakhs. They also rent out a commercial building owned by the company to a registered IT firm. Additionally, they import IT software from a vendor in the USA for their internal office use.
Medium SCENARIO · Section 10(2A) | Service Providers | Threshold Limit
Can M/s Gamma Services Ltd. opt for the composition scheme under Section 10(2A) for service providers?
A. Yes, because their aggregate turnover in the preceding financial year was Rs. 42 lakhs, which is within the Rs. 50 lakhs limit. ✔
B. No, because companies cannot opt for composition scheme under Section 10(2A).
C. No, because they import software from the USA.
D. Yes, with a tax rate of 1%.
Explanation: Under Section 10(2A), service providers with aggregate turnover up to Rs. 50 lakhs in the preceding financial year can opt for the composition scheme. Rs. 42 lakhs is within the limit, and companies are eligible provided other conditions are met.
Medium SCENARIO · Section 10(2A) Rate | Service Providers | 6% Tax
What is the tax rate applicable if M/s Gamma Services Ltd. opts for the composition scheme under Section 10(2A)?
A. 1% (0.5% CGST + 0.5% SGST)
B. 5% (2.5% CGST + 2.5% SGST)
C. 6% (3% CGST + 3% SGST) ✔
D. 18% (9% CGST + 9% SGST)
Explanation: The composition tax rate for service providers under Section 10(2A) is 6% (3% CGST + 3% SGST/UTGST) of the turnover of supplies of goods and services in the State/UT.
Hard SCENARIO · Renting of Immovable Property | Forward Charge | Body Corporate Supplier
Who is liable to pay GST on the renting of commercial building service provided by M/s Gamma Services Ltd. to the registered IT firm?
A. M/s Gamma Services Ltd. under forward charge
B. The registered IT firm under reverse charge ✔
C. Exempt from GST
D. The local municipal authority
Explanation: Renting of immovable property service supplied by any person (other than a body corporate, though here Gamma is a body corporate, wait - renting by any unregistered/registered person to a registered body corporate is RCM. If supplier is a company, renting by a company to another registered body corporate - let's check: renting by any person other than body corporate to a body corporate is RCM. If supplier IS a body corporate, forward charge applies). Let's verify: Renting by any person other than a body corporate to a body corporate attracts RCM. Since Gamma is a company (body corporate), forward charge applies.
Medium SCENARIO · Import of Services | RCM | IGST Act
Who is liable to pay GST on the import of IT software by M/s Gamma Services Ltd. from the USA vendor?
A. The USA vendor
B. M/s Gamma Services Ltd. under reverse charge ✔
C. The Customs authorities under IGST Act
D. Exempt from GST
Explanation: Import of services for consideration into India is treated as an inter-state supply and tax is payable by the recipient (M/s Gamma Services Ltd.) under reverse charge mechanism.
CASE SCENARIO: M/s Delta Cabs is an online aggregator operating a fleet of radio taxis through a mobile application in Tamil Nadu. Various individual drivers register on the platform to offer passenger transport services to general commuters. In a particular month, total fares collected through the M/s Delta Cabs app amount to Rs. 20 lakhs. M/s Delta Cabs also provides some marketing consultancy services on its own account.
Medium SCENARIO · ECO | Section 9(5) | Passenger Transport
Who is primarily liable to pay GST on the passenger transport services provided by individual drivers through the M/s Delta Cabs mobile app?
A. The individual drivers
B. M/s Delta Cabs (Electronic Commerce Operator) under Section 9(5) ✔
C. The passengers booking the cabs
D. Exempt from GST
Explanation: Under Section 9(5) of the CGST Act, 2017, the Electronic Commerce Operator (M/s Delta Cabs) is liable to pay GST on passenger transport services supplied through its electronic portal.
Hard SCENARIO · ECO Registration Exemption | Section 9(5) | Threshold Limit
Are the individual drivers operating through M/s Delta Cabs required to obtain separate GST registration if their turnover from such transport services is below the threshold limit?
A. Yes, mandatory registration is required for all ECO suppliers.
B. No, because Section 9(5) places the tax liability on the ECO, exempting individual drivers from compulsory registration solely for supplies through ECO, provided turnover is below threshold (or specific exemption notification). ✔
C. Yes, registration is required under Section 24.
D. No, because transport services are completely exempt.
Explanation: As per specific clarifications and notifications, suppliers supplying services through ECO where ECO is liable to pay tax under Section 9(5) are exempt from obtaining registration, provided their aggregate turnover does not exceed the threshold limit.
Medium SCENARIO · Passenger Transport Rate | Radio Taxi | 5% GST
What is the tax rate generally applicable to passenger transport services provided by radio taxis?
A. 5% with ITC (or 12% with ITC depending on vehicle type) ✔
B. 18%
C. 28%
D. Exempt
Explanation: Passenger transport services by a radio taxi / motor cab attract GST at 5% (without ITC) or 12% (with ITC), commonly 5% without ITC under notification.
Medium SCENARIO · ECO Liability | Section 9(5) | Recovery
If M/s Delta Cabs fails to pay GST on the services notified under Section 9(5), can recovery proceedings be initiated against them?
A. No, recovery must be made from the individual drivers.
B. Yes, because the ECO is treated as the person liable to pay tax for those services under Section 9(5). ✔
C. Only with approval of the Supreme Court.
D. No, recovery can only be made from passengers.
Explanation: Since Section 9(5) mandates that the ECO shall pay the tax as if the ECO is the supplier liable for paying tax, all provisions of the Act apply to the ECO for payment and recovery of such tax.
