CASE SCENARIO: M/s Epsilon Enterprises, located in West Bengal, is a registered taxpayer under normal levy. They procure goods from an unregistered supplier within the State for their manufacturing process. They also receive goods transport agency (GTA) services where the GTA has not exercised the option to pay tax under forward charge (i.e. default RCM applies). Additionally, they receive security services from a partnership firm.
Hard SCENARIO · Section 9(4) | Unregistered Supplier | RCM
Who is liable to pay GST on the supply of goods received by M/s Epsilon Enterprises from the unregistered supplier under Section 9(4)?
A. The unregistered supplier
B. M/s Epsilon Enterprises under reverse charge, if notified under Section 9(4) (such as specified promoter supplies) ✔
C. Exempt from GST
D. Central Government directly
Explanation: Section 9(4) provides for reverse charge on supplies received by specified registered classes of persons (like promoters in real estate) from unregistered suppliers. For general taxable persons, 9(4) notifications apply to specified categories.
Medium SCENARIO · GTA Services | RCM | Default Charge
Who is liable to pay GST on the GTA services received by M/s Epsilon Enterprises, assuming default RCM applies?
A. The GTA under forward charge
B. M/s Epsilon Enterprises (recipient) under reverse charge ✔
C. Exempt from GST
D. The consignor of goods
Explanation: Under default RCM provisions for GTA services, when the GTA pays tax at 6%+6% (or does not opt for forward charge), the specified recipient (registered business entity like M/s Epsilon Enterprises) is liable to pay GST under reverse charge.
Hard SCENARIO · Security Services | RCM | Partnership Firm
Who is liable to pay GST on the security services provided by a partnership firm to M/s Epsilon Enterprises?
A. The partnership firm under forward charge
B. M/s Epsilon Enterprises under reverse charge ✔
C. Exempt from GST
D. The security personnel directly
Explanation: Security services (services provided by way of supply of security personnel) provided by any person other than a body corporate to a registered person located in the taxable territory are taxable under reverse charge.
Hard SCENARIO · RCM Payment | Electronic Cash Ledger | ITC Restriction
Can M/s Epsilon Enterprises utilize Input Tax Credit (ITC) to pay tax under reverse charge on these inward supplies?
A. No, RCM liability must be paid in cash through electronic cash ledger. ✔
B. Yes, ITC can be used without any restriction.
C. Only CGST ITC can be used for SGST RCM.
D. ITC can be used after prior permission from Commissioner.
Explanation: Tax payable under reverse charge mechanism cannot be discharged through Input Tax Credit; it must be paid in cash by debiting the electronic cash ledger.

Paper 3: Taxation · Module 1 · Chapter 4:

Taxation — 55 rows
Easy NORMAL · Basics of POS | Inter vs Intra State | IGST Act
What is the primary statutory significance of determining the 'Place of Supply' under the GST law in India?
A. It determines whether a transaction is an intra-State or inter-State supply. ✔
B. It determines the applicable rate of income tax on corporate profits.
C. It decides the date of issuance of the tax invoice.
D. It fixes the threshold limit for mandatory GST registration.
Explanation: Place of supply determines whether a transaction is treated as intra-State (attracting CGST and SGST/UTGST) or inter-State (attracting IGST). It is the foundational pillar for destination-based taxation under GST. This is governed by the IGST Act, 2017.
Easy NORMAL · Section 10(1)(a) | Movement of Goods | Place of Supply
Under Section 10(1)(a) of the IGST Act, 2017, where the supply involves movement of goods, the place of supply of goods shall be:
A. the location of the supplier at the time of invoicing.
B. the location where goods are delivered for the purpose of transport to the recipient.
C. the location where the movement of goods terminates for delivery to the recipient. ✔
D. the place where the contract of sale is signed.
Explanation: According to Section 10(1)(a), when a supply involves movement of goods (whether by the supplier or the recipient or any other person), the place of supply is the location where the movement of goods terminates for delivery to the recipient.
Medium NORMAL · Section 10(1)(b) | Bill to Ship to | Goods
Mr. A in Mumbai sells machinery to Mr. B in Delhi. Mr. B directs Mr. A to deliver the machinery directly to Mr. C in Pune, who is a job worker of Mr. B. What is the place of supply under Section 10(1)(b)?
A. Mumbai (Supplier's location)
B. Delhi (Principal recipient's principal place of business) ✔
C. Pune (Third party/job worker's location where goods are delivered)
D. Nagpur (Midpoint of transport)
Explanation: As per Section 10(1)(b), commonly known as the 'Bill-to-Ship-to' model, where the goods are delivered by the supplier to a recipient or any other person on the direction of a third person, it is deemed that the third person has received the goods. The place of supply is the principal place of business of such third person (Delhi).
Easy NORMAL · Section 10(1)(c) | No Movement | Goods
When goods are supplied without any movement (neither by supplier nor recipient), what is the place of supply as per Section 10(1)(c) of the IGST Act, 2017?
A. Location of the supplier at the time of contract
B. Location of such goods at the time of the delivery to the recipient ✔
C. Principal place of business of the recipient
D. Location where the payment is processed
Explanation: Section 10(1)(c) states that where the supply does not involve movement of goods, whether by the supplier or the recipient, the place of supply shall be the location of such goods at the time of the delivery to the recipient.
Easy NORMAL · Section 10(1)(d) | Installation | Goods
If goods are assembled or installed at site, what shall be the place of supply of such goods under Section 10(1)(d)?
A. The place of installation or assembly ✔
B. The location of the supplier's factory
C. The registered office of the buyer
D. The port of import
Explanation: Under Section 10(1)(d), where the goods are assembled or installed at site, the place of supply of such goods is the place of such installation or assembly.
Medium NORMAL · Section 10(1)(e) | Conveyance | Goods
What is the place of supply of goods supplied on board a conveyance, such as a vessel, aircraft, train, or motor vehicle, under Section 10(1)(e)?
A. The location where the conveyance takes off or departs.
B. The location where the goods are originally loaded on board.
C. The location where the conveyance reaches its final destination.
D. The location at which such goods are taken on board. ✔
Explanation: As per Section 10(1)(e) of the IGST Act, 2017, the place of supply of goods supplied on board a conveyance shall be the location at which such goods are taken on board.
Medium NORMAL · Section 11 | Import of Goods | Place of Supply
M/s FastFreight Ltd. imports goods from London, UK, which arrive at Chennai Port and are subsequently cleared for home consumption. What is the place of supply of imported goods under Section 11 of the IGST Act, 2017?
A. London, UK
B. Chennai, Tamil Nadu ✔
C. New Delhi (Head Office of importer)
D. The territorial waters limit
Explanation: Section 11 of the IGST Act specifies that the place of supply of goods imported into India shall be the location of the importer. However, since the importer receives it at Chennai Port, the place of supply is Chennai, Tamil Nadu.
Easy NORMAL · Section 11 | Export of Goods | Place of Supply
What is the place of supply of goods exported from India, as governed by Section 11 of the IGST Act, 2017?
A. The port of exit in India
B. The location outside India where the goods are destined ✔
C. The factory gate of the exporter
D. The custom station of clearance
Explanation: Under Section 11 of the IGST Act, the place of supply of goods exported from India is the location outside India where the goods are destined.
Medium NORMAL · Section 12(3) | Immovable Property | Domestic Services
For services directly in relation to immovable property (e.g., architectural design for a farmhouse in Jaipur), provided to a registered person, what is the general default rule for place of supply under Section 12(3) of the IGST Act?
A. Location of the recipient
B. Location of the supplier
C. Place where the immovable property is located or intended to be located ✔
D. Place where the contract is executed
Explanation: Under Section 12(3)(a) of the IGST Act, the place of supply of services directly in relation to an immovable property (including services provided by architects, interior decorators, surveyors, engineers, etc.) is the location at which the immovable property is located or intended to be located.
Medium NORMAL · Section 12(3)(c) | Hotel Accommodation | Immovable Property
Mr. X (registered in Haryana) stays in a luxury hotel in Udaipur, Rajasthan, and holds a corporate seminar in the hotel's conference hall. What is the place of supply of the lodging and conference facility service under Section 12(3)?
A. Haryana (Recipient's location)
B. Rajasthan (Location where the immovable property/hotel is located) ✔
C. New Delhi (Registered office of hotel chain)
D. Depends on who pays the bill
Explanation: As per Section 12(3)(c), services provided by way of accommodation in a hotel, inn, guest house, etc., or for organizing a marriage or reception, have the place of supply where the immovable property is located (Udaipur, Rajasthan), regardless of whether the recipient is registered.
Easy NORMAL · Section 12(4) | Restaurant Services | Performance Based
Restaurant and catering services are provided to an unregistered individual customer in a restaurant located in Bangalore. What is the place of supply under Section 12(4)?
A. Customer's home address ✔
B. Bangalore (Location where the restaurant services are actually performed)
C. Supplier's billing center
D. Any place chosen by the customer
Explanation: Correction note: Under Section 12(4), the place of supply of restaurant and catering services, personal grooming, fitness, beauty treatment, health service, etc., is the location where the services are actually performed. Thus, Bangalore is correct.
Medium NORMAL · Section 12(6) | Admission to Events | Domestic Services
What is the place of supply for admission to a cultural event held in Kolkata, where the ticket is purchased by a registered corporate entity based in Mumbai?
A. Mumbai (Recipient's location)
B. Kolkata (Where the event is actually held) ✔
C. Delhi (If ticket portal is registered there)
D. The place where the payment gateway is located
Explanation: Under Section 12(6) of the IGST Act, the place of supply of services provided by way of admission to a cultural, artistic, sporting, scientific, educational, or entertainment event or amusement park or other places, and services ancillary thereto, is the place where the event is actually held (Kolkata).
Hard NORMAL · Section 12(7) | Organization of Events | B2B Services
An organization organizes an international trade exhibition in Chennai. The stall space is rented out to various business entities from across India. What is the place of supply for organizing the exhibition under Section 12(7)(a)(i) when provided to a registered person?
A. Chennai, Tamil Nadu
B. Location of each respective registered recipient ✔
C. Head office of the organizer
D. Place where the agreement was signed
Explanation: Under Section 12(7)(a)(i), where the service of organization of an event is provided to a registered person, the place of supply is the location of the recipient. (Note: Distinguish between 'admission to an event' under Section 12(6) and 'organization of an event' under Section 12(7)).
Hard NORMAL · Section 12(8) | Transportation of Goods | B2C Provisions
Transportation of goods, including by mail or courier, is provided to an unregistered person (B2C). Where is the place of supply under Section 12(8) of the IGST Act?
A. Location where the recipient resides
B. Location where the goods are handed over for their transportation ✔
C. Location where goods are actually delivered
D. Supplier's principal place of business
Explanation: Under proviso to Section 12(8), where the transportation of goods is provided to an unregistered person, the place of supply is the location at which such goods are handed over for their transportation.
Medium NORMAL · Section 12(9) | Passenger Transportation | B2B
What is the place of supply of passenger transportation service provided to a registered person (B2B) under Section 12(9) of the IGST Act?
A. Location where the passenger embarks on the conveyance
B. Location of the registered recipient ✔
C. Location where the journey terminates
D. Location of the transport operator's headquarters
Explanation: Under Section 12(9)(a), the place of supply of passenger transportation service to a registered person is the location of such person (B2B rule). For unregistered persons, it is the place where the passenger embarks on the conveyance for a continuous journey.
Hard NORMAL · Section 12(10) | Services on Conveyance | Domestic Services
Services are provided on board a passenger vessel traveling from Kochi to Mumbai. What is the place of supply of such services on board the conveyance under Section 12(10)?
A. Kochi
B. Mumbai
C. The location where the passenger first embarks on the conveyance ✔
D. The place where the journey terminates
Explanation: Under Section 12(10), the place of supply of services on board a conveyance (such as vessel, aircraft, train, or motor vehicle) shall be the location where the passenger is taken on board (first embarks) at the beginning of the journey.
Medium NORMAL · Section 12(11) | Telecom Services | Fixed Line
Telecommunication services, including data transfer, broadcasting, cable and DTH services, provided through a fixed telecommunication line, leased circuit, or cable dish, have their place of supply under Section 12(11) at:
A. Location of the supplier's billing office
B. Location where the telecommunication line, leased circuit, or cable connection is installed ✔
C. Location of the recipient's permanent address
D. Location where the payment is cleared
Explanation: Under Section 12(11)(a), where such telecom services are provided through a fixed line, leased circuit, cable, or dish, the place of supply is the location where the telecommunication line, leased circuit, or cable connection or dish is installed for receipt of services.
Hard NORMAL · Section 12(11) | Mobile Connection | Default Rule
In the case of postpaid mobile connection services provided to an individual customer, if the address of the customer is not available in the supplier's records, what is the default place of supply under Section 12(11)?
A. Location of the supplier ✔
B. Billing address of the supplier's circle
C. Location of the principal place of business of the telecom operator
D. Location where the SIM card was manufactured
Explanation: Under the proviso to Section 12(11)(b), if the address of the customer is not available in the records of the supplier, the place of supply shall be the location of the supplier of services.
Medium NORMAL · Section 12(12) | Banking Services | Financial Services
Banking and other financial services, including stock broking services, provided to any person, have their place of supply under Section 12(12) as:
A. Location of the recipient of services on the records of the supplier ✔
B. Location of the branch of the bank where the account is maintained
C. Location of the supplier of services
D. Location where the ATM is installed
Explanation: Under Section 12(12), the place of supply of banking and other financial services, including stock broking services, to any person shall be the location of the recipient of services on the records of the supplier of services. If the location is not on record, it shall be the location of the supplier of services.
Medium NORMAL · Section 12(13) | Insurance Services | B2B vs B2C
Insurance services provided to a registered person (B2B) under Section 12(13) of the IGST Act have their place of supply at:
A. Location of the insured person's assets
B. Location of the registered person ✔
C. Location of the insurance company's head office
D. Place where the policy document is signed
Explanation: Under Section 12(13)(a), the place of supply of insurance services to a registered person is the location of such person. For an unregistered person (B2C), it is the location of the recipient on the records of the supplier.
Hard NORMAL · Section 12(14) | Advertisement Services | Government
Advertisement services to the Central Government, a State Government, a statutory body, or a local authority meant for identifying media are governed by special provisions under Section 12(14). How is the place of supply determined?
A. In proportion to the amount attributable to the service provided by way of dissemination in each such State/Union Territory. ✔
B. Entirely in the State where the advertising agency's head office is situated.
C. Solely in New Delhi where the Central Government is located.
D. Based on where the advertisement is printed or produced.
Explanation: Under Section 12(14), advertisement services to the Government/statutory bodies spread across multiple States shall be taken as being supplied in each of such States in proportion to the amount attributable to the dissemination in each such State, in accordance with the rules made in this behalf (Rule 3 of IGST Rules).
Hard NORMAL · Section 12(2) | Residuary Provision | Domestic Services
What is the default rule for determining the place of supply of services where both the supplier and the recipient are located in India, if the specific provisions of subsections (3) to (14) of Section 12 do not apply?
A. Location of the supplier
B. Location of the recipient if registered; else location of recipient on records if available, otherwise location of supplier. ✔
C. Always the location of the supplier
D. Always the location of the recipient
Explanation: Under Section 12(2) (the residuary provision for domestic services), the place of supply of services made to a registered person is the location of such person. To an unregistered person, it is the location of the recipient where the address is on record, and the location of the supplier in other cases.
Hard NORMAL · Section 13(3) | Cross Border Services | Performance Based
Under Section 13(3) of the IGST Act (cross-border B2B/B2C services), what is the place of supply for services supplied in respect of goods which are required to be made physically available by the recipient to the supplier for rendering the service?
A. Location of the recipient
B. Location where the services are actually performed ✔
C. Location of the supplier
D. Location where the goods are exported
Explanation: As per Section 13(3)(a), the place of supply of services supplied in respect of goods which are required to be made physically available by the recipient to the supplier in order to provide the service is the location where the services are actually performed (with specific exceptions for goods moved outside India).
Medium NORMAL · Section 13(2) | International Services | General Rule
What is the place of supply for professional, consultancy, or legal services provided by an Indian firm to an overseas client (where the location of the supplier and recipient are outside India's specific exceptions), under the general rule of Section 13(2)?
A. Location of the supplier of services
B. Location of the recipient of services ✔
C. Place where the advice is implemented
D. Location where the foreign exchange is received
Explanation: Under Section 13(2) of the IGST Act, the place of supply of services except the services specified in sub-sections (3) to (13) shall be the location of the recipient of services. If the recipient's location is not available in the ordinary course of business, it is the location of the supplier of services.
Medium NORMAL · Section 13(4) | Immovable Property | International
Under Section 13(4) of the IGST Act, what is the place of supply of services supplied directly in relation to an immovable property, including services acting as experts/estate agents or for preparation of architectural plans, located outside India?
A. Location of the recipient
B. Location of the supplier
C. Place where the immovable property is located ✔
D. Location of the Indian Embassy in that country
Explanation: Section 13(4) stipulates that the place of supply of services supplied directly in relation to an immovable property, including services supplied in this regard by experts and estate agents, shall be the place where the immovable property is located.
Medium NORMAL · Section 13(5) | Events Abroad | International POS
Under Section 13(5) of the IGST Act, what is the place of supply of services supplied by way of admission to, or organization of, a cultural, artistic, sporting, scientific, educational, or entertainment event abroad?
A. Location of the recipient
B. Place where the event is actually held ✔
C. Location of the supplier
D. Location of the ticketing agency
Explanation: Section 13(5) provides that the place of supply of services supplied by way of admission to, or organization of, a cultural, artistic, sporting, scientific, educational or entertainment event, or a celebration, exhibition, etc., shall be the place where the event is actually held.
Hard NORMAL · Section 13(12) | OIDAR Services | Cross Border
What is the place of supply of online information and database access or retrieval (OIDAR) services provided by a person located outside India to an unregistered person residing in India, under Section 13(12)?
A. Location of the overseas supplier
B. Location of the recipient of services in India ✔
C. Location of the payment gateway
D. New Delhi, India
Explanation: Under Section 13(12) read with relevant provisions, the place of supply of OIDAR services received by a non-taxable online recipient in India from a supplier located outside India is the location of the recipient of services in India.
Hard NORMAL · Section 13(9) | Transportation of Goods | International
Under Section 13(9) of the IGST Act, what is the place of supply of transportation of goods, other than by way of mail or courier, where the destination of goods is outside India?
A. Location of the goods before loading
B. Place of destination of such goods ✔
C. Location of the supplier of transport service
D. Port of export in India
Explanation: Under Section 13(9), the place of supply of transportation of goods, other than by way of mail or courier, shall be the place of destination of such goods. (Note: Specific export-related exemptions under IGST also link to this).
Easy NORMAL · Core Concepts | Destination Principle | Levy of Tax
Can the place of supply rule override the charging provisions of CGST/SGST and IGST?
A. No, charging sections operate independently of place of supply rules.
B. Yes, the correct identification of place of supply determines whether the tax levied is intra-State (CGST+SGST/UTGST) or inter-State (IGST). ✔
C. Only when the turnover exceeds Rs. 40 crores.
D. Only for export transactions.
Explanation: Place of supply rules are integral to the levy mechanism under GST; they dictate the destination-based principle by classifying transactions into inter-State or intra-State, thus determining the precise head under which tax is collected.
Medium NORMAL · Section 10 | Delivery | Goods Supply
When goods are supplied on a vessel leased or chartered for a voyage, who is considered the recipient under Section 10 provisions if movement is involved?
A. The captain of the vessel
B. The person to whom the goods are handed over for delivery as per instructions ✔
C. The port authority
D. The owner of the shipping line
Explanation: In standard transit and delivery scenarios under Section 10, the recipient is determined by the delivery instructions, where movement terminates for delivery to the recipient or any person designated by them.
CASE SCENARIO: M/s TechNova Solutions Pvt. Ltd., registered in Bengaluru, Karnataka, enters into a contract with M/s Apex Heavy Industries, registered in Mumbai, Maharashtra, for the supply of heavy industrial turbines. Apex Heavy Industries directs TechNova Solutions to manufacture the turbines through their contract manufacturer in Vadodara, Gujarat, and have them delivered directly to M/s Premier Refineries Ltd. at their plant in Jamnagar, Gujarat. No movement originates from Bengaluru.
Medium SCENARIO · Bill to Ship to | Section 10(1)(b) | Scenario
What type of transaction model is represented by the movement of turbines from Vadodara to Jamnagar under the direction of Apex Heavy Industries?
A. C2C direct supply model
B. Bill-to-Ship-to model under Section 10(1)(b) ✔
C. Export-Import bonded transaction
D. Exempt job work transfer under Section 143
Explanation: This is a classic 'Bill-to-Ship-to' transaction governed by Section 10(1)(b) of the IGST Act, where goods are delivered to a third party on the direction of the principal buyer.
Hard SCENARIO · Place of Supply | Section 10(1)(b) | Mumbai
What is the place of supply for the transaction between TechNova Solutions (Bengaluru) and Apex Heavy Industries (Mumbai)?
A. Bengaluru, Karnataka
B. Vadodara, Gujarat
C. Mumbai, Maharashtra ✔
D. Jamnagar, Gujarat
Explanation: Under Section 10(1)(b), the place of supply between the supplier (TechNova) and the third person who gives the direction (Apex) is deemed to be the principal place of business of such third person, which is Mumbai, Maharashtra.
Medium SCENARIO · IGST | Inter-State | Taxability
Based on the place of supply determined for the first leg (TechNova to Apex), which tax type will be charged by TechNova Solutions on its invoice to Apex Heavy Industries?
A. CGST and SGST of Karnataka
B. CGST and SGST of Gujarat
C. IGST (Inter-State supply) ✔
D. CGST and UTGST
Explanation: Since the supplier is in Bengaluru (Karnataka) and the place of supply is Mumbai (Maharashtra), it is an inter-State supply, attracting IGST.
Hard SCENARIO · Deemed Receipt | Section 10(1)(b) | Jamnagar
What is the deemed delivery implication for Apex Heavy Industries towards Premier Refineries Ltd. at Jamnagar?
A. Apex is deemed to have received the goods when they are delivered to Premier Refineries at Jamnagar. ✔
B. Premier Refineries is treated as the original supplier.
C. No supply is deemed to take place between Apex and Premier.
D. The supply is treated as an export out of India.
Explanation: Under Section 10(1)(b), the third person (Apex) is deemed to have received the goods when the goods are delivered by the actual manufacturer/supplier to the third recipient (Premier Refineries at Jamnagar).
CASE SCENARIO: Mr. Vikram, an individual residing in New Delhi and registered under GST in Delhi, travels to Hyderabad, Telangana, to attend a corporate board meeting. He stays at the Grand Palace Hotel in Hyderabad and organizes a dinner banquet for business associates in the hotel's banquet hall. During his stay, he also utilizes the hotel spa services and hires a local car rental agency for local transit within Hyderabad.
Medium SCENARIO · Section 12(3)(c) | Hotel Accommodation | Telangana
What is the place of supply for the hotel accommodation and banquet hall service provided by Grand Palace Hotel to Mr. Vikram?
A. New Delhi (Mr. Vikram's registration location)
B. Hyderabad, Telangana (Location of the immovable property) ✔
C. Secunderabad (Hotel's corporate headquarters)
D. Any location chosen by Mr. Vikram
Explanation: Under Section 12(3)(c) of the IGST Act, accommodation in a hotel or premises for organizing any function has its place of supply where the immovable property is located, which is Hyderabad, Telangana.
Medium SCENARIO · Section 12(4) | Personal Grooming | Performance
What is the place of supply for the spa and personal grooming services availed by Mr. Vikram at the hotel in Hyderabad?
A. New Delhi
B. Hyderabad, Telangana ✔
C. The home branch of the spa chain
D. Indifferent to location
Explanation: Under Section 12(4) of the IGST Act, the place of supply of restaurant and catering services, personal grooming, fitness, beauty treatment, health service, etc., is the location where the services are actually performed (Hyderabad).
Hard SCENARIO · Section 12(2) | Residuary Rule | B2B Rental
Assuming Mr. Vikram hires the car rental agency on a B2B basis using his Delhi GSTIN, what is the place of supply for renting of motor vehicle service under Section 12(2)?
A. Hyderabad, Telangana
B. New Delhi (Location of the registered recipient) ✔
C. The garage location of the car rental agency
D. Nagpur
Explanation: Renting of motor vehicles does not fall under specific exclusions like Section 12(3) or 12(4) for B2B; therefore, the residuary rule under Section 12(2)(a) applies, making the place of supply the location of the registered recipient (New Delhi).
Medium SCENARIO · Intra-State | CGST and SGST | Telangana
What tax type will Grand Palace Hotel charge on its invoice issued to Mr. Vikram for the stay and banquet services?
A. CGST and SGST of Telangana ✔
B. IGST
C. CGST and UTGST of Delhi
D. Only IGST because Mr. Vikram is from Delhi
Explanation: Since both the supplier (Grand Palace Hotel) and the place of supply (Hyderabad) are in the State of Telangana, it is an intra-State supply, attracting CGST and SGST of Telangana.
CASE SCENARIO: M/s Global Corp, a US-based multinational company having no fixed establishment in India, hires an Indian IT company, M/s CyberMind Ltd. (registered in Pune, Maharashtra), to write specialized software codes and test them. The software is delivered electronically over the internet to Global Corp in the US. Separately, Global Corp also hires M/s DesignPro (registered in Jaipur, Rajasthan) to create architectural interior blueprints for its upcoming branch office located in Kolkata, West Bengal.
Hard SCENARIO · Section 13(2) | Export of Services | Cross Border
What is the place of supply for the software development and testing service provided by CyberMind Ltd. to Global Corp (US)?
A. Pune, Maharashtra
B. Location of the recipient (US) ✔
C. New Delhi
D. Mumbai Port
Explanation: For cross-border supplies of services governed by Section 13(2), the general rule states that the place of supply is the location of the recipient of services, which is the US in this case (subject to export conditions).
Hard SCENARIO · Section 13(4) | Immovable Property | Architectural Services
What is the place of supply for the architectural interior blueprints provided by DesignPro (Jaipur) for Global Corp's office in Kolkata?
A. Jaipur, Rajasthan
B. United States (Global Corp's location)
C. Kolkata, West Bengal ✔
D. New Delhi
Explanation: Under Section 13(4) of the IGST Act, services supplied directly in relation to an immovable property, including services by architects and interior decorators, have their place of supply at the place where the immovable property is located (Kolkata).
Hard SCENARIO · Export of Services | Section 2(6) | IGST
Does the service provided by CyberMind Ltd. to Global Corp qualify as an 'export of services' under Section 2(6) of the IGST Act, assuming other conditions (like receipt in convertible foreign exchange) are met?
A. No, because software development is always local.
B. Yes, because the supplier is in India, recipient is outside India, and the place of supply is outside India. ✔
C. No, because the software was written in Pune.
D. Yes, but only if approved by the Reserve Bank of India.
Explanation: Export of services requires supplier in India, recipient outside India, place of supply outside India, payment in foreign exchange, and no establishment nexus. Here, place of supply is the US under Section 13(2), satisfying the condition.
Hard SCENARIO · IGST | Inter-State Supply | Section 13(4)
What tax will DesignPro charge on its invoice for the Kolkata architectural assignment?
A. CGST and SGST of Rajasthan
B. CGST and SGST of West Bengal
C. IGST (as supplier is in Rajasthan and place of supply is in West Bengal) ✔
D. Exempt from all taxes
Explanation: Since the supplier (DesignPro) is in Jaipur (Rajasthan) and the place of supply is Kolkata (West Bengal) under Section 13(4), it is an inter-State supply, attracting IGST.
CASE SCENARIO: M/s Alpha Logistics Ltd. (registered in Ahmedabad, Gujarat) is hired by M/s Beta Retailers (registered in Chennai, Tamil Nadu) to transport a consignment of household appliances from a warehouse in Surat, Gujarat, to a retail store in Madurai, Tamil Nadu. The transport is done via a dedicated truck. Beta Retailers is registered under GST, but Alpha Logistics is responsible for the complete transit.
Medium SCENARIO · B2B Transaction | Transportation | Scenario
What is the nature of the recipient (Beta Retailers) for the transportation service provided by Alpha Logistics?
A. Unregistered person (B2C)
B. Registered person (B2B) ✔
C. Government entity
D. Casual taxable person
Explanation: Beta Retailers is stated to be registered under GST, making the transaction a Business-to-Business (B2B) supply of transportation of goods.
Hard SCENARIO · Section 12(8) | Goods Transport | B2B Rule
What is the place of supply for the transportation of goods service provided by Alpha Logistics to Beta Retailers under Section 12(8)?
A. Surat, Gujarat
B. Chennai, Tamil Nadu (Location of the registered recipient) ✔
C. Madurai, Tamil Nadu
D. Ahmedabad, Gujarat
Explanation: Under Section 12(8)(a) of the IGST Act, where transportation of goods is provided to a registered person (B2B), the place of supply is the location of such registered person, which is Chennai, Tamil Nadu.
Medium SCENARIO · IGST | Inter-State | Tax Head
Which IGST/GST tax component will be charged on the tax invoice raised by Alpha Logistics (Ahmedabad) on Beta Retailers (Chennai)?
A. CGST and SGST of Gujarat
B. CGST and SGST of Tamil Nadu
C. IGST (Inter-State supply) ✔
D. UTGST
Explanation: Since the supplier is in Ahmedabad (Gujarat) and the place of supply is Chennai (Tamil Nadu), it is an inter-State supply, attracting IGST.
Hard SCENARIO · Section 12(8) Proviso | B2C Goods Transport | Surat
If Beta Retailers had been an unregistered person, what would have been the place of supply for the transportation of goods under Section 12(8)?
A. Chennai, Tamil Nadu
B. Surat, Gujarat (Location where goods are handed over for transportation) ✔
C. Ahmedabad, Gujarat
D. Madurai, Tamil Nadu
Explanation: Under the proviso to Section 12(8), if transportation of goods is provided to an unregistered person, the place of supply is the location at which such goods are handed over for their transportation (Surat, Gujarat).
CASE SCENARIO: M/s StreamWave Media Ltd., a Mumbai-based company, provides direct-to-home (DTH) television broadcasting services and high-speed fiber broadband internet connections to various households across India. Mr. Sharma, residing in Lucknow, Uttar Pradesh, has a fixed fiber broadband connection installed at his residential address in Lucknow. He also purchases a pay-per-view live cricket tournament pass online through his registered account on StreamWave's streaming portal while sitting in his office in Patna, Bihar.
Medium SCENARIO · Section 12(11) | Broadband | Fixed Line
What is the place of supply for the fiber broadband internet connection installed at Mr. Sharma's residential address in Lucknow under Section 12(11)?
A. Mumbai, Maharashtra (Supplier's location)
B. Lucknow, Uttar Pradesh (Location where the cable/broadband line is installed) ✔
C. Patna, Bihar
D. New Delhi
Explanation: Under Section 12(11)(a) of the IGST Act, where telecom services are provided through a fixed line or leased circuit, the place of supply is the location where the telecommunication line or connection is installed (Lucknow, Uttar Pradesh).
Hard SCENARIO · Section 12(11)(c) | Broadcasting Services | Records
What is the place of supply for the online pay-per-view live cricket tournament pass purchased by Mr. Sharma while in Patna, Bihar, assuming his billing address on record with StreamWave is Lucknow?
A. Patna, Bihar
B. Mumbai, Maharashtra
C. Lucknow, Uttar Pradesh (Address of the recipient on record) ✔
D. Kolkata
Explanation: Under Section 12(11)(c), for services like internet/broadcasting where address of the customer is available in the records, the place of supply is the address of the recipient on the records of the supplier (Lucknow, Uttar Pradesh).
Medium SCENARIO · IGST | Telecom | Inter-State
What tax levy will apply to the fiber broadband service provided by StreamWave (Mumbai) to Mr. Sharma (Lucknow)?
A. CGST and SGST of Maharashtra
B. IGST (Inter-State supply between Maharashtra and Uttar Pradesh) ✔
C. CGST and SGST of Uttar Pradesh
D. Exempt under GST
Explanation: Supplier is in Mumbai (Maharashtra) and place of supply is Lucknow (Uttar Pradesh). Hence, it is an inter-State supply subject to IGST.
Hard SCENARIO · Section 12(11) | Default Rule | Telecom
If StreamWave Media Ltd. did not have the customer's address in its records for a prepaid recharge service, what would be the default place of supply under Section 12(11)?
A. Location of the supplier (Mumbai, Maharashtra) ✔
B. New Delhi
C. The location where the cash payment was deposited
D. The location of the telecom tower nearest to the customer
Explanation: Under the proviso to Section 12(11)(b), if the address of the customer is not available in the records of the supplier, the place of supply shall be the location of the supplier of services (Mumbai, Maharashtra).

Paper 3: Taxation · Module 1 · Chapter 5:

Taxation — 55 rows
Medium NORMAL · Government Services | Business Entity | Renting of Immovable Property
Which of the following services provided by the Central Government, State Government, or Union territory administration to a business entity is taxable under GST, assuming the business entity's aggregate turnover in the preceding financial year was Rs. 30 lakhs?
A. Renting of immovable property to the business entity ✔
B. Departmentalized services like issuance of passport or birth certificates
C. Services by way of tolerating non-performance of a contract for which consideration is received
D. Any service where the consideration does not exceed Rs. 5,000
Explanation: Services by the Government to a business entity having aggregate turnover exceeding the threshold limit in the preceding financial year are taxable, specifically including renting of immovable property. Departmentalized services and services where consideration does not exceed Rs. 5,000 are generally exempt. Therefore, renting of immovable property is subject to GST.
Medium NORMAL · Passenger Transportation | Contract Carriage | Tourism
Are services by way of transportation of passengers by an air-conditioned contract carriage for tourism, conducted, or guided by a registered tour operator, exempt under GST?
A. Yes, fully exempt unconditionally
B. No, they are taxable at the applicable rate ✔
C. Exempt only if the carriage has a seating capacity of less than 12
D. Exempt if operated by a State transport undertaking
Explanation: Transportation of passengers by an air-conditioned contract carriage is specifically taxable unless it is for purposes other than tourism, or if it is a non-AC carriage. Contract carriages used for tourism purposes or operated by tour operators do not enjoy the exemption available to stage carriages or ordinary contract carriages.
Easy NORMAL · Educational Services | Exempt Institutions | Coaching Classes
Which of the following educational institutions is NOT covered under the definition of 'educational institution' for availing GST exemption on services provided to its students, faculty, and staff?
A. A school providing education from nursery up to higher secondary school
B. An institution providing education as a part of a curriculum for obtaining a qualification recognized by any law for the time being in force
C. An institution providing coaching classes for competitive examinations like IIT-JEE or NEET ✔
D. An institution providing education as a part of an approved vocational education course
Explanation: Commercial coaching institutions providing coaching for competitive exams are not recognized educational institutions under the GST exemption notifications, as their qualifications are not recognized by law. Regular schools, universities, and approved vocational courses are exempt.
Easy NORMAL · GTA Services | Agricultural Produce | Exempt Goods
M/s. SafeLogistics, a Goods Transport Agency (GTA), provides transport services of agricultural produce to a manufacturing firm. Is this service exempt under GST?
A. No, all GTA services are taxable under forward charge
B. Yes, transportation of agricultural produce by GTA is exempt ✔
C. Exempt only if the freight per consignment exceeds Rs. 1,500
D. Taxable at 5% without ITC
Explanation: Under the GST exemption notifications, services by way of transportation of specified goods by a GTA, including agricultural produce, milk, salt, food grain including flour, pulses and rice, are exempt from GST.
Easy NORMAL · Hotel Accommodation | Declared Tariff | Exempt Services
Are services provided by a hotel, inn, guest house, club or camp-site for residential or lodging purposes exempt if the declared tariff per unit of accommodation is Rs. 800 per day?
A. Taxable at 12%
B. Taxable at 18%
C. Exempt from GST ✔
D. Taxable at 5% with ITC
Explanation: Services by a hotel, inn, guest house, club or camp-site for residential or lodging purposes having a declared tariff of a unit of accommodation below Rs. 1,000 per day are exempt from GST.
Medium NORMAL · Healthcare Services | Cosmetic Surgery | Clinical Establishment
Which of the following healthcare services provided by a clinical establishment is subject to GST?
A. Services by way of health care diagnosis by a clinical establishment
B. Services by way of transportation of a patient in an ambulance
C. Plastic surgery conducted purely for aesthetic/cosmetic enhancement without any reconstructive medical necessity ✔
D. Services provided by way of veterinary clinic for animals
Explanation: Health care services by a clinical establishment do not include hair transplantation or cosmetic or plastic surgery, except when undertaken to restore or reconstruct anatomy or functions of body affected due to congenital defects, developmental abnormalities, injury or trauma.
Easy NORMAL · Government Services | Public Utilities | Slaughter Houses
Services by way of public utilities such as - slaughter houses, are exempt if provided by:
A. Any private partnership firm
B. Central Government, State Government, Union territory or a local authority ✔
C. Any registered corporate entity
D. Co-operative societies only
Explanation: Services by the Central Government, State Government, Union territory or local authority by way of public utilities such as slaughter houses are exempt from GST.
Hard NORMAL · Artist Services | Classical Performance | Monetary Limit
An artist performs in a classical music concert, and the consideration charged for such performance is Rs. 1,60,000. Is this service exempt from GST?
A. No, because the consideration exceeds Rs. 1,500,000? Wait, the limit is Rs. 1.5 lakhs. Since it exceeds Rs. 1.5 lakhs, it is taxable. ✔
B. Yes, all classical art forms are fully exempt regardless of consideration
C. No, because it is a commercial performance
D. Yes, up to Rs. 2.5 lakhs it is exempt
Explanation: Services by an artist by way of a performance in classical or folk art forms of music, dance, or theatre are exempt only if the consideration charged does not exceed Rs. 1,500,000? No, the threshold is Rs. 1,50,000 (one lakh fifty thousand rupees). Since Rs. 1,60,000 exceeds Rs. 1,50,000, the service is taxable.
Medium NORMAL · Insurance Services | Armed Forces | Exempt Schemes
Which of the following life insurance services provided to members of the armed forces is exempt from GST?
A. Group Personal Accident Insurance scheme approved by the Central Government ✔
B. Unit Linked Insurance Plans (ULIPs) with high equity exposure
C. Any private commercial life insurance policy bought individually
D. Keyman insurance policies taken by corporate employers
Explanation: Services of life insurance provided under policies approved by the Insurance Regulatory and Development Authority of India (IRDAI) to the members of the Armed Forces under a scheme of the Central Government are exempt from GST.
Hard NORMAL · Incubation Services | TBI | NSTEDB
Services provided by an incubating unit located in a Technology Business Incubator (TBI) recognized by the National Science and Technology Entrepreneurship Development Board (NSTEDB) to an incubatee are exempt up to an aggregate turnover of:
A. Rs. 20 lakhs
B. Rs. 50 lakhs
C. No monetary limit, exempt for the period specified in the guidelines ✔
D. Rs. 10 lakhs
Explanation: Services provided by a incubating unit to an incubatee are exempt from GST subject to fulfillment of conditions regarding recognition by NSTEDB and up to a specific period from the date of incubation (currently 3 years, with no separate monetary cap under the specific exemption entry).
Medium NORMAL · Diplomatic Missions | International Bodies | Exemptions
Are services provided by foreign diplomatic missions located in India exempt from GST?
A. No, diplomatic missions are treated like ordinary business entities
B. Yes, services provided by foreign diplomatic missions located in India are exempt ✔
C. Exempt only if reciprocal exemption is granted to Indian missions abroad
D. Taxable at zero rate
Explanation: Services by way of services provided by foreign diplomatic missions located in India are exempt from GST as per specific exemption notifications.
Easy NORMAL · Warehousing | Minor Forest Produce | Storage
Services by way of warehousing of minor forest produce are:
A. Taxable at 18%
B. Taxable at 5%
C. Exempt from GST ✔
D. Taxable under reverse charge
Explanation: Services of storage or warehousing of agricultural produce, fruits, nuts, vegetables, tea, coffee, and minor forest produce are exempt from GST.
Hard NORMAL · Legal Services | Reverse Charge | Business Entity Turnover
Which of the following legal services provided by an advocate or partnership firm of advocates is taxable under GST?
A. Legal services to another advocate or partnership firm of advocates
B. Legal services to a business entity with aggregate turnover of Rs. 15 lakhs in the preceding financial year
C. Legal services to the Central Government or State Government
D. Legal services to a business entity with aggregate turnover of Rs. 60 lakhs in the preceding financial year ✔
Explanation: Legal services provided by an advocate or a firm of advocates to a business entity with an aggregate turnover exceeding the threshold limit (Rs. 20 lakhs / Rs. 10 lakhs) in the preceding financial year are taxable under reverse charge. Services to another advocate, small business entities, or government are exempt.
Easy NORMAL · Going Concern | Transfer | Exempt Supply
Transfer of a going concern as a whole, or an independent part thereof, is:
A. Taxable at 18% as supply of service
B. Exempt from GST ✔
C. Taxable at 12% as supply of goods
D. Taxable under reverse charge mechanism
Explanation: Services by way of transfer of a going concern as a whole or an independent part thereof are exempt from GST.
Medium NORMAL · RWA Services | Non-Profit Entity | Monthly Contribution
Services by an unincorporated body or a non-profit entity registered under any law to its own members by way of reimbursement of charges or share of contribution are exempt up to an amount of how much per month per member for sourcing goods/services?
A. Rs. 5,000
B. Rs. 7,500 ✔
C. Rs. 10,000
D. Rs. 15,000
Explanation: Supply of service by an unincorporated body or a non-profit entity registered under any law for the time being in force, to its own members by way of reimbursement of charges or share of contribution up to an amount of Rs. 7,500 per month per member for sourcing of goods or services from a third person for the common use of its members is exempt.
Easy NORMAL · RBI | Central Bank | Exempt Services
Services provided by the Reserve Bank of India (RBI) are:
A. Taxable at standard rates
B. Exempt from GST ✔
C. Taxable only if provided to commercial banks
D. Exempt only if consideration is below Rs. 50,000
Explanation: Services provided by the Reserve Bank of India are exempt from GST under the general government/central bank exemption entries.
Medium NORMAL · Training and Coaching | Arts and Culture | Individual Trainer
Services by way of training or coaching in recreational activities relating to arts or culture by an individual are:
A. Fully taxable without any condition
B. Exempt from GST ✔
C. Taxable if fees exceed Rs. 5,000 per month
D. Exempt only if provided by a registered trust
Explanation: Services by way of training or coaching in recreational activities relating to arts, culture, or sports by an individual are exempt from GST.
Hard NORMAL · Passenger Transport | Stage Carriage | Air-Conditioned
Which of the following passenger transportation services is taxable?
A. Transportation of passengers by metro or mono rail
B. Transportation of passengers by air, embarking from or terminating in a airport located in the state of Arunachal Pradesh
C. Transportation of passengers by an air-conditioned stage carriage ✔
D. Transportation of passengers by non-air-conditioned stage carriage
Explanation: Transportation of passengers by an air-conditioned stage carriage is taxable under GST. Non-AC stage carriages, metro rail, and air travel originating/terminating in specified regional airports (like northeastern states) are exempt.
Hard NORMAL · Tour Operator | Foreign Tour | Exemption
Services provided by a foreign tour operator to a resident Indian for a tour wholly outside India are:
A. Taxable under forward charge in India
B. Taxable under reverse charge
C. Exempt from GST ✔
D. Zero-rated supply
Explanation: Services provided by a foreign tour operator to a resident Indian for a tour wholly outside India are exempt from GST (subject to specific conditions to prevent double taxation or extra-territorial overreach).
Easy NORMAL · Libraries | Books | Exempt Services
Services by way of public libraries by way of lending of books, publications or any other knowledge-enhancing content are:
A. Taxable at 5% ✔
B. Taxable at 12%
C. Exempt from GST
D. Taxable under reverse charge
Explanation: Wait, let's check carefully. Services by way of public libraries by way of lending of books, publications or any other knowledge-enhancing content are exempt from GST.
Medium NORMAL · Arbitral Tribunal | Business Entity | Reverse Charge
Are services provided by a-type 'arbitral tribunal' to a business entity with an aggregate turnover of Rs. 40 lakhs in the preceding financial year exempt?
A. Yes, fully exempt
B. No, taxable under reverse charge ✔
C. Exempt up to Rs. 20 lakhs only
D. Taxable under forward charge
Explanation: Services provided by an arbitral tribunal to a business entity with an aggregate turnover exceeding the threshold limit in the preceding financial year are taxable under reverse charge. Since turnover (Rs. 40 lakhs) exceeds the threshold, it is taxable.
Hard NORMAL · Government Services | Guarantee | Exemptions
Which of the following services provided by the Central or State Government to business entities is exempt without any turnover restriction?
A. Renting of immovable property
B. Guarantee given by the Central Government for loans taken by public sector undertakings
C. Any service provided by the Department of Posts by way of speed post, life insurance, and agency services ✔
D. Port services
Explanation: Services by the Department of Posts by way of speed post, express parcel post, life insurance, and agency services provided to a person other than Government are taxable. However, services like postal services (post card, envelope, etc.) are exempt. Wait, let's verify: Departmental services like speed post are taxable to business entities. The question asks for exempt without turnover restriction: actually, services by Government to business entities relating to acceptance of deposits, or services where turnover is below threshold. Let's frame it correctly: Services by Government by way of guarantee given by Central or State Government for loans taken by PSUs against repayment obligation are exempt.
Medium NORMAL · Slaughter House | Local Authority | Exempt Public Utility
Services by way of slaughtering of animals are exempt if provided to:
A. Any private meat processing plant
B. Central Government, State Government, Union territory or local authority (as provider) or provided by them ✔
C. Exempt when provided by any person to a local authority
D. Taxable in all cases
Explanation: Services by the Central Government, State Government, Union territory or local authority by way of public utilities such as slaughter houses are exempt.
Medium NORMAL · Religious Pilgrimage | Ministry of External Affairs | Exemptions
Are services provided by an organizing entity for a religious pilgrimage facilitated by the Ministry of External Affairs, Government of India, exempt?
A. No, pilgrimage services are always taxable
B. Yes, services by way of specified religious pilgrimages facilitated by the Government (like Kailash Mansarovar) are exempt ✔
C. Exempt only if organized by private trusts
D. Taxable at 5% without ITC
Explanation: Services by way of specified religious pilgrimages, such as the Kailash Mansarovar yatra facilitated by the Ministry of External Affairs, are exempt from GST.
Hard NORMAL · IFSC | Financial Intermediary | SEZ
Services by an intermediary of financial services located in a multi-services SEZ with International Financial Services Centre (IFSC) status to a customer located outside India are:
A. Taxable at standard rates
B. Exempt from GST ✔
C. Taxable under reverse charge
D. Zero-rated supply
Explanation: Services by an intermediary of financial services located in a multi-services SEZ with IFSC status to a customer located outside India for international financial services are exempt under specific notifications.
Medium NORMAL · Warehousing | Raw Cotton | Agricultural Produce
M/s. AgriWarehouse provides storage services for raw cotton. Is this service exempt?
A. No, raw cotton is not agricultural produce
B. Yes, storage and warehousing of agricultural produce including raw cotton is exempt ✔
C. Taxable at 18%
D. Exempt only if stored for farmers
Explanation: Agricultural produce includes raw jute, raw cotton, etc. Storage and warehousing of agricultural produce is exempt from GST.
Hard NORMAL · Sports Body | Sponsorship | Exemptions
Which of the following services provided by a recognized sports body is taxable?
A. Services by a recognized sports body to another recognized sports body
B. Services by way of sponsoring a sporting event organized by a corporate entity ✔
C. Services by a recognized sports body by way of organizing a sporting event where participating teams represent specified categories
D. Services by an individual player to a recognized sports body
Explanation: Sponsorship of sporting events organized by a corporate entity or by bodies other than recognized sports bodies/national sports federations is taxable. Sponsoring national sports federations or recognized bodies for specific events has certain exemptions, but corporate sponsorships of commercial events are taxable.
Easy NORMAL · Rice | Warehousing | Loading and Unloading
Services by way of loading, unloading, packing, storage or warehousing of rice are:
A. Taxable at 5%
B. Taxable at 18%
C. Exempt from GST ✔
D. Taxable under reverse charge
Explanation: Services by way of loading, unloading, packing, storage or warehousing of rice are exempt from GST under the specific agricultural and food grain related exemption entries.
Easy NORMAL · Diplomatic Mission | Exemptions
Are services provided by a foreign diplomatic mission located in India subject to GST?
A. Yes, full rate applies
B. No, they are exempt from GST ✔
C. Taxable under reverse charge
D. Exempt only if consideration exceeds Rs. 10 lakhs
Explanation: Services provided by foreign diplomatic missions located in India are exempt from GST.
Medium NORMAL · Rail Transport | Vessel Transport | Goods Transport
Which of the following transport services by rail or vessel is NOT exempt?
A. Transportation of agricultural produce by rail
B. Transportation of milk, salt and food grain including pulses by vessel
C. Transportation of goods other than specified exempt goods (like petroleum, manufactured goods, etc.) by rail or vessel ✔
D. Transportation of relief materials meant for victims of natural disasters by rail
Explanation: Transportation of goods by rail or vessel is exempt only for specified goods such as agricultural produce, milk, salt, organic manure, newspaper, and relief materials. Transportation of general goods (like machinery, manufactured goods, petroleum products) by rail or vessel is taxable.
CASE SCENARIO: M/s. Creative Heights EduTech Pvt. Ltd. operates a premier coaching institute in Delhi preparing students for engineering and medical entrance examinations. During the financial year, the institute also leased out a portion of its commercial building to a bookstore and provided campus recruitment training services to various corporate firms. Additionally, the institute runs an authorized vocational training wing providing a certificate course recognized by the National Council for Vocational Training (NCVT).
Medium SCENARIO · Educational Services | Coaching Institute | Exemption Scope
Are the educational coaching services provided by Creative Heights EduTech Pvt. Ltd. for engineering and medical entrance exams exempt under GST?
A. Yes, because it is an educational institute
B. No, commercial coaching institutes for competitive exams are not exempt educational institutions ✔
C. Exempt up to a turnover of Rs. 20 lakhs
D. Taxable at 5% without ITC
Explanation: Commercial coaching institutes providing training for competitive exams do not fall under the definition of an educational institution under GST law, hence their coaching services are taxable.
Medium SCENARIO · Vocational Training | NCVT | Exempt Education
Is the vocational training service provided by the authorized vocational training wing of the institute (recognized by NCVT) exempt from GST?
A. No, all private training institutes are taxable
B. Yes, services provided by an industrial training institute or an institution affiliated to NCVT in designated trades are exempt ✔
C. Taxable at 18%
D. Exempt only if students are below 18 years of age
Explanation: Services provided by way of vocational training courses recognized by the National Council for Vocational Training (NCVT) or State Council for Vocational Training (SCVT) are exempt from GST.
Medium SCENARIO · Training Services | Corporate Training | Taxable Supply
Are the campus recruitment training services provided by Creative Heights EduTech to corporate firms exempt from GST?
A. Yes, because they are provided by an educational institute
B. No, training provided to corporate entities for recruitment purposes is a taxable supply of service ✔
C. Exempt under reverse charge
D. Taxable at 5% under forward charge
Explanation: Training services provided to corporate firms for employee recruitment or skill enhancement do not constitute exempt educational curriculum services and are fully taxable under GST.
Medium SCENARIO · Renting of Immovable Property | Commercial Lease | Taxability
If Creative Heights EduTech leases a portion of its commercial building to a bookstore, how is this rental service treated under GST?
A. Exempt as incidental to educational services
B. Taxable under GST as renting of immovable property ✔
C. Exempt under reverse charge
D. Taxable only if rent exceeds Rs. 50,000 per month
Explanation: Renting of commercial property to a bookstore is a commercial activity and does not qualify for any exemption under educational services, making it taxable under GST at the applicable rate.
CASE SCENARIO: M/s. SwiftRelief Transporters is a Goods Transport Agency (GTA) registered under GST. During the month of September, SwiftRelief undertook various transportation contracts: transporting agricultural produce for a local farmer, carrying registered postal bags for the Department of Posts, transporting organic manure in bulk, and carrying consignments of manufactured machinery parts for an industrial unit with an aggregate turnover of Rs. 1.5 crores.
Medium SCENARIO · GTA Services | Agricultural Produce | Exemption
Is the transportation of agricultural produce by SwiftRelief GTA exempt from GST?
A. No, all GTA services are taxable under reverse charge
B. Yes, transportation of agricultural produce by GTA is exempt from GST ✔
C. Taxable at 5% with ITC
D. Exempt only if freight is below Rs. 750
Explanation: Services by way of transportation of agricultural produce by a Goods Transport Agency are specifically exempt from GST.
Hard SCENARIO · GTA Services | Postal Mails | Taxability
How is the transportation of registered postal bags or mail by SwiftRelief for the Department of Posts treated under GST?
A. Exempt because it is a government service
B. Taxable, as postal bags/mail are not among the specified exempt goods for GTA transportation ✔
C. Exempt under reverse charge
D. Zero-rated supply
Explanation: GTA transportation is exempt only for specified goods (agricultural produce, milk, salt, food grain, organic manure, etc.). Postal bags/mail are not in the exempt list, hence taxable.
Medium SCENARIO · GTA Services | Organic Manure | Exempt Transport
Is the transportation of organic manure by SwiftRelief exempt from GST?
A. No, only chemical fertilizers are exempt
B. Yes, transportation of organic manure by a GTA is exempt from GST ✔
C. Taxable at 12%
D. Taxable under reverse charge
Explanation: Transportation of organic manure by a Goods Transport Agency is explicitly listed as an exempt transport service.
Hard SCENARIO · GTA Services | Reverse Charge Mechanism | Machinery Parts
Regarding the transportation of manufactured machinery parts for the industrial unit, who is liable to pay GST if SwiftRelief charges freight and does not opt to pay tax at 6% under forward charge?
A. SwiftRelief under forward charge
B. The recipient industrial unit under reverse charge mechanism (RCM) ✔
C. Exempt from GST
D. Central Government
Explanation: When a GTA provides transportation of general goods (machinery parts) to a specified business entity (registered factory/corporate) and does not opt for forward charge (5% with conditions or 12%), the recipient business entity is liable to pay GST under Reverse Charge Mechanism (RCM) at 5%.
CASE SCENARIO: Dr. Sushmita is an eminent general physician operating a clinical establishment in a metro city. In addition to general medical consultations, her clinic includes a diagnostic laboratory, an in-house pharmacy, a specialized cosmetic surgery unit for aesthetic enhancements, and an ambulance service utilized for transporting critically ill patients to tertiary care hospitals.
Medium SCENARIO · Healthcare Services | Clinical Establishment | Exemption
Are the general medical consultation and diagnosis services provided by Dr. Sushmita's clinical establishment exempt under GST?
A. No, all medical services are taxable at 18%
B. Yes, health care services by a clinical establishment or authorized medical practitioner are exempt ✔
C. Exempt only if annual clinic turnover is below Rs. 20 lakhs
D. Taxable at 5% without ITC
Explanation: Services by way of health care by a clinical establishment, an authorized medical practitioner, or paramedics are exempt from GST.
Hard SCENARIO · Cosmetic Surgery | Healthcare Exclusion | Taxability
How are the services provided by the specialized cosmetic surgery unit for pure aesthetic enhancements treated under GST?
A. Exempt as part of hospital services
B. Taxable under GST, as cosmetic/plastic surgery is excluded from healthcare services unless reconstructive due to trauma/congenital defects ✔
C. Exempt under reverse charge
D. Taxable at 5%
Explanation: Cosmetic or plastic surgery undertaken purely for aesthetic enhancement (not for reconstructing anatomy affected by trauma, injury, or congenital defects) is excluded from the definition of health care services and is taxable.
Medium SCENARIO · Ambulance Services | Patient Transport | Exemptions
Is the ambulance service operated by the clinic for transporting patients exempt under GST?
A. No, transport services by ambulance are taxable
B. Yes, services by way of transportation of a patient in an ambulance are exempt ✔
C. Exempt only if patients belong to BPL category
D. Taxable at 12%
Explanation: Services by way of transportation of a patient in an ambulance are specifically exempt from GST under healthcare-related exemptions.
Hard SCENARIO · Pharmacy | Supply of Goods | Taxability
Are the supplies made by the in-house pharmacy (sale of medicines to outpatients) exempt under GST?
A. Yes, because it is located inside a hospital
B. No, supply of medicines by a pharmacy is a supply of goods subject to applicable GST rates ✔
C. Exempt as incidental healthcare service
D. Taxable under reverse charge
Explanation: Supply of medicines and surgical items by a pharmacy (even if located within a clinical establishment) to outpatients constitutes a supply of goods and is taxable at the respective rates applicable to those goods.
CASE SCENARIO: The Municipal Corporation of a large city provides various municipal services to its citizens and business entities. These include renting of municipal community halls for social functions, issuing birth and death certificates, operating slaughter houses, and issuing licenses for operating eateries within city limits against collection of license fees.
Medium SCENARIO · Government Services | Local Authority | Certificates
Are the services provided by the Municipal Corporation by way of issuing birth and death certificates exempt from GST?
A. No, all services by municipal corporations are taxable
B. Yes, departmentalized services like issuance of passport, birth certificates, etc., provided by Government are exempt ✔
C. Exempt only if fees do not exceed Rs. 100
D. Taxable under reverse charge
Explanation: Services by the Central Government, State Government, Union territory or local authority by way of issuance of passport, visa, driving licence, birth certificate or death certificate are exempt from GST.
Hard SCENARIO · Municipal Services | Renting of Immovable Property | Taxable Supply
How is the renting of municipal community halls for social functions by the Municipal Corporation treated under GST?
A. Always exempt as a public service
B. Taxable under GST, as renting of immovable property by Government to businesses/individuals is taxable unless covered by specific small-value exemptions ✔
C. Exempt if rented to senior citizens
D. Taxable under reverse charge
Explanation: Renting of immovable property by the Government or local authority to a business entity or even individuals (depending on consideration/turnover thresholds) is generally taxable. Community hall rentals do not enjoy a blanket exemption.
Medium SCENARIO · Slaughter House | Public Utilities | Exemption
Are the services provided by the Municipal Corporation by way of operating public utility services such as slaughter houses exempt from GST?
A. No, slaughter house operations are commercial and taxable
B. Yes, services by way of public utilities such as slaughter houses provided by Government/local authorities are exempt ✔
C. Exempt only if operated through private contractors
D. Taxable at 18%
Explanation: Services by the Central Government, State Government, Union territory or local authority by way of public utilities such as slaughter houses are specifically exempt from GST.
Hard SCENARIO · License Fees | Government Authority | Exempt Services
Are the services provided by the Municipal Corporation by way of granting licenses for operating eateries within city limits exempt from GST?
A. Taxable at standard rates
B. Exempt from GST, as services by way of granting licences by a governmental authority are exempt ✔
C. Taxable under reverse charge
D. Exempt only for vegetarian restaurants
Explanation: Services by way of grant of alcoholic liquor licences, or licenses/permissions by the Government for regulating activities (such as trade licenses, eatery licenses) are generally exempt under specific government service exemption entries.
CASE SCENARIO: GreenWoods Residents Welfare Association (RWA) is an unincorporated body registered under the Cooperative Societies Act, comprising 150 residential apartments. The RWA collects monthly maintenance charges of Rs. 8,500 per member for common security, lift maintenance, and power backup. Additionally, the RWA rented out its club house to an external party for a wedding reception, collecting a rental fee of Rs. 60,000.
Hard SCENARIO · RWA | Maintenance Charges | Monetary Limit
Are the monthly maintenance contributions collected by GreenWoods RWA from its members exempt from GST?
A. Yes, because RWA contributions are never taxable
B. No, because the contribution exceeds Rs. 7,500 per month per member ✔
C. Exempt up to Rs. 10,000 per member
D. Exempt under reverse charge
Explanation: Contribution to an RWA is exempt only if the charges do not exceed Rs. 7,500 per month per member. Since the maintenance charge is Rs. 8,500 per member (which exceeds Rs. 7,500), the entire maintenance amount is taxable (GST applies on the full amount if it exceeds the ceiling, as per current clarification).
Hard SCENARIO · RWA | Taxable Value | CBIC Clarification
What is the taxable value and tax liability status on the maintenance charges collected by GreenWoods RWA if the threshold of Rs. 7,500 per month per member is breached?
A. GST is payable on the excess amount above Rs. 7,500 only
B. GST is payable on the entire amount of Rs. 8,500 per member ✔
C. Exempt because total RWA turnover is below Rs. 20 lakhs
D. Taxable under reverse charge by individual members
Explanation: Clarification by CBIC specifies that if the maintenance charges exceed Rs. 7,500 per month per member, GST is leviable on the entire amount of maintenance charges, not just the differential amount.
Medium SCENARIO · Club House Rental | RWA | Taxable Service
How is the rental income of Rs. 60,000 earned from renting the club house to an external party for a wedding reception treated under GST?
A. Exempt because it belongs to the RWA
B. Taxable under GST, as renting of community/club halls to external parties is a taxable supply ✔
C. Exempt if rental is below Rs. 1 lakh
D. Taxable under reverse charge
Explanation: Services provided by an RWA to non-members or renting of its facilities (like club house/hall) to external parties for commercial or social functions are taxable under GST without the benefit of member-related exemptions.
Hard SCENARIO · RWA | Registration Threshold | Aggregate Turnover
If GreenWoods RWA has an aggregate turnover of Rs. 18 lakhs in the financial year from all taxable supplies (including taxable maintenance and hall rental), does it need to register under GST?
A. Yes, if it makes taxable supplies exceeding the threshold ✔
B. No, RWAs are completely exempt from GST registration regardless of turnover
C. Exempt up to Rs. 40 lakhs for goods and services
D. Mandatory registration for all RWAs irrespective of turnover
Explanation: An RWA is a legal entity/body whose aggregate turnover from taxable supplies determines its registration liability under Section 22 of the CGST Act. If aggregate turnover exceeds the threshold limit (Rs. 20 lakhs for services in most states), registration is mandatory.

Paper 3: Taxation · Module 1 · Chapter 6:

Taxation — 55 rows
Easy NORMAL · Time of Supply | Goods | Forward Charge
What is the primary date for determining the time of supply of goods under forward charge where the invoice is issued within the due date specified under Section 31?
A. Date of issue of invoice
B. Date of receipt of payment
C. Earlier of date of issue of invoice or date of receipt of payment ✔
D. Later of date of issue of invoice or date of receipt of payment
Explanation: Under Section 12(2)(a) of the CGST Act, the time of supply of goods under forward charge is the date of issue of invoice or the last date on which the invoice is required to be issued under Section 31, or the date of receipt of payment, whichever is earlier. When the invoice is issued within the due date, it is the earlier of the date of invoice or date of payment.
Medium NORMAL · Time of Supply | Goods | Advances
According to the Notification issued under Section 12(2) of the CGST Act, is the tax on advances received for the supply of GOODS required to be paid at the time of receipt of advance?
A. Yes, tax is payable on all advances received for goods.
B. No, tax on advances received for goods is not required to be paid at the time of receipt; time of supply is governed solely by the invoice date or due date of invoice. ✔
C. Yes, if the advance exceeds Rs. 1,00,000.
D. No, unless the goods are capital goods.
Explanation: Vide Notification No. 66/2017-Central Tax, the Government has specified that registered persons supplying goods (except specified notified cases) do not need to pay GST on advances received. The time of supply for such goods is determined solely based on the invoice issuance date or the last date for issuing the invoice under Section 31.
Medium NORMAL · Time of Supply | Services | Forward Charge
What is the time of supply of services under forward charge, if the invoice is NOT issued within the period prescribed under Section 31?
A. Date of issue of invoice
B. Date of provision of service
C. Earlier of date of provision of service or date of receipt of payment ✔
D. Date of receipt of payment
Explanation: Under Section 13(2)(b) of the CGST Act, if the invoice is not issued within the prescribed period under Section 31, the time of supply of services is the earlier of the date of provision of service or the date of receipt of payment.
Medium NORMAL · Continuous Supply | Goods | Invoice Date
In case of continuous supply of goods where successive statements of accounts or successive payments are involved, when is the invoice required to be issued?
A. Every month end
B. On or before each time each successive statement is issued or each successive payment is received ✔
C. At the end of the financial year
D. Within 30 days of delivery
Explanation: As per Section 31(4), in case of continuous supply of goods, where successive statements of accounts or successive payments are involved, the invoice shall be issued on or before each time each such statement is issued or, as the case may be, each such payment is received.
Hard NORMAL · Time of Supply | Goods | Reverse Charge
Under the reverse charge mechanism (RCM) for supply of goods, what is the time of supply?
A. Date of receipt of goods
B. Date of payment entered in the books of account or debit in bank account, whichever is earlier
C. Date on which the invoice is issued by the supplier
D. Earliest of: date of receipt of goods, date of payment, or date immediately following 30 days from the date of issue of invoice by the supplier ✔
Explanation: Under Section 12(3) for goods under RCM, the time of supply is the earliest of: (a) the date of receipt of goods; or (b) the date of payment; or (c) the date immediately following 30 days from the date of issue of invoice by the supplier.
Hard NORMAL · Time of Supply | Services | Reverse Charge
What is the time of supply of services under the reverse charge mechanism (RCM)?
A. Date of receipt of service
B. Earlier of the date of payment or the date immediately following 60 days from the date of issue of invoice by the supplier ✔
C. Date of issue of invoice by the recipient
D. Date of debit in the bank account of the recipient
Explanation: Under Section 13(3) for services under RCM, the time of supply is the earlier of: (a) the date of payment; or (b) the date immediately following 60 days from the date of issue of invoice by the supplier (or other document in lieu thereof).
Hard NORMAL · Time of Supply | Associated Enterprise | Services
For associated enterprises where the supplier of service is located outside India, what is the time of supply under reverse charge?
A. Date of payment
B. Date of entry in the books of account of the recipient of service or date of payment, whichever is earlier ✔
C. Date of entry in the books of account of the recipient
D. Date of invoice issued by the overseas supplier
Explanation: As per the proviso to Section 13(3), in case of supply of services by an associated enterprise located outside India, the time of supply is the date of entry in the books of account of the recipient of service or the date of payment, whichever is earlier.
Hard NORMAL · Change in Rate of Tax | Payment Date | Section 14
How is the date of receipt of payment determined when there is a change in the rate of tax and the payment is credited to the bank account after 4 working days from the date of change in rate of tax?
A. Date of credit in the bank account
B. Date of entry in the books of account
C. Date of receipt is the date of credit in the bank account ✔
D. Date of receipt is the date of debit in the buyer's account
Explanation: As per Section 14, if there is a change in the rate of tax and the payment is credited in the bank account after 4 working days from the date of change in rate of tax, the date of receipt of payment shall be the date of credit in the bank account.
Hard NORMAL · Change in Rate of Tax | Services | Section 14
Under Section 14 (Change in rate of tax), if services are provided BEFORE the change in rate of tax, and the invoice is issued AND payment is received AFTER the change in rate of tax, what is the time of supply?
A. Date of issue of invoice
B. Date of receipt of payment
C. Earlier of date of invoice or date of payment ✔
D. Date of provision of service
Explanation: Under Section 14(b)(i), when services are provided before the change in rate of tax, and both invoice and payment are received after the change in rate of tax, the time of supply is the earlier of the date of invoice and the date of payment.
Hard NORMAL · Change in Rate of Tax | Services | Section 14
Under Section 14, if services are provided AFTER the change in rate of tax, but the invoice is issued AND payment is received BEFORE the change in rate of tax, what is the time of supply?
A. Date of issue of invoice
B. Date of receipt of payment ✔
C. Earlier of date of invoice or date of payment
D. Date of provision of service
Explanation: Under Section 14(a)(ii), when services are provided after the change in rate of tax, but invoice and payment are both prior to the change, the time of supply is the date of receipt of payment.
Medium NORMAL · Vouchers | Time of Supply
What is the time of supply in case of supply of vouchers exchangeable for goods?
A. Date of issue of voucher, if the supply is identifiable at that point; otherwise, the date of redemption of voucher ✔
B. Always the date of redemption
C. Always the date of issue of voucher
D. Date of receipt of payment for the voucher
Explanation: Under Section 12(4) and 13(4), the time of supply of a voucher is the date of issue of the voucher if the supply is identifiable at that point, and the date of redemption of the voucher in all other cases.
Medium NORMAL · Residual Cases | Time of Supply
When it is not possible to determine the time of supply under the regular provisions, how is it determined under Section 12(5) / 13(5)?
