A. Date on which periodic return is required to be filed ✔
B. Date on which CGST/SGST is actually paid
C. Date of receipt of periodical return or date of assessment
D. Date on which central tax/state tax/integrated tax is paid
Explanation: As per Section 12(5) and 13(5), where it is not possible to determine the time of supply, it shall be the date on which the periodic return is required to be filed, or in any other case, the date on which the tax is paid.
Medium NORMAL · Addition to Value | Interest | Late Fee
What is the time of supply of addition to value in terms of interest, late fee or penalty for delayed payment of consideration?
A. Date when the delay occurs
B. Date when the supplier receives such addition in value ✔
C. Date when the original invoice was issued
D. Date of end of the financial year
Explanation: Under Section 12(6) and 13(6), the time of supply in respect of an addition to value by way of interest, late fee or penalty for delayed payment of consideration is the date on which the supplier receives such addition in value.
Easy NORMAL · Continuous Supply | Services | Invoice Date
For a continuous supply of services, where the due date of payment is ascertainable from the contract, when must the invoice be issued?
A. Every month end
B. On or before the due date of payment ✔
C. Within 30 days of completion of service
D. Whenever payment is received
Explanation: As per Section 31(5), in case of continuous supply of services, where the due date of payment is ascertainable from the contract, the invoice shall be issued on or before each such due date.
Medium NORMAL · Continuous Supply | Services | Invoice
For a continuous supply of services, where the due date of payment is NOT ascertainable from the contract, when must the invoice be issued?
A. On or before the time when the supplier of service receives the payment ✔
B. Within 30 days of completion of each month
C. At the end of the financial year
D. On or before completion of the service
Explanation: As per Section 31(5)(b), where the due date of payment is not ascertainable from the contract for continuous supply of services, the invoice shall be issued on or before the time when the supplier of service receives the payment.
Easy NORMAL · Invoice | Time Limit | Services
In case of supply of services where the invoice is required to be issued within 30 days of supply of service, what is the maximum time limit for a normal taxable person (other than insurance/banking companies)?
A. 15 days
B. 30 days ✔
C. 45 days
D. 60 days
Explanation: As per Section 31(2), a registered person supplying taxable services shall, before or after the provision of service but within a period of 30 days from the date of supply of service, issue a tax invoice.
Easy NORMAL · Invoice | Banking | Time Limit
What is the time limit for issuing an invoice in case of banking companies, financial institutions, or NBFCs supplying taxable services?
A. 30 days from the date of supply
B. 45 days from the date of supply ✔
C. 60 days from the date of supply
D. 90 days from the date of supply
Explanation: As per Rule 47 of CGST Rules, insurers, banking companies, financial institutions, and NBFCs are allowed 45 days from the date of supply of service to issue an invoice.
Medium NORMAL · Approval Basis | Goods | Invoice
When goods are sent on approval or sale or return basis, before or at the time of supply or within 6 months from the date of removal, whichever is earlier, when should the invoice be issued?
A. At the time of supply / when it becomes known that supply has taken place, or 6 months from removal, whichever is earlier ✔
B. At the end of every month
C. Within 30 days of removal
D. Only when payment is received
Explanation: As per Section 31(7), where goods are sent on approval for sale or return, the invoice shall be issued before or at the time when it becomes known that the supply has taken place, or six months from the date of removal, whichever is earlier.
Medium NORMAL · Excess Payment | Time of Supply
What is the time of supply of goods in case of excess payment of up to Rs. 1,000 where the supplier chooses to take the date of communication of invoice / receipt of excess amount?
A. Date of issue of invoice for such excess amount ✔
B. Date of original invoice
C. Date of receipt of payment
D. Date of entry in books
Explanation: As per the second proviso to Section 12(2) / Rule 50, where the payment is received in excess of the invoice amount up to Rs. 1,000, the time of supply for such excess amount shall, at the option of the supplier, be the date of issue of invoice for such excess amount.
Easy NORMAL · Section 12(2) | Goods | Forward Charge
Which section of the CGST Act governs the time of supply of goods under forward charge?
A. Section 12(1)
B. Section 12(2) ✔
C. Section 13(2)
D. Section 14
Explanation: Section 12(2) of the CGST Act, 2017 governs the time of supply of goods under forward charge.
Easy NORMAL · Section 13(2) | Services | Forward Charge
Which section of the CGST Act governs the time of supply of services under forward charge?
A. Section 12(2)
B. Section 13(1)
C. Section 13(2) ✔
D. Section 14
Explanation: Section 13(2) of the CGST Act, 2017 governs the time of supply of services under forward charge.
Medium NORMAL · Time of Supply | Goods | Practical
If a supplier of goods issues an invoice on 10th May for goods removed on 5th May, and payment is received on 1st June, what is the time of supply under forward charge?
A. 5th May
B. 10th May ✔
C. 1st June
D. 15th May
Explanation: For goods under forward charge, time of supply is earlier of invoice date (10th May) or last date for issuing invoice (5th May). Since invoice is issued on 10th May, which is within the due date, the time of supply is 10th May. (Note: As per Notification No. 66/2017-CT, payment date is irrelevant for goods under forward charge).
Medium NORMAL · Time of Supply | Services | Practical
In the case of supply of services, if the invoice is issued on 10th October for services completed on 1st October, and payment is credited to the bank account on 5th October, what is the time of supply?
A. 1st October
B. 5th October ✔
C. 10th October
D. 12th October
Explanation: For services under forward charge, time of supply is earlier of invoice date (10th Oct) or payment date (5th Oct), assuming invoice is issued within the due date (30 days). Comparing 10th Oct and 5th Oct, the earlier is 5th October.
Easy NORMAL · Liability | Section 12(1) | Goods
When does the liability to pay GST on goods arise under forward charge?
A. At the time of registration
B. At the time of supply of goods determined under Section 12 ✔
C. At the time of filing annual return
D. At the time of physical delivery of goods
Explanation: Section 12(1) states that the liability to pay central/state tax on goods shall arise at the time of supply as determined in accordance with the provisions of Section 12.
Easy NORMAL · Liability | Section 13(1) | Services
When does the liability to pay GST on services arise under forward charge?
A. At the time of raising a purchase order
B. At the time of supply of services determined under Section 13 ✔
C. At the time of receipt of payment
D. At the time of entering into a contract
Explanation: Section 13(1) states that the liability to pay central/state tax on services shall arise at the time of supply as determined in accordance with the provisions of Section 13.
Medium NORMAL · E-Commerce | Time of Supply
In a case where goods are supplied through e-commerce operator where TCS is required to be collected, does this alter the basic provisions of time of supply of goods?
A. Yes, time of supply is postponed to TCS deposit date
B. No, time of supply is determined as per normal provisions of Section 12 ✔
C. Yes, time of supply is the date of order placement
D. Yes, time of supply is the date of delivery by ECO
Explanation: E-commerce provisions (TCS under Section 52) do not alter the fundamental time of supply rules under Section 12, which continue to apply based on invoice and payment rules.
Hard NORMAL · Registration | Time of Supply
What is the relevant date for determining the time of supply when a person is newly registered and liability arises under Section 18 / continuous transition?
A. Date of grant of registration
B. Date of supply of goods or services ✔
C. Date of application for registration
D. Date of physical verification
Explanation: The time of supply is governed by Section 12 and 13 respectively based on the underlying transaction dates (invoice, payment, provision of service), irrespective of the registration status at the exact micro-moment, subject to specific transitional provisions if any.
Hard NORMAL · Change in Rate of Tax | Section 14
Under Section 14, if services are provided AFTER the change in rate of tax, and the invoice is issued AFTER the change in rate of tax, but payment is received BEFORE the change in rate of tax, what is the time of supply?
A. Date of receipt of payment ✔
B. Date of issue of invoice
C. Date of provision of service
D. Earlier of invoice or payment
Explanation: Under Section 14(a)(i), when services are provided after the change in rate of tax and invoice is issued after the change, but payment is received before the change in rate of tax, the time of supply is the date of receipt of payment.
Hard NORMAL · Change in Rate of Tax | Bank Credit | Section 14
Can the date of receipt of payment be the date when the payment is entered in the books of account even if it is credited to the bank account later, outside the 4-day window for rate change scenarios?
A. Yes, always
B. No, for change in rate of tax, specific rules under Section 14 regarding bank credit apply if credit is after 4 working days ✔
C. Only for goods
D. Only for services under RCM
Explanation: Under Section 14, when there is a change in the rate of tax, the date of receipt of payment is specifically deemed to be the date of credit in the bank account if such credit happens after 4 working days from the date of change in rate of tax, overriding book entry date.
Medium NORMAL · Time of Supply | Goods | Exclusion of Payment
Which of the following dates is NOT a component in determining time of supply of goods under forward charge?
A. Date of issue of invoice
B. Last date on which invoice is required to be issued under Section 31
C. Date of receipt of payment ✔
D. Date of removal of goods
Explanation: Vide Notification No. 66/2017-CT, the date of receipt of payment is excluded from determining the time of supply of goods under forward charge. The components are invoice date, last date for invoice, and removal date (indirectly via Section 31 due date).
CASE SCENARIO: M/s Alpha Enterprises, a registered supplier of machinery, sold a specialized industrial machine to M/s Beta Ltd. The machine was removed from the factory of Alpha Enterprises on 10th August. The tax invoice was issued on 15th August. M/s Beta Ltd. made the full payment by a cheque which was handed over on 18th August and credited to Alpha's bank account on 22nd August. The due date for issuing the invoice under Section 31 was 10th August.
Medium SCENARIO · Invoice Date | Goods | Section 31
What is the last date for issuing the tax invoice for the supply of machinery under Section 31?
A. 10th August ✔
B. 15th August
C. 18th August
D. 22nd August
Explanation: As per Section 31(1) of the CGST Act, in case of supply of goods, the invoice must be issued on or before the time of removal of goods for supply or delivery. Since goods were removed on 10th August, the last date for issuing the invoice is 10th August.
Medium SCENARIO · Invoice Date | Due Date | Goods
Was the invoice issued within the due date prescribed under Section 31 in this case?
A. Yes
B. No ✔
C. Yes, because it was issued within 30 days
D. Not applicable
Explanation: The goods were removed on 10th August, making 10th August the due date for the invoice. However, the invoice was issued on 15th August, which is after the due date.
Hard SCENARIO · Time of Supply | Goods | Section 12(2)
What is the time of supply of the machinery under forward charge for M/s Alpha Enterprises?
A. 10th August ✔
B. 15th August
C. 18th August
D. 22nd August
Explanation: Under Section 12(2)(b), if the invoice is NOT issued within the due date under Section 31, the time of supply is the earlier of the date of removal of goods (which precedes or equals the due date of invoice) or date of payment. Here, removal / last date of invoice was 10th August, and payment date was 18th/22nd August. Thus, the time of supply is 10th August.
Hard SCENARIO · Time of Supply | Goods | Forward Charge
If the invoice had been issued on 8th August instead of 15th August, what would be the time of supply?
A. 8th August ✔
B. 10th August
C. 18th August
D. 22nd August
Explanation: Under Section 12(2)(a), when the invoice is issued within the due date (8th August is on or before 10th August), the time of supply is the date of issue of the invoice, which is 8th August. (Payment date is ignored for goods under forward charge per Notification No. 66/2017-CT).
CASE SCENARIO: M/s Delta Consultants, a registered firm of management consultants, provided advisory services to M/s Omega Corp. The services were completed on 12th September. M/s Delta Consultants issued the tax invoice on 5th October. M/s Omega Corp made an advance payment of Rs. 50,000 on 1st September and the balance payment on 10th October.
Medium SCENARIO · Invoice Date | Services | Section 31
What is the last date for issuing the tax invoice for the advisory services under Section 31?
A. 12th September
B. 1st October
C. 12th October ✔
D. 5th October
Explanation: As per Section 31(2) read with Rule 47, a tax invoice for services must be issued within 30 days from the date of supply of service. Services were completed on 12th September; hence, 30 days expire on 12th October.
Medium SCENARIO · Invoice Date | Time Limit | Services
Was the invoice issued within the prescribed time limit under Section 31?
A. Yes, it was issued on 5th October, which is within 30 days of 12th September. ✔
B. No, it was delayed.
C. Yes, because it was issued before final payment.
D. No, invoices for services must be issued on the same day.
Explanation: Since the services were completed on 12th September, the due date for the invoice was 12th October. The invoice issued on 5th October is well within the 30-day limit.
Hard SCENARIO · Time of Supply | Services | Advances
What is the time of supply for the advance payment of Rs. 50,000 received on 1st September?
A. 1st September ✔
B. 12th September
C. 5th October
D. 12th October
Explanation: Under Section 13(2)(a), for services, if the invoice is issued within the prescribed period, the time of supply is the earlier of invoice date or payment date. For the advance received on 1st September, the payment date (1st September) precedes the invoice date (5th October). Thus, time of supply for the advance is 1st September.
Hard SCENARIO · Time of Supply | Services | Forward Charge
What is the time of supply for the balance payment received on 10th October?
A. 12th September
B. 5th October ✔
C. 10th October
D. 12th October
Explanation: For the balance payment, the payment date is 10th October, while the invoice date is 5th October. Since the invoice was issued within the due date, the time of supply is the earlier of invoice date (5th October) or payment date (10th October), which is 5th October.
CASE SCENARIO: M/s Gamma Logistics (a GTA) provided goods transport agency services to M/s Paramount Ltd. (a registered body corporate liable to pay tax under RCM). The date of provision of service was 10th November. M/s Gamma Logistics issued the invoice on 15th November. M/s Paramount Ltd. made the payment on 20th December, and the goods transport receipt was entered in its books on 18th November.
Medium SCENARIO · RCM | GTA | Services
Under which mechanism is the GST payable on the GTA service provided by M/s Gamma Logistics to M/s Paramount Ltd.?
A. Forward Charge
B. Reverse Charge Mechanism (RCM) ✔
C. E-commerce Operator mechanism
D. Exempted supply
Explanation: GTA services provided to a registered body corporate like M/s Paramount Ltd. are taxable under Reverse Charge Mechanism (RCM) under Section 9(3) / 9(4) of the CGST Act.
Medium SCENARIO · Invoice Date | GTA
What is the date of issue of invoice by the supplier in this scenario?
A. 10th November
B. 15th November ✔
C. 18th November
D. 20th December
Explanation: The question explicitly states that M/s Gamma Logistics issued the invoice on 15th November.
Hard SCENARIO · Time of Supply | RCM | Calculation
What is the date immediately following 60 days from the date of issue of invoice by the supplier?
A. 14th January
B. 15th January ✔
C. 16th January
D. 18th January
Explanation: Invoice date is 15th November. November has 30 days (remaining days = 15). December has 31 days. January has 14 days (15 + 31 + 14 = 60 days). The date immediately following 60 days is 15th January.
Hard SCENARIO · Time of Supply | RCM | Services
What is the time of supply of service for M/s Paramount Ltd. under RCM?
A. 10th November
B. 15th November
C. 18th November ✔
D. 20th December
Explanation: Under Section 13(3) for RCM on services, time of supply is earlier of payment date (20th December) or the date immediately following 60 days from invoice (15th January). Wait! Let's re-check the options. Payment is 20th December, 60 days + 1 = 15th January. Earlier is 20th December. But wait, is there an earlier date? Let's check entry in books: 18th November. For RCM services, is books entry a trigger? No, Section 13(3) triggers are payment or 61st day from invoice. Wait, payment is 20th December. 61st day is 15th January. Between 20th December and 15th January, earlier is 20th December. Let's re-evaluate the options provided: (A) 10th Nov, (B) 15th Nov, (C) 18th Nov, (D) 20th Dec. Thus, 20th December is correct.
CASE SCENARIO: A notification was issued changing the rate of tax on a particular category of taxable services from 12% to 18% with effect from 1st October. M/s Zenith Ltd. provided these services and completed them on 20th September. Zenith Ltd. issued the invoice on 5th October. The payment for the services was credited to Zenith's bank account on 28th September.
Medium SCENARIO · Change in Rate of Tax | Services
When was the service provided in relation to the date of change in rate of tax?
A. Before the change in rate of tax ✔
B. After the change in rate of tax
C. Simultaneous with the change in rate of tax
D. Not determinable
Explanation: The service was completed on 20th September, while the rate change occurred on 1st October. Hence, the service was provided before the change in rate of tax.
Medium SCENARIO · Change in Rate of Tax | Invoice Date
When was the invoice issued in relation to the date of change in rate of tax?
A. Before the change in rate of tax
B. After the change in rate of tax ✔
C. On the date of change
D. None of the above
Explanation: The invoice was issued on 5th October, which is after the rate change date of 1st October.
Medium SCENARIO · Change in Rate of Tax | Payment Date
When was the payment received in relation to the date of change in rate of tax?
A. Before the change in rate of tax ✔
B. After the change in rate of tax
C. On the date of change
D. Not applicable
Explanation: The payment was credited to the bank account on 28th September, which is before the rate change date of 1st October.
Hard SCENARIO · Section 14 | Change in Rate of Tax | Time of Supply
What is the time of supply of service and consequently the applicable tax rate under Section 14?
A. 28th September; rate is 12% ✔
B. 5th October; rate is 18%
C. 20th September; rate is 12%
D. 1st October; rate is 18%
Explanation: Under Section 14(b)(ii), when services are provided before the change in rate of tax, and payment is received before the change but invoice is issued after the change, the time of supply is the date of receipt of payment (28th September). Therefore, the applicable tax rate is the pre-revision rate of 12%.
CASE SCENARIO: M/s Apex Traders sells gift vouchers of various denominations to customers. On 15th June, Apex Traders sold a specific voucher worth Rs. 5,000 redeemable against purchase of specific electronic appliances (specifically, washing machines). The customer redeemed this voucher on 10th August to purchase a washing machine. Separately, on 20th June, Apex sold a generic gift voucher worth Rs. 2,000 redeemable against any store merchandise, which was redeemed on 5th September.
Medium SCENARIO · Vouchers | Identifiable Supply
Is the supply identifiable at the time of issuance of the specific voucher sold on 15th June?
A. Yes, because it is redeemable against specific electronic appliances (washing machines). ✔
B. No, it is a generic voucher.
C. Only upon redemption.
D. Never identifiable.
Explanation: Since the voucher is redeemable against a specific category of goods (washing machines), the supply is identifiable at the point of issuance of the voucher.
Hard SCENARIO · Vouchers | Time of Supply | Section 12(4)
What is the time of supply for the specific voucher sold on 15th June?
A. 15th June (Date of issue) ✔
B. 10th August (Date of redemption)
C. 20th June
D. 5th September
Explanation: As per Section 12(4)(a) / 13(4)(a), if the supply is identifiable at the point of issuance, the time of supply of the voucher is the date of issue of the voucher, which is 15th June.
Medium SCENARIO · Vouchers | Generic Vouchers
Is the supply identifiable at the time of issuance of the generic voucher sold on 20th June?
A. Yes, it is identifiable.
B. No, because it can be redeemed against any store merchandise (non-identifiable at issuance). ✔
C. Yes, because the value is fixed at Rs. 2,000.
D. Not applicable.
Explanation: A generic voucher that can be applied to any store merchandise does not point to a specific supply at the time of its issuance; hence, the supply is not identifiable at issuance.
Hard SCENARIO · Vouchers | Redemption | Time of Supply
What is the time of supply for the generic voucher sold on 20th June?
A. 20th June (Date of issue)
B. 5th September (Date of redemption) ✔
C. 15th June
D. 10th August
Explanation: As per Section 12(4)(b) / 13(4)(b), where the supply is not identifiable at the point of issuance, the time of supply of the voucher is the date of redemption of the voucher, which is 5th September.

Paper 3: Taxation · Module 1 · Chapter 7:

Taxation — 55 rows
Easy NORMAL · Transaction Value | Section 15(1) | Sole Consideration
What is the primary basis for determining the value of a taxable supply under Section 15(1) of the CGST Act, 2017 when the supplier and recipient are not related and price is the sole consideration?
A. Market value of the goods or services
B. Transaction value, which is the price actually paid or payable ✔
C. Cost of production plus 10% markup
D. Wholesale price index adjusted value
Explanation: According to Section 15(1) of the CGST Act, 2017, the value of a supply of goods or services shall be the transaction value, which is the price actually paid or payable for the said supply, provided the supplier and the recipient are not related and price is the sole consideration.
Easy NORMAL · Section 15(2) | Incidental Expenses | Additions to Value
Which of the following components must be ADDED to the price actually paid or payable to arrive at the value of supply under Section 15(2)?
A. Any discount given after the supply has been effected, if known beforehand
B. Incidental expenses charged by the supplier up to the time of delivery of goods ✔
C. Central GST and State GST charged separately on the invoice
D. Subsidies received from a non-government individual
Explanation: Under Section 15(2)(c), any amount that the supplier is liable to pay in relation to such supply but which has been incurred by the recipient of the supply and not included in the price actually paid or payable, and incidental expenses charged by the supplier up to the time of delivery, must be added to the transaction value.
Medium NORMAL · Section 15(2)(a) | Taxes and Duties | Value Inclusions
Under Section 15(2)(a), which of the following taxes, duties, cesses, and fees are to be included in the value of supply?
A. CGST, SGST, UTGST, and IGST
B. GST Compensation Cess
C. All taxes, duties, cesses, and fees levied under any law FOR THE TIME BEING IN FORCE other than CGST, SGST, UTGST, and IGST ✔
D. Only municipal taxes levied on commercial properties
Explanation: Section 15(2)(a) mandates the inclusion of any taxes, duties, cesses, fees, and charges levied under any law for the time being in force other than the CGST, the SGST, the UTGST, and the IGST, if charged separately by the supplier.
Medium NORMAL · Section 15(2)(d) | Delayed Payment | Interest and Late Fee
Interest, late fee or penalty for delayed payment of any consideration for any supply is treated as part of the value of supply. When should this amount be included in the taxable value?
A. At the time when the invoice for the original supply was issued
B. Only when the supplier actually receives such interest, late fee, or penalty ✔
C. At the end of the financial year in which the delay occurred
D. When the buyer agrees in writing to pay the penalty
Explanation: As per Section 15(2)(d), the value of supply includes interest, late fee or penalty for delayed payment of any consideration. According to the proviso to Section 12/13 and valuation rules, this is taxable in the period in which it is actually received by the supplier.
Easy NORMAL · Section 15(3) | Discounts | Exclusions from Value
When can a discount be EXCLUDED from the value of supply under Section 15(3)(a)?
A. If the discount is given after the supply is completed based on annual turnover targets
B. If the discount is established and agreed upon before or at the time of the supply and specifically linked to relevant invoices ✔
C. If the discount is offered at the sole discretion of the supplier without prior agreement
D. If the discount exceeds 50% of the list price
Explanation: Section 15(3)(a) states that a discount shall not be included in the value of supply if it is given before or at the time of the supply and has been duly recorded in the invoice issued in respect of such supply.
Hard NORMAL · Post-supply Discounts | Section 15(3)(b) | ITC Reversal
A company offers a post-supply discount to its dealers. Under what condition is such post-supply discount deductible from the value of supply under Section 15(3)(b)?
A. It must be known to the dealer at the time of placing the initial order and linked to specific invoices, with the corresponding ITC reversed by the recipient ✔
B. It can be given at any time without any documentation as long as payment is received
C. It must be approved by the jurisdictional Commissioner of Central Tax
D. Post-supply discounts are never deductible under GST
Explanation: Under Section 15(3)(b), post-supply discounts are deductible if established in terms of a pre-existing agreement, linked to specific invoices, and the recipient has reversed the proportional input tax credit attributable to such discount.
Easy NORMAL · Rule 27 | Non-monetary Consideration | CGST Rules
What is the valuation rule applicable when the consideration for a supply is NOT solely in money?
A. Rule 27 of the CGST Rules, 2017 ✔
B. Rule 28 of the CGST Rules, 2017
C. Rule 30 of the CGST Rules, 2017
D. Rule 32 of the CGST Rules, 2017
Explanation: Rule 27 of the CGST Rules, 2017 governs the valuation of taxable supplies where the consideration supplied is not solely in money.
Medium NORMAL · Rule 27 | Sequential Valuation | Open Market Value
Under Rule 27 of the CGST Rules, 2017, if the value of supply cannot be determined by the open market value, what is the next sequential method?
A. Cost of supply plus 10% markup
B. Sum total of consideration in money and such further amount in money as is equivalent to the consideration not in money, if such amount is known ✔
C. Resale price of goods minus 20%
D. Value of like kind and quality
Explanation: As per Rule 27, where the supply is not solely in money, the value shall be: (a) open market value; if not available, (b) sum total of consideration in money and the monetary equivalent of the non-monetary consideration, if known.
Hard NORMAL · Rule 28 | Related Persons | Distinct Persons
How is the value of supply determined between distinct persons or related persons (other than through an agent) under Rule 28 of the CGST Rules, 2017?
A. Always at actual cost of manufacture
B. Open market value; if not available, value of supply of goods/services of like kind and quality; if not available, Rule 30 or Rule 31 ✔
C. At 50% of the MRP printed on the goods
D. At the discretion of the management of the supplier company
Explanation: Rule 28 prescribes the sequential valuation for supplies between distinct/related persons: Open market value -> Value of goods/services of like kind and quality -> Cost-based value (Rule 30) or residual value (Rule 31). (Note: Proviso also allows recipient's ITC eligibility to determine OMV under certain conditions).
Hard NORMAL · Rule 28 Proviso | Further Supply | 90% Rule
In the context of Rule 28, what is the special provision if the goods supplied to a related person are intended for further supply as such by the recipient?
A. Value must be 110% of the manufacturing cost
B. At the option of the supplier, the value may be 90% of the price charged for the supply of goods of like kind and quality by the recipient to his unrelated customer ✔
C. Value must be zero since intra-entity transfers are not taxable
D. Value must be equal to the MRP
Explanation: The first proviso to Rule 28 allows that where the goods are intended for further supply as such by the recipient, the value shall, at the option of the supplier, be an amount equivalent to 90% of the price charged for the supply of goods of like kind and quality supplied by the recipient to his unrelated customer.
Medium NORMAL · Rule 30 | Cost Method | 110% of Cost
What is the valuation method prescribed under Rule 30 (Cost Method) of the CGST Rules, 2017?
A. 100% of the direct material cost
B. 110% of the cost of production or manufacture or the cost of acquisition of such goods or the cost of provision of such services ✔
C. Cost of production plus 15% profit margin
D. Book value as per audited balance sheet
Explanation: Rule 30 stipulates that where the value of a supply cannot be determined under Rule 27 or Rule 28, the value shall be 110% of the cost of production/manufacture/acquisition of such goods or cost of provision of such services.
Medium NORMAL · Rule 31 | Residual Method | Reasonable Means
When valuation cannot be ascertained under any of the preceding rules (Rules 27 to 30), what does Rule 31 (Residual Method) require?
A. Supply is exempt from GST
B. Value shall be determined using reasonable means consistent with the principles and general provisions of Section 15 ✔
C. Value shall be determined by a chartered accountant certificate only
D. Value shall be deemed to be zero
Explanation: Rule 31 provides that where the value of supply of goods or services cannot be determined under rules 27 to 30, the same shall be determined using reasonable means consistent with the principles and general provisions of Section 15 and the provisions of Chapter IV.
Medium NORMAL · Rule 32(5) | Second-hand Goods | Margin Scheme
What is the special valuation rule under Rule 32(5) for second-hand goods sold by a dealer who deals in buying and selling second-hand goods?
A. GST is payable on the total sale price
B. Value of supply is the difference between the selling price and the purchase price, and if the margin is negative, it is ignored ✔
C. GST is exempted on all second-hand goods
D. Value of supply is 50% of the purchase price
Explanation: Under Rule 32(5), where a taxable person supplies second-hand goods after minor processing that does not change their nature, the value of supply shall be the difference between the selling price and the purchase price. If the margin is negative, it is ignored.
Hard NORMAL · Rule 32(2) | Foreign Currency | Forex Conversion
How is the taxable value determined under Rule 32(2)(a) for a foreign exchange (forex) conversion service where one of the currencies exchanged is Indian Rupees (INR)?
A. Difference between buying rate/selling rate and RBI reference rate, multiplied by total units ✔
B. 1% of the gross amount of Indian Rupees provided
C. Total commission charged by the bank
D. RBI reference rate multiplied by the exchange rate
Explanation: Under Rule 32(2)(a), for currency conversion where one currency is INR, the value is the difference between the buying rate or selling rate and the Reserve Bank of India (RBI) reference rate for that day, multiplied by the total units of currency.
Hard NORMAL · Rule 32(4) | Life Insurance | Insurance Valuation
For life insurance business, what is the value of supply under Rule 32(4) in case of an annuity policy where policy allocation is for investments/savings?
A. Gross premium charged from the policyholder
B. Actual amount allocated for investments/savings if intimated to the policyholder
C. 25% of the premium charged in the first year and 12.5% in subsequent years ✔
D. 10% of the gross premium charged
Explanation: Under Rule 32(4)(a), in case of life insurance where the policyholder's fund is managed, the value is the single premium charged minus the amount allocated for investment/savings (if intimated). For other policies, it is 25% of premium in year 1 and 12.5% in subsequent years (or 10% for single premium annuity).
Hard NORMAL · Rule 32(3) | Travel Agent | Air Travel Booking
What is the taxable value of supply for services provided by a travel agent in relation to booking of tickets for air travel under Rule 32(3)?
A. 10% of the basic air fare for domestic bookings and 15% for international bookings ✔
B. 5% of the basic fare for domestic bookings and 10% for international bookings
C. Actual commission received from the airline
D. Total ticket price paid by the customer
Explanation: As per Rule 32(3), the value of supply of services in relation to air travel booking by a travel agent shall be 5% of the basic fare in case of domestic bookings and 10% in case of international bookings. (Note: Basic fare means that part of the air fare on which commission is normally earned).
Medium NORMAL · Rule 33 | Pure Agent | Exclusion of Expenses
Under Rule 33, what expenses incurred by a pure agent can be EXCLUDED from the value of supply?
A. All overhead expenses incurred by the supplier during the execution of the contract
B. Expenditure incurred by the supplier as a pure agent of the recipient of supply, subject to specified conditions ✔
C. Transportation and handling charges incurred by the supplier up to the buyer's premises
D. Cost of raw materials supplied by third party subcontractors
Explanation: Rule 33 allows the exclusion of expenditure incurred by a supplier as a pure agent of the recipient of supply, provided conditions such as separate billing, no holding of goods for self, and actual reimbursement are satisfied.
Medium NORMAL · Rule 33 | Pure Agent Conditions | Exclusions
Which of the following conditions is NOT mandatory for qualifying as a 'pure agent' under Rule 33?
A. The supplier acts as a pure agent of the recipient of supply, when he makes payment to the third party for the goods or services procured
B. The supplier holds title to the goods and uses them for his own business operations ✔
C. The supply of service procured by the pure agent is in addition to the primary services he provides on his own account
D. The recovery is separately indicated in the invoice issued by the pure agent
Explanation: Holding title to the goods and using them for own business operations disqualifies a person from being a pure agent. A pure agent does not hold title to the goods or services procured and only acts on authorization.
Medium NORMAL · Vouchers | Coupons | Redeemable Value
How is the value of supply determined in cases where a coupon, voucher, or stamp (other than postage stamp) is redeemable against a supply of goods or services?
A. Face value of the voucher
B. Value of the goods or services redeemable against such voucher ✔
C. Zero, until the voucher is actually redeemed
D. Cost of printing the voucher
Explanation: Section 15 read with general principles establishes that the value of supply of a token, voucher, coupon, or stamp (other than postage stamp) that is redeemable against a supply of goods or services is equal to the money value of the goods or services redeemable against such voucher.
Easy NORMAL · Packing Charges | Section 15(2)(c) | Incidental Expenses
In determining the value of supply, packing charges levied by the supplier separately in the invoice are:
A. Deductible from the transaction value
B. Includible in the value of supply ✔
C. Exempt from GST entirely
D. Taxable only if they exceed 5% of the goods value
Explanation: Packing charges (whether incidental or otherwise up to delivery) are specifically includible in the value of supply under Section 15(2)(c) as incidental expenses incurred by the supplier in respect of the supply.
Medium NORMAL · Post-supply Discounts | Section 15(3)(b) | Ineligibility
Can a discount given AFTER the supply has been effected be deducted from the value of supply if it was NOT linked to any pre-existing agreement or invoice?
A. Yes, provided the recipient reverses the ITC
B. No, because post-supply discounts not known at or before supply and not linked to invoices are not deductible under Section 15(3)(b) ✔
C. Yes, up to a maximum limit of 10% of turnover
D. Yes, if approved by the GST Council
Explanation: Section 15(3)(b) explicitly requires that post-supply discounts must be established in terms of an agreement entered into before or at the time of such supply and specifically linked to relevant invoices. If not, they cannot be deducted.
Hard NORMAL · Section 15(2)(b) | Municipal Taxes | Rental Supply
What is the valuation treatment of municipal taxes paid by the tenant on behalf of the landlord directly to the municipality, where such tax liability is legally that of the landlord?
A. It is excluded from the value of supply of rental service
B. It is included in the value of supply of rental service as it represents consideration paid to a third party on behalf of the supplier ✔
C. It is treated as a pure supply of municipal service and taxed at 0%
D. It is deducted from the monthly rent
Explanation: Under Section 15(2)(b), any amount that the supplier is liable to pay in relation to such supply but which has been incurred by the recipient of the supply forms part of the value of supply. Since property tax is the statutory liability of the landlord (supplier), its payment by the tenant is added to the rental value.
Hard NORMAL · Rule 31A | Railways | Special Valuation
Which of the following provisions governs the valuation of services of booking/cancellation of tickets by an agent of Indian Railways?
A. Rule 32(3)
B. Rule 31A ✔
C. Rule 32(5)
D. Rule 27
Explanation: Rule 31A specifically deals with the value of supply in relation to lottery, betting, gambling, and horse racing, while Rule 32(3) specifically covers air travel agents. (Note: Indian Railways ticket booking agent value is governed by Rule 31A / specific trade circulars as applicable under Rule 32 provisions).
Hard NORMAL · Rule 31A | Lottery | State Government Lottery
How is the value of supply determined for a lottery run by a State Government?
A. 100/112 of the face value of the ticket or the price notified in the Official Gazette, whichever is higher ✔
B. 100/128 of the face value of the ticket or the price notified in the Official Gazette, whichever is higher
C. Actual collections minus prize payouts
D. Face value of the ticket excluding GST
Explanation: Under Rule 31A(2), the value of supply of lottery run by a State Government shall be 100/112 of the face value of the ticket or of the price notified in the Official Gazette, whichever is higher.
Hard NORMAL · Rule 31A | Authorized Lottery | Private Organizer
What is the value of supply of lottery authorized by a State Government (private organizer)?
A. 100/128 of the face value of the ticket or the price notified in the Official Gazette, whichever is higher ✔
B. 100/112 of the face value of the ticket
C. Gross collections from ticket sales
D. 50% of the face value
Explanation: Under Rule 31A(2), the value of supply of lottery authorized by a State Government is 100/128 of the face value of the ticket or of the price notified in the Official Gazette, whichever is higher.
Hard NORMAL · Rule 32(2) | RBI Reference Rate Missing | Forex Valuation
In the case of foreign exchange transactions, if the RBI reference rate is not available on that day, how is the value determined under Rule 32(2)(a)?
A. 1% of the gross amount of currency exchanged
B. The value shall be 1% of the gross amount of Indian Rupees provided or received ✔
C. The buying rate and selling rate are averaged
D. Exchange rate published by IMF
Explanation: As per the proviso to Rule 32(2)(a), where the RBI reference rate is not available for a currency on a given day, the value shall be 1% of the gross amount of Indian Rupees provided or received by the person converting the money.
Medium NORMAL · Section 15(2)(e) | Subsidies | Non-Government Subsidies
Can subsidies directly linked to the price, received from a Non-Government NGO, be excluded from the value of supply under Section 15?
A. Yes, all subsidies are excluded
B. No, only subsidies provided by the Central Government and State Governments are excluded from the value of supply ✔
C. Yes, if approved by the supplier's board
D. No, subsidies can never be excluded
Explanation: Under Section 15(2)(e), subsidies directly linked to the price shall be included in the value of supply, *except* subsidies provided by the Central Government and State Governments. Hence, subsidies from NGOs are included.
Easy NORMAL · Section 15(3)(a) | Trade Discount | Invoice Level Discount
A supplier offers a 20% trade discount on goods at the time of supply and records it correctly on the invoice. How should this discount be treated?
A. It must be added back to the invoice value for tax calculation
B. It is excluded from the value of supply, and GST is levied only on the net discounted price ✔
C. It is treated as a subsidy and taxed separately
D. It is deductible only if the buyer pays within 7 days
Explanation: Under Section 15(3)(a), discounts given before or at the time of supply and recorded in the invoice are excluded from the value of supply. GST is charged on the net value after deducting such discount.
Hard NORMAL · Rule 30 | Cost of Production | Exclusions from Cost
Which of the following items is EXCLUDED from the cost of production when applying Rule 30 (Cost Method)?
A. Direct material and direct wages
B. Direct expenses and factory overheads
C. GST paid on the procurement of inputs used in the manufacture of goods ✔
D. Administrative overheads directly attributable to production
Explanation: In determining the cost of production/manufacture under Rule 30, input tax credit (ITC) available in respect of inputs or input services is not part of the cost borne by the taxpayer; moreover, CGST/SGST/IGST paid are taxes, not production costs.
Medium NORMAL · Credit Note | Time Limit | Post-supply Discount
What is the timeline for issuance of credit notes under GST for post-supply discounts so that the supplier can reduce their output tax liability?
A. Any time before the end of the financial year
B. Up to 30th November following the end of the financial year in which such supply was made, or the date of furnishing of the relevant annual return, whichever is earlier ✔
C. Within 180 days from the date of supply
D. There is no time limit specified in the GST law
Explanation: Under Section 34 read with Section 15(3)(b), a credit note for post-supply discount must be issued and declared up to 30th November following the end of the financial year in which such supply was made, or the date of furnishing of the relevant annual return, whichever is earlier.
CASE SCENARIO: M/s. Apex Machines Ltd. manufactures industrial machinery in Mumbai. They sell a specialized lathe machine to M/s. Beta Enterprises in Pune for an agreed invoice price of Rs. 10,00,000 (exclusive of taxes). The following additional costs are incurred in relation to the supply: (i) Municipal tax levied on the factory premises amounting to Rs. 25,000, paid by Beta Enterprises on behalf of Apex Machines Ltd.; (ii) Loading and handling charges incurred up to the delivery site amounting to Rs. 15,000; (iii) Inspection charges mandated by the buyer before delivery, paid directly by Beta Enterprises amounting to Rs. 10,000; (iv) Apex Machines Ltd. offers a 2% trade discount on the basic price as it was pre-agreed and recorded in the invoice. Beta Enterprises delays payment beyond the stipulated 30 days and pays interest of Rs. 12,000 in a subsequent month.
Medium SCENARIO · Section 15(3)(a) | Trade Discount | Scenario Valuation
What is the net basic price after considering the pre-agreed trade discount under Section 15(3)(a)?
A. Rs. 10,00,000
B. Rs. 9,80,000 ✔
C. Rs. 9,75,000
D. Rs. 9,50,000
Explanation: A pre-agreed trade discount of 2% on Rs. 10,00,000 amounts to Rs. 20,000. Under Section 15(3)(a), this discount is excluded from the value of supply, leaving a net price of Rs. 9,80,000.
Medium SCENARIO · Section 15(2)(b) | Recipient Liability | Addition to Value
How should the municipal tax of Rs. 25,000 paid by the recipient (Beta Enterprises) on behalf of the supplier be treated under Section 15?
A. Ignored as it is a local tax
B. Added to the value of supply under Section 15(2)(b) ✔
C. Deducted from the transaction value
D. Taxes separately under Reverse Charge Mechanism
Explanation: Under Section 15(2)(b), any amount that the supplier is liable to pay in relation to the supply but incurred by the recipient and not included in the price must be added to the value of supply.
Hard SCENARIO · Total Value of Supply | Section 15 Calculation | Incidental Expenses
What is the total value of supply (excluding the delayed payment interest) for the lathe machine transaction?
A. Rs. 10,00,000
B. Rs. 10,20,000
C. Rs. 10,30,000 ✔
D. Rs. 10,42,000
Explanation: Calculation: Net price after discount = Rs. 9,80,000 + Municipal tax paid by buyer (Sec 15(2)(b)) = Rs. 25,000 + Loading/handling charges (Sec 15(2)(c)) = Rs. 15,000 + Inspection charges paid by buyer (Sec 15(2)(c)) = Rs. 10,000. Total = 9,80,000 + 25,000 + 15,000 + 10,000 = Rs. 10,30,000.
Medium SCENARIO · Section 15(2)(d) | Delayed Payment Interest | Time of Supply
When is the interest of Rs. 12,000 received for delayed payment taxable under GST?
A. At the time of supply of the lathe machine
B. At the time when the interest is actually received by Apex Machines Ltd. ✔
C. At the end of the financial year
D. It is exempt from GST
Explanation: As per the proviso to Section 12/13 and Section 15(2)(d), interest, late fee, or penalty for delayed payment is taxable in the tax period in which it is actually received by the supplier.
CASE SCENARIO: M/s. Radiant Electronics, a registered dealer, supplies smart TVs to its related corporate entity, M/s. Nebula Retailers, for internal corporate gifting. The manufacturing cost per TV is Rs. 40,000. The open market value of such smart TVs is not readily available. However, identical smart TVs are sold by Radiant Electronics to unrelated wholesale buyers at Rs. 55,000 per unit. Alternatively, Nebula Retailers could also procure similar TVs from another independent manufacturer in the market for Rs. 52,000. Nebula Retailers intends to further supply these TVs *as such* to its independent retail customers at Rs. 60,000.
Medium SCENARIO · Rule 28 | Related Persons | Valuation Rules
Which valuation rule applies primarily to supplies made between related persons such as Radiant Electronics and Nebula Retailers?
A. Rule 27
B. Rule 28 ✔
C. Rule 30
D. Rule 31
Explanation: Rule 28 of the CGST Rules, 2017 prescribes the valuation methods for supplies of goods or services made between distinct persons or related persons.
Medium SCENARIO · Rule 28(a) | Open Market Value | Related Supply
What is the primary value of supply under Rule 28 when supplies are made to a related person, given the facts of the case?
A. Rs. 40,000 (Manufacturing cost)
B. Rs. 55,000 (Open market value / price of goods of like kind and quality to unrelated buyers) ✔
C. Rs. 60,000 (Recipient's retail price)
D. Rs. 44,000 (110% of cost)
Explanation: Under Rule 28(a), the value of supply between related persons shall be the open market value of such supply. Here, the price of goods of like kind and quality supplied to unrelated wholesale buyers is Rs. 55,000.
Hard SCENARIO · Rule 28 Proviso | Further Supply | 90% Rule Option
If Nebula Retailers intends to further supply the goods *as such* to unrelated customers at Rs. 60,000, what optional value can Radiant Electronics adopt under the first proviso to Rule 28?
A. Rs. 54,000 (90% of Rs. 60,000) ✔
B. Rs. 60,000
C. Rs. 44,000 (110% of cost)
D. Rs. 52,000
Explanation: Under the first proviso to Rule 28, where goods are intended for further supply as such by the recipient, the supplier may opt for 90% of the price charged for the supply of goods of like kind and quality by the recipient to his unrelated customer (90% of Rs. 60,000 = Rs. 54,000).
Medium SCENARIO · Rule 28 Fallback | Rule 30 | Cost Method
If neither open market value nor the 90% proviso nor any other Rule 28 criteria can be applied, what fallback method does Rule 28 prescribe before resorting to residual rules?
A. Value shall be deemed to be zero
B. Cost of production plus 10% markup under Rule 30 ✔
C. 50% of the manufacturing cost
D. Book value certified by cost accountant
Explanation: Rule 28 directs that if value cannot be determined under clause (a) or (b) of Rule 28, it shall be determined under Rule 30 (110% of cost of production/manufacture) or Rule 31.
CASE SCENARIO: M/s. Swift Express Logistics acts as a pure agent for its client, M/s. Global Traders. Swift Express Logistics incurred the following expenses on behalf of Global Traders during the month of October: (i) Freight charges paid to transporters amounting to Rs. 50,000; (ii) Municipal octroi charges paid to the municipal corporation amounting to Rs. 5,000; (iii) Packing and sorting charges incurred by Swift Express Logistics in its own warehouse amounting to Rs. 8,000; (iv) Statutory inspection fee paid to the port authority amounting to Rs. 12,000. All out-of-pocket expenses (freight, octroi, and inspection fee) were billed to Global Traders at actuals in separate debit notes along with Swift's own service fee of Rs. 20,000 for logistical coordination.
Medium SCENARIO · Rule 33 | Pure Agent | Exclusions
Which rule governs the exclusion of expenses incurred by a supplier acting as a pure agent from the value of supply?
A. Rule 27
B. Rule 30
C. Rule 32
D. Rule 33 ✔
Explanation: Rule 33 of the CGST Rules, 2017 specifies the conditions and methodology for excluding expenditure incurred by a supplier as a pure agent of the recipient of supply.
Hard SCENARIO · Rule 33 Conditions | Pure Agent Expenses | Exclusion Eligibility
Which of the following expenses incurred by Swift Express Logistics qualifies for exclusion under Rule 33 as a pure agent?
A. Packing and sorting charges of Rs. 8,000
B. Freight charges of Rs. 50,000, municipal octroi of Rs. 5,000, and inspection fee of Rs. 12,000 ✔
C. Logistical coordination service fee of Rs. 20,000
D. None of the expenses qualify
Explanation: Freight, municipal octroi, and port inspection fees were incurred by Swift as a pure agent on behalf of Global Traders, billed at actuals separately, and represent third-party statutory/service liabilities of the client. Packing/sorting charges are the supplier's own operational costs.
Hard SCENARIO · Taxable Value Calculation | Pure Agent Exclusion | Service Fee
What is the taxable value of supply for Swift Express Logistics excluding the pure agent reimbursements?
A. Rs. 20,000 (Service fee only)
B. Rs. 28,000 (Service fee + packing charges) ✔
C. Rs. 95,000 (Gross billing)
D. Rs. 87,000
Explanation: The taxable value includes Swift's own service fee (Rs. 20,000) and its own operational expenses like packing/sorting (Rs. 8,000), totaling Rs. 28,000. Pure agent reimbursements (Rs. 50,000 + Rs. 5,000 + Rs. 12,000) are excluded under Rule 33.
Medium SCENARIO · Pure Agent Definition | Rule 33 Conditions | Title to Goods
Which of the following is NOT a mandatory condition for Swift Express Logistics to be treated as a pure agent under Rule 33?
A. Swift acts as a pure agent of Global Traders when making payment to third parties
B. Swift holds title to the goods procured and uses them for its own consumption ✔
C. The supply of service procured by the pure agent is in addition to the primary service provided
D. The recovery is separately indicated in the invoice
Explanation: Holding title to goods or services and using them for one's own account violates the definition of a pure agent. A pure agent must not hold title to the goods or services procured.
CASE SCENARIO: M/s. Zenith Forex Bureau, a registered person under GST, undertakes currency exchange transactions. During the week, it converts USD 10,000 into Indian Rupees (INR). On that day, the RBI reference rate for USD is Rs. 82.50 per USD. Zenith buys the USD from the customer at an exchange rate of Rs. 82.10 per USD. In another transaction, Zenith converts EUR 5,000 into INR, but the RBI reference rate for EUR is not announced/available on that day. For this EUR transaction, the gross amount of Indian Rupees provided to the customer is Rs. 4,50,000.
Medium SCENARIO · Rule 32(2) | Foreign Currency | Money Changing
Which rule of the CGST Rules, 2017 specifically governs the valuation of supply of foreign exchange services?
A. Rule 32(2) ✔
B. Rule 32(4)
C. Rule 32(5)
D. Rule 33
Explanation: Rule 32(2) of the CGST Rules, 2017 prescribes the special valuation methods for the supply of services in relation to the purchase or sale of foreign currency, including money changing.
Hard SCENARIO · Rule 32(2)(a) | Forex Calculation | RBI Reference Rate
What is the taxable value of supply for the conversion of USD 10,000 under Rule 32(2)(a)?
A. Rs. 8,25,000
B. Rs. 8,21,000
C. Rs. 4,000 ✔
D. Rs. 40,000
Explanation: Under Rule 32(2)(a), when one currency is INR, value = (RBI reference rate - buying rate) * total units = (82.50 - 82.10) * 10,000 = Rs. 0.40 * 10,000 = Rs. 4,000.
Hard SCENARIO · Rule 32(2) Proviso | Missing RBI Rate | Forex Valuation
How is the value of supply determined for the EUR 5,000 transaction where the RBI reference rate is not available on that day?
A. 1% of the gross amount of Indian Rupees provided (1% of Rs. 4,50,000) ✔
B. Difference between buying rate and selling rate
C. 0.5% of the total EUR converted
D. Exempt from GST due to absence of RBI rate
Explanation: As per the proviso to Rule 32(2)(a), where the RBI reference rate is not available, the value shall be 1% of the gross amount of Indian Rupees provided or received (1% of Rs. 4,50,000 = Rs. 4,500).
Hard SCENARIO · Rule 32(2)(b) | Slab-based Valuation | Money Changing Options
What is the alternative method available for valuing foreign exchange transactions under Rule 32(2)(b) if the taxpayer opts for slab-based valuation instead of Rule 32(2)(a)?
A. Fixed percentage of the total transaction value based on tiered slabs of currency converted ✔
B. Flat Rs. 1,000 per transaction
C. 10% of the commission charged
D. Actual gross profit earned
Explanation: Rule 32(2)(b) permits a taxable person to opt for valuation based on slab rates (e.g., 1% up to Rs. 1 lakh, etc.) of the gross amount of currency exchanged, once exercised for a financial year.
CASE SCENARIO: M/s. Vintage Wheels, a registered second-hand car dealer, purchases a pre-owned luxury car from an unregistered individual for Rs. 15,00,000. Vintage Wheels undertakes minor cleaning, denting, and painting costing Rs. 50,000 (which does not alter the fundamental nature of the car) and sells the car to a retail customer for Rs. 18,50,000. In a separate transaction during the same month, Vintage Wheels purchases another old motorcycle for Rs. 40,000 and sells it for Rs. 35,000.
Medium SCENARIO · Rule 32(5) | Second-hand Goods | Margin Scheme Rule
Which specific valuation rule applies to the supply of second-hand goods by a dealer engaged in buying and selling second-hand goods?
A. Rule 32(3)
B. Rule 32(4)
C. Rule 32(5) ✔
D. Rule 33
Explanation: Rule 32(5) of the CGST Rules, 2017 governs the valuation of taxable supplies of second-hand goods dealt in by a registered person after minor processing.
Hard SCENARIO · Rule 32(5) Calculation | Car Margin | Second-hand Valuation
What is the taxable value of supply for the luxury car under Rule 32(5)?
A. Rs. 18,50,000
B. Rs. 15,00,000
C. Rs. 3,50,000 ✔
D. Rs. 3,00,000
Explanation: Under Rule 32(5), the value of supply of second-hand goods is the difference between the selling price and the purchase price (Margin = Selling price Rs. 18,50,000 - Purchase price Rs. 15,00,000 = Rs. 3,50,000). Minor processing costs are ignored in computing the margin.
Medium SCENARIO · Rule 32(5) Proviso | Negative Margin | Second-hand Goods
How is the transaction involving the motorcycle (purchase Rs. 40,000, sale Rs. 35,000) treated for GST purposes under Rule 32(5)?
A. The negative margin of Rs. 5,000 can be set off against the car's positive margin
B. The negative margin of Rs. 5,000 is ignored, and the taxable value for this transaction is nil ✔
C. GST refund is available for the negative margin
D. The purchase price is adjusted to Rs. 35,000
Explanation: The proviso to Rule 32(5) explicitly states that if the margin is negative (selling price is less than purchase price), it shall be ignored and cannot be used to offset margins of other transactions.
Medium SCENARIO · Rule 32(5) Condition | ITC Prohibition | Margin Scheme
What is a mandatory pre-condition for a dealer to adopt the margin scheme under Rule 32(5) for second-hand goods?
A. Input tax credit must have been availed on the purchase of the second-hand goods
B. No input tax credit has been availed on the purchase of such second-hand goods ✔
C. The purchase must be made from a registered manufacturer only
D. The selling price must exceed 200% of the purchase price
Explanation: Rule 32(5) applies only if no input tax credit (ITC) has been availed on the purchase of the second-hand goods from the unregistered supplier or person.

Paper 3: Taxation · Module 2 · Chapter 8:

Taxation — 55 rows
Easy NORMAL · Section 16(2) | Conditions for ITC | Eligibility
Which of the following conditions is NOT mandatory for a registered person to avail Input Tax Credit (ITC) under Section 16(2) of the CGST Act, 2017?
A. Possession of a tax invoice or debit note issued by a registered supplier
B. Receipt of goods or services or both
C. Filing of the annual return by the recipient for the relevant financial year ✔
D. Furnishing of the return under Section 39 by the registered person
Explanation: Section 16(2) prescribes four primary conditions for claiming ITC: possession of tax invoice/debit note, receipt of goods/services, tax charged has been paid to the government, and furnishing of the return under Section 39. Filing of the annual return is not a pre-condition for availing ITC during the financial year.
Medium NORMAL · Section 16(3) | Capital Goods | Depreciation
M/s. ABC Ltd. purchased machinery worth Rs. 10,00,000 (exclusive of GST at 18%) for factory use. The company capitalized the full invoice value including the GST component of Rs. 1,80,000 in its books of accounts and claimed depreciation on the total capitalized amount under the Income-tax Act, 1961. What is the correct position regarding ITC on this machinery?
A. ITC can be claimed fully along with depreciation on the GST component
B. ITC cannot be claimed on the GST component since depreciation has been claimed on it under the Income-tax Act ✔
C. ITC can be claimed up to 50% of the GST amount and depreciation on the remaining 50%
D. ITC can be claimed by reversing the depreciation subsequently within 30 days
Explanation: As per the proviso to Section 16(3) of the CGST Act, 2017, if the registered person has claimed depreciation on the tax component of the cost of capital goods and plant and machinery under the Income-tax Act, 1961, the input tax on the said component shall not be allowed as ITC.
Easy NORMAL · Section 16(4) | Time Limit | ITC Availment
What is the time limit for availing Input Tax Credit under Section 16(4) of the CGST Act, 2017 for any invoice or debit note relating to a financial year?
A. Due date of filing return for the month of September of the subsequent financial year
B. Actual date of filing of the annual return for the relevant financial year or 30th November of the subsequent financial year, whichever is earlier ✔
C. 31st December of the subsequent financial year
D. Actual date of filing of the annual return for the relevant financial year or 30th November of the subsequent financial year, whichever is later
Explanation: Section 16(4) mandates that ITC pertaining to any invoice or debit note can be availed up to the earlier of: (i) the thirtieth day of November following the end of financial year to which such invoice/debit note relates, or (ii) the date of furnishing of the relevant annual return.
Medium NORMAL · Section 16(4) | Time Limit | Invoice Date
An invoice was issued by a supplier on 15th October 2024 for FY 2024-25. Due to an oversight, the recipient did not claim the ITC in time. What is the maximum date up to which the recipient can avail ITC on this invoice, assuming the annual return for FY 2024-25 is filed on 31st December 2025?
A. 30th November 2025 ✔
B. 31st December 2025
C. 15th October 2025
D. 30th September 2025
Explanation: As per Section 16(4), the time limit is the earlier of 30th November of the subsequent financial year (30th November 2025) or the date of filing the annual return (31st December 2025). Thus, 30th November 2025 is the correct date.
Medium NORMAL · Section 16(2) | Goods in Lots | Proviso
When goods are received in lots or installments by a registered person, when can the Input Tax Credit be claimed against the tax invoice?
A. When the first installment of goods is received
B. When the last lot or installment of the goods is received ✔
C. Proportionately as and when each lot or installment is received
D. Only after the invoice is fully paid within 180 days
Explanation: As per the second proviso to Section 16(2), where the goods against an invoice are received in lots or installments, the registered person shall be entitled to take input tax credit upon the receipt of the last lot or installment.
Easy NORMAL · Section 16(2) | Non-payment | 180 Days Rule
If a recipient fails to pay to the supplier the value of goods or services along with the tax payable thereon within what period from the date of issue of invoice, an amount equal to the ITC availed is required to be added to output tax liability along with interest?
A. 90 days
B. 180 days ✔
C. 270 days
D. 365 days
Explanation: As per the second proviso to Section 16(2), if the recipient fails to pay the value of supply plus tax within 180 days from the date of issue of invoice, an amount equal to the ITC availed shall be added to their output tax liability, along with applicable interest.
Medium NORMAL · Section 17(5) | Blocked Credit | Motor Vehicles
Which of the following inward supplies is NOT blocked under Section 17(5) of the CGST Act, 2017?
A. Motor vehicles for transportation of persons having approved seating capacity of not more than 13 persons (including driver), used for general business travel
B. Food and beverages, outdoor catering, beauty treatment, health services, except where outward taxable supply is of the same category
C. Goods or services used for personal consumption
D. Motor vehicles used for transportation of goods ✔
Explanation: Under Section 17(5), motor vehicles for transportation of goods are explicitly excluded from the blocked credit category, meaning ITC is available on them. The other three options represent blocked credits under Section 17(5).
Hard NORMAL · Section 17(5) | Blocked Credit | Exceptions
Under Section 17(5), ITC is available on motor vehicles having a seating capacity of not more than 13 persons (including driver) when they are used for which of the following specified purposes?
A. Transportation of employees to and from workplace as a statutory obligation
B. Further supply of such vehicles, or transportation of passengers, or imparting training on driving such vehicles ✔
C. General conveyance of the Managing Director for business meetings
D. Leasing or renting of vehicles for employee recreation trips
Explanation: Section 17(5)(a) blocks ITC on motor vehicles for transportation of persons <= 13 capacity, except when they are used for making taxable supplies of: (i) further supply of such vehicles; (ii) transportation of passengers; or (iii) imparting training on driving such vehicles.
Medium NORMAL · Rule 42 | Reversal | Common ITC
Rule 42 of the CGST Rules, 2017 deals with the reversal of Input Tax Credit in respect of inputs and input services used for which type of supplies?
A. Exclusively taxable supplies
B. Exclusively exempt supplies
C. Both effected for business purposes and non-business/personal purposes, or partly for taxable and partly for exempt supplies ✔
D. Capital goods used for both taxable and exempt supplies
Explanation: Rule 42 of the CGST Rules, 2017 prescribes the manner of determination of eligible input tax credit in respect of inputs or input services and reversal thereof when used partly for business/non-business or partly for taxable/exempt supplies. Rule 43 deals with capital goods.
Hard NORMAL · Rule 43 | Capital Goods | Useful Life
What is the useful life in quarters considered for calculation of reversal of ITC on capital goods used commonly for taxable and exempt supplies under Rule 43 of the CGST Rules, 2017?
A. 20 quarters (5 years) ✔
B. 60 quarters (15 years)
C. 10 quarters (2.5 years)
D. 36 quarters (9 years)
Explanation: Under Rule 43 of the CGST Rules, 2017, the useful life of any capital goods is taken as 5 years from the date of invoice, which equates to 20 quarters. The common ITC attributable to exempt supplies is calculated on a quarterly pro-rata basis over this period.
Hard NORMAL · Section 18(4) | Composition Scheme | Stock Reversal
When a registered person switches from the regular scheme to the Composition Scheme under Section 10, how must they treat the ITC lying in their electronic credit ledger on the day immediately preceding the date of switch?
A. They can carry forward and utilize the credit against future composition tax liability
B. They must pay an amount equivalent to the credit of input tax in respect of inputs held in stock and inputs contained in semi-finished or finished goods held in stock, and capital goods, by debiting electronic credit or cash ledger ✔
C. The credit automatically lapses and cannot be adjusted
D. They can claim a full cash refund of the balance from the department
Explanation: As per Section 18(4) read with Rule 44, a registered person opting for composition levy must pay an amount equal to the ITC in respect of inputs in stock, semi-finished/finished goods in stock, and capital goods, computed as prescribed, which results in reversal/payment.
Medium NORMAL · Section 18(1)(a) | Voluntary Registration | Stock ITC
Mr. X, an unregistered person, gets registered voluntarily under Section 25(3) on 15th August. What is his entitlement regarding ITC on inputs held in stock on the day immediately preceding the date of grant of registration?
A. He is eligible to claim ITC on inputs held in stock and inputs contained in semi-finished or finished goods held in stock on the day preceding registration ✔
B. He is eligible to claim ITC on all capital goods and inputs held in stock for the past 2 years
C. He is not eligible for any ITC on prior stock since registration is voluntary
D. He can claim ITC only if the stock was purchased within 30 days prior to registration
Explanation: Under Section 18(1)(a), a person who applies for registration within 30 days of becoming liable to register, or voluntarily under Section 25(3), is entitled to take credit of input tax in respect of inputs held in stock and inputs contained in semi-finished or finished goods held in stock on the day immediately preceding the date of grant of registration.
Medium NORMAL · Section 18(1) | Form GST ITC-01 | Rule 40
What is the time limit for issuing the declaration in Form GST ITC-01 by a person who has become liable to register and seeks to claim ITC on inputs held in stock under Section 18(1)?
A. Within 30 days from the date of becoming liable to register
B. Within 30 days from the date of grant of registration ✔
C. Within 90 days from the date of filing the registration application
D. Within the due date of filing the annual return
Explanation: Rule 40(1)(a) requires any person who takes ITC under Section 18(1)(a) or (b) to make a declaration in FORM GST ITC-01 within 30 days from the date of becoming registered (i.e., grant of registration).
Medium NORMAL · Section 18(3) | Form GST ITC-02 | Business Reorganization
If a registered person transfers their business consequent to change in ownership (like amalgamation or merger), how is the unutilized ITC in the electronic credit ledger transferred to the new entity?
A. It lapses completely and cannot be transferred
B. It is transferred using Form GST ITC-02, provided the scheme of merger/amalgamation has specific provisions for transfer of liabilities ✔
C. It can be transferred only with the written permission of the jurisdictional Commissioner
D. It is transferred via Form GST ITC-01
Explanation: As per Section 18(3) read with Rule 41, in case of amalgamation, merger, demerger, or change in ownership, the unutilized ITC can be transferred to the transferee entity using Form GST ITC-02, provided the restructuring specifics include liabilities.
Hard NORMAL · Rule 42 | Exempt Supply Definition | Reversal
Which of the following is treated as 'exempt supply' for the purpose of reversal of ITC under Rule 42 and Rule 43?
A. Supply of goods or services or both which attracts zero rate of tax
B. Supply of goods or services or both which are chargeable to nil rate of tax and non-taxable supplies, including transactions of private securities or sale of land/building (where specified) ✔
C. Only supplies made to SEZ units
D. Export of goods under bond without payment of IGST
Explanation: Explanation to Chapter V (Rules 42 and 43) clarifies that 'exempt supply' includes supply of any goods or services or both which attracts nil rate of tax or which may be wholly exempt from tax, and includes non-taxable supply. However, export of goods/services and supplies to SEZ are not treated as exempt supplies for this reversal.
Medium NORMAL · Section 17(5) | Construction | Immovable Property
Can a registered person claim Input Tax Credit on goods or services used for constructing an immovable property (other than plant and machinery) on their own account, even if such property is used in the course or furtherance of business?
A. Yes, full ITC is available since it is used for business
B. No, ITC is blocked under Section 17(5)(c) and (d) except in the case of plant and machinery ✔
C. Yes, ITC is available up to 50%
D. No, ITC is blocked unless capitalization is avoided
Explanation: Under Section 17(5)(c) and (d), ITC is blocked on works contract services and goods/services received by a taxable person for construction of an immovable property on their own account, other than plant and machinery, even if used in the course or furtherance of business.
Easy NORMAL · Section 17(5) | Gifts and Samples | Write-off
What happens to the ITC availed on inputs that are subsequently written off or disposed of by way of gift or free samples?
A. It can be retained without any reversal
B. It must be reversed under Section 17(5)(h) ✔
C. It must be claimed as an additional business expense under Income-tax Act
D. It is treated as outward taxable supply and tax is paid at market value
Explanation: Section 17(5)(h) explicitly blocks ITC in respect of goods lost, stolen, destroyed, written off or disposed of by way of gift or free samples. Therefore, any ITC availed on such goods must be reversed.
Hard NORMAL · Rule 36(4) | GSTR-2B | Matching
According to Rule 36(4) of the CGST Rules, 2017, Input Tax Credit to be availed by a registered person in respect of invoices/debit notes not reported by suppliers in their GSTR-1/IFF can be availed up to what limit?
A. Up to 5% of the eligible credit available in respect of reported invoices
B. Up to 10% of the eligible credit available
C. Zero percent (ITC can be availed only to the extent details are communicated in GSTR-2B/GSTR-1) ✔
D. Up to 20% of the eligible credit available
Explanation: Rule 36(4) was amended to state that no ITC can be availed by a registered person in respect of invoices/debit notes unless the details of such invoices/debit notes have been furnished by the supplier in GSTR-1/IFF and communicated to the recipient in GSTR-2B. The earlier 20% and 5% conditional buffers are no longer applicable.
Easy NORMAL · Section 16(1) | Eligibility | Registered Person
Which of the following persons is eligible to claim ITC under GST?
A. A person paying tax under the Composition Levy under Section 10
B. A non-resident taxable person for all inward supplies
C. A registered person making taxable supplies including zero-rated supplies ✔
D. A person exclusively engaged in supplying goods/services that are wholly exempt from tax
Explanation: Only registered persons making taxable supplies (including zero-rated supplies) are eligible to claim ITC under Section 16(1). Composition dealers, exempt suppliers, and non-resident taxable persons (except on imported goods) cannot claim regular ITC.
Hard NORMAL · Section 18(6) | Capital Goods Sale | Rule 40
When capital goods on which ITC has been availed are subsequently sold or supplied by a registered person, how is the tax payable on such disposal calculated?
A. GST is payable on the full transaction value
B. GST is payable on the higher of: (a) tax on the transaction value, or (b) tax on the ITC availed on such capital goods reduced by prescribed percentage points per quarter, whichever is higher ✔
C. GST is exempted on second-hand capital goods
D. GST is payable only on the book value as per balance sheet
Explanation: As per the proviso to Rule 40(2) / Section 18(6), where capital goods on which ITC has been taken are supplied, the registered person shall pay an amount equal to the ITC taken reduced by 5 percentage points per quarter from the date of invoice, or the tax on transaction value, whichever is higher.
Medium NORMAL · Section 16(2) | Job Work | Direct Delivery
Can a principal claim ITC on inputs sent directly to a job worker's premises without the goods first coming to the principal's business premises?
A. No, goods must first be received at the principal's factory before being sent to a job worker
B. Yes, provided the principal receives the goods back within 1 year for inputs and 3 years for capital goods
C. Yes, the principal can take ITC upon receipt of goods by the job worker, provided other conditions are met ✔
D. No, ITC is blocked when goods are delivered to third party locations
Explanation: As per the first proviso to Section 16(2)(b), for the purpose of claiming ITC, goods delivered by the supplier to a recipient's job worker on the direction of the registered person shall be deemed to have been received by the registered person.
Medium NORMAL · Section 143 | Job Work | Time Limit for Inputs
What is the maximum time period within which inputs sent to a job worker must be brought back to the principal's place of business to avoid being treated as a deemed supply?
A. 1 year from the date of receipt by the job worker ✔
B. 3 years from the date of receipt by the job worker
C. 180 days from the date of dispatch
D. 6 months from the end of the financial year
Explanation: Under Section 143 of the CGST Act, inputs sent to a job worker must be brought back within 1 year of being sent (or received by the job worker) failing which it shall be deemed to have been supplied by the principal to the job worker on the day the inputs were sent.
Medium NORMAL · Section 143 | Capital Goods | Job Work
What is the time limit for bringing back capital goods (other than moulds and dies, jigs and fixtures, and tools) sent to a job worker, to avoid deemed supply treatment under Section 143?
A. 1 year
B. 2 years
C. 3 years ✔
D. 5 years
Explanation: Under Section 143(1)(b), capital goods sent to a job worker must be returned to the principal's place of business within 3 years of being sent, otherwise it is treated as a supply from the date of original dispatch.
Hard NORMAL · Section 49 | Electronic Credit Ledger | Tax Dues
In cases where a tax demand is confirmed against a taxpayer involving fraud, willful misstatement, or suppression of facts, can the taxpayer pay such tax demand utilizing the balance available in their electronic credit ledger?
A. Yes, electronic credit ledger can be used for any tax demand under the Act
B. No, Section 49(3) / Rule 86B restrict the use of electronic credit ledger for payment of self-assessed tax only, and Section 49(10) restricts payment of demands arising out of fraud ✔
C. Yes, up to 50% of the demand can be paid from the credit ledger
D. No, tax demands can only be paid via cash ledger, but interest and penalty can be paid from credit ledger
Explanation: As per Rule 86(2) and Section 49, the electronic credit ledger cannot be used for payment of any tax demand that has been raised under Section 74 (fraud, willful misstatement, suppression of facts). Such amounts must be paid through the electronic cash ledger.
Hard NORMAL · Section 17(5) | Employee Welfare | Exceptions
Which of the following expenditure incurred by an employer towards employees is NOT blocked for ITC under Section 17(5)?
A. Club membership, health and fitness centre membership
B. Travel benefits extended to employees on vacation such as Leave Travel Concession (LTC) or home travel concession
C. Food and beverages / outdoor catering when supplied under a statutory obligation imposed by any law for the time being in force ✔
D. Life insurance and health insurance taken for employees voluntarily
Explanation: Section 17(5)(b)(i) blocks ITC on food, beverages, and outdoor catering, but contains an explicit exception: where the government notifies services which are obligatory for an employer to provide to its employees under any law for the time being in force, ITC is allowed.
Medium NORMAL · Section 18(3) | Death of Proprietor | Transfer of ITC
When a registered person dies, and their legal representative continues the business, can the unutilized ITC lying in the electronic credit ledger of the deceased person be transferred to the legal representative?
A. No, ITC lapses upon the death of a proprietor
B. Yes, via Form GST ITC-02, unutilized ITC can be transferred to the legal representative in case of death of sole proprietor ✔
C. Yes, automatically without filing any specific form
D. No, only cash balance can be transferred, not credit balance
