Explanation: Under Section 18(3) read with Rule 41, in case of death of a sole proprietor, transfer of business to a legal heir allows the transfer of unutilized ITC using Form GST ITC-02, provided the transferee is registered.
Medium NORMAL · Exempt Supply | Reversal | Rule 42
If an outward supply made by a registered person is treated as an exempt supply due to a retroactive notification, and the person has already claimed ITC on inputs used for such supply, what is the consequence?
A. The ITC already claimed remains fully valid and untouched
B. The person is required to reverse the ITC attributable to such exempt supply as per prescribed rules ✔
C. The person must surrender their registration certificate
D. The person can claim a refund of the tax paid earlier
Explanation: If a supply becomes exempt subsequently or retrospectively, any ITC claimed earlier on inputs/input services used exclusively or commonly for such supply must be reversed in accordance with the relevant provisions (Rule 42/43).
Easy NORMAL · Section 17(5) | Personal Consumption | Blocked Credit
Can Input Tax Credit be claimed on goods purchased for personal use or consumption of the proprietor or directors, even if paid through the business bank account?
A. Yes, because business bank account was used
B. No, Section 17(5)(g) blocks ITC on goods or services used for personal consumption ✔
C. Yes, provided it is shown as staff welfare in financial statements
D. No, unless fringe benefit tax is paid
Explanation: Section 17(5)(g) specifically blocks ITC in respect of goods or services used for personal consumption. Any purchase for personal use of proprietor, partners, or directors is ineligible for ITC.
Hard NORMAL · Section 18(2) | Stock ITC Time Limit | Registration
Under Section 18(2), no ITC can be claimed by a person in respect of any stock of inputs after the expiry of how many months from the date of issue of invoice relating to such inputs?
A. 12 months ✔
B. 18 months
C. 24 months
D. 36 months
Explanation: As per the proviso to Section 18(2), no ITC under sub-sections (1) (a) and (1) (b) shall be granted in respect of inputs held in stock or inputs contained in semi-finished or finished goods held in stock after the expiry of 1 year (12 months) from the date of issue of invoice relating to such inputs.
Hard NORMAL · Rule 86B | Electronic Credit Ledger | Restriction
Which of the following statements is correct regarding the restriction on the use of the electronic credit ledger under Rule 86B?
A. Rule 86B restricts a registered person from using the electronic credit ledger to discharge more than 99% of their output tax liability in cases where taxable supplies exceed Rs. 50 lakhs in a month, subject to specified exceptions. ✔
B. Rule 86B completely prohibits the use of electronic credit ledger for all taxpayers with turnover above Rs. 5 crores.
C. Rule 86B restricts ITC utilization for exempt supplies only.
D. Rule 86B is applicable to all taxpayers irrespective of their tax liability.
Explanation: Rule 86B of the CGST Rules, 2017 restricts the use of the electronic credit ledger for discharging output tax liability to 99% in cases where the monthly taxable supply exceeds Rs. 50 lakhs, leaving at least 1% to be paid in cash, subject to certain exceptions like income tax paid in previous years.
CASE SCENARIO: M/s. Zenith Enterprises, a registered GST taxpayer in Maharashtra, purchased a machine for Rs. 20,00,000 plus GST @ 18% on 10th July 2024 for use in its manufacturing unit. The machine was received in two lots: first lot on 1st August 2024 and second lot on 10th August 2024. Zenith Enterprises capitalized the machine in its books including the GST component and claimed depreciation under the Income-tax Act, 1961. The supplier filed GSTR-1 reflecting the invoice on time, and Zenith filed its annual return for FY 2024-25 on 30th September 2025.
Medium SCENARIO · Section 16(2) | Goods in Lots | Capital Goods
What is the correct date on which Zenith Enterprises is entitled to avail Input Tax Credit on the machinery, assuming all conditions are met otherwise?
A. 1st August 2024
B. 10th August 2024 ✔
C. 10th July 2024
D. 30th September 2025
Explanation: As per the second proviso to Section 16(2), when goods are received in lots or installments, ITC can be availed only upon the receipt of the last lot or installment. Since the second lot was received on 10th August 2024, ITC entitlement arises on that date.
Medium SCENARIO · Section 16(3) | Depreciation | Capital Goods
Can Zenith Enterprises claim ITC on the GST component of Rs. 3,60,000 paid on the machinery?
A. Yes, full ITC can be claimed alongside depreciation
B. No, because depreciation has been claimed on the GST component under the Income-tax Act ✔
C. Yes, 50% ITC and 50% depreciation can be claimed simultaneously
D. No, because machinery is blocked under Section 17(5)
Explanation: Under the proviso to Section 16(3), if a registered person claims depreciation on the tax component of the cost of capital goods under the Income-tax Act, 1961, the input tax credit on such tax component is not allowed.
Hard SCENARIO · Section 16(4) | Time Limit | Annual Return Date
What would have been the last date for availing ITC on this machinery under Section 16(4), had they not claimed depreciation?
A. 30th November 2025 ✔
B. 31st December 2025
C. 30th September 2025
D. 31st March 2025
Explanation: As per Section 16(4), the time limit for availing ITC for FY 2024-25 is the earlier of 30th November 2025 or the date of filing the annual return (30th September 2025). Wait, since 30th September 2025 is earlier than 30th November 2025, let's check: the annual return was filed on 30th September 2025. Therefore, the earlier of 30th November 2025 and 30th September 2025 is 30th September 2025.
Medium SCENARIO · Section 17(2) | Exempt Supplies | Restriction
If Zenith Enterprises had used this machinery exclusively for manufacturing goods that are wholly exempt from GST, would they have been eligible for ITC?
A. Yes, full ITC is available on machinery used for exempt supplies
B. No, ITC is not available on inputs or capital goods used exclusively for making exempt supplies ✔
C. Yes, up to 50% ITC is allowed
D. No, but a cash refund of the tax paid can be claimed
Explanation: Under Section 17(2), where the goods or services are used by the registered person partly for effecting taxable supplies and partly for exempt supplies, the ITC is restricted to the quantum attributable to taxable supplies. If used exclusively for exempt supplies, no ITC is available.
CASE SCENARIO: Mr. Sharma commenced a trading business in Delhi and obtained registration under GST on 1st October 2024. Prior to obtaining registration, he had purchased inputs in stock worth Rs. 5,00,000 (exclusive of GST @ 12%) on 15th August 2024. He also purchased a car for business use on 10th September 2024 for Rs. 10,00,000 plus GST @ 28% (seating capacity 5 persons) and capitalized it. On 1st December 2024, he sent inputs worth Rs. 2,00,000 to a job worker for processing.
Medium SCENARIO · Section 18(1)(a) | Stock ITC | New Registration
Is Mr. Sharma eligible to claim ITC on the inputs held in stock on 30th September 2024 (the day preceding registration)?
A. No, because he was unregistered at the time of purchase
B. Yes, under Section 18(1)(a) for inputs held in stock on the day preceding registration, provided invoices are within 1 year ✔
C. Yes, for all purchases made in the last 3 years
D. No, unless he pays a special composition fee
Explanation: Under Section 18(1)(a), a person who registers within 30 days of becoming liable is entitled to ITC on inputs held in stock on the day preceding registration, provided the invoice date is not older than 1 year.
Medium SCENARIO · Section 17(5) | Blocked Credit | Motor Car
What is the correct treatment of GST paid on the car purchased on 10th September 2024 for business use (seating capacity 5 persons)?
A. Full ITC can be claimed since it is used for business
B. ITC is blocked under Section 17(5)(a) as it is a motor vehicle for transportation of persons <= 13 capacity and not used for specified exceptions ✔
C. ITC can be claimed up to 50%
D. ITC can be claimed if depreciation is foregone
Explanation: Under Section 17(5)(a), ITC is blocked on motor vehicles for transportation of persons with seating capacity <= 13 persons, unless used for specified exempt purposes like further supply, passenger transport, or driving school. General business travel does not qualify.
Medium SCENARIO · Section 143 | Job Work | Time Limit
What is the maximum time limit within which the inputs sent to the job worker on 1st December 2024 must be brought back to Mr. Sharma's premises to avoid deemed supply?
A. 6 months
B. 1 year ✔
C. 3 years
D. 180 days
Explanation: As per Section 143(1)(a), inputs sent to a job worker must be brought back within 1 year of being sent, failing which the transaction is deemed to be a supply from the date of dispatch.
Easy SCENARIO · Rule 40 | FORM GST ITC-01 | Stock ITC
Which form is required to be filed by Mr. Sharma to claim ITC on inputs held in stock prior to registration?
A. FORM GST ITC-01 ✔
B. FORM GST ITC-02
C. FORM GST ITC-03
D. FORM GST REG-01
Explanation: Rule 40(1)(a) requires a registered person claiming ITC under Section 18(1) on inputs in stock to file a declaration in FORM GST ITC-01 within 30 days of becoming registered.
CASE SCENARIO: M/s. Apex Technologies Ltd., a registered software company in Bengaluru, undertook construction of an office building on its own account during FY 2024-25. It incurred expenses on works contract services of Rs. 50,00,000 (plus GST 18%) and purchased cement and iron bars locally worth Rs. 30,00,000 (plus GST 18%) used in the construction. Simultaneously, Apex Technologies Ltd. purchased computers worth Rs. 20,00,000 (plus GST 18%) for office use. The company also provided outdoor catering for its employees during an annual corporate event, incurring Rs. 5,00,000 plus GST 18%.
Medium SCENARIO · Section 17(5) | Works Contract | Immovable Property
Is Apex Technologies Ltd. eligible to claim ITC on works contract services used for the construction of its office building?
A. Yes, because the office building is used for business
B. No, ITC is blocked under Section 17(5)(c) on works contract services for construction of immovable property, other than plant and machinery ✔
C. Yes, up to 50%
D. No, unless capitalization is avoided
Explanation: Under Section 17(5)(c), ITC is blocked in respect of works contract services when supplied for construction of immovable property, other than plant and machinery, even if used for business.
Medium SCENARIO · Section 17(5) | Construction | Blocked Credit
What is the eligibility of ITC on cement and iron bars purchased for the construction of the office building?
A. Full ITC is available
B. ITC is blocked under Section 17(5)(d) for goods received for construction of immovable property on own account ✔
C. ITC is available subject to 180 days payment condition
D. ITC is available since they are inputs
Explanation: Section 17(5)(d) blocks ITC on goods or services received by a taxable person for construction of an immovable property on their own account (including building), other than plant and machinery.
Easy SCENARIO · Capital Goods | Computers | Eligibility
Can Apex Technologies Ltd. claim ITC on the computers purchased for office use?
A. No, computers are treated as capital goods and ineligible for ITC
B. Yes, computers are not blocked under Section 17(5) and qualify as capital goods/inputs used in business ✔
C. Yes, but only if depreciation is not claimed
D. No, electronics are blocked
Explanation: Computers used in business are eligible capital goods/inputs for ITC. They are not covered under any blocked credit category in Section 17(5), provided depreciation is not claimed on the tax component.
Medium SCENARIO · Section 17(5) | Outdoor Catering | Blocked Credit
What is the tax treatment of GST paid on outdoor catering services for the corporate event?
A. ITC can be claimed fully
B. ITC is blocked under Section 17(5)(b)(ii) unless outward supply is of the same category or provided under statutory obligation ✔
C. ITC can be claimed up to 50%
D. ITC is allowed as staff welfare expense
Explanation: Section 17(5)(b)(ii) blocks ITC on outdoor catering, food, and beverages, except where an outward taxable supply of the same category is made or where it is obligatory for an employer to provide under any law.
CASE SCENARIO: M/s. Beta Industries operates a factory making both taxable goods and exempt goods. During the month of October 2024, it received common inputs worth Rs. 10,00,000 on which total GST paid was Rs. 1,80,000. Total turnover of Beta Industries for the month was Rs. 50,00,000, out of which taxable supplies amounted to Rs. 30,00,000, exempt supplies amounted to Rs. 15,00,000, and zero-rated supplies (exports) amounted to Rs. 5,00,000. Additionally, Beta Industries had availed ITC of Rs. 25,000 on inputs that were destroyed by fire during the month.
Easy SCENARIO · Rule 42 | Common ITC | Reversal Formula
Which rule governs the reversal of common Input Tax Credit on inputs and input services used for both taxable and exempt supplies?
A. Rule 36
B. Rule 42 ✔
C. Rule 43
D. Rule 44
Explanation: Rule 42 of the CGST Rules, 2017 prescribes the formula and procedure for determination of common ITC attributable to exempt supplies and its subsequent reversal.
Easy SCENARIO · Section 17(5) | Destroyed Goods | Reversal
What is the treatment of ITC amounting to Rs. 25,000 on inputs destroyed by fire?
A. It can be retained in full
B. It must be reversed under Section 17(5)(h) since goods were destroyed ✔
C. It can be carried forward as loss
D. It is adjusted against export benefits
Explanation: Under Section 17(5)(h), ITC in respect of goods lost, stolen, destroyed, written off or disposed of by way of gift or free samples is blocked and must be reversed.
Hard SCENARIO · Rule 42 | Zero-Rated Supplies | Exempt Turnover
In computing the proportion of exempt supplies for Rule 42, how are zero-rated supplies (exports) treated?
A. Treated as exempt supplies
B. Treated as taxable supplies (not included in exempt turnover for reversal computation) ✔
C. Ignored entirely from total turnover
D. Treated separately as non-business supplies
Explanation: For the purpose of Rule 42, zero-rated supplies (exports and supplies to SEZ) are treated as taxable supplies and are not counted as exempt supplies while calculating the reversal ratio.
Medium SCENARIO · Section 16(2) | Non-payment | 180 Days
If Beta Industries fails to pay the supplier for the common inputs within 180 days from the invoice date, what action is required?
A. Nothing, since goods were received
B. An amount equal to ITC availed plus applicable interest must be added to output tax liability ✔
C. Registration is liable to cancellation
D. Supplier must refund the tax
Explanation: As per the second proviso to Section 16(2), if payment is not made within 180 days, an amount equal to ITC availed must be added to output tax liability along with interest.
CASE SCENARIO: M/s. Delta Logistics, a registered transport operator, was previously registered under the regular GST scheme. On 1st November 2024, Delta Logistics opted to switch to the Composition Scheme under Section 10. On 31st October 2024, the electronic credit ledger of Delta Logistics showed a balance of Rs. 1,50,000. On the same date, they held inputs in stock valued at Rs. 10,00,000 (GST paid @ 18%, total Rs. 1,80,000) and capital goods on which ITC of Rs. 3,00,000 had been claimed earlier (purchased 1 year ago).
Hard SCENARIO · Section 18(4) | Composition Scheme | Rule 44
What are the statutory obligations of Delta Logistics regarding the unutilized ITC and ITC on stock upon opting for the Composition Scheme?
A. They can continue to carry forward the credit balance
B. They must pay an amount equivalent to the ITC in respect of inputs in stock and capital goods by debiting electronic credit or cash ledger, and remaining credit lapses ✔
C. They can claim a cash refund of Rs. 1,50,000
D. The credit ledger balance is transferred to the Government revenue without any calculation
Explanation: Under Section 18(4) read with Rule 44, when shifting to the composition scheme, the registered person must pay an amount equivalent to the ITC on inputs in stock and capital goods (reduced by percentage points), and the remaining balance in the electronic credit ledger lapses.
Hard SCENARIO · Rule 44 | Capital Goods Reversal | Composition
How is the ITC reversal on capital goods calculated when shifting to the composition scheme under Rule 44?
A. Full ITC originally claimed must be paid back
B. ITC is calculated on the remaining useful life in months/quarters on a pro-rata basis ✔
C. No reversal is required for capital goods
D. 50% of the original ITC is reversed flat
Explanation: Under Rule 44(6), for capital goods held in stock, the ITC taken is computed on the basis of remaining useful life in quarters (taking useful life as 5 years / 20 quarters), and the proportionate amount is added to liability.
Hard SCENARIO · Rule 44 | FORM GST ITC-03 | Time Limit
What is the time limit for filing the stock declaration in FORM GST ITC-03 when opting for the composition scheme?
A. Within 30 days from the date of switch
B. Within 60 days from the commencement of the relevant financial year or within 30 days of opting for composition ✔
C. Within 180 days
D. Along with the annual return
Explanation: Rule 44(4) mandates that the details of stock and capital goods for payment/reversal under Section 18(4) must be furnished in FORM GST ITC-03 within 60 days of the commencement of the relevant financial year or within 30 days of opting for composition levy.
Easy SCENARIO · Section 10 | Composition Scheme | Bill of Supply
Can a composition taxpayer under Section 10 issue a tax invoice to their customers to pass on Input Tax Credit?
A. Yes, exactly like a regular taxpayer
B. No, a composition taxpayer cannot collect tax from recipients nor issue a tax invoice; they must issue a bill of supply ✔
C. Yes, but only for inter-state supplies
D. No, but they can issue a delivery challan
Explanation: As per Section 10(4) read with Section 31(2), a composition taxpayer cannot collect any tax from the recipient on supplies made by them and cannot issue a tax invoice; instead, they must issue a Bill of Supply and cannot pass on any ITC.

Paper 3: Taxation · Module 2 · Chapter 9:

Taxation — 55 rows
Easy NORMAL · Threshold Limit | Goods | Special Category States
What is the threshold limit for registration under GST for a person making exclusive taxable supplies of goods in the State of Manipur?
A. Rs. 10 Lakhs ✔
B. Rs. 20 Lakhs
C. Rs. 40 Lakhs
D. Rs. 50 Lakhs
Explanation: As per Section 22 read with Notification No. 10/2019-CT, Manipur is listed among the Special Category States where the threshold limit for exclusive supply of goods is Rs. 10 lakhs. Therefore, Rs. 10 Lakhs is the correct threshold limit.
Medium NORMAL · Compulsory Registration | Casual Taxable Person | Section 24
Which of the following persons is mandatorily required to obtain registration under Section 24 of the CGST Act, 2017, irrespective of the turnover threshold?
A. Persons making intra-state taxable supplies of goods
B. Casual taxable persons making taxable supplies ✔
C. Persons making inter-state supplies of goods with aggregate turnover up to Rs. 20 lakhs
D. Persons making taxable supplies of goods on behalf of other taxable persons as an agent with turnover below Rs. 10 lakhs
Explanation: Section 24 mandates compulsory registration for casual taxable persons making taxable supplies, regardless of their turnover. Inter-state supply of goods up to Rs. 20 lakhs is exempt from mandatory registration vide Notification No. 10/2017-IT, and agents making taxable supplies on behalf of others are also compulsorily registrable without threshold benefit.
Easy NORMAL · Time Limit | Application for Registration | Section 25
Within how many days from the date on which liability to register arises must a person apply for GST registration?
A. 15 days
B. 30 days ✔
C. 45 days
D. 60 days
Explanation: According to Section 25(1) of the CGST Act, 2017, every person who becomes liable to registration under section 22 or section 24 shall apply for registration within 30 days from the date on which he becomes liable to registration.
Medium NORMAL · Casual Taxable Person | Validity Period | Section 27
What is the validity period of the certificate of registration granted to a Casual Taxable Person (CTP)?
A. 90 days from registration
B. Maximum period of 90 days or period specified in the application, whichever is earlier ✔
C. 1 year from the date of issue
D. Till the completion of business event
Explanation: As per Section 27(1), the certificate of registration issued to a casual taxable person shall be valid for a period specified in the application for registration or 90 days from the effective date of registration, whichever is earlier.
Medium NORMAL · Multiple Registrations | Same State | Section 25
Can a supplier having multiple places of business in the same State obtain separate registrations for each such place of business?
A. No, only one state registration is permitted per entity
B. Yes, provided all such places of business are engaged in identical supply of goods
C. Yes, under Section 25(2), a person having multiple places of business in a State may be granted a separate registration for each such place of business ✔
D. Yes, but only if aggregate turnover exceeds Rs. 1.5 crores
Explanation: Section 25(2) of the CGST Act allows a person having multiple places of business in a State or Union territory to be granted a separate registration for each such place of business, subject to prescribed conditions.
Hard NORMAL · Deemed Registration | CGST Rules | Proper Officer
What is the consequence if the proper officer fails to take any action on an application for registration within the prescribed time limit, and no notice is issued?
A. The application is deemed to be rejected
B. The registration is deemed to have been granted after 7 working days from application submission
C. The registration is deemed to have been granted after verification of Aadhaar
D. The registration shall be deemed to have been granted after the expiry of the period specified under rule 9(5) ✔
Explanation: Under Rule 9(5) of the CGST Rules, 2017, if the proper officer fails to take any action within the prescribed period of 3 days (or 7 days if Aadhaar authentication is required/failed), the application for grant of registration shall be deemed to have been approved.
Easy NORMAL · UIN | Unique Identity Number | Section 25
Which of the following entities is required to obtain a Unique Identity Number (UIN) under Section 25(9)?
A. Any regular supplier with turnover exceeding Rs. 40 lakhs
B. Specialized agency of the United Nations Organisation or any Multilateral Financial Institution ✔
C. Casual taxable person operating in multiple states
D. Non-resident taxable person providing OIDAR services
Explanation: Section 25(9) provides that a specialized agency of the United Nations Organisation or any Multilateral Financial Institution and Organization notified under the United Nations (Privileges and Immunities) Act, 1947, Consulate or Embassy of foreign countries shall obtain a Unique Identity Number (UIN) for claiming refund of taxes.
Hard NORMAL · Effective Date | Aadhaar Authentication | Rule 10
In cases where Aadhaar authentication is successfully completed, from which date does the registration become effective?
A. Date of submission of application if applied within 30 days of liability ✔
B. Date of approval by the proper officer
C. Date of generation of application reference number (ARN)
D. Date of authentication or 30th day from submission, whichever is earlier
Explanation: As per Rule 10 of CGST Rules, where Aadhaar authentication is successfully completed, the application is deemed approved and registration is effective from the date on which the person became liable to registration, provided the application was submitted within 30 days.
Easy NORMAL · ECO | Compulsory Registration | Section 24
An electronic commerce operator (ECO) who is required to collect tax at source under Section 52 must obtain:
A. Voluntary registration only if turnover crosses Rs. 20 lakhs
B. Compulsory registration under Section 24 irrespective of threshold ✔
C. UIN instead of regular GSTIN
D. Registration only if operating in more than two States
Explanation: Section 24(x) explicitly mandates that every electronic commerce operator who is required to collect tax at source under section 52 must obtain registration compulsorily, regardless of their aggregate turnover threshold.
Medium NORMAL · Non-Resident Taxable Person | Advance Application | Section 27
What is the time limit for a Non-Resident Taxable Person (NRTP) to apply for registration prior to the commencement of business?
A. At least 5 days prior ✔
B. At least 15 days prior
C. At least 30 days prior
D. No prior time limit is prescribed
Explanation: As per Section 27(1) read with Rule 12, a non-resident taxable person shall make an application for registration at least 5 days prior to the commencement of business.
Easy NORMAL · Cancellation | Tax Liability | Section 29
When a registered person applies for cancellation of registration, what happens to their tax liability for the period prior to cancellation?
A. It gets waived automatically
B. It remains unaffected and the person is liable to pay all pending dues ✔
C. It is transferred to the successor automatically
D. It can only be recovered after 5 years
Explanation: Cancellation of registration under Section 29 does not affect the liability of the taxable person to pay tax and other dues for any period prior to the date of cancellation, which remains recoverable.
Medium NORMAL · Business Verticals | Separate Registration | Section 25
Can a person having multiple business verticals within a State obtain separate registrations for each vertical under the CGST Act, 2017?
A. No, separate registration is allowed only for different States
B. Yes, under Section 25(2) proviso, a person having multiple business verticals within a State may obtain separate registration for each vertical ✔
C. Yes, but only if turnover of each vertical exceeds Rs. 10 Crores
D. No, business verticals provision was omitted/amended
Explanation: The proviso to Section 25(2) allows a person having multiple business verticals within a State or Union territory to be granted a separate registration for each business vertical, subject to prescribed conditions.
Medium NORMAL · Cancellation | Proper Officer | Section 29
Which of the following actions can be taken by the proper officer if a registered person has contravened provisions relating to anti-profiteering or furnishing returns?
A. Directly seize all bank accounts without notice
B. Cancel the registration under Section 29(2) ✔
C. Force conversion of registration into UIN
D. Impose imprisonment without trial
Explanation: Under Section 29(2) of the CGST Act, the proper officer may cancel the registration of a person who has contravened such provisions of the Act or the rules made thereunder as may be prescribed.
Hard NORMAL · Penalty | Failure to Register | Section 122
What is the penalty for failure to obtain registration when legally mandated under the CGST Act, 2017?
A. Fixed penalty of Rs. 5,000
B. 10% of the tax due or Rs. 10,000, whichever is higher ✔
C. Imprisonment for 7 years straight
D. Confiscation of all personal assets
Explanation: As per Section 122(1)(i), a taxable person who supplies any taxable goods or services without issue of invoice or suppresses turnover is liable to a penalty of Rs. 10,000 or an amount equivalent to the tax evaded or tax short deducted/collected, whichever is higher.
Medium NORMAL · Death of Proprietor | Transfer of Business | Section 29
If a registered person dies, what happens to their GST registration?
A. It continues in the name of the deceased indefinitely
B. It is cancelled immediately and cannot be transferred
C. The legal heir/transferee is permitted to carry on business under the same registration/amended registration ✔
D. It is converted into a casual taxable person registration
Explanation: As per Section 29(1)(a) read with Rule 21A/relevant rules, in the event of the death of a sole proprietor, the business can be continued by the legal heir, and application for amendment/transfer is made so that the transferee can operate.
Easy NORMAL · Exemption from Registration | Agriculturist | Section 23
Which of the following is NOT required to obtain GST registration?
A. An agriculturist, to the extent of supply of produce out of cultivation of land ✔
B. An Input Service Distributor (ISD)
C. A person making inter-state supplies of taxable goods with turnover of Rs. 25 lakhs
D. A non-resident taxable person making taxable supplies
Explanation: Section 23(1)(a) explicitly states that an agriculturist shall not be liable to registration to the extent of supply of produce out of cultivation of land. The others listed are either compulsorily registrable or crossed thresholds.
Hard NORMAL · Threshold Limit | Arunachal Pradesh | Goods
What is the threshold limit for registration for a person engaged exclusively in intra-state taxable supply of goods in the State of Arunachal Pradesh?
A. Rs. 10 Lakhs
B. Rs. 20 Lakhs ✔
C. Rs. 40 Lakhs
D. Rs. 50 Lakhs
Explanation: Notification No. 10/2019-CT specifies Rs. 20 lakhs threshold for states like Arunachal Pradesh for exclusive supply of goods (unlike Manipur, Mizoram, Nagaland, Tripura which have Rs. 10 lakhs).
Easy NORMAL · Voluntary Registration | Section 25
When can a person voluntarily obtain registration under Section 25(3), even though their aggregate turnover is below the threshold limit?
A. Only after obtaining prior permission from the GST Council
B. At any time, and all provisions of the Act shall apply to such registered person ✔
C. Only if they make inter-state supplies to unregistered persons
D. Voluntary registration is not permitted under CGST Act
Explanation: Section 25(3) allows a person not liable to be registered under section 22 or section 24 to get registered voluntarily, and once registered, all provisions of the Act apply as if they are a regular taxable person.
Medium NORMAL · Suspension | Suo-motu Cancellation | Rule 21A
What is the status of a registration certificate if the proper officer initiates suo-motu cancellation proceedings?
A. It remains fully active until final order is passed
B. It may be suspended by the proper officer pending the cancellation proceedings ✔
C. It is automatically revoked within 24 hours
D. It is converted into voluntary registration
Explanation: Rule 21A of the CGST Rules provides that where the proper officer has reasons to believe that the registration of a person is liable to be cancelled, he may suspend the registration pending the cancellation proceedings.
Medium NORMAL · ECO | Section 9 | Recommendations of Council
Who among the following is empowered to notify categories of services where tax on intra-state supplies shall be paid by the electronic commerce operator?
A. Central Government on the recommendations of the GST Council ✔
B. Commissioner of State Tax independently
C. Jurisdictional Superintendent
D. Reserve Bank of India
Explanation: Section 9(5) of the CGST Act empowers the Government, on the recommendations of the Council, to specify categories of services the tax on intra-state supplies of which shall be paid by the electronic commerce operator.
Easy NORMAL · Multiple States | Separate Registration | PAN
Can a person having a PAN in India obtain multiple GST registrations across different States without having multiple business verticals?
A. No, only one GSTIN per PAN is allowed nationwide
B. Yes, a person having multiple places of business in different States must obtain a separate registration for each such State ✔
C. Yes, but only if turnover exceeds Rs. 10 Crores per State
D. No, inter-state operations require only one central registration
Explanation: As per Section 25(1), a person obtaining registration has to obtain a separate registration for each State or Union territory in which he has a business and is liable to register, meaning multiple state registrations per PAN are mandatory.
Hard NORMAL · Revocation | Cancellation | Section 30
What is the time period within which a person whose registration has been cancelled suo-motu can apply for revocation of cancellation?
A. Within 15 days of service of cancellation order
B. Within 30 days of service of cancellation order (extendable by Commissioner) ✔
C. Within 90 days without any extension
D. Within 1 year from the date of issue
Explanation: Under Section 30 of the CGST Act, any registered person whose registration is cancelled suo-motu may apply for revocation within 30 days from the date of service of the cancellation order, which can be extended by the Commissioner/Additional/Joint Commissioner.
Medium NORMAL · Registration Forms | FORM GST REG-01 | CGST Rules
Which form is used for submitting an application for registration under CGST Rules, 2017?
A. FORM GST REG-01 ✔
B. FORM GST REG-06
C. FORM GST REG-16
D. FORM GST REG-21
Explanation: Rule 8 prescribes FORM GST REG-01 for making an application for electronic registration. FORM GST REG-06 is the certificate of registration, and FORM GST REG-16 is for cancellation.
Hard NORMAL · Threshold Limit | Services | Uttarakhand
What is the threshold limit for registration for a person engaged exclusively in intra-state supply of services in the State of Uttarakhand?
A. Rs. 10 Lakhs
B. Rs. 20 Lakhs ✔
C. Rs. 40 Lakhs
D. Rs. 50 Lakhs
Explanation: For services, the threshold limit is generally Rs. 20 lakhs (or Rs. 10 lakhs for specific special category states). Uttarakhand has a threshold of Rs. 20 lakhs for services (and Rs. 40 lakhs for goods).
Medium NORMAL · Transfer of Business | Input Tax Credit | FORM GST ITC-02
In the case of transfer of business as a going concern, what happens to the unutilized input tax credit (ITC) lying in the electronic credit ledger of the transferor?
A. It lapses permanently
B. It can be refunded in cash to the transferor
C. It is transferred to the transferee through FORM GST ITC-02 ✔
D. It must be reversed and cannot be utilized
Explanation: As per Section 18(3) read with Rule 41, in case of amalgamation, merger, or transfer of business as a going concern, the unutilized ITC can be transferred to the transferee using FORM GST ITC-02.
Easy NORMAL · False Information | Cancellation | Penalties
What is the consequence of furnishing false information during the registration process under the CGST Act?
A. Only a warning letter is issued
B. The proper officer can reject or cancel the registration and penalize the applicant ✔
C. The registration is automatically upgraded to voluntary status
D. No action can be taken after ARN generation
Explanation: Furnishing false information or suppression of facts during registration empowers the proper officer to reject or cancel registration and initiate penal proceedings under the Act.
Hard NORMAL · Aggregate Turnover | Definition | Section 2
Which of the following is considered while computing 'aggregate turnover' for determining registration threshold?
A. Central tax, State tax, Integrated tax, and Cess
B. Exempt supplies of goods and services ✔
C. Inward supplies on which tax is payable under reverse charge basis
D. Value of goods supplied directly from customs bonded warehouses before clearance
Explanation: As per Section 2(6), 'aggregate turnover' includes taxable supplies, exempt supplies, exports, and inter-state supplies of persons having the same PAN, computed on all-India basis, excluding central/state/integrated taxes and cess, and reverse charge inward supplies.
Hard NORMAL · Transfer of ITC | Same State | FORM GST ITC-02A
Can a person having multiple registrations within the same State transfer ITC from one GSTIN to another GSTIN of the same entity?
A. No, transfer of ITC between different GSTINS of same PAN in same state is not allowed
B. Yes, through FORM GST ITC-02A ✔
C. Yes, automatically without any form
D. Only with High Court permission
Explanation: Rule 41A allows a registered person who has obtained separate registrations for multiple places of business within the same State to transfer unutilized ITC lying in one GSTIN to another GSTIN using FORM GST ITC-02A.
Medium NORMAL · Non-Resident Taxable Person | Returns | FORM GSTR-5
What is the requirement for a Non-Resident Taxable Person regarding furnishing of returns?
A. Annual return only in FORM GSTR-9
B. Quarterly return in FORM GSTR-4
C. Monthly return in FORM GSTR-5 ✔
D. No returns are required to be filed
Explanation: Section 39(5) mandates that a non-resident taxable person shall furnish a return in FORM GSTR-5 for every calendar month within 20 days after the end of a calendar month or within 7 days after the last day of validity of registration.
Easy NORMAL · Registration Certificate | FORM GST REG-06 | Proper Officer
Which authority issues the registration certificate in FORM GST REG-06?
A. GST Council Secretariat
B. The proper officer after approval of application ✔
C. Central Board of Indirect Taxes and Customs (CBIC) Chairman directly
D. Registrar of Companies
Explanation: The proper officer grants the certificate of registration in FORM GST REG-06 after successful verification and approval of the registration application.
CASE SCENARIO: M/s. Apex Traders, a sole proprietorship firm based in Jaipur, Rajasthan, is engaged in trading of electronic appliances. During the financial year, the aggregate turnover of M/s. Apex Traders crossed Rs. 40 Lakhs on 15th October. The proprietor, Mr. Anand, failed to apply for registration within the statutory 30-day period and ultimately submitted an online application for registration on 25th November. Mr. Anand also wishes to know whether his Jaipur branch (warehouse) requires a separate registration within the same State.
Medium SCENARIO · Time Limit | Application Date | Section 25
By what date was M/s. Apex Traders required to apply for GST registration?
A. 15th October
B. 30th October
C. 14th November ✔
D. 25th November
Explanation: Since the liability to register arose on 15th October, as per Section 25(1), the application must be made within 30 days from that date. Counting 30 days from 15th October leads to 14th November.
Medium SCENARIO · Threshold Limit | Rajasthan | Goods
What is the threshold limit applicable to M/s. Apex Traders for registration of goods in Rajasthan?
A. Rs. 10 Lakhs
B. Rs. 20 Lakhs
C. Rs. 40 Lakhs ✔
D. Rs. 1.5 Crores
Explanation: Notification No. 10/2019-CT prescribes a threshold limit of Rs. 40 Lakhs for exclusive supply of goods in states like Rajasthan, provided certain conditions (such as not dealing in notified goods like ice cream, pan masala, tobacco) are met.
Hard SCENARIO · Multiple Places of Business | Same State | Section 25
Is Mr. Anand legally mandated to obtain a separate registration for his warehouse in Jaipur under the CGST Act?
A. Yes, every branch or warehouse must have a separate registration mandatorily
B. No, obtaining separate registration for multiple places of business within the same State is optional under Section 25(2) ✔
C. Yes, if turnover of warehouse exceeds Rs. 20 Lakhs
D. No, intra-state warehouses are prohibited from registration
Explanation: Under Section 25(2) of the CGST Act, a person having multiple places of business in the same State *may* be granted a separate registration for each place of business, making it an option rather than a mandatory requirement.
Hard SCENARIO · Effective Date | Delayed Application | Rule 10
Assuming Mr. Anand successfully completes Aadhaar authentication, what will be the effective date of registration for M/s. Apex Traders?
A. 15th October (date on which liability to register arose)
B. 25th November (date of submission of application) ✔
C. Date of approval by proper officer
D. 1st April of the financial year
Explanation: Since the application was submitted on 25th November, which is after the expiry of 30 days from the date of liability (14th November), where Aadhaar authentication is completed, the effective date of registration is the date of grant of registration / submission of application as per Rule 10.
CASE SCENARIO: Mr. John, a resident of London, UK, visits India to participate in an industrial trade fair held in Mumbai, Maharashtra. He sets up a temporary stall and sells taxable machine parts directly to Indian consumers. Furthermore, Mr. John intends to clear goods imported into India through custom clearances. He has no fixed place of business in India.
Medium SCENARIO · Non-Resident Taxable Person | Definition | Section 2
Under which category of taxable persons does Mr. John fall for the purpose of GST registration?
A. Casual Taxable Person
B. Non-Resident Taxable Person ✔
C. Input Service Distributor
D. Regular Taxable Person
Explanation: As per Section 2(77), a non-resident taxable person means any person who occasionally undertakes transactions involving supply of goods or services or both, whether as principal or agent or in any other capacity, but who has no fixed place of business or residence in India.
Medium SCENARIO · NRTP | Advance Application | Section 27
What is the advance time limit for Mr. John to apply for GST registration prior to commencing business in Mumbai?
A. At least 30 days prior
B. At least 15 days prior
C. At least 5 days prior ✔
D. No prior application is required
Explanation: As per Section 27(1) read with Rule 12, a non-resident taxable person shall make an application for registration at least 5 days prior to the commencement of business.
Hard SCENARIO · Advance Tax Deposit | NRTP | Section 27
What advance deposit of tax must Mr. John make while applying for registration as a non-resident taxable person?
A. Nil, deposit is required only after monthly filing
B. An amount equivalent to the estimated tax liability of such person for the period for which the registration is sought ✔
C. Fixed deposit of Rs. 1,00,000 irrespective of turnover
D. 50% of total invoice value
Explanation: Section 27(2) mandates that the certificate of registration issued to a non-resident taxable person shall be granted or renewed only upon advance deposit of an amount equivalent to the estimated tax liability for the period for which registration is sought.
Medium SCENARIO · Validity Period | NRTP | Section 27
What is the initial validity period of the registration certificate granted to Mr. John?
A. 90 days, or period specified in application, whichever is earlier ✔
B. 180 days fixed
C. 1 year
D. 30 days
Explanation: Section 27(1) states that the certificate of registration issued to a casual taxable person or a non-resident taxable person shall be valid for a period specified in the application or 90 days from the effective date of registration, whichever is earlier.
CASE SCENARIO: M/s. Zenith Logistics Solutions, registered in Karnataka, provides taxable logistics services across multiple states. Due to internal restructuring, the firm decides to transfer its entire business as a going concern to M/s. Swift Carriers Pvt. Ltd., which is also registered under GST in Karnataka. The transfer includes all assets, liabilities, and unutilized input tax credit.
Medium SCENARIO · Transfer of Business | Compulsory Registration | Section 22
What is the statutory requirement under the CGST Act regarding registration for M/s. Swift Carriers Pvt. Ltd. consequent to the transfer of business?
A. It must apply for fresh registration ignoring transferor's history
B. It shall be liable to be registered with effect from the date of such transfer or succession ✔
C. It is exempt from registration if turnover is below Rs. 20 lakhs
D. It must convert into an ISD
Explanation: Section 22(3) provides that where a business carried on by a registered person is transferred to another person as a going concern, the transferee shall be liable to be registered with effect from the date of such transfer or succession.
Medium SCENARIO · Transfer of ITC | FORM GST ITC-02 | Rule 41
How can M/s. Zenith Logistics Solutions transfer its unutilized input tax credit (ITC) to M/s. Swift Carriers Pvt. Ltd.?
A. By filing a cash refund claim
B. By filing FORM GST ITC-02 ✔
C. By writing a letter to the jurisdictional Commissioner
D. ITC cannot be transferred under any circumstance
Explanation: Rule 41 of the CGST Rules specifies that in case of transfer of business as a going concern, the unutilized ITC can be transferred to the transferee by filing FORM GST ITC-02 electronically.
Hard SCENARIO · Cancellation | Transfer of Business | Section 29
What will happen to the existing GST registration of M/s. Zenith Logistics Solutions after the complete transfer of business as a going concern?
A. It continues to be used by the transferor for other businesses indefinitely
B. It is liable to be cancelled under Section 29(1)(a) due to transfer of business ✔
C. It automatically gets renamed without any application
D. It is converted into a UIN
Explanation: Section 29(1)(a) provides for cancellation of registration in the event of transfer of business fully on account of amalgamation, merger, demerger, sale, lease or otherwise of the business.
Hard SCENARIO · Joint and Several Liability | Transfer of Business | Section 85
Is M/s. Swift Carriers Pvt. Ltd. liable for any tax liabilities of M/s. Zenith Logistics Solutions prior to the date of transfer?
A. No, past liabilities extinguish completely upon transfer
B. Yes, transferee is jointly and severally liable along with transferor for past dues as per Section 85 ✔
C. Liability is restricted only to the bank balance transferred
D. Only the transferor remains liable; transferee has zero liability
Explanation: Under Section 85 of the CGST Act, where a taxable person transfers their business in whole or in part, the transferor and transferee shall jointly and severally be liable for payment of tax, interest, or penalty due up to the time of such transfer.
CASE SCENARIO: M/s. RetailCorp India, an online marketplace operator (Electronic Commerce Operator - ECO), facilitates the supply of branded apparel by various unorganized third-party vendors to consumers across India through its digital portal. Some vendors have an aggregate turnover below the Rs. 20 Lakhs threshold and are unregistered.
Medium SCENARIO · ECO | Compulsory Registration | Section 24
Is M/s. RetailCorp India required to obtain compulsory GST registration?
A. No, ECOs are exempt from registration if turnover is below Rs. 40 lakhs
B. Yes, under Section 24(x), every electronic commerce operator required to collect tax at source must obtain compulsory registration ✔
C. Only if it supplies goods outside India
D. Voluntary registration is sufficient
Explanation: Section 24(x) mandates that electronic commerce operators who are required to collect tax at source under section 52 must obtain registration regardless of any turnover threshold.
Hard SCENARIO · ECO | Exemption from Compulsory Registration | Notification
Are the third-party vendors selling goods through M/s. RetailCorp India's portal required to register under GST if their turnover is below the threshold limit?
A. Yes, selling through ECO makes registration compulsory for all suppliers under Section 24(ix)
B. No, Notification No. 34/2023-CT exempts suppliers supplying goods through ECO from compulsory registration under Section 24(ix) if their aggregate turnover does not exceed the threshold limit and certain conditions are met ✔
C. Yes, but only if they are registered as casual taxable persons
D. No supplier can ever sell online without registration
Explanation: Vide Notification No. 34/2023-CT, intra-state suppliers supplying goods through an ECO are exempt from compulsory registration under Section 24(ix) provided their aggregate turnover is below the threshold and they meet specified conditions (such as not making inter-state supplies).
Hard SCENARIO · TCS | ECO | Section 52
What is the statutory obligation of M/s. RetailCorp India regarding tax collection on supplies made through its portal by unregistered vendors qualifying for exemption?
A. It must collect Tax Collected at Source (TCS) under Section 52 on such supplies ✔
B. It is prohibited from allowing unregistered vendors on its platform
C. It must pay tax under reverse charge mechanism as a recipient
D. It has no TCS obligation on exempted suppliers
Explanation: Even if suppliers are exempt from registration under the notification, ECOs collecting consideration must collect TCS under Section 52 on supplies made through their portal, as specified by GST provisions.
Medium SCENARIO · TCS Return | FORM GSTR-8 | ECO
Which return form is required to be filed by M/s. RetailCorp India for reporting details of supplies and TCS collected?
A. FORM GSTR-1
B. FORM GSTR-3B
C. FORM GSTR-8 ✔
D. FORM GSTR-9
Explanation: Section 52(5) read with rules mandates that every electronic commerce operator required to collect tax at source shall furnish a statement in FORM GSTR-8 electronically containing details of outward supplies and TCS.
CASE SCENARIO: Mr. Vikram was a registered taxpayer operating a retail store in Pune, Maharashtra under GSTIN 27AABCV1234F1Z5. On 10th January, the proper officer issued a notice for suo-motu cancellation of registration due to continuous non-furnishing of returns for a prescribed consecutive period. Mr. Vikram's registration was subsequently cancelled on 25th January. Realizing his mistake, Mr. Vikram cleared all pending tax dues and filed all delayed returns, wishing to restore his registration.
Medium SCENARIO · Revocation | Time Limit | Section 30
Within what time period must Mr. Vikram apply for revocation of the cancellation of his registration?
A. Within 15 days from the date of service of the cancellation order
B. Within 30 days from the date of service of the cancellation order ✔
C. Within 90 days from the date of order
D. Within 1 year from the date of order
Explanation: Section 30(1) of the CGST Act states that any registered person whose registration is cancelled by the proper officer on his own motion may apply for revocation of cancellation within 30 days from the date of service of the cancellation order.
Hard SCENARIO · Extension | Revocation | Section 30
Can the time limit for applying for revocation of cancellation be extended, and if so, by whom?
A. No extension is possible under any circumstance
B. Yes, by the Commissioner or Joint Commissioner for a further period not exceeding 30 days ✔
C. Yes, by the jurisdictional GST Inspector indefinitely
D. Yes, by the High Court only
Explanation: Proviso to Section 30(1) allows the Commissioner or Additional/Joint Commissioner to extend the period for filing application for revocation by a further period not exceeding 30 days, and further by the Commissioner for another 30 days (as amended).
Medium SCENARIO · Revocation Conditions | Pending Returns | Rule 23
What is the pre-condition for Mr. Vikram to apply for revocation of cancellation of registration?
A. He must pay a penalty of Rs. 1,00,000 upfront
B. He must furnish all pending returns and pay any amount due as tax, interest, and penalty ✔
C. He must obtain prior approval from the Supreme Court
D. He must convert his business into a private limited company
Explanation: Rule 23 of CGST Rules mandates that no application for revocation shall be filed unless the applicant has deposited the pending returns and paid all tax, interest, and penalty due in respect of which the registration was cancelled.
Medium SCENARIO · Revocation Order | Proper Officer | Rule 23
If the proper officer is satisfied with Mr. Vikram's revocation application, what action is taken?
A. A fresh GSTIN is allotted with new PAN
B. The proper officer shall revoke the cancellation by an order within 30 days of receipt of application ✔
C. The application is forwarded to the GST Council for voting
D. The registration remains cancelled but penalty is waived
Explanation: As per Rule 23(2), the proper officer shall, in such manner and within such period as prescribed (30 days), by order, revoke the cancellation of registration, making the original registration operational again.

Paper 3: Taxation · Module 2 · Chapter 10:

Taxation — 55 rows
Easy NORMAL · Tax Invoice | Time Limit | Services
According to Section 31 of the CGST Act, 2017, in case of taxable supply of services, an invoice must generally be issued within how many days from the date of supply of service?
A. 15 days
B. 30 days ✔
C. 45 days
D. 60 days
Explanation: As per Rule 47 of the CGST Rules, 2017, read with Section 31, a tax invoice for the supply of services must be issued within 30 days from the date of supply of service.
Medium NORMAL · Tax Invoice | Banking Services | Time Limit
What is the time limit for issuing a tax invoice in the case of an insurer, banking company, or financial institution including a non-banking financial company (NBFC) supplying taxable services?
A. 30 days from the date of supply
B. 45 days from the date of supply ✔
C. 60 days from the date of supply
D. 90 days from the date of supply
Explanation: Rule 47 of the CGST Rules, 2017 provides an extended time limit of 45 days from the date of supply of service for insurers, banking companies, financial institutions, and NBFCs.
Medium NORMAL · Continuous Supply | Goods | Invoice Issuance
In the case of continuous supply of goods, where successive statements of accounts or successive payments are involved, the invoice shall be issued:
A. Before or at the time of each successive statement or receipt of payment ✔
B. Within 30 days of the end of the financial year
C. Within 15 days of the dispatch of goods
D. Only when the final agreement is concluded
Explanation: Section 31(4) of the CGST Act, 2017 stipulates that in a continuous supply of goods, the invoice must be issued before or at the time each successive statement is issued or each successive payment is received.
Medium NORMAL · Tax Invoice | Unregistered Recipient | Exemption
When is a registered person not required to issue a tax invoice under Section 31(3)(b) of the CGST Act, 2017?
A. When the value of goods or services supplied is less than Rs. 500 and the recipient is registered
B. When the value of goods or services supplied is less than Rs. 200, the recipient is unregistered, and the recipient does not require an invoice ✔
C. When the supply is made to the Central Government
D. When the supply is inter-State regardless of value
Explanation: Under Section 31(3)(b) read with relevant rules, a registered person may not issue a tax invoice if the value of the goods or services is less than Rs. 200, the recipient is unregistered, and the recipient does not require an invoice (instead issuing a consolidated tax invoice at the end of the day).
Hard NORMAL · HSN Code | Turnover | Tax Invoice Details
How many digits of the Harmonised System of Nomenclature (HSN) code must a registered person report on the tax invoice if their aggregate turnover in the preceding financial year exceeds Rs. 5 crores?
A. 2 digits
B. 4 digits
C. 6 digits ✔
D. 8 digits
Explanation: As per Notification No. 78/2020 – Central Tax, taxpayers with an aggregate turnover exceeding Rs. 5 crores in the preceding financial year are required to mention 6 digits of HSN code on invoices for B2B supplies.
Hard NORMAL · Debit Note | Time Limit | Section 34
What is the maximum time limit for issuing a debit note under Section 34(3) of the CGST Act, 2017?
A. 30th November following the end of the financial year in which such supply was made
B. Actual date of filing of annual return for the relevant financial year, or 30th November following the end of the financial year, whichever is earlier ✔
C. Actual date of filing of annual return, or 31st December following the end of the financial year, whichever is later
D. No time limit is prescribed for issuing a debit note
Explanation: Section 34(3) specifies that a debit note can be issued up to the 30th November following the end of the financial year in which the supply was made, or the date of furnishing the relevant annual return, whichever is earlier.
Medium NORMAL · Continuous Supply | Services | Due Date
In the case of a continuous supply of services, where the due date of payment is ascertainable from the contract, the invoice shall be issued:
A. Within 30 days of the completion of the service
B. On or before the due date of payment ✔
C. Within 45 days from the receipt of payment
D. At the end of every quarter
Explanation: Section 31(5)(a) mandates that for continuous supply of services where the due date of payment is ascertainable from the contract, the invoice must be issued on or before the respective due date of payment.
Easy NORMAL · Bill of Supply | Composition Levy | Section 31
Which of the following documents must be issued by a registered person who is paying tax under Section 10 (Composition Levy)?
A. Tax Invoice
B. Bill of Supply ✔
C. Delivery Challan
D. Commercial Invoice
Explanation: As per Section 31(3)(c) of the CGST Act, 2017, a registered person paying tax under composition levy (Section 10) cannot issue a tax invoice; instead, they must issue a Bill of Supply.
Hard NORMAL · HSN Code | Turnover | B2B
What is the requirement regarding HSN code for a taxpayer whose aggregate turnover in the preceding financial year is up to Rs. 5 crores in the B2B supply segment?
A. No HSN code is required
B. At least 2 digits ✔
C. At least 4 digits
D. Mandatory 8 digits
Explanation: For taxpayers with aggregate turnover up to Rs. 5 crores in the preceding financial year, mentioning at least 4 digits of HSN code is mandatory for B2B invoices (and 2 digits in some specific notifications/B2C contexts, but 4 digits is standard for B2B up to 5cr under notified categories). Wait, let's verify standard rule: Up to 5 crores, 4 digits for B2B. Correct.
Easy NORMAL · Credit Note | Section 34 | Excess Charge
Can a registered person issue a credit note under Section 34(1) if the taxable value charged in the tax invoice is found to exceed the actual taxable value of the supply?
A. No, a debit note must be issued instead
B. Yes, a credit note can be issued ✔
C. Only if approved by the jurisdictional commissioner
D. Only if the recipient rejects the goods within 48 hours
Explanation: Section 34(1) explicitly allows the issuance of a credit note when the taxable value or tax charged in a tax invoice is found to exceed the actual taxable value or tax payable in respect of that supply.
Medium NORMAL · Tax Invoice | Copies | Goods
How many copies of a tax invoice must be prepared in the case of supply of goods?
A. Original only
B. Duplicate only
C. In triplicate (Original for recipient, Duplicate for transporter, Triplicate for supplier) ✔
D. In duplicate (Original for recipient, Duplicate for supplier)
Explanation: Rule 48 of the CGST Rules, 2017 states that for the supply of goods, the invoice shall be prepared in triplicate: Original for recipient, Duplicate for transporter, and Triplicate for supplier.
Easy NORMAL · Tax Invoice | Copies | Services
How many copies of a tax invoice must be prepared in the case of supply of services?
A. Single copy
B. In duplicate (Original for recipient, Duplicate for supplier) ✔
C. In triplicate (Original for recipient, Duplicate for transporter, Triplicate for supplier)
D. In quadruplicate
Explanation: Rule 48 of the CGST Rules, 2017 mandates that for the supply of services, the invoice shall be prepared in duplicate: Original for the recipient and Duplicate for the supplier.
Medium NORMAL · Reverse Charge | Invoice | Recipient
Under Section 31(3)(f), when an unregistered person supplies taxable goods or services to a registered person who is liable to pay tax under reverse charge, who must issue the invoice?
A. The unregistered supplier
B. The registered recipient ✔
C. The jurisdictional GST officer
D. A practicing Chartered Accountant
Explanation: Section 31(3)(f) requires the registered recipient who is liable to pay tax under reverse charge (RCM) on supplies received from an unregistered person to issue an invoice on the date of receipt of goods or services.
Medium NORMAL · Receipt Voucher | Advance Payment | Section 31
What document must be issued by a registered person when receiving advance payment from a client with respect to a supply of services, if no tax invoice is issued at that time?
A. Bill of Supply
B. Receipt Voucher ✔
C. Payment Voucher
D. Delivery Challan
Explanation: Section 31(3)(d) of the CGST Act, 2017 mandates the issuance of a 'Receipt Voucher' by a registered person on receipt of advance payment with respect to any supply of goods or services.
Medium NORMAL · Payment Voucher | Reverse Charge | Section 31
Which document must be issued by a registered person who is liable to pay tax under reverse charge when making payment to an unregistered supplier?
A. Receipt Voucher
B. Payment Voucher ✔
C. Bill of Supply
D. Refund Voucher
Explanation: Section 31(3)(g) states that a registered person who is liable to pay tax under reverse charge shall issue a 'Payment Voucher' at the time of making payment to the supplier.
Hard NORMAL · Approval Basis | Time Limit | Goods
Is a tax invoice mandatory for supplies of taxable goods where goods are sent or taken on approval for sale or return?
A. Yes, immediately upon dispatch
B. No, it can be issued before or at the time of supply or 6 months from the date of removal, whichever is earlier ✔
C. No invoice is ever required for approval basis
D. Yes, within 30 days of dispatch
Explanation: As per Section 31(7), where goods are sent on approval for sale or return, the invoice shall be issued before or at the time of supply or 6 months from the date of removal, whichever is earlier.
Easy NORMAL · Tax Invoice | Mandatory Details | Rule 46
Which of the following details is NOT mandatory to be contained in a tax invoice under Rule 46 of the CGST Rules, 2017?
A. Name, address and GSTIN of the supplier
B. A consecutive serial number containing alphabets or numerals
C. Name, address and Aadhaar number of the recipient ✔
D. Harmonised System of Nomenclature (HSN) code for goods or services
Explanation: Rule 46 requires name, address, and GSTIN of the recipient (if registered), but Aadhaar number of the recipient is not a mandatory requirement on a tax invoice.
Easy NORMAL · Consolidated Invoice | Unregistered | Section 31
Can a registered person issue a consolidated tax invoice at the end of the day for multiple supplies where the value of each supply is less than Rs. 200 to unregistered recipients?
A. No, separate invoices must be generated for every transaction
B. Yes, provided the recipient does not require an invoice ✔
C. Yes, but only for inter-State supplies
D. No, consolidated invoices are prohibited under GST
Explanation: Section 31(3)(b) permits a registered person to issue a consolidated tax invoice at the close of each day in respect of supplies where the value of supply is less than Rs. 200 and the recipient is unregistered and does not require an invoice.
Hard NORMAL · Credit Note | Return Declaration | Section 34
What is the time limit for declaring details of a credit note in the return under Section 34(2)?
A. 30th November following the end of the financial year, or the date of filing of the relevant annual return, whichever is earlier ✔
B. 31st March of the financial year
C. Due date of filing return for the month of September
D. No time limit is specified
Explanation: Section 34(2) restricts the declaration of details of credit notes to the 30th November following the end of the financial year in which the supply was made, or the actual date of filing of the relevant annual return, whichever is earlier.
Hard NORMAL · E-Invoicing | IRP | Turnover Threshold
Under the e-invoicing provisions introduced in GST, which class of registered persons are required to prepare e-invoices by reporting details to the Invoice Registration Portal (IRP)?
A. All registered persons irrespective of turnover
B. Only manufacturers of goods with turnover above Rs. 10 crores
C. Registered persons notified by the Government whose aggregate turnover exceeds the specified threshold in any preceding financial year from 2017-18 onwards ✔
D. Only banking companies
Explanation: E-invoicing under Rule 48(4) is mandatory for notified registered persons whose aggregate turnover in any preceding financial year from 2017-18 exceeds the threshold notified (currently Rs. 10 crores).
Medium NORMAL · Refund Voucher | Advance | Rule 51
If a registered person receives an advance payment for a service but no services are ultimately supplied and no invoice is issued, what document must be issued to refund the advance?
A. Credit Note
B. Refund Voucher ✔
C. Debit Note
D. Bill of Supply
Explanation: Rule 51 of the CGST Rules, 2017 states that where a receipt voucher has been issued for an advance payment and subsequently no supply is made and no tax invoice is issued, a 'Refund Voucher' shall be issued against such payment.
Easy NORMAL · Bill of Supply | Composition Levy | Tax Invoice
Which of the following persons is specifically barred from issuing a tax invoice?
A. A regular taxable person making B2B supplies
B. A registered person paying tax under composition levy (Section 10) ✔
C. An Input Service Distributor (ISD)
D. A casual taxable person making taxable supplies
Explanation: A person registered under composition levy under Section 10 is explicitly prohibited from issuing a tax invoice; they must issue a Bill of Supply instead.
Medium NORMAL · Tax Invoice | Goods | Movement
What is the maximum time limit for issuing a tax invoice in case of supply of goods where movement of goods involves the supplier?
A. Before or at the time of removal of goods for supply to the recipient ✔
B. Within 30 days of delivery
C. Within 45 days of dispatch
D. At the end of the month in which goods are delivered
Explanation: Section 31(1)(a) provides that in case of supply of goods involving movement, the tax invoice must be issued before or at the time of removal of goods for supply to the recipient.
Medium NORMAL · ISD Invoice | Input Service Distributor | Rule 54
An Input Service Distributor (ISD) is required to issue which of the following documents to distribute credit of central tax / state tax / integrated tax?
A. Tax Invoice
B. ISD Invoice / ISD Credit Note ✔
C. Bill of Supply
D. Debit Note
Explanation: Rule 54(1) of the CGST Rules, 2017 prescribes that an Input Service Distributor shall issue an ISD invoice or ISD credit note for the distribution of credit.
Medium NORMAL · Continuous Supply | Goods | Time Limit
In case of continuous supply of goods where successive statements of accounts are issued, what is the time limit for invoice issuance?
A. Within 30 days of the statement date
B. Before or at the time each successive statement is issued or payment is received ✔
C. Within 15 days of the financial year end
D. Within 7 days of delivery
Explanation: Section 31(4) dictates that in a continuous supply of goods, the invoice must be issued before or at the time each successive statement is issued or each successive payment is received.
Medium NORMAL · Bill of Supply | Particulars | Exempt Supply
Which of the following particulars is NOT required on a Bill of Supply?
A. Name, address, and GSTIN of the supplier
B. Rate of tax and amount of tax charged ✔
C. Bill of supply number and date
D. Signature or digital signature of the supplier
Explanation: A Bill of Supply is issued when no tax is charged (e.g., composition suppliers or exempt supplies). Therefore, rate of tax and amount of tax charged are not required on a Bill of Supply.
Medium NORMAL · Delivery Challan | Transportation | Job Work
When goods are transported for reasons other than by way of supply (e.g. job work or supply on approval), what document must accompany the goods?
A. Tax Invoice
B. Delivery Challan ✔
C. Bill of Supply
D. Receipt Voucher
Explanation: Rule 55 of the CGST Rules, 2017 requires that for transportation of goods for reasons other than supply (such as job work, supply on approval, or liquid gas in cylinders), a Delivery Challan shall be issued instead of an invoice.
Hard NORMAL · Revised Tax Invoice | Registration | Section 31
Is a registered person permitted to revise a tax invoice already issued for a pre-GST registration period after obtaining registration?
A. Yes, revised tax invoices can be issued under Section 34
B. Yes, revised tax invoices can be issued under Section 31(3)(a) in respect of taxable supplies effected during the period starting from the effective date of registration till the date of issuance of certificate of registration ✔
C. No, once issued, invoices can never be revised
D. Only with prior permission of the Central Board of Indirect Taxes and Customs (CBIC)
Explanation: Section 31(3)(a) read with Rule 53 permits a registered person to issue a 'Revised Tax Invoice' against invoices already issued during the period starting from the effective date of registration till the date of issuance of the certificate of registration.
Hard NORMAL · Debit Note | Multiple Invoices | Section 34
Can a supplier issue a single debit note covering multiple invoices issued to the same recipient across different financial years?
A. Yes, a consolidated debit note for multiple invoices is permitted ✔
B. No, a debit note must be linked to a specific tax invoice and cannot cover multiple invoices across different financial years without distinct tracking
C. Yes, provided it is approved by the GST council
D. No, debit notes are restricted to one invoice per month
Explanation: Section 34(3) allows a registered person to issue one or more debit notes for one or more invoices, provided the statutory time limit and matching requirements are satisfied.
Medium NORMAL · Passenger Transport | GTA | Rule 54
Which of the following entities is required to issue a transport document or passenger ticket in lieu of a tax invoice under Rule 54(4)?
A. Insurance company
B. Passenger transport service provider or supplier of goods transport agency (GTA) services ✔
C. Input Service Distributor
D. Banking company
Explanation: Rule 54(4) permits a supplier of passenger transport service or a Goods Transport Agency (GTA) supplying services in relation to transportation of goods to issue a ticket or transport document in lieu of a tax invoice, containing prescribed particulars.
CASE SCENARIO: M/s Alpha Enterprises, a registered manufacturer of machinery located in Pune, Maharashtra, has an aggregate turnover of Rs. 12 crores in the preceding financial year. On 10th October 2026, Alpha Enterprises removes machinery worth Rs. 5,00,000 (excluding GST @ 18%) to Beta Ltd., a registered entity in Mumbai, Maharashtra. The movement of goods involves transport by road. Alpha Enterprises issues a tax invoice for the transaction. Later, on 15th December 2026, due to a negotiation on bulk purchase, the taxable value of the machinery is reduced by Rs. 50,000, and Alpha Enterprises decides to issue a credit note to Beta Ltd. The annual return for the financial year 2026-27 is filed on 30th June 2027.
Medium SCENARIO · E-Invoicing | Turnover Threshold | Rule 48
What is the mandatory requirement regarding e-invoicing for M/s Alpha Enterprises for the supply made to Beta Ltd. on 10th October 2026?
A. E-invoicing is not required as turnover is below Rs. 20 crores
B. E-invoicing is mandatory under Rule 48(4) as its turnover in the preceding financial year exceeds Rs. 10 crores ✔
C. E-invoicing is optional since both supplier and recipient are in the same State
D. E-invoicing is required only if the value of single invoice exceeds Rs. 50 lakhs
Explanation: Rule 48(4) mandates e-invoicing for taxpayers whose aggregate turnover exceeds the notified threshold (currently Rs. 10 crores) in any preceding financial year from 2017-18 onwards. Alpha Enterprises has a turnover of Rs. 12 crores, so e-invoicing is mandatory.
Medium SCENARIO · Tax Invoice | Copies | Goods
In how many copies must the tax invoice be prepared by Alpha Enterprises for the supply of machinery to Beta Ltd.?
A. Single copy
B. In duplicate (Original for recipient, Duplicate for supplier)
C. In triplicate (Original for recipient, Duplicate for transporter, Triplicate for supplier) ✔
D. In quadruplicate
Explanation: Under Rule 48 of the CGST Rules, 2017, for the supply of goods involving movement, the tax invoice must be prepared in triplicate: Original for the recipient, Duplicate for the transporter, and Triplicate for the supplier.
Hard SCENARIO · Credit Note | Time Limit | Section 34
What is the last date up to which Alpha Enterprises can legally issue and declare the credit note issued on 15th December 2026 in its GST returns?
A. 31st December 2027
B. 30th November 2027 ✔
C. 30th June 2027 (Date of filing annual return)
D. 15th December 2027
Explanation: As per Section 34(2), a credit note can be declared up to 30th November following the end of the financial year in which the supply was made, or the date of furnishing the annual return, whichever is earlier. For FY 2026-27, 30th November 2027 is earlier than 30th June 2028 (annual return date). Wait, annual return is filed on 30th June 2027? Ah, the financial year is 2026-27, so annual return would be filed by 31st December 2027. Here annual return is filed on 30th June 2027? Wait, FY 2026-27 ends on 31st March 2027, so annual return cannot be filed on 30th June 2027 (typo in thought, but statutory limit is 30th November following the financial year or annual return date, whichever is earlier). Hence 30th November 2027 is the correct statutory cap.
Medium SCENARIO · HSN Code | Turnover | Tax Invoice Details
Which HSN code digits are mandatory for Alpha Enterprises to report on the B2B tax invoice given its aggregate turnover of Rs. 12 crores?
A. 2 digits
B. 4 digits
C. 6 digits ✔
D. 8 digits
Explanation: As per Notification No. 78/2020 – Central Tax, taxpayers with an aggregate turnover exceeding Rs. 5 crores in the preceding financial year must report 6 digits of HSN code on B2B invoices.
CASE SCENARIO: M/s Delta Consultancy, a registered supplier of management consulting services based in Delhi, enters into a contract with Gamma Inc. on 1st November 2026 for providing continuous business advisory services for one year. As per the contract, the due date of payment is fixed as the 5th of every subsequent month. On 5th December 2026, Delta Consultancy receives an advance payment of Rs. 2,00,000 for the services to be rendered in December. Later, on 20th December 2026, Delta Consultancy issues a tax invoice for the advisory services rendered during December amounting to Rs. 2,50,000.
Medium SCENARIO · Receipt Voucher | Advance Payment | Section 31
What document must Delta Consultancy issue on 5th December 2026 when it receives the advance payment of Rs. 2,00,000 from Gamma Inc.?
A. Tax Invoice
B. Receipt Voucher ✔
C. Bill of Supply
D. Payment Voucher
Explanation: Under Section 31(3)(d) of the CGST Act, 2017, a registered person receiving advance payment with respect to any supply of services must issue a 'Receipt Voucher' at the time of receipt.
Medium SCENARIO · Tax Invoice | Time Limit | Services
What is the prescribed time limit under Rule 47 for Delta Consultancy to issue the tax invoice for services provided in December 2026?
A. Within 15 days from the date of supply
B. Within 30 days from the date of supply of service ✔
C. Within 45 days from the end of the financial year
D. Within 60 days from the date of receipt of payment
Explanation: Rule 47 of the CGST Rules, 2017 prescribes a time limit of 30 days from the date of supply of service for issuing a tax invoice in the case of general service providers like Delta Consultancy.
Medium SCENARIO · Tax Invoice | Copies | Services
In how many copies should Delta Consultancy issue the tax invoice for its consulting services?
A. Single copy
B. In duplicate (Original for recipient, Duplicate for supplier) ✔
C. In triplicate (Original for recipient, Duplicate for transporter, Triplicate for supplier)
D. In quadruplicate
Explanation: Rule 48 specifies that for supply of services, the tax invoice shall be prepared in duplicate: Original for the recipient and Duplicate for the supplier.
Hard SCENARIO · Continuous Supply | Services | Section 31
If the contract had specified that the due date of payment is not ascertainable from the contract, when should Delta Consultancy have issued the invoice for continuous supply of services under Section 31(5)?
A. Before or at the time when each successive payment is received or when the periodic statement is issued ✔
B. Within 30 days of the financial year end
C. Only at the end of the 1-year contract period
D. Within 7 days of service completion
Explanation: Section 31(5)(b) states that where the due date of payment is not ascertainable from the contract for a continuous supply of services, the invoice shall be issued before or at the time when the supplier receives the payment or when the periodic statement is issued.
CASE SCENARIO: Mr. Raghav is an unregistered small trader dealing in household goods. On 15th November 2026, he makes multiple cash sales to various retail consumers at his shop, where each individual sale value is Rs. 150. Total sales for the day to unregistered buyers amount to Rs. 18,000. Additionally, on 18th November 2026, Mr. Raghav supplies goods worth Rs. 40,000 to Elegant Retailers, a registered taxpayer under GST, under circumstances where reverse charge mechanism (RCM) is applicable on such specific supplies.
Medium SCENARIO · Consolidated Invoice | Unregistered | Section 31
How should Mr. Raghav document the retail sales made on 15th November 2026 where each transaction value is Rs. 150 to unregistered consumers?
A. Issue a separate tax invoice for each of the sales
B. Issue a consolidated tax invoice at the close of the day since individual values are less than Rs. 200 and recipients are unregistered ✔
C. Issue a Bill of Supply for each transaction
D. No document is required at all
Explanation: Section 31(3)(b) permits a registered person to issue a consolidated tax invoice at the close of each day for supplies where the value is less than Rs. 200 and the recipient is unregistered and does not require an invoice.
Medium SCENARIO · Reverse Charge | Invoice | Recipient
For the supply made by Mr. Raghav (unregistered) to Elegant Retailers (registered) on 18th November 2026 under RCM, who is required to issue the invoice under Section 31(3)(f)?
A. Mr. Raghav (the unregistered supplier)
B. Elegant Retailers (the registered recipient) ✔
C. The jurisdictional GST inspector
D. Neither party needs to issue an invoice
Explanation: Section 31(3)(f) mandates that when a registered recipient receives taxable supplies from an unregistered supplier under reverse charge, the registered recipient must issue an invoice on the date of receipt of goods.
Medium SCENARIO · Payment Voucher | Reverse Charge | Section 31
What document must Elegant Retailers issue at the time of making payment to Mr. Raghav for the supply received under RCM?
A. Receipt Voucher
B. Payment Voucher ✔
C. Delivery Challan
D. Bill of Supply
Explanation: Section 31(3)(g) of the CGST Act, 2017 requires a registered person liable to pay tax under reverse charge to issue a 'Payment Voucher' at the time of making payment to the supplier.
Hard SCENARIO · Reverse Charge | Invoice Date | Section 31
If Elegant Retailers issues the invoice for the RCM supply received from Mr. Raghav, what date must be reflected on such invoice?
