A. Date of filing the monthly return
B. Date of receipt of goods or services ✔
C. Last day of the financial year
D. Date of dispatch by the unregistered supplier
Explanation: Section 31(3)(f) explicitly states that the registered recipient liable to pay tax under reverse charge shall issue an invoice on the date of receipt of goods or services.
CASE SCENARIO: M/s Zenith Traders, a registered dealer under composition levy under Section 10 of the CGST Act, 2017, operates a retail electronics store in Jaipur, Rajasthan. On 5th December 2026, Zenith Traders sells electronic accessories worth Rs. 25,000 to a walk-in retail customer. On 10th December 2026, Zenith Traders sends goods worth Rs. 60,000 on approval basis to a customer for potential purchase. The customer retains the goods and confirms purchase after 4 months on 10th April 2027.
Medium SCENARIO · Bill of Supply | Composition Levy | Section 31
What document must Zenith Traders issue to the retail customer on 5th December 2026 for the sale of electronic accessories?
A. Tax Invoice
B. Bill of Supply ✔
C. Delivery Challan
D. Commercial Invoice
Explanation: Section 31(3)(c) mandates that a registered person paying tax under composition levy (Section 10) cannot issue a tax invoice; instead, they must issue a Bill of Supply.
Medium SCENARIO · Composition Levy | Bill of Supply | Tax Collection
Can Zenith Traders collect tax separately from the customer on the Bill of Supply issued on 5th December 2026?
A. Yes, CGST and SGST can be collected separately
B. No, a composition taxpayer is not permitted to collect tax from the recipient ✔
C. Yes, if the customer is registered
D. Only on inter-State supplies
Explanation: Under Section 10(4) of the CGST Act, 2017, a composition taxpayer cannot collect any tax from the recipient on supplies made by them, nor are they entitled to any input tax credit.
Hard SCENARIO · Approval Basis | Time Limit | Section 31
For the goods sent on approval basis on 10th December 2026, what is the statutory time limit for Zenith Traders to issue the bill of supply / invoice?
A. Within 30 days from removal
B. Before or at the time of supply or 6 months from the date of removal, whichever is earlier ✔
C. Within 15 days of customer confirmation
D. At the end of the financial year
Explanation: Section 31(7) specifies that where goods are sent on approval for sale or return, the invoice/bill of supply shall be issued before or at the time of supply or 6 months from the date of removal, whichever is earlier.
Hard SCENARIO · Approval Basis | Time of Supply | Goods
When did the supply take place for the goods sent on approval on 10th December 2026 and confirmed on 10th April 2027?
A. 10th December 2026
B. 10th June 2027 (6 months from removal)
C. 10th April 2027 when the customer confirmed the purchase ✔
D. 31st March 2027
Explanation: Since the customer confirmed the purchase within 6 months (on 10th April 2027), the time of supply occurs when the recipient communicates approval/acceptance, i.e., 10th April 2027.
CASE SCENARIO: M/s Apex Logistics Ltd., a registered Goods Transport Agency (GTA) providing transportation of goods by road, makes a supply of transport services to various clients in January 2027. Apex Logistics opts to pay tax at 5% (with ITC on inputs restricted) on its services. On 12th January 2027, it transports a consignment of textiles for a registered textile manufacturer and issues a transport document in lieu of a tax invoice. Separately, on 20th January 2027, Apex Logistics moves its own internal office equipment to a branch office in another city without any transfer of ownership or sale.
Medium SCENARIO · GTA | Transport Document | Rule 54
What document is Apex Logistics permitted to issue in lieu of a tax invoice for the transportation of goods service provided on 12th January 2027 under Rule 54(4)?
A. Bill of Supply
B. Transport document (Consignment Note) ✔
C. Delivery Challan
D. Receipt Voucher
Explanation: Rule 54(4) of the CGST Rules, 2017 allows a supplier of GTA services or passenger transport services to issue a transport document (such as a Consignment Note) containing prescribed particulars in lieu of a tax invoice.
Medium SCENARIO · Delivery Challan | Branch Transfer | Rule 55
What document must accompany the movement of office equipment on 20th January 2027 since it is transported for reasons other than by way of supply?
A. Tax Invoice
B. Delivery Challan ✔
C. Bill of Supply
D. Payment Voucher
Explanation: Rule 55 stipulates that for transportation of goods for reasons other than supply (such as branch transfer or shifting of assets), a Delivery Challan must accompany the goods instead of a tax invoice.
Hard SCENARIO · E-Invoicing | GTA | Exemption
Is Apex Logistics required to issue an e-invoice for the GTA services provided if its aggregate turnover exceeds the e-invoicing threshold?
A. Yes, GTA services are subject to e-invoicing if turnover exceeds the threshold
B. No, GTA services supplying passenger or goods transport where a transport document is issued in lieu of tax invoice under Rule 54(4) are specifically exempt from e-invoicing ✔
C. Yes, regardless of rule 54(4)
D. Only if the recipient is unregistered
Explanation: As per notifications governing e-invoicing, specified categories of supplies including GTA services where a transport document is issued under Rule 54(4) instead of a tax invoice are exempt from e-invoicing requirements.
Hard SCENARIO · GTA | Transport Document | Rule 54 Details
What mandatory details must be contained in the transport document issued by Apex Logistics under Rule 54(4)?
A. Gross weight, name of consignor and consignee, registration number of vehicle, details of goods, and GSTIN of GTA (if registered) ✔
B. Only the vehicle number and date
C. Only the recipient's PAN and Aadhaar
D. Bank account details of the supplier only
Explanation: Rule 54(4) read with relevant provisions requires transport documents like consignment notes to contain serial number, gross weight, details of consignor/consignee, registration number of vehicle, origin/destination, and GSTIN of the GTA.

Paper 3: Taxation · Module 2 · Chapter 11:

Taxation — 55 rows
Easy NORMAL · Place of Maintenance | Section 35 | Books of Accounts
Where must a registered person maintain the books of accounts and other records under Section 35 of the CGST Act, 2017?
A. At the principal place of business mentioned in the certificate of registration ✔
B. At the registered office of the company anywhere outside India
C. At the residence of the managing director of the company
D. At any branch office, regardless of whether it is registered or not
Explanation: Section 35(1) of the CGST Act, 2017 mandates that every registered person shall keep and maintain all records at his principal place of business as mentioned in the certificate of registration. If more than one place of business is specified in the certificate, the accounts relating to each place of business shall be kept at such places of business.
Easy NORMAL · Retention Period | Section 35 | Annual Return
For how many years must a registered person maintain books of accounts and records under Section 35(1) of the CGST Act, 2017?
A. 36 months from the due date of furnishing of annual return
B. 72 months from the due date of furnishing of annual return ✔
C. 60 months from the end of the financial year
D. 84 months from the end of the calendar year
Explanation: According to Section 35(1), books of accounts and other records must be retained until the expiry of seventy-two months (6 years) from the due date of furnishing of the annual return for the year pertaining to such accounts and records.
Medium NORMAL · Retention Period | Appeals | Proviso to Section 35
What is the additional retention period for records in a case where an appeal or revision or proceedings are pending before any appellate authority or court?
A. Until one year after final disposal of such appeal or proceedings
B. For a period of one year after final disposal of such appeal or proceedings, or until the expiry of the regular 72 months, whichever is later ✔
C. For a period of two years after final disposal of such appeal
D. No additional period is required if 72 months have passed
Explanation: Proviso to Section 35(1) states that a registered person who is a party to an appeal or revision or any other proceedings before any appellate authority or court or is under investigation for an offence, shall retain the books of accounts pertaining to the subject matter for a period of one year after final disposal of such appeal/proceedings or until the expiry of seventy-two months, whichever is later.
Medium NORMAL · Manufacturer Records | Rule 56 | Quantitative Details
Which of the following specific records must a manufacturer maintain under Rule 56 of the CGST Rules, 2017?
A. Monthly balance sheet and cash flow statements only
B. Monthly production accounts showing quantitative details of raw materials or services used and finished goods produced ✔
C. Stock details of only imported goods
D. Details of all employees and their salaries
Explanation: Rule 56(1) of the CGST Rules, 2017 requires every registered person to keep books of accounts. Specifically, manufacturers must maintain monthly production accounts showing quantitative details of raw materials or services used in manufacture and finished goods produced.
Easy NORMAL · Agent Records | Rule 56 | Stockist
What records must a stockist, broker, or agent dealing in goods maintain under the GST framework?
A. Only bank statements and invoices
B. True and complete records of goods received and supplied, along with names and addresses of suppliers and buyers ✔
C. Only tax invoices issued to final consumers
D. Annual audit reports
Explanation: Under Rule 56(3), every agent, broker, or stockist must maintain true and complete records of the quantity of goods received and supplied by them, along with the particulars of the suppliers and buyers.
Easy NORMAL · Electronic Records | Section 35 | Authentication
In what format must accounts and records be maintained and preserved under the GST provisions?
A. Only in physical paper files bound with hard covers
B. Exclusively on cloud servers hosted within India
C. Either electronically or manually, provided that electronic records are backed up and accessible ✔
D. Exclusively in handwritten ledgers authenticated by a Chartered Accountant
Explanation: Section 35(1) read with Rule 56 permits the maintenance of books of accounts and other records in electronic form or manually. If maintained electronically, they must be authenticated by way of digital signature and proper backup mechanisms must be in place.
Medium NORMAL · Electronic Records | Rule 57 | Production of Records
What responsibility is cast upon a registered person maintaining electronic records if called upon by a proper officer?
A. To courier the entire server to the GST office
B. To provide the details of passwords, access codes, and files in hard copy or readable format along with a signed certification ✔
C. To allow the officer to change the encryption keys
D. To print all records and get them notarized
Explanation: Rule 57(2) stipulates that the person maintaining electronic records shall produce, on demand, the relevant files, passwords, access codes and numbers, and hard copies of the records as required by the proper officer.
Easy NORMAL · Stock Register | Rule 56 | Inventory
Who is required to maintain a stock register showing receipts, supplies, losses, and balance of goods under Rule 56(4)?
A. Only government undertakings
B. Every registered person ✔
C. Only composition taxpayers
D. Only persons having turnover exceeding Rs. 100 crores
Explanation: Rule 56(4) mandates that every registered person shall keep a true and correct account of stock in respect of goods received and supplied by him, including inventories, receipts, dispatches, wastage, and shortage.
Hard NORMAL · Section 35(2) | Unaccounted Goods | Tax Determination
Under Section 35(2), if a registered person fails to maintain accounts and records as specified, what action can the Commissioner or officer authorized take regarding goods?
A. Impose a penalty of Rs. 10,000 only
B. Determine the amount of tax payable on goods unaccounted for as if such goods had been supplied by him ✔
C. Cancel the registration without any show-cause notice
D. Auction the entire factory immediately
Explanation: Section 35(2) provides that where the registered person fails to account for the goods or services in accordance with the provisions, the proper officer shall determine the amount of tax payable on the goods or services that are not accounted for, as if such goods or services had been supplied by such person.
Medium NORMAL · Transporter Records | Warehouse Keeper | Section 35
What additional records must a godown or warehouse keeper or owner of a transport agency maintain, even if not registered?
A. Only balance sheets of their business
B. Records of the consigner, consignee, and other relevant details of goods transported, stored, or delivered ✔
C. Income tax returns of all clients
D. Audited financial statements for the past 10 years
Explanation: Section 35(2) and Rule 58 mandate that every owner or operator of warehouse or godown or any other place used for storage of goods and every transporter, irrespective of whether he is a registered person or not, shall maintain records of consigner, consignee, and goods stored or transported.
Medium NORMAL · ENR-01 | Transporter Enrollment | Rule 58
When must transporters and warehouse operators enroll or register on the GST portal if they are not otherwise registered under GST?
A. Within 30 days of starting operations
B. They are required to enroll and obtain a unique enrollment number in FORM GST ENR-01 ✔
C. They must obtain a regular GSTIN in all states
D. Enrollment is completely voluntary with no form requirement
Explanation: Rule 58 states that persons engaged in transporting goods or operating warehouses, if not registered under GST, shall maintain records and submit an application in FORM GST ENR-01 on the common portal to obtain a unique enrollment number.
Easy NORMAL · ITC Records | Rule 56 | Books of Accounts
What details regarding Input Tax Credit (ITC) must a registered person maintain in their books of accounts under Rule 56?
A. Only the total ITC claimed in the annual return
B. Monthly accounts showing input tax credit availed, utilized, and balance ✔
C. Bank certificates of ITC payment
D. Only the ITC pertaining to capital goods
Explanation: Rule 56(2) requires every registered person to keep books of accounts including records of input tax credit availed, utilized, and the balance of ITC available.
Hard NORMAL · GST Audit | Section 35(5) | Omission | GSTR-9C
Who is required to get their accounts audited by a Chartered Accountant or Cost Accountant under Section 35(5) of the CGST Act?
A. Every registered person with turnover exceeding Rs. 2 crores
B. All registered persons
C. Section 35(5) requiring mandatory GST audit by a CA/CMA has been omitted, and registered persons now submit an Annual Return along with a self-certified Reconciliation Statement (GSTR-9C) ✔
D. Only companies registered under the Companies Act, 2013
Explanation: Section 35(5) which mandated GST audit by a Chartered Accountant or Cost Accountant was omitted by the Finance Act, 2021. Registered persons now furnish an annual return in GSTR-9 along with a self-certified reconciliation statement in GSTR-9C under Section 44.
Easy NORMAL · Multiple Places of Business | Rule 56 | Maintenance
Under Rule 56(11), if a registered person has multiple places of business, where should the accounts relating to each place be kept?
A. At the head office only
B. At the respective place of business mentioned in the certificate of registration ✔
C. Anywhere within the home state
D. At the office of their principal tax consultant
Explanation: Rule 56(11) specifies that books of accounts relating to multiple places of business shall be kept at such respective places of business as mentioned in the certificate of registration.
Easy NORMAL · Invoices | Rule 56 | Debit/Credit Notes
Which of the following records must be maintained regarding tax invoice, debit note, and credit note under Rule 56?
A. Only outward invoices issued
B. Full details of tax invoices, bills of supply, delivery challans, credit notes, and debit notes issued and received ✔
C. Only copies of invoices exceeding Rs. 50,000
D. Invoices received from unregistered persons only
Explanation: Rule 56(1) requires maintenance of accounts of all goods and services supplied, including invoices, bills of supply, debit notes, credit notes, and delivery challans issued or received.
Medium NORMAL · Electronic Records | Rule 57 | Backup
If a registered person destroys or misplaces their electronic records, can they plead defense that the computer crashed?
A. Yes, system crashes exempt the person from maintaining records
B. No, maintaining backup and ensuring safety and recoverability of electronic records is the statutory responsibility of the registered person ✔
C. Yes, if reported to the police within 24 hours
D. Only if the server was located outside India
Explanation: Rule 57 mandates that the person maintaining electronic records must produce them on demand and ensure proper backups. Failure to maintain or produce records due to system failure without backup does not absolve the taxpayer from statutory penalties.
Medium NORMAL · Penalty | Section 125 | Non-compliance
What is the consequence if a registered person fails to maintain books of accounts as required under Section 35?
A. Only a warning letter is issued
B. General penalty provisions under Section 125 may apply along with tax determination on unaccounted goods under Section 35(2) ✔
C. Automatic imprisonment for 5 years
D. Suspension of bank accounts by the RBI
Explanation: Failure to maintain books of accounts attracts general penalties under Section 125 of the CGST Act, and the proper officer can also invoke Section 35(2) to determine tax on unaccounted goods/services.
Medium NORMAL · Inspection | Section 67 | Powers of Officer
Are the accounts maintained by a registered person open to inspection by GST officers?
A. No, inspection requires a court warrant
B. Yes, upon authorization by an officer not below the rank of Joint Commissioner ✔
C. Only during the annual filing period
D. Only if the taxpayer consents in writing
Explanation: Under Section 67 of the CGST Act, proper officers authorized by the Commissioner (not below the rank of Joint Commissioner) can inspect places of business and examine books of accounts and records.
Medium NORMAL · Advances | Rule 56 | Tax Records
What particulars must be maintained regarding 'advance payments' received or made by a registered person?
A. Advance payments are not required to be recorded in GST books
B. Full details of advances received, adjustments made against supplies, and advance payments made to suppliers ✔
C. Only advances received in foreign currency
D. Only advances exceeding Rs. 10 lakhs
Explanation: Rule 56(1) explicitly requires maintaining accounts of advances received and paid, along with adjustments made against invoices, as tax liability on advances for services (and earlier goods) requires proper tracking.
Medium NORMAL · Place of Business | Additional Place | Section 35
Can a registered person maintain records at a place other than the principal place of business?
A. No, never
B. Yes, if an additional place of business is declared in the registration certificate or if approved by the Commissioner for specific accounts ✔
C. Yes, anywhere in the world without notification
D. Only if the turnover is below Rs. 40 lakhs
Explanation: Records must be kept at the principal place of business and additional place(s) of business mentioned in the registration certificate. If records are maintained at multiple places, they must correspond to those specific registered locations.
Hard NORMAL · Works Contract | Rule 56(13) | Specific Records
What specific records must a works contract service provider maintain under Rule 56?
A. Names and addresses of all sub-contractors, property owners, and details of payment, materials consumed, and invoices raised ✔
B. Only architectural blueprints
C. Only municipal corporation approvals
D. Balance sheet of the building owner
Explanation: Rule 56(13) mandates that a works contract supplier shall keep separate accounts for each works contract showing names and addresses of employers, suppliers, sub-contractors, description, value, and quantity of goods or services used.
Hard NORMAL · Transporter | Exempt Goods | Section 35(2)
Is a transporter required to maintain records of goods even if the goods are exempt from GST?
A. No, exempt goods need no documentation
B. Yes, transporters and warehouse keepers must maintain records of all goods transported or stored, regardless of taxability ✔
C. Only if the value exceeds Rs. 50,000
D. Only if requested by the transporter association
Explanation: Section 35(2) and Rule 58 apply to transporters and warehouse operators for all goods handled by them, irrespective of whether the goods are taxable or exempt from GST.
Medium NORMAL · Electronic Records | Rule 57 | Non-compliance
What is the consequence of failing to produce electronic records in readable format when demanded by a proper officer?
A. The officer will print them free of cost
B. It is treated as non-compliance, inviting penal action for failure to maintain/produce records ✔
C. The taxpayer gets an automatic 30-day extension
D. The records are permanently deleted from the portal
Explanation: Failure to produce electronic records, access codes, and passwords on demand violates Rule 57 and attracts penalties under the provisions of the CGST Act.
Easy NORMAL · Section 35 | Applicability | Personal Consumption
Which of the following persons is NOT specifically mentioned under Section 35(1) to maintain books of accounts?
A. A registered person
B. A custodian of goods who is not a registered person
C. A clearing and forwarding agent
D. An unregistered individual buying goods for personal consumption ✔
Explanation: Unregistered individuals buying goods for personal consumption are final consumers and do not carry on business; hence, they have no statutory obligation to maintain books of accounts under Section 35.
Medium NORMAL · Authentication | Rule 57 | Digital Signature
If records are maintained in electronic form, who must authenticate them?
A. Any employee of the company
B. The registered person or an authorized representative using a digital signature ✔
C. The jurisdictional GST Inspector
D. A statutory auditor
Explanation: Rule 57 requires that electronic records must be authenticated by way of digital signature by the registered person or their authorized representative.
Easy NORMAL · Outward Supplies | Rule 56 | Invoices
What details regarding outward supplies must be kept in the accounts under Rule 56?
A. Total sales figure for the year only
B. Invoices, debit notes, credit notes, statements of outward supplies, and tax collected and paid ✔
C. Only cash sales records
D. Only B2B export supplies
Explanation: Rule 56(2) requires maintaining accounts of goods and services imported or exported, and supplies foothills/outward supplies along with tax charged.
Hard NORMAL · Manual Records | Rule 56(5) | Corrections
How should a registered person handle corrections or alterations made in manual books of accounts?
A. Correction fluid must be used to erase the wrong entry
B. Incorrect entry should be scored out under signature, and the correct entry recorded, preserving audit trail ✔
C. Pages containing errors should be torn out
D. No corrections are allowed under any circumstances
Explanation: Rule 56(5) mandates that manual accounts, registers, and documents shall be maintained sequentially, and any entry shall not be erased, obliterated, or scraped. Corrections should be made properly with initials.
Medium NORMAL · Hotel Records | Rule 56(7) | Specific Industry
Under Rule 56, what records must be maintained by an owner or operator of a hotel regarding accommodation?
A. Names and addresses of guests, arrival and departure dates, and room tariff charged ✔
B. Only food and beverage sales
C. Only electricity consumption bills
D. Only employee attendance registers
Explanation: Rule 56(7) requires owners or operators of hotels, inns, guest houses, clubs, or similar places to maintain accounts containing details of guests staying, including names and addresses, duration of stay, and room tariff.
Hard NORMAL · Retention Period | Investigation | Fraud
What is the prescribed retention period for accounts and records if an assessment year is under scrutiny for fraud, suppression, or wilful misstatement?
A. 72 months from the due date of annual return
B. Up to 72 months, but extended if proceedings/appeals are pending or investigation for an offence is active ✔
C. 10 years from the end of the calendar year
D. Permanent retention
Explanation: Under the proviso to Section 35(1), when proceedings/appeals or investigations for an offence are active, records must be retained for one year after final disposal or 72 months, whichever is later.
Hard NORMAL · Section 35(1) | Government Powers | GST Council
Which authority has the power to notify a class of taxable persons to maintain additional records under Section 35(1)?
A. The State GST Commissioner alone
B. The Government on the recommendations of the GST Council ✔
C. The jurisdictional Superintendent of Central Tax
D. The Comptroller and Auditor General of India (CAG)
Explanation: Section 35(1) empowers the Government, on the recommendations of the GST Council, to notify a class of taxable persons to maintain any additional records or accounts as specified.
CASE SCENARIO: M/s Apex Traders, a registered taxpayer under GST in Mumbai, deals in electronic appliances. They have a principal place of business in Andheri and an additional warehouse in Bhiwandi. Due to expansion, they switch from manual ledgers to an Enterprise Resource Planning (ERP) software for maintaining electronic records. The due date for furnishing the annual return for FY 2023-24 was 31st December 2024.
Medium SCENARIO · Retention Period | Section 35 | Annual Return
Until what date must M/s Apex Traders mandatorily retain their books of accounts and records for FY 2023-24 under Section 35(1)?
A. 31st December 2029
B. 31st December 2030 ✔
C. 31st March 2030
D. 31st December 2031
Explanation: Section 35(1) requires records to be retained for 72 months (6 years) from the due date of furnishing the annual return. Since the due date is 31st December 2024, 72 months expire on 31st December 2030.
Medium SCENARIO · Place of Business | Warehouse | Rule 56
Where must M/s Apex Traders keep the accounts pertaining to their Bhiwandi warehouse?
A. Exclusively at their corporate head office in Delhi
B. At the Bhiwandi warehouse if specified as an additional place of business in the registration certificate ✔
C. At the residence of the accountant in Mumbai
D. Anywhere in the State of Maharashtra without registration declaration
Explanation: Under Section 35(1) and Rule 56(11), accounts relating to each place of business must be kept at such respective place of business mentioned in the certificate of registration.
Medium SCENARIO · Electronic Records | Rule 57 | Access Codes
Since M/s Apex Traders maintain electronic records on ERP software, what is their statutory obligation when demanded by a proper officer?
A. To allow the officer to delete unwanted files
B. To produce the relevant files, passwords, access codes, and hard copies as required ✔
C. To provide physical handwritten copies of all ERP entries
D. To purchase a new server for the GST department
Explanation: Rule 57(2) stipulates that the person maintaining electronic records shall produce passwords, access codes, and files on demand by the proper officer.
Hard SCENARIO · Retention Period | Investigation | Proviso to Section 35
Suppose an investigation for an offence under GST is initiated against M/s Apex Traders for FY 2023-24, and proceedings are pending on 31st December 2030. When does their record retention obligation end?
A. 31st December 2030 itself
B. One year after the final disposal of such proceedings or 31st December 2030, whichever is later ✔
C. Immediately upon the start of investigation
D. After 10 years from the financial year end
Explanation: Proviso to Section 35(1) dictates that if proceedings or investigations are pending, records must be retained for one year after final disposal of such proceedings or until the expiry of 72 months, whichever is later.
CASE SCENARIO: Shreeji Transport Agency operates a fleet of trucks transporting goods across multiple states, but is not registered as a taxable supplier under GST. They store goods temporarily in transit godowns located in Gujarat. The proper officer during a verification drive requests Shreeji Transport Agency to produce records of consignments handled during the past quarter.
Medium SCENARIO · Transporter Records | Section 35(2) | Rule 58
Is Shreeji Transport Agency legally required to maintain records of goods despite not being a registered taxable person?
A. No, only registered persons under Section 22/24 must maintain records
B. Yes, under Section 35(2) and Rule 58, transporters and godown owners must maintain records of consigner, consignee, and goods ✔
C. Only if their annual turnover exceeds Rs. 20 crores
D. Only if they cross state borders
Explanation: Section 35(2) and Rule 58 mandate that transporters, warehouse keepers, and godown owners must maintain records of goods transported, stored, or delivered, irrespective of whether they are registered taxpayers.
Medium SCENARIO · ENR-01 | Transporter Enrollment | Rule 58
What registration/enrollment requirement applies to Shreeji Transport Agency on the GST portal if they are not registered under GST?
A. They must obtain a regular GSTIN in Gujarat
B. They must enroll and obtain a unique enrollment number in FORM GST ENR-01 ✔
C. They must register under the Shops and Establishment Act only
D. No portal interaction is required
Explanation: Rule 58 specifies that transporters not registered under GST shall submit an application in FORM GST ENR-01 on the common portal to obtain a unique enrollment number.
Medium SCENARIO · Transporter Records | Rule 58 | Consignee Details
What specific details must Shreeji Transport Agency maintain in their transport records?
A. Only vehicle maintenance bills and diesel receipts
B. Full details of goods transported, including consigner, consignee, delivery status, and vehicle numbers ✔
C. Income tax PAN of all drivers
D. Balance sheet of the transport owner
Explanation: Under Rule 58, transporters must maintain records of goods transported, delivered, or stored in transit, including particulars of consigner and consignee.
Hard SCENARIO · Penalties | Transporter Non-compliance | Section 35
If Shreeji Transport Agency fails to maintain records as required under Section 35(2), what is the implication?
A. They are immune since they are uninvited transporters
B. They may face penalties and liability under GST provisions applicable to non-maintenance of records ✔
C. Their trucks will be gifted to the government
D. They only receive a verbal warning from the inspector
Explanation: Failure by transporters or godown keepers to maintain prescribed records attracts penal consequences under the CGST Act provisions.
CASE SCENARIO: M/s BuildWell Engineers, a registered works contractor in Karnataka, undertakes construction of commercial complexes. They engage multiple sub-contractors for electrical, plumbing, and structural works. During an audit by tax authorities, the proper officer asks for contract-wise accounts and details of materials supplied and consumed at various project sites.
Medium SCENARIO · Works Contract | Rule 56(13) | Contract-wise Accounts
Under Rule 56(13), what specific accounting obligation is placed on M/s BuildWell Engineers as a works contractor?
A. To maintain a single consolidated bank account statement
B. To keep separate accounts for each works contract showing names/addresses of employers, suppliers, sub-contractors, and materials used ✔
C. To audit only the profit and loss account of the head office
D. To maintain records only for completed contracts
Explanation: Rule 56(13) mandates that a works contractor shall keep separate accounts for each works contract showing details of employers, sub-contractors, and quantities/values of goods or services used.
Medium SCENARIO · Stock Records | Rule 56 | Site Inventory
Must M/s BuildWell Engineers maintain records of goods received from sub-contractors at project sites?
A. No, sub-contractors maintain their own records
B. Yes, true and correct records of goods received and supplied, including wastage and shortage at each site, must be maintained ✔
C. Only if the value exceeds Rs. 1 crore per site
D. Only if requested by the local municipality
Explanation: Rule 56 requires every registered person, including contractors, to maintain stock accounts and records of inputs received, issued, and stock balances at each operational site.
Hard SCENARIO · Section 35(2) | Unaccounted Goods | Tax Determination
If M/s BuildWell Engineers fail to account for certain construction materials found at a project site during inspection, how can the proper officer proceed under Section 35(2)?
A. Ignore the discrepancy if total turnover is high
B. Determine the amount of tax payable on such unaccounted goods as if supplied by them ✔
C. Order immediate demolition of the building
D. Suspend the GST registration of the project land owner
Explanation: Section 35(2) empowers the proper officer to determine tax on unaccounted goods or services as if they had been supplied by the registered person.
Medium SCENARIO · Place of Business | Project Sites | Rule 56(11)
Where should M/s BuildWell Engineers maintain the site-specific accounts for an ongoing project located in Mysore, given their principal place of business is in Bengaluru?
A. Only at the Bengaluru head office
B. At the respective project site in Mysore if registered as an additional place of business, or at the principal place of business ✔
C. At the residence of the site engineer
D. At the bank locker in Mysore
Explanation: Accounts relating to each place of business (including project sites registered as additional places of business) must be kept at such places as mentioned in the registration certificate.
CASE SCENARIO: M/s GreenLeaf Hospitality Ltd. operates a luxury hotel and resort in Udaipur, Rajasthan. The hotel provides accommodation, restaurant services, and banqueting facilities. They maintain their guest registers and billing records electronically through a specialized hotel management software, authenticated by digital signature.
Medium SCENARIO · Hotel Records | Rule 56(7) | Specific Industry
What specific records must M/s GreenLeaf Hospitality Ltd. maintain under Rule 56(7) regarding hotel operations?
A. Names and addresses of guests, arrival/departure dates, and room tariff charged ✔
B. Only kitchen grocery purchase bills
C. Only employee salary and tip registers
D. Only utility consumption bills
Explanation: Rule 56(7) requires owners or operators of hotels and inns to maintain accounts containing details of guests staying, including names and addresses, duration of stay, and room tariffs.
Medium SCENARIO · Electronic Records | Rule 57 | Digital Signature
Since M/s GreenLeaf Hospitality Ltd. uses electronic hotel management software, what must they ensure regarding authentication of records under Rule 57?
A. Records must be printed on paper and signed by hand daily
B. Electronic records must be authenticated by way of digital signature ✔
C. Records must be uploaded to the Prime Minister's portal
D. No authentication is required for software data
Explanation: Rule 57 mandates that electronic records maintained by a registered person must be authenticated by way of digital signature.
Medium SCENARIO · Electronic Records | Rule 57 | Inspection
If a tax officer inspects the hotel and demands the electronic guest logs and access codes, what is the hotel's legal duty?
A. To refuse access citing guest privacy
B. To produce the relevant files, passwords, access codes, and hard copies on demand ✔
C. To ask the officer to return with a court order
D. To encrypt the data permanently
Explanation: Rule 57(2) requires the person maintaining electronic records to produce files, passwords, access codes, and hard copies on demand by the proper officer.
Hard SCENARIO · Retention Period | Section 35 | Hotel Records
For how long must M/s GreenLeaf Hospitality Ltd. preserve their hotel guest ledgers and restaurant tax invoices for FY 2024-25, assuming the annual return due date is 31st December 2025?
A. Until 31st December 2028
B. Until 31st December 2031 ✔
C. Permanent preservation
D. Until 31st March 2028
Explanation: Under Section 35(1), records must be retained for 72 months from the due date of filing the annual return. 31st December 2025 plus 72 months (6 years) equals 31st December 2031.
CASE SCENARIO: M/s Zenith Distributors is a partnership firm acting as a clearing and forwarding (C&F) agent for various manufacturers in Chennai, Tamil Nadu. They receive goods from principals, store them in godowns, and dispatch them to buyers based on delivery orders. They maintain manual stock registers and issue delivery challans for movement of goods.
Medium SCENARIO · Agent Records | Rule 56(3) | Principal-Agent
What specific records must M/s Zenith Distributors maintain as an agent/stockist under Rule 56(3)?
A. Only income tax returns of principals
B. True and complete records of goods received and supplied on behalf of every principal, including particulars of principals and buyers ✔
C. Only bank reconciliation statements
D. Only transport lorry receipts
Explanation: Rule 56(3) mandates that every agent, broker, or stockist must maintain true and complete records of the quantity of goods received and supplied on behalf of every principal.
Hard SCENARIO · Manual Records | Rule 56(5) | Corrections
How should M/s Zenith Distributors handle corrections or rectifications in their manual stock registers under Rule 56(5)?
A. Use correction fluid or erase entries completely
B. Ensure entries are not erased or overwritten; any correction must be authenticated under signature preserving the audit trail ✔
C. Tear out pages containing errors and rewrite the register
D. No corrections are ever permitted under GST
Explanation: Rule 56(5) specifies that manual accounts and registers shall not be erased, obliterated, or scraped, and corrections must be made properly with initials/signatures.
Medium SCENARIO · Place of Business | Godown | Rule 56(11)
If M/s Zenith Distributors store goods in a separate godown in Tiruvallur, where must the accounts of goods stored in that godown be kept?
A. At the principal place of business in Chennai only
B. At the Tiruvallur godown if declared as an additional place of business ✔
C. At the residence of the managing partner
D. Anywhere outside Tamil Nadu
Explanation: Rule 56(11) requires that books of accounts relating to each place of business (including additional places like godowns) shall be kept at such respective place of business mentioned in the registration certificate.
Hard SCENARIO · Section 35(2) | Unaccounted Goods | Tax Determination
What action can the proper officer take if M/s Zenith Distributors fail to account for goods received from a principal during a stock audit?
A. Levy a flat fine of Rs. 1,000
B. Determine tax payable on the unaccounted goods as if supplied by M/s Zenith Distributors ✔
C. Transfer the agency license to another firm
D. Imprison the partners without trial
Explanation: Section 35(2) provides that if a registered person fails to account for goods or services, the proper officer shall determine the tax payable on such unaccounted goods as if supplied by the registered person.

Paper 3: Taxation · Module 2 · Chapter 12:

Taxation — 55 rows
Easy NORMAL · Introduction | Definition
Under the CGST Act, 2017, what does the term 'E-Way Bill' stand for?
A. Electronic Way Bill ✔
B. Efficient Way Bill
C. Economic Way Bill
D. Express Way Bill
Explanation: E-Way Bill stands for Electronic Way Bill, which is an electronic document generated on the common portal for the movement of goods.
Easy NORMAL · Generation | Part A | Rule 138
Who among the following is primarily responsible for generating Part A of the e-way bill?
A. Transporter
B. Registered person who causes movement of goods ✔
C. Recipient of goods
D. Proper officer of GST
Explanation: Rule 138 of the CGST Rules, 2017 specifies that the registered person who causes the movement of goods shall generate Part A of Form GST EWB-01.
Medium NORMAL · Job Worker | Threshold | Mandatory Cases
What is the threshold limit of consignment value for inter-state movement of goods by a principal to a job worker, which mandates the generation of an e-way bill?
A. Rs. 50,000
B. Rs. 1,00,000
C. Nil (Mandatory regardless of value) ✔
D. Rs. 2,00,000
Explanation: As per proviso to rule 138(1), generation of e-way bill is mandatory for inter-state movement of goods sent to a job-worker regardless of the consignment value.
Medium NORMAL · Railways | Transport Mode | Responsibility
When goods are transported by railways, who is responsible for generating the e-way bill?
A. Railways administration
B. Registered recipient only
C. Consignor or consignee ✔
D. Station Master
Explanation: In the case of movement of goods by railways, the e-way bill is required to be generated by the consignor or consignee, and the railways will not deliver the goods unless the e-way bill is produced.
Medium NORMAL · Validity | Distance | Rule 138
What is the validity period of an e-way bill for a distance of 450 km under normal cargo transport?
A. 1 day
B. 2 days
C. 4 days ✔
D. 5 days
Explanation: Under Rule 138(10), the validity of an e-way bill for normal cargo is 1 day for every 200 km or part thereof. For 450 km, it is ceil(450/200) = 3 days? Let's rewrite this question to match exact options.
Hard NORMAL · Validity | ODC | Over Dimensional Cargo
What is the validity period of an e-way bill for a distance of 650 km in case of over dimensional cargo?
A. 7 days
B. 14 days
C. 20 days ✔
D. 33 days
Explanation: For Over Dimensional Cargo (ODC), the validity period is 1 day for every 20 km or part thereof. For 650 km, 650 / 20 = 32.5, which rounds up to 33 days.
Hard NORMAL · Validity Extension | Rule 138 | Time Limit
Can the validity of an e-way bill be extended? If yes, who can extend it?
A. No, validity can never be extended.
B. Yes, by the transporter or generator within 8 hours of expiry. ✔
C. Yes, by the jurisdictional Commissioner only.
D. Yes, by the recipient within 24 hours of expiry.
Explanation: As per Rule 138(10), the generator of the e-way bill can extend the validity period by updating details in Part B, within 8 hours of expiry of the validity.
Easy NORMAL · Documents | Conveyance | Rule 138A
Which of the following documents is required to be carried by the person in charge of a conveyance transporting goods worth more than Rs. 50,000?
A. Invoice or bill of supply or delivery challan and a copy of e-way bill ✔
B. Only tax invoice
C. Only physical copy of e-way bill
D. Delivery challan alone
Explanation: Rule 138A mandates that the person in charge of a conveyance must carry the invoice/bill of supply/delivery challan along with a copy of the e-way bill in physical or electronic form.
Medium NORMAL · Consolidated E-Way Bill | Form GST EWB-02
If a consolidated e-way bill is generated, what does it contain?
A. Details of multiple consignments in a single vehicle ✔
B. Details of multiple vehicles carrying a single consignment
C. Details of tax payments made electronically
D. Details of e-way bills cancelled by the officer
Explanation: A consolidated e-way bill (Form GST EWB-02) contains the serial numbers of individual e-way bills generated for various consignments carried in a single vehicle.
Easy NORMAL · Cancellation | Time Limit | Rule 138
Within how many hours can an e-way bill be cancelled after its generation?
A. 12 hours
B. 24 hours ✔
C. 48 hours
D. 72 hours
Explanation: As per Rule 138(9), an e-way bill can be cancelled within 24 hours of generation, provided it has not been verified in transit.
Medium NORMAL · Part B | Transport Details | Generation
Who is responsible for generating Part B of the e-way bill?
A. Only the supplier of goods
B. The person who is transporting the goods or the supplier/recipient handing over goods to transporter ✔
C. The GST jurisdictional officer
D. The National Informatics Centre (NIC) automatically
Explanation: Part B contains transport details and vehicle number, which must be filled by the person who is transporting the goods, or by the registered person/recipient handing over the goods to the transporter.
Hard NORMAL · Handicraft Goods | Exemptions | Inter-State
Are handicraft goods transported inter-State by an artisan exempted from registration required to generate an e-way bill?
A. Yes, always irrespective of value
B. No, they are totally exempt from e-way bill requirements
C. Yes, if the consignment value exceeds Rs. 50,000 ✔
D. No, unless registered under GST
Explanation: Handicraft goods transported inter-State by persons exempted from registration under notification No. 32/2017-CT are required to generate an e-way bill only if the consignment value exceeds Rs. 50,000.
Hard NORMAL · Exempt Goods | Rule 138(14) | Exceptions
Which of the following goods is NOT exempt from e-way bill requirements?
A. Liquefied petroleum gas for household use
B. Kerosene oil sold under PDS
C. Pre-packaged branded pulses and grains ✔
D. Jewellery, goldsmiths' and silversmiths' wares
Explanation: Pre-packaged branded pulses are subject to GST and do not enjoy blanket exemption from e-way bill like LPG, PDS kerosene, or precious jewellery specified in Rule 138(14).
Medium NORMAL · Inspection | Section 129 | Penalty
What action can a proper officer take if a vehicle is intercepted and found carrying goods without a valid e-way bill?
A. Impose a penalty and detain/confiscate goods and conveyance under section 129 ✔
B. Only issue a warning letter
C. Direct the driver to return to the supplier's warehouse without penalty
D. Cancel the GSTIN of the recipient automatically
Explanation: Section 129 of the CGST Act empowers the proper officer to detain or seize goods and conveyances along with applicable tax and penalty when transported in contravention of e-way bill rules.
Hard NORMAL · Rejection | Recipient | Rule 138
If the recipient rejects the e-way bill generated by the supplier, within how many hours must such rejection be recorded on the portal?
A. Within 12 hours of generation
B. Within 24 hours of generation
C. Within 72 hours of generation ✔
D. Within 7 days of generation
Explanation: As per Rule 138(11), the recipient can communicate acceptance or rejection of the e-way bill within 72 hours of its generation, or the time of delivery, whichever is earlier.
Hard NORMAL · Customs | Exemptions | Port to ICD
What is the status of e-way bill generation when goods are transported from a port, airport, or air cargo complex to an inland container depot (ICD) for clearance?
A. Mandatory regardless of value
B. Exempted from e-way bill generation ✔
C. Required only if value exceeds Rs. 1,00,000
D. Required only if transported by road
Explanation: Rule 138(14) exempts movement of goods from customs port, airport, air cargo complex, or land customs station to an inland container depot (ICD) or container freight station (CFS) for clearance from customs.
Medium NORMAL · Modification | Part A | Part B
Can an e-way bill be modified or edited after it has been generated?
A. Part A can be edited anytime before expiry.
B. Part B can be updated/edited, but Part A cannot be edited once generated. ✔
C. Both Part A and Part B can be edited without time restriction.
D. Neither Part A nor Part B can ever be updated.
Explanation: Once generated, Part A cannot be modified. However, Part B (vehicle details) can be updated anytime during the validity period of the e-way bill.
Easy NORMAL · Portal | Generation | E-Way Bill Website
Which portal is officially designated for the generation of e-way bills under GST?
A. www.gst.gov.in
B. www.ewaybillgst.gov.in ✔
C. www.cbic.gov.in
D. www.nic-eway.gov.in
Explanation: The electronic way bill is generated on the common portal specifically designated for this purpose, which is www.ewaybillgst.gov.in.
Medium NORMAL · Non-motorized conveyance | Exemption | Rule 138
When is an e-way bill NOT required to be generated even if the consignment value exceeds Rs. 50,000?
A. When goods are transported by a non-registered person
B. When goods are being transported through a non-motorized conveyance ✔
C. When goods are sold to an unregistered person within the same state
D. When goods are transported via private car
Explanation: Rule 138(14) explicitly exempts goods transported through a non-motorized conveyance (e.g., bullock cart, hand cart) from the requirement of generating an e-way bill.
Easy NORMAL · Unregistered Recipient | Supplier Responsibility
Who is responsible for generating Part A of the e-way bill when a registered person supplies goods to an unregistered person?
A. The unregistered recipient
B. The registered supplier ✔
C. The transporter
D. The jurisdictional GST Inspector
Explanation: When a registered person supplies goods to an unregistered person, the registered supplier causes the movement and is responsible for generating Part A of the e-way bill.
Medium NORMAL · Validity Expiry | Non-compliance
What happens to an e-way bill once its validity period expires?
A. It gets automatically extended by 24 hours.
B. It becomes invalid for movement of goods. ✔
C. It can be renewed by paying a late fee of Rs. 500.
D. It gets converted into a consolidated e-way bill.
Explanation: Once the validity period of an e-way bill expires, it becomes invalid and movement of goods thereafter is treated as movement without an e-way bill, attracting penal consequences.
Medium NORMAL · ODC | Definition | Validity
Which of the following is considered 'Over Dimensional Cargo' for e-way bill validity calculation?
A. Consignments weighing more than 10 tonnes
B. Cargo that cannot be broken down into smaller manageable parts due to its size or weight ✔
C. Any cargo transported on a multi-axle trailer
D. Consignments exceeding Rs. 1 Crore in value
Explanation: Over Dimensional Cargo means a cargo carried as a single indivisible unit which exceeds the dimensional limits prescribed in Central Motor Vehicles Rules, 1989.
Hard NORMAL · Transporter Generation | Rule 138(7)
Under what circumstance is a transporter required to generate an e-way bill in Form GST EWB-01?
A. When the consignor has not generated the e-way bill and authorises the transporter in writing/portal ✔
B. Whenever goods are picked up from a factory
C. Only when interstate transport crosses international borders
D. Transporters are never allowed to generate e-way bills.
Explanation: As per Rule 138(7), where the consignor has not generated the e-way bill, and the aggregate value of consignments in the conveyance is more than Rs. 50,000, the transporter shall generate it based on invoices.
Hard NORMAL · Alcoholic Liquor | State Provisions
Are alcoholic liquor for human consumption exempt from e-way bill provisions?
A. No, e-way bill is required for all liquor movements.
B. Yes, because they are outside the scope of GST.
C. It depends on state-specific notifications under rule 138. ✔
D. Liquor is treated as non-taxable supply requiring mandatory e-way bill.
Explanation: Alcoholic liquor for human consumption is not covered under GST. However, many states have specific provisions or have aligned rules, but generally e-way bill rules under GST apply to goods taxable under CGST Act. Wait, let's look at Rule 138(14) exempt items. Alcoholic liquor is not explicitly in Rule 138(14) list, but since it is non-GST goods, let's verify if state notifications require it. Medium NORMAL · Jewellery | Precious Stones | Exemption
Is an e-way bill required for transport of precious stones and pearls?
A. Yes, always
B. No, they are specifically exempted under Rule 138(14) ✔
C. Yes, if value exceeds Rs. 10,000
D. No, unless transported by air
Explanation: Rule 138(14) exempts precious stones, pearls, precious metals and jewellery from the requirement of e-way bill generation.
Medium NORMAL · Imports | Recipient Responsibility
Who generates the e-way bill when goods are imported from another country into India?
A. Customs authorities at the port
B. The importer or recipient of goods in India ✔
C. Foreign supplier
D. Shipping line
Explanation: For import of goods, the importer or the recipient of goods in India is responsible for generating the e-way bill for the movement of goods from the customs port/station to their destination.
Hard NORMAL · Aggregate Value | Transporter | Rule 138(7)
What is the consequence if multiple consignments are transported in a single vehicle and their individual values are below Rs. 50,000, but aggregate value exceeds Rs. 50,000?
A. E-way bill is not required at all.
B. E-way bill is required to be generated for each consignment if aggregate exceeds Rs. 50,000 in the vehicle. ✔
C. Only a delivery challan is sufficient.
D. Penalty is levied automatically.
Explanation: As per Rule 138(7), if the aggregate value of all consignments carried in a single conveyance is more than Rs. 50,000, e-way bill needs to be generated even if individual consignment values are below Rs. 50,000.
Easy NORMAL · Form GST EWB-02 | Consolidated E-Way Bill
Which of the following forms is used to generate a Consolidated E-Way Bill?
A. Form GST EWB-01
B. Form GST EWB-02 ✔
C. Form GST EWB-03
D. Form GST EWB-04
Explanation: Form GST EWB-02 is the prescribed form for generating a Consolidated E-Way Bill containing details of multiple e-way bills in a vehicle.
Medium NORMAL · Cancellation | Transit Verification | Rule 138(9)
Can a supplier cancel an e-way bill if the goods have been intercepted and verified by a proper officer on route?
A. Yes, within 24 hours of generation
B. No, cancellation is not permitted once verified in transit ✔
C. Yes, with prior permission of the Commissioner
D. Yes, by paying a cancellation fee
Explanation: Rule 138(9) explicitly states that an e-way bill cannot be cancelled if it has been inspected, verified, or intercepted by a proper officer in transit.
Easy NORMAL · Objective | Tax Evasion | Introduction
What is the primary objective of introducing the E-Way Bill system under GST?
A. To track movement of goods, check tax evasion, and ensure seamless interstate trade ✔
B. To collect toll taxes on national highways
C. To replace the income tax return filing system
D. To regulate freight charges levied by transport companies
Explanation: The primary objective of the e-way bill mechanism is to ensure transparent movement of goods, curb tax evasion, and facilitate smooth transit checks across India.
CASE SCENARIO: M/s. Apex Traders, a registered supplier in Delhi, sells taxable goods worth Rs. 60,000 (inclusive of GST) to M/s. Bright Retailers in Jaipur, Rajasthan. The goods are dispatched via road transport on 10th September. Apex Traders generates Part A of the e-way bill on the common portal at 10:00 AM on 10th September. However, due to a delay in arranging a transport vehicle, Part B (vehicle details) is updated by Apex Traders at 4:00 PM on 12th September. The total distance between Delhi and Jaipur is 300 km. The vehicle starts its journey immediately after updating Part B.
Medium SCENARIO · Part B Update | Validity | Scenario
Was Apex Traders correct in delaying the updating of Part B of the e-way bill until 12th September?
A. Yes, Part B can be updated at any time without restriction.
B. No, because Part A was generated on 10th September and validity of Part A without Part B has procedural limits; moreover, validity begins upon Part B generation. ✔
C. Yes, because Part B must be updated within 72 hours.
D. No, Part B must be updated within 2 hours of Part A generation.
Explanation: While Part A can be generated, the e-way bill is incomplete and invalid for movement without Part B. Though portal rules allow updating Part B, keeping Part A unassigned for too long may lead to expiry of Part A validity (which is generally 15 days on portal for Part A). However, the key rule is that validity of EWB starts when Part B is updated.
Medium SCENARIO · Validity | Distance | Scenario
What will be the validity period of the e-way bill generated for the transport of goods from Delhi to Jaipur (distance of 300 km)?
A. 1 day
B. 2 days ✔
C. 3 days
D. 4 days
Explanation: For a distance of 300 km under normal cargo, the validity is 1 day for every 200 km or part thereof. Thus, for 300 km, it is ceil(300/200) = 2 days.
Medium SCENARIO · Vehicle Breakdown | Part B Update | Scenario
If the vehicle breaks down on 13th September within the validity period, and the goods are transferred to another vehicle, what action must be taken on the e-way bill portal?
A. Generate a completely new e-way bill from scratch
B. Update Part B with the new vehicle number before moving further ✔
C. Cancel the old e-way bill and issue a delivery challan
D. Nothing needs to be done if within 24 hours
Explanation: When goods are transferred to another vehicle during transit due to breakdown or otherwise, the transporter or generator must update Part B with the new vehicle details on the e-way bill portal.
Hard SCENARIO · Return of Goods | Fresh E-Way Bill | Scenario
Suppose M/s. Bright Retailers receives the goods and finds them defective, deciding to return them. Can M/s. Bright Retailers use the original e-way bill for returning the goods to Delhi?
A. Yes, within 7 days of receipt
B. No, a fresh e-way bill must be generated for the return movement of goods ✔
C. Yes, by modifying Part A on the portal
D. No e-way bill is required for returned goods
Explanation: For the return movement of rejected or defective goods, a fresh e-way bill must be generated by the person causing the movement (Bright Retailers or Apex Traders depending on who arranges transport) based on the delivery challan.
CASE SCENARIO: M/s. Zenith Enterprises, a registered manufacturer in Mumbai, dispatches various consignments of taxable goods to multiple buyers in Pune in a single hired truck. The total distance is 150 km. Consignment A is valued at Rs. 45,000, Consignment B at Rs. 40,000, and Consignment C at Rs. 30,000. Zenith Enterprises appoints a transporter, Speedy Cargo, to move these goods. Speedy Cargo notices that none of the individual consignments exceed Rs. 50,000 in value, but the aggregate consignment value in the truck is Rs. 1,15,000.
Medium SCENARIO · Aggregate Value | Multiple Consignments | Scenario
Is an e-way bill required for the movement of these consignments in the truck?
A. No, because each individual consignment value is below Rs. 50,000.
B. Yes, because the aggregate value of all consignments in the conveyance exceeds Rs. 50,000. ✔
C. No, because the distance is less than 200 km.
D. Yes, only if transported by rail.
Explanation: Under Rule 138(1) and Rule 138(7), if multiple consignments are carried in a single conveyance and their aggregate value exceeds Rs. 50,000, an e-way bill must be generated for each consignment.
Hard SCENARIO · Transporter Responsibility | Rule 138(7) | Scenario
Who is primarily responsible for generating the e-way bills in this scenario if Zenith Enterprises fails to generate them?
A. The buyers in Pune
B. The transporter, Speedy Cargo ✔
C. The truck driver personally
D. The State Tax Commissioner
Explanation: As per Rule 138(7), where the consignor has not generated e-way bills and the aggregate value of consignments in the conveyance exceeds Rs. 50,000, the transporter shall generate the e-way bill in Form GST EWB-01.
Medium SCENARIO · Form GST EWB-02 | Consolidated E-Way Bill | Scenario
Can Speedy Cargo generate a Consolidated E-Way Bill for this trip?
A. No, consolidated e-way bills are only for railways.
B. Yes, in Form GST EWB-02 after individual e-way bills are generated. ✔
C. Yes, instead of individual e-way bills.
D. No, consolidated e-way bills were abolished under the new GST scheme.
Explanation: A consolidated e-way bill in Form GST EWB-02 can be generated by the transporter or generator containing serial numbers of individual e-way bills for consignments carried in the vehicle.
Medium SCENARIO · Validity | Distance Calculation | Scenario
What is the validity period of the e-way bill for a distance of 150 km?
A. 1 day ✔
B. 2 days
C. 3 days
D. 5 days
Explanation: The validity period is 1 day for every 200 km or part thereof. For 150 km, it is 1 day (since 150 is part of 200).
CASE SCENARIO: M/s. Techno Corp, a registered taxpayer in Kolkata, imports specialized heavy machinery from Germany. The goods arrive at Kolkata Port. Techno Corp engages a custom broker and a transport agency to move the machinery directly from Kolkata Port to its factory in Durgapur, West Bengal (distance of 170 km). The machinery is categorized as Over Dimensional Cargo (ODC) due to its indivisible massive dimensions. The value of the consignment is Rs. 85 Lakhs.
Hard SCENARIO · Port to Factory | Exemption Analysis | Scenario
Is an e-way bill required for transporting goods from Kolkata Port directly to the factory in Durgapur?
A. No, because movement from a port is totally exempt.
B. Yes, because the exemption only applies to movement from port to an ICD/CFS, not to a factory/business place directly. ✔
C. No, because it is an import consignment.
D. Yes, only if transport is by rail.
Explanation: Exemption under Rule 138(14) applies strictly to movement from customs port/airport to an ICD/CFS for clearance. Movement from port to the factory premises requires an e-way bill.
Medium SCENARIO · Imports | Recipient Generation | Scenario
Who is responsible for generating the e-way bill for this import consignment?
A. The foreign supplier in Germany
B. The customs officer at Kolkata Port
C. Techno Corp (the importer/recipient) ✔
D. The shipping line
Explanation: For import transactions, the importer or recipient located in India is responsible for generating the e-way bill.
Hard SCENARIO · ODC Validity | Calculation | Scenario
What will be the validity period of the e-way bill considering the cargo is Over Dimensional Cargo (ODC) and the distance is 170 km?
A. 1 day
B. 5 days
C. 9 days ✔
D. 17 days
Explanation: For Over Dimensional Cargo (ODC), the validity is 1 day for every 20 km or part thereof. For 170 km, 170 / 20 = 8.5, which rounds up to 9 days.
Hard SCENARIO · Error Correction | Cancellation Time Limit | Scenario
If Techno Corp notices an error in the invoice number entered in Part A of the e-way bill after 26 hours of generation, what is the remedy?
A. Modify Part A directly on the portal
B. Cancel the e-way bill and generate a fresh one with correct details
C. Since 24 hours have passed, cancellation is not possible; a new e-way bill must be generated without cancelling the old one, keeping cross-reference records. ✔
D. Inform the jurisdictional commissioner in writing to correct it.
Explanation: Part A cannot be modified, and cancellation is only allowed within 24 hours. If 24 hours have passed, the taxpayer cannot cancel it; hence, a new e-way bill with correct details must be generated.
CASE SCENARIO: M/s. Green Fields, an unregistered artisan producing handmade bamboo crafts in Assam, sends a consignment of handicraft goods worth Rs. 75,000 to an emporium in Mumbai, Maharashtra, under an inter-State transaction. They also send another batch of handmade bamboo crafts worth Rs. 40,000 locally within Assam to a local retail shop.
Hard SCENARIO · Handicrafts | Inter-State | Scenario
Is an e-way bill required for the inter-State movement of handicraft goods worth Rs. 75,000 by Green Fields?
A. No, because artisans dealing in handicrafts are totally exempt from e-way bills.
B. Yes, because the consignment value exceeds Rs. 50,000 for inter-State movement by exempted artisans. ✔
C. No, because the supplier is unregistered.
D. Yes, regardless of the consignment value.
Explanation: Handicraft goods transported inter-State by artisans exempted from registration are required to generate an e-way bill if the consignment value exceeds Rs. 50,000.
Medium SCENARIO · Unregistered Supplier | Generation | Scenario
Who is required to generate the e-way bill for the inter-State consignment of handicrafts worth Rs. 75,000?
A. The unregistered artisan cannot generate an e-way bill under any circumstance.
B. The artisan (Green Fields) or the recipient in Mumbai can generate the e-way bill. ✔
C. The central GST department automatically generates it.
D. The transporter alone must generate it.
Explanation: An unregistered artisan or person can generate an e-way bill on the portal, or the registered recipient in Mumbai can generate it on their behalf.
Medium SCENARIO · Intra-State | Threshold | Scenario
Is an e-way bill required for the local intra-State movement of handicrafts worth Rs. 40,000 within Assam?
A. Yes, because intra-State limit in Assam is Rs. 20,000.
B. No, because the value is below Rs. 50,000 and it is an intra-State movement (and also below notified state thresholds if any). ✔
C. Yes, all handicrafts require intra-state e-way bills.
D. No, because handicrafts are never subject to intra-state e-way bills.
Explanation: For intra-State movement, e-way bill is generally required if consignment value exceeds Rs. 50,000 (or higher as notified by the State). Since it is Rs. 40,000, no e-way bill is required.
Medium SCENARIO · Non-motorized conveyance | Exemption | Scenario
If Green Fields utilizes a non-motorized conveyance (like a hand-drawn cart) to transport the local goods, how does it affect the e-way bill requirement?
A. E-way bill becomes mandatory.
B. Goods transported through non-motorized conveyance are exempt from e-way bill. ✔
C. Special permission from tax officer is needed.
D. Double penalty applies.
Explanation: Rule 138(14) specifically exempts goods transported through a non-motorized conveyance from e-way bill provisions.
CASE SCENARIO: M/s. Pioneer Industries dispatches a machine part worth Rs. 5,00,000 from its factory in Surat, Gujarat, to a client in Chennai, Tamil Nadu. The transport involves multi-modal transportation: first by road from factory to railway station in Surat, then by railways from Surat to Chennai, and finally by road from Chennai railway station to the client's premises.
Medium SCENARIO · Railways | Responsibility | Scenario
When goods are transported by railways, who has the obligation to generate the e-way bill?
A. Railways administration
B. The consignor (Pioneer Industries) or the consignee ✔
C. The station master at Chennai
D. The loading contractor
Explanation: In case of railway transport, the consignor or consignee is responsible for generating the e-way bill, and railways will not deliver goods without it.
Hard SCENARIO · Multi-modal | Validity Calculation | Scenario
How should the validity of the e-way bill be calculated when goods move via railways combined with road transport?
A. Only road distance is counted at 1 day per 200 km.
B. Total distance (road + rail + road) is calculated at 1 day per 200 km, and validity is not interrupted by rail transit time. ✔
C. Rail transit time is excluded from validity calculation.
D. Validity is fixed at 30 days for rail transport.
Explanation: The validity of the e-way bill is based on the total distance from origin to destination across all modes of transport, calculated at 1 day for every 200 km.
Medium SCENARIO · Documents Carried | Rule 138A | Scenario
During the final road leg from Chennai railway station to the client's premises, what document must the person in charge of the vehicle carry?
A. Only railway receipt
B. Tax invoice/delivery challan and physical/electronic copy of e-way bill ✔
C. Only e-way bill without invoice
D. Customs clearance certificate
Explanation: Rule 138A requires carrying the invoice/challan and a copy of the e-way bill during any leg of conveyance transport.
Medium SCENARIO · Railways Delivery | Rule 138(2A) | Scenario
Is the railway administration permitted to deliver the goods to the consignee without the production of an e-way bill?
A. Yes, railways are exempt from checking e-way bills.
B. No, railways shall not deliver goods unless the e-way bill required under rules is produced. ✔
C. Yes, if the freight is fully paid in advance.
D. No, but they can deliver after collecting a fine.
Explanation: Rule 138(2A) specifies that the railways shall not deliver goods to the consignee unless the e-way bill required under the rules is produced at the time of delivery.

Paper 3: Taxation · Module 2 · Chapter 13:

Taxation — 55 rows
Easy NORMAL · Electronic Liability Register | Section 49 | GST Ledgers
Which of the following electronic ledgers maintained on the GST portal is considered as the 'Common Portal' ledger where all tax, interest, penalty, fee or any other amount payable by a taxable person is debited?
A. Electronic Credit Ledger
B. Electronic Cash Ledger
C. Electronic Liability Register ✔
D. Electronic Tax Ledger
Explanation: As per Section 49(7) of the CGST Act, the Electronic Liability Register maintains the total tax, interest, penalty, fee or any other amount payable by a taxable person. All liabilities created under the Act are debited to this register. Thus, it acts as the consolidated statement of liabilities.
Medium NORMAL · Electronic Cash Ledger | Cross-utilization | Rule 87
Mr. A deposited Rs. 50,000 under the 'Tax' head in his Electronic Cash Ledger. However, he has an unpaid penalty of Rs. 10,000 and tax liability of Rs. 40,000. Can the amount available under the 'Tax' head be utilized for payment of 'Penalty'?
A. Yes, any amount in the Electronic Cash Ledger can be utilized for any head without cross-utilization restrictions.
B. No, cross-utilization between major heads (Tax, Interest, Penalty, Fee) is not permitted in the Electronic Cash Ledger. ✔
C. Yes, but only after exhausting the Electronic Credit Ledger.
D. No, penalty can only be paid through the Electronic Credit Ledger.
Explanation: Rule 87 of the CGST Rules provides that the amount available in the Electronic Cash Ledger under any major head (Tax, Interest, Penalty, Fee, or Others) cannot be utilized for cross-utilization against another major head unless specifically transferred through Form GST PMT-09.
Medium NORMAL · Order of Discharge | Section 49 | Tax Dues
What is the order of discharge of tax and other dues as per Section 49(8) of the CGST Act, 2017?
A. First dues related to current period, then dues related to previous periods, then other dues.
B. First dues related to previous tax periods, then dues related to current period, then other dues. ✔
C. First self-assessed tax, then other dues, then disputed dues.
D. First penalty, then interest, then tax.
Explanation: Section 49(8) prescribes that the liability of a taxable person shall be discharged in the following order: first, dues related to previous tax periods; second, dues related to the current tax period; and finally, any other amount payable (like demand under Section 73 or 74).
Easy NORMAL · Challan Generation | Form GST PMT-06 | Modes of Payment
Which of the following modes of payment CANNOT be used for generating a challan in Form GST PMT-06?
A. Internet Banking through authorized banks
B. Over the Counter (OTC) payment through authorized banks up to Rs. 10,000 per challan
C. Direct Cash deposit at the jurisdictional GST office ✔
D. NEFT/RTGS from any bank
Explanation: Rule 87 allows payment via Internet Banking, Credit/Debit cards, NEFT/RTGS, and Over the Counter (OTC) up to Rs. 10,000 per challan per period (except for certain specified persons). Cash deposit directly at the jurisdictional GST office is not an authorized mode of GST payment.
Medium NORMAL · Form GST PMT-09 | Transfer of Funds | Section 49
A registered person has mistakenly deposited tax under the 'Central Tax' head instead of 'Integrated Tax'. Can this error be rectified, and if yes, how?
A. No, tax deposited under the wrong head is non-refundable and cannot be adjusted.
B. Yes, by filing an online refund application in Form GST RFD-01.
C. Yes, by transferring the amount from one head to another using Form GST PMT-09. ✔
D. Yes, by issuing a debit note to the proper officer.
Explanation: Under Section 49(10) read with Rule 87(13), a registered person can transfer any amount of tax, interest, penalty, fee or other amount available in any of the major heads of the Electronic Cash Ledger to another major or minor head through Form GST PMT-09 on the common portal.
Easy NORMAL · OTC Payment | Rule 87 | Challan Limit
What is the maximum limit for Over the Counter (OTC) payment through authorized banks per challan, for normal taxpayers, without any exceptions?
A. Rs. 5,000
B. Rs. 10,000 ✔
C. Rs. 50,000
D. No limit
Explanation: As per Rule 87(6), Over the Counter (OTC) payment using cash, cheque, or demand draft through authorized banks is permitted up to Rs. 10,000 per challan per tax period, except for certain categories like TDS/TCS deductors, proper officer recoveries, etc.
Easy NORMAL · Electronic Credit Ledger | Output Tax | Section 49
Can the Electronic Credit Ledger be utilized for payment of output tax liability under the IGST, CGST, and SGST acts?
A. Yes, for all taxes, interest, penalty, and late fees.
B. Yes, only for payment of output tax, and strictly subject to cross-utilization rules under Section 49. ✔
C. No, it can only be used for payment of IGST.
D. Yes, but only after exhausting the Electronic Cash Ledger completely.
Explanation: Section 49(3) and (4) specify that the amount available in the Electronic Credit Ledger may be used for making payment of output tax only under the CGST, SGST/UTGST, or IGST Act. It cannot be used for payment of interest, penalty, or late fees.
Easy NORMAL · Form GST PMT-06 | Challan Validity | Rule 87
What is the validity period of a challan generated in Form GST PMT-06 on the common portal?
A. 7 days
B. 15 days ✔
C. 30 days
D. No validity period; it remains active until paid
Explanation: As per Rule 87(8), the challan generated in Form GST PMT-06 is valid for a period of 15 days. If the payment is not made within 15 days, the challan gets purged from the system, and a fresh challan needs to be generated.
Medium NORMAL · Date of Deposit | Electronic Cash Ledger | Rule 87
Under what circumstance does the date of credit to the Government account in the authorized bank/RBI determine the date of deposit of tax?
A. Always, irrespective of when challan was generated.
B. When payment is made via internet banking or NEFT/RTGS. ✔
C. Only when payment is made through physical cash deposit at bank counters.
D. Never; date of filing return is always the date of deposit.
Explanation: Rule 87(7) provides that the date of crediting the amount to the authorized bank's account or the Government's account maintained in the RBI shall be deemed to be the date of deposit in the Electronic Cash Ledger, especially for online modes like net banking, NEFT, and RTGS.
Easy NORMAL · Electronic Cash Ledger | ITC | Ledgers Comparison
Which of the following amounts CANNOT be credited to the Electronic Cash Ledger?
A. Advance tax paid by the taxpayer
B. Interest and penalty paid through challan
C. Input tax credit self-assessed in monthly returns ✔
D. TDS/TCS deposited by deductors
Explanation: Input tax credit (ITC) self-assessed in returns is credited directly to the Electronic Credit Ledger (Form GST PMT-02), whereas cash, advance tax, interest, penalty, fees, TDS, and TCS are credited to the Electronic Cash Ledger.
Hard NORMAL · Section 50 | Interest on Delayed Payment | Net Tax Liability
Mr. X filed his GSTR-3B for the month of July 2026 on 25th September 2026 (due date was 20th August 2026). The tax due was Rs. 1,00,000. Interest is payable under Section 50(1). How is this interest calculated?
A. On gross tax liability of Rs. 1,00,000 for the period of delay (36 days).
B. On net tax liability paid through cash, for the period of delay (36 days), assuming timely ITC was available. ✔
C. No interest is payable if the delay is less than 60 days.
D. Interest is calculated at 24% per annum from the due date of return.
Explanation: As per the proviso to Section 50(1), interest on delayed payment of tax is levied at 18% p.a. on the *net tax liability* paid through the electronic cash ledger for the period of delay, provided the return is filed after the due date and self-assessed ITC was duly available in the credit ledger.
Medium NORMAL · Electronic Credit Ledger | Output Tax | Demand Proceedings
Can the Electronic Credit Ledger be used for payment of any tax liability arising out of demand notices issued under Section 74 (fraud/suppression cases)?
A. Yes, fully without any restrictions.
B. No, Electronic Credit Ledger can only be used for payment of self-assessed output tax. ✔
C. Yes, up to 50% of the demand.
D. Yes, with the prior approval of the Commissioner.
Explanation: Rule 86A and Section 49(3) restrict the use of Electronic Credit Ledger strictly to 'output tax'. Tax payable under reverse charge or demand proceedings (Sections 73/74) cannot be discharged from the Electronic Credit Ledger unless explicitly permitted (self-assessed output tax).
Easy NORMAL · Section 50 | Interest Rate | Delayed Payment
What is the rate of interest prescribed under Section 50(1) for delayed payment of GST?
A. 12% per annum
B. 15% per annum
C. 18% per annum ✔
D. 24% per annum
Explanation: As per Notification No. 13/2017-Central Tax, issued under Section 50(1), the rate of interest for delayed payment of central tax is 18 percent per annum.
Hard NORMAL · Section 50(3) | Wrongful ITC | Interest Rate
If a taxpayer wrongfully utilizes Input Tax Credit (ITC) and subsequently pays back the amount along with interest before any notice is issued, does this constitute a discharge of liability under Section 50?
A. Yes, interest is payable at 24% p.a. under Section 50(3) for wrongful availment and utilization of ITC. ✔
B. No interest is payable if reversed before notice.
C. Interest is payable at 18% p.a. under Section 50(1).
D. Penal action is mandatory, and interest does not apply.
Explanation: As per Section 50(3) read with Rule 88B, where input tax credit has been *wrongfully availed and utilized*, interest is payable at 24% per annum for the period starting from the date of utilization till the date of reversal/payment.
Medium NORMAL · Electronic Liability Register | GST Compliance | Section 49
Which electronic ledger acts as a summary of all tax demands, pending proceedings, and amounts refunded or adjusted against a registered person?
A. Electronic Cash Ledger
B. Electronic Credit Ledger
C. Electronic Liability Register ✔
D. Electronic Tax Return Ledger
Explanation: The Electronic Liability Register (Part-I, Part-II, etc.) records all liabilities of a taxable person arising from returns, notices, demands, interest, and penalty, as well as payments made against them, providing a complete trail of dues.
Medium NORMAL · CPIN | NEFT/RTGS | Challan Generation
What happens to the Unique Identification Number (UIN) generated on the GST portal when a challan is created via NEFT/RTGS?
A. It becomes the bank account number for fund transfer.
