Explanation: Under FOB destination terms, title and control pass when goods reach the destination. Since delivery occurred on April 4, the sale must be reversed from 2025-26 to adhere to cut-off rules.
Medium SCENARIO · Trade Payables | Disputed Claims | Provisions
What audit procedure should be performed regarding the supplier dispute of INR 20 lakhs included in trade payables?
A. Confirm the disputed amount directly with the supplier, review legal/correspondence files, and assess whether a provision or contingent liability disclosure is required. ✔
B. Force the client to pay the supplier immediately before signing the audit report.
C. Delete the balance from accounts payable without discussion.
D. Treat it as other income.
Explanation: Disputed liabilities require reviewing correspondence, legal advice, and assessing whether an obligation exists (provision) or a possible obligation exists (contingent liability) as per AS 29 / Ind AS 37.
Hard SCENARIO · PPE Revaluation | SA 620 | Expert Evaluation
In auditing the upward revaluation of factory land by INR 5 crores, what is the auditor's primary responsibility regarding the independent valuer?
A. Rely entirely on the valuer without assessing their competence or independence, as they are professionals.
B. Evaluate the competence, capabilities, and objectivity of the valuer, understand their work, and check if revaluation surplus is properly credited to Other Comprehensive Income (OCI) / Revaluation Reserve. ✔
C. Perform an independent engineering valuation of the land themselves.
D. Reject the revaluation entirely because land cannot appreciate.
Explanation: When management's expert is used, SA 620 requires the auditor to evaluate the expert's competence, capabilities, and objectivity, and verify proper accounting treatment of revaluation reserves.
Medium SCENARIO · Cash Verification | Subsequent Count | Reconciliation
If a cash count conducted after year-end (April 2) is reconciled back to March 31, what transactions must the auditor account for during the intervening period?
A. Only cash sales made on April 1 and April 2.
B. Cash receipts and cash payments made between March 31 and April 2. ✔
C. Bank transactions only.
D. No adjustments are necessary.
Explanation: To reconcile a subsequent cash count back to the balance sheet date, the auditor must add back cash payments made during the intervening period and subtract cash receipts collected during that period.
CASE SCENARIO: M/s Pioneer Engineering Works is undergoing its statutory audit for the year ended March 31, 2026. The company has significant foreign currency transactions, including a long-term loan in USD taken for importing capital equipment. During the year, the company issued debentures at a discount and incurred legal fees for drafting the debenture trust deed. The company also carries a large provision for expected credit losses on its trade receivables. The internal audit report highlighted weak controls over scrap disposal.
Hard SCENARIO · Foreign Currency | Long-term Loan | AS 11 / Ind AS 21
How should the auditor verify the foreign currency long-term loan taken for importing capital equipment at the balance sheet date?
A. Translate the loan at the original historical exchange rate.
B. Translate the outstanding loan at the closing exchange rate, and check if exchange differences are appropriately adjusted or capitalized as permitted by relevant accounting standards. ✔
C. Ignore exchange fluctuations until the loan is fully repaid.
D. Use the average rate of the year.
Explanation: Foreign currency monetary items are translated at the closing rate. For long-term foreign currency monetary items related to depreciable assets, options under AS 11 or Ind AS 21 govern capitalization or P&L recognition of exchange differences.
Medium SCENARIO · Debenture Issue Expenses | Securities Premium | Verification
How should the legal fees incurred for drafting the debenture trust deed be treated by the company?
A. Treated as an operating expense of the current year immediately.
B. Written off against Securities Premium Account or amortized over the tenure of the debentures. ✔
C. Capitalized as part of factory land.
D. Ignored in the financial statements.
Explanation: Expenses incurred on the issue of debentures (including legal fees for trust deeds) are typically written off against securities premium or amortized over the life of the debentures.
Hard SCENARIO · Trade Receivables | ECL | Ind AS 109
What is the primary audit check regarding the provision for expected credit losses (ECL) on trade receivables?
A. Verifying that the provision is based on a provision matrix considering historical credit loss experience adjusted for forward-looking information. ✔
B. Ensuring the provision is exactly 5% of turnover regardless of debtor aging.
C. Checking that no debtors are ever provided for.
D. Confirming that ECL calculations are done only by tax authorities.
Explanation: Under Ind AS 109, expected credit losses are assessed using practical expedients like a provision matrix that incorporates historical default rates and forward-looking macroeconomic factors.
Medium SCENARIO · Scrap Sales | Internal Controls | Substantive Procedures
Given the weak internal controls over scrap disposal highlighted by internal audit, what substantive procedure should the statutory auditor perform?
A. Rely completely on management's verbal report on scrap sales.
B. Perform a comprehensive review of scrap generation records, weighment slips, gate passes, and trace cash/bank realizations to verify completeness of scrap income. ✔
C. Disregard scrap sales as immaterial.
D. Check only the electricity bills of the factory.
Explanation: Weak controls over scrap demand extended substantive testing, including reconciling production output with scrap generated, checking gate inward/outward registers, and verifying realization into bank accounts.
CASE SCENARIO: M/s Horizon Technologies Ltd. presents its financial statements for the year ended March 31, 2026. The audit team is focusing on several key areas. The company has capitalized software development costs internally. It holds investments in unquoted equity instruments of subsidiary companies. Employee benefit expenses include provisions for compensated absences (leave encashment). Finally, the company received a massive government grant towards the acquisition of pollution-control equipment.
Hard SCENARIO · Intangible Assets | Software Development | AS 26
In verifying internally generated software development costs capitalized as intangible assets, what must the auditor specifically substantiate?
A. That all research phase costs were capitalized alongside development costs.
B. That technical feasibility, intent, and ability to use or sell the software, and availability of resources to complete it have been demonstrated. ✔
C. That software is depreciated over 50 years.
D. That management's verbal estimate of future sales is sufficient evidence.
Explanation: AS 26 / Ind AS 38 prescribes strict criteria for capitalizing intangible assets arising from development, requiring proof of technical feasibility, intention to complete, and ability to generate future economic benefits.
Medium SCENARIO · Investments | Subsidiaries | Impairment
How should the auditor verify investments in unquoted equity instruments of subsidiary companies?
A. Verify share certificates, check valuation against audited financial statements of the subsidiaries, and evaluate for any impairment in value. ✔
B. Check the stock exchange daily ticker for quoted prices.
C. Assume book value is always equal to market value.
D. Accept management certificates without checking subsidiary financials.
Explanation: Unquoted investments are verified through physical inspection of share certificates and assessing whether the subsidiary's net worth indicates impairment requiring provision under accounting standards.
Hard SCENARIO · Employee Benefits | AS 15 | Actuarial Valuation
What actuarial or accounting check should the auditor perform on the provision for compensated absences (leave encashment)?
A. Verify that the provision is measured on the basis of an actuarial valuation using the Projected Unit Credit Method as required by AS 15 / Ind AS 19. ✔
B. Calculate it as a flat 2% of total gross salaries.
C. Ensure no provision is made if employees do not encash leave immediately.
D. Verify that leave encashment is treated as a capital asset.
Explanation: AS 15 / Ind AS 19 requires defined benefit obligations, including long-term compensated absences, to be measured using actuarial valuation methods such as the Projected Unit Credit Method.
Medium SCENARIO · Government Grants | AS 12 / Ind AS 20 | PPE
How should the government grant received for acquiring pollution-control equipment be verified and presented in the financial statements?
A. Credited directly to the Statement of Profit and Loss as other income in full immediately.
B. Recognized as deferred income or deducted from the carrying amount of the asset, and recognized in P&L over the useful life of the asset. ✔
C. Added to share capital.
D. Ignored as it is a government subsidy.
Explanation: As per AS 12 / Ind AS 20, grants related to depreciable assets are either set up as deferred income and recognized in P&L on a systematic basis over the useful life, or deducted in calculating the carrying amount of the asset.
CASE SCENARIO: M/s Metro Retail Chain operates multiple stores across the country and is undergoing audit for the financial year ended March 31, 2026. Store inventories are counted on a rotation basis throughout the year. The company has substantial lease liabilities for its retail store locations under Ind AS 116 / AS 19 equivalent standards. Trade payables include balances with several Micro, Enterprises registered under the MSMED Act, 2006. Finally, cash collections from retail outlets are deposited in local bank accounts before being transferred to the central pool account.
Medium SCENARIO · Inventories | Perpetual Inventory | Continuous Count
When retail store inventories are counted on a continuous/rotation basis throughout the year instead of a single year-end count, what must the auditor verify?
A. That continuous inventory records (perpetual inventory system) are well maintained, differences are investigated, and proper cut-off controls exist. ✔
B. That physical counts at year-end are entirely unnecessary under all circumstances.
C. That inventory is valued at selling price.
D. That store managers have sole discretion over inventory adjustments.
Explanation: Continuous inventory counts require effective perpetual inventory records, regular reconciliation of physical counts with book balances, and robust controls over inventory movements.
Hard SCENARIO · Leases | RoU Assets | Ind AS 116
In auditing lease liabilities and Right-of-Use (RoU) assets for retail stores, what primary verification procedure should the auditor perform?
A. Check lease agreements for lease terms, discount rates, initial direct costs, and verify lease liability amortization schedule.
B. Treat lease payments purely as rental expenses without recognizing RoU assets. ✔
C. Ignore lease agreements if they are operational leases.
D. Verify physical existence of leased store buildings only.
Explanation: Under Ind AS 116, lessees recognize a Right-of-Use asset and a lease liability for almost all leases, requiring auditors to verify lease terms, discount rates, and amortization schedules.
Hard SCENARIO · MSMED Act | Trade Payables | Schedule III Disclosures
What specific statutory disclosure and verification requirement applies to trade payables due to Micro and Small Enterprises under the MSMED Act, 2006?
A. Identifying overdue amounts due to MSMEs and calculating interest payable thereon as per statutory provisions for separate disclosure in financial statements. ✔
B. Ignoring MSMED Act compliance since it is a tax matter.
C. Confirming that MSME suppliers receive no interest on delayed payments.
D. Classifying all MSME payables as long-term borrowings.
Explanation: Schedule III of the Companies Act, 2013 mandates separate disclosure of dues to Micro and Small Enterprises, including principal amounts remaining unpaid, interest due thereon, and delayed payment analysis under the MSMED Act.
Medium SCENARIO · Cash and Bank | Cash-in-Transit | Subsequent Verification
How should the auditor verify cash-in-transit between local store bank accounts and the central pool account at year-end?
A. Trace the subsequent credit in the central pool bank statement in the subsequent period and verify bank transfer advices.
B. Assume the cash is lost if not credited on March 31. ✔
C. Send confirmation requests to store cashiers only.
D. Review the petty cash voucher book.
Explanation: Cash-in-transit between bank accounts at year-end is verified by checking bank transfer advices and tracing the corresponding credit entries in the receiving bank statement in the early days of the subsequent period.

Paper 5: Auditing and Ethics · Module 2 · Chapter 6:

Audit — 55 rows
Easy NORMAL · SA 230 | Audit Documentation | Auditor Responsibility
Which standard on auditing primarily establishes the auditor's responsibility to prepare audit documentation for an audit of financial statements?
A. SA 200
B. SA 230 ✔
C. SA 240
D. SA 500
Explanation: SA 230, 'Audit Documentation', deals with the auditor's responsibility to prepare audit documentation for an audit of financial statements. It sets out the core requirements for recording procedures performed, evidence obtained, and conclusions reached.
Easy NORMAL · Purpose of Documentation | SA 230 | Audit Evidence
What is the primary purpose of maintaining adequate audit documentation according to SA 230?
A. To provide a detailed billing record for professional fees
B. To provide sufficient and appropriate record of the basis for the auditor's report and evidence that the audit was planned and performed in accordance with SAs ✔
C. To replace the client's accounting books and financial records in case of loss
D. To serve as a permanent marketing brochure for the auditing firm
Explanation: According to SA 230, audit documentation provides evidence of the auditor's basis for a conclusion about the achievement of the overall objectives and evidence that the audit was planned and performed in accordance with SAs and applicable legal requirements.
Easy NORMAL · Secondary Benefits | Audit Documentation | SQC 1
Which of the following is NOT typically considered an administrative purpose or secondary benefit of audit documentation?
A. Enabling the audit team to plan and perform the audit
B. Enabling quality control reviews and inspections in accordance with SQC 1 / Standard on Quality Management (SQM)
C. Enabling the conduct of statutory tax assessments for the client's customers ✔
D. Enabling the auditor to be accountable for their work
Explanation: Assisting tax assessments of the client's customers has no relation to audit documentation. Secondary benefits include quality control reviews, enabling the team to plan/perform, and accountability.
Easy NORMAL · Audit File | Definitions | SA 230
In the context of audit documentation, what does the term 'Audit File' refer to?
A. The client's general ledger and trial balance
B. One or more folders or other storage media, in physical or electronic form, containing the records that comprise the audit documentation for a specific engagement ✔
C. The complete permanent file maintained by the client's internal audit department
D. The statutory minute books of the company under audit
Explanation: SA 230 defines an audit file as one or more folders or other storage media, in physical or electronic form, containing the records that comprise the audit documentation for a specific engagement.
Easy NORMAL · File Assembly | Time Limit | SA 230
When should the assembly of the final audit file be completed after the date of the auditor's report, as per the guidelines under SA 230?
A. Within 30 days
B. Within 60 days ✔
C. Within 90 days
D. Within 180 days
Explanation: SQC 1 and SA 230 require that the assembly of the final audit file is typically completed on a timely basis after the date of the auditor's report, not exceeding 60 days.
Medium NORMAL · Retention Period | SQC 1 | Audit File
What is the minimum recommended retention period for audit documentation for companies under standard professional practice guidelines and SQC 1 / SQM (unless laws require otherwise)?
A. Not less than 3 years
B. Not less than 5 years
C. Not less than 7 years ✔
D. Not less than 10 years
Explanation: SQC 1 / SQM 1 requires firms to establish policies and procedures for the timely completion of the assembly of audit files, usually providing a retention period of not less than 7 years from the date of the auditor's report.
Easy NORMAL · Permanent Audit File | Audit Files | Documentation Structure
Which of the following describes the nature of 'Permanent Audit File' (PAF)?
A. Contains documents of continuing importance and relevance to audits of subsequent years ✔
B. Contains working papers applicable solely to the current year's audit engagement
C. Contains the confidential tax records of the engagement partner
D. Contains permanent permanent-loan agreements between the directors and the bank
Explanation: A Permanent Audit File (PAF) contains information of continuing importance to subsequent audits, such as memorandum of association, major legal contracts, and organization structure charts.
Easy NORMAL · Current Audit File | Audit Working Papers | PAF vs CAF
Which of the following documents would typically be filed in the Current Audit File (CAF) rather than the Permanent Audit File (PAF)?
A. Articles of Association of the company
B. Copy of the borrowing powers memorandum
C. Substantive test working papers for trade receivables confirmation for the current year ✔
D. Long-term lease agreements signed 10 years ago with indefinite renewal
Explanation: Substantive test working papers for current year transactions (like receivables confirmation) pertain strictly to the current period and are filed in the Current Audit File.
Medium NORMAL · Experienced Auditor | SA 230 | Judgment
An experienced auditor, with no previous connection to the audit, reviews the audit documentation. What standard of sufficiency must this documentation meet?
A. It must allow the experienced auditor to replicate the entire client business model
B. It must enable an experienced auditor, having no previous connection with the audit, to understand the significant professional judgments made ✔
C. It must permit the experienced auditor to manage the client's tax audits directly
D. It must provide word-for-word audio transcripts of all management interviews
Explanation: SA 230 requires that audit documentation be sufficient to enable an experienced auditor, having no previous connection with the audit, to understand the significant professional judgments made, nature/timing/extent of procedures, and results.
Medium NORMAL · Reviewers | Sign-offs | SA 230 Requirements
In preparing audit documentation, the auditor should record who performed the audit work and the date such work was completed. What else must be documented regarding the review?
A. Who reviewed the audit work performed and the date and extent of such review ✔
B. The personal background and academic qualifications of the reviewer
C. The exact salary grade of the review assistant
D. The software license key used by the reviewer
Explanation: SA 230 mandates documenting who performed the audit work and the date of completion, as well as who reviewed the audit work performed and the date and extent of such review.
Hard NORMAL · Exceptional Circumstances | Post-Report Documentation | SA 230
If, in exceptional circumstances, the auditor performs new or additional audit procedures or draws new conclusions after the date of the auditor's report, what must the auditor document?
A. Only the revised final balance sheet
B. The exceptional circumstances encountered, new procedures performed, evidence obtained, conclusions reached, and when and by whom the changes were made ✔
C. An apology letter to the board of directors explaining the delay
D. The internal performance review score of the audit junior
Explanation: When exceptional circumstances arise after the date of the auditor's report, SA 230 requires the auditor to document the circumstances, the new procedures performed, evidence obtained, conclusions reached, and who made and reviewed the changes.
Medium NORMAL · File Assembly | Completion | SQC 1
When is the assembly process of an audit file legally or professionally considered to be finalized?
A. When the draft report is sent to the client via email
B. Once the final audit file has been fully assembled within the 60-day limit following the auditor's report date ✔
C. When the audit fee is fully collected and receipted
D. When the Annual General Meeting (AGM) is concluded
Explanation: Audit file assembly is the administrative process of aggregating working papers into the final audit file, completed typically within 60 days after the date of the auditor's report, marking finalization of the file.
Medium NORMAL · Retention | Prohibition of Deletion | SQC 1
Can an auditor delete or discard audit documentation after the audit report has been issued?
A. Yes, any working paper older than 30 days can be deleted at the partner's discretion
B. No, after the assembly of the final audit file has been completed, the auditor shall not delete or discard audit documentation of any nature before the end of its retention period ✔
C. Yes, all digital working papers can be deleted once the client pays the final bill
D. Yes, working papers that contain negative findings can be destroyed to protect client relations
Explanation: Once the final audit file assembly is completed, the auditor must not delete or discard audit documentation before the end of the retention period, as per SQC 1 / SQM 1 and SA 230 principles.
Medium NORMAL · Form and Content | SA 230 Factors | Complexity
Which of the following factors affects the form, content, and extent of audit documentation?
A. The size and complexity of the entity ✔
B. The personal political affiliations of the audit team members
C. The color scheme used in the client's corporate office
D. The auditor's personal preference for paper-based vs electronic media
Explanation: SA 230 states that the form, content, and extent of audit documentation depend on factors such as the size and complexity of the entity, the nature of the audit procedures to be performed, and identified risks of material misstatement.
Medium NORMAL · Working Papers | Ownership | Confidentiality
What does an 'Audit Working Paper' property principle dictate regarding ownership?
A. Working papers belong jointly to the client and the auditor
B. Working papers belong exclusively to the auditor ✔
C. Working papers belong to the Ministry of Corporate Affairs upon completion
D. Working papers belong to the client because the client paid the audit fee
Explanation: Audit working papers are the property of the auditor. They contain the auditor's confidential records, professional judgments, and working notes, and are not public or client property.
Medium NORMAL · Identifying Characteristics | Traceability | SA 230
In documenting the nature, timing, and extent of audit procedures performed, what specific details must the auditor record according to SA 230?
A. The identifying characteristics of the specific items or matters tested ✔
B. The astrological sign of the client's chief accountant during the test period
C. The brand and model number of the client's office printers
D. The exact weather conditions on the day physical inventory count was observed
Explanation: SA 230 explicitly requires recording the identifying characteristics of the specific items or matters tested (e.g., specific invoice numbers or sample IDs) to ensure traceability and reproducibility.
Hard NORMAL · Inconsistent Information | Significant Matters | SA 230
If an auditor identifies information that contradicts or is inconsistent with the auditor's final conclusion regarding a significant matter, how should it be handled in documentation?
A. It must be immediately shredded to avoid confusing the audit reviewer
B. The auditor shall document how the inconsistency was addressed in reaching the final conclusion ✔
C. It should be ignored if the audit partner decides to issue an unmodified opinion
D. It should be handed over to the client's legal counsel without noting it in the file
Explanation: SA 230 requires that if the auditor identifies information that is inconsistent with the auditor's final conclusion regarding a significant matter, the auditor shall document how the inconsistency was addressed.
Hard NORMAL · Significant Matters | Risk Assessment | SA 230
Which of the following is considered a 'significant matter' in audit documentation?
A. Minor rounding errors of Rs. 10 in miscellaneous expense ledger
B. Matters that give rise to significant risks, results of audit procedures indicating potential material misstatement, and circumstances causing significant difficulty in applying necessary audit procedures ✔
C. The choice of lunch restaurant by the audit assistants during fieldwork
D. Routine verification of 5 petty cash vouchers
Explanation: Significant matters include those giving rise to significant risks, results indicating material misstatements, revised risk assessments, and circumstances causing significant difficulty in applying procedures.
Hard NORMAL · Legal Implications | Burden of Proof | Documentation Failure
What is the primary implication if an auditor fails to document a crucial audit procedure performed to verify revenue?
A. It is legally presumed that the procedure was never performed, shifting the burden of proof onto the auditor in regulatory/legal proceedings ✔
B. The client will receive an automatic tax refund from the Income Tax Department
C. The audit report automatically converts from unmodified to adverse
D. The ICAI will increase the firm's annual membership fee
Explanation: Under auditing standards and legal precedents, 'what is not documented is not done'. Failure to document creates a rebuttable presumption that the work was not performed, leaving the auditor vulnerable in legal or disciplinary reviews.
Easy NORMAL · Tick Marks | Working Paper Conventions | Auditing Techniques
Which of the following describes 'Tick Marks' used in audit working papers?
A. Symbols or abbreviations used to denote specific audit work done, accompanied by a legend explaining their meaning ✔
B. Electronic notifications sent to the client when an invoice is paid
C. Time sheets filled out by audit interns at the end of every week
D. Checkmarks used by the tax authorities to verify GST returns
Explanation: Tick marks are standardized symbols or shorthand annotations (e.g., footed, agreed to invoice) used in working papers to indicate specific checking steps, accompanied by an explanatory legend.
Medium NORMAL · Custody and Integrity | SQC 1 | Confidentiality
Under SQC 1 / SQM 1, what policy must an audit firm establish regarding the confidentiality, safe custody, integrity, accessibility, and retrievability of engagement documentation?
A. Policies and procedures designed to maintain them throughout the retention period ✔
B. Policies permitting open access to all audit documentation by general public investors
C. Policies requiring all physical working papers to be burned after 1 year
D. Policies allowing client executives to edit working papers at their convenience
Explanation: SQC 1 / SQM requires firms to establish policies and procedures to maintain confidentiality, safe custody, integrity, accessibility, and retrievability of engagement documentation.
Hard NORMAL · File Assembly | Administrative Changes | SA 230
Can working papers be prepared after the date of the auditor's report during the file assembly period?
A. No, absolutely no documentation can be added or sorted after the report date
B. Yes, sorting, collating, and cross-referencing working papers or signing off on completion checklists are administrative changes permitted during file assembly ✔
C. Yes, substantive audit procedures not performed before the report date can be completed and backdated
D. Yes, new substantive sample testing can be conducted and inserted as if done prior to the report
Explanation: During the final file assembly period, the auditor may make administrative changes (sorting, collating, signing off checklists) but cannot perform new audit procedures or draw new conclusions unless exceptional circumstances exist.
Medium NORMAL · Oral Discussions | Significant Matters | SA 230
How should an auditor document oral discussions with management regarding significant matters arising during the audit?
A. Oral discussions need never be documented under any circumstances
B. By recording the significant matters discussed, when and with whom the discussions took place, and the resultant summaries of management responses ✔
C. By video-recording every conversation and uploading it to social media
D. By asking management to sign a blank sheet of paper
Explanation: When the auditor has discussions of significant matters with management, those discussions must be documented, including when and with whom they took place and the summary of responses.
Medium NORMAL · Standardized Templates | Professional Skepticism | Audit Risk
What is the primary risk associated with over-reliance on standardized or pre-printed audit documentation templates?
A. It saves too much time for the engagement team
B. It may lead to mechanical check-box auditing without exercising adequate professional skepticism and tailoring procedures to specific entity risks
C. It reduces the paper cost for the audit firm ✔
D. It automatically violates Company Law provisions
Explanation: Option 2 is correct: over-reliance on standardized templates can lead to rote check-box auditing without exercising proper professional skepticism or tailoring working papers to entity-specific risks.
Easy NORMAL · Cross-Referencing | Working Papers | Audit Technique
Which of the following best defines 'Cross-Referencing' in audit working papers?
A. Linking figures and schedules in the working papers to ensure consistency between the trial balance, lead schedules, and detailed substantiation sheets ✔
B. Comparing the client's financial statements with competitor companies in the same industry
C. Checking whether the client's bank statements cross-match with customer invoices
D. Sharing working papers with rival audit firms for peer comparison
Explanation: Cross-referencing connects related audit schedules and working papers (e.g., tying a lead schedule balance to a detailed testing schedule), facilitating review and verification.
Easy NORMAL · Electronic Documentation | Audit Tools | SA 230
If an auditor uses automated electronic audit tools and software, are these outputs considered part of audit documentation?
A. No, only handwritten notes on paper qualify as audit documentation
B. Yes, electronic working papers, automated data analytics outputs, and system logs form an integral part of audit documentation ✔
C. Only if printed out and signed in wet ink by the CEO
D. Only if stored on a physical floppy disk
Explanation: Audit documentation can be recorded on paper or on electronic or other media. Electronic workpapers, screenshots, and analytics outputs are fully valid and form part of the documentation.
Medium NORMAL · Audit Plan Modification | Risk Response | Documentation
When an engagement partner modifies an audit plan during the course of an audit due to unexpected risks, what must be documented regarding the change?
A. The reasons for the modification and the resulting amended audit procedures ✔
B. Only the budget overrun caused by the change
C. A formal apology to the audit senior
D. Nothing, as internal planning changes do not need documentation
Explanation: Significant changes to the overall audit strategy and audit plan, and the reasons therefor, must be documented to show how the auditor responded to assessed risks.
Medium NORMAL · Dating Working Papers | Review Process | SA 230
Why is it important to include the date on each individual working paper?
A. To establish when the specific procedure was performed and facilitate chronological review by supervisors ✔
B. To calculate employee monthly payroll and overtime hours
C. To determine the exact expiry date of the client's tax registration
D. To fulfill standard office stationery branding rules
Explanation: Dating individual working papers establishes the timeline of execution and helps the reviewer verify that work was completed timely and before the auditor's report date.
Medium NORMAL · Lead Schedule | Working Paper Structure | Audit Schedules
In the context of statutory audit documentation, what is a 'Lead Schedule'?
A. A summary working paper that groups related sub-accounts (e.g., various bank accounts) and ties the total to the financial statement line item ✔
B. The schedule of audit partner meetings with the CEO
C. The timeline of tax deadlines set by the government
D. The checklist used to onboard new audit trainees
Explanation: A lead schedule summarizes individual account balances (sub-schedules) and ties them directly into the primary financial statement figures, acting as a bridge in working papers.
Hard NORMAL · Confidentiality Exception | Regulatory Inspection | Ethics
If a regulatory authority (such as NFRA or ICAI Quality Review Board) requests audit working papers, does releasing them violate client confidentiality?
A. Yes, releasing working papers to anyone under any circumstances violates confidentiality
B. No, disclosure required by law or professional regulatory mandates (e.g., QRB inspections or statutory investigations) is an established exception to confidentiality ✔
C. Yes, unless the client's shareholders pass a unanimous special resolution
D. No, provided the auditor charges a review fee to the regulator
Explanation: Client confidentiality is subject to legal and professional exceptions, such as quality reviews by ICAI's QRB, regulatory investigations, or court orders, where the auditor is required to produce working papers.
CASE SCENARIO: M/s Sharma & Associates, Chartered Accountants, are conducting the statutory audit of Apex Pharmaceuticals Ltd. for the financial year 2025-26. During the audit, the engagement senior, CA Rahul, tests trade receivables and notes a significant divergence between customer confirmations and ledger balances. Furthermore, management provides verbal explanations that directly contradict an internal audit memo found in the client's file. CA Rahul prepares working papers on electronic media, signs off on them, and submits them to the engagement partner, CA Sharma, for review. The audit report is signed on May 30, 2026.
Hard SCENARIO · Inconsistent Information | SA 230 | Significant Matters
How should CA Rahul and CA Sharma document the contradictory evidence between management's oral explanation and the internal audit memo?
A. Ignore the internal audit memo as it is an internal document
B. Document the inconsistency and how it was addressed in reaching the final conclusion ✔
C. Discard the customer confirmations to maintain harmony with management
D. Request management to rewrite the internal audit memo with matching dates
Explanation: As per SA 230, if the auditor identifies information that is inconsistent with the final conclusion regarding a significant matter, the auditor must document how the inconsistency was addressed.
Hard SCENARIO · File Assembly | Time Limit | SQC 1
What is the final deadline for M/s Sharma & Associates to complete the assembly of the final audit file for Apex Pharmaceuticals Ltd.?
A. June 30, 2026
B. July 29, 2026 ✔
C. August 28, 2026
D. November 26, 2026
Explanation: Under SQC 1 / SQM 1 and SA 230, the assembly of the final audit file should be completed typically not more than 60 days after the date of the auditor's report (May 30, 2026 + 60 days lands in late July 2026).
Medium SCENARIO · Electronic Working Papers | SA 230 | Media
Can CA Rahul include electronic working papers and digital analytics output as part of the audit documentation?
A. No, audit documentation must be strictly handwritten in bound books
B. Yes, electronic forms of working papers are fully acceptable provided they meet SA 230 requirements ✔
C. Only if converted into notarized physical paper within 24 hours
D. Only if approved in writing by the company's Board of Directors
Explanation: SA 230 explicitly permits audit documentation to be recorded on electronic or other media, provided the integrity and accessibility of the files are maintained.
Medium SCENARIO · Ownership | Working Papers | Professional Ethics
Who holds the legal ownership of the audit working papers prepared by CA Rahul during the audit of Apex Pharmaceuticals Ltd.?
A. Apex Pharmaceuticals Ltd. because they paid the audit fees
B. M/s Sharma & Associates, the audit firm ✔
C. The Institute of Chartered Accountants of India (ICAI)
D. Jointly owned by the audit partner and the company's CFO
Explanation: Audit working papers are the exclusive property of the auditor (M/s Sharma & Associates), subject to professional confidentiality and regulatory retention rules.
CASE SCENARIO: In August 2026, during a peer review of M/s Verma & Co., the reviewer examines the audit documentation for a manufacturing client audited for the year ended March 31, 2026. The reviewer notices that for a major property, plant, and equipment (PPE) addition, the working paper lacks identifying characteristics of the specific invoice tested. Furthermore, the engagement partner wishes to add a few explanatory notes to the current file after the assembly period has lapsed, citing a minor clarification received from a plant engineer.
Hard SCENARIO · Identifying Characteristics | SA 230 | Peer Review
What is the implication of the working paper lacking identifying characteristics for the PPE invoice tested?
A. It violates SA 230 requirements, making it impossible for an external reviewer to identify and re-test the exact item ✔
B. It is completely acceptable as long as the PPE total matches the trial balance
C. It triggers an automatic tax penalty for the client
D. It invalidates the client's depreciation policy permanently
Explanation: SA 230 requires recording identifying characteristics of items tested so that the work is reproducible and verifiable by reviewers. Lacking this violates documentation standards.
Hard SCENARIO · File Modification | Post-Assembly | SQC 1
Can the engagement partner add new explanatory notes to the audit file after the final file assembly has been completed?
A. Yes, partners can alter files anytime before the next annual general meeting
B. No, after assembly completion, the auditor shall not delete or discard documentation, and additions are restricted unless exceptional circumstances apply (and must be documented as such) ✔
C. Yes, administrative clarifications can be freely added without restriction at any point
D. Yes, provided the client signs a consent form
Explanation: Once final file assembly is completed, modification of audit documentation is generally prohibited except for administrative changes during assembly or under exceptional post-report circumstances with proper documentation.
Medium SCENARIO · Retention Period | SQC 1 | Audit File
What is the minimum retention period M/s Verma & Co. must maintain for this audit file under SQC 1 / SQM standards?
A. At least 3 years from the date of the auditor's report
B. At least 5 years from the date of the auditor's report
C. At least 7 years from the date of the auditor's report ✔
D. Indefinitely until the company is wound up
Explanation: The standard retention period for engagement documentation under SQC 1 / SQM 1 is not less than 7 years from the date of the auditor's report.
Hard SCENARIO · Confidentiality | Peer Review | Ethics Exception
During the peer review, the reviewer requests access to the working papers. Does granting this access breach client confidentiality?
A. Yes, showing files to a peer reviewer is a direct violation of professional ethics
B. No, professional bodies' quality review / peer review programs are recognized exceptions where confidentiality obligations are superseded by regulatory requirements ✔
C. Yes, unless the client's managing director is present during the review
D. No, because peer reviewers are employees of the client company
Explanation: Disclosing working papers to authorized peer reviewers or quality review boards does not breach confidentiality as it is conducted under statutory or professional regulatory authority.
CASE SCENARIO: CA Kapoor is reviewing the audit working files prepared by the audit team for a major retail client, HyperMart Retail Ltd. During the review, CA Kapoor finds that several working papers lack sign-offs indicating who performed the work and when it was completed. Additionally, a complex leasing transaction was evaluated, but the team omitted documentation regarding the professional judgment applied in determining lease classification under Ind AS 116.
Medium SCENARIO · Sign-offs | SA 230 Requirements | Review
What does the omission of sign-offs (who performed the work and date of completion) violate under SA 230?
A. It violates the requirement to document who performed the work and the date of completion, as well as who reviewed it ✔
B. It violates the client's corporate governance code
C. It violates the Income Tax Act audit filing deadline
D. It violates the banking covenant agreements
Explanation: SA 230 explicitly requires the auditor to record who performed the audit work and the date of completion, as well as who reviewed the work and the date/extent of review.
Hard SCENARIO · Professional Judgment | Significant Matters | SA 230
Why is the omission of documentation regarding professional judgments on the lease classification under Ind AS 116 critical?
A. Because lease accounting has no impact on financial statements
B. Because significant professional judgments must be documented to enable an experienced auditor to understand the basis for conclusions on significant matters ✔
C. Because leasing is solely an internal management decision
D. Because all lease files must be sent directly to the Registrar of Companies
Explanation: SA 230 requires documenting significant professional judgments to demonstrate that the auditor evaluated complex accounting treatments and reached appropriate conclusions.
Hard SCENARIO · Experienced Auditor | Standard of Review | SA 230
If an experienced auditor with no prior connection to HyperMart Retail Ltd. reviews this file, what standard must the documentation meet?
A. It must enable them to understand the significant professional judgments, nature, timing, extent of procedures, and results ✔
B. It must allow them to audit the client's tax returns for the next 5 years without assistance
C. It must provide a complete video record of all stock-taking counts
D. It must replicate the client's ERP database structure
Explanation: The benchmark under SA 230 is that documentation must enable an experienced auditor having no previous connection with the audit to understand the work, evidence, and judgments.
Medium SCENARIO · Working Paper Completion | Partner Review | Pre-Issuance
How should CA Kapoor rectify the missing sign-offs and documentation deficiencies before the audit report is issued?
A. Instruct the team members to complete and sign off their respective working papers with actual completion dates prior to report finalization ✔
B. Sign off all working papers personally as the partner without verifying the work
C. Ignore the omissions since the financial numbers are correct
D. Issue a qualified audit report solely due to missing working paper signatures
Explanation: Before the audit report is finalized and issued, the engagement team should ensure all working papers are properly completed, reviewed, and signed off.
CASE SCENARIO: M/s Gupta & Co. completed the audit of Stellar Tech Ltd. and issued the audit report on June 15, 2026. On July 10, 2026, while the final file assembly was still underway, the audit senior discovered a major unrecorded liability that existed at the balance sheet date. The engagement partner decided to perform additional audit procedures, modify the risk assessment, and ultimately revise the audit report on July 25, 2026.
Hard SCENARIO · Exceptional Circumstances | Post-Report Procedures | SA 230
Can the audit team perform additional audit procedures and modify the audit report during the file assembly period?
A. No, once the original report date of June 15 has passed, no further procedures can ever be performed
B. Yes, exceptional circumstances (such as discovering a major unrecorded liability before assembly completion) permit performing new procedures and modifying conclusions, with mandatory documentation ✔
C. Yes, provided the client pays an extra fee
D. Yes, but the revision must be backdated to June 15
Explanation: When exceptional circumstances arise after the date of the auditor's report (such as discovering a significant misstatement during assembly), the auditor may perform additional procedures and document the circumstances.
Hard SCENARIO · Documentation Requirements | Exceptional Circumstances | SA 230
What specific details must M/s Gupta & Co. document regarding these post-report procedures?
A. Only the new revised net profit figure
B. The exceptional circumstances, new procedures performed, evidence obtained, conclusions reached, and when and by whom changes were made and reviewed ✔
C. A letter of resignation from the audit senior
D. The updated software license agreement
Explanation: SA 230 explicitly prescribes documenting the exceptional circumstances, new procedures, evidence, conclusions, and the personnel involved in making and reviewing the changes.
Hard SCENARIO · File Assembly | Time Limit | Revised Report
When does the 60-day period for final file assembly begin in this scenario where a revised audit report was issued on July 25, 2026?
A. June 15, 2026 (the date of the original report)
B. July 25, 2026 (the date of the revised auditor's report) ✔
C. March 31, 2026 (the balance sheet date)
D. August 15, 2026
Explanation: When reports are reissued or revised due to exceptional circumstances, the final assembly time limit runs from the date of the final/revised auditor's report (July 25, 2026).
Medium SCENARIO · Audit File Integrity | Retention | SA 230
Is the original working paper file for Stellar Tech Ltd. discarded when the new procedures are performed?
A. Yes, old working papers must be destroyed immediately
B. No, audit documentation must retain both the original records and the documentation of the changes and subsequent procedures ✔
C. Yes, to save electronic storage space
D. Only if approved by the client's internal audit committee
Explanation: The audit file must maintain a complete and accurate historical record, including the original documentation, the exceptional circumstances, and the subsequent modifications.
CASE SCENARIO: CA Meera is appointed as the statutory auditor of a newly incorporated manufacturing company, Nova Steel Works Pvt. Ltd. During the planning phase, CA Meera establishes the overall audit strategy and creates both a Permanent Audit File (PAF) and a Current Audit File (CAF). She instructs her team on how to cross-reference schedules, use standardized tick marks, and document every discussion held with the plant managers regarding production capacity.
Easy SCENARIO · Permanent Audit File | Audit Files | PAF vs CAF
Which of the following documents should CA Meera place in the Permanent Audit File (PAF) for Nova Steel Works Pvt. Ltd.?

B. Bank confirmation letters for the current financial year ending March 31
C. Substantive sample testing sheets for trade payables
D. The current year physical inventory observation count sheets

Easy SCENARIO · Cross-Referencing | Working Papers | Audit Technique
What is the primary function of cross-referencing working papers in CA Meera's audit engagement?
A. To link lead schedules with detailed sub-schedules and financial statement line items for easy verification and review ✔
B. To connect the auditor's personal bank account with the client's payroll
C. To match the client's invoices with competitor pricing data
D. To comply with GST filing invoice matching rules
Explanation: Cross-referencing creates an audit trail within working papers, linking summary lead schedules to underlying detail schedules, ensuring mathematical and logical consistency.
Medium SCENARIO · Oral Discussions | Documentation | SA 230
How should the audit team document their discussions with plant managers regarding production capacity?
A. By recording the date, participants, significant matters discussed, and summary of management responses ✔
B. By recording only the names of the managers without any notes
C. By asking the managers to record an audio file and keeping it on a personal phone

Explanation: SA 230 requires documenting oral discussions of significant matters, including when and with whom they took place and the summary of responses.
Easy SCENARIO · Tick Marks | Working Paper Conventions | Audit Techniques
What is the purpose of using standardized tick marks in the working papers of Nova Steel Works Pvt. Ltd.?

B. To decorate the working papers for the annual report
C. To calculate employee bonuses automatically

Paper 5: Auditing and Ethics · Module 2 · Chapter 7:

Audit — 55 rows
Easy NORMAL · SA 560 | Subsequent Events | Auditor Responsibility
According to SA 560, what is the auditor's responsibility regarding subsequent events during the period from the date of the financial statements to the date of the auditor's report?
A. The auditor has no responsibility to perform audit procedures during this period.
B. The auditor shall perform audit procedures designed to identify all events that may require adjustment of, or disclosure in, the financial statements.
C. The auditor shall perform audit procedures specifically designed to obtain sufficient appropriate audit evidence that all events occurring up to the date of the report that require adjustment or disclosure have been identified. ✔
D. The auditor shall only rely on management representation letters regarding events after the balance sheet date.
Explanation: Under SA 560 (Subsequent Events), the auditor must perform audit procedures specifically designed to obtain sufficient appropriate audit evidence that all events up to the date of the auditor's report requiring adjustment or disclosure are identified.
Medium NORMAL · SA 560 | Facts Known After Issuance | Management Discussion
When an auditor becomes aware of a fact that, had it been known to the auditor at the date of the auditor's report, may have caused the auditor to amend the report, and the financial statements have already been issued, what is the first step the auditor should take according to SA 560?
A. Immediately notify regulatory authorities without discussing with management.
B. Discuss the matter with management and, where appropriate, those charged with governance. ✔
C. Issue a revised auditor's report immediately without management input.
D. Take no action since the financial statements are already issued.
Explanation: As per SA 560, when facts come to light after issuance that would have affected the report, the auditor must first discuss the matter with management and those charged with governance to determine if the financial statements need revision.
Easy NORMAL · SA 570 | Going Concern | Financial Indicators
In the context of SA 570 (Going Concern), which of the following is considered a financial indicator that may cast significant doubt on an entity's ability to continue as a going concern?
A. Loss of key management personnel without replacement.
B. Net liability or net current liability position. ✔
C. Proceedings against the entity that may result in claims the entity is unlikely to satisfy.
D. Changes in law or regulation expected to adversely affect the entity.
Explanation: SA 570 classifies indicators into financial, operating, and other categories. A net liability or net current liability position is a prime financial indicator casting doubt on going concern.
Medium NORMAL · SA 570 | Management Assessment | Modified Opinion
Under SA 570, if management is unwilling to make or extend its assessment of the entity's going concern ability when requested by the auditor, what implication does this have for the audit opinion?
A. The auditor shall express an unmodified opinion with an Emphasis of Matter paragraph.
B. The auditor may issue an unmodified opinion if other evidence is sufficient.
C. The auditor shall consider the implications for the audit report, which may include modifying the opinion. ✔
D. The auditor must immediately withdraw from the engagement regardless of legal constraints.
Explanation: If management is unwilling to make or extend its assessment when requested, the auditor needs to consider the implications, as this inability or unwillingness can lead to a modified opinion under SA 570.
Easy NORMAL · SA 580 | Written Representations | Management Responsibilities
What is the primary purpose of obtaining a Written Representation letter from management under SA 580?
A. To replace other audit procedures that the auditor is too lazy to perform.
B. To confirm that management has fulfilled its responsibility for the preparation of the financial statements and for the completeness of information provided. ✔
C. To legally bind management for any future audit failures or fraud discovered later.
D. To serve as the sole audit evidence for material financial statement assertions.
Explanation: SA 580 states that written representations are necessary to confirm that management has fulfilled its responsibilities for preparing financial statements and providing complete information, though they do not provide sufficient appropriate audit evidence on their own.
Medium NORMAL · SA 580 | Refusal of Representations | Scope Limitation
If management modifies or refuses to provide requested written representations considered necessary by the auditor, how should the auditor respond under SA 580?
A. Issue an unmodified opinion with an Other Matter paragraph.
B. Disclaim an opinion or withdraw from the engagement, where withdrawal is legally permitted. ✔
C. Assume management is honest and proceed to sign the report without restrictions.
D. Issue a qualified opinion based solely on lack of internal controls.
Explanation: Under SA 580, if management does not provide requested written representations, it constitutes a limitation on scope, requiring the auditor to disclaim an opinion or withdraw from the engagement.
Easy NORMAL · SA 260 | TCWG | Communication Requirements
According to SA 260 (Communication with Those Charged with Governance), which of the following matters should the auditor communicate?
A. Every single routine transaction tested during the interim audit.
B. The auditor's views about significant qualitative aspects of the entity's accounting practices, including accounting policies and estimates. ✔
C. The exact personal compensation details of all staff members in the finance department.
D. The internal audit schedule for the next three financial years.
Explanation: SA 260 requires the auditor to communicate significant findings from the audit, including the auditor's views about significant qualitative aspects of the entity's accounting practices.
Medium NORMAL · SA 220 | SQ 1 | Engagement Quality Review
What is the objective of the engagement quality review (EQR) performed under SQ 1 and SA 220?
A. To perform the audit procedures on behalf of the engagement partner to save time.
B. To provide an objective evaluation, before the auditor's report is dated, of the significant judgments the engagement team made and the conclusions they reached. ✔
C. To rewrite the financial statements to ensure compliance with tax laws.
D. To negotiate the audit fee with the entity's audit committee.
Explanation: Under SA 220 and SQ 1, an Engagement Quality Review provides an objective evaluation of significant judgments made by the team and conclusions reached before the report is issued.
Medium NORMAL · SA 450 | Uncorrected Misstatements | Evaluation
In evaluating misstatements identified during the audit, how should the auditor treat uncorrected misstatements under SA 450?
A. Ignore them if individually they are below overall materiality.
B. Communicate uncorrected misstatements to those charged with governance and request that they be corrected. ✔
C. Automatically issue an adverse opinion without further communication.
D. Accumulate them only if they relate to inventory valuations.
Explanation: SA 450 requires the auditor to communicate uncorrected misstatements to those charged with governance and request that they be corrected, and determine the effect of uncorrected misstatements individually or in aggregate.
Easy NORMAL · Audit Completion | Review Phase | Audit Process
What does the 'Finalization Stage' or completion phase of an audit primarily involve?
A. Planning the audit strategy and allocating resources to junior staff members.
B. Reviewing subsequent events, evaluating going concern, obtaining written representations, and forming the audit opinion. ✔
C. Conducting physical verification of inventory at the very beginning of the financial year.
D. Signing the contract of appointment with the board of directors.
Explanation: The completion phase of an audit involves reviewing subsequent events, evaluating going concern assumptions, obtaining written management representations, and finalizing the overall audit opinion.
Medium NORMAL · SA 560 | Post-Report Period | Auditor Obligations
Under SA 560, what is the auditor's obligation regarding events occurring between the date of the auditor's report and the date the financial statements are issued?
A. The auditor has no active obligation to perform audit procedures during this period. ✔
B. The auditor must conduct a full re-audit of all financial statement balances.
C. The auditor must issue a daily update report to the stock exchange.
D. The auditor must resign immediately to avoid subsequent liability.
Explanation: Under SA 560, after the date of the auditor's report, the auditor has no active obligation to perform audit procedures regarding the financial statements; however, if a fact becomes known that would have affected the report, action must be taken.
Medium NORMAL · SA 570 | Operating Indicators | Going Concern
Which of the following is an example of an operating indicator of going concern problems under SA 570?
A. Arrears or discontinuance of dividends.
B. Loss of major markets, key customer, or key supplier. ✔
C. Inability to comply with terms of loan agreements.
D. Negative operating cash flows indicated by historical or prospective financial statements.
Explanation: Loss of major markets, key customers, or key suppliers represents operating difficulties (operating indicators), whereas dividend arrears and loan covenant breaches are financial indicators.
Medium NORMAL · SA 570 | Assessment Period | Going Concern
When management's assessment of going concern covers a period of less than 12 months from the date of financial statements, what must the auditor do under SA 570?
A. Accept the assessment without question as management knows best.
B. Request management to extend its assessment period to at least 12 months from that date. ✔
C. Issue an adverse opinion immediately.
D. Disclaim an opinion without any further discussion.
Explanation: Under SA 570, if management's assessment covers less than 12 months, the auditor must request management to extend the assessment period to at least 12 months from the date of the financial statements.
Hard NORMAL · SA 570 | Material Uncertainty | Reporting
If going concern is a material uncertainty and it is adequately disclosed in the financial statements, how should the auditor's report be modified under SA 570?
A. Issue an adverse opinion due to fundamental accounting failure.
B. Issue an unmodified opinion and include a separate section under the heading 'Material Uncertainty Related to Going Concern'. ✔
C. Issue a qualified opinion due to scope limitation.
D. Omit any mention of going concern in the auditor's report to prevent panic.
Explanation: Under SA 570, when a material uncertainty exists and is adequately disclosed, the auditor expresses an unmodified opinion and includes a separate section in the auditor's report titled 'Material Uncertainty Related to Going Concern'.
Medium NORMAL · SA 580 | Written Representations | Scope Limitation
What should the auditor do if management refuses to provide a written representation on a matter that the auditor considers essential for the audit?
A. Treat it as a scope limitation and modify the opinion or withdraw. ✔
B. Sign the report with an unmodified opinion anyway.
C. Ask the shareholders to provide the written representation instead.
D. Issue a disclaimer of opinion without communicating with TCWG.
Explanation: Refusal by management to provide a written representation considered necessary by the auditor constitutes a limitation on scope, leading to a modified opinion (qualified or disclaimer) or resignation.
Medium NORMAL · SA 580 | Date of Representation | Audit Report
Which date should the written representation letter bear?
A. The date the audit engagement was initially accepted.
B. The exact date of the financial year-end balance sheet.
C. As near as practicable to, but not after, the date of the auditor's report. ✔
D. Any date chosen arbitrarily by management after the report is issued.
Explanation: Under SA 580, written representations must be dated as near as practicable to, but not after, the date of the auditor's report, to ensure they cover the relevant period up to the report date.
Hard NORMAL · SA 450 | Uncorrected Misstatements | Communication
Under SA 450, what must the auditor communicate to those charged with governance regarding uncorrected misstatements?
A. Only misstatements exceeding overall materiality.
B. The aggregate effect of uncorrected misstatements and whether they consider it material, individually or in aggregate. ✔
C. Only misstatements identified during the interim audit phase.
D. That management is prohibited from correcting any misstatements.
Explanation: SA 450 requires the auditor to communicate uncorrected misstatements and their potential effect on the audit opinion, detailing whether individual or aggregate uncorrected misstatements are material.
Medium NORMAL · SA 220 | SQ 1 | EQCR Mandate
When is an Engagement Quality Control Review (EQCR) mandatory for listed entities under SQ 1 and SA 220?
A. Only when the audit fee exceeds one crore rupees.
B. For audits of financial statements of all listed entities and other engagements as determined by firm policy or law. ✔
C. Only when requested by the Reserve Bank of India.
D. EQCR is never mandatory for listed entities.
Explanation: Under SQ 1 and SA 220, an engagement quality control review is mandatory for all audits of financial statements of listed entities and other high-risk engagements determined by the firm's quality control policies.
Medium NORMAL · SA 520 | Analytical Procedures | Overall Review
What is the primary objective of performing analytical procedures near the end of the audit during the overall review stage (SA 520)?
A. To test internal control operating effectiveness.
B. To assist the auditor in forming an overall conclusion as to whether the financial statements are consistent with the auditor's understanding of the entity. ✔
C. To replace substantive testing of inventory balances.
D. To calculate the exact tax liability of the entity.
Explanation: As per SA 520, analytical procedures performed near the end of the audit assist the auditor in forming an overall conclusion on whether the financial statements are consistent with the auditor's understanding of the entity.
Hard NORMAL · SA 230 | Audit Documentation | Working Papers
Which of the following documents forms part of the final audit documentation (audit file) that must be assembled within the completion time limit?
A. Superseded drafts of working papers and financial statements that were corrected.
B. Notes on contradictory matters that were resolved during the audit. ✔
C. Personal diaries of audit staff members unrelated to the audit.
D. Unrelated correspondence with potential clients.
Explanation: Under SA 230, the audit file must include documentation of how contradictory or inconsistent information regarding significant matters was addressed and resolved.
Easy NORMAL · SA 230 | SQ 1 | File Assembly Time Limit
According to SQ 1 / SA 230, what is the standard time limit for assembling the final audit file after the date of the auditor's report?
A. Not more than 30 days.
B. Not more than 60 days. ✔
C. Not more than 90 days.
D. Not more than 120 days.
Explanation: SQ 1 and SA 230 specify that the assembly of the final audit file should typically be completed not more than 60 days after the date of the auditor's report.
Hard NORMAL · SA 560 | Revised Financial Statements | New Report
What action should the auditor take if, after the financial statements have been issued, a subsequent event is discovered that requires amendment and management agrees to revise the financial statements?
A. Issue a new auditor's report on the revised financial statements containing an emphasis of matter regarding the revision. ✔
B. Verbally inform shareholders without issuing a new report.
C. Resign from the audit immediately.
D. Take no further action since the report was already issued.
Explanation: Under SA 560, if management revises financial statements after issuance, the auditor shall carry out necessary procedures and issue a new auditor's report on the revised financial statements.
Hard NORMAL · SA 570 | Inappropriate Going Concern | Adverse Opinion
When evaluating the going concern assumption, if events or conditions indicate a material uncertainty but management refuses to prepare the financial statements on a going concern basis, what type of opinion should the auditor issue?
A. Unmodified opinion.
B. Adverse opinion. ✔
C. Disclaimer of opinion.
D. Qualified opinion due to scope limitation.
Explanation: If financial statements are prepared inappropriately on a going concern basis (or management refuses when required), the financial statements are materially misstated, leading to an Adverse opinion under SA 570.
Easy NORMAL · SA 580 | Written Representations | Content
Which of the following is NOT a required content of written representations under SA 580?
A. Management has fulfilled its responsibility for preparing the financial statements.
B. Management has provided all relevant information and access as agreed.
C. Management guarantees that the company will remain profitable for the next five years. ✔
D. All uncorrected misstatements are immaterial, individually and in aggregate.
Explanation: Written representations do not require management to provide guarantees of future profitability; they cover responsibilities for financial statement preparation, completeness of information, and uncorrected misstatements.
Medium NORMAL · SA 706 | Emphasis of Matter | Audit Report
What is the primary purpose of an 'Emphasis of Matter' paragraph in the auditor's report?
A. To highlight a matter appropriately presented or disclosed in the financial statements that, in the auditor's judgment, is of such importance that it is fundamental to users' understanding. ✔
B. To qualify the audit opinion because of a material misstatement.
C. To report on illegal acts committed by the entity's competitors.
D. To excuse the auditor from liability regarding subsequent events.
Explanation: An Emphasis of Matter paragraph draws users' attention to a properly disclosed matter in the financial statements that is fundamental to their understanding, without modifying the audit opinion (SA 706).
Medium NORMAL · SA 260 | Independence | TCWG
Under SA 260, what should the auditor communicate regarding the independence of the audit firm to those charged with governance?
A. A statement that the audit firm and network firms have complied with relevant ethical requirements regarding independence. ✔
B. A detailed breakdown of the personal salaries of all audit partners.
C. Nothing, unless specifically requested by regulatory authorities.
D. An agreement that the audit firm will not charge any fees if the company suffers a loss.
Explanation: SA 260 requires the auditor to communicate a statement that the engagement team and others in the firm have complied with relevant ethical requirements regarding independence.
Medium NORMAL · SA 450 | Clearly Trivial | Misstatements
If an auditor identifies a misstatement during the audit, when is it considered 'clearly trivial' under SA 450?
A. When it is of a magnitude that will not need to be accumulated because it is clearly immaterial, whether taken individually or in aggregate. ✔
B. When management refuses to correct it under any circumstances.
C. When it exceeds overall materiality by at least 10%.
D. When it relates strictly to payroll deductions.
Explanation: Under SA 450, 'clearly trivial' misstatements are those of a completely different (smaller) order of magnitude than materiality, and do not need to be accumulated because they are clearly inconsequential.
Hard NORMAL · SA 230 | Documentation Modification | Audit File
What is the impact on the audit file if working papers are modified or added after the 60-day assembly period under SA 230?
A. Modifications are strictly prohibited under all circumstances.
B. The auditor must document the specific reasons for the modification, when and by whom they were made and reviewed. ✔
C. Working papers can be altered freely without any documentation requirement.
D. The audit report automatically becomes void.
Explanation: Under SA 230, if circumstances require amendments to audit documentation after the assembly period, the auditor must document the specific reasons, date, and person making and reviewing the changes.
Medium NORMAL · Subsequent Events | Type 1 Events | Adjusting Events
Which of the following is considered a 'Type 1' subsequent event under financial reporting frameworks (AS / Ind AS)?
A. An event indicating conditions that arose after the reporting period (e.g., major factory fire after year-end).
B. An event providing evidence of conditions that existed at the end of the reporting period (e.g., settlement of a court case after year-end). ✔
C. A routine change in the top management team six months after the balance sheet date.
D. A significant merger announcement taking place in the next financial year.
Explanation: Type 1 subsequent events provide evidence of conditions that existed at the end of the reporting period, requiring financial statement adjustments, whereas Type 2 events indicate conditions arising after year-end.
Easy NORMAL · SA 220 | Engagement Partner | Ultimate Responsibility
In the final review stage, who holds the ultimate responsibility for the audit opinion expressed on the entity's financial statements?
A. The engagement quality control reviewer.
B. The engagement partner. ✔
C. The audit senior in charge of fieldwork.
D. The Chief Financial Officer of the entity.
Explanation: Under SA 220, the engagement partner takes ultimate responsibility for the overall audit engagement and the resulting audit opinion, notwithstanding any reviews or consultations.
CASE SCENARIO: Zenith Ltd is finalising its financial statements for the year ended 31 March 2026. The audit team led by CA Raman is in the final review stage. On 10 May 2026, a major debtor owing ₹85 lakhs went into liquidation. The audit report is scheduled to be signed on 25 May 2026. Furthermore, management has provided a draft assessment of going concern covering only the next 8 months, citing long-term business uncertainty. CA Raman also noted several uncorrected misstatements amounting to ₹12 lakhs in aggregate, while overall materiality was set at ₹10 lakhs.
Hard SCENARIO · SA 560 | Subsequent Events | Debtor Liquidation
How should CA Raman treat the liquidation of the major debtor on 10 May 2026 under SA 560?
A. Ignore it because the liquidation occurred after the balance sheet date.
B. Treat it as an adjusting subsequent event providing evidence of conditions existing at year-end, requiring financial statement adjustment. ✔
C. Disclose it only in the Board of Directors' report without touching financial statements.
D. Issue a disclaimer of opinion due to bad debts.
Explanation: Under SA 560 and accounting standards, events providing evidence of conditions existing at the balance sheet date (such as debtor insolvency arising from financial distress present at year-end) are adjusting events requiring financial statement modification.
Medium SCENARIO · SA 570 | Going Concern Assessment | 12-Month Period
Regarding management's going concern assessment covering only 8 months, what action should CA Raman take under SA 570?
A. Accept the 8-month period since management knows the business best.
B. Request management to extend its assessment period to at least 12 months from the date of the financial statements. ✔
C. Issue an adverse opinion immediately without requesting any extension.
D. Resign from the audit engagement on the spot.
Explanation: Under SA 570, if management's assessment of going concern covers less than 12 months from the date of financial statements, the auditor must request management to extend the assessment period to at least 12 months.
Hard SCENARIO · SA 450 | Uncorrected Misstatements | Materiality Exceeded
Given that uncorrected misstatements amount to ₹12 lakhs against an overall materiality of ₹10 lakhs, what is CA Raman's evaluation requirement under SA 450?
A. Ignore the misstatements since the difference is only ₹2 lakhs.
B. Evaluate whether uncorrected misstatements are material, individually or in aggregate, and communicate them to management and TCWG requesting correction. ✔
C. Automatically issue an adverse opinion without communicating with management.
D. Record the misstatements in the engagement letter for the next year.
Explanation: Under SA 450, when uncorrected misstatements exceed materiality in aggregate, the auditor must evaluate their materiality and communicate them to management and those charged with governance, requesting correction.
Hard SCENARIO · SA 450 | SA 705 | Modified Opinion
If management refuses to adjust the financial statements for the debtor's liquidation and refuses to correct the uncorrected misstatements exceeding materiality, what audit opinion is CA Raman most likely required to issue?
A. Unmodified opinion.
B. Qualified or Adverse opinion depending on the pervasiveness of the misstatements. ✔
C. Disclaimer of opinion due to lack of written representations.
D. Clean report with an Emphasis of Matter paragraph.
Explanation: Under SA 450 and SA 705, if management refuses to correct misstatements that exceed materiality, the auditor must express a qualified or adverse opinion, depending on whether the effect is pervasive.
CASE SCENARIO: During the final review of Apex Pharma Ltd for the year ended 31 March 2026, engagement partner CA Priya reviews the audit documentation. The audit report date is 15 June 2026. The audit team obtained written representations from management dated 15 June 2026. However, CA Priya notices that documentation regarding a complex related-party transaction has contradictory evidence which was resolved orally but not documented in the working papers. Hard SCENARIO · SA 230 | Contradictory Evidence | Documentation
What does SA 230 require regarding the contradictory evidence on related-party transactions resolved orally?

C. The audit file should be destroyed and restarted from scratch.

Explanation: Under SA 230, if the auditor identifies information that is inconsistent with the auditor's final conclusion regarding a significant matter, the audit documentation must include how the inconsistency was addressed.
Medium SCENARIO · SA 580 | Written Representations | Report Date
What is the correct date for the written representation letter obtained by CA Priya's team?
A. 1 April 2025 (beginning of the financial year).
B. 15 June 2026 (as near as practicable to, but not after, the date of the auditor's report). ✔
C. 30 July 2026 (after the audit report is published).
D. Any arbitrary date chosen by the chief accountant.
Explanation: Under SA 580, written representations must be dated as near as practicable to, but not after, the date of the auditor's report.
Medium SCENARIO · SA 230 | SQ 1 | File Assembly Timeline
What is the mandatory timeline for assembling the final audit file for Apex Pharma Ltd after 15 June 2026 under SQ 1 and SA 230?
A. Within 15 days.
B. Within 30 days.
C. Within 60 days. ✔
D. Within 180 days.

Medium SCENARIO · SA 220 | EQCR | Quality Review
What is the primary role of the Engagement Quality Control Reviewer (EQCR) in the audit of Apex Pharma Ltd?
A. To perform all substantive testing of cash balances.
B. To provide an objective evaluation of the significant judgments made by the engagement team and conclusions reached before the report is dated. ✔
C. To negotiate audit fees with the board of directors.

Explanation: Under SA 220 and SQ 1, the EQCR provides an objective evaluation of significant judgments and conclusions of the engagement team before the auditor's report is dated.
CASE SCENARIO: Star Industries Ltd is facing severe financial difficulties. The company defaulted on bank loan repayments due on 28 February 2026, and its key supplier has cut off credit lines. CA Mehta is the statutory auditor for the year ended 31 March 2026. Management has prepared the financial statements on a going concern basis and included comprehensive disclosures regarding the financial difficulties and the bank restructuring negotiations currently underway.
Medium SCENARIO · SA 570 | Material Uncertainty | Indicators
Based on the facts, how should CA Mehta evaluate the going concern status under SA 570?
A. No going concern issue exists because management is negotiating.
B. Events indicate a material uncertainty that may cast significant doubt on the entity's ability to continue as a going concern. ✔
C. Star Industries Ltd must immediately be liquidated without audit reporting.
D. The auditor must issue an adverse opinion automatically.
Explanation: Loan defaults and loss of credit lines are major financial and operating indicators representing a material uncertainty regarding going concern under SA 570.
Hard SCENARIO · SA 570 | Adequate Disclosure | Reporting
Given that the material uncertainty is adequately disclosed in Star Industries Ltd's financial statements, what reporting requirement applies under SA 570?
A. Issue an adverse opinion because of the loan defaults.
B. Issue an unmodified opinion and include a separate section in the auditor's report titled 'Material Uncertainty Related to Going Concern'. ✔
C. Issue a disclaimer of opinion due to bank defaults.
D. Omit all references to going concern to avoid alarming shareholders.
Explanation: Under SA 570, if adequate disclosure of a material uncertainty is made in the financial statements, the auditor shall express an unmodified opinion and include a separate section under 'Material Uncertainty Related to Going Concern'.
Hard SCENARIO · SA 570 | Inadequate Disclosure | Modified Opinion
