What would be the reporting consequence under SA 570 if Star Industries Ltd refused to disclose the material uncertainty regarding its going concern?
A. The auditor shall express a qualified opinion or an adverse opinion. ✔
B. The auditor shall issue an unmodified opinion with an emphasis of matter.
C. The auditor shall ignore the lack of disclosure if management is cooperative.
D. The auditor shall issue a clean report.
Explanation: If adequate disclosure about a material uncertainty is not made in the financial statements, SA 570 requires the auditor to express a qualified opinion or an adverse opinion, as appropriate.
Easy SCENARIO · SA 570 | Financial Indicators | Loan Default
Which of the following is considered a financial indicator of going concern problems present in Star Industries Ltd?
A. Loss of key management personnel.
B. Default on loan repayments and loss of supplier credit lines. ✔
C. Changes in government environmental regulations.
D. Shortage of skilled technical workforce.
Explanation: Default on loan repayments and loss of supplier credit lines are prime financial indicators under SA 570.
CASE SCENARIO: During the final completion phase of Delta Engineering Ltd for the year ended 31 March 2026, statutory auditor CA Kumar reviews various communications and representation requirements. Management provides the signed written representation letter on 10 June 2026. CA Kumar communicates significant audit findings with Those Charged with Governance (TCWG) on 12 June 2026, and signs the audit report on 14 June 2026. An uncorrected misstatement of ₹5 lakhs was identified, which management refused to adjust, while overall materiality was set at ₹15 lakhs.
Medium SCENARIO · SA 450 | Uncorrected Misstatements | Evaluation
How should CA Kumar evaluate the uncorrected misstatement of ₹5 lakhs against the overall materiality of ₹15 lakhs under SA 450?
A. It must be forced as an adjustment since any error is material.
B. Since it is below overall materiality, CA Kumar should evaluate if it is material in aggregate or qualitatively, and communicate it to TCWG. ✔
C. It should be ignored entirely without documentation or communication.
D. It requires an immediate adverse opinion.
Explanation: Under SA 450, uncorrected misstatements below materiality must still be communicated to TCWG and evaluated for aggregate or qualitative materiality.
Medium SCENARIO · SA 260 | TCWG Communication | Significant Findings
What is the requirement regarding communication with TCWG under SA 260 during this final review phase?
A. The auditor must communicate significant findings from the audit, including accounting practices and uncorrected misstatements. ✔
B. Communication with TCWG is optional if the audit report is unmodified.
C. The auditor only communicates with the internal audit team, not TCWG.
D. TCWG must approve the audit report wording before signature.
Explanation: SA 260 requires the auditor to communicate significant findings from the audit, auditor's views on qualitative aspects of accounting, and uncorrected misstatements to those charged with governance.
Medium SCENARIO · SA 580 | Representation Date | Compliance
Was the written representation letter dated correctly under SA 580, given it was signed on 10 June 2026 and the report was signed on 14 June 2026?
A. No, it should have been dated 31 March 2026.
B. Yes, because it is dated as near as practicable to, but not after, the date of the auditor's report. ✔
C. No, it must be dated exactly 30 days after the report date.
D. No, written representations are not required to be dated.
Explanation: Under SA 580, the written representation letter must be dated as near as practicable to, but not after, the date of the auditor's report (10 June vs 14 June is appropriate).
Hard SCENARIO · SA 580 | Refusal | Scope Limitation
What is the implication if management refused to sign the written representation letter required by SA 580?
A. CA Kumar can issue an unmodified opinion without representation.
B. CA Kumar shall disclaim an opinion or withdraw from the engagement. ✔
C. CA Kumar should sign the report and blame management in a footnote.
D. CA Kumar must take over management responsibilities.
Explanation: Under SA 580, refusal by management to provide written representations constitutes a limitation on scope, requiring a disclaimer of opinion or withdrawal.
CASE SCENARIO: Global Tech Ltd published its audited financial statements on 1 July 2026. On 15 August 2026, auditor CA Sunil discovered a serious fraud perpetrated by the CFO that existed prior to 31 March 2026 (the balance sheet date) but was concealed effectively. Had CA Sunil known this during the audit, the audit report dated 20 June 2026 would have been significantly modified.
Hard SCENARIO · SA 560 | Facts After Issuance | Auditor Duty
Under SA 560, what is CA Sunil's responsibility regarding facts discovered after the financial statements have been issued?
A. CA Sunil has no responsibility since the report was already issued and published.
B. CA Sunil shall discuss the matter with management, determine if the statements need revision, and inquire how management intends to address the matter. ✔
C. CA Sunil must immediately liquidate the company's assets.
D. CA Sunil should personally rewrite the financial statements.
Explanation: Under SA 560, when facts discovered after issuance would have affected the report, the auditor must discuss with management and determine if revision is necessary and how management intends to address it.
Hard SCENARIO · SA 560 | Revised Statements | New Audit Report
If management of Global Tech Ltd revises the financial statements, what subsequent action must CA Sunil take under SA 560?
A. Perform necessary audit procedures on the revision and issue a new auditor's report. ✔
B. Do nothing further as management handled the revision.
C. Issue a verbal apology to the shareholders.
D. Resign from the audit firm immediately.
Explanation: Under SA 560, if management revises financial statements after issuance, the auditor shall carry out necessary procedures and provide a new auditor's report on the revised financial statements.
Hard SCENARIO · SA 560 | Management Refusal | Preventing Reliance
What should CA Sunil do if management refuses to take necessary steps to revise the financial statements despite the discovered fraud?
A. Keep silent to protect the audit firm's reputation.
B. Notify management and those charged with governance that the auditor will seek to prevent future reliance on the auditor's report. ✔
C. Approve the financial statements personally.
D. File a criminal lawsuit against the shareholders.
Explanation: Under SA 560, if management refuses to revise the financial statements when the auditor believes they need revision, the auditor shall notify management and TCWG that action will be taken to prevent reliance on the auditor's report.
Medium SCENARIO · SA 560 | Active Period | Audit Procedures
During the active audit period (before the report was issued), what was CA Sunil's obligation regarding subsequent events under SA 560?
A. To perform audit procedures designed to identify all events up to the date of the report that may require adjustment or disclosure. ✔
B. To audit all transactions occurring in the next five financial years.
C. To rely solely on management's verbal assurances.
D. To refrain from performing any tests after the balance sheet date.
Explanation: Under SA 560, between the balance sheet date and the date of the auditor's report, the auditor must perform audit procedures designed to identify events requiring adjustment or disclosure.

Paper 5: Auditing and Ethics · Module 2 · Chapter 8:

Audit — 55 rows
Easy NORMAL · SA 700 | Audit Report Basics | Forming an Opinion
Which of the following standards on auditing primarily establishes the requirements for forming an opinion and reporting on financial statements?
A. SA 700 (Revised) ✔
B. SA 705 (Revised)
C. SA 706 (Revised)
D. SA 570 (Revised)
Explanation: SA 700 (Revised), 'Forming an Opinion and Reporting on Financial Statements', deals with the auditor's responsibility to form an opinion on the financial statements and the form and content of the audit report. SA 705 and SA 706 deal with modifications and emphasis of matter paragraphs respectively. SA 570 deals with going concern.
Medium NORMAL · SA 705 | Modified Opinion | Adverse Opinion | Qualified Opinion
When the auditor concludes that the financial statements as a whole are not free from material misstatement, which type of modified opinion should be expressed?
A. Unmodified opinion with an Emphasis of Matter paragraph
B. Qualified opinion or Adverse opinion ✔
C. Qualified opinion or Disclaimer of opinion
D. Adverse opinion or Disclaimer of opinion
Explanation: According to SA 705 (Revised), the auditor shall express a qualified opinion when the auditor, having obtained sufficient appropriate audit evidence, concludes that misstatements, individually or in the aggregate, are material but not pervasive. The auditor shall express an adverse opinion when the auditor, having obtained sufficient appropriate audit evidence, concludes that misstatements, individually or in the aggregate, are both material and pervasive.
Easy NORMAL · SA 701 | Key Audit Matters | Listed Entities
Under SA 701, for which entities are auditors required to communicate Key Audit Matters (KAM) in the independent auditor's report?
A. All companies registered under the Companies Act, 2013
B. Listed entities and entities required by law/regulations ✔
C. Entities with a turnover exceeding INR 250 crores
D. Banking companies and insurance companies only
Explanation: SA 701 applies to audits of complete sets of general purpose financial statements of listed entities and whenever the auditor otherwise decides to communicate key audit matters in the auditor's report.
Medium NORMAL · SA 705 | Disclaimer of Opinion | Scope Limitation
An auditor is unable to obtain sufficient appropriate audit evidence on which to base the opinion, and the possible effects on the financial statements of undetected misstatements could be both material and pervasive. What is the appropriate audit report modification?
A. Qualified opinion
B. Adverse opinion
C. Disclaimer of opinion ✔
D. Unmodified opinion with Other Matter paragraph
Explanation: Per SA 705 (Revised), when the auditor is unable to obtain sufficient appropriate audit evidence and the possible effects could be both material and pervasive, the auditor shall disclaim an opinion.
Medium NORMAL · SA 700 | Report Structure | Auditor Responsibilities
Where should the 'Auditor's Responsibilities for the Audit of the Financial Statements' section be typically located in an independent auditor's report prepared under SA 700 (Revised)?
A. Before the Management's Responsibility section
B. After the Auditor's Opinion section ✔
C. As an appendix attached to the financial statements
D. Inside the Notes to Accounts
Explanation: Under SA 700 (Revised), the standard structure of the auditor's report places the Auditor's Opinion first, followed by the Basis for Opinion, followed by Key Audit Matters (if applicable), Management's Responsibilities, and then the Auditor's Responsibilities for the Audit.
Easy NORMAL · SA 706 | Emphasis of Matter | Audit Report Structure
What is the primary purpose of including an 'Emphasis of Matter' (EOM) paragraph in an auditor's report under SA 706 (Revised)?
A. To modify the auditor's opinion because of a disagreement with management
B. To draw users' attention to a matter appropriately presented or disclosed that is of such importance that it is fundamental to users' understanding ✔
C. To report on other regulatory and legal requirements outside the financial statements
D. To highlight a matter that constitutes a scope limitation imposed by management
Explanation: SA 706 (Revised) defines an Emphasis of Matter paragraph as a paragraph included in the auditor's report that refers to a matter appropriately presented or disclosed in the financial statements that, in the auditor's judgment, is of such importance that it is fundamental to users' understanding.
Medium NORMAL · SA 706 | Other Matter Paragraph | Audit Reporting
Under what circumstances must an auditor include an 'Other Matter' (OM) paragraph in the auditor's report according to SA 706 (Revised)?
A. When the auditor wishes to emphasize a matter related to going concern uncertainty
B. When a matter other than those presented or disclosed in the financial statements is relevant to users' understanding of the audit, the auditor's responsibilities, or the auditor's report ✔
C. When management refuses to correct a material misstatement that is pervasive
D. When key audit matters are communicated for a private limited company
Explanation: SA 706 (Revised) states that an Other Matter paragraph refers to a matter other than those presented or disclosed in the financial statements that is relevant to users' understanding of the audit, the auditor's responsibilities, or the auditor's report.
Medium NORMAL · SA 705 | Basis for Opinion | Report Formatting
When expressing a modified opinion, where does the auditor place the 'Basis for Qualified/Adverse/Disclaimer of Opinion' section?
A. Directly below the Auditor's Opinion ✔
B. At the very end of the report after signature
C. Inside the Notes to Accounts
D. As a footnote to the Balance Sheet
Explanation: According to SA 705 (Revised), when the auditor modifies the audit opinion, the auditor shall use the heading 'Basis for Qualified Opinion', 'Basis for Adverse Opinion', or 'Basis for Disclaimer of Opinion', as appropriate, and position this section immediately after the Auditor's Opinion section.
Hard NORMAL · SA 710 | Comparative Information | Corresponding Figures
In the context of reporting on comparative information under SA 710, when corresponding figures are presented, the auditor's opinion shall:
A. Refer to each period for which financial statements are presented
B. Refer only to the current period because corresponding figures are an integral part of the current period financial statements ✔
C. Not mention the previous period under any circumstance
D. Express a separate opinion on the prior period balance sheet alone
Explanation: Per SA 710, when corresponding figures are presented, the auditor's opinion shall not refer to the corresponding figures except in specific circumstances (such as when the prior period report was modified or a material misstatement exists in corresponding figures). The opinion is on the current period financial statements as a whole, including the corresponding figures.
Easy NORMAL · Companies Act 2013 | Audit Report Headings | SA 700
Which of the following is NOT a required heading in the independent auditor's report for a company under the Companies Act, 2013 and relevant SAs?
A. Report on Other Legal and Regulatory Requirements
B. Management's Responsibility for the Financial Statements
C. Auditor's Assessment of Corporate Profits ✔
D. Auditor's Responsibility
Explanation: Standard audit reports contain sections like Report on the Financial Statements, Management's Responsibility, Auditor's Responsibility, Opinion, and Report on Other Legal and Regulatory Requirements. 'Auditor's Assessment of Corporate Profits' is not a standard heading.
Hard NORMAL · SA 570 | Going Concern | Scope Limitation
Under SA 570 (Revised), if management is unwilling to make or extend its assessment of the entity's ability to continue as a going concern when requested, what should the auditor do?
A. Issue an unmodified opinion with an Emphasis of Matter paragraph
B. Consider the implications for the audit report, which may include modifying the opinion ✔
C. Immediately resign from the audit engagement without notification
D. Issue a clean report since management's assessment is optional
Explanation: Per SA 570 (Revised), if management is unwilling to make or extend its assessment, the auditor shall evaluate the implications of this lack of information on the audit report, which may result in a modified opinion due to a scope limitation.
Easy NORMAL · SA 700 | True and Fair View | Unmodified Opinion
When the auditor's report contains an unmodified opinion on financial statements, what phrase is typically used under the opinion section?
A. 'In our opinion and to the best of our information... the financial statements give a true and fair view...' ✔
B. 'The financial statements are completely accurate and free from any error...'
C. 'We guarantee that the financial statements reflect exact market value...'
D. 'In our opinion, the management has prepared infallible records...'
Explanation: Under the Companies Act, 2013 and SA 700 (Revised), the standard phrasing for a true and fair view in India includes statements expressing that the financial statements give a true and fair view of the state of affairs, profit/loss, and cash flows.
Hard NORMAL · SA 705 | Pervasive | Terminology
What does the term 'pervasive' mean in the context of SA 705 (Revised) regarding misstatements?
A. Misstatements that affect only a single minor ledger account
B. Misstatements that are confined to specific elements and do not represent a fundamental portion of the financial statements
C. Misstatements that, in the auditor's judgment, are not confined to specific elements, accounts or items of the financial statements; or if confined, represent or could represent a substantial proportion of the financial statements ✔
D. Misstatements that are detected solely after the date of the auditor's report
Explanation: SA 705 (Revised) defines 'pervasive' as a term used to describe the effects on financial statements of misstatements or the possible effects on financial statements of undetected misstatements, if any, that are not confined to specific elements, etc.
Hard NORMAL · SA 710 | Comparative Information | Predecessor Auditor
If an auditor detects a material misstatement in the comparative financial statements (comparative financial reports where prior period figures are compared directly), and the prior period figures were audited by a predecessor auditor, what should the current auditor do if the predecessor auditor's report is not reissued?
A. State in an Other Matter paragraph that the predecessor auditor reported on the corresponding figures ✔
B. Modify the current year's opinion directly without reference to the predecessor
C. Ignore the prior period misstatement since it belongs to a different auditor
D. Re-audit the entire prior period from scratch and issue a combined opinion
Explanation: Under SA 710, when comparative financial statements are presented and the prior period was audited by a predecessor auditor whose report is not reissued, the current auditor may state in an Other Matter paragraph that the predecessor auditor reported on the financial statements of the prior period.
Medium NORMAL · Companies Act 2013 | Section 143(3) | Regulatory Requirements
Which of the following matters is a mandatory inclusion in the 'Report on Other Legal and Regulatory Requirements' under the Companies Act, 2013?
A. Whether proper books of account as required by law have been kept by the company ✔
B. Detailed analysis of the company's marketing strategy and competitor benchmarking
C. A list of all employees drawing a salary above INR 1 crore per annum
D. Verification of the personal bank accounts of the company's directors
Explanation: Under Section 143(3) of the Companies Act, 2013, the auditor's report must state whether proper books of account as required by law have been kept by the company, among other statutory attestations.
Medium NORMAL · CARO 2020 | Applicability | Exemptions
In discharging reporting duties under CARO 2020 (Companies (Auditor's Report) Order, 2020), which type of companies are generally exempt from its application?
A. All Private Limited Companies regardless of size
B. Banking companies, Insurance companies, Section 8 companies, and specified small private companies meeting certain criteria ✔
C. All listed companies with a foreign direct investment
D. Government companies incorporated under Section 2(45)
Explanation: CARO 2020 exempts banking companies, insurance companies, companies registered for charitable purposes (Section 8), and certain small private companies (meeting paid-up capital, borrowing, and turnover thresholds).
Medium NORMAL · CARO 2020 | Statutory Dues | Clause (vii)
When reporting under CARO 2020, what must the auditor report regarding statutory dues such as GST, Provident Fund, and Income Tax?
A. Whether the company has paid all dues within 7 days of month-end
B. Whether the company is regular in depositing undisputed statutory dues, and if not regular, the extent of arrears outstanding for more than six months from the date they became payable ✔
C. Only whether income tax has been deducted at source
D. Whether the company owes money to foreign tax authorities
Explanation: Paragraph 3(vii)(a) of CARO 2020 requires reporting on whether the company is regular in depositing undisputed statutory dues and, where not regular, the extent of arrears outstanding for a period of more than six months.
Medium NORMAL · SA 701 | Key Audit Matters | Professional Judgment
Under SA 701, how does the auditor determine which matters are 'Key Audit Matters'?
A. By selecting matters that resulted in a modified opinion only
B. By selecting matters of most significance in the audit of the financial statements of the current period, based on areas of higher assessed risk of material misstatement or significant auditor attention ✔
C. By listing all items that appeared in the audit program
D. By asking the Board of Directors to nominate five items for disclosure
Explanation: SA 701 defines Key Audit Matters as those matters that, in the auditor's professional judgment, were of most significance in the audit of the financial statements of the current period, drawn from areas of significant auditor attention.
Hard NORMAL · SA 701 | Disclaimer of Opinion | KAM Prohibition
Can an auditor communicate Key Audit Matters in the auditor's report if the audit opinion is a Disclaimer of Opinion?
A. Yes, whenever required by law or regulation
B. No, SA 701 prohibits communicating KAM when the auditor disclaims an opinion on the financial statements, unless required by law or regulation ✔
C. Yes, provided management gives written consent
D. No, KAM is only permitted when an adverse opinion is issued
Explanation: According to SA 701, when the auditor disclaims an opinion on the financial statements, the auditor shall not communicate key audit matters in the auditor's report, unless required by law or regulation, because doing so might contradict the disclaimer.
Medium NORMAL · SA 570 | Going Concern | Material Uncertainty
If a material uncertainty related to going concern is adequately disclosed in the financial statements, how should the auditor report on it under SA 570 (Revised)?
A. Issue an adverse opinion due to fundamental uncertainty
B. Issue an unmodified opinion and include a separate section under the heading 'Material Uncertainty Related to Going Concern' ✔
C. Omit any reference to it to avoid alarming shareholders
D. Issue a disclaimer of opinion because of the existence of uncertainty
Explanation: Under SA 570 (Revised), if adequate disclosure of a material uncertainty is made in the financial statements, the auditor shall express an unmodified opinion and include a separate section in the auditor's report titled 'Material Uncertainty Related to Going Concern'.
Hard NORMAL · SA 570 | Inadequate Disclosure | Qualified or Adverse Opinion
What is the consequence under SA 570 (Revised) if management's assessment of going concern discloses a material uncertainty, but that uncertainty is NOT adequately disclosed in the financial statements?
A. The auditor shall express a qualified opinion or an adverse opinion ✔
B. The auditor shall express an unmodified opinion with an Emphasis of Matter paragraph
C. The auditor shall issue a clean report with an Other Matter paragraph
D. The auditor shall take no action if the business is profitable
Explanation: Per SA 570 (Revised), if adequate disclosure is not made in the financial statements, the auditor shall express a qualified opinion or an adverse opinion, as appropriate, in accordance with SA 705.
Easy NORMAL · Companies Act 2013 | Section 143(3) | Accounting Standards
Under Section 143(3) of the Companies Act, 2013, what must the auditor report regarding the financial statements' compliance with Accounting Standards?
A. Whether the financial statements comply with the Accounting Standards referred to in Section 133 ✔
B. Whether the financial statements comply with International Financial Reporting Standards exclusively
C. Whether the financial statements comply with tax audit guidelines issued by CBDT
D. Whether the financial statements comply with the internal policies of the parent company
Explanation: Section 143(3)(e) of the Companies Act, 2013 requires the auditor to state whether, in their opinion, the financial statements comply with the Accounting Standards referred to in Section 133.
Medium NORMAL · SA 700 | Date of Audit Report | Audit Evidence
What should the date of the independent auditor's report be, according to SA 700 (Revised)?
A. The date on which the annual general meeting (AGM) is held
B. The date on which the auditor has obtained sufficient appropriate audit evidence on which to base the opinion on the financial statements ✔
C. The date on which management signs the directors' report
D. The financial year-end date
Explanation: SA 700 (Revised) specifies that the auditor's report shall be dated no earlier than the date on which the auditor has obtained sufficient appropriate audit evidence on which to base the opinion on the financial statements, including evidence that the financial statements have been prepared.
Medium NORMAL · CARO 2020 | Benami Property | Clause (xi)
Under CARO 2020, does the auditor need to report on whether any proceedings have been initiated or are pending against the company for holding any benami property under the Benami Transactions (Prohibition) Act, 1988?
A. No, this is outside the scope of CARO 2020
B. Yes, reporting on benami property proceedings is specifically required under CARO 2020 clause (xi) ✔
C. Only if the company is a public sector undertaking
D. Only if requested by the Income Tax Department
Explanation: Clause (xi) of paragraph 3 of CARO 2020 requires reporting on whether any proceedings have been initiated or are pending against the company for holding any benami property under the Benami Transactions (Prohibition) Act, 1988 and rules made thereunder.
Easy NORMAL · SA 705 | Adverse Opinion | True and Fair View
Which of the following describes an 'Adverse Opinion' issued under SA 705 (Revised)?
A. The auditor expresses no opinion because of a severe scope limitation
B. The auditor states that the financial statements give a true and fair view except for specific misstatements
C. The auditor states that the financial statements do not give a true and fair view in accordance with the financial reporting framework due to pervasive misstatements ✔
D. The auditor highlights a significant uncertainty without modifying the core opinion
Explanation: An adverse opinion is expressed when the auditor, having obtained sufficient appropriate audit evidence, concludes that misstatements, individually or in the aggregate, are both material and pervasive to the financial statements.
Hard NORMAL · SA 706 | Emphasis of Matter | Paragraph Placement
In an audit report, if an Emphasis of Matter paragraph is included, can it be placed before the Opinion section?
A. Yes, if management prefers it to be prominent
B. No, SA 706 (Revised) requires the EOM paragraph to be included subsequent to the Opinion and Basis for Opinion sections ✔
C. Yes, provided it is highlighted in bold font
D. It can be placed anywhere in the Notes to Accounts
Explanation: SA 706 (Revised) mandates that if the auditor includes an Emphasis of Matter paragraph in the auditor's report, the auditor shall locate it separately with an appropriate heading, after the Opinion and Basis for Opinion sections.
Medium NORMAL · Companies Act 2013 | Section 143(1) | Loans and Advances
Under Section 143(1) of the Companies Act, 2013, what inquiry is the auditor specifically required to make regarding loans and advances?
A. Whether loans and advances made by the company are properly secured and whether terms are prejudicial to the interest of the company or its members ✔
B. Whether loans and advances exceed 50% of the share capital
C. Whether all loans carry an interest rate higher than the bank rate
D. Whether loans were disbursed in cash exceeding INR 10,000
Explanation: Section 143(1)(a) requires the auditor to inquire whether loans and advances made by the company on the basis of security have been properly secured and whether the terms on which they have been made are prejudicial to the interests of the company or its members.
Easy NORMAL · Companies Act 2013 | Board Approval | Audit Report Signature
When can an auditor sign the independent auditor's report of a company?
A. Before the financial statements are approved by the Board of Directors
B. After the financial statements have been approved by the Board of Directors and signed by authorized signatories ✔
C. At any time during the financial year regardless of financial statement preparation
D. Only after the Annual General Meeting concludes
Explanation: The auditor can sign the audit report only after the financial statements have been approved by the Board of Directors under Section 134(5) of the Companies Act, 2013 and signed in accordance with statutory requirements.
Hard NORMAL · CARO 2020 | Tax Assessments | Clause (xix)
What is the requirement under CARO 2020 regarding unrecorded income surrendered or disclosed as income in tax assessments?
A. No reporting required under CARO 2020
B. Whether any transactions not recorded in the books of account have been surrendered or disclosed as income during the year in the tax assessments under the Income Tax Act, and whether such income has been properly recorded in the books ✔
C. Only report if tax penalty exceeds INR 1 crore
D. Report whether income tax returns were filed before the due date
Explanation: Clause (xix) of paragraph 3 of CARO 2020 requires the auditor to report on whether any unrecorded transactions have been surrendered or disclosed as income in tax assessments and whether they were recorded in the books.
Easy NORMAL · SA 700 | Auditor Signature | Firm Registration Number
Under SA 700 (Revised), what constitutes the signature of the auditor in the independent auditor's report?
A. Only the name of the audit firm in block letters
B. The personal name of the engagement partner along with the firm's registration number and membership number, signed in the personal name of the individual auditor ✔
C. A digital QR code generated by the Ministry of Corporate Affairs
D. The signature of the Managing Director of the auditee company
Explanation: The auditor's report must be signed in the personal name of the auditor and/or engagement partner, along with their membership number and the firm's registration number assigned by ICAI.
CASE SCENARIO: Zenith Pharma Ltd., a listed pharmaceutical company, is undergoing its annual audit for the year ended March 31, 2026. During the audit, the statutory auditors discovered that a massive inventory valuation dispute with tax authorities has been ongoing. The amount involved is material but restricted to specific inventory batches in one manufacturing plant. Furthermore, the management refused to allow the auditor to inspect third-party confirmation replies for trade receivables amounting to 4% of total assets, citing confidentiality agreements with overseas clients.
Medium SCENARIO · SA 705 | Inventory Valuation | Qualified Opinion
Based on the inventory valuation dispute (which is material but restricted to specific batches), how should the auditor evaluate its impact on the audit opinion under SA 705?
A. Issue an Adverse opinion because inventory is a core asset
B. Issue a Qualified opinion because the misstatement is material but not pervasive ✔
C. Issue a Disclaimer of opinion due to lack of cooperation
D. Issue an Unmodified opinion with an Emphasis of Matter paragraph
Explanation: Under SA 705, when misstatements are material but not pervasive (confined to specific batches/items), the appropriate modification is a qualified opinion.
Medium SCENARIO · SA 705 | Scope Limitation | Management Imposed
Regarding the management's refusal to permit inspection of third-party receivable confirmations (representing 4% of total assets), how should the auditor classify this situation?
A. A management-imposed scope limitation ✔
B. A routine accounting policy disagreement
C. A subsequent event disclosure requirement
D. A key audit matter only
Explanation: Denying access to necessary audit evidence, such as receivable confirmations, constitutes a scope limitation imposed by management under SA 705.
Medium SCENARIO · SA 701 | Listed Entity | Key Audit Matters
Since Zenith Pharma Ltd. is a listed entity, what standard governs the communication of significant audit matters like the inventory dispute in the audit report?
A. SA 700 (Revised)
B. SA 701 ✔
C. SA 706 (Revised)
D. SA 570 (Revised)
Explanation: SA 701 governs the communication of Key Audit Matters for listed entities, highlighting matters of most significance.
Hard SCENARIO · SA 705 | Basis for Opinion | Report Structure
Where in the independent auditor's report should the specific reasons for modifying the opinion due to the inventory and receivable issues be articulated?
A. In the Basis for Qualified Opinion section immediately following the Auditor's Opinion ✔
B. In the Notes to Accounts prepared by management
C. In the Director's Report under Corporate Governance
D. In the Other Information section
Explanation: SA 705 requires that when the opinion is modified, the 'Basis for Qualified Opinion' section must be placed immediately after the Auditor's Opinion section to explain the reasons.
CASE SCENARIO: Sunrise Textiles Ltd., an unlisted public company, has incurred net operating losses for three consecutive years. Its current liabilities exceed its current assets by INR 45 crores. The company's key lender has issued a formal notice recalling a term loan due to covenant breaches. However, management has prepared cash flow projections showing that an impending sale of surplus land in the next quarter will generate adequate liquidity to settle the term loan and fund operations. Management has made adequate disclosures regarding these conditions and plans in the notes to the financial statements.
Medium SCENARIO · SA 570 | Going Concern | Auditor Responsibilities
Which auditing standard primarily governs the auditor's responsibilities relating to going concern in this audit engagement?
A. SA 500
B. SA 570 (Revised) ✔
C. SA 701
D. SA 710
Explanation: SA 570 (Revised) deals with the auditor's responsibilities in the audit of financial statements relating to going concern.
Hard SCENARIO · SA 570 | Material Uncertainty | Unmodified Opinion
Given that a material uncertainty exists regarding going concern but adequate disclosure has been made in the financial statements, how should the auditor report on this?
A. Issue a Disclaimer of opinion
B. Issue an Unmodified opinion with a separate section titled 'Material Uncertainty Related to Going Concern' ✔
C. Issue an Adverse opinion because of covenant breaches
D. Issue a clean report without mentioning the uncertainty
Explanation: Under SA 570 (Revised), if adequate disclosure of a material uncertainty is made, the auditor expresses an unmodified opinion and includes a distinct section titled 'Material Uncertainty Related to Going Concern'.
Hard SCENARIO · SA 570 | Inadequate Disclosure | Adverse Opinion
If management refused to disclose the material uncertainty regarding the term loan recall and land sale in the notes to accounts, what would be the appropriate audit report modification?
A. Qualified or Adverse opinion ✔
B. Emphasis of Matter paragraph only
C. Unmodified opinion with Other Matter paragraph
D. No modification required
Explanation: Per SA 570 (Revised), if adequate disclosure is not made in the financial statements, the auditor shall express a qualified opinion or an adverse opinion.
Medium SCENARIO · SA 701 | Key Audit Matters | Unlisted Entities
Since Sunrise Textiles Ltd. is an unlisted company, is it mandatory for the auditor to communicate Key Audit Matters under SA 701?
A. Yes, for all companies under the Companies Act, 2013
B. No, unless required by law/regulation or voluntarily decided by the auditor ✔
C. Yes, whenever losses exceed INR 10 crores
D. No, SA 701 applies exclusively to banking companies
Explanation: SA 701 applies to audits of listed entities. For unlisted entities like Sunrise Textiles Ltd., KAM communication is not mandatory unless required by law/regulation or elected by the auditor.
CASE SCENARIO: M/s Apex & Associates, Chartered Accountants, are auditing Omega Engineering Ltd. for the financial year 2025-26. The financial statements include corresponding figures for the prior year (2024-25). The prior year's financial statements were audited by a predecessor auditor, whose report expressed a qualified opinion due to unverified work-in-progress inventory. In the current year, the matter giving rise to the prior qualification has been completely resolved. However, during the current audit, a new and material dispute regarding patent infringement arises, which remains unresolved at the signing date.
Medium SCENARIO · SA 710 | Comparative Information | Corresponding Figures
Which auditing standard governs the auditor's responsibilities regarding comparative information and corresponding figures in this scenario?
A. SA 700
B. SA 710 ✔
C. SA 705
D. SA 706
Explanation: SA 710 deals with the auditor's responsibilities relating to comparative information, including corresponding figures and comparative financial statements.
Hard SCENARIO · SA 710 | Resolved Qualification | Corresponding Figures
How should the auditor report on the prior year's qualification given that the matter has been fully resolved in the current period?
A. The current auditor's report generally should not refer to the previous qualification since it is resolved ✔
B. The current auditor must re-issue the predecessor's qualified report
C. The current auditor must express an adverse opinion on the current year's figures
D. The current auditor must add an Emphasis of Matter regarding the old WIP
Explanation: Under SA 710, when the prior period matter that caused a qualification is resolved, the current period opinion does not need to refer to the previous qualification.
Medium SCENARIO · SA 705 | Current Period Misstatement | Modified Opinion
How should the current auditor deal with the new and material patent infringement dispute that is unresolved at the signing date?
A. Ignore it because it relates to legal matters
B. Evaluate its materiality and pervasiveness and modify the current year's audit opinion accordingly (qualified or adverse) ✔
C. Issue an unmodified opinion with an Other Matter paragraph
D. Issue a disclaimer of opinion automatically without assessment
Explanation: A current period material misstatement or scope limitation regarding a patent dispute requires the auditor to modify the opinion on the current financial statements in accordance with SA 705.
Hard SCENARIO · SA 710 | Predecessor Auditor | Other Matter Paragraph
If the predecessor auditor's report on the prior period's financial statements was NOT reissued, what paragraph may the current auditor include in the report under SA 710?
A. An Other Matter paragraph stating that the prior period financial statements were audited by a predecessor auditor ✔
B. An Emphasis of Matter paragraph modifying the opinion on prior balances
C. A Key Audit Matter paragraph detailing predecessor fees
D. A CARO reporting clause on predecessor competence
Explanation: SA 710 permits the current auditor to include an Other Matter paragraph indicating that the prior period financial statements were audited by a predecessor auditor, the opinion expressed, and the date thereof.
CASE SCENARIO: Delta Commercial Ltd. is a manufacturing company registered under the Companies Act, 2013. During the statutory audit for 2025-26, the auditor reviews compliance with CARO 2020 and the Companies Act, 2013. The auditor finds that the company has defaulted in repayment of dues to a financial institution for 90 days. Furthermore, the company has taken unsecured loans from three directors, the terms of which the auditor suspects may be prejudicial to the company's interest. Lastly, management has used short-term working capital borrowings amounting to INR 12 crores to fund long-term capital machinery acquisitions.
Medium SCENARIO · CARO 2020 | Default in Repayment | Clause (ix)
Under CARO 2020, how should the auditor report on the default in repayment of dues to the financial institution?
A. Report under clause (ix) regarding default in repayment of loans or other borrowings to any financial institution, bank, government, or debenture holders ✔
B. Report under clause (i) on Fixed Assets
C. Report under Section 143(3) only without CARO reference
D. Ignore if settled before the AGM
Explanation: Paragraph 3(ix) of CARO 2020 requires reporting on whether the company has defaulted in repayment of loans or other borrowings or in the payment of interest thereon to any lender.
Medium SCENARIO · Companies Act 2013 | Section 143(1) | Loans and Advances
Regarding the unsecured loans taken from directors, which statutory inquiry under Section 143(1) of the Companies Act, 2013 is directly triggered?
A. Whether loans and advances made by the company are prejudicial, and whether loans taken are properly managed
B. Whether terms on which loans and advances have been made are prejudicial to the interests of the company or its members ✔
C. Whether directors have paid tax on such loans
D. Whether loans exceed the paid-up capital of the company
Explanation: Section 143(1)(a) requires the auditor to inquire whether terms on which loans and advances made by the company are prejudicial to the interests of the company or its members.
Hard SCENARIO · CARO 2020 | Short-term vs Long-term Funds | Clause (ix)
Which specific CARO 2020 clause requires reporting when short-term funds are utilized for long-term purposes?
A. Clause (ix)(e) regarding funds raised on short term basis being used for long term purposes ✔
B. Clause (iii) regarding loans granted to parties covered in register
C. Clause (vii) regarding statutory dues
D. Clause (xi) regarding managerial remuneration
Explanation: CARO 2020 paragraph 3(ix)(e) requires reporting on whether the company has taken any funds from any entity or person on account of or to meet the obligations of its subsidiaries, associates, or joint ventures, and clause (ix)(f) covers short-term funds used for long-term purposes.
Medium SCENARIO · CARO 2020 | Report Annexure | Companies Act 2013
Where must the CARO 2020 report be presented in relation to the main independent auditor's report under the Companies Act, 2013?
A. As an annexure/addendum attached to the independent auditor's report ✔
B. Inside the Director's Report as a separate chapter
C. Submitted directly to SEBI without attaching to the audit report
D. As part of the Notes to Accounts
Explanation: The CARO report is issued as an annexure to the independent auditor's report under the Companies Act, 2013, addressing the specific matters prescribed by the Central Government.
CASE SCENARIO: Aura Tech Solutions Ltd. is a software development company. During the audit for the year ended March 31, 2026, the engagement partner decided to include an Emphasis of Matter (EOM) paragraph in the auditor's report to highlight a catastrophic fire incident that occurred at the company's primary server facility after the balance sheet date but before the signing of the audit report. Management has made full and appropriate disclosure of this event in Note 24 of the financial statements. Additionally, the auditor observed that the financial statements include a supplementary unaudited schedule required by a specific industry regulator.
Medium SCENARIO · SA 706 | Emphasis of Matter | Server Fire Incident
Which auditing standard governs the inclusion of the Emphasis of Matter paragraph regarding the fire incident?
A. SA 700
B. SA 706 (Revised) ✔
C. SA 560
D. SA 570
Explanation: SA 706 (Revised) deals with Emphasis of Matter paragraphs and Other Matter paragraphs in the auditor's report.
Medium SCENARIO · SA 706 | Unmodified Opinion | EOM Nature
Is the inclusion of the EOM paragraph for the fire incident a substitute for modifying the auditor's opinion?
A. Yes, EOM replaces a qualified opinion when management is cooperative
B. No, an Emphasis of Matter paragraph is not a modification of the auditor's opinion ✔
C. Yes, because the event occurred after the balance sheet date
D. No, but it automatically converts an unmodified opinion into a disclaimer
Explanation: SA 706 explicitly clarifies that an Emphasis of Matter paragraph is not a modification of the auditor's opinion; the opinion remains unmodified.
Hard SCENARIO · SA 706 | Other Matter Paragraph | Supplementary Information
How should the auditor report on the supplementary unaudited schedule required by the industry regulator?
A. Using an Other Matter paragraph under SA 706 to draw attention to a matter other than those presented in financial statements ✔
B. By modifying the core opinion on the main financial statements
C. By issuing a separate audit report with a qualified opinion
D. By ignoring the supplementary schedule entirely
Explanation: An Other Matter paragraph is used when the auditor needs to communicate a matter other than those presented or disclosed in the financial statements that is relevant to users' understanding, such as reporting on supplementary information.
Hard SCENARIO · SA 706 | Paragraph Placement | Audit Report Formatting
Where should the Emphasis of Matter paragraph regarding Note 24 be positioned within the independent auditor's report?
A. Before the Auditor's Opinion section
B. After the Opinion and Basis for Opinion sections, and before Key Audit Matters (if applicable) ✔
C. As a footnote on the Balance Sheet
D. In the Report on Other Legal and Regulatory Requirements
Explanation: SA 706 (Revised) requires the EOM paragraph to be located separately in the auditor's report, after the Opinion and Basis for Opinion sections.

Paper 5: Auditing and Ethics · Module 2 · Chapter 9:

Audit — 55 rows
Easy NORMAL · Cooperative Societies | Statutory Framework | Audit Mandate
Which of the following is the primary document governing the audit of a registered cooperative society in India?
A. The Companies Act, 2013
B. The Multi-State Cooperative Societies Act, 2002 or respective State Cooperative Societies Act ✔
C. The Banking Regulation Act, 1949
D. The Indian Trusts Act, 1882
Explanation: Cooperative societies are formed and registered under specific legislative frameworks such as the State Cooperative Societies Act or the Multi-State Cooperative Societies Act, 2002, which govern their administration and audit requirements.
Medium NORMAL · Cooperative Audit | Bye-laws Compliance | Statutory Reporting
In the audit of a cooperative society, the auditor is specifically required to report on which of the following due to statutory mandates?
A. Personal investments of the managing committee members
B. Violation of the provisions of the Cooperative Societies Act, rules, and bye-laws ✔
C. Market share and competitor pricing strategies
D. Private business transactions of ordinary members
Explanation: Special audit reports for cooperative societies heavily emphasize checking compliance with the governing Act, registered rules, and the society's specific bye-laws, particularly regarding loans, investments, and utilization of funds.
Hard NORMAL · Cooperative Audit | Loans to Non-members | Statutory Violation
While auditing a cooperative society, an auditor notices that loans have been advanced to non-members. Under general cooperative principles, what is the appropriate audit position?
A. It is acceptable if authorized by a majority vote in the annual general meeting.
B. It is a violation unless specifically permitted by the Registrar or the Act/Bye-laws. ✔
C. It is standard banking practice and requires no special comment.
D. It is permitted if secured by adequate immovable property.
Explanation: Cooperative societies are mutual associations intended primarily to serve their members. Advancing loans to non-members is generally prohibited unless specific exemptions exist under the Act, rules, or bye-laws, or with the Registrar's sanction.
Medium NORMAL · Cooperative Audit | Auditor Appointment | Registrar
Who has the statutory authority to appoint the auditor of a cooperative society in most jurisdictions in India?
A. The Board of Directors of the society
B. The Registrar of Cooperative Societies ✔
C. The Comptroller and Auditor General of India (C&AG)
D. The Reserve Bank of India
Explanation: In most cooperative societies, the statute vests the power of appointing the auditor directly in the Registrar of Cooperative Societies, or the audit is conducted directly by the Registrar's staff.
Easy NORMAL · NGO Audit | Charitable Trust | Object Compliance
What is the primary objective of an audit of a charitable institution or NGO?
A. To maximize net profit distributable to founders
B. To ensure that funds are applied towards the objects of the trust and comply with legal provisions ✔
C. To verify compliance with the SEBI Listing Regulations
D. To assess the personal tax liability of the trustees
Explanation: Charitable trusts and NGOs operate for public or mutual benefit. The auditor must verify that income and donations are applied strictly in accordance with the objects specified in the trust deed or memorandum of association.
Medium NORMAL · NGO Audit | Anonymous Donations | Internal Controls
When auditing anonymous donations received by a charitable trust, which audit procedure is most critical?
A. Confirming the identity of each donor through PAN cards
B. Checking internal controls over collection boxes, receipt issuance, and recording in books ✔
C. Inspecting the minutes of the board meeting for personal approvals
D. Verifying that tax has been deducted at source on such donations
Explanation: Anonymous donations present a high risk of misappropriate handling. Auditors must evaluate internal controls governing physical collection, hundi boxes, and timely accounting to ensure completeness.
Hard NORMAL · NGO Audit | Income Tax Act | Form 10
Under Indian tax laws applicable to trusts and NGOs, accumulation of income beyond the permissible limit requires filing which form or compliance?
A. Form 10 to accumulate income for specific purposes ✔
B. Form 3CD for tax audit
C. Form 15G for non-deduction of tax
D. Form 26AS reconciliation
Explanation: Under Section 11(2) of the Income-tax Act, 1961, if a trust wishes to accumulate or set apart income exceeding 15% for application to charitable or religious purposes, it must file Form 10 within the prescribed time.
Easy NORMAL · Educational Institution | Fee Revenue | Audit Procedures
In the audit of an educational institution (like a school or college), what is the key verification step regarding tuition fee revenue?
A. Checking fee collection against student rolls, admission registers, and concession records ✔
B. Inspecting the market value of land owned by the institution
C. Verifying the personal salary advances given to teaching staff
D. Tracing all expenditure vouchers to the university syndicate resolutions
Explanation: Fee income is the lifeblood of educational institutions. Auditors must reconcile fee collections with student attendance/admission rolls and verify that any fee concessions are properly authorized by competent authorities.
Hard NORMAL · Educational Institution | Caution Money | Liabilities
While auditing a university, the auditor notices that caution money collected from students has been utilized to finance day-to-day administrative expenses. How should the auditor treat this?
A. Accept it as normal working capital management
B. Qualify the report as caution money is a liability that should be kept separately or invested safely ✔
C. Suggest transferring it to the general reserve fund immediately
D. Ignore it if the amount is less than 5% of total revenue
Explanation: Caution money is a refundable deposit received from students and represents a liability. Utilizing it for operational expenses without maintaining liquid funds or specific investments is improper and warrants qualification.
Medium NORMAL · Hospital Audit | Governing Statutes | Entity Types
What is the prime governing statute for the audit of a localized hospital run by a public trust?
A. The Companies Act, 2013 exclusively
B. The Clinical Establishments Act and the Trust Act / Societies Registration Act under which it is formed ✔
C. The Insurance Regulatory and Development Authority Act
D. The Pharmacy Act, 1948
Explanation: Hospitals operate under various legal structures—trusts, societies, corporate bodies, or government departments. Their audit is governed by the specific statute of incorporation along with applicable medical regulations.
Medium NORMAL · Hospital Audit | Inventory Valuation | Expiry Risk
When auditing pharmaceutical inventories and surgical stores in a hospital, which specific audit risk must the auditor address?
A. Foreign exchange fluctuations on imported medicines
B. Obsolescence, expiry dates, and proper valuation of drugs and consumables ✔
C. Capitalization of consumable items as fixed assets
D. Depreciation of medicines using the straight-line method
Explanation: Hospital inventories include drugs, consumables, and surgical items that are prone to expiration and obsolescence. Auditors must verify physical stock verification and proper valuation at the lower of cost and net realizable value.
Medium NORMAL · Hotel Audit | Night Audit | Revenue Controls
In a hotel audit, which of the following represents a crucial internal control area regarding room occupancy and billing?
A. Reconciliation of front office daily night audit reports with housekeeping reports and kitchen orders ✔
B. Verification of export duty drawback claims
C. Checking compliance with factory labor welfare legislation
D. Ensuring actuarial valuation of gratuity for permanent staff
Explanation: Hotels rely heavily on front office systems. The night audit reconciles room occupancy records with actual billings, restaurant KOTs (Kitchen Order Tickets), and cash collections to prevent revenue leakage.
Easy NORMAL · Hotel Audit | Guest Ledger | Receivables
Which of the following documents is most essential for an auditor to review when verifying guest ledger balances in a hotel audit?
A. The guest register, bill folios, and daily summary of cash/credit card collections ✔
B. The charter of incorporation
C. The annual general meeting minutes book
D. The title deeds of the hotel building
Explanation: Guest ledger balances represent amounts due from currently staying or recently departed guests. Reviewing bill folios and daily collection summaries ensures that receivables are accurately stated and collected.
Medium NORMAL · SHG Audit | Micro-finance | Internal Records
What is a distinguishing feature of a Self-Help Group (SHG) audit that sets it apart from a corporate audit?
A. Focus on informal group dynamics, micro-savings, internal lending records, and resolution books ✔
B. Mandatory compliance with Ind AS and quarterly financial reporting to stock exchanges
C. Extensive testing of derivatives and hedging instruments
D. Verification of consolidated financial statements of global subsidiaries
Explanation: SHGs are informal or semi-formal micro-finance groups. Their audits focus heavily on meeting minutes, internal savings registers, inter-loaning records, and repayment tracking among members rather than complex accounting standards.
Easy NORMAL · Cinema Audit | Box Office | Revenue Verification
When auditing a cinema hall or multiplex, what is the primary source document for verifying box office collections?
A. Daily movie-wise/show-wise statement of tickets sold, counter counterfoils, and computerized ticketing system logs ✔
B. Electricity consumption bills of the theater
C. Maintenance contracts for projection equipment
D. Catering vendor agreement files
Explanation: Box office revenue in a cinema is verified using computerized ticketing system reports, physical counterfoil checks, and daily show statements reconciled with seat occupancy data.
Hard NORMAL · Club Audit | Life Membership | Capitalization
In a club audit, what is the treatment of life membership fees received from members?
A. Credited entirely to the income and expenditure account in the year of receipt
B. Capitalized and treated as a liability/capital fund, amortized over a period or retained as corpus ✔
C. Distributed as dividends to founding members
D. Treated as an advance tax liability
Explanation: Life membership fees represent amounts received for lifetime services and are generally capitalized in the balance sheet under capital fund or reserves, recognizing them as income over the expected period of membership or retaining them as corpus as per bye-laws.
Medium NORMAL · Hire Purchase Audit | Ownership | Finance Companies
Which of the following is a critical check when auditing a hire-purchase finance company?
A. Ensuring that the ownership of the asset remains with the financier until the final installment is paid ✔
B. Confirming that hire charges are recognized as income entirely on the date of agreement
C. Checking that leased assets are depreciated in the books of the hirer only
D. Verifying that no interest element is included in installment amounts
Explanation: In hire-purchase transactions, legal ownership remains with the financier until the option to purchase is exercised by payment of the final installment, which dictates asset and revenue recognition principles.
Easy NORMAL · Local Bodies Audit | Budgetary Control | Sanctions
What special consideration must an auditor keep in mind when auditing a local body (such as a Gram Panchayat, Municipality, or Municipal Corporation)?
A. Compliance with municipal budgetary sanctions, fund allocations, and statutory sanctioning powers ✔
B. Maximization of shareholder dividend yields
C. Transfer pricing documentation requirements
D. Inventory turnover ratios for finished goods
Explanation: Local body audits focus extensively on regularity and propriety, ensuring that expenditure does not exceed budgetary allocations and that statutory approvals and sanctioning powers are strictly adhered to.
Hard NORMAL · Government Audit | Audit Against Sanction | C&AG
When conducting an audit of a government department, the auditor (C&AG or person acting on its behalf) must verify 'Sanction to Expenditure'. What does this entail?
A. Checking whether every item of expenditure is covered by a sanction, general or special, given by competent authority ✔
B. Verifying that the department made a net profit on its operational activities
C. Ensuring that all employees have filed their personal income tax returns
D. Confirming that goods were procured from the lowest bidder regardless of quality
Explanation: Audit against sanction is a key pillar of government audit, ensuring that no expenditure is incurred without proper authority and competence as laid down in financial rules and delegation of financial powers.
Medium NORMAL · Propriety Audit | Public Sector | Wasteful Expenditure
What is the primary purpose of 'Propriety Audit' in government and public sector undertakings?
A. To check whether the expenditure is incurred with financial wisdom, public interest, and avoidance of extravagance ✔
B. To verify arithmetical accuracy of accounting entries
C. To ensure compliance with corporate income tax filing deadlines
D. To calculate the exact market capitalization of the entity
Explanation: Propriety audit goes beyond mere legality. It requires the auditor to examine whether public funds have been spent with due regard to public interest, economy, and freedom from wasteful expenditure.
Medium NORMAL · Bank Audit | NPA Classification | RBI Norms
In the audit of a branch of a nationalized bank, what is the primary focus regarding Non-Performing Assets (NPAs)?
A. Classification of advances based on RBI prudential norms regarding overdue periods and security realization ✔
B. Checking whether the branch has achieved its annual deposit mobilization targets
C. Verifying the physical count of stationery items
D. Inspecting the personal loan files of bank directors
Explanation: Bank branch audits require rigorous verification of loan accounts to classify them into Standard, Sub-standard, Doubtful, or Loss categories strictly in accordance with RBI income recognition and asset classification (IRAC) norms.
Easy NORMAL · C&AG Audit | Constitutional Mandate | Government Entities
Which of the following entities is subject to audit by the Comptroller and Auditor General of India (C&AG) under the Constitution of India?
A. Only Central Government ministries and departments
B. Central Government, State Governments, and Government Companies as specified by law ✔
C. All private limited companies registered in India
D. Only cooperative societies registered under Multi-State Acts
Explanation: Under Article 149-151 of the Constitution and the CAG (DPC) Act, 1971, the C&AG audits the accounts of the Union, States, Union Territories, and government companies/corporations.
Medium NORMAL · Transport Company | Fuel Consumption | Operational Audit
When auditing a transport company (fleet operator), which operational expense requires special audit attention and testing for fuel leakage or misuse?
A. High-Speed Diesel (HSD) consumption compared with mileage logs and vehicle route sheets ✔
B. Depreciation of office computers
C. Audit fees paid to the statutory auditor
D. Board meeting refreshment expenses
Explanation: For transport operators, fuel is a major cost component. Auditors must correlate fuel purchases and consumption with distance traveled, vehicle efficiency, and logbooks to detect pilferage or misuse.
Hard NORMAL · Electricity Company | Distribution Loss | Utility Audit
In the context of an electricity distribution company (Discom) audit, what is 'Distribution Loss' and why is it audited?
A. The difference between energy injected into the distribution system and energy billed to consumers, audited to detect technical losses and commercial theft ✔
B. The loss incurred on the sale of copper scrap by the utility
C. Financial losses arising from foreign currency loans taken for power plants
D. Depreciation of power transformers over their useful life
Explanation: Distribution loss in power utilities represents electricity lost due to technical factors and theft/meter tampering. Auditors review loss figures as they directly impact regulatory tariff determinations and operational efficiency.
Easy NORMAL · Grants-in-Aid | Government Audit | Utilization
What is the key audit objective when examining 'Grants-in-Aid' received by an institution from the government?
A. Verifying that the grants are utilized strictly for the specific purpose and conditions stipulated by the sanctioning authority ✔
B. Treating the grant as general business revenue without restrictions
C. Checking whether income tax has been paid on the grant amount
D. Ensuring the grant is distributed as bonus to employees
Explanation: Government grants are typically tied to specific projects or conditions. Auditors must verify utilization certificates, separate accounting, and compliance with all terms of the grant order.
Hard NORMAL · Mutual Fund Audit | NAV Calculation | SEBI Regulations
While auditing a mutual fund, what responsibility does the auditor have regarding the Net Asset Value (NAV) computation?
A. Verifying that NAV is computed in accordance with SEBI Regulations and valuation policies, and checking methodology for asset valuation ✔
B. Guaranteeing investors a minimum rate of return on their investments
C. Managing the day-to-day portfolio buy/sell decisions
D. Filing quarterly income tax returns on behalf of investors
Explanation: Mutual fund auditors evaluate the systems and controls surrounding NAV calculation, ensuring securities are valued as per SEBI guidelines and units are correctly priced.
Medium NORMAL · NBFC Audit | Credit Concentration | RBI Norms
In an audit of a Non-Banking Financial Company (NBFC), how are credit concentration norms verified by the auditor?
A. Checking whether credit exposure to single borrowers and borrower groups exceeds the limits prescribed by the RBI ✔
B. Verifying that the NBFC only lends to government entities
C. Ensuring that all borrowings are unsecured
D. Checking that administrative overheads do not exceed 10% of income
Explanation: RBI prudential norms for NBFCs prescribe concentration limits on lending and investments to single borrowers and group borrowers to mitigate credit risk. Auditors must verify compliance.
Medium NORMAL · Publisher Audit | Royalty Verification | Agreements
What is a primary audit concern when examining the accounts of a publisher regarding royalty payments to authors?
A. Ensuring royalties are calculated accurately based on sales/royalty agreements and verifying stock records of books sold versus unsold ✔
B. Checking whether authors are permanent employees of the publishing house
C. Verifying that royalty expenses are capitalized under intangible assets
D. Confirming that royalty is paid in advance before manuscript printing
Explanation: Publishers pay royalties based on contractual terms linked to sales or editions. Auditors must reconcile royalty statements with sales registers and stock movement records to ensure correct expenses.
Medium NORMAL · Cooperative Housing | Share Transfer | Nomination Register
When auditing a cooperative housing society, what is the significance of examining the 'Share Transfer Register' and 'Nomination Register'?
A. To ensure proper legal transfer of flat ownership, membership rights, and succession in case of a member's demise ✔
B. To calculate the corporate tax liability of the society
C. To verify the market valuation of building construction materials
D. To check the electricity meter readings for each apartment
Explanation: In cooperative housing societies, shares are linked to flat ownership. Verifying transfer and nomination registers ensures that voting rights and property rights vest in legally valid members.
Hard NORMAL · Manufacturing Audit | CWIP | Capitalization
What is the auditor's primary concern when reviewing 'Capital Work-in-Progress' (CWIP) in the audit of a manufacturing enterprise undergoing expansion?
A. Ensuring that pre-operative expenses are properly allocated and capitalization ceases when assets are ready for intended use
B. Checking whether employees working on the project are paid overtime ✔
C. Verifying that CWIP is depreciated at the standard rate of 15% per annum
D. Ensuring all project funds are kept in current accounts without interest
Explanation: CWIP represents assets not yet ready for use and is not depreciated. The auditor must verify that capitalization stops when the asset is ready for its intended use, and pre-operative expenses are allocated properly.
CASE SCENARIO: Green Valley Cooperative Housing Society Ltd., registered under the State Cooperative Societies Act, has 150 members. During the financial year 2025-26, the managing committee undertook major repairs to the society's water tank costing Rs 15 lakhs without inviting competitive tenders, citing urgency. Additionally, the society advanced a temporary loan of Rs 2 lakhs from its reserve fund to a committee member for personal medical emergencies. The statutory auditor appointed by the Registrar is reviewing the accounts.
Hard SCENARIO · Cooperative Audit | Procurement Tenders | Bye-laws Compliance
How should the auditor evaluate the contract for water tank repairs given that no competitive tenders were invited?
A. Ignore it since managing committees have absolute discretion in emergencies.
B. Verify whether the bye-laws or procurement rules of the society require tenders and whether emergency powers were validly exercised and ratified. ✔
C. Qualify the report solely based on the quantum of expenditure without checking bye-laws.
D. Treat the entire repair cost as a personal liability of the committee members.
Explanation: Cooperative societies must adhere to procurement procedures laid down in their bye-laws or state rules. The auditor must examine if emergency provisions exist and if the committee acted within its delegated powers.
Hard SCENARIO · Cooperative Audit | Loans to Members | Statutory Violation
What is the audit implication of the temporary loan of Rs 2 lakhs advanced from the reserve fund to a committee member?
A. It is completely valid if the member repays it within 30 days with interest.
B. It constitutes a statutory violation as cooperative funds and reserves cannot generally be lent to committee members unless specifically authorized by the Act/Registrar. ✔
C. It is acceptable as long as majority members consented informally at a tea party.
D. It should be reclassified as an administrative expense of the society.
Explanation: Lending society funds—especially reserve funds—to managing committee members is strictly regulated or prohibited under cooperative laws to prevent conflict of interest and misuse of mutual funds. This requires strong adverse reporting.
Medium SCENARIO · Cooperative Audit | Auditor Appointment | Registrar
Who is legally responsible for appointing the statutory auditor for Green Valley Cooperative Housing Society Ltd.?
A. The Managing Committee of the society
B. The Registrar of Cooperative Societies ✔
C. The Institute of Chartered Accountants of India
D. The National Housing Bank
Explanation: Under cooperative legislation, the statutory audit of cooperative societies is under the direct control of the Registrar of Cooperative Societies, who appoints the auditor from an approved panel.
Hard SCENARIO · Cooperative Audit | Special Report | Registrar
If the auditor discovers widespread financial irregularities, to whom must the special report under cooperative law be submitted?
A. Only to the Chairman of the managing committee
B. To the Registrar of Cooperative Societies and presented at the general body meeting as required ✔
C. To the local police station directly without informing management
D. To the stock exchange regulators
Explanation: Statutory audit reports of cooperative societies are submitted directly to the Registrar of Cooperative Societies, and significant irregularities must also be brought to the notice of the general body of members.
CASE SCENARIO: Hope Charitable Trust runs an educational hospital and a school. During 2025-26, the trust received Rs 50 lakhs as corpus donations with specific directions from donors that the amount be kept as permanent endowment. It also received Rs 10 lakhs in cash through hundi collection boxes without names. The trust utilized 70% of its total income for charitable objects, accumulated 15% under Section 11(2) by filing Form 10, and retained the remaining 10% as unspent surplus. The auditor is conducting the annual audit under the Income-tax Act and trust deed.
Hard SCENARIO · NGO Audit | Corpus Donations | Income Tax Act
How should the auditor verify the Rs 50 lakhs received as corpus donations?
A. Treat them as revenue income taxable at normal corporate rates.
B. Verify donor letters/instructions confirming corpus nature and ensure they are credited directly to the corpus fund balance sheet head, exempt under Section 11(1)(d). ✔
C. Deduct 30% tax at source before recording them in books.
D. Transfer them immediately to the income and expenditure account.
Explanation: Corpus donations received with specific directions that they shall form part of the corpus of the trust are exempt from income tax under Section 11(1)(d), provided they are invested or deposited in approved modes.
Hard SCENARIO · NGO Audit | Anonymous Donations | Internal Controls
What audit procedures are appropriate for verifying the Rs 10 lakhs collected through anonymous hundi boxes?
A. Obtain PAN cards of every devotee who dropped cash into the hundi.
B. Verify internal controls over hundi box opening, dual custody, physical counting in the presence of authorized trustees, and proper receipt issuance. ✔
C. Treat the entire hundi collection as taxable income without checking records.
D. Ignore the amount as it is below materiality thresholds.
Explanation: Anonymous donations in hundis lack direct donor identification. Auditors must rely heavily on robust internal controls governing hundi opening, counting committees, and contemporaneous documentation.
Hard SCENARIO · NGO Audit | Income Accumulation | Section 11
Is the accumulation of income by the trust compliant with income tax provisions governing charitable trusts?
A. No, trusts must spend 100% of income in the same year.
B. Yes, application of 70% plus accumulation of 15% (plus remaining surplus within statutory limits) along with filing Form 10 complies with Section 11 requirements. ✔
C. No, Form 10 is only filed by profit-making companies.
D. Yes, provided the surplus is distributed among the trustees.
Explanation: Under Section 11, a trust must apply at least 85% of its income to charitable purposes. It can accumulate up to 15% unconditionally, and further amounts if Form 10 is filed specifying the purpose and period.
Medium SCENARIO · NGO Audit | Trust Deed | Governance
What is the primary governing document the auditor must examine to verify the powers of the trustees of Hope Charitable Trust?
A. The Memorandum of Association of local commercial companies
B. The registered Trust Deed or Trust Indenture ✔
C. The SEBI Listing Obligations and Disclosure Requirements
D. The Banking Regulation Act guidelines
Explanation: The trust deed is the foundational legal document establishing a charitable trust, outlining the objects, powers of trustees, investment criteria, and governance rules.
CASE SCENARIO: Grand Palace Hotel, a luxury 5-star hotel, is undergoing its annual financial audit. The hotel operates a front office, multiple restaurants, a spa, and banquet halls. During the audit, the auditor reviews the night audit reports, guest ledger reconciliations, and inventory of food, beverages, and operating supplies (linen, cutlery). The auditor notes a significant variance between the stock of high-end liquor in the main cellar and the quantities issued to bars based on Kitchen Order Tickets (KOTs) and point-of-sale logs.
Medium SCENARIO · Hotel Audit | Night Audit | Revenue Controls
What is the primary purpose of the 'night audit' function in a hotel that the auditor must test?
A. To verify physical security guard attendance at night
B. To reconcile daily room occupancies, food and beverage sales, and guest billing totals to ensure all revenues are captured accurately ✔
C. To calculate annual corporate income tax provisions
D. To perform actuarial valuation of employee retirement benefits
Explanation: The night audit is a critical operational control in hotels where daily transactions across all revenue centers are audited, balanced, and posted to guest accounts before the next business day starts.
Hard SCENARIO · Hotel Audit | Inventory Variance | Pilferage
How should the auditor address the significant variance in liquor stock between the cellar and bar issues?
A. Write off the variance as normal evaporation without further inquiry.
B. Investigate physical security, issue slips, breakage records, complimentary drinks policy, and potential pilferage or unrecorded sales. ✔
C. Adjust the variance by capitalizing it under fixed assets.
D. Report it as a contingent liability in the notes to accounts.
Explanation: Unexplained variances in high-value inventory like liquor indicate potential leakage, theft, or unbilled sales. The auditor must perform detailed substantive testing and review internal controls.
Medium SCENARIO · Hotel Audit | Advance Deposits | Liabilities
What audit procedure should be performed regarding 'advance deposits' received from guests for future banquet bookings?
A. Recognize them immediately as hotel revenue on the date of receipt.
B. Verify that they are recorded as current liabilities (advance from customers) and not recognized as income until the banquet event actually takes place. ✔
C. Treat them as corpus donations exempt from tax.
D. Ignore them as they do not affect the balance sheet.
Explanation: Advance deposits for future room or banquet bookings represent cash received for services not yet rendered. They must be accounted for as liabilities until the service is delivered.
Medium SCENARIO · Hotel Audit | Receivables | External Confirmation
When verifying trade receivables (guest ledger and city ledger balances) in the hotel audit, what is the best corroborative audit procedure?
A. Sending direct confirmation requests to corporate clients and travel agents listed in the city ledger ✔
B. Asking the hotel general manager to verbally guarantee all outstanding balances
C. Tracing hotel room keys to guest names
D. Checking the electricity tariff rates applied by the utility provider
Explanation: External confirmation of receivables (especially corporate accounts and travel agents in the city ledger) provides reliable audit evidence regarding the existence and valuation of receivables.
CASE SCENARIO: Sunrise Power Distribution Ltd. (Discom) is audited by joint auditors appointed under the Electricity Act, 2003 and the Companies Act, 2013. The company has massive consumer connections across urban and rural areas. During the audit, the auditors review power purchase costs, transmission and distribution (T&D) losses, consumer meter readings, and subsidy receivables from the State Government. The audit team notes that subsidy claims amounting to Rs 25 crores for free power supplied to agricultural pump sets remain unconfirmed by the state government department.
Hard SCENARIO · Discom Audit | Government Subsidy | Receivables Valuation
What is the key audit concern regarding the unconfirmed government subsidy receivables of Rs 25 crores?
A. It has no impact since government dues are always recoverable.
B. It affects the valuation and recoverability of receivables under revenue recognition principles, requiring management representation and adequate provisioning if realization is doubtful. ✔
C. It should be capitalized as part of power transmission lines.
D. It must be treated as a contingent asset disclosed with high certainty.
Explanation: Unconfirmed subsidy claims from the government represent significant revenue and receivables risk. If the state government disputes or delays payment, provisioning or qualification may be necessary.
Hard SCENARIO · Discom Audit | Power Purchase Cost | Regulatory Tariffs
How should the auditors verify power purchase costs, which form the largest expense item for the Discom?
A. Check power purchase agreements (PPAs), CERC/SERC tariff orders, energy bills from generating companies, and joint meter readings at grid substations. ✔
B. Verify personal expense vouchers of plant engineers.
C. Inspect the share capital register of the power company.
D. Trace electricity bills of individual domestic consumers.
